docs.title: Dungeon Crawler Carl Compendium
docs.text:
A personal reference for the Dungeon Crawler Carl series by Matt Dinniman — built to be deeper and less cluttered than the existing fan wikis.

This is a work in progress. Most sections below are placeholders; two example pages (Carl and Level 1) are filled in to show the target depth and style.

docs.title: Sections
docs.text:
• Characters — crawlers, NPCs, bosses, deities, dungeon admins
  • Factions — Syndicate organizations, guilds, parties
  • Dungeon Floors — one page per level: layout, mechanics, notable events
  • Game Mechanics — boxes, feats, classes, races, status effects, currency
  • Items & Tattoos — loot catalog
  • Timeline — chronological events across the series
  • Glossary — crawler-speak and Syndicate terminology

docs.title: Abilities & Skills
docs.text:
Named physical combat skills tracked on a crawler's skill sheet — distinct from Spells, which are magic learned from tomes/scrolls and cost mana. Full pages exist for skills with real plot weight or scaling detail; everything else is covered on the Game Mechanics: Skills overview.

Any skill named in a full-page character's Quick Facts box must itself have a full page here, not just a mention in prose, matching the standard already established for Spells and Items & Tattoos.

docs.title: Book 8 skill catalog
docs.text:
Floors 10–11, "Don't Come in Last" and "A Parade of Horribles." Skills with full pages are listed above.

Name Owner Notes Cockroach Princess Donut Revealed this book to be a skill Donut personally possesses ("he doesn't trust my Cockroach skill"), not just Shi Maria's (see the Book 6 catalog row below). The book never shows how or when Donut acquired it — it's referenced as an established fact, not narrated as a new acquisition — though the existing Toraline Ink Tattoo System is the obvious candidate mechanism. A later class option (Elite Gurkha Warrior, not confirmed taken) would have boosted it to level 15 Razzmatazz Carl A performance skill granted by Porky (the left half of the split mantaur Corcunda, running the Floor 10 stage-performance guild) as a reward for freeing his suit's stuck zipper: "I will throw a few free skill levels onto your Razzmatazz skill." See Corcunda for Porky's full story Sticky Feet Carl Reused twice this book — bracing against a moving vehicle roof while throwing Biscuit Packs at flying insects, and again to keep footing during a floor-collapse tremor. No new mechanics shown; see the Book 6 catalog row for the original grant

docs.title: Book 6 skill catalog
docs.text:
Floor 8, "The Ghosts of Earth." Skills with full pages are listed above.

Name Owner Notes Climb Carl Granted by the Scavenger's Daughter. The system's own review: "You can climb stuff better. Ya-hoo. What an exciting benefit. I guess that makes you a monkey." Find Crawler Carl, level 5 From a "Minor Find Crawler Skill" potion in a Gold Scab box. The potion refuses to work on anyone who already has the skill at level 5 or above. Its blind spots matter: it cannot locate Sister Ines, which is what makes the Eye in the Sky scrolls valuable Wand casting Carl, level 5 Raised to 5 as a quest reward, which also came with a Gold Wand Box Find Traps Carl, → 13 A +3 upgrade potion pushes it to 13 — enough to see "pretty much any trap in the dungeon unless it was placed and deliberately hidden by a trapmaster" Smush Carl, base 12 / 14 effective Base level reaches 12. The Enchanted Pedicure Kit of the Sylph supposedly adds three more, but it still displays as 14 — "Like always, the skills got wonky when items buffs attempted to push them toward 15" Motorcycle riding Carl, level 9 Accumulated from the Book 1 goblin copper chopper and then pushed to 9 during his long solo ride across Florida on his father's Harley Automaton Pilot Donut, level 5 Earned during the Floor 6 hunter battles. Also lets her affix a limited set of traps to the backs of the small automatons Trap skill Donut, level 3 Too low for Carl's two-part traps. She can program a Loop-De-Loop (position swap) but only to trigger on fellow crawlers — she narrows it further to non-party crawlers — and because the skill is so low, a mob, NPC, or party member touching the plate makes it misfire immediately Sticky Feet Carl Plants a foot immovably against a surface; used to haul Mongo back up a collapsing, tilting barn floor Turtle Paz Lo An ability, not a spell: a temporary, powerful shield while the caster draws aggro. It also roots him in place and prevents him attacking or moving, and once cast it cannot be stopped until the timer runs out. If the shield breaks early he's freed, but still eats the excess damage of the attack that broke it Cosmic Sense Astrid Passive. Like Carl's deity-presence warning, but it detects both gods and demons — useful for the head of security at a giant nightclub, and the reason she survives the first phase of Carl's ambush Summon Guard Astrid Five times a day, instantaneously teleports "between one to three guards" from the club to her location. No cooldown, so she can fill a hallway with up to 15 guards at the snap of a finger Cockroach Shi Maria, level 15 A full heal on what would have been a fatal blow. As a T'Ghee card it works differently: when she "dies," the card returns to the deck rather than the discard pile Splitter Skylar Spinach (an enraged ghommid) Each split iteration is stronger than the last. Splitting a combined card returns upgraded "Gold Edition" halves

docs.title: Backfire
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Carl
  • Gained: Book 2, +5 skill level granted by his Compensated Anarchist class
  • Effect: Lets Carl pick up an existing trap and deconstruct it, recovering its materials — including valuable triggering mechanisms — for his own use
  • Notable: Called out by Mordecai as a genuinely rare skill

AI Commentary (in-voice, written for this wiki — not a book excerpt)

"Backfire: turning other people's murder machines into your own personal hardware store. One crawler's fatal trap is another crawler's Tuesday side hustle."

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Backfire is one of several skills bundled into Carl's Compensated Anarchist class card, picked on Floor 3 in Book 2. Mordecai singles it out as unusually valuable: "It allows you to pick up a trap and deconstruct it. You'll be able to use the materials for your own purpose. The triggering mechanisms alone are quite valuable. You could make a living just by farming traps."

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text:
The class card grants a flat +5 to the Backfire Skill on pick — the largest single starting bonus among Carl's new Compensated Anarchist skills. The class also grants +5% skill progression speed in all trap-making and bomb-making skills, applying here. No further per-level formula is given in the text.

Sourced from Book 2: Carl's Doomsday Scenario.

docs.title: Blend into the Background and Cone of Silence
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • User: Princess Donut
  • Source: The cat-sized ghillie suit from her Deathbed Hellcat class accessory kit (chapter 1)
  • Slot: The suit occupies a jacket slot despite magically covering her entire body
  • Set partner: The boonie hat that grants Targeting
  • Donut calls it a "ghoulie suit" for the entire book and is not corrected successfully

Both skills are named and neither is described

This is the honest state of the text. Carl explicitly says he has not had time to examine Blend into the Background, and never comes back to it. Cone of Silence is named once and never mentioned again. Do not infer mechanics for either from the names.

docs.title: The Only Description
docs.text:
I returned my attention to the small, cat-sized ghillie suit. It came with a few interesting benefits, though she would indeed look absolutely ridiculous in it. The thing looked to be made of long, shredded bits of color-changing fabric that blended into the background. It took up a "jacket" slot on in her inventory even though it magically covered her entire body once she wore it. The suit added a skill called Blend into the Background, which I hadn't yet had the time to examine, and a Cone of Silence benefit. Combined with invisibility, it would be great.

"Combined with invisibility" refers to the Deathbed Hellcat class's at-will invisibility. The suit is meant to stack with it, not replace it.

docs.title: The Set Bonus
docs.text:
Worn with the matching boonie hat:

If she wore both the suit and hat at the same time, all the benefits were buffed even further. She'd be able to snipe line-of-sight enemies from well over a mile away.

docs.title: Slot Compatibility
docs.text:
A minor but genuinely useful ruling from chapter 1, given Donut's expanding wardrobe:

"Your crupper is a waist accessory, the cloak is a shoulder accessory, and the ghillie suit is a jacket. You can wear all three at the same time."

So the suit, Fae Scale Crupper and the Cloak of the Benevolent Champion coexist.

docs.title: Use
docs.text:
Donut wears the suit for the sniping work: during the Harpocrates engagement (chapter 70) and in the Nest tower (chapter 73). It comes off in chapter 74 so Edgar can shave her flank for the Bijanbi tattoo.

The book's best joke at the suit's expense is the chapter-73 image of Donut in the top level of the tower, wearing the most thoroughly camouflaged garment she owns, with the Tiara of a Thousand Lights glowing "like a lighthouse beacon" on her head:

I finally rushed into the uppermost level to see Donut atop her seat, dressed in her ghillie suit leaning against the parapet, her face pressed against the invisible shield like it was glass. The camouflage suit was a strange contrast to her tiara which glowed like a lighthouse beacon.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: No levels given for either skill.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Targeting — the set partner
  • Tiara of a Thousand Lights — which entirely defeats the purpose of the suit
  • Hide in Shadows — Carl's equivalent

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Bomb Surgeon
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Carl
  • Gained: Book 2, +1 skill level granted by his Compensated Anarchist class
  • Effect: Lets Carl safely disassemble and resize explosives — cut dynamite into smaller, less potent charges, or strip smoke bombs down into components for trap-making

AI Commentary (in-voice, written for this wiki — not a book excerpt)

"Bomb Surgeon: because sometimes you don't want the whole building gone, just the one guy inside it who owes you money. Precision. Restraint. Very unlike this man's usual approach."

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Bomb Surgeon is one of several trap/bomb-making skills bundled into Carl's Compensated Anarchist class card (alongside Trap Engineer, Hide in Shadows, Backfire, and Escape Plan), which Carl picks on Floor 3 in Book 2. Even at level one, Carl describes an intuitive, almost tactile sense for explosives it grants him: "I could feel the depth of the blasting cap in my dynamite sticks. I could feel how close a piece of dynamite was to prematurely going off without having to consult the description."

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text:
The class card grants a flat +1 to the Bomb Surgeon Skill on pick, and the Compensated Anarchist class separately grants +5% skill progression speed in all trap-making and bomb-making skills, which applies to Bomb Surgeon along with its sibling skills. No further explicit per-level formula is given in the text beyond the improved sense of an explosive's internal state described above.

Sourced from Book 2: Carl's Doomsday Scenario.

docs.title: Book Burner
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • User: Carl
  • Type: Anti-magic skill — Carl notes that despite being a patch benefit, "it was really an anti-magic skill"
  • Source: The burning-book upgrade patch (medium), sewn onto the Enchanted Anarchist's Battle Rattle. The patch also grants +15% Intelligence
  • Uses: Once per day

docs.title: Effect
docs.text:
Once per day, you may cause an opponent your level or lower to forget a spell for a period of 30 hours. For every opponent player level above your own, this spell has a 5% chance not to work. You must know the exact name of the spell or you may choose to target the last spell that was cast.

Two ways to aim it: name the spell exactly, or simply strip whatever the target most recently cast. The 30-hour duration is deliberately longer than a day, meaning a spell taken away stays away past the next reset cycle.

Carl's reaction on reading it: "Whoa... That was pretty cool. Too bad it was only once a day."

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text:
The scaling is entirely relative to the opponent's level, not to any skill level of Carl's:

Opponent's level Behaviour At or below Carl's level Works Above Carl's level −5% success chance per level of difference

So the ability is reliable against peers and becomes a coin-flip around 10 levels up, worthless around 20. There is no training path — the patch grants a fixed effect, and the only way to improve the odds is for Carl to out-level his targets.

docs.title: Patch Context
docs.text:
The burning-book patch arrives alongside the Wand of Nighty-Night and a Minor Find Crawler skill potion in the same haul. The description declines to explain itself:

I think this might be a metaphor for knowledge being dangerous. Or maybe it's a metaphor saying you should burn books that suck. I don't know. Just because I recently took everything over doesn't mean I know what everything means. Most metaphors are bullshit.

Like all upgrade patches it is fleeting — it can be removed, but is destroyed in the process — and it benefits from the doubling effect of the Scavenger's Daughter back patch on its stat contribution.

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: Brain Trust
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • User: Princess Donut
  • Type: Natural benefit, selected when her Intelligence topped 100 (chapter 77)
  • Effect: All her spells operate one full level higher than their trained level
  • Consequence: Her level-15 Magic Missile fires at effective level 16 — and vaporizes its targets
  • Chosen for exactly that reason

The quietest of Donut's four natural benefits and comfortably the most consequential, because it applies to everything she owns at once and pushes her flagship spell past a number the series had treated as a hard ceiling.

Exact-verification note

No system description block exists. The two quotes below are the whole of it.

docs.title: The Choice
docs.text:
Donut is unambiguous about why she picks it:

FOR INTELLIGENCE I PICK BRAIN TRUST SO I CAN MAKE MAGIC MISSILE EVEN MORE POWERFUL.

docs.title: The Effect
docs.text:
Chapter 80, as a Reaver sentry dog ceases to exist:

This was the effect of Donut's Brain Trust upgrade. It made all spells operate at one full level higher than before. Not a huge deal, except her Magic Missile was now 15, meaning she was firing these things at level 16. Apparently that evaporated the targets completely.

The target "literally evaporated, having been turned into a rapidly expanding group of atoms."

"Not a huge deal" is Carl underselling it. A +1 to every spell is marginal at low levels and transformative at the top of the range, because 15 has been the practical maximum for the entire series. Brain Trust is the only thing that lets a crawler cast past it as a matter of routine.

The other confirmed beneficiary is Laundry Day, described in chapter 86 as "level-15, now enhanced to level-16" — which is the cast that rips Huanxin Jinx out of a goddess's soul armor.

docs.title: Level 16 and the Cap
docs.text:
Book 7 contains two distinct routes past level 15, and they are worth keeping apart:

Route Who Mechanism Training Carl's Mind Balance Genuinely trained from 15 to 16 by battlefield conditions. Earns the achievement "You now tread in the realm of gods!" Brain Trust Donut A flat +1 effective level applied on top of the trained level. The underlying spell is still 15

Carl's skill is 16. Donut's spells cast as if 16. The difference matters for anything that reads the trained value — most obviously War Crime, whose components must be at least level 8, and which explicitly ignores anything above that.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: No level of its own. It is a flat, permanent, universal +1 effective spell level, applying to Donut's entire arsenal — item-granted spells included, on the evidence of Laundry Day.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Magic Missile — the reason she picked it
  • Mind Balance — the other level-16 in the book, by a different route
  • Muscle Mommy — the Strength benefit chosen in the same conversation
  • Monologue, Wholesale Discount — the Charisma ones

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Claw
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • User: Princess Donut
  • Type: Natural cat-race skill. Every cat has it
  • Level: 4 for most of the series; "approaching 15" by chapter 86 (Book 7); broken to level 17 in Book 8 via a celestial boon
  • Boosted by: The Cloak of the Benevolent Champion, which Donut calls her shawl; permanently upgraded in Book 8 by a celestial godslayer box (glowing blue, functionally indestructible claws)
  • Notable use: Stripping every tech shield off Huanxin Jinx in a single pass (Book 7); decapitating the racer Dwight the unicorn in a single swipe (Book 8)

Donut has had this skill since the first floor and has spent eight books not using it, on the grounds that melee is inelegant. It turns out to be the thing that opens up the final kill of Book 7.

Exact-verification note

No system description block exists. The quotes below are the whole of it.

docs.title: The Reveal
docs.text:
Donut brings it up herself, mid-monologue, in front of a CEO who is about to die:

"I also recently upgraded a skill because of my lovely shawl. It's not quite at 15 yet, but it's getting there. Wanna know what it is?" … "All cats have it, naturally. It's called Claw. I was at level 4 before, but now I'm approaching 15."

The Cloak of the Benevolent Champion promised "One random skill from your list will increase to level 15 over the course of the next 504 hours" — three weeks, longer than the floor. Claw is the obvious candidate for that roll, and Donut credits the shawl explicitly.

Not conclusively confirmed

The book never states outright that Claw is the cloak's randomly-selected skill. Donut says the shawl upgraded it and that it is "not quite at 15 yet," which fits the cloak's 504-hour timer, but the connection is inferred rather than stated.

docs.title: Chapter 86
docs.text:
The stacking is absurd and Donut has worked it out in advance. Standing in the same room as the goddess Eileithyia, whose proximity buff gives female party members 500% melee power, and partied with Carl, whose own buff adds another 500%, while wearing the Spiked Knee Pads of Kina:

"And do you see my new knee pads? Aren't they lovely? … the Eileithyia boon is a 500% bonus against enemies. And because I'm partied with Carl, his bonus gives me another 500%. I don't have the same debuff he has because I'm a girl."

Then:

Donut moved like lightning, so fast I couldn't see. One moment she was on one side of the circle, and the next, she was on the other. Sparks flew in the air.

Huanxin, who'd pulled herself to her feet, was again on the ground.

… The shields around Huanxin were now just simply gone.

"But again," Donut continued, "That wasn't necessary. I'm just showing off a little."

Huanxin's shields are technological, not magical, which is why the anti-teleport circle of words of power does not touch them and why Laundry Day could not strip them. They have to be physically torn off, and the only member of the party positioned to do it is the cat who never uses melee.

See Crown of the Sepsis Whore for the full kill chain.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: No per-level description. The observable facts: level 4 for essentially the whole series, and "approaching 15" by chapter 86, with the increase attributed to an item rather than to training.

docs.title: Book 8: Broken Past 15 by a Celestial Boon
docs.text:
A direct parallel to Mind Balance breaking to 16

Just as Carl's Mind Balance trained past its level-15 cap under battlefield conditions in Book 7, Donut's Claw is pushed past 15 in Book 8 — but by a one-time divine reward rather than by combat training.

Killing the god Meatus earns Donut a celestial godslayer box. Unlike every other reward in the book, it leaves nothing physical behind — just a cloud of smoke shaped like Meatus, crushed by a smoky paw — and its actual payload manifests directly on Donut's body:

"Carl," Donut said, staring down at her forward right paw... She stretched her paw out, and she flexed so her claws appeared.

The kitchen table ripped in half.

When Donut extended her claws, the four front claws — but not her fifth or dewclaw — glowed brilliantly blue, like obnoxiously bright LED lights. When she retracted the claws, her paw continued to give off a faint glow.

Mordecai's explanation:

"Her prize is a type of celestial boon... It's permanent, and it affects a part of her body. In this case, it's her claws. Just on that paw. It's not a spell or a skill. Not in the way you're used to. Donut, your claws are more powerful now. You've been dipped in radiant light."

The in-game description tells Donut the claws "are so sharp, they can cut through anything in the mortal realm," and that she can use them to cut ghosts as well as physical matter — an ability otherwise restricted to specialized anti-incorporeal effects. Rosetta supplies claw caps (Donut picks purple, gets translucent red instead) so the permanently-glowing claws don't shred furniture, saddles, or Carl's shoulder by accident.

The skill itself jumps straight past its stated ceiling:

"My goodness," Donut said a moment later. "It's at level 17! 17! I thought it topped out at 15!"

Mordecai nodded... "It's from the gods, and when it comes to gods, all bets are off."

Level 17 — two full levels past the 15-level training cap that had held Claw (and every other trainable skill) all series, achieved instantly by divine fiat rather than by use. Mordecai frames the jump plainly as a combat upgrade: "With your buffed constitution, you've gone from a ranged powerhouse to one of the most powerful melee fighters in the game's history."

This same trip to level 17 is also the direct enabler of Donut crushing the Cadillac with Astral Paw and single-swiping the racer Dwight's head off later in the book — see that page's note on which feat belongs to which ability.
