docs.title: Soul Reaper (The Daughter's Kiss)
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • User: Carl
  • Type: Granted melee benefit — a charged finishing attack, not a spell (no mana cost, no casting, purely physical delivery)
  • Source: The Scavenger's Daughter back patch
  • Interface: Adds a Soul Essence bar directly below Carl's mana bar
  • Activated skill name: The Daughter's Kiss

Why this lives in Abilities

Soul Reaper is the passive item benefit; The Daughter's Kiss is the active skill it puts on Carl's skill sheet. Like Talon Strike — an item-granted, non-magical physical attack — it is catalogued here rather than under Items, with the patch that grants it cross-linked both ways.

docs.title: The Mechanic
docs.text:
For every creature you kill with a melee attack, the Scavenger's Daughter patch is charged with the essence of the fallen. Once fully charged, you may transfer this energy to a single melee attack, which will completely drain all the essence. This attack will have varying effects depending on the nature of the essence stored.

The associated essence bar is now visible in your interface. The total amount of soul essence you may store increases each time your essence bar is topped off and then drained. In other words, the more stuff you kill, the stronger you get.

Melee kills only. When the bar fills, the system announces "The Scavenger's Daughter has been fed. Unleash her wrath." Activating The Daughter's Kiss empties the bar into Carl's next melee strike.

docs.title: Purity Matters
docs.text:
The single most important rule is one the description only hints at and Carl works out in play: an essence bar built from one species is roughly twice as powerful, and reproduces that species' signature attack.

The power of the Daughter's Kiss special attack was much more potent if the captured souls in my back patch were all of the same species. If I killed nothing but Howling Gulls, and the soul essence bar was pure, when I unleashed my melee attack, it was almost twice as powerful than it would be otherwise. Plus, the residual effects of the attack were stronger. Howling Gulls used a scream attack, and when I dispersed the charge, it not only obliterated the monster, it unleashed a scream multiple times more powerful than what the Howling Gulls usually cast.

A pure charge spent on a dog-sized iguana mob called a Yuanat turns the creature to literal dust and leaves a ten-foot crater. Mixed charges are far less predictable: the effects vary "with the nature of the essence stored," and one release that Carl expects to make a ghommid explode instead snaps its donkey head clean off "with the sound of breaking pottery."

Mordecai's illustration of the ceiling: he once saw a crawler fill her essence reserve purely with gorgon souls, then kill a country boss with a single attack — turning it to stone and shattering it.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text:
The bar's capacity grows every cycle: each time it is topped off and then fully drained, the next bar requires more souls and delivers a bigger attack. By the midpoint of Floor 8 Carl has cycled it at least three times in one sitting and reports the attacks are "noticeably stronger already." There is no stated cap.

The practical scaling constraint is not the bar but the kill pool — a big bar takes longer to fill, and filling it purely requires finding enough of one species in a row.

docs.title: The Danger of a Full Bar
docs.text:
Carrying a full, undischarged bar is explicitly unsafe. The item's own warning buries it in a joke:

Warning: you know how asbestos is really bad for you? Like, it doesn't hurt you immediately, but it builds up in your lungs and eventually screws you over? Actually, you know what? Just ignore this warning. Forget I said anything. Carrying corrupted essence around on your back builds character. You already have a ring that's doing much worse to you anyway.

Mordecai is blunter: "Just make sure you drain the essence bar each time it fills up, and you'll be fine. That skill is ridiculously powerful. Just don't store the stuff for too long."

Carl feels it physically — a persistent itch at his neck and a rising unease as the bar approaches full — and is repeatedly tempted to bank a charge for a boss instead of spending it. What "screws you over" actually means is never stated.

Unresolved at book's end

The book closes with Carl having forgotten to discharge a full bar. A voice in his mind tells him: "You did not diffuse your soul power from the Scavenger's Daughter. That was a mistake. You should never allow it to linger within you. I need you alive, Carl. I need you reasonably sane." The consequence is not shown.

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: Deflection
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Holder: Princess Donut
  • Obtained: Book 4 — automatically unlocked on reaching Dodge skill level 10
  • Type: Passive combat buff, no mana cost

docs.title: Effect
docs.text: A permanent passive that halves the accuracy of both magical and physical ranged attacks (missiles and arrows) aimed at Donut. Per Mordecai, it isn't complete protection — it doesn't stop an attack outright, just makes it meaningfully more likely to miss.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: Unlocked at a specific skill threshold (Dodge 10) rather than scaling further with level; the book doesn't describe additional tiers.

docs.title: Side Effect
docs.text: Because Deflection only reduces the chance an attack hits Donut, redirected shots have to land somewhere — Mordecai notes this makes it statistically more likely that a missed attack meant for Donut instead strikes Carl or Mongo if either is standing nearby.

docs.title: Role in the Story
docs.text:
Donut's Dodge skill had been stuck at level 9 for a long stretch before a Book 4 loot-box skill potion finally pushes it to 10, immediately granting Deflection. It isn't shown saving her from a specific hit on-page before Floor 5 ends, but Carl and Katia both treat it as a meaningful survivability upgrade for a character with chronically low Constitution.

Sourced from Book 4: The Gate of the Feral Gods.

docs.title: Escape Plan
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Carl
  • Gained: Book 2, +5 skill level granted by his Compensated Anarchist class
  • Effect: Reveals hidden doors more readily, and grants access to the Dungeon Locator — an undocumented system feature even Mordecai had never encountered before
  • Notable: Functions more like a fixed perk unlock than a scaling combat skill

AI Commentary (in-voice, written for this wiki — not a book excerpt)

"Escape Plan: for the crawler who read the terms of service and found a clause even we forgot we wrote. Congratulations. You get a secret menu. Try not to tell anyone."

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Escape Plan functions as the Compensated Anarchist class's substitute for a proper Pathfinder skill (something several other classes, like Trickster, get outright). Mordecai is genuinely surprised by it — "Odd. It looks like it's an old skill, but I've never come across it before. You learn something new every day." Beyond improving hidden-door detection, its real value is unlocking access to the Dungeon Locator, a system feature the game itself doesn't explain: "It says it offers access to the Dungeon Locator, but it doesn't say what that is or how to access it." Mordecai happens to already know how to find and read it, despite never having seen the skill that grants access to it before.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text:
The class card grants a flat +5 to the Escape Plan Skill on pick. Unlike the other Compensated Anarchist skills, the text doesn't frame Escape Plan as something that scales its effect predictably with level — it reads more like a perk/access-unlock (hidden doors, the Dungeon Locator) than a stat that multiplies or improves numerically per level. No explicit per-level formula is given.

Sourced from Book 2: Carl's Doomsday Scenario.

docs.title: Find Weakened
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • User: Princess Donut
  • Source: The Cloak of the Benevolent Champion, Book 7 chapter 3
  • Granted at: Level 5
  • Stated effect: "So you'll always know who to protect first"
  • Actual use, per Carl's grim aside: Quan Ch, the item's previous owner, used it "for the exact opposite of its intended purpose. He'd used it to find and pick off the weakest crawlers in a group."

docs.title: Effect
docs.text: Among three or more creatures of a similar type, Find Weakened flags whichever one is closest to death. Framed by the AI as a healer's tool — triage at a glance — so a caster always knows who needs help first.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: No stated per-level progression; granted flatly at level 5 by the cloak, and not separately trained in Book 7.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Cloak of the Benevolent Champion — the source item

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Foot Soldier
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Carl
  • Gained: Level 3, Book 1
  • Effect: Increases damage dealt while kicking

AI Commentary (in-voice, written for this wiki — not a book excerpt)

"Foot Soldier: the sensible half of Carl's leg-based murder portfolio. Don't worry, the other half gets much, much weirder. See: Smush."

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Foot Soldier is gained at Level 3, in the same notification wave as Smush, and is the comparatively normal one of the pair — it simply increases the damage Carl deals with kicks, without any of Smush's unsettling in-voice flavor text. It rounds out Carl's leg-based offense alongside Smush's bare-foot finishing moves.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text:
The book doesn't give an explicit per-level percentage for Foot Soldier (unlike Smush's stated 10%-per-level pressure increase). It's tracked and leveled alongside Carl's other bare-knuckle skills — reported at Level 5 by the point he and Donut clear the Scatterer nest near the Hoarder fight, and Level 6 shortly after The Juicer fight.

Sourced from Book 1: The Apocalypse Will Be Televised.

docs.title: Fursona ("Fursuiter")
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • User: Carl
  • Type: New temporary-class mechanic — wearing a killed mob's skin as a costume grants temporary class benefits tied to that skin's type
  • Unlocking achievement: "Weaseler"
  • Granted class while active: Fursuiter
  • Revealed by: The kangaroo-costume infiltration of the boss Prison Pocket

Fursona is not flavor text — it's a genuine new game mechanic, distinct from any spell or ordinary trained skill, that the AI unlocks retroactively based on something Carl was already doing out of desperation.

docs.title: How It Starts
docs.text:
Racing to reach a two-space Nothing Spot before an engineer NPC could be claimed by a rival team, Carl skins a dead joey off the boss Prison Pocket's own trail of corpses and wears it as a costume to disguise himself as one of the boss's "babies":

Enchanted Juvenile Macropus Dominus Skin.

This item fills a costume slot. This can be worn as an outer garment.

Equipping this costume imbues the following effects:

Protection from Seeping Acid.

A level 10 Jump skill.

+5 to the Lotion Application skill.

Warning: This is a 12-hour timed item.

He hops (unable to walk normally in the suit — "Then I guess you gotta act like one") into Prison Pocket's pouch and detonates two hidden satchels from inside, killing the boss from within — see Prison Pocket for the full kill.

docs.title: The Skill Itself
docs.text:
Wearing the costume triggers a new personal skill, separate from the item's own listed benefits:

Or, at least, it worked once I hit level 5 in my new "Fursona" skill.

With each new skill level, the sensation that the suit was my actual body increased, which was terrifying.

Your Fursona skill is now level 8!

Yiffing is unlocked!

Carl declines to investigate what "Yiffing" does. The skill scales the immersion — how much the worn skin feels like the wearer's own body — rather than granting a stated combat benefit on its own.

docs.title: The Achievement: Weaseler
docs.text:
Killing Prison Pocket while wearing the kangaroo skin, from inside its own pouch, triggers a new achievement that formalizes the mechanic for the whole party going forward:

New Achievement! Weaseler!

You've donned the corpse of an enemy in an attempt to fool another creature! And then you ENTERED that creature.

Reward: Temporary classes while wearing corpse suits have been unlocked! You will now receive benefits and buffs associated with the suit you are wearing. These skills will go away once the suit is removed.

Current temporary class: Fursuiter.

This is the actual mechanic: prior to "Weaseler," wearing a corpse-skin costume like the Macropus Dominus skin presumably granted only its listed item benefits (Jump, Lotion Application, acid protection). After the achievement unlocks, wearing any corpse-suit costume also grants a temporary class — "Fursuiter" in Carl's case — with its own associated benefits and buffs, which disappear the moment the suit comes off.

docs.title: What Fursuiter Grants
docs.text: Not fully itemized on the page. What's shown: continued access to the suit's own listed benefits (Jump, Lotion Application, acid protection) plus whatever additional class-level buffs "Fursuiter" carries, layered on top of the escalating Fursona-skill immersion effect. The book doesn't give a complete Fursuiter class kit, and this page should not invent one.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Prison Pocket — the boss killed via this costume
  • Enriched Pet Biscuits — another Book 8 mechanic built around transformation and disguise

Sourced from Book 8: A Parade of Horribles.

docs.title: Heathen Scald
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • User: Carl
  • Type: Celestial Boon — a passive damage add-on, not a cast spell (no mana cost, no cast action; it simply applies)
  • Granted: Chapter 51, as the Reward for completing the church quest Kill the Blasphemer during the assault on Club Vanquisher — the AI frames it explicitly as "a Celestial Boon" from Emberus
  • Level: 15, flat, on receipt — not trained up to it
  • Duration: Floor-limited — "for the remainder of this floor"
  • Also referred to as: The "Heathen Burn" benefit (chapter 57) — the visible symptom is Carl's hands glowing

docs.title: The Grant
docs.text:
Immediately after Mork the ram-cultist's death completes the quest, and immediately after ten seconds of Emberus's own unhinged laughter over the comms:

Reward: You have received a Celestial Boon!

You have been blessed by your deity, Emberus. You have received a Celestial Boon!

Level 15 Heathen Scald Received.

For the remainder of this floor, any punch attack will add the Heathen Scald skill damage.

Carl's own reaction is a non-reaction: "I didn't have time to look that one up. All around, new things were happening" — the grant lands in the middle of the room full of trophy heads coming to life, and he never circles back to examine it properly on-page.

docs.title: Why This Is an Ability, Not a Spell
docs.text: The wiki splits Carl's Quick Facts spell list by the standing convention: mana-cost, cast-and- targeted effects go under Spells; passive or automatically-triggered combat effects with no mana cost go here. Heathen Scald fits the ability side cleanly — it is never "cast," has no mana cost, and simply adds bonus damage to an existing physical action (a punch) automatically for the rest of the floor, the same shape as Carl's other passive strike-boosting skills like Powerful Strike and Iron Punch.

docs.title: What It Does
docs.text:
The system gives no further breakdown of the "skill damage" figure it adds — no number, no percentage, no combat log ever quotes a bonus-damage value directly attributable to it. The only other confirmation in the text is indirect: a chapter-57 aside, while Li Jun needles Carl about his haul from the raid, that his hands are visibly glowing —

"I shrugged, suddenly uncomfortable. The glow came from the Heathen Burn benefit I had for the rest of the floor."

— which is the same boon under an informal name, still active six chapters later, still tied to "the rest of the floor" as originally stated.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: There is effectively nothing to scale: Heathen Scald is granted directly at a flat level 15 as a one-time Celestial reward rather than trained up through use, the way Carl's other skills are. No lower-level version is ever shown, no formula or per-level effect is given, and the text never revisits it with a specific damage number. It is not an example of training past the level-15 cap (contrast Mind Balance, which the wiki documents as actually broken past that cap by sustained battlefield conditions) — this is simply a boon issued at the cap and left there.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Floor-limited by its own grant text ("for the remainder of this floor"). It is never mentioned again after chapter 57, and does not appear anywhere in Book 8 — consistent with expiring at the Floor 8-to-9 transition along with Carl's other Club Vanquisher floor boon, The Martyr's Path.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• The Martyr's Path — Carl's other Emberus floor boon, also from Book 6/7's Emberus quest chain, also floor-limited
  • Powerful Strike — Carl's other passive per-punch damage skill
  • Mind Balance — for contrast, the series' actual example of a skill trained past the level-15 cap

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Hide in Shadows
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Carl
  • Gained: Book 2, +2 skill level granted by his Compensated Anarchist class
  • Effect: Stealth/concealment — self-explanatory per Carl, though he immediately notes its limits

AI Commentary (in-voice, written for this wiki — not a book excerpt)

"Hide in Shadows: a fantastic skill for the stealthy solo operative. Carl travels with a cat the size of a throw pillow and a velociraptor. Godspeed."

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Hide in Shadows is one of several skills bundled into Carl's Compensated Anarchist class card, picked on Floor 3 in Book 2. Carl calls it "self-explanatory" the moment he sees it, but immediately undercuts its usefulness for his own build: "with Donut and Mongo in tow, I imagined it wouldn't be too useful" — a stealth-class NPC-partner mismatch the book plays for a quick laugh rather than a real mechanical problem.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text:
The class card grants a flat +2 to the Hide in Shadows Skill on pick. No further per-level formula is given in the text.

Sourced from Book 2: Carl's Doomsday Scenario.

docs.title: Hover
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • User: Princess Donut
  • Type: Item-granted movement skill
  • Source: The Enchanted Tiara of the Inebriated Dragonfly
  • Level: 10 (fixed by the item)
  • Uses: 5 per day
  • Duration: ~90 seconds
  • Height: 2–3 feet
  • Cooldown: 5 minutes

docs.title: Effect
docs.text:
Donut hovers two to three feet off the ground and can move freely while doing so — Carl's description of her is "literally walking on air, tail swishing."

Two properties separate it from the Levitate spell:

  1. It is not negated by taking damage. Donut is struck hard enough by a flying bicycle to lose health and simply stays airborne.
  2. It arrests a fall. Activated mid-drop, it sets the user gently on the ground — which, as Carl notes, means both he and Donut now have fall protection.

Carl's honest assessment: "It was like a dollar store version of what Elle had."

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text:
The skill is locked at level 10 by the tiara and has no training path — losing the tiara loses the skill (and 10 Intelligence with it), which is the main argument against Donut wearing any of her other several hundred hats.

The real constraint is the five-a-day limit, which becomes a running gag and a recurring logistical problem. Donut burns hovers on practice ("I'm practicing, Carl. If I don't practice, how will I know how to use it?"), on showing off to other crawlers mid-mission, and on not walking. Carl spends much of Floor 8 telling her to stop wasting them, and at one point has to physically restrain himself from chiding her for burning one purely to demonstrate the skill to Tran's squad.

docs.title: Role in the Story
docs.text:
Her reaction on first equipping the tiara sets the tone for the rest of the book:

"I can fly now. Carl, I can fly! I'm like Wonder Woman!"

"Wonder Woman can't fly," I said.

Beyond the comedy, it gives Donut independent vertical mobility for the first time — she considers using it to scale a climb rather than ride Carl's shoulder, and it keeps her airborne and out of reach during the FOCSA street fight, where a bicycle passes straight through the space she'd have been standing in.

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: Iron Punch
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Carl
  • First seen: Level 3, Book 1
  • Official description: "When simple brutality isn't enough. Newsboy cap not included."
  • Granted by: Also boosted +2 skill levels by the Enchanted War Gauntlet of the Exalted Grull

AI Commentary (in-voice, written for this wiki — not a book excerpt)

"Iron Punch: for crawlers who looked at 'Pugilism' and thought, 'sure, but what if it also had a union card and a grudge?' Newsboy cap sold separately. We checked. It really isn't included."

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Iron Punch is first reported at Level 3, with a system description leaning into an old-timey "street tough" theme: "With a skill like this, you can always find work as a 1920s street tough or a collection agent for a bookie." It's a blunt-force punching skill distinct from the more academic-sounding Pugilism, though both stack together as part of Carl's overall unarmed-damage output.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text:
No explicit per-level formula is stated. It's tracked at Level 3 early on, then reported at Level 5 shortly after The Juicer fight. The War Gauntlet of the Exalted Grull, obtained around that same point, grants a flat +2 skill levels to Iron Punch on top of whatever Carl trains up naturally through combat.

Sourced from Book 1: The Apocalypse Will Be Televised.

docs.title: Love Vampire
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Princess Donut
  • Type: Passive Charisma-based ability
  • Unlock condition: 100 Charisma, reached in Book 3

docs.title: Effect
docs.text: Reflects damage back onto an attacking mob, provided that mob is a lower level than Donut herself.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: Not described in detail — the ability is newly unlocked and untriggered as of its introduction, so no scaling curve has been shown yet.

docs.title: Role in the Story
docs.text: Donut reaches 100 Charisma and unlocks Love Vampire partway through Floor 4, on Carl's earlier advice to prioritize the stat. She hasn't gotten to use it in practice by the time it's introduced, since the party has been deliberately keeping her out of situations where she'd take a hit from a lower-level mob.

docs.title: Book 5: Working "At Scale"
docs.text:
During the Butcher's Masquerade's climactic battle, with her Charisma temporarily boosted well past 300 by a benefactor tiara and other buffs, Donut announces mid-fight that "my love vampire skill works really good when it's this high" — at that moment, multiple elves in the crowd around her are shown fighting with little heart icons over their heads, apparently smitten with her ("It doesn't work on the bugs.").

Sourced from Book 3: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook and Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade.

docs.title: Mind Balance
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • User: Carl
  • Source: The Enchanted Toe Ring of the Well-Balanced, chapter 4 — left pinky toe
  • Granted at: Level 5
  • Stated effect: "Allows protection from Enslavement and Conscription"
  • Actual effect: Also blocks every attempt Shi Maria makes to seize Carl's body from inside him
  • Reaches level 16 — the first skill in the series trained past 15 by battlefield conditions rather than potions

This is the most important defensive skill Carl acquires in Book 7, and for the first ten chapters he has no idea it is doing anything at all.

docs.title: The Grant
docs.text:
Mind Balance, Level 5. Allows protection from Enslavement and Conscription.

Followed immediately, on equipping the ring:

Mind Balance is currently triggered.

"It didn't give any more information than that." Carl reads it, does not understand it, and moves on. It was triggered because it had already started working.

The stated purpose is Floor 9's defining threat: Conscript is how factions enslave unaffiliated crawlers, and the whole reason Carl bought a Faction Wars team in Book 6 was to avoid it. The AI's framing on the ring's description — "this has been given to you to save your ass because you're too dumb to realize how much danger you're in" — is about something else entirely.

docs.title: The Spam Folder
docs.text:
Chapter 14. Carl digs into the notifications he has been suppressing and finds hundreds of entries:

Gloom Wraith Phase failed to activate. Mind Balance prevented activation.

Your attempt to disable Mind Balance was prevented by Mind Balance.

Your Mind Balance has risen to level nine.

There were hundreds of these entries, over and over again. There were pages of me attempting to cast something, and each time, it got stopped.

Shi Maria — sealed in the Eye of the Bedlam Bride tattoo on his chest — has been trying to use Carl's own spells and skills, continuously, for weeks. Each attempt is logged as Carl attempting to cast, because from the system's point of view it is his body. And each one has been stopped.

The second line is the one that matters most: "Your attempt to disable Mind Balance was prevented by Mind Balance." She tried to turn the lock off, and the lock stopped her turning it off.

The specific Gloom Wraith Phase attempt logged there would have killed the ogre Carl was fighting and detonated his non-magical bombs in the process, which would have killed Donut.

docs.title: The arms race
docs.text:
The Mind Balance skill came from my new toe ring, though now it was trained up so much, I'd still have the skill, minus five levels, even if I took the ring off. I didn't dare.

The spider had managed to speak in my mind, despite the Mind Balance skill. She was getting stronger with each attempt to control me. But so was I. It was a race... She was constantly fighting against the Mind Balance skill.

That is the whole shape of it. Every attempt she makes trains the thing stopping her. She is levelling his defence by attacking it, and neither of them can stop.

The skill also outgrows its item. Once trained above the ring's level-5 grant, Carl retains it at minus five levels without the ring. He keeps wearing the ring.

docs.title: Level 16 — Breaking the Cap
docs.text:
Chapter 65, at the All Tree, under saturation psionic bombardment:

Warning: Your Mind Balance is currently overwhelmed as you are getting absolutely hammered with psionic debuffs.

You've been infected with ten more instances of Endless Thread of Distraction.

You've been infected with Self Harm.

You've been infected with Intrusive Thoughts.

Carl is reduced to a babbling idiot with his bare feet buried in an All Tree root. A voice — not Shi Maria, not Hapanzi, never identified — speaks to him: "You're family now, after what you did… Good, Carl. Good. She would be proud of you.*" Then:

Your Mind Balance is now Level 16.

New Achievement! You now tread in the realm of gods!

You've trained a skill past 15 using battlefield conditions, as opposed to just taking a bunch of potions to do it. That's quite the accomplishment. I'd ramble on and on about this, but you're currently a babbling idiot with your bare feet buried in an All Tree root. So let's speed up this Empire Strikes Back cave scene bullshit and get back to the action.

Reward: The skill is the reward. The good news is this level-16 Mind Balance will now wake your ass up.

The All Tree root dies and crumbles when he pulls free.

docs.title: What level 16 adds
docs.text:
I could now see them. The ones casting mind magic. That had come with my skill hitting 16.

He immediately starts painting the enemy mind mages for missile strikes. And in the same chapter:

Your Mind Balance has negated Bear Witness.

A level-16 crawler skill negating Bear Witness — a level-20 divine ceremony by the goddess Eris that freezes every mortal outdoors on the floor — is the clearest statement of what breaking the cap is worth. Carl is one of a tiny handful of people on Floor 9 who does not get scooped up.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text:
Level Event 5 Granted by the toe ring. Protection from Enslavement and Conscription 9 By chapter 14, purely from blocking Shi Maria's attempts 16 Chapter 65, from battlefield conditions. Grants visibility of mind-magic casters; negates a level-20 divine cast

Above level 5, the skill is retained without the ring at minus five levels.

Exact-verification note on 'first past 15'

The achievement frames training past 15 through combat as an extraordinary feat, and it is the first time the series shows it. Two other level-16 effects appear later in Book 7, but both come from Donut's Brain Trust natural benefit — a flat +1 to effective spell level — rather than from training. Her Magic Missile fires at 16 and her Laundry Day is described as "level-15, now enhanced to level-16." Those are a different mechanism.

docs.title: Book 8: Still Holding, and a Sibling Break
docs.text:
Mind Balance keeps doing its job in Book 8. During a mind-magic barrage, a single line confirms it is still silently blocking hostile psionic effects exactly as it did in Book 7:

Soul Suck has been negated by your Mind Balance skill.

Separately, Book 8 gives the series its second example of a skill broken past the level-15 training cap — this time Donut's Claw, pushed to level 17 by a one-time celestial boon rather than by battlefield conditions. See that page's "Broken Past 15 by a Celestial Boon" section for the full scene; the two breaks make an interesting contrast in mechanism (Carl's came from sustained combat pressure, Donut's from a single divine reward) even though both blow past the same wall.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Enchanted Toe Ring of the Well-Balanced — the source, and its two sibling skills
  • The Eye of the Bedlam Bride — what it is holding shut
  • Conscript — the threat it was issued for
  • Gloom Wraith Phase — the skill Shi Maria kept trying to fire
  • Bear Witness — the level-20 cast it negated
  • Claw — Donut's own level-15 break, in Book 8

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin and Book 8: A Parade of Horribles.

docs.title: Monologue
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • User: Princess Donut
  • Type: Natural benefit — one of several unlocked when a boosted stat tops 300
  • Stat: Charisma
  • Effect: Terrifies enemies by monologuing at them. The more terrified they are, the more experience she receives
  • Not a spell. It is a Charisma-derived benefit, tracked with her skills

The single most on-brand ability in the series. Donut has spent seven floors talking at people who would rather she stopped, and the dungeon has now decided to pay her for it.

Exact-verification note

No system description block exists. The narration below is the whole of it. The threshold is given as boosted stats topping 300 in this passage; Wholesale Discount is separately stated to unlock at Charisma topping 200, so the natural-benefit system evidently has tiers.

docs.title: The Description
docs.text:
Chapter 86, during the confrontation with Huanxin Jinx:

Donut's movements were mesmerizing. She was weaving a new charisma-based skill that terrified the enemy. The more terrified they were, the more experience points she received. It was called Monologue. It was something called a natural benefit. One of several benefits crawlers received when their boosted stats topped 300.

docs.title: Use
docs.text:
Its one shown use is the last confrontation of the book, and it is not incidental — it is the reason the scene takes the shape it does.

Huanxin Jinx is already beaten by the time Donut starts talking. She has been ripped out of the goddess Eileithyia's soul armor by Laundry Day, dumped into an anti-teleport circle of words of power, and had every tech shield shredded off her by Claw. The crossbow is already mounted on Donut's back.

Donut then stalks in slow circles around her, monologuing, farming experience off the CEO's terror, before delivering the actual point:

"Again," Donut said, continuing her slow, panther-like stalk in circles around Huanxin. "We don't really need to go through all this. But we want to. We want to show those of you on the 12th floor what's coming. You're strong, yes. But we are getting stronger every day. And you know what? We don't need to kill the gods and goddesses to win. No, honey..."

The crossbow on her back fired…

"...We just need to kill you."

"We don't really need to go through all this. But we want to" is a character statement and a mechanical one at the same time. The monologue is the attack.

See Crown of the Sepsis Whore for the full sequence.

docs.title: Spell or Skill?
docs.text: Tracked here rather than under Spells because the text is explicit that it is a natural benefit — an unlock earned by crossing a stat threshold, like Love Vampire at 100 Charisma or Muscle Mommy at 100 Strength — rather than something learned from a tome or costing mana.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: No level and no numbers. The only stated variable is the target's level of terror, which governs the experience payout.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Love Vampire — Donut's 100-Charisma natural benefit
  • Wholesale Discount — her 200-Charisma one
  • Muscle Mommy and Brain Trust — the Strength and Intelligence equivalents
  • Claw — what she uses in the same scene

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Muscle Mommy
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • User: Princess Donut
  • Type: Natural benefit, selected when her Strength topped 100 (chapter 77)
  • Effect: Boosts Mongo's Strength by 25% of Donut's own
  • Chosen over: The "Swole" benefit, on explicitly aesthetic grounds
  • Mordecai has reservations about the name

Donut reaches 100 Strength and 100 Intelligence in the same chapter and is offered a natural-benefit choice for each. She picks Brain Trust for Intelligence and this for Strength.

Exact-verification note

No system description block exists. Everything below is party chat and narration.

docs.title: The Choice
docs.text:
Mordecai sets it up: "You'll have a few choices you need to make for both your intelligence and strength now that they're both over 100."

Donut's reasoning, in her usual register:

Donut: GOODNESS, I'M NOT GOING TO PICK THE SWOLE BENEFIT. DO YOU REMEMBER WHAT IT DID TO CARL? CAN YOU IMAGINE? I'M GOING TO PICK MUSCLE MOMMY FOR STRENGTH SO MONGO IS STRONGER...

Mordecai: Uh, are you sure about that Muscle Mommy benefit?

Mordecai's hesitation is left hanging and never explained. He does not object to the effect; he objects, apparently, to the name — and Donut does not notice.

The decision itself is entirely in character: offered a personal Strength benefit, she immediately converts it into a Mongo buff.

docs.title: The Effect
docs.text:
Donut's own statement:

"with my new Muscle Mommy benefit, his strength is boosted by 25% of my own strength!"

So the benefit is a transfer, not a share: a quarter of Donut's Strength is added on top of Mongo's. As she trains Strength further, Mongo scales with her automatically.

Confirmed visually two chapters later: "Mongo was decidedly more buff with the Muscle Mommy benefit."

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: No level. It is a flat 25% of the owner's Strength, applied to the pet, and therefore scales for as long as Donut's own Strength keeps climbing.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Brain Trust — the Intelligence benefit chosen in the same conversation
  • Monologue and Wholesale Discount — the Charisma ones
  • Love Vampire — her first natural benefit, at 100 Charisma
  • Twinkle Toes — Donut's other Mongo buff

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Pied Piper
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • User: Carl
  • Granted by: The god Harpocrates, chapter 70, via the Scavenger's Daughter's deity-proximity mechanic
  • Level: 15
  • Made permanent: Chapter 76, by a coin flip from the goddess Eris
  • What it actually does: Lets you play musical instruments
  • "It's not like the fairy tale and has nothing to do with rodents"

The most anticlimactic permanent ability in the series, acquired by the most dramatic means available.

docs.title: The Grant
docs.text:
Chapter 70. Carl's back patch opens her eyes near a god:

You are in the presence of a deity. The Scavenger's Daughter has opened her eyes.

You are now within range of the god Harpocrates.

Temporary effect from Harpocrates:

Level 15 Pied Piper skill.

Standard Scavenger's Daughter behaviour: a random, temporary, god-specific effect that fades when the deity leaves range.

docs.title: The Coin Flip
docs.text:
Chapter 76. Eris — goddess of chaos, currently rolled up inside a screaming ball of tens of thousands of people thanks to Donut's Rolling Battle Formation — comes into range:

You are in range of Eris.

Random Effect! As Eris is the goddess of chaos, this effect will change each time you are in her presence.

Temporary effect from Eris:

One current god effect will be permanent!

Carl has exactly two active god effects at that moment. A spinner appears in front of him with two entries on it:

Dick will fall off!

Level-15 Pied Piper!

The first is from the feral god Meatus, whose chapter-76 contribution was "Your dick will fall off if you get an erection."

It stopped on Dick will fall off! hovered for a second, then ticked over to Level-15 Pied Piper!

Your benefit from Harpocrates is permanent!

A 50/50 spin, landing on the wrong side first, then moving. Carl permanently acquires the ability to play musical instruments instead of permanently acquiring a genital curse.

He gets the other one anyway

The Meatus effect is separately made permanent in chapter 77, when the god "hasn't exactly left the realm. He's now slap-chopped all over the realm" and the system announces "the benefit fades, though you now have it permanently, which, I gotta tell you, ain't all that exciting." Carl does not win the coin flip so much as defer one half of it.

docs.title: What It Does
docs.text:
Chapter 79, Carl explaining to Donut, who has ideas:

"I didn't get to keep Pied Piper until after that had happened, and the skill allows me to play musical instruments. It's not like the fairy tale and has nothing to do with rodents."

Donut had suggested combining it with her Oak Fell spell Gather Ye, Vermin, which draws all small mammals within ten kilometres to her location. The combination would, in fairness, be a fairly accurate reconstruction of the fairy tale. Carl declines. His bagpipes remain in the "probably-never-going-to-need-this-stuff" folder.

At level 15 — the practical maximum — Carl is now among the best instrumentalists in the dungeon, and has no use for it whatsoever.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: Fixed at level 15 by the grant. No progression described.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• The Scavenger's Daughter — the deity-proximity mechanic that supplied it
  • Bear Witness — Eris's other, much larger intervention
  • Speedster — the other benefit Carl gains this book, and a considerably more useful one

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Powerful Strike
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Carl
  • First seen: Book 1, via the Enchanted Toe Ring of the Splatter Skunk (+3 to the skill)
  • Effect: Multiplies unarmed damage per skill level
  • Granted by: Also boosted +1 skill level by the Enchanted War Gauntlet of the Exalted Grull

AI Commentary (in-voice, written for this wiki — not a book excerpt)

"Powerful Strike does exactly what it says on the tin, which frankly is rare for this dungeon. No innuendo, no foot fetish, just pure multiplication. Almost suspicious, really."

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Per Mordecai, Powerful Strike is one of the most mechanically significant skills in Carl's build: "Each level multiplies your damage when you're not wielding a weapon. So at level three, each kick or punch does three times the damage it normally would." Combined with Unarmed Combat and Pugilism, Mordecai notes it's already making Carl's fists hit harder than either of his starting melee weapons — and suggests a monk class might enhance it further.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text:
This is one of the few skills in Carl's kit with an explicit, stated formula: each skill level directly multiplies unarmed damage (level 3 = 3x normal damage). It was first boosted +3 by the Enchanted Toe Ring of the Splatter Skunk, and later gains a further +1 skill level from the War Gauntlet of the Exalted Grull — a direct, permanent boost to the multiplier on top of whatever level he trains up naturally.

Sourced from Book 1: The Apocalypse Will Be Televised.

docs.title: Pugilism
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Carl
  • First seen: Level 4, early Book 1
  • Official description: "The art of beating the shit out of your opponents with closed fists."

AI Commentary (in-voice, written for this wiki — not a book excerpt)

"Pugilism: for when 'punching' needs a fancier word so it sounds like a skill and not just a bar fight. Same result either way — somebody's teeth end up on the floor."

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Pugilism is one of the earliest named combat skills Carl gains, first reported at Level 4 via a system notification during his Level 1 fights. It's the closed-fist counterpart to skills like Foot Soldier (kicking) and Smush (bare-foot finishers) — together these make up the core of Carl's refusal to carry a real weapon.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text:
No explicit per-level formula is given in the text (unlike Powerful Strike's stated damage multiplier). It's tracked alongside Carl's other bare-knuckle skills and rises through repeated use — reaching Level 10 by the back half of Book 1, at which point the system explicitly calls out the milestone: "Your Pugilism Skill has been increased by 3! Your Pugilism Skill is now level 10." Combined with Iron Punch, Powerful Strike, and his base Unarmed Combat, it's cited as the reason his fists eventually pack "just as much damage" as Brandon's lightning maul.

Sourced from Book 1: The Apocalypse Will Be Televised.

docs.title: Rush (and Crowd Blast)
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Katia
  • Type: Physical active skill (no mana cost)
  • Cooldown: Once daily (base Rush) → once every 5 minutes (upgraded Crowd Blast, Book 3)
  • Upgrade source: Enchanted Shade Gnoll Riot Forces Crowd Control Shield

docs.title: Effect
docs.text:
Rush propels Katia's body forward like a battering ram, dealing heavy impact damage to whatever she hits. Both its distance and aim are canonically unreliable — it's been observed to travel anywhere from roughly 5 to 20 feet and doesn't always land on the intended target.

Crowd Blast, its Book 3 upgrade, keeps the forward-charge mechanic but adds a wide damage cone in front of Katia as she moves: everything caught in the cone (not just whatever she directly hits) takes an additional 10–20% of the primary impact's damage.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: No stated per-level formula for raw damage. The meaningful scaling shown so far is in cooldown: base Rush is limited to once per day; the Crowd Blast upgrade drops that to once every five minutes, making it viable as a repeatable combat tool rather than an emergency-only option.

docs.title: Role in the Story
docs.text:
Rush is first used to punch Katia through a solid wall during the Book 2 Doomsday Scenario crisis. In Book 3, a Rush attack aimed at Eva Sigrid misses and instead slams into Hekla, killing her outright — the single most consequential use of the skill so far, and the reason Katia is visibly reluctant to use it again even after it's upgraded. Once upgraded to Crowd Blast, she uses it deliberately to break through packed hallways of Krakaren monsters and ghouls during the Iron Tangle's floor-wide crisis.

Sourced from Book 2: Carl's Doomsday Scenario and Book 3: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook.

docs.title: Smush
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Carl
  • Gained: Level 3, Book 1 (alongside Foot Soldier)
  • Effect: +10% bare-foot crushing pressure per skill level
  • Notable: The origin of the System AI's running "foot fetish" joke about Carl

AI Commentary (in-voice, written for this wiki — not a book excerpt)

"Look, I don't make the rules. I just really, really enjoy reading them out loud. Especially this one. Especially to him."

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Smush is delivered with noticeably different narration than any other skill Carl receives — the system's voice turns "deeper, more throaty than usual," described as sounding like someone "beating himself off while he said it." The official description reads:

Smush: Skill Level 3

"Killing with your feet. Your bare, beautiful feet."

"Taking your bare foot, placing it on top of a living, conscious life, and then pressing lovingly down until that life ceases to be. Is there a more noble way to kill?"

"The amount of pressure you can bring to bear upon an enemy with your unshod foot is increased by 10% with each level of this skill."

Carl concludes the AI (or whatever controls the game's descriptions) "really did have some sort of foot fetish." This isn't a one-off joke — it recurs throughout Book 1 in the form of foot-focused achievements, item flavor text, and narration bits, cementing it as one of the series' most persistent running gags.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text:
Explicitly stated: +10% bare-foot crushing pressure per skill level. It levels alongside Carl's other bare-knuckle skills through use — reaching Level 5 by the point he clears the Scatterer nest near the Hoarder fight, and Level 6 shortly after The Juicer fight. The Enchanted Pedicure Kit of the Sylph also grants temporary bare-foot combat buffs that complement it, including an "unbreakable" feet effect that saves Carl's life during an explosion later in Book 1.

Sourced from Book 1: The Apocalypse Will Be Televised.

docs.title: Speedster
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • User: Carl
  • Source: The Enchanted Hairbrush of the Beefmaster, chapter 56 — active for 30 hours per use
  • Effect: Move short distances extremely quickly
  • Best feature: Multiplies the distance he can cover while phased with Gloom Wraith Phase
  • Rarity: Mordecai had never seen it awarded by an item. It is normally a rare natural unlock at Dexterity 100

Exact-verification note

No system description block exists for the benefit itself — only the hairbrush's item block listing it. The explanation below is Carl's narration.

docs.title: What It Does
docs.text:
The benefit was similar to Donut's Twinkle Toes spell, though instead of casting it on Mongo, it worked on myself. I could already run super-fast thanks to my strength and dexterity, but Speedster basically allowed me to move short distances very, very quickly. I wouldn't be quite like the Flash superhero, but I was still impressively quick. And while I couldn't do it long distance, I could flash across the battlefield in seconds. And best of all, I could combine it with my Gloom Wraith Phase, allowing the distance I could travel while phased to be much further.

The constraint is important and Carl states it twice: short distances only. This is not a travel skill. It is a repositioning skill, for crossing a battlefield in bursts.

docs.title: The Combination
docs.text:
The real value is stacking it with Gloom Wraith Phase, Carl's Celestial non-corporeal lunge. That skill's range is a function of how far he can move during the phased window, and Speedster extends exactly that.

At level 10, Gloom Wraith Phase lets him hold the phased state for five seconds. Five seconds of Speedster movement, passing through unenchanted walls and flesh, is a considerably longer distance than five seconds of running.

docs.title: Rarity
docs.text:
Mordecai's reaction is the tell:

Mordecai said he'd never seen the Speedster benefit awarded like this before. It was usually something someone could sometimes get when their dexterity naturally reached 100, though even then, it was rare. The crawler Osvaldo, who was not a member of the Princess Posse, supposedly had the benefit.

So Speedster is normally a natural benefit — the same category as Donut's Muscle Mommy and Brain Trust — and not a guaranteed one even at the threshold. Getting it from a hairbrush is anomalous.

docs.title: The Catch
docs.text:
It is not permanent. Every use of the hairbrush buys 30 hours, and the hairbrush can only be used once per day, on one person, for five continuous minutes, and only by someone with at least 25 cm of hair.

Which means Speedster can in practice be kept running indefinitely — thirty hours of benefit on a twenty-four-hour cooldown leaves six hours of slack — provided Carl performs a five-minute screaming hair-brushing ritual every day of a war and never cuts his hair.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: No level is ever given.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Enchanted Hairbrush of the Beefmaster — the source, and the other three benefits
  • Gloom Wraith Phase — what it multiplies
  • Twinkle Toes — Carl's own comparison
  • Pied Piper — the other benefit he picks up from a god this book

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Talon Strike
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Carl
  • Granted by: The Enchanted Necklace of the Haute Bourgeoisie (a Poor Sapphire gem tied to the Medium Skyfowl Settlement), not trained independently — Book 3
  • Type: Physical melee skill, not a spell
  • Effect: Turns a bare-foot kick into a slashing weapon, with a chance to instakill

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Talon Strike arrives as a +5-level bonus attached to a gem on a leadership necklace Carl loots from a Platinum Tyrant's Box — a reward tied to his accidental, brief rule over the Medium Skyfowl Settlement on Floor 4. Its official description leans into the same over-the-top violence theme as Smush:

"Birds have ugly feet. Disgusting feet, really. Still, there's something sensual about the sight of a hawk swooping down upon its prey, talons out, and slashing... Turns the side of your bare foot into a fast-moving slashing weapon, increasing the damage against opponents by up to (Level of skill) times your regular kicking damage for (Level of skill) seconds. Each kick using this skill has a 2% chance to cast the instakill spell Eviscerate. This melee skill has a cooldown of five minutes."

Carl uses it in combat almost immediately, smashing open two downed monsters' heads with quick foot jabs, and later during a drop-kick against the mob "Gore-Gore" and in the climactic Iron Tangle train battle alongside Bang Bro.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text:
Explicitly stated: damage multiplier and effect duration both scale directly with skill level (level N = N-times kicking damage for N seconds), and the 2% Eviscerate proc chance increases at higher levels too, per the same description. At level 15, Talon Strike becomes permanently active rather than needing to be triggered — the highest confirmed cap for a Carl skill so far.

Sourced from Book 3: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook.

docs.title: Targeting
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • User: Princess Donut
  • Original source: The boonie hat that ships with her Deathbed Hellcat class accessory kit (chapter 1)
  • Permanent source: Absorbed into the Tiara of a Thousand Lights in chapter 3; confirmed active in the tiara by chapter 32
  • Effect: Zoom in on and examine mobs at a distance, plus a range increase to all her spells
  • This is the skill the Book 6 "advanced targeting" flag was pointing at

Exact-verification note

No system description block exists for this skill. The narrated paragraph below is the entire description Book 7 gives.

docs.title: The Description
docs.text:
The floppy hat added a Targeting skill, which allowed her to zoom in and examine mobs from afar. It was similar to the gnomish farseerer, but a lot less awkward. It also increased the range of all her spells, even more than they were already buffed.

"Even more than they were already buffed" refers to the Deathbed Hellcat class, which by itself quadruples the range of every spell Donut owns. Targeting stacks on top of that.

The hat is beige and, per Donut, "extra floppy, and that's always a nice bonus. I do like floppy. Though it completely clashes with my fit." Carl identifies it: "We call those boonie hats. It's not the same thing as a bucket hat. It's what snipers wear.*"

docs.title: The Set Bonus
docs.text:
Worn together with the matching ghillie suit from the same accessory kit:

If she wore both the suit and hat at the same time, all the benefits were buffed even further. She'd be able to snipe line-of-sight enemies from well over a mile away.

See Blend into the Background and Cone of Silence for the suit.

docs.title: Into the Tiara
docs.text:
Mordecai's very first instruction on receiving the Tiara of a Thousand Lights charge pillow is to drain this specific hat before anything else:

"The first thing you'll want to put on that pillow is that hat you just got with the targeting ability. And set a timer in your own interface… You can't see if it worked until you pull the drained item off, so you have to be extra, extra careful."

The transfer is confirmed in chapter 32: "Donut was examining the orc prince via her new Targeting skill which had just been added to her crown." (She uses it to correctly identify King Rust rather than Prince Stalwart, which is the first time the skill earns its keep.)

The point of moving it into the tiara is that Donut no longer has to wear a beige hat that clashes with her fit in order to have it.

docs.title: The Payoff — Chapter 61
docs.text:
This is the line the Book 6 flags on Magic Missile and Tiara of Mana Genita were reaching for:

Crack! That was a new sound, and it took a moment for me to realize what it was. It was Donut casting Magic Missile. With her tiara's advanced targeting skills and Donut's elevated position, along with her Deathbed Hellcat class, she could hit anything she could see with any of her long-range spells. It was louder than expected.

docs.title: Why It Reshapes the Endgame
docs.text:
The Nest tower was designed to give Donut exactly this capability:

Originally, we planned on making it a straight-up sniper tower, which would greatly enhance Donut's ability to zero in on a target across the battlefield. But it turned out with her tiara, that was unnecessary. All Donut needed was line of sight to apply her sniper skills.

Which, in turn, allowed us to assign a different synergy to the tower.

The Nest was instead built to have synergy with something called Atrocity-class spells.

So a floppy beige hat, drained into a tiara, is the reason War Crime can be cast over an entire battlefield instead of a narrow cone.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: No level is ever given for Targeting, and no per-level behaviour is described. The two stated multipliers are the Deathbed Hellcat class's 4× spell range and the ghillie suit set bonus.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Tiara of a Thousand Lights — its permanent home
  • Magic Missile — the spell it most obviously serves
  • Blend into the Background and Cone of Silence — the set partner
  • War Crime — what the freed tower synergy enabled

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: The Martyr's Path
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • User: Carl
  • Type: Floor boon — granted by Emberus, valid for Floor 8 only, and revocable by the god at any time
  • Granted: By high priest Pater Coal, who washes Carl's feet "in the fires of the dying sun" in the Emberus temple at Club Vanquisher: "Now every step you take will be in Emberus's path"
  • Requires: Remaining in Emberus's grace (see Deity worship)
  • Bundled with: +10% Strength

docs.title: The Boon
docs.text:
The fire of righteousness fills you with power. You have been granted a floor boon. This boon will remain in place for the remainder of this floor as long as you remain in Emberus' grace. He may revoke this boon at any time.

The Martyr's Path. Every step you take may be your last, so make them count. Every step you make while you are outside a structure will be marked on the map. If your health reaches 5%, you have the option to release a gout of flame from each spot upon which you stood. Steps reset each time this is activated. This will activate automatically upon your death.

The mechanic is a slow-burn trap laid by walking. Every outdoor footstep Carl takes is recorded on an internal map. At 5% health or below he may detonate all of them simultaneously, sending a gout of flame up from every marked spot at once. The step map resets on each activation, and it fires automatically if he dies — which is what makes it a martyr's path rather than a tactical option.

Two constraints matter in play: outdoors only (indoor movement is not recorded), and the 5% health gate means the ability can only ever be used from the edge of death.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: No level and no numbers. The ability's power is a function of distance walked outdoors since the last activation, which makes it unusual among Carl's abilities — it scales with patience and routing rather than with training. Across the back half of Floor 8 Carl covers an enormous amount of Havana on foot and by motorcycle, so by the climax the marked map is effectively the whole city.

docs.title: The Climax (Chapter 70)
docs.text:
Carl uses it once, deliberately, at the worst possible moment by design. His reasoning, laid out in advance:

If I wanted my eighth-floor-only Martyr's Path benefit to activate, I would have to be under 5% health. It would release flames over all of my outside-of-buildings footsteps. Since my fire attacks were currently enhanced with Sheol fire, and since I'd run underneath the demon, it would bathe the demon in Sheol fire. It would enhance his power. Hopefully enough.

That is the whole plan stacked in one sentence. The Scavenger's Daughter patch, reacting to the presence of a prince of Sheol, had upgraded all of Carl's fire attacks to Sheol Fire. So the flame released from thousands of footprints across Havana is not fire — it is hellfire. And Carl had been careful to route himself directly beneath Amayon.

The Martyr's Path has engulfed your steps.

The result bathes a city and a level-250 demon prince in Sheol Fire simultaneously — which, per the quest terms, is exactly what Amayon needed to gather the strength to cast his way home.

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
The boon is explicitly floor-limited. It does not carry past Floor 8.

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: Trap Engineer
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Carl
  • Gained: Book 2, +1 skill level granted by his Compensated Anarchist class
  • Effect: Not elaborated on beyond the class bonus itself

AI Commentary (in-voice, written for this wiki — not a book excerpt)

"Trap Engineer. Exactly what it sounds like, no follow-up needed — which, for this dungeon, is basically a miracle."

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Trap Engineer is one of several trap/bomb-making skills bundled into Carl's Compensated Anarchist class card (alongside Bomb Surgeon, Hide in Shadows, Backfire, and Escape Plan), picked on Floor 3 in Book 2. Unlike Bomb Surgeon and Backfire, the text doesn't give Carl an in-scene moment demonstrating what the skill actually does beyond its name — it's simply listed on the class card.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text:
The class card grants a flat +1 to the Trap Engineer Skill on pick. The Compensated Anarchist class also grants +5% skill progression speed in all trap-making and bomb-making skills, which applies here. No book text yet clarifies a specific per-level effect.

Sourced from Book 2: Carl's Doomsday Scenario.

docs.title: Unarmed Combat
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Carl
  • Starting level: 3 (from his real-world Coast Guard hand-to-hand training)
  • Type: Foundational physical combat skill, not a spell

AI Commentary (in-voice, written for this wiki — not a book excerpt)

"Achievement unlocked: 'Unarmed Combat' — awarded the instant this idiot strolled into a dimension-hopping death dungeon without so much as a butter knife. Braver than he looks, or dumber. We're still workshopping which."

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Unarmed Combat is the base hand-to-hand skill already present on Carl's character sheet the moment he enters the dungeon, a holdover from his real-world background as a Coast Guard MK (machinery technician) with above-average hand-to-hand training. It's the foundation his entire bare-knuckle fighting style is built on top of — every other combat skill he picks up (Pugilism, Foot Soldier, Iron Punch, Powerful Strike, Smush) stacks on top of this base rather than replacing it.

Entering the dungeon with no weapon at all also triggers a dedicated system achievement:

"So. You just gonna waltz right into something called a 'World Dungeon' and you're not even going to bring a weapon? You're either braver than you look, or you're just an idiot. Good luck with that, Van Damme."

Reward: You've received a Bronze Weapon Box!

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text:
The book doesn't give an explicit per-level formula for Unarmed Combat specifically (unlike Powerful Strike, which has a stated multiplier). It's described as rising alongside Carl's other bare-knuckle skills through repeated use — by late Book 1 it's one of several stacked skills that, combined with gear like the War Gauntlet, let his fists hit as hard as an enchanted weapon.

Sourced from Book 1: The Apocalypse Will Be Televised.

docs.title: Walk on Air
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • User: Carl — stolen from Li Jun
  • Acquired: Book 6, chapter 71, when Shi Maria forced Carl to gouge out Li Jun's eye with a tattoo stick and eat it. Carl did not know he had it until Book 7, chapter 4
  • Effect: Literally walk on air, for very short periods
  • Cooldown: One minute — though a follow-up jump can be made without it
  • Li Jun lost it permanently. His brother had to buy a book to relearn it

This is the first documented transfer in what becomes the toraline ink tattoo system, and the party works the entire mechanic out backward from it.

docs.title: "(Already Obtained)"
docs.text:
Carl discovers it by accident, reading the description of his new Enchanted Toe Ring of the Well-Balanced:

Physical Balance, Level 5. At level five, this skill imbues both the Extra Steady Balance skill and the Walk on Air Skill (already obtained.)

"Already obtained?" I asked out loud. That didn't make sense. I moved into my menu. I knew what Walk on Air did, but I didn't have that skill. It was what Li Jun…

I swallowed, suddenly feeling very, very dirty.

It was what Li Jun used when he fought.

The memory of the taste of Li Jun's eye flooded my mouth. I had the sudden urge to vomit. I remembered what Shi Maria had said after she'd plucked the eye out of him. That I might gain some of his skills.

Carl messages Li Jun to apologise and gets no answer.

docs.title: What It Does
docs.text:
The only description in the text is Carl's own, in the same chapter:

The skill worked exactly how it sounded. It allowed one to literally walk on air for very short periods of time, which was especially useful in hand-to-hand combat. It was kung fu movie stuff, and it required a lot of practice to get right.

Which is generous. In use it is considerably less elegant, and Carl says so in chapter 68:

The skill was not a flying skill, and it didn't work all that great. It was more of a glorified long jump.

The Walk on Air had a one minute cooldown, but I could make the next jump without it.

That last clause is the useful bit of mechanical detail: a second jump can be chained immediately, and only then does the minute run.

docs.title: The Rule It Establishes
docs.text:
Rosetta, chapter 47, stating the tattoo system's central rule and citing this exact case as her evidence:

Spells and skills taken against the owner's will were much more powerful and resulted in the owner losing them permanently. My Walk on Air skill, stolen from Li Jun, was proof of that.

The cost fell entirely on Li Jun. He lost the skill permanently, and the eye is unhealable. Chapter 40 notes that "her brother got Walk on Air back, but they had to buy a book" — a replacement purchase, not a recovery.

Compare the consensual version: Li Na donates blood freely for Profane Iron, temporarily loses five levels, keeps the ability, and recovers over four days. Same mechanic, opposite ethics, radically different bill.

docs.title: Use
docs.text:
• Chapter 15 — chained with Gloom Wraith Phase: "I activated Walk on Air and rushed upward, like I was running up a set of stairs"
  • Chapter 68 — repeated jumps across a gap, which is where its limitations are spelled out
  • Chapter 71 — after the mass bomb drop on Larracos, it is not enough: "my Walk on Air didn't have enough juice to get me to the edge of Shanty Town. I rushed forward through the air, making it about ¾'s of the way before I dropped like a bucket of concrete." He finishes the trip with Climb

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: No level is ever given for Carl's copy. The toe ring's Physical Balance would grant it at level 5 if he did not already have it, which suggests level 5 is a baseline rather than a ceiling, but nothing confirms what level Carl's stolen version sits at.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Enchanted Toe Ring of the Well-Balanced — how he found out
  • The Toraline Ink Tattoo System — the mechanic this case proved
  • The Eye of the Bedlam Bride — the night it happened
  • Profane Iron — the consensual counterpart

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride and Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Wholesale Discount
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • User: Princess Donut
  • Type: Natural benefit, selected when her Charisma topped 200 (chapter 77)
  • Effect: Everything at cost at the store
  • That is the entire documented effect

This page is short because the text is

No system description block exists, and the book gives exactly two lines about this benefit. Both are quoted in full below. Nothing else is stated about what it does, whether it applies to all merchants or only the Desperado Club store, or whether it stacks with other discounts. Do not fill in the gaps.

docs.title: The Two Lines
docs.text:
The trigger threshold:

I ALSO HAVE ONE TO PICK FOR MY CHARISMA TOPPING 200. I'M GOING TO PICK ONE CALLED WHOLESALE DISCOUNT.

The effect:

Donut: PLUS I GET EVERYTHING AT COST AT THE STORE. IT'S FANTASTIC!

docs.title: The Threshold, and What It Implies
docs.text:
This is the useful structural detail. Wholesale Discount unlocks at Charisma topping 200, while Monologue is described as one of the benefits crawlers receive "when their boosted stats topped 300."

So the natural-benefit system has tiers at 100, 200 and 300, with a fresh selection offered at each:

Threshold Donut's pick Charisma 100 Love Vampire (Book 3) Charisma 200 Wholesale Discount Charisma 300 Monologue Strength 100 Muscle Mommy Intelligence 100 Brain Trust

Donut, alone among the party, is high enough in a single stat to be collecting the 300-tier benefits.

docs.title: Value
docs.text: Donut gets it in chapter 77, with ten chapters of the book remaining, most of them spent in an active war rather than shopping. It never visibly changes anything on-page. Its real value is presumably banked for later floors, where the party's spending runs into the millions of gold.

docs.title: Wrecking Ball
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • User: Rend, Carl's Tummy Acher pet
  • Type: Innate species special ability. "The only skill he had"
  • Effect: Increases the user's mass and speed during a charge
  • Species reputation: "considered a terror on any battlefield"
  • Pairs with: The Enchanted Tooth Cap of Hi-Yo Silver, which supplies the speed for free
  • Kill: Gustavo 3, the second of Lucia Mar's two rottweilers

Exact-verification note

No system description block exists. The species entry and the one narrated use below are the whole of it.

docs.title: The Species Entry
docs.text:
Foreshadowed in chapter 5, in Rend's species description:

Tummy Achers, also known as Belly Achers, also known as Colon Worms, are named such because they were originally parasites, living in the intestinal tracts of Jotan-class Titans. They are generally good-natured, though infants can be a little... difficult to control. They are voracious eaters, and when they reach full size can swallow just about anything. They have multiple tank-based special abilities and are generally resistant to most types of damage. They can survive in almost any environment. In addition, while not necessarily known for their offensive skills, their Wrecking Ball attack is considered a terror on any battlefield.

That is the shape of the creature: a resilient, good-natured, indestructible eating machine with exactly one offensive option, and the one option is extremely good.

docs.title: The Combination
docs.text:
Wrecking Ball scales with mass and speed, which means its output is limited by how fast the pet can get moving before it arrives. The Enchanted Tooth Cap of Hi-Yo Silver solves that: it yanks Rend toward Carl's position from up to five kilometres away, "inexorably… at great speed," smashing through any wall in the way.

Carl notes the synergy when Rend receives the cap in chapter 65: "for Rend, it would work well, especially when combined with his new Wrecking Ball special ability."

The targeting method is the clever part. The tooth cap always summons the pet to the owner. So to fire Rend at something, Carl puts himself on the far side of it.

docs.title: The Kill — Chapter 72
docs.text:
Carl is being blown off his feet by gale magic, at close range, with Lucia Mar's second rottweiler on him:

"Wrecking Ball!" I wheezed as I cast Hi-Yo Silver a second time. Another gale hit me, and I spun head over heels landing on my stomach.

I watched, as if in slow motion, as Rend started rolling toward me. And as he was magically pulled in my direction, he activated the only skill he had. Wrecking Ball. The special attack increased his mass and speed, and it did exactly what the name implied. The back half of Gustavo 3, the second of Lucia Mar's two rottweilers, terror of the dungeon, exploded in a red mist as Rend rushed right up to me, stopping inches from my face.

Rend stops inches from Carl's face. The dog does not.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: No level. The two stated variables are mass and speed, both increased by the ability on activation and the second of which can be supplied externally by the tooth cap.

docs.text:

  • Rush (and Crowd Blast) — Katia's equivalent momentum charge
  • Smush — Carl's own mass-based finisher

docs.title: Bosses
docs.text:
The dungeon's boss system has a strict tier ladder — Mordecai lists it as Neighborhood, Borough, City, Province, Country, and Floor bosses, plus a separate, rarer category called Elites. Neighborhood bosses are the most common and guard a single room; each tier up scales in danger, group size required, and reward quality (a Bronze Boss Box for Neighborhood, Silver for Borough, and so on). Killing a boss earns a permanent star next to a crawler's name.

Full pages exist for every boss defeated by Carl and Donut — including ones like the Goblin War Chieftain, killed remotely without ever entering the boss room or triggering an official boss-card sequence. The one exception is Ringmaster Grimaldi, a City Boss + Elite resolved through negotiation rather than a kill — given a full page anyway because of how central the confrontation is to Book 2's main quest. Bosses only seen secondhand (via other crawlers, on broadcast) are listed in the table below.

Two floors break the ladder entirely. Floor 8 runs on T'Ghee card combat, where bosses are flagged rather than killed. Floor 9 has no ladder at all — Faction Wars replaces it with enemy warlords and with gods, and neither category can be killed the usual way.

docs.text: Listed by floor, in the order Carl and Donut actually encounter them.

docs.title: Floor 8 (Book 6)
docs.text:
Floor 8 runs on T'Ghee card combat, which changes what "boss" means. Several of the floor's bosses are never killed at all — they are flagged into totem cards, negotiated with, or (in the case of the deities) simply invulnerable. Full pages are given anyway, per the same exception that covers Ringmaster Grimaldi and Big Tina.

City bosses and demons

  • Asojano, Lord of Smallpox — Level 130 City Boss, a non-corporeal Orisha spirit; not killed — flagged into a T'Ghee card by Carl at the last second
  • Shi Maria / The Bedlam Bride — Level 140 City Boss, Reaper Spider Minion and demi-god; the title boss of the book. Flagged by mutual agreement, then rips herself free by tattooing into Carl's chest
  • Madre de Aguas — Level 125 City Boss; charmed by Sister Ines, then killed by her own zombism curse. Her corpse becomes Amayon's shell
  • The Reminiscence Hydra of Malicious Compliance — Level 125 City Boss, nine heads built from Carl's and Donut's dead; the first boss in dungeon history created by the System AI with no input parameters at all
  • Minge — Level 225 Minor Feral Demon, Slit's sister; released from the Nothing through a rigged knife game and killed by the Desperado Club's vorpals
  • Amayon — Level 250 Demon Prince of Sheol; not killed (invulnerable). Freed, buffed to full power and sent home — the event that scours the world and saves the stranded crawlers

Deities

  • Ogun — Level 250 God of Blacksmithery and Armor, unsponsored; never fought, appears in person to smite Paz Lo and kill Anton Lopez
  • Yemaya — Level 250 Goddess of Rivers, a previously locked deity; re-ascended by Carl's shrine choice
  • Eileithyia — Level 250 Goddess of Childbirth and Female Pain, sponsored by Huanxin Jinx; grants a floor boon and the "Spiders" cover quest
  • Ysalte, the Vinegar Bitch — Level 250 Goddess of Hopelessness and Insanity; killed by her own summoned totem, Paz Lo

Deckmasters

  • The Visitor — Level 70 Nightgaunt, deckmaster 7 of 10; killed by Jola the Yule Cat after Carl's nightgaunt cloak enraged it past using its own deck
  • Tom — Level 75, "Bereft Shaman of Meleagris Gallopavo Rex," deckmaster 8 of 10
  • Sharp-Elbows — Level 80 ogre necromancer witch, deckmaster 9 of 10; killed by Raul the crab
  • Robert the Human — Level 40; Donut's solo card-combat tutorial fight in the Florida Keys, ended instantly by Mongo

Mock battle arena

  • Der Schachmeister — Level 25 boy deckmaster; a pure lockdown deck, and Carl and Donut's only practice loss in the book
  • Rude-Dolph the Blood-Nosed Slay-Deer — Level 100 Puppet-Master; intangible until all eight reindeer puppets are dead

docs.title: Floor 9 (Book 7)
docs.text:
Floor 9 has no boss ladder at all. Faction Wars is a war, not a dungeon crawl: there are no Neighborhood/Borough/City tiers, no boss boxes and no stars. What fills the role is two entirely separate things —

  • the warlords of the nine other Faction Wars teams, each of whom has to be eliminated for the Princess Posse to win, and
  • the gods, level 250 and invulnerable, who get onto the battlefield through a series of loopholes and then cannot be removed by force.

The gods are the only Floor 9 entities that get full pages here, because the warlords are people and belong on Characters.

Deities

  • Khepri — Level 250 God of Rebirth and the Sunrise, with a literal bug for a head. Secretly worshipped by Princess Vinata and summoned into his own temple as a trap; the one real boss-battle sequence of the floor (ch. 53). Not killed — banished by Hellik
  • Hellik — Level 250, brother of Emberus. Appears in person, banishes Khepri, and delivers the book's densest lore dump; names Carl a "friend of the church" despite Carl's standing quest to kill him
  • Meatus — a feral god freed from the Nothing; a sapient stolen penis with a gremlin attached. Killed outright by Donut's War Crime
  • Harpocrates — Level 250 God of Silence, and the owner of the stolen half of Meatus. Conscripted with a hell-kissed level-18 potion and used as a weapon by Li Na; beats Yarilo to death before leaving the realm enraged
  • Yarilo — Level 250 feral god of lust, also freed from the Nothing; conscripted by the War Mage Rebellion and then killed by Harpocrates
  • Eris — Level 250 Goddess of Chaos. Loses her pilot mid-book and runs unsponsored; casts the once-ever Ceremony of Chaos, freezing and piling ~80,000 combatants for Donut's Rolling Battle Formation. A prime contender for the vacant Ascendent Throne
  • Eileithyia — Level 250 Goddess of Childbirth, returning from Floor 8. Loses her vessel Huanxin Jinx when Donut kills her, then grants Katia's boon (ch. 86)
  • Emberus — Level 250, Carl's own god. Arrives at the end of the book and destroys the entire floor on a 66-minute timer

The looming threat

  • Scolopendra — never appears on the page. Warned as "stirring" twice, then "has awakened" in the book's final lines. Not a stat block; a flag for future books — she finally appears in person, and gets a full stat block, in Book 8 (see below)
