docs.text:
Nine enemy teams plus the mid-season "non-team entity," all eliminated. (The Bone Clan / Skull Empire gets two rows: its war chief and its warlord die separately.) Warlords who also have character pages are covered in full there; this table records the combat outcome only.

Warlord Team Outcome Kill credit Commander Stockade Democratic (Lemig) Sortion His own plot backfires: he uses a level-15 Summon Ally on an unconscious Carl to pull Shi Maria into his own court, and she massacres his people instead. Stockade smashes his own brains out against the floor during the adjudication "Ruled as a psychosis-induced suicide." Defeat ruled voluntary, so all Lemig Sortion assets went to the Madness Empress D'Nadia Prism Kingdom Marked with the Ring of Divine Suffering, stripped of shields by Donut's clockwork Mongos, killed by Mongo — see Princess D'Nadia Pet Mongo of the Princess Posse Hortense Leadership Unit Operatic Collective Killed when Weeper Commander Volteeg deliberately removed his tank's fire-control chamber and detonated it in the centre of the Bloc force, killing over 10,000 of his own side at once "Ruled as either accidental or a fragging incident, which would be funny as shit. Investigation is pending" Princess Vinata, the Sepsis Whore Blood Sultanate Hunted down in the Temple of Khepri on Operation: Snake Pit; killed with a hatchet between the eyes the instant her Khepri-granted immortality expired Sluggalette Kandy "Bigs" Newton of the Princess Posse King Rust (war chief) Bone Clan / Skull Empire Decapitated by Rosetta Thagra at the parley, mid-handshake, with a lasso and a blade — a centuries-old personal debt, and cover for a bank heist run off his hand and retina Rosetta (not system-credited as a warlord kill — Rust was war chief, not warlord) King Stalwart (warlord) Bone Clan / Skull Empire Torn apart by his own conscripted war mages, who broke their Conscription with a combination of Pull spells. This is the act that creates the War Mage Rebellion "Three members of the War Mage Rebellion." Assets went to Team Retribution Architect Houston The Madness Killed by Carl in the burning Madness castle; Carl escapes the room with Gloom Wraith Phase and never fully sees what happened. Li Jun dies in the same sequence Warlord Carl of the Princess Posse Warlord Fang The Reavers Hid inside his own dragon, Calliope. Died when the Reaver castle's stockpile of mini tactical nukes cooked off after Carl detonated a No Disassemble dropped by a wraith-possessed Louis Santiago 51% Carl, 1% Louis, 40% Juice Box — "the rest is going to the now-deceased Fang for hiding in the worst possible place, which was inside the dragon" Epitome Tagg The Dream Secretly grafted into Louis Santiago's chest as a replacement heart and lungs. Removed by transplant surgery on a tent table; Mongo ate the discarded organs Pet Mongo — "I almost called it a suicide... Consider it a present for the baby shower" Akuma (+ Agatha, unwanted co-warlord) War Mage Rebellion Akuma voluntarily leaves the realm once he has what he came for. Agatha had already been stripped of her warlord slot for abandoning her post, and escapes to Floor 10 "The War Mage rebellion has been defeated. They have no assets to award" Juice Box & Ferdinand Team Retribution (the NPC team) Both leave the realm in the second casting of Zerzura, which lifts the entire city of Larracos to the twelfth floor. Abandoning their posts is the Princess Posse's actual win condition "They have abandoned their posts and have forfeited their position." → The Princess Posse has won Faction Wars

See The Faction Wars Teams for the teams themselves.

See Yemaya Adrasteia Khepri's patron after Khnum's death Named in Khepri's boss description as having "an outside shot" at the Ascendent throne Khnum Khepri's former patron Dead before the book starts — "mysteriously dropped dead a few days back," one of a string of deaths in that sub-pantheon that Carl reads as a twelfth-floor purge Mazu — Historical only: in a previous season the Viceroy team summoned her and she razed the ring of buildings outside Larracos, burying the Club Vanquisher entrance temple and stranding Vinata Resheph — Off-page: the teleported city of Larracos lands on a convent of his nuns, and he is reportedly losing his mind about it Inpewt Source of the Children of Inpewt revenant curse Off-page; Eileithyia reports that Odette "has already taken out Inpewt" and taken control of his zombies Taranis Worshipped by the Basilica Guards Never appears in Book 7. Not in Book 7

Dodola is a Book 6 deity (a storm goddess, sponsored by Huanxin Jinx). She is not mentioned anywhere in Book 7 and has been left out of the table above rather than invented into it.

docs.title: Floor 10-11 (Book 8)
docs.text:
Floor 10 ("Don't Come in Last") is a vehicle-racing gauntlet; Floor 11 ("A Parade of Horribles") is a single-arena finale. Between them they resolve or introduce most of the book's major deity and dungeon-boss threads.

  • Scolopendra — Level 500 Dungeon Boss, the first-ever-named tier above Floor Boss. Summoned by Carl at the Floor 11 arena as the crawlers' joint choice; neither killed nor abandoned, but transformed by an enriched pet biscuit into a sapient Level 1 party member
  • Krakaren Prime — Level 235 Floor Boss; a real, individual entity previously only referenced (see Krakaren Clone for the Book 1 copy fought instead). Added to the arena unilaterally by the AI, not requested by Carl; left badly wounded and carried away by Taranis
  • Taranis — Deity, God of Lightning; previously named but unseen since Book 5. Appears in person for the first time, kills his own brother Emberus, and departs with Krakaren Prime and a stowaway Samantha
  • Mitch — Level 120 Adolescent Shadow Mimic posing as the Desperado Club's new croupier; frozen by Carl (transformed into a dog) opening the Eye of the Bedlam Bride, then killed by Donut
  • Emberus — killed by his own brother Taranis after Carl publicly renounces his faith and confesses to Geyrun's murder; permanence unconfirmed
  • Eris — gives Carl a five-sided fate coin, takes a new monstrous physical form at the climax, and confirms the goddess Apito survives in scattered pieces
  • Khepri — brief reappearance as a decoy accusation, dismissed by Taranis

Grull — a gap, not an omission

Grull, the war god of the Mantaurs, reappears substantially in Book 8: ejected from his own body (which conceals an orc host called "the Maestro") by Princess Donut's Laundry Day spell during Floor 10's fifth heat, then driven off — not killed, since gods cannot die on Floor 10 specifically — by Dong Quixote and Corcunda's suicidal, magnet-boosted lance charge. No grull.md page exists yet despite Grull being referenced since Book 1 (worshipped by the Mantaurs; see Gore-Gore the Mantaur). This is a gap for a future pass, not a deliberate exclusion — his Book 8 scene is summarized in the table below in the meantime.

docs.title: Amayon
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Tier: Demon Prince of Sheol — one of the four crown princes
  • Level: 250
  • Floor: 8 ("The Ghosts of Earth"), Havana, Cuba
  • Resolution: Not killed — invulnerable on this floor. Freed from the Madre de Aguas snake corpse, buffed to full power by Katia and Carl, and sent home to Sheol (ch. 69–70)
  • Consequence: His departure spell scours the entire world and gives every stranded crawler a path to Floor 9
  • Personal: Youngest of the four princes; expelled by one of his three brothers; Ysalte's former lover and the father of her child

docs.title: Arrival
docs.text:
Amayon does not choose to come. He "involuntarily slip[s] into the realm" through the vulnerability created when the Madre de Aguas dies of her zombism curse during an active Demon Eviction event, and lands in her risen snake corpse.

Samantha recognises the name immediately: one of the four crown princes of Sheol, "the youngest one I think," fond of setting things on fire — "Kinda like Emberus, actually. They don't like each other."

For most of the floor's endgame he sits atop the tallest building in Havana, ramrod straight, pouring fire into the sky in a tornado of demon birds and bats, held in the snake shell and under the control of Sister Ines Quiteria.

docs.title: The Quest: The Missing Piece
docs.text:
Quest description (Book 6, ch. 62)

"Amayon, one of the four princes of Sheol has been betrayed by one of his brothers. After being unceremoniously expelled from the kingdom of Sheol, the demon prince has managed to just barely hold on long enough to pull himself onto the equivalent of a very, very small ledge. The level 250 demon lord now inhabits the body of a lesser deity, a once-worshiped sea serpent who went by the name of the Madre de Aguas. In order to return home, Amayon simply must cast a spell. But nobody, not even a prince, rides the river for free. A tithe of souls is required to pass back downward."

The quest offers three options: kill Sister Ines to break his tether, free Amayon from his shell, or kill him. Carl's party takes option two — with the AI's dry note attached: "We've never had a full-powered, untethered hell prince unleashed on a lower floor before. I'm sure it'll be fine."

docs.title: The Card Battle: "The Big O"
docs.text:
Killing Sister Ines does not free him. Her death instead summons her sponsor-goddess Ysalte, the Vinegar Bitch, who seizes Amayon directly, intending to take him to the Ascendency as her retainer — which would strand every remaining crawler without a key.

The result is a five-squad hybrid world quest, fought as a card battle on two fronts at once:

  • Offense against Amayon — kill his six totems as fast as possible, which lets the crawlers talk to him
  • Defense against Ysalte — she cannot be killed, so the squads must keep her deck from running dry for ten minutes; the moment she runs out of cards she can "nuke us from orbit"

The mechanic behind his power-up is a piece of the AI's own bureaucratic malice. The Demon Eviction event only fired because the AI decided to classify crab sperm as mobs; the same ruling means the soul tithe for Amayon's spell can be paid the same way. Carl summons Raul the crab and, in the book's own phrasing, "jerked off a crab" to flood the world with souls, while Carl's Martyr's Path floor benefit bathes the demon in Sheol fire to buff his strength.

Ysalte is killed by Paz Lo with two seconds left on the timer. Amayon casts. Powered by "the flash presence of billions of souls," the spell's area expands from the point of origin to cover the entire world — which is what saves the thousands of crawlers stranded across every other region.

docs.title: The Geyrun Answer
docs.text:
While the Why are you Hitting Yourself? spell is still running on him, Carl cashes in the quest update Emberus attached to Amayon's arrival:

Amayon, Book 6, ch. 69

"That's what he sent you to ask? To ask about his son? You tell him that I know exactly what happened to his child. I was witness to the deal being signed. If he assists in helping me kill my three brothers, I will tell him."

This is the biggest movement on Carl's standing Emberus quest to find Geyrun's murderer (see Carl) since it was issued on Floor 5 — a named witness, with a price.

Amayon then dismisses any debt between them: "You also helped slay Ysalte, the mother of my child, so we are even, and I owe you nothing, mortal. The act of speaking to you already delivered the message to Emberus. Soon, this entire world will be scoured." He tips Carl and Samantha off his hand toward the fire and goes home to wage war on his brother.

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: Asojano, Lord of Smallpox
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Boss tier: City Boss
  • Level: 130
  • Floor: 8 ("The Ghosts of Earth"), the Colón Cemetery ghommid settlement outside Havana, Cuba
  • Full title: "Asojano – Orisha"; also known as the Lord of Smallpox
  • Type: Non-corporeal spirit — a faded god reduced to a ghommid
  • Resolution: Not killed. Carl flagged him into a T'Ghee totem card at the instant his health started to blink (ch. 15)
  • Later fate as a card: Combined with Uzi Jesus into Lazarus-A-Bang-Bang; when that fused card later died it reverted, returning him as Lord of Blight – Gold Edition

docs.title: A God Who Outlived His Worshippers
docs.text:
Asojano's own monster description lays out the mechanism that drives most of Floor 8's Orisha storyline:

Monster description (Book 6, ch. 11)

"Also known as the Lord of Smallpox, Asojano is one of the most respected and feared of the Orishas, a former god made flesh upon the rise of the Ascendency. As the worshippers of these gods grew more and more extinct, their temples crumbled, and the power of these former deities waned. Eventually, they faded into nothing, slipping away beyond the veil, becoming nothing more than any other ghommid, only able to visit the physical world on occasion. One day, not so long ago, Asojano found himself here in this small town, visiting the world he once helped rule. There was no malice to his actions. He came just so he could look upon what he once had and what he had lost. Still, power lingers, even in the most forgotten of shells. Asojano is disease incarnate. He kills, and he heals. He is life, and he is death. He also wears a reed hat that makes it difficult to see where he's going, so he bumps into stuff a lot."

He burned the last remaining power of his shrine to enter the cemetery town and is now unable to leave. His mere presence is what corrupted the settlement: per the Pueblo de los Olvidados quest text, "The vile power of his presence has altered the minds of the town's residents, turning them mad. Remove him to free the town." A health bar appears over him on sight and drains on its own, with nobody attacking — being cut off from the other ghommids drains him further still.

docs.title: The Shrine Choice
docs.text:
The boss encounter is not a straight fight. Inside La Iglesia de los Olvidados, five broken Orisha shrines stand around a floating gem called the Sun of Reawakening, and the party may repair exactly one. Repairing Asojano's shrine wins the quest outright and cures the ghommids; refusing turns it into a City Boss battle. The other claimants each make their own pitch — Oshun's raw charm aura, Papa Legba's bribery, the mute Inle, and Ogun, whose two worshippers (Paz Lo and Anton Lopez, of Sister Ines Quiteria's squad) are threatened with a smite if any other shrine is chosen.

Carl instead chooses Yemaya's shrine, on the strength of a message from Katia — a decision that re-ascends a locked goddess (see Yemaya) and gets Ogun's two worshippers smited in person (see Ogun).

docs.title: The Fight and the Flag
docs.text:
Asojano screams "Betrayal!" and breaks the temple's protection, letting the ghommid horde surge the building. Princess Donut does most of the damage with a swarm of ghost-possessed armor and daggers, backed by Clockwork Triplicate on Mongo and a Mute spell that lands just as he tries to re-cast. His shield burns down, and his health continues to drain on its own once Carl chocks the door shut and severs him from the other ghommids.

With his health blinking, Carl gives up the boss boxes entirely: he sprints across the room, drives a flag into the top of the orisha's head, and turns him into a card. Underneath the grass skirts is "nothing more than a pale, albino man, wide-eyed and afraid," half his face covered in boils. Carl immediately catches SlugPox for the trouble — an escalating affliction that pops Pox Slug mobs out of his skin (see Mobs).

docs.title: As a Card
docs.text:
Asojano ends up one of the party's six starting totems, alongside Geraldo the monk seal, Skylar Spinach, Uzi Jesus, Raul the crab, and Shi Maria. He is also one of the two worst behaved. Carl's assessment is blunt — "As expected, Asojano was a complete dick" — his first act in the mock battle arena being an attempt to debuff Donut, blocked only by arena safeties.

Donut eventually uses a Combo card to fuse Asojano (level 130, undead, seven utility slots) with Uzi Jesus (level 140, given to the party by Florin) into the level-140 unique card Lazarus-A-Bang-Bang — a bazooka-wielding, boil-covered figure in a crown of thorns introduced by the AI as "the calamitous, rapturous, and ultimately hazardous master of the life-death boomerang." Lazarus is better behaved than either parent card and is later combined again, this time with the splitter ghommid Skylar Spinach.

That second combination has a consequence. When Lazarus is killed during the Desperado Club fight against Quan, he reverts to the two cards he was built from — and because Skylar is a splitter whose iterations get stronger, both halves come back upgraded: Uzi Jesus – Gold Edition and Lord of Blight – Gold Edition, Asojano in woven gold with a sugar-skull staff.

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: Ball of Swine
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Boss tier: Borough Boss
  • Level: 15
  • Also known as: The Porkchop Express
  • Floor: 1 — guards Floor 1's only known stairwell down to Floor 2 (not a Floor 2→3 stairwell)
  • Killed by: Carl, Donut, and the "Team Meadow Lark" elderly-evacuee group, plus Agatha (mixed party, 7 crawlers)
  • Reward: Silver Boss Box each; multiple group-fight achievements ("Killing a borough boss with a mixed group," "...with more than 10 minions," "...in under 10 minutes")

AI Commentary (in-voice, written for this wiki — not a book excerpt)

"Thirty-plus tuskling aristocrats, a night of orgiastic battle-rage, and one giant rolling ball of pork violence — welcome to the single horniest, deadliest dance number this season has produced. Six crawlers, zero shoes between the humans, and somehow still the classiest thing on this channel tonight."

docs.title: B... B... B... Boss Battle
docs.text:
Per the in-universe boss-battle card:

"Also known as the Porkchop Express, the Ball of Swine is one of the rarest, most deadly battle formations of the Tuskling. Encompassing at least 30 Tuskling knights and their lady loves, a Ball formation requires a specific set of circumstances to create... The Tusklings, the ruling class of the Orcish Supremacy, shape into an inseparable sphere that rolls onto the countryside. The ball of pork won't stop its night of terror until it has crushed the poor, the weak, and the lesser citizens under its unstoppable weight."

docs.title: Encounter
docs.text:
Carl and Donut find this boss's lair — a circular "spiral maze" reached after a full day of chopper scouting down a highway corridor — while searching for a way off Floor 1 entirely; the map marks the location itself as "Stairwell to Floor Two." Graffiti at the entrance warns "DO NOT go deeper into the spiral or you will activate the borough boss." Mordecai's advice is to skip it and find an unguarded stairwell elsewhere, but Carl, having found only this one exit after a full day of searching, decides they can't risk not finding another and chooses to fight it head-on alongside Brandon An's group.

The fight takes place in a fortified position built from scavenged furniture and a ninja-star-covered tabletop trap. The Ball itself disassembles into dozens of individual Tuskling combatants (Knights, Courtesans, and at least one "Tuskling Dominatrix") once engaged — Donut fights primarily with Magic Missile, Carl with improvised melee and his fists, and Brandon's group with a sword and a hammer. Everyone in the mixed party survives the fight itself.

With the boss dead, the red forcefield around the stairwell drops. Carl and Donut descend immediately afterward, arriving on Floor 2 within minutes (confirmed when producer Lexis congratulates them shortly after on "making it down to the second floor"). The broader Meadow Lark evacuation continues onto Floor 2 as well, and costs the group a member there (see Carl for the Rage Elemental aftermath).

Sourced from Book 1: The Apocalypse Will Be Televised.

docs.title: Big Tina
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Boss tier: City Boss
  • Level: 80
  • Floor: 6 ("The Hunting Grounds"), roaming the river towns near Point Mongo
  • Full title: none given — a mutated Allosaurus, "Immortalized"
  • Resolution: Not killed. Pacified via a staged dance recital (the "The Recital" quest) and reunited with her mother mid-battle at the Butcher's Masquerade
  • Mother: Kiwi, Mongoliensis Pack Leader, later briefly restored to her original Ursine form and tamed as a minion of Princess Donut

AI Commentary (in-voice, written for this wiki — not a book excerpt)

"When Big Things happen on such a large scale, it's easy to forget sometimes that these Big Things are also happening to the little things in the world, too. Tina's time as an allosaurus — and briefly, as an undead-in-training vampiric monstrosity — has been an education that not many receive. She barely remembers who she used to be. She does, however, remember the horror and loss she felt when she realized everything she'd been working for wasn't going to happen. That spark of helpless, impotent rage has done nothing but grow over the past few centuries. That rage ain't so impotent anymore."

docs.title: A Recital, Interrupted
docs.text:
Long before Scolopendra's nine-tier attack, Tina was an eight-year-old Ursine girl — daughter of a Floor 6 village's head cleric — training in secret for a forbidden dance recital, since her father's strict, dancing-and-singing-banned religious order considered ballet sinful. On the night of the performance, her father and a group of fellow clerics stormed the recital just as Tina was about to take the stage, whipping her mother nearly to death in front of the audience and shoving Tina aside hard enough to break the magic sparkle-wand she'd been given for the show. Before the clerics could punish the rest of the children involved, Scolopendra's attack struck the whole world at once, transmuting nearly every female Ursine (including Tina and her mother, Kiwi) into dinosaurs. Tina's mind never recovered from the trauma; she became Big Tina, an enormous, deranged, permanently-enraged Allosaurus who spends her unnaturally long life (per her monster card, she's the "Immortalized" only child ever turned this way) hunting and slaughtering Ursine wherever she finds them.

Kiwi and the surviving mothers from that night — now the pack of ordinary Mongoliensis raptors led by Kiwi herself — have spent centuries quietly following Tina around, trying and mostly failing to contain her rampages.

docs.title: "The Recital" Quest
docs.text:
Carl and Donut first learn Tina's identity from Prudence, a captured Ursine barmaid, after Tina's attacks escalate into full village massacres feeding a separate, unrelated crisis (see The Creeping Apocalypse). The system's own quest text is blunt about the intended solution: "Kill her. Or give her what she wants." Donut correctly identifies the reference (Footloose, not Rambo, in her words) — Tina doesn't want to be killed, she wants to finish the recital her father interrupted, and she wants her mother back, whom her ruined mind no longer recognizes even though Kiwi has never once left her side.

Complicating things further, a vampire-hunter elite's Floor 6 storyline (see Sierra) briefly infects Tina with vampirism after Miriam Dom fights her; Tina is cured along with every other victim the moment Miriam sacrifices herself, but the rampage and the reanimated-body-part crisis it kicks off is already underway by then.

docs.title: The Performance
docs.text:
Donut books Tina — under a false pretense that it's just a dinosaur act — into the pet/talent double bill at the Butcher's Masquerade, using a recharge scroll to restore the last charge in Tina's original sparkle wand. On stage, the wand casts a genuine charm spell, The Recital, layering real, uncomplicated joy over everyone watching as Tina finally performs her interrupted "Water Ballad" alongside a chorus line of thirty-plus raptors and Mongo, all in hand-sewn sea-creature costumes.

Mid-battle during the Masquerade's climactic ambush, Donut has Kiwi swallow a smuggled dose of the I Take it All Back potion (a benefactor-box item explicitly labeled "Give this to Princess Donut... Do NOT give to Tina"), which strips Scolopendra's Transmutation curse — turning Kiwi back into a very pregnant Ursine woman on the spot. Tina, still in dinosaur form, sees the transformation and finally recognizes her mother, roaring the word "Mommy" for the first time in centuries. Quest Complete: The Recital. Tina herself is never cured or killed — she remains an Allosaurus, last seen transported away with the rest of the Butcher's Masquerade battlefield when the ruined High Elf castle teleports to Floor 9.

Sourced from Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade.

docs.title: Claude Sludgington the Fourth
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Boss tier: Borough Boss
  • Level: 65
  • Floor: 6 ("The Hunting Grounds"), throne room of Fort Freedom
  • Full title: Eryops Gigantis, a.k.a. "The River Squatter" or "The Mud Kato"
  • Killed by: Carl (accidental Protective Shell launch + a bare-fisted dive through its exposed stomach), Donut (Fireball), and Mongo (finishing the job from the inside out)
  • Loot: A neighborhood field guide showing safe/naiad-occupied river crossings

AI Commentary (in-voice, written for this wiki — not a book excerpt)

"Oh boy are you in for a treat. These bottom-dwelling, lightning-tossing water pigs will ruin just about anyone's day. It's pretty much what they live for. Also known as the River Squatter or the Mud Kato, one of the cardinal rules of living under the water in a river is that you never, ever invite an Eryops into your home. Why? Because they never goddamn leave."

docs.title: The Uninvited Guest
docs.text:
Claude is an eight-foot-tall, fifteen-foot-long, tailless amphibian — half frog, half squished alligator — who crashed a fundraising gala the cash-strapped Naiad Confederacy threw years earlier to cover the upkeep on their crumbling river palace. The party charged a 50-gold cover; almost nobody showed, because the starving regular naiad citizenry ate anyone who got too close to the water. Claude walked in anyway at the last minute, and the guards let him through despite his reputation. He never left, eventually squatting in the throne room itself and displacing whatever government remained.

Eryops receive a 10x constitution bonus while rooted in place and can fire branching lightning bolts from their eyes; per the AI, they're "notoriously difficult to kill. Or even move." As a lizard-class mob, Claude also deals 20% bonus damage against Carl thanks to his Extinction Sigil.

docs.title: The Fight
docs.text:
Claude isn't fought on purpose — he's discovered mid-battle, teleported directly on top of Carl during Tsarina Signet's assault on Fort Freedom, after Samantha gets herself swallowed by him while scouting the flooded throne room instead of teleporting back as ordered. The impact scatters the nearby fight (Donut, Mongo, and the elite Areson the Wise) and vomits up an unconscious Holger the were-castor along with Samantha, both still alive inside the frog's gut.

The monster-card hint — "rooted in place... difficult to kill or even move" — points straight at the solution: expose the stomach. Carl casts Protective Shell too close and at too shallow an angle, accidentally launching Claude straight up into the night sky instead of flipping him sideways. As the boss falls back to earth, Donut lands a level-10 Fireball directly into his exposed belly, catching him fully alight and knocking him into the treeline, where he gets stuck face-down, legs waving, unable to fall either way before the shell's duration runs out.

With seconds left, Carl throws his weakest hob-lobber into the open wound while Donut finishes with magic missiles. Mongo dives headfirst into the wound and eats his way straight through the creature — dragging Carl in behind him when the trees finally give way and launch the boss backward like a spring-loaded mousetrap. Carl is briefly trapped and crushed inside the still-dying Eryops before Mongo claws his way out the other side, pulling Carl with him. The whole fight lasts roughly thirty seconds.

docs.title: Aftermath
docs.text:
• Carl receives the "Uprooted" achievement — for making a Rooted-in-Place boss monster move, with an unusually sincere, non-sarcastic wording that stands out from the AI's normal voice
  • The fight ends up being a genuine surprise "boss kill before the actual quest trigger," earning the "Premature Questjaculation" achievement (no reward) since Signet's team hadn't yet fully cleared the castle when it happened
  • Confirms Fort Freedom as liberated shortly after, completing Part One of the Vengeance of the Daughter quest

Sourced from Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade.

docs.title: Denise the Feral Goose Mother
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Boss tier: Borough Boss
  • Level: 53
  • Floor: 5 ("The Bubbles"), bubble #543, Air Quadrant — inside Commandant Kane's floating house/"castle"
  • Format: A timed knockout fight with both No Magic and No Physical Damage rules in effect
  • Killed by: Carl and Donut — shoved head-first into a kitchen garbage disposal
  • Killed: Commandant Kane, moments before the fight begins

AI Commentary (in-voice, written for this wiki — not a book excerpt)

"The house is falling. The clock is running. Your magic doesn't work, your fists don't work, and the only working appliance in the building just ate the last person who tried to reason with a goose. Ladies and gentlemen, tonight's main event: a washed-up dungeon anarchist versus a homicidal waterfowl, refereed by a kitchen sink. Place your bets!"

docs.title: An Ordinary-Looking Pet
docs.text:
Commandant Kane originally acquired Denise as a replacement pet for his daughter Bonnie after her original pig, Sausage, was taken hostage by the Bactrians. Denise looks like an unremarkable white goose in a frilly bonnet and shawl — until her card reveals she was "plucked directly from the seventh floor" when Emperor Anser first brought his people to this world through a gate, and that she lingered too long in the Nothing on the way, driving her mad and granting her an environmental damage type: she is immune to both magic and ordinary physical attacks, but vulnerable to blunt trauma from objects already present in the room (furniture, dishware, the sink) rather than any weapon a crawler brings in themselves.

When Carl and Donut arrive to loot Kane's corpse, Denise is out getting food; she returns partway through the encounter, having already killed Kane off-screen for reasons Bonnie — under a grief-numbing potion at the time — can't fully explain.

docs.title: The Fight
docs.text:
The moment Carl accidentally triggers the boss card, the game locks out both offense types at once — no spells, no scrolls, no gauntlet formation, and no benefit from unarmed combat skills. Mongo ignores the warning and engages anyway, taking heavy, near-lethal damage for no effect on Denise's health. Bonnie, oblivious to the danger, keeps trying to get the party to test her lemonade recipe throughout the fight — which turns out to be a deliberate misdirection: the "important-looking" pitcher is just Mountain-Dew-colored lemonade, confirmed by an achievement mocking Carl for assuming it was a quest item (Wild Goose Chase).

The actual clue is environmental: a mug and a serving pitcher both visibly damage Denise's health when thrown, and Bonnie's earlier gesture toward the kitchen sink turns out to be a hint about what really killed her father. With the timer at ten seconds, Carl wrestles Denise's head into the sink drain and has Donut flip the garbage disposal switch, killing her instantly.

docs.title: Aftermath
docs.text:
• The fight ends with the standard "throne room" bubble notification — the Air Quadrant is liberated the moment Denise dies
  • Neither Carl nor Donut gain more than a single level from the kill; Mordecai has no explanation for why boxed experience payouts feel arbitrary
  • Carl and Donut inherit custody of Bonnie, the orphaned gnome child, who is later left in Juice Box's care in Hump Town
  • The house's soul-crystal-powered balloon and the second piece of the Gate of the Feral Gods (a second pocket watch, looted from Kane's corpse) both pass to Carl afterward

Sourced from Book 4: The Gate of the Feral Gods.

docs.title: Der Schachmeister
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Tier: Mock battle arena opponent (deckmaster)
  • Level: 25
  • Floor: 8 ("The Ghosts of Earth"), the mock battle arena
  • Deck: Twenty cards including six totems, with an eight-second summoning cooldown
  • Result: Carl and Donut lose. Their only practice defeat in the book

docs.title: The Kid
docs.text:
A human boy of about twelve in a tuxedo and round glasses, who appears at the top of a hill between two summoned wolves, wipes his nose on his sleeve and flips the party off.

Monster description (Book 6, ch. 29)

"Holds a deck consisting of twenty cards, including six totems. Has an eight-second card summoning cooldown. Focuses on debuffs and disabling the opponent. He's an annoying little prick without any regard for his own personal safety. You'll have to deal with him the same way you would if this were a middle school playground. You gotta kick his ass before he outsmarts you and gets the adults involved."

The eight-second cooldown is the detail that alarms Carl. Donut's own cards take ten seconds to refresh; he had assumed that was a hard rule of the system rather than a stat an opponent could beat.

docs.title: His Totems
docs.text:
• Der Kornwolf (level 100) — a giant ethereal wolf
  • Die Kartoffelwölfin (level 100) — visually identical to the first, different name only

docs.title: How He Wins
docs.text:
Der Schachmeister is a pure lockdown/mystic deck and he never once needs to fight.

  1. Summon lock — a flaming animated padlock over Donut's hand with a 30-second countdown, chaining her cards. She cannot summon Shi Maria or anything else
  2. Peekaboo! — a mystic card that opens a pair of bloodshot eyes over Donut's deck and shows him her hand for the remainder of the battle
  3. To Hell With Ya! — a legendary card that force-discards the Shi Maria card and every other copy of it in hand and deck. Donut only has one, so she loses her best totem outright and cannot summon her again for the rest of the fight

Raul kills Der Kornwolf with a ranged Bris, but the second wolf tackles him and rolls down the hill with him. Samantha nearly saves the fight with a new, unexplained glowing-blue power, but fizzles out mid-charge ("God mother damnit. I used it all up"). The surviving wolf reaches Donut.

Book 6, ch. 29

"Simulation Failed. Congratulations. If this was a real fight, you would all be dead right now."

Donut's verdict: "That guy was a cheater. How are we supposed to win if we can't use our deck?"

docs.title: Why It Matters
docs.text:
The loss is the turning point in the party's card strategy. Carl's conclusion is that their deck is too slow and too dependent on one dominant totem, and that the reliable answer to a mage-type deckmaster is the same as it always was — they can't cast their spells when you're punching them in the face. From here on he and Mongo practise rushing the deckmaster directly rather than trading totems, and the party starts deliberately rebuilding the deck for speed.

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: Eileithyia
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Tier: Deity — Goddess of Childbirth and Female Pain
  • Level: 250
  • Sponsor: Huanxin Jinx of the Grixist Swarm, CEO of Icon Industries
  • Floors: 8 ("The Ghosts of Earth"), the Temple of Yemaya, Colón Cemetery (ch. 17); returns on Floor 9 ("Faction Wars") in Book 7, ch. 86
  • Resolution: Never fought — invulnerable on both floors. She arrives alongside Yemaya to hand out boons and open a quest, and returns a book later to collect on the bargain
  • Presence effect: All damage struck against female opponents is quartered; all female party members strike with 500% melee power — "Girl power, bitches!"

docs.title: Who She Is
docs.text:
Eileithyia is the old friend who never stopped remembering Yemaya, and Yemaya's re-ascension is effectively her win. She is not a Greek goddess despite the borrowed name — she appears as a five-foot, blue-and-black-haired, bipedal alien with six eyes in a V on a bug-like face, four three-fingered arms, a long thin neck and a heavily distended belly, wearing a blood-red toga and a laurel crown. Carl notes she is not wearing soul armor, meaning this is who she really is rather than a sponsor's projection.

Monster description (Book 6, ch. 17)

"Eileithyia is something of an oddity. She's benevolent. Unlike most of these psychos, she's known for her kind heart. She's prayed to by all mothers, both when they're attempting to sow the seeds and when the harvest comes. And while she does many things, she's mostly known as She Who Eases Pain. Both the physical pain of childbirth and the inevitable darkness that comes to those who are unable to complete their most sacred task. When the stillness comes, she is not the one who has caused the heartbreak. But she is the one holding the grieving mother's hand. She's not known to be someone who seeks the throne, which likely makes her one of the most qualified of the deities to claim the title. Hopefully her sponsor this season is someone who shares the same grace as her character."

That last line is doing a great deal of work. Her sponsor is the grixist CEO Huanxin Jinx, whom Odette describes as "the most evil person I know, and that's saying a lot" — out purely for revenge, and dangerous precisely because she is smart.

docs.title: The Floor Boon
docs.text:
Boon (Book 6, ch. 17)

"The light of grace fills you with peace. You have been granted a floor boon. This boon will remain in place for the remainder of this floor as long as you remain in Eileithyia's grace. She may revoke this boon at any time. Protection from Spiritual Possession. 10% Healing speed. Plus 10% Constitution."

docs.title: Quest: "Spiders"
docs.text:
New Quest! Spiders.

"Warning: This quest comes from a deity you do not worship. You are not required to complete this quest, but they might not like it if you ignore them. Kill five spiders in my name every day until I ask you to stop. Reward: You will receive another boon from me."

The quest is a cover, and she says so in a deity message the system is not permitted to monitor: it exists to give her a private channel to Carl and a legal mechanism to grant his party further boons. Carl has to scratch his left arm to acknowledge, since any typed reply would be visible.

The real bargain: when Odette offers to serve as Faction Wars team Adjutant, Carl must accept. In exchange, Eileithyia guarantees the votes to turn team protections off on the ninth floor, and promises to clear the outstanding problem with the Crown of the Sepsis Whore that threatens Katia and Princess Donut. Carl must tell nobody — not Donut, not Mordecai, not Odette, not aloud and not through the bathroom system — or the deal is void and, in her words, "I will make certain everyone you've ever known and loved is pounded into dirt."

Her closing pitch is the reason the quest matters well past Floor 8: "I will make certain you survive until the twelfth floor, where you and Katia and the cat will help me claim the Celestial Throne once and for all... I help my friends, Carl. I utterly destroy my enemies."

docs.title: Floor 9 (Book 7): Losing Her Pilot
docs.text:
Eileithyia returns at the very end of Faction Wars, summoned by Katia consuming the Orchid of Eileithyia's Grace — a 60-minute process forced into the floor's final hour by Emberus's doomsday timer.

System messages (Book 7, ch. 86)

"The Orchid of Eileithyia has been consumed. The goddess has been summoned. ... Eileithyia has entered the realm. You are in the presence of a deity. The Scavenger's Daughter has opened her eyes. She fills with power. Temporary effect from Eileithyia: All damage you strike against female opponents is quartered. All female members of your party strike with a melee power of 500%. Girl power, bitches!"

Her boss readout is unchanged from Book 6 — Level 250, sponsored by Huanxin Jinx, invulnerable on this floor, summoned to this location — but this is the first time the party sees her true form rather than the grixist's projection: a large humanoid woman with olive skin, dark curly hair and flowers in it, white and gold robes, three fingers on each hand and three toes on each foot, and a distinctly alien lower face.

docs.title: The exploit that kills her sponsor
docs.text:
A quirk of the system freezes a sponsored deity in place between her summoning and the worshiper's choice — Baroness Victory calls it a long-standing exploit that is hard to set up, requiring both a choice option and a sponsored god. With Eileithyia frozen and unable to intervene, Huanxin Jinx — ejected from the goddess's shell and standing in the tent in person — is trapped in a circle of words of power and executed by Princess Donut, with a crossbow bolt tipped with Mordecai's mother's ashes, fired from a quadruped weapon mount on Donut's back.

Donut, Book 7, ch. 86

"You're strong, yes. But we are getting stronger every day. And you know what? We don't need to kill the gods and goddesses to win. No, honey... We just need to kill you."

Carl loots the body immediately, "because we didn't want Eileithyia to get too upset." The goddess then unfreezes as an unsponsored, unpiloted deity and finishes her business as if nothing had happened.

docs.title: Granting Katia's boon
docs.text:
Katia's three options under the Orchid deal are an extreme constitution boost, becoming a celestial attendant in Eileithyia's court, or pregnancy. Eileithyia presses her toward the safety of the court — "as a woman with gift, your challenges will be even greater... I promise you will be kept safe" — and Katia declines. The goddess makes her human again, restores her body (revealing how much of it Katia had quietly lost: an arm, a leg, most of the other leg, an ear), and grants the boon.

Book 7, ch. 86

"'Then it will be so,' Eileithyia said... She put her hand on Katia's stomach. 'First, you will be made human again.' ... 'It is done. It will be a boy.'"

Katia is flagged Ineligible and removed from the dungeon; Eileithyia fades out after her. She also delivers, in passing, a burst of twelfth-floor news: the teleported city of Larracos has splattered a convent of Resheph's nuns, and Odette has taken control of the resulting zombies "because she's already taken out Inpewt."

Scope

Katia's exit and what the boon means for her are a Characters-pass topic — see Katia. This page records only the mechanics of the goddess granting it.

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride and Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Emberus
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Tier: Deity — Carl's own god, patron of martyrs; brother of Hellik, father of the murdered Geyrun
  • Level: 250 (deity tier)
  • Floor: 9 ("Faction Wars"), entering the realm in ch. 84 and destroying the floor in ch. 87
  • Resolution (Book 7): Not fought. Burns the entire ninth floor to the ground on a 66-minute doomsday timer, and leaves an explicit promise to burn Carl "exquisitely" later
  • Resolution (Book 8): Stripped of invulnerability by Katia's Bolt of Ophiotaurus and pinned by a Danforth bolt, after Carl publicly renounces his faith and (falsely) confesses to killing Geyrun; killed by his own brother Taranis at the Floor 11 arena climax — permanence unconfirmed (see below)
  • Recurring since: Book 3 — Carl's patron deity, tracked through the Enchanted Pauper's Ring of the Steadfast Emberus

docs.title: Role Through the Floor
docs.text:
For most of Book 7, Emberus is a voice rather than a presence: a burning ring on Carl's finger, a stream of quests, and an escalating tone. His Floor 9 quest chain runs through the Kill Hellik thread — obtain an audience with Issitoq at a Club Vanquisher Temple of the Watch, break the Sheol truce, and kill his brother before the collapse of the eleventh floor.

Because Carl worships Emberus, every Hellik worshiper on the floor is automatically hostile to him, which the Larracos rams turn into a 500,000-gold Holy Crusade bounty on Carl's head. Emberus's response — "This worshiper of Hellik has insulted me. Kill him," with the reward scaling to how entertaining Carl makes it — produces one of the book's better set pieces and a Celestial Boon.

docs.title: After Hellik's Message
docs.text:
When Carl relays Hellik's message — that Hellik did not kill Geyrun, that their mother and sister Apito has been corrupted, that the All Tree is rotting, that Nekhebit has returned, and that Scolopendra stirs — it does not calm Emberus down. It makes everything worse.

He issues a new quest (Kill 100 worshipers of Hellik, before the collapse of the eleventh floor), then follows it with a private, contemplative message that is effectively a death sentence with a delay on it.

Emberus to Carl (Book 7, ch. 55)

"Am I wrong to hate him? He has treated with Issitoq on our behalf, who has in turn allowed the peace to be breached. I am now allowed to kill the other Sheol princes in exchange for the information Amayon has about Geyrun. And what does he mean about our mother and sister? You, my martyr, be vigilant. If you survive killing Hellik, like he surely deserves, I fear I may turn my rage and grief on you for daring to hurt my own kin, and for this, I love you, beloved but doomed worshiper. I promise the burning will be exquisite."

Unresolved threat for future books

Carl is now caught between two incompatible obligations from the same god: kill Hellik, and be punished for killing Hellik. The promise of an "exquisite" burning is not discharged in Book 7 — Emberus burns the floor for unrelated reasons and Carl escapes. It remains outstanding.

docs.title: Entering the Realm
docs.text:
At the very end of the book, Samantha confesses to having taken part in Geyrun's murder. Emberus comes in person.

System Message (Book 7, ch. 84)

"Emberus has entered the realm."

Team quest — no host, no opt-out (Book 7, ch. 84)

"A very angry god that many of you are familiar with has just entered the realm. His name is Emberus. His son, Geyrun, was murdered... But a demigod named 'Samantha' has just admitted to having taken part in the crime. Emberus, being the loving father he is, has come to the realm to question this demigod. Regardless of what Samantha says to him, Emberus is going to turn the entirety of the 9th floor into a cremation chamber. This will happen in at least 66 minutes, but your cremation may be delayed slightly if Samantha actually shows up to the interrogation. Regardless, everything and everybody on this floor is going to die. This is not something that can be stopped. That is, unless you manage to kill Emberus, which as we all know is possible, but unlikely. So here's the quest part. You need to win faction wars. You gotta do it fast. And once you do that, get the hell out of there before the world goes up in flames."

The reward for surviving: one year off any indentureship contract negotiated on the next floor, and all food boxes upgraded with the "extra toasty" option.

docs.title: What the Timer Forces
docs.text:
The 66 minutes is the engine of the entire endgame. Everything the Princess Posse had planned to do over days has to happen inside an hour:

  • Katia must eat the Orchid of Eileithyia's Grace immediately, because it takes exactly 60 minutes to work — collapsing her goodbye into nothing
  • The Louis Santiago transplant surgery that removes Epitome Tagg from his chest has to be rushed
  • The second casting of Zerzura — the Princess Posse's actual win condition — has to be triggered while the clock runs
  • Every remaining crawler on the floor has to sprint for the stairwells early

Samantha is sent to stall him, and does: she tells him everything she knows, which only makes him angrier. The heat rises across the map for the whole hour, with Emberus bellowing for her in the distance.

Book 7, ch. 87

"Warning: Emberus will destroy the 9th floor in three minutes."

He is, at the end, explicitly enraged at both Carl and Hellik, and the floor burns: "One was Emberus, who filled the world with fire."

docs.title: Renounced and Confessed
docs.text:
At the Floor 11 arena climax, Carl deliberately springs a trap on his own god. He pulls off the Enchanted Pauper's Ring of the Steadfast Emberus, publicly renounces his faith, and confesses on the record to the crime his own Emberus church quest had been circling since Book 6 — that he, not Hellik, killed Emberus's son Geyrun:

Book 8, ch. 95

"The other guy to kill your worthless smear of a son was me. That's right. I killed him with my bare hands, and as he died, I said, 'I'm doing this because your dad is a little bitch.'"

The confession is a lie — the renunciation is not

These are two separate acts and only one of them is sincere. Carl really does leave the faith: he removes the ring, confirms the menu prompt, eats the smite, and carries the resulting Mark of the Damned scars for the rest of the book. The confession, by contrast, is pure provocation — Carl says so in narration one page earlier: "I actually had no idea for certain who killed Geyrun, though I now knew this was something — if I survived this — I would still have to figure out." The murder of Geyrun therefore remains an open mystery at the end of Book 8, not a solved one.

Carl first names Khepri as the killer — a decoy accusation, and also a pretext for summoning him, since it is Khepri's deity-presence effect (routed through Penny's Kneepads of Kina) that grants Penny ninety seconds of invulnerability at the critical moment. Only then does Carl deliver the "second killer" line about himself. See Carl's own page for the smite's aftermath (the Emberus tattoos on the backs of Carl's hands are burned into permanent, unexplained scars called the Mark of the Damned).

docs.title: Pinned and Killed by His Own Brother
docs.text:
The confession is the second half of a two-part trap. Donut, firing from her Scorpion's Bite weapon mount the instant Emberus rears back to attack, puts two different bolts into his two eye sockets: first Katia's Bolt of Ophiotaurus, which strips his invulnerability for roughly fifteen seconds, then one of her ten Danforth bolts, which anchors him in place so he cannot move while vulnerable. The first half of the trap is Penelope, used as bait to draw both Emberus and his brother Taranis into the same place; see Taranis's own page for the mechanics of that lure.

Vulnerable and enraged, Emberus hurls a fire attack that would have killed Carl outright — the party's Four-Leaf Clover Patch redirects it onto Penny instead. Taranis, watching his own brother's attack land on the pig he has become instantly infatuated with, kills Emberus without hesitation, one second before his invulnerability would have returned:

Book 8, ch. 96

"Taranis, seeing his little brother rising in the arena and knowing he was the one who had fired the attack at his beloved pig, raised his hand. Emberus paused, a moment of lucidity coming over the insane deity. 'Brother, no,' he said. Taranis twisted his wrist... With one second left on his invulnerability, Emberus, god of sun and ash, exploded."

System Message

"A deity has fallen. The heavens tremble with rage."

See Taranis for the full confrontation from the killer's side.

docs.title: Permanence Not Confirmed
docs.text: Book 8 never states that Emberus is gone for good, and this page does not assert it either. Gods in this series have "died" and returned before — Diwata was killed on Floor 6 and was active again by Book 7 (see the Book 7 gods table). Whether the same holds for Emberus, whose Memorial Crystal Carl recovers from the arena dirt moments later, is left an open question for future books.

docs.title: Loose Threads
docs.text:
• The long-running Kill Hellik church quest and the promised "exquisite" burning smite (see above) are both rendered moot by Carl's renunciation, but neither is explicitly closed out on the page.
  • Emberus's Memorial Crystal is looted from the arena floor by Carl immediately after the kill — a second Apito-family memorial crystal alongside Prepotente's stolen one (see Taranis).
  • No full page yet exists documenting Emberus's earlier appearances in Books 5–6; this page still begins at Book 7 and should be backfilled by a future pass rather than expanded from scratch here.

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin and Book 8: A Parade of Horribles.

docs.title: Eris
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Tier: Deity — Goddess of Chaos
  • Level: 250
  • Floor: 9 ("Faction Wars"), the Dream's territory and then the whole map (ch. 61–76)
  • Sponsor: Nami, a model and influencer who outbid the Priory for the slot — killed mid-book, after which Eris runs loose and unsponsored: "This deity has lost her sponsor and can no longer be sponsored this season"
  • Resolution: Never fought. Escapes the Rolling Battle Formation ball, speaks privately with Carl, and leaves the realm of her own accord
  • Presence effect: Random Effect! As Eris is the goddess of chaos, this effect will change each time you are in her presence
  • Standing: "Eris is a prime contender for the Ascendent Throne"

docs.title: Who She Is
docs.text:
Tall, elf-like with a strangely long neck and a few serpentine features that suggest a distant naga relative; long blonde hair, a forked tongue, a black-and-white striped floor-length jacket over glowing Valkyrie armor, and over-inflated lips tattooed with a spiral. Her symbol is two back-to-back Cs with a flaming lance through them.

Deity description (Book 7, ch. 76)

"Eris. Goddess of Chaos. Half-sister of Taranis, mother to nobody, lover of parties, drinking, chaos—of course, and generally known as the Ascendency's worst, most unapologetic gossip. If she were mortal and human, she'd be called a wine aunt. She'd have a rich, dead husband who died under mysterious circumstances. She would split her time between the hair salon and spending her days on the local community Facebook page where she would be constantly creating utter pandemonium with her posts and her 'this is just my opinion, but...' style messages. All of her nieces and nephews love her. In fact, everybody loves her, even though they all know deep down she's an utter piece of shit... One of her abilities is being All Knowing. She knows everybody's business, which makes her a dangerous foe and an even more dangerous friend. If she gives you information, it's probably true, and it's probably something that's going to get you into trouble for knowing. While she's able to lie, she rarely does. Why bother when the truth is often so much worse?"

The description notes this is a genuinely unique season: there has never been a Faction Wars where Eris was not sponsored, so this is the first time her real personality has been allowed to operate. Her pilot Nami had cosmetic surgery to look and sound like the old crawler Hekla, which is why Eris speaks in Hekla's voice — fading once Nami is dead.

docs.title: Losing Her Pilot
docs.text:
Eris is dragged into the Meatus–Harpocrates fight almost immediately, with Meatus wrapping around her and swinging her as a battering ram. She panics and starts casting.

A War Mage Rebellion mage later reaches her inside the ball and strips her soul armor, ejecting Nami — who is spat out of the ball as an ordinary body, immediately skinned by a flesher and destroyed by Carl's hob-lobber before she can become a new war mage. From that point Eris is unsponsored, unpiloted and entirely her own.

docs.title: The Ceremony of Chaos
docs.text:
Panicking mid-fight, Eris casts a pair of spells she is normally supposed to save for the twelfth floor: Bear Witness, followed by Bring Forth the Witnesses.

System warning (Book 7, ch. 65)

"Warning. The Goddess Eris has cast Bear Witness in a wide area around her current position. This will only affect those outside of structures. The area of effect is marked on your map, but it's pretty much the whole floor."

Mordecai on the Ceremony of Chaos (Book 7, ch. 66)

"This is exclusive to Eris, and she usually does this on the 12th floor... Some gods can only claim the Ascendent throne if there are no mortals present, so Eris sometimes causes chaos by summoning mortal witnesses to the ceremony. It's called the Ceremony of Chaos. The witnesses are protected from the gods during this, hence the invulnerability, and she can keep them in the Witness state as long as she wants... They're brought to her in a giant pile. It's... it's a thing. She can only cast this once. Ever."

The result: roughly 80,000 combatants frozen, blinded to the chat, made invulnerable and teleported into one enormous heap beside the ruined Dream castle. The backlash also kills long-range teleportation floor-wide for an hour and interrupts the lava-abatement plan for Larracos.

That heap is what Donut then wraps in her tower-amplified Rolling Battle Formation, producing the mile-wide rolling ball that dominates the rest of the floor. Carl's assessment afterward, relayed to Donut: "That's on that dead alien who was driving Eris. You saved them by casting the Battle Formation spell. If you hadn't done it, half of everyone would be dead by now."

Eris wakes inside the ball, switches her Witness spell off — which changes nothing, because Donut's spell is now doing the immobilising — and is trapped there until it breaks.

docs.title: The Conversation with Carl
docs.text:
When the ball finally breaks, Eris freezes the world and appears beside Carl at human scale. She is explicitly not under War Mage control. She spins him a two-item wheel that makes one of his current god-effects permanent (Meatus's curse, or Harpocrates's Pied Piper skill — it lands on Pied Piper), bites his ear, snaps his pinkie for laughing at, and recruits.

Eris's pitch (Book 7, ch. 76)

"Don't die, Carl... I know you worship grumpy ol' Emberus, but we'll change that soon, especially now he has put you in an impossible situation. See how Donut was just named Champion? I can do that to you as well. You'll have to kill all three, of course. Taranis, Emberus, and Hellik. But don't worry. I'll help."

Then she hands over the two pieces of information that drive the rest of the book:

Book 7, ch. 76

"The War Mages traded the Gate of the Feral Gods with a merchant named Paca at the Midnight Market. Paca is an agent for Krakaren Prime, who is stuck in the Nothing. Paca has the gate in her stomach. Get the gate back and give it to that insane Skyfowl who built the antennae underneath your castle, and maybe you can actually win this thing. Also, Britney picked that axe off the ground and is now possessed."

Unverified: the Britney claim

Eris's statement that Britney is possessed is never confirmed or denied on the page in Book 7. Nothing later in the book resolves it, and Carl's own description of Eris — that when she gives you information "it's probably true, and it's probably something that's going to get you into trouble for knowing" — is the only weight behind it. Treat it as an open thread, not an established fact.

Carl relays everything Eris said to Rosetta, Tipid, Donut and most of the officers. Both Rosetta and Tipid are wary of the idea of fetching the Gate of the Feral Gods for Justice Light, being protective of the skyfowl; Carl advocates for it anyway.

docs.title: Afterward
docs.text:
• Eris leaves the realm on her own terms — "Eris has left the Realm. The Scavenger's Daughter looks away"
  • She had earlier re-enacted the teleport ban that strands crawlers late in the floor
  • Carl is on her "friend of the church" list, which he finds a mystery
  • At the very end of the book, Carl hears laughter "distinctly like that of Eris" from inside the river in his own head — a late, unexplained beat
  • She appears once more in the epilogue, in person, in a shop, asking whether anyone is really going to ask Eris, goddess of chaos, if she is wearing a costume

docs.title: Book 8: A Parade of Horribles
docs.text: Eris's presence escalates sharply across Book 8, culminating in a new, far more monstrous physical form at the Floor 11 climax.

docs.title: The Five-Sided Coin
docs.text:
Early in Floor 10, Eris appears to Carl in Hungry Eyes Village, casually warns him he's "running out of time" on his Emberus problem, and hands him a fate coin:

Book 8

"She spat into her own hand, and a large coin appeared. 'Ever seen one of these? It's a five-sided coin.'"

The coin shows four permanent-effect outcomes on its faces — Donut's death ("RIP"), Carl's feet severed ("de-feeted"), most of Carl's friends dying, and Carl hanged-but-smiling ("I become what they accuse me of") — with a fifth, unrevealed side. Before her pet Uzi Jesus can flip it, Carl grabs the coin out of the air himself, which Eris declares unlocks the random fifth outcome instead of committing to one of the first four: "You picked the fifth side! Great! Chaos wins again!" A swirling tattoo appears on his palm as a permanent marker. By the end of the book, the coin's result is still undetermined — Eris's parting words are "we have until the end of the twelfth to figure out how the fifth side lands."

In the same scene, Eris confirms her price for patronage explicitly names three gods Carl would have to kill: Taranis, Emberus, and Hellik — and drops early hints about the goddess Apito's "scattered pieces" that pay off at the climax.

docs.title: The Arena Form
docs.text:
At the Floor 11 finale, immediately after Emberus's death, Eris appears again — freezing the world, swapping every nearby crawler's inventory at random as her chaos effect, and revealing a physical form nothing like her earlier human-scale appearance:

Book 8, ch. 97

"Eris, her voice howling with laughter, cracked into existence, standing directly over me, her body huge, nothing like the form I was used to. Her serpentine face was the same, but her body was that of a Saccathian mixed with the Krakaren boss still in the stands. But instead of tentacles, her lower mass was nothing but the tails of snakes. Thousands of them, like a reverse Medusa, many with rattles on them."

She taunts Taranis for his relationship with their mother/wife Apito and confirms the goddess is not fully gone:

Book 8, ch. 97

"Our mom is going to be so pissed when she fully comes back from the dead... Four of her five pieces are in here right now watching you try to literally fuck a pig!"

This is the book's clearest confirmation that Apito — introduced across Books 5–7 as "both dead and not dead" — survives in some scattered, five-piece form, with unfinished business explicitly teed up for Floor 12 and beyond: "if we let those guys downstairs win the Ascendency, it's lights out. No more fun."

docs.title: Aftermath
docs.text:
• Eris departs on her own terms, as always — "Eris has left the realm. Your inventory has been restored" — leaving the fate coin's outcome and Apito's condition both explicitly unresolved.
  • She remains, per her own words, unconcerned with worship in the traditional sense: "You are chaos incarnate... I don't need you to worship me."

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin and Book 8: A Parade of Horribles.

docs.title: Goblin War Chieftain
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Boss tier: Neighborhood Boss (never officially confirmed — no boss card ever triggered)
  • Level: Not shown; both crawlers jumped to Level 8 immediately after the kill
  • Floor: 1, in a goblin engineering workshop
  • Defeated by: Carl & Princess Donut — via cart bomb, without ever entering the boss room
  • Reward: A bronze star each (no boss box fanfare, since the fight never officially started)

AI Commentary (in-voice, written for this wiki — not a book excerpt)

"No card, no cutscene, no big scary reveal — just a cart full of Hobgoblin Pus and some truly questionable life choices. Folks, this is what we in the industry call 'skipping the boss fight by blowing up the boss room.' Efficient. Deniable. Absolutely going to haunt somebody's dreams tonight."

docs.title: Encounter
docs.text:
After trading intel to spark a "meth war" between the local goblins and a rival llama gang (see Rory & Lorelai), Carl and Donut are left alone in an abandoned goblin engineering workshop, with the chieftain sealed behind a single door on the far side of the room. Rather than open the door and trigger a conventional boss fight, they loot the workshop for black powder and a rare C4-like explosive called "Hobgoblin Pus," load it onto a cart, shove the cart through the door into the boss room, seal the door, retreat several rooms away, and detonate it remotely.

Donut catches a brief glimpse inside before the door closes: the chieftain "sitting down, reading a book" — and, critically, a room full of goblin infants and pregnant goblins she doesn't mention until after Carl has already pushed the trigger. The explosion kills the chieftain (confirmed by an achievement wall and a bronze star for both crawlers, jumping them to Level 8), but Carl realizes afterward that he's just killed goblin children along with it.

This is Book 1's darkest moment for Carl — see Carl's Personal Rules for the "You will not break me" mantra he adopts in its aftermath.

Sourced from Book 1: The Apocalypse Will Be Televised.

docs.title: Gore-Gore the Mantaur
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Boss tier: Neighborhood Boss
  • Level: 40
  • Floor: 4 ("The Iron Tangle")
  • Full title: Gore-Gore the Mantaur! Train Engineer! Adherent of Grull the War God! Berserker Extreme!
  • Killed by: Carl (solo, with Katia/Donut/Mongo support) — via electrocution
  • Reward: A Neighborhood Boss box; the fight's aftermath directly triggers Carl's sponsorship by the Valtay Corporation

AI Commentary (in-voice, written for this wiki — not a book excerpt)

"Ladies and gentlemen, a Mantaur just found out the hard way that third rails don't care about your religion. Ten out of ten form on the drop kick, minus several points for nearly summoning an invulnerable war god by accident. Grull says hi, by the way. He'll be along shortly."

docs.title: B... B... B... Boss Battle
docs.text:
Per the in-universe boss-battle reveal:

"You've enraged an NPC. But not just any NPC! It's a neighborhood boss! It's... GORE-GORE THE MANTAUR! TRAIN ENGINEER! ADHERENT OF GRULL THE WAR GOD! BERSERKER EXTREME! LEVEL 40!"

docs.title: Encounter
docs.text:
Gore-Gore bursts out of Club Vanquisher after a ram-headed cleric tips him off that Carl's group crashed one of his trains. He's a Mantaur — a centaur-adjacent, four-armed warrior race devoted to the war god Grull — wielding metallic claw weapons and immune to Magic Missile damage. The fight takes place on and around a wrecked, smoking train platform.

The fight has a real complication: Carl's War Gauntlet carries a small, cumulative chance to involuntarily summon the god Grull on every successful punch. Carl doesn't realize the odds stack (1.5%, 3.0%, 4.5%...) until the counter is already at 7.5%, and by the time Gore-Gore is staggered, the summon has been triggered — a ten-second countdown begins. Carl finishes Gore-Gore off with a flying Talon Strike drop kick that sends the boss's body onto the subway's live third rail, electrocuting him — killing the boss and ending the fight (and, crucially, the summon countdown) in the same instant, mere seconds before Grull would have fully manifested.

Carl is knocked around badly by the fight (a throat-grab into a fall through wreckage, several electrical burns) but survives; the encounter closes with a live sponsorship notification from the Valtay Corporation — Carl's first Valtay sponsor.

Sourced from Book 3: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook.

docs.title: Harpocrates
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Tier: Deity — God of Silence
  • Level: 250
  • Floor: 9 ("Faction Wars"), roaming the open battlefield and Shanty Town (ch. 59–77)
  • Sponsor: None — he arrives on his own, chasing the feral god Meatus
  • Resolution: Not killed. Conscripted into the Princess Posse with a hell-kissed level-18 Conscription potion, used as a weapon by Li Na, and finally leaves the realm enraged after Meatus is destroyed
  • Presence effect: Grants Carl the level-15 Pied Piper skill — which Eris's chaos spinner then makes permanent

docs.title: Who He Is
docs.text:
Harpocrates is the god whose genitalia was stolen, sewn onto a gremlin, and thereby became the separate god Meatus. It is, per Mordecai, "an old story and kind of a dumb, recurring joke" that normally plays out during the Ascendency battles rather than in the dungeon.

He is not mute and he is not deaf — he is the god of silence, and "he can hear the heartbeat of a fly from half a planet away." Sound enrages him. Mordecai's standing order the entire time he is on the map is that Donut must not use her PA system.

Seen up close from the Nest tower, he is a kaiju: taller than the tower itself, slim, younger-looking than expected, and otherwise near-human, in white and gold robes torn and filthy from fighting his own penis, with the front stained red as a permanent visual reminder of what was taken from him.

Rosetta's read on him is that he is fundamentally a decent sort — "Harpocrates hasn't cast his worst spells because he's generally a good guy. He doesn't want to level the town if he doesn't have to. But he's still a god."

docs.title: The Chase
docs.text:
Harpocrates enters the realm chasing Meatus and fights him across the whole map. Donut's loud commentary and music earn her a personal marked-for-death flag, and he spends much of the back half of the floor stalking the Nest tower. Two obstacles slow him:

  • the Larracos deflector towers, which he pauses at but will eventually push past
  • a pair of changelings disguised as ogre basilica guards, whose Untouchable status means a god may not attack them or cross the threshold they hold. They stand firm and keep him out of Shanty Town

When Donut's Rolling Battle Formation swallows Meatus and Eris into one enormous ball, Harpocrates picks the ball up by the shaft and uses it as a flail — and casts a protective spell over it to keep its health from dropping, inadvertently preserving thousands of trapped combatants.

docs.title: The Conscription
docs.text:
The War Mage Rebellion is the first faction to try enslaving a god, using hell-kissed Conscription potions brewed in the Nothing by Krakaren Prime; their attempt on Yarilo works, and the casting war mage promptly explodes from the level disparity. Li Na loots the duplicate potion off the dead war mage, has it copied with her brother's scroll of potion duplication, and uses the original on Harpocrates.

Warlord message (Book 7, ch. 72)

"Harpocrates has been successfully conscripted. Harpocrates, level 250 is now a member of the Princess Posse."

Hell-Kissed Potion of Conscription, level 18 (Book 7, ch. 72)

"This works like a regular potion of Conscription, but it has been hell-kissed. At level 18, it will work against pretty much any non-affiliated entities, regardless of their protections, including most deities. Most. It was brewed in the dark recesses of the Nothing by Krakaren Prime, who is said to yearn for domination, which was why she'd been banished there in the first place."

Under Li Na's control he is rank Legionnaire in the White Dragons, with Under Orders over his head. She rides him like a mount and lets Juice Box's changelings climb aboard as well. The god is visibly enraged by this and fights the compulsion the whole time — "he's harder to control when I'm not near him," she reports, and later, "I think Harpocrates is fighting the Conscription, so we need to do this now."

docs.title: Killing Yarilo
docs.text:
Li Na's first order is to set Harpocrates on Yarilo, the other freed feral god, who had been conscripted onto the War Mage team. Harpocrates beats him to death with the Rolling Battle Formation ball — a weapon larger than Yarilo himself — while Yarilo throws chunks of buildings at him and begs: "Stop! Not my face. Anything but my face!"

System message (Book 7, ch. 73)

"A deity has fallen. And while Yarilo was damned to the Nothing, his death has angered the gods. The heavens tremble with rage."

docs.title: Departure
docs.text:
Harpocrates's last act under conscription is to toss the ball over the lip of Larracos and into the funnel, setting up the Nest-tower endgame. When the ball breaks and Donut destroys Meatus with War Crime, he watches his own stolen half get pulverised.

Book 7, ch. 77

"'Noooooooooooo!' came a deep scream, shaking the Nest. Harpocrates. The god wasn't mute after all. He raised his arms in the air. 'My cock! My beloved cock! You will pay for this, Champion of Nekhebit!' And with that, he too, disappeared. Harpocrates has left the realm."

Carl keeps the Pied Piper skill permanently; Donut keeps the grudge.

Unresolved

The text does not narrate a formal end to the Conscription — Harpocrates simply leaves the realm at the moment Meatus is destroyed, threatening Donut on the way out. His threat against the "Champion of Nekhebit" is left open.

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Heather the Bear
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Boss tier: Neighborhood Boss
  • Level: 19
  • Floor: 3 (Over City ruins, near Grimaldi's circus)
  • Killed by: Carl, solo
  • Reward: A Platinum Lucky Bastard Box for surviving her level-15+ opening spell hit (the "Lazarus" achievement), plus standard boss loot; her death triggers Tsarina Signet's blood-sacrifice summoning

AI Commentary (in-voice, written for this wiki — not a book excerpt)

"Roller skates. Worm claws. A pink tutu. Folks, I've seen a lot of monstrosities in my time narrating this circus of horrors, but tonight's contestant really said 'why not all three?' Five stars for commitment to the bit, minus several thousand for what it did to Carl's pants."

docs.title: Encounter
docs.text:
Heather is Tsarina Signet's chosen "sacrifice" for her nightly blood-summoning ritual against Grimaldi's circus — captured and put under a sleep curse rather than killed outright, since Signet's Ink Marauder spell requires her to personally witness the kill, not perform it. Carl is manipulated into the fight after Signet puts both him and Princess Donut to sleep with a Water Lily curse, then wakes only Carl and forces him to fight alone as the price of Donut's safety.

Heather is a former circus attraction — a "roller-skating bear" act — transformed by the same cataclysm that warped the rest of Grimaldi's troupe. She stands roughly eight feet tall on her skates, with living, worm-like growths in place of claws that burrow into flesh and speak directly into a victim's mind ("Strong he is... he will feed our clowns well"). Carl survives her opening attack (an unnamed spell over level 15) only by luck, severs the worm-claws with his Protective Shell, then improvises: he douses her in flammable moonshine and sets her alight, then finishes the fight with a lottery scratch-ticket that could have gone either way — a level-15 fireball, or a healing custard splash. It rolls custard.

The healing "kill" turns out to be the real solution: curing the wounds also kills the parasitic worms controlling her, restoring the real Heather underneath — an old, gray-muzzled circus bear, free of the mind control for the first time since the cataclysm, and clearly asking with her eyes to be put out of her misery. Carl obliges, ending the fight with two punches and a stomp.

docs.title: Notable Achievements
docs.text:
• Lazarus — for surviving an offensive spell above level 15 without dying (reward: Platinum Lucky Bastard Box)
  • A standard boss achievement/star and Boss Box for the kill itself

Sourced from Book 2: Carl's Doomsday Scenario.

docs.title: Hellik
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Tier: Deity — brother of Emberus, Carl's own god
  • Level: 250 (deity tier; never given an explicit level readout on the page — Carl cannot read his description at all)
  • Floor: 9 ("Faction Wars"), the entrance vestibule of Club Vanquisher (ch. 54)
  • Resolution: Never fought. Appears in person, banishes Khepri, delivers a message, and leaves
  • Standing quest: Carl is under an active Emberus quest to kill Hellik before the end of the eleventh floor — unresolved, and made worse by this meeting

docs.title: Who He Is
docs.text:
Hellik is the brother of Emberus and the main suspect in the murder of Geyrun, Emberus's son — the crime that underwrites Carl's entire religious storyline since Book 4. He is a widely worshiped god on Floor 9: the Larracos ram NPCs follow him, and any Hellik worshiper is automatically hostile to Carl on sight, which Carl exploits for bounty quests and Emberus's favour.

He appears as an ordinary, olive-skinned human man who sits down cross-legged next to a dying Carl as though joining him at a restaurant table. The only thing marking him as a god is the heat coming off him, which cooks Carl's skin while they talk.

docs.title: The Message
docs.text:
Hellik arrives in the middle of the Operation: Snake Pit disaster, banishes Khepri with a single line, waves away the burning immortal bugs, and hands Carl the most information-dense speech in the book. Carl is, at this moment, being beaten to death by Princess Vinata; Hellik simply talks over it.

Hellik's message for Emberus (Book 7, ch. 54)

"Tell my brother I did not kill his son. Tell him he cannot kill me, no matter how hard he tries. Tell him I love him, despite his madness. Tell him everything he thinks about me is a lie. Tell him our mother and sister, Apito, has been corrupted. There is a malevolent presence about her, and I believe my nephew learned of it. Tell him the All Tree is beginning to rot. Tell him Nekhebit has returned, and I believe she is behind it all. Tell him we need to work together if we want to survive and discover what happened to our mother and his son. I know you seek an audience with Issitoq to break the truce. I will treat with him on your behalf. Scolopendra stirs. It is all connected."

That is five separate plot threads handed over in one breath: Apito's corruption, the rot in the All Tree, Nekhebit's return, Hellik's intercession with Issitoq on the Sheol truce, and the first in-scene use of the phrase "Scolopendra stirs" — see Scolopendra.

docs.title: Friend of the Church
docs.text:
System message (Book 7, ch. 54)

"You have been marked as a friend of the church by Hellik. Worshipers of Hellik will no longer be automatically hostile toward you."

Carl is named a friend of Hellik's church while still carrying an active quest to kill him — a contradiction he notes explicitly. When the Club Vanquisher raid settles, his "friend of the church" list reads: Apito. Eileithyia. Eris. Grull. Hellik. Issitoq. Nekhebit. Theia. Yemaya. Carl finds Hellik's inclusion surprising, Grull's inexplicable, and Issitoq's and Eris's a mystery.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
Delivering the message does not defuse anything. It enrages Emberus, who responds with a new quest (Kill 100 worshipers of Hellik, before the collapse of the eleventh floor and, as a practical matter, before the Kill Hellik quest itself) and then a far more alarming private note.

Emberus, after receiving the message (Book 7, ch. 55)

"Am I wrong to hate him? He has treated with Issitoq on our behalf, who has in turn allowed the peace to be breached. I am now allowed to kill the other Sheol princes in exchange for the information Amayon has about Geyrun. And what does he mean about our mother and sister? You, my martyr, be vigilant.
