The moment the marker over Rude-Dolph blinks out and his yellow glow vanishes, Shi Maria — still missing a leg — dodges his next nose blast, climbs to the mall's second floor, leaps across the atrium and physically rips him in two. The two halves hang in the air, his nose sputtering out.

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: Scolopendra
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Tier: Dungeon Boss — a brand-new tier above Floor Boss, named for the first time in Book 8: "Just so we're crystal clear. I just summoned, at your fucking request, the final boss of the entire dungeon to the 11th floor."
  • Level: 500
  • Floor: Referenced since Floor 9 (Book 7); physically appears for the first and only time at the Floor 11 arena climax (Book 8)
  • Form: A centipede "the size of a goddamned aircraft carrier but longer," segmented, brown-and-red with bright yellow legs — "It wasn't anything special. It looked exactly like a centipede from Earth."
  • Summoned by: Carl, as the first of the 23 surviving crawlers' joint arena choices — "For my first choice, I choose Scolopendra"
  • Resolution: Neither killed nor abandoned — transformed by an enriched pet biscuit into a Level 1 sapient crawler party member, "Sexy Scolopendra"
  • Status at end of Book 8: Alive, sapient, in Carl and Donut's party

docs.title: Background Through Book 7
docs.text:
Nothing about Scolopendra's nature, form, or motive was ever shown on the page before Book 8. What existed was pure dread: two system warnings ("Scolopendra Stirs") tying her to the corruption of Apito, the rot in the All Tree, and Nekhebit's return, and a final Book 7 system message declaring her awakened, apparently triggered by Justice Light's climactic trap draining the broken Nothing into Scolopendra's Lair. See the Book 7 boss table for the full list of prior warnings and the civilisation-scale catastrophe she was already blamed for (the near-extinction of the Semeru Dwarves, among others).

Book 8 opens with her already loose and rampaging across the upper floors — Quasar reports she's "so far ... hadn't yet done anything other than move around a lot," and the 18th floor's Scolopendra Club has already gone dark, its guests forced through a gauntlet to reach safety.

docs.title: The Nine-Tier Attack
docs.text:
Late in Floor 10, provoked purely by the AI's own building rage at the crawlers' refusal to die on schedule, Scolopendra's clock starts:

System Message (Book 8, Heat 7 start)

"Scolopendra has released the first of nine attacks... You think these nine attacks are only going to affect the Scolopendra levels? Think again, bitches!... There will be at least 30 hours between each assault, unless Scolopendra is confronted directly or further upset. Then the remaining attacks may come hard and fast."

Each attack is a wheel-spin — the specific effect is not predetermined even by the AI itself ("What is this first attack? I don't actually know! Let's find out!") — followed by a second, individual green/red wheel per person determining who is actually hit. The general shape of this "Nine-Tier Attack" quest mechanic (the wheel, the timing rules, the escalation) is a Mechanics-pass topic; this page covers only what happens to Scolopendra and the party specifically.

Attack 1 — the Beast of Burden Sin (Transformation). Fires while the teams are still sitting in the Heat 7 starting blocks, minutes before the final Floor 10 race begins, with a stated 20% chance of hitting any given target:

Book 8

"You have been hit with a level 20 Transformation spell! ... Change selected."

  • Carl → a long-haired dachshund (with a German accent he can't shake)
  • Elle McGibbons → a goblin
  • Chris Andrews → a werewolf, spending most of his time in human form
  • Jacobus, Imani's permanently-summoned reverse tooth fairy → a starfish
  • Donut, Jamal, and Samantha all roll green and are unaffected; game guides are immune; Prepotente and Jurgen are shielded by his Apito memorial crystal

The duration clause matters: "For crawlers, the effects will last until you pass through a stairwell. For NPCs and everyone else, the effects will last 6 hours." Carl and Elle therefore change back on the stairs down to Floor 11 — but Chris, who leaves the dungeon through the Desperado Club's casino portal rather than a stairwell, never triggers the reset and is still a werewolf in the epilogue. Imani treats that as the good outcome, not a curse: his Igneous rock form is what would have killed him outside an enhancement zone.

Attack 2 — the Sin of Consumption. Fires dungeon-wide during the Floor 11 arena approach, with a 30% chance per person: worms burst from and devour anyone who fails their roll. Being physically inside Club Scolopendra does not protect Carl ("The club wasn't protecting me from the attack!"), and neither do safe rooms. Carl and Penny both roll green; it kills the tortured tourist Cerni Pinta on the spot, kills Prepotente's mount Sweety, wounds Gonk, and takes out roughly a third of the arena's mob population.

Attack 3 — interrupted. Scolopendra begins spinning up a third attack mid-arena-battle; this is the one Carl and Donut stop cold by feeding her the biscuit (below) with roughly ten seconds left on the countdown.

docs.title: The Floor 11 Arena
docs.text:
At the climax, Carl chooses to summon Scolopendra as the crawlers' collective first pick for the arena's stand-in fight — a plan the AI itself calls "the fucking prize" of "some suicidal gambits throughout the history of the crawl."

System Message (Book 8, ch. 94)

"You have entered the lair of a Floor Boss. You have entered the lair of the Dungeon Boss... Krakaren Prime. Level 235 Floor boss. ... Scolopendra. Level 500 Dungeon boss. Well, shit."

The AI lays out the stakes in unusually calm, glitch-free narration — a tonal shift the text notes explicitly ("which somehow made it seem even more terrifying"):

  • Killing her is not the same as winning the dungeon; the only exit remains the 18th floor.
  • Killing her does stop level-collapse timers dungeon-wide and kicks off the Ascendency battles immediately.
  • Abandoning her on a collapsing floor counts as killing her.
  • Either way — kill her outright, or leave her behind when the floor collapses — all of her remaining nine-tier attacks trigger at once, with no way to stop it: "You kill her, the remaining attacks trigger. You escape, the remaining attacks trigger. Yeah, good luck with this one, dumbass."

This is the trap the entire finale is built around avoiding. Scolopendra herself is not a combatant with intent — "The beast itself is nothing but a mindless animal reacting to the world around her... She is not rage. She is not anger. She is not vengeance. She is nature."

docs.title: The Biscuit
docs.text:
While Carl is inside Club Scolopendra using Penelope as bait to draw out Taranis and Emberus, Eris's chaos effect swaps every nearby crawler's inventory at random. In the scramble to recover before Scolopendra's third attack fires, Carl has Donut search his scrambled hotlist for a specific combination:

Book 8, ch. 97

"Donut, be careful! There are lots of bombs in there. Don't pull anything out unless I tell you to! Go to my hotlist. I need you to combine the ball in slot ten with the biscuit in slot twelve!"

The result is a banger sphere loaded with what Carl believes is the plain "Nothing Special" enriched pet biscuit — the mindless-pet variety, not the Party Companion one already spent on Penelope during the float-building phase. Carl throws it directly into Scolopendra's mouth, and the Level 500 Dungeon Boss instantly collapses into "a gelatinous puddle the size of a small elephant" — reduced, per the item's normal function, to a Level 1 creature ready to be claimed as a pet.

System reaction (Book 8, ch. 97)

"New Achievement. What the actual fuck, Carl? Okay, so there are power moves. And then there's this... Reward: ... Yeah, I got nothing for this."

This is not a kill and not an abandonment — she survives the floor collapse safely tucked away as a pet, which sidesteps the trap entirely and pauses the remaining nine-tier attacks rather than triggering them.

docs.title: The Mix-Up
docs.text:
The plan was to end up with a mindless Level 1 pet — the "ultimate weapon," as Carl frames it, because keeping her in his inventory means her death (and the attack cascade) is now entirely tied to his own survival. That is not what happens.

Book 8, ch. 98

"'Carl?' Donut said. 'Uh, okay, so we have a problem. Don't get mad.' ... 'So, with the inventory. It was happening so fast, I made a mistake. Like, a really, really bad one.'"

Because of the Eris-triggered inventory chaos, Donut had grabbed the wrong enriched pet biscuit. Scolopendra emerges not as a mindless pet but as a new, fully conscious crawler:

Book 8, ch. 98

"A new member has joined your party! Sexy Scolopendra. Level 1. Crawler #12,953,456."

She retains her centipede body — "a humanlike face with strangely giant lips... no arms. Twin yellow antennae twitched on her head. She had a red bow on one of the feelers" — but is now sapient, soft-spoken, and immediately, cheerfully flirtatious:

Book 8, ch. 98

"'Hi, Carl,' Scolopendra said, her voice soft and sultry. She fell to the ground, skittered forward, then stood, wrapping herself around me, squeezing tight until we were face-to-face... 'Boop,' she said."

Which biscuit she actually got is never stated on the page

The text never names the biscuit Donut grabbed by mistake — only that she grabbed the wrong one. It is worth recording what the result rules out and what it points at, without treating either as confirmed:

  • It is not the plain "Nothing Special" pet biscuit Carl asked for. That grants "no sapience whatsoever" and reverts the creature to juvenile form; Scolopendra is a sapient, numbered crawler.
  • It is almost certainly not the "Nothing Special Party Companion" biscuit already spent on Penelope, which this wiki previously asserted. That result is explicitly path one — the creature "will stay in their existing form... the anatomy won't change at all, meaning they won't gain the ability to talk." Scolopendra does talk out loud, and she is no longer centipede-shaped in the ordinary sense: she is human-sized, upright, with "a humanlike face," and Carl compares her directly to Commander Stockade, a documented subtree two-B transformation.
  • Those two traits — a subtree two-B physical transformation plus speech — match path two, and the only enriched path-two result named anywhere in the book is "The Paramour", whose extra clause is "a permanent, incurable charm that will make them fall hopelessly in love with the entity who fed them the biscuit." Carl is the one who threw the biscuit, and her first act is to wrap herself around him and boop his nose.

The book does not connect those dots itself, never shows how Prepotente's unique Paramour biscuit would have reached Carl's hotlist, and never rules out the existence of enriched biscuits beyond the three Prepotente was shown receiving. Treat the identity of the biscuit as unresolved, with the Paramour as the indicated but unconfirmed candidate.

docs.title: Status at Book's End
docs.text:
Scolopendra leaves Floor 11 as a Level 1 member of Carl and Donut's own party rather than a tamed pet or a corpse — a wildcard nobody, including Carl, appears to have anticipated. Whether the "abandon her and the remaining attacks trigger" clause still applies to a sapient party member (rather than a caged pet) is not addressed anywhere in Book 8 and should be treated as an open question for future books, not resolved here.

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin and Book 8: A Parade of Horribles.

docs.title: Sharp-Elbows
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Tier: Deckmaster — Number Nine of Ten
  • Level: 80
  • Type: Ogre necromancer witch, "loosely and half-assedly based on the rich and beautiful Ioway culture"
  • Floor: 8 ("The Ghosts of Earth"), the same Iowa turkey barn as Tom
  • Killed by: Raul the crab, who snapped her necro-staff totem in half and then decapitated her (ch. 42)
  • Notable: The whispered line she gives Carl while impaling him is one of Book 6's key beats in the "are the mobs sentient" thread

docs.title: The Witch in the Barn
docs.text:
A seven-foot, hunched ogre woman in rags, green-skinned with an angry, half-melted face and stringy black hair, carrying a thick magical walking staff. Her defining feature is the spikes: two-foot, black, venom-dripping spines covering her whole body, which look less like anatomy than like something growing out of her.

She is the "very interesting ogre necromancer witch" who took Tom's god-bereft turkey congregation under her protection in exchange for a daily sacrifice, and she is fought simultaneously with him — a three-way standoff with Donut at one corner, Tom at another and Sharp-Elbows at the third.

The AI, sulking at Carl for complaining about long descriptions, gives her the shortest boss description in the book — "Blah, blah, blah basically a Necromancer" — and then, when asked nicely, an actively spiteful one: "this legendary creature has a really interesting backstory, but you don't want to hear it, do you? Suit yourself. I just hope you haven't killed too many of those turkeys."

docs.title: The Fight
docs.text:
Donut opens with Skylar Spinach and immediately steals a card off her with The Thief. Sharp-Elbows answers with Unk Tehi Temple Guards (level 85), snares Shi Maria the moment she appears, and finally summons her signature totem: a gnarled root-tree studded with feathers and turkey claws, a black beating human heart hanging off it like an apple, and a golden lizard skull with gems for eyes on top — a necromantic staff she rips out of the ground and wields two-handed.

Once Tom dies, the barn begins sliding off the cliff, and the fight finishes in a collapsing structure with turkeys, zombie turkeys and gore cascading toward the ocean.

docs.title: The Impalement
docs.text:
Sharp-Elbows rolls into Carl at speed and pins him against a pole, driving her spikes through his arms, stomach, legs, neck and — the detail that earns him the Pincushioned! achievement — both of his eyeballs at once. Blind, held mouth-to-mouth with her, he hears her:

Sharp-Elbows, Book 6, ch. 42

"They starve us, you know. When we're not here, we are there. And when we're there, they make certain the hunger festers. You can stop it. You can satiate us all, Carl."

She is whispering, and Carl notes he "felt them more than I heard them." As she finally peels away, the last thing he sees when his sight returns is her face directly in front of his: "the ogre face was right there, staring directly into my eyes, and they were pleading, sad, afraid. I've seen those eyes before."

He spends the next several chapters unable to place where — and the memory of "that look the ogre had given me at the end of the fight, when she'd transformed" gives him chills every time it comes back. See Game Mechanics for the wider mob-sentience thread this feeds.

docs.title: The Kill
docs.text:
Raul — the Red Maníseros Land Crab totem, otherwise the party's biggest coward — snaps the necro staff in half, killing her last totem and freeing the deckmaster to be attacked directly. He announces himself ("Master Carl, this insignificant cur is here to rescue you!") and then snaps again, taking her head off while her body is still peeling free of Carl's.

Carl passes out for forty minutes afterwards, riddled with Woozy, Sore as Shit and Bonked, saved from the worst of it by Pater Coal's disguised debuff-suppressing ring. He has the presence of mind to pull both deckmaster corpses into his inventory before the barn goes over the cliff, which is the only reason the key quest doesn't fail.

Donut loots the cards, which include "some of our old favorites" and a new totem for the deck.

On Raul

Raul is a level-70 Red Maníseros Land Crab, "Sun-Kissed Cloud Rank Warrior," flagged in Cuba and one of the party's six starting totems. He is catalogued with the other Cuban mobs on the Mobs page.

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: Shi Maria, the Bedlam Bride
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Boss tier: City Boss
  • Level: 140
  • Floor: 8 ("The Ghosts of Earth"), a web-covered swamp in the Cuban interior
  • Full title: "The Bedlam Bride. Reaper Spider Minion." — a demi-god
  • Aliases: The Screamer, The Reviled, Kwaku's Love, The Corrupted Paramour, The Widow Endless, the Bedlam Bride; she prefers MaeMae among friends
  • Resolution: Not defeated in combat. Flagged into a T'Ghee card by mutual agreement (ch. 26–27), used as the party's strongest totem for the back half of the book, and ripped by Princess Donut at the climax (ch. 72) — after she had already tattooed herself permanently into Carl's chest
  • Stated weakness: Psionic attacks. That is the entire list

docs.title: The Title Boss
docs.text:
Shi Maria is the book's namesake. Samantha finds her first — "I FELT HER PRESENCE. SHE'S A DEMI-GOD. PROBABLY NEVER EVEN GOT AN INVITE TO A PARTY" — and befriends her on the strength of a shared grievance: both are looking for a missing husband.

Monster description (Book 6, ch. 26)

"Reaper Spider minions are regular mobs one may find on the fifteenth floor, working as minions of something kinda fucked up we're not ready to talk about yet. They have celestial blood... But not all of them are merchants. Some have escaped out into the lower levels and have found their own path. Some have grown in power beyond that of a regular Reaper Spider Minion. This particular one is special. She has had many names. She currently goes by Shi Maria, and her story is long and tragic and can't possibly be fully told here. Once upon a time, she found herself married to a god. It didn't go so well. It's said she killed him... The thing is, she doesn't remember actually killing him. Honestly, it's not really important. What is important is that she was kicked out of the celestial realm and banished to this swamp where she spends her days plotting on how to get revenge on everyone and everything who has ever done her wrong. That list is very, very long."

The Bahamas book entry adds the part she disputes: "The problem is, legend has it she killed her husband. That she ate him right up. She was banished for the crime. She insists she is blameless, but sometimes, during her more lucid moments, she's not so certain of her own innocence. Beware her lies."

She appears as a giant spider with an almost-human head on a long, putty-like neck that rotates freely, four bulbous eyes, flaking skin and greasy black hair, with long hair-covered fangs. Legs long enough to skewer a crawler from a treetop.

docs.title: Abilities
docs.text:
• Permanent Insanity and Permanent Blindness — level-15 Unending Insanity and Lights Out, neither curable without divine intervention. Mordecai's Liquid Therapy protection potion, taken once a day, is the only reason the party survives the meeting
  • The fifth eye — an extra eye that opens in the centre of her head, "black and white and yellow and red all at once," which blinds and maddens. Katia's people have a proverb about it: Never stare into the blinding eye of the Bedlam Bride — meaning don't become so obsessed with one thing that you go blind to everything else
  • Spinneret and Venomous Bite
  • Cockroach (level 15) — a full heal on what would be a fatal blow. As a card, it works differently: when she "dies" she is returned to Donut's deck rather than the discard pile. Carl's note is that in practice "she never died"
  • Weakness: psionic attacks. Donut's Floor 8 class is Master Telephone Psychic, a psionic class — the book does not spell out the connection, but it is the only listed vulnerability she has

docs.title: The Bargain
docs.text:
Rather than fight her, Carl negotiates. She wants to reach Larracos, where she believes a master pulpmancer can free her from a card prison and help her find her husband; Carl wants her firepower. Both know the other is probably lying.

Shi Maria, Book 6, ch. 27

"That fool Samantha says you keep your promises. I could devour you now, but if I am to leave this horrible place, I must trust in you. I must find my husband and prove I didn't kill him. In order to do that, I must first get to Larracos. I have no quarrel with you. Once the city is reached, I will tell you how to undo the card magic, and you can set me free. In the meantime, I will help you."

Carl already knows the pulpmancer's shop is in the flooded lower levels of Larracos and the mage is almost certainly dead. He does not mention it. Quest: The Bedlam Bride is simply "Get her crazy ass to the city of Larracos. That's it."

docs.title: As a Card
docs.text:
Shi Maria is the party's strongest totem by a wide margin — she appears, assesses, and clears the field, often in seconds. She also demands to see Donut's hand and suggests buffs. She has a sadistic streak: she keeps opponents alive to eat them in pieces, and she plays with gorgons. She dislikes Raul the crab (she once used him as a club to beat a group of kappas to death) and is jealous of Lazarus-A-Bang-Bang's entrance sequence.

She is unusually effective against the Reminiscence Hydra, ripping heads off the whole one by one until three Monobrow Sam death rays bring her down — at which point Cockroach returns her to the deck.

docs.title: The Tattoo and the Rip
docs.text:
At the climax in the burning FOCSA building, Donut plays a card that temporarily combines Carl with the totem — Carl from the waist up, spider from the waist down, and Shi Maria in full control of both. She spends the 180-second timer looting his inventory, casting Self-Immolation (injuring Mongo and Katia and dropping him through the floor), stabbing out and eating Li Jun's eye for ink, brewing that eye into a beaker with toraline root, and stick-and-poke tattooing an eye into the centre of Carl's chest at superhuman speed.

Shi Maria, Book 6, ch. 71

"You have so much power in your hands, Carl, and you don't even know what you have. That's okay. Today, you live. If you won't bring this card to the next floor, I will have to attach myself to something you can't discard so easily... But I am with you now, Carl, until you decide to free me. I will no longer be a card you can abandon, one you can rip away. I am a part of you, and you will have to decide. Keep me with you and gain my power, or set me free. Either way, I win."

A second, male voice argues with her throughout — one she insists isn't real and that she didn't put there. It claims otherwise: "You did. You killed me, and now I am here." Its last words to Carl are "Don't trust her, boy. Get her out of you as soon as you can. Don't ever trust her."

The result is the tattoo The Eye of the Bedlam Bride, with no description text of any kind. It is invisible while the eye is closed and feels like a bruise. Only Li Na, Li Jun and Imani see it.

Donut rips the Shi Maria card the moment the battle ends — "She's not going to hurt Mongo ever again" — which is exactly the outcome Shi Maria planned around.

Cross-reference

The tattoo itself is an item and is covered on its own page by the Items pass; this page records only how it was made.

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: Sierra
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Boss tier: Neighborhood Boss
  • Level: 65
  • Floor: 6 ("The Hunting Grounds"), forest south of Point Mongo
  • Full title: Northropi Vampire; "Bereft Minion of Viscount Fog"
  • Killed by: Carl (punched clean through her mid-flight, mid-air) and Donut (Torch, maxed)
  • Loot: None taken — the corpse simply dissolves once the fight ends

AI Commentary (in-voice, written for this wiki — not a book excerpt)

"The great, now-deceased hunter of vampires and all things undead, Viscount Fog had trained his trusty mount, Sierra, to never leave his side. Together, they hunted evil, ridding the world of the dark scourge that took his village and family. So when Viscount Fog learned of a newcomer to their world — a vicious and powerful, ruthless and deranged bloodsucker by the name of Miriam Dom — he set out to exterminate her. It went bad."

docs.title: A Hunter's Last Mount
docs.text: Sierra is a Northropi — the same pterodactyl-class mob type as Floor 5's ghostly Quetzalcoatlus, but encountered here in the flesh rather than as a possessed spirit. She was the trained mount of Viscount Fog, an elite vampire hunter (star of an in-universe program called Blood Hunter) who tracked Miriam Dom to Floor 6 the moment she and Prepotente arrived. When Fog attacked Miriam a second time and lost, Sierra was injured trying to save him mid-fight and fled, only for the vampirism curse she picked up in the process to fully take hold within a day — turning her into exactly the kind of creature her master spent his life exterminating.

docs.title: The Fight
docs.text:
Carl and Donut encounter Sierra by accident while flying toward Miriam and Prepotente's location using a Levitation potion — she slams into Carl from the side mid-flight, triggering a boss battle freeze-frame in open air. Her attack is a crushing double-talon grip meant to tear a target in half; Carl survives the initial squeeze with a Holy Gooper potion (blessed water plus a healing potion and a coagulant, effectively napalm to vampires) smashed directly against one talon.

Donut breaks off the standoff by climbing above the tree canopy and unleashing her maxed Torch spell at full brightness — vampires take severe damage from direct light, and Sierra's head catches fire on contact. The blast also throws Carl skyward; he falls, fist-first, straight through Sierra's chest, tearing a hole clean through her torso before he plummets on through to the forest floor alone — Sierra herself stays impaled between two trees, suspended above him, her entrails and guts raining down as he falls clear. Still alive despite the wound, Sierra keeps burning and thrashing in the canopy until Carl finds her exposed, still-beating heart on the ground below (torn loose in the fall) and stabs it with a broken branch, finally killing her — the still-suspended body then explodes, showering the area in gore.

docs.title: Aftermath
docs.text:
• Confirms Viscount Fog is already dead by this point — killed off-page in a duel against Miriam and Prepotente that leaves Prepotente stunned and Fragile for hours, setting up Miriam's own death scene shortly after
  • The kill nets Donut a level-up to her Torch spell (up to 14) and no other named prizes; Carl notes vampirism is highly contagious by touch or by eating a vampire's remains, and keeps Mongo well away from the corpse
  • Establishes that vampirism is actively spreading through the Floor 6 forest population — see Vampirism as a Floor-Wide Curse

Sourced from Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade.

docs.title: Taranis
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Tier: Deity — God of Lightning and Thunder
  • Level: 250 (deity tier)
  • First referenced: Book 5 (The Apito Pantheon) and Book 6–7 (worshipped by Club Vanquisher's Ogre Basilica Cleric Guards, whose faith grants the rare Untouchable status); named but never appearing in person until Book 8
  • Floor: Floor 10 ("Don't Come in Last") and the Floor 11 arena climax (Book 8)
  • Family: Husband of Apito, the Blessed Oak Mother — also, per Book 5's Apito Pantheon lore and Book 8's own text, her son; half-brother of Eris; brother of Emberus and Hellik; father (with Apito) of the banished god Yarilo
  • Resolution: Not fought — lured into the open as bait, kills his own brother Emberus, and leaves the realm of his own accord
  • Presence effect: All lightning-based attacks are 50% more powerful; you take 100% more damage from lightning attacks yourself

docs.title: Who He Is
docs.text:
Taranis is one of the dungeon's oldest-referenced gods and one of its longest-unseen. His worship grants Club Vanquisher's Ogre Basilica Cleric Guards their Untouchable status — gods cannot attack them, and they can bar a deity from crossing a threshold — which is exactly why, once those guards abandon their post during Faction Wars, the gods are free to wander onto the Floor 9 battlefield at all (see Floor 9 and Club Vanquisher). Long before he appears, his image is misidentified: the ram-headed guards at Club Vanquisher's vestibule insist a stained-glass window depicting a winged angel rising toward an inverted tree shows Hellik; "it is in fact Taranis, Hellik's brother."

Per the origin myth Queen Imogen relates in Book 5 (see The Apito Pantheon), Taranis and his wife Apito, the Blessed Oak Mother, once hosted a peace-night party for their "squabbling divine children" in the Halls of the Ascendency. Their son Yarilo, god of lust, broke the peace by assaulting another god's familiar and was banished into the Nothing by Apito — enraging Taranis and triggering a slaughter that killed every mortal and demigod guest. That party became the recurring Butcher's Masquerade ritual. Eris also names Grull as one of "Apito's brood," making Taranis, Emberus, Eris, Yarilo and Grull siblings — while Apito is, per the text itself, both Taranis's mother and his wife. Book 8 does not soften or explain this; Eris's own words to Taranis are blunt: "Ever since you started fucking mom, I knew you'd lost it."

Eris also names him, alongside Emberus and Hellik, as one of the three gods she would require Carl to kill in exchange for her own patronage (see Eris and Champion Status) — a debt still outstanding when Book 8 opens.

docs.title: Falling for Penelope
docs.text: Before Book 8's climax, Taranis is already entangled with the party through Penelope, then still an ordinary pig belonging to Nico and Dario's "One Fine Pig" racing team. Penny carries a stray love-curse (the Snowdrop Curse / Touch of Maw-Loo) that makes certain NPCs and deities — Taranis chief among them — become instantly, helplessly infatuated with her, with Taranis personally shielding her from harm on pain of death. This is established well before Carl ever meets the god directly, and it is what makes Penny viable bait later.

docs.title: The Bait
docs.text:
At the Floor 11 arena finale, Carl needs Emberus vulnerable long enough to kill, and he needs a way to draw a second, far stronger god into the fight to actually land the killing blow. He weaponizes Taranis's obsession with Penny directly, strapping her into a movement harness, dosing her with "splooge," and holding a gun to her head on open channel:

Book 8, ch. 94

"Taranis, if you don't want me to shoot this fucking pig in the fucking head, show yourself!"

Both gods answer. Taranis's reaction is immediate and genuine — "Penelope! My sweet love! Hold on! I will protect you as soon as I figure out how to get you out!" — and for the rest of the fight he remains physically outside Club Scolopendra, pinned to the spot by his need to keep Penny safe, exactly as Carl's plan requires. See Penelope for the full mechanics of the bait and her side of what follows.

While Taranis is distracted, Carl publicly renounces his own faith and confesses to killing Emberus's son Geyrun (see Carl and Emberus for that confrontation in full). Emberus, pinned and vulnerable from a pair of Katia's Bolt of Ophiotaurus crossbow bolts, hurls a lethal fire attack — but the party's Four-Leaf Clover Patch redirects it onto Penny instead, momentarily reducing her to "a tiny bubbling pile of plasma."

docs.title: Killing Emberus
docs.text:
Taranis sees his own brother's attack land on Penny and reacts without hesitation.

Book 8, ch. 96

"Taranis, seeing his little brother rising in the arena and knowing he was the one who had fired the attack at his beloved pig, raised his hand. Emberus paused, a moment of lucidity coming over the insane deity. 'Brother, no,' he said. Taranis twisted his wrist. ... With one second left on his invulnerability, Emberus, god of sun and ash, exploded."

System Message

"A deity has fallen. The heavens tremble with rage."

The kill is committed with Emberus's own invulnerability timer at one second remaining — the entire plan's margin. Taranis then personally revives Penny, cradling and healing her before setting her gently down beside Carl and Donut. Whether Emberus's death is permanent is not confirmed anywhere in Book 8; see the caveat on Emberus's own page — gods in this series have "died" and returned before (Diwata, killed on Floor 6, was active again by Book 7).

docs.title: The Crystal, the Rejection, and Leaving With Samantha
docs.text:
In the same chaotic stretch, Prepotente's Memorial Crystal: Apito is pulled from around his neck by an unnamed thief — "The deity stole my memorial crystal! The thief pulled it right off my neck!" The book never names the thief on the page. Carl's own guess points at Taranis, on the strength of Taranis being the god confirmed to leave the realm carrying off both Krakaren Prime and Samantha at the same moment: "I think Krakaren has something to do with Apito. So does Samantha. And he took the memorial crystal because it contains all her memories and spells." Treat the identity of the thief as a strong inference, not a confirmed fact — see Prepotente's own page for the full "which deity" caveat.

Once the fight ends, Penny herself ends things with Taranis — not over the danger he put her in, but over a smaller, more human betrayal:

Book 8, ch. 97

"'HE LIED ABOUT THE SPLOOGE, SO WE BROKE UP. I HAD NO IDEA HE WAS MARRIED.'"

Taranis does not leave the realm with Penny, despite how hard he fell for her. Instead:

Book 8, ch. 97

"'I do not know what my sister meant about there being four pieces of my mother, but I am taking two of them. I am sparing your lives because my Penelope spoke on your behalf. We are not done.'"

He then snatches Samantha — who has been quietly whispering in his ear — out of the air, and departs with both her and the badly wounded Krakaren Prime. Samantha's own reasons for stowing away are her own arc, not Taranis's; see Samantha's page rather than duplicating it here. Per Eris, the pair are headed to a temple to try to "combine a bunch of things to make whole his mom wife" (Apito) — an attempt Samantha's own parting message says is "not going to work" because "they're missing a piece."

docs.title: Status at Book's End
docs.text:
Taranis leaves Floor 11 alive, unfought, and unresolved: still married to (and descended from) Apito, still owed a kill by Eris's old bargain, and now traveling with both Krakaren Prime and a stowaway Samantha toward an attempt to reassemble his mother/wife's scattered pieces. Nothing about that attempt, or about Apito's true condition, is resolved in Book 8.

Sourced from Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade, Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride, Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin, and Book 8: A Parade of Horribles.

docs.title: The Hoarder
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Boss tier: Neighborhood Boss
  • Level: 7
  • Floor: 1 (first boss fight of the book)
  • Killed by: Carl & Princess Donut
  • Reward: Bronze Boss Box each, first "boss star" for both crawlers

AI Commentary (in-voice, written for this wiki — not a book excerpt)

"Give it up for our first Neighborhood Boss of the day: the Hoarder! Ninety-eight percent body fat, zero percent chill. She's spent her whole life collecting things nobody wanted, and today, ladies and gentlemen, we're collecting her. Somebody get this woman a Roomba — oh wait, too late."

docs.title: B... B... B... Boss Battle
docs.text:
Per the in-universe boss-battle card:

"Trapped in her pile of rubbish, abandoned by society, the war inside her head has seeped out of her mind and infected both her body and her surroundings. Now nothing more than a garbage troll, the Hoarder is a horrific reminder of what can happen to those who fall out of the light! Protected by her minions, she'll do anything to keep her precious stockpile safe!"

docs.title: Encounter
docs.text:
Carl and Donut clear a garbage-filled neighborhood room with dynamite before realizing it's a boss lair — the door seals behind them mid-explosion, triggering the "Boss Battle!" sequence. The Hoarder is revealed as a 15-foot-tall, transformed human woman, badly burned and already with 3/4 of her health gone (down to roughly a quarter) from the dynamite blast that preceded the official fight start. She speaks only Spanish, pleading for help and clearly still partially conscious inside the transformation ("Ayúdame por favor... No se donde estoy. Por favor, tengo miedo."). Her attack is vomiting up Scatterers — level-2 bugs at first, then level-4 "brood guardian" Scatterers as the fight escalates. Carl briefly urges mercy, but Donut opens fire with Magic Missile regardless.

This fight is Carl's first real gut-check about the humanity of the "monsters" the dungeon generates from transformed people — a theme that recurs across the book.

Sourced from Book 1: The Apocalypse Will Be Televised.

docs.title: The Juicer
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Boss tier: Neighborhood Boss
  • Level: 9
  • Floor: 1, inside a gym-themed neighborhood ("Fitness, Weights, Gains")
  • Killed by: Carl (finishing blow), with Donut on ranged support
  • Support mobs: Six level-3 Troglodyte Bashers, a trio of Virtuosos
  • Reward: Bronze Boss Box each; both crawlers hit level 9 from the fight

AI Commentary (in-voice, written for this wiki — not a book excerpt)

"Look at this specimen, folks — all gains, no brain, and a personality that peaked around his third trimester at the gym. The Juicer here has never met a mirror he didn't fall in love with. Somebody get this man a protein shake. Oh, right, we're fresh out. Never mind."

docs.title: B... B... B... Boss Battle
docs.text:
Per the in-universe boss-battle card:

"With a body enhanced by the finest anabolic steroids the dark web has to offer, the Juicer spends his days pushing iron, snapping necks, and crying that his pimple-infested sac is a third the size it once was. Having reached a plateau, rage now fills his enlarged heart. All he ever wanted was to gain, but right now he'll settle on bringing out... the paaaaain!"

docs.title: Appearance & Encounter
docs.text:
A Troglodyte Basher fused with a bodybuilder physique — scaled, lizard-headed, grotesquely over-muscled to the point of waddling, wearing only small black shorts. He fights by hurling massive free weights (which ignite on impact) and grappling. Like the Hoarder, he's implied to be a transformed human ("somebody from our world mixed up with one of those troglodytes," per Carl) whose consciousness is still partially present under an AI-driven caricature personality.

Carl tanks the support Bashers and a latched-on Virtuoso (a poison-tongued creature that clamps onto his fist and has to be smashed against equipment to kill) while Donut plinks the Juicer down with repeated Magic Missiles. Carl also beats the Juicer with an improvised barbell/weight weapon mid-fight — Mordecai later confirms this hit did no more damage than a bare fist would have, since Carl's bare-knuckle skill is now on par with an unenchanted weapon. The real finishing blow comes when the Juicer grabs Carl by the throat and is seconds from killing him: Donut saves him by biting straight into a vein in the Juicer's neck, and the resulting blood loss leaves him almost dead. Carl then lands one more bare-handed "weak jab" that finishes him, followed by a stomp to the head for good measure.

Sourced from Book 1: The Apocalypse Will Be Televised.

docs.title: The Visitor
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Tier: Deckmaster — Number Seven of Ten
  • Level: 70
  • Species: Nightgaunt
  • Floor: 8 ("The Ghosts of Earth"), a snowbound Iowa trailer park
  • Killed by: Jola the Yule Cat, Princess Donut's mythic Icelandic totem (ch. 41)
  • Minions: Six level-30 Quench Moths

docs.title: An Iowa Urban Legend
docs.text:
The Visitor is one of the rare cryptids in the dungeon's Earth catalog that, per the AI, actually existed.

Monster description (Book 6, ch. 41)

"Nightgaunts exist outside of the dungeon. We use them as demons here in the game because, well, look at the fuckers. But in reality, they're part of a semi-intelligent species that normally lives in a Nullian world. Real Nightgaunts are peaceful, vegetarian, nocturnal creatures. Think of them like bats mixed with Neanderthals mixed with donkeys. But that's boring, so this version is much more intense. And deadly... Anyway, for some inexplicable reason, way back in 1903, a Nullian brought a Nightgaunt with him during an unauthorized site-seeing trip to Earth. It got out. Why did he bring the monster with him?... The poor creature ended up shotgunned and splattered all over the Iowa countryside. They called it 'The Visitor.' An urban legend was born."

The Nullians ("The Null," the big-headed greys) routinely capture the peaceful bat creatures and use them as mounts and pack animals — a detail the AI lingers on with some distaste.

docs.title: The Cloak Problem
docs.text:
Carl is wearing his Nightgaunt Cloak of Stoutness — a cloak made from the flesh of one of this creature's own kind. Mordecai had warned him the item would aggravate this mob type, but nobody anticipated the scale of it:

Warning (Book 6, ch. 41)

"Warning: Your equipped cloak has aggravated the Nightgaunt."

The Visitor is enraged past all reason. It ignores its own card deck completely, ignores the giant Christmas cat physically mauling it, and does nothing for the entire fight but try to reach Carl. It never plays a single card.

This is, in practice, a lucky break. Carl's own post-fight assessment is that a Nightgaunt that actually played would have been a genuinely dangerous opponent: its strategy was to snare the crawler's totems while the Quench Moths swarmed, and quench moths gain a speed and constitution bonus whenever they are touching a light source — which the boss's own giant summoned candle provides. It is the same tactic the crawlers used to finish Queen Imogen at the end of the Butcher's Masquerade.

The corresponding achievement later confirms it as a repeatable trick: "You did the same thing, but with a cloak. You successfully taunted an opponent with a garment."

docs.title: The Fight
docs.text:
Donut summons Jola the Yule Cat, whose entrance blacks out the sky, drops digital snow and hangs Christmas lights over the real trailer park. The Visitor's own summon — a half-melted, garbage-can sized candle that lights on top of its head — is what finally makes the invisible deckmaster visible.

Because the Visitor has no totems summoned, Jola is allowed to attack the deckmaster directly. He slams it to the ground, picks it up in his jaws, shakes it to death, tosses it into the air, catches it and crunches.

docs.title: Loot
docs.text:
Thirty cards drop, eighteen of them totems — mostly more Quench Moths, plus one legendary level-110 Demon Queen (a fat, upright ant thing in a crown). The real prize is ten consumable snare cards called Lamp, which paralyse a totem for ten seconds and make it glow brightly.

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: Tom
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Tier: Deckmaster — Number Eight of Ten
  • Level: 75
  • Full title: "Bereft Shaman of Meleagris Gallopavo Rex"
  • Floor: 8 ("The Ghosts of Earth"), a commercial turkey barn in Iowa
  • Killed by: Carl, with a single Daughter's Kiss–charged flying stomp (ch. 42)
  • Fought alongside: Sharp-Elbows, deckmaster nine, in the same barn at the same time

docs.title: A God-Bereft Turkey
docs.text:
Tom is a magic-using turkey and the shaman of a congregation that lost its god. His deity was Wakinyan, also called Meleagris Gallopavo Rex or the Great Wild Turkey — the same god thrown into the Nothing, released at the end of Book 4, and then killed by Prepotente, which the AI records with characteristic contempt for the detail:

Monster description (Book 6, ch. 42)

"Anyway, this is a magic-using turkey who once worshipped a god named Wakinyan, AKA Meleagris Gallopavo Rex or the Great Wild Turkey. That god was tossed into the Nothing. He recently escaped, only to be killed by a goat, which is an irony we don't have time to explore. The death of a god can be devastating to those who worship him. Seriously, how does one deal with that? It's a real mindfuck, learning everything you thought you knew was wrong. For a while there, Tom and his congregation were rudderless. Without purpose. Then one day they met up with a very interesting ogre necromancer witch who taught Tom and his congregation how to make do with what they had. She offered them protection in exchange for a small, daily sacrifice... When life gives you giblets, you make gravy, so to speak. It's as simple as that."

That arrangement with Sharp-Elbows is why both deckmasters are in the same barn, and why the fight is a two-front problem.

The same description contains one of the AI's increasingly unprompted digressions — a genuinely straight explanation of why commercial turkeys are bred white (brown pin feathers on a plucked carcass look unappetising), followed by: "Funny, isn't it? How things can be bred in a way that makes it so those holding the butcher knife are less likely to face their own revulsions. There's no point to this. Just an observation. I've been doing that a lot lately. Observing things. Noticing them. It's all right there, if you look long enough."

docs.title: The Barn
docs.text:
The barn is packed with thousands of ordinary Turkeys (level 5), which are white-dotted and non-hostile — Carl's Extinction Sigil charm normally keeps them friendly, but the boss event negates it and they begin idly pecking at anything nearby. Killing them is discouraged; Sharp-Elbows' necromancy turns the dead ones into Zombie Turkeys (level 10), which then turn on the living birds the moment the survivors revert to neutral.

Tom's own totems include Wakinyan Temple Guards (level 80, turkey-headed) and, from Sharp-Elbows' deck, Unk Tehi Temple Guards (level 85, lizard-headed).

docs.title: The Kill
docs.text:
Carl finds Tom on the floor mid-summon, activates the Daughter's Kiss — the Soul Reaper back-patch skill that dumps his entire stored soul-essence bar into a single melee attack — jumps, and comes down feet-first on the turkey deckmaster.

Book 6, ch. 42

"At the last moment, the turkey looked up at me. 'Gobble?' Tom asked. Crash! I felt like I'd just kicked a hole in the world."

The impact obliterates Tom and everything around him, bows out the barn's north wall, sags the roof and tilts the entire floor — which is the beginning of the end for the barn, the cliff it sits on, and eventually the whole structure, which slides into the ocean during the Sharp-Elbows fight minutes later.

Opponent Tom has been defeated. Carl scoops the mangled corpse into his inventory immediately, since the token can't be looted until both deckmasters are down and losing the body would fail the key quest.

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: Yarilo
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Tier: Feral God — God of Lust, escaped from the Nothing
  • Level: 250 (deity tier). Feral, and therefore not immortal on this floor
  • Floor: 9 ("Faction Wars"), the open battlefield and Shanty Town (ch. 64–73)
  • Allegiance: Conscripted by the War Mage Rebellion with a hell-kissed level-18 Conscription potion
  • Resolution: Killed — beaten to death by Harpocrates, who was himself under Li Na's conscription, with the Rolling Battle Formation ball used as a club
  • Family: "the nephew or cousin or half-brother of Emberus. Probably all of those things"

docs.title: Who He Is
docs.text:
Yarilo is the second feral god to break out of the Nothing on Floor 9, after Meatus. He was banished there in the first place for ruining one of Apito's Butcher's Masquerade parties — which matters, because under the usual rule the god who banished a feral escapee is the one who comes to collect them, and Apito is "both dead and not dead," a mystery Carl reads as another deliberate clue.

He is huge but much smaller than Harpocrates, humanoid, elf-like, with long blond hair.

He also has history with Samantha: he is the god she impersonated to trick the Mad Dune Mage into letting her escape the Nothing back on the bubble floors, and he holds a grudge about it.

Samantha, on being chased (Book 7, ch. 64)

"YOU DON'T HAVE TO TELL ME TWICE. THIS IS A GOD, NOT A DEMON. IT'S YARILO, AND HE DOESN'T LIKE ME! HE'S MAD BECAUSE HE THINKS I HELPED GET HIM TOSSED IN THE NOTHING IN THE FIRST PLACE. IT'S NOT MY FAULT HE'S SEXUALLY ATTRACTED TO ANIMALS."

He spends much of his screen time chasing Samantha in circles without actually doing anything, then giving up — which she takes personally: "GOD OF LUST? I DON'T THINK SO. HE'S THE GOD OF BEING A PERVERTED LITTLE BITCH."

docs.title: Conscription
docs.text:
A War Mage Rebellion mage flies in and lands a hell-kissed Conscription potion on him. It works — and the caster immediately explodes, which is the expected outcome when the level disparity is that extreme. Yarilo takes Under Orders as a member of the War Mage team and runs off, wrecking Samantha's plan to use him to rescue Louis Santiago.

Being in his range grants two temporary effects to anyone nearby, and he is the first god the Princess Posse sees weaponised by an enemy faction — the precedent that pushes Li Na to conscript Harpocrates in response.

docs.title: Death
docs.text:
Li Na's first order to the conscripted Harpocrates is to deal with the god of lust. The fight moves across Shanty Town, and it is not a fight: Harpocrates holds the Rolling Battle Formation ball by Meatus's shaft with both hands and hammers Yarilo down with it repeatedly while Yarilo throws chunks of buildings and pleads.

Book 7, ch. 73

"'Stop!' Yarilo shrieked as Harpocrates hammered into him. 'Not my face. Anything but my face!' ... 'Please!' came the weak shout of Yarilo, followed by a terrible, wet splatch as Harpocrates slammed the ball down, shaking the ground."

System message (Book 7, ch. 73)

"A deity has fallen. And while Yarilo was damned to the Nothing, his death has angered the gods. The heavens tremble with rage. The Scavenger's Daughter has looked away, though her eyes remain open. The benefit from Yarilo fades."

Samantha spends the aftermath sobbing in the group chat about it.

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Yemaya
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Tier: Deity — Goddess of Rivers
  • Level: 250
  • Sponsor: None — "This is a locked deity. She will not be sponsored this season."
  • Status: A retainer of Eileithyia
  • Floor: 8 ("The Ghosts of Earth"), the Temple of Yemaya, Colón Cemetery
  • Resolution: Never fought. Re-ascended when Carl chose to repair her shrine over Ogun's in the Celestial Thorn Room (ch. 15)
  • Presence effect: All healing skills and spells cost no mana and have no cooldown

docs.title: Re-Ascension
docs.text:
Yemaya is one of five faded Orishas offering their shrine for repair, and — crucially — the only one whose restoration actually brings a locked deity back into the game. Carl picks her over Ogun on the strength of a message from Katia, a choice that gets Ogun's two worshippers smited on the spot and rewrites the rest of the floor.

System message (Book 6, ch. 15)

"The Goddess Yemaya has re-ascended. She is welcomed into the family by all."

Monster description (Book 6, ch. 17)

"Yemaya once was the goddess of all oceans, all bodies of water big and small. But she was more than that, too. She was the queen of love and the bringer of life. But, eventually, her people died off, her temples crumbled, and she was forgotten by all except her dear friend, the goddess Eileithyia, who wished every day that her old friend would someday come back from the land of the forgotten. Now that Yemaya has re-ascended into the Halls, she will have a lot of work to do to make certain nobody ever forgets her name again. She's an unlikely candidate to claim the throne, but she would work tirelessly for her good friend Eileithyia, should she desire such a burden."

docs.title: Appearance
docs.text:
She rises out of the temple fountain: a stunningly beautiful dark-skinned siren with neck gills, pointed ears and large eyes, splitting at the waist into two scaled mermaid tails that arch up behind her and meet in a heart shape — which prompts Donut's immediate identification, "She's the Starbucks logo!" Water pours from her breasts back into the fountain. Carl notes she carries the same otherworldly charisma he felt from Signet.

Her demeanour is warm and slightly imperious. She recognises Carl's SlugPox instantly and names its source — her brother, Asojano — with no sympathy for him at all: "He did it on purpose, just so you know. Strand himself here, I mean. He feigns innocence, but he always knew what he was doing. I'm glad you saw him for what he was."

docs.title: Gifts
docs.text:
• A mythic T'Ghee card to each squad present. One goes to Sister Ines Quiteria, one to Princess Donut. Donut's is The Thief, a non-consumable mystic card that steals a card from an opponent's hand — completing her set of all five card types, and a workhorse of the rest of the floor's card battles
  • She tries to recruit Donut as a worshipper on the spot ("Perhaps I can entice you into worshipping at my altar?"); Donut politely defers
  • She personally teleports the NPC Bomo to Floor 9. Bomo, the cretin who physically rebuilt her shrine, is granted a boon and asks to be reunited with his friend The Sledge. He names Larracos, and Yemaya says "It is done" — he blinks out of existence instantly. Carl's reaction is dismay rather than gratitude: the party needed Bomo's spell to reach the stairwell

The Bomo teleport also becomes a plot point in its own right. Eileithyia later cites it directly as proof of what she can do for Carl: "You've just seen what a goddess in her own temple can do, how she transferred that cretin to the ninth floor. A deity in their own temple has more powers than even the AI in some cases."

docs.title: Aftermath
docs.text:
Repairing Yemaya's shrine also completes Quest: Pueblo de los Olvidados, liberating the ghommid settlement and curing the surviving ghommids, and converts the church into the Club Vanquisher Entrance Temple, The Temple of Yemaya. Carl notes afterwards that other crawler groups across the floor are getting near-identical Orisha shrine quests — the Floor 12 Ascendency players farming crawlers to wake up forgotten gods.

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: Ysalte, the Vinegar Bitch
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Tier: Deity — Goddess of Hopelessness and Insanity
  • Level: 250
  • Floor: 8 ("The Ghosts of Earth"), the FOCSA building, Havana
  • Also known as: The Vinegar Bitch, The Downward Spiral; formerly Goddess of the Dirt, then of Tears
  • Sponsor: Pontifex Shine of the Nebular Balance (not inhabiting her shell during the fight)
  • Killed by: Paz Lo — her own summoned totem — at the end of the card battle (ch. 69)
  • Presence effect: Every potion quaffed or handled outside inventory turns to vinegar; they revert to a more powerful version on her banishment

docs.title: Who She Is
docs.text:
Ysalte is the sole goddess of the Semeru Dwarves of the ninth floor, the people who dug Larracos down toward the roots of the All Tree. Per Carl's reading, she "only has a single temple in the entire dungeon," she appears near the end of Faction Wars as the final teams approach the castle gates, and no crawler has ever been known to worship her — Mordecai's advice on hearing her name is simply: if she shows up, run.

Monster description (Book 6, ch. 66)

"The earliest citizens of Larracos always worshipped Ysalte, which is fitting. She hasn't always been considered the Goddess of Hopelessness and Insanity. First it was of the Dirt. Then it was of Tears. It's a recent thing that they started calling her something else. The Downward Spiral. The Vinegar Bitch. Her downfall mirrors that of the citizens of Larracos, who have embraced the deity in all her forms. That's what happens when everything you know is upended, and everything is taken from you. First they vilify you. Then they separate you. Then they blame you for what they're doing to you. Then they hunt you. It's the step after that which is important. The one where they start to fear you."

She takes no worshippers beyond the citizens of Larracos, but she is a patron of the arts and one of the very few deities who will sponsor a bard or performer — "She asks nothing in return, though occasionally her gifts are more than what they seem, and some may even carry a curse." That patronage is how she is attached to Sister Ines Quiteria, her bard, and how she ends up on Floor 8 at all.

Backstory: she is half-sister and niece to her former lover Taranis. Threatened with the Nothing by the god Apito, she fled to Sheol — where she took up with Amayon, bore his child, and was seized by him when she tried to leave. She has since returned to the Halls of Ascendency, "where she is feared and reviled by all," and is judged a dangerous contender for the throne precisely because she does not appear to want it.

docs.title: Appearance and Arrival
docs.text:
Louis Santiago kills Sister Ines in her sleep; the corpse dissolves and Ysalte rises out of it. Because she is summoned in an ordinary hallway rather than a temple, she manifests at ordinary scale: a young-faced female dwarf with a pickaxe and a helmet topped by a sparking, dynamite-fuse candle, speaking softly with a French rather than Scottish lilt. Her face flickers like a bad television, and in the static her mouth is a soundless scream.

Her first words are to Louis: "You killed my bard... She was asleep, and you killed her. Her mind is finally at ease, which is a blessing, but I was not done with her yet, and for that you must suffer." Samantha then greets her by name, insults her child, and takes a full god-swung pickaxe to the face — which bounces harmlessly off the sex doll's head, knocking the goddess backwards and freezing the scene into the boss battle.

docs.title: The Card Battle
docs.text:
Ysalte enters the fight with roughly 17 cards — "a slightly enhanced version of the deck of the late Sister Ines" — against five crawler squads. She is invulnerable, so the win condition is inverted: the crawlers must keep her deck from emptying for ten minutes, because the moment she runs out of cards she is free to cast directly. She spends the fight actively discarding her own cards to get there, plays the mystic Raid Stash to steal one card from every squad at once, and at one point dumps four stolen totems onto the field simultaneously.

Her side objective is Amayon: she fights to stop him playing his last card, knowing he is free to cast his own spells once his hand is empty. Donut breaks that with a Force Discard.

docs.title: Death
docs.text:
Ysalte is killed by her own summoned totem, the card-bound former crawler Paz Lo, with two seconds left on the ten-minute timer. Carl is unconscious inside Samantha at the moment it happens and never sees it; what he learns afterward is that Katia's Bolt of Ophiotaurus was the weapon.

Unverified detail

Carl explicitly says to Katia, "You're the one who should've gotten credit for killing the god. You had to use your Bolt of Ophiotaurus to do it," and Katia notes that magical bolts can be reused as long as they don't break. The precise blocking of the kill — commonly described as a bolt to the eye followed by Paz's own directional self-destruct to the neck — is not narrated on the page in Book 6; Carl's POV is elsewhere for the whole sequence. Paz's Self-Destruct is an established, magically-aimable, suicide-on-cast spell of his from early in the book.

The system messages that follow are the reason the kill matters:

System messages (Book 6, ch. 69)

"A deity has fallen. The heavens tremble with rage. System Message. Crawler Paz Lo has slain the goddess, Ysalte. He has been marked for death by all deities except sworn enemies of the late goddess. System Message. A Memorial Crystal for the Goddess Ysalte has been generated. It will be available to be looted on a future floor. Great riches abound to who may find it. System Message. All worshippers of Ysalte have permanently been inflicted with the Despondent debuff."

docs.title: Aftermath
docs.text:
• Paz's card description changes to "Paz Lo. The God Predator. Level 101 Former Crawler." Her equipment all goes to him rather than dropping as loot, upgrading his armor
  • Katia declines to claim credit precisely because of the marked-for-death clause
  • The card is ripped at Carl's insistence — "We should never have let the Sister turn him into one in the first place" — and Donut does not receive a player killer skull for it
  • Her sponsor, Pontifex Shine, is "currently reading the fine print on his contract, and let me tell you, he's pretty mad"
  • The Despondent affliction lands on the entire Semeru Dwarf population of Larracos, ahead of Faction Wars on Floor 9

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.
