Chapter 1 — The Harvest

At 2:23 AM PST on January 3rd, Carl (27, ex-Coast Guard MK/marine tech, Seattle) and his ex-girlfriend Beatrice's cat Donut survive only because they're outside retrieving Donut from a tree when every roofed structure on Earth is instantly crushed. A neighbor, Mrs. Parsons, dies in front of Carl. The Syndicate/Borant Corporation announcement plays: Earth defaulted on a resource-rights appeal, and Borant has chosen "Option 3, the 18-Level World Dungeon" as the reclamation method. 150,000 Level-1 entrances open for exactly one hour, halving each level down to two entrances (one exit) on Level 18. Carl runs toward a nearby glowing entrance, Donut in his arms.

Chapter 2 — Into the Dungeon

Carl descends an ornate staircase into Floor 1 (five-day collapse timer). Achievements fire rapid-fire as the system registers him and Donut as crawlers — Donut as Crawler #4,119 (Level 1, Race Cat, Class Not yet assigned), Carl as Crawler #4,122. A Goblin Murder Dozer ambushes them in the tunnel. Carl flees, finds a hidden Tutorial Guild door, but the guildmaster Mordecai refuses entry while mobs are still nearby. Carl bare-handedly kills one goblin against the guild door while Donut sneaks inside through the cracked door.

Chapter 3 — Mordecai's Guild

Mordecai (Rat Hooligan, Level 50, Non-Combatant NPC) scolds Carl for the mess Donut made. Carl goes back out and kills the remaining goblins, narrowly escaping the Murder Dozer's boiler explosion. Mordecai begins explaining who he is: a displaced alien ("skyfowl") who reached Floor 11 generations ago in his own crawl, on his last posting before retirement. Only one crawler in history — another human, from a different world — has ever reached Floor 13, and died within 30 minutes.

Chapter 4 — The Rules of the Game

Mordecai lays out the setup: the Syndicate seeds worlds with six starter species, waits millennia, then returns; Earth defaulted on its 50-year appeal window. Borant profits from mining and from broadcasting the dungeon as an interstellar reality show to quintillions of viewers. He explains the Ratings system (Views → Followers → Favorites → Patrons), loot box tiers (Bronze through Celestial, plus rare Benefactor Boxes), Party mechanics, permanent death ("Dead is dead"), and staircase/collapse rules — and namedrops the rival Squim Conglomerate's brutal battle-royale format.

Chapter 5 — Opening the Boxes

Mordecai activates Carl's inventory (unlimited dimensional storage) and hotlist. Carl opens his 10 starting loot boxes, receiving a Toad Cudgel, a Poker, the Goblin Pass tattoo (branded onto his forearm), the Enchanted Nightgaunt Cloak of Stoutness and Enchanted Trollskin Shirt of Pummeling, the Enchanted Toe Ring of the Splatter Skunk, and finally an Enhanced Pet Biscuit — which Donut impulsively eats herself, dissolving into a quivering blob with a "Waiting..." status.

Chapter 6 — Suiting Up

While waiting on Donut, Carl equips his new gear and discovers an old arcade Frogger high score buried in his exhaustive skills list. Donut then wakes from her blob state — talking.

Chapter 7 — Donut Wakes Up Talking

Donut demands to be addressed by her full title, "GC, BWR, NW Princess Donut the Queen Anne Chonk." Her transformed stats come with a permanent buff granting bonus Strength/Intelligence/Charisma every level with no manual allocation. She receives a self-taught Tome of Magic Missile and, from a Legendary box, the Enchanted Crown of the Sepsis Whore — a Fleeting/Unique item that irrevocably enrolls her in the royal line of succession for the Blood Sultanate on Floor 9. She puts it on anyway because it's purple. She renames the party "The Royal Court of Princess Donut," crowning herself "Grand Champion Best in Dungeon" and dubbing Carl her "Royal Bodyguard."

Chapter 8 — First Blood

Leaving the guild, Mordecai gives Carl a cryptic parting warning about Floor 12. Wandering the tunnels, Donut admits she remembers her whole cat life and noticed Carl considering "catnapping" her instead of returning her to Beatrice's family. They kill a lava-spitting Bad Llama, then fight through rats and Scatterer cockroaches — Carl levels up, gaining the Foot Soldier and Smush skills (the game's recurring foot-fetish joke). They discover every dungeon "bathroom" leads to the same identical stall.

Chapter 9 — The Safe Room and Tally

They find a Safe Room built from an intact Polish fast-food restaurant, complete with playground. Screens show the collapse countdown and a remaining-crawler count already cratering from 10 million to ~4.3 million. They meet Tally, a Bopca Protector who cooks Carl an incredible meal and calls Donut "Your Highness." They decide to base out of this room and clear a nearby Scatterer nest for experience.

Chapter 10 — Grinding Scatterers

After sleeping and showering, they clear a Scatterer Brood Guardian and roughly two dozen more Scatterers, hitting Level 5, before reaching a locked, garbage-smelling door marked with a health-department warning sign.

Chapter 11 — Dynamite in the Dark

Carl tosses dynamite into the dark room beyond the door, badly injuring himself — and triggering a boss encounter. The Hoarder (Level 7 Neighborhood Boss) emerges: a 15-foot-tall transformed woman, pleading in Spanish, vomiting up Scatterers as an attack. Carl chokes her with a found chain while Donut fires Magic Missiles; he finishes her off bare-handed.

Chapter 12 — The Boss Tier Lesson

At a nearby guild, a hungover Mordecai explains the boss tier ladder (Neighborhood, Borough, City, Province, Country, Floor, plus rarer "Elites") and that boss kills grant a permanent star and a tier-matched Boss Box. Carl receives the Tome of Wisp Armor (handed to Donut, since his mana pool can't cover its cost) and his first leg armor, the Enchanted Spiked Kneepads of the Shade Gnoll Riot Forces.

Chapter 13 — Rebecca W.

Investigating a marked corpse, they find fellow crawler Rebecca W., shot dead and looted down to a single apple core — "Killed by Crawler Frank Q." Realizing another crawler is murdering and robbing people, Carl decides they should hunt him down.

Chapter 14 — The Premiere

Dungeon Crawler World: Earth airs its premiere via immersive alien broadcast. A recap of the rival Squim Conglomerate's brutal format plays; Earth's own premiere frames humanity at its worst to justify the "rescue" narrative. Highlighted crawlers include the first team to kill a Borough Boss and breakout star Lucia Mar. Despite killing the Hoarder, Carl and Donut get zero screen time.

Chapter 15 — Slimes and Charm

A green slime nearly dissolves Carl's arm off — a lesson that slimes are a no-go for now. Using Carl's Goblin Pass tattoo for free passage into goblin territory, Donut discovers her absurd Charisma lets her charm and command almost any non-hostile NPC. They're led to a workshop guarded by Goblin Shamankas, including the heavily pierced Rory, whom Donut emotionally manipulates into full cooperation.

Chapter 16 — The Goblin Chopper

Donut talks the shamankas into building Carl a custom vehicle — the Goblin Copper Chopper — in trade for looted drugs. She then deliberately tips the goblins off that a rival group (the llamas) is holding drugs, triggering a "meth war" raid that empties the workshop, clearing the way to loot everything and go after the Goblin War Chieftain.

Chapter 17 — Building the Cart Bomb

They strip the abandoned workshop and build a cart bomb using a rare explosive and single-use magic detonators. They shove the loaded cart into the chieftain's sealed room, retreat, and detonate it remotely — Donut mentions, only after the trigger's pulled, that she saw goblin infants inside.

Chapter 18 — Collateral Damage

The blast kills the Goblin War Chieftain (a bronze star, Level 8, no boss card ever triggered) — but Carl is horrified to learn he's killed goblin children along with him. The workshop burns, and they flee before the raiding party returns.

Chapter 19 — You Monster

Dark-comedy achievement notifications needle Carl over the infant deaths. They fight through a Rot Sticker neighborhood to a safe room with a quirky daily "experience cookie." Loot includes an unexplained Desperado Pass tattoo for both of them and Donut's Enchanted Fae Scale Quadruped Crupper of the Fleet. Carl settles on a private mantra: "You're not going to break me."

Chapter 20 — Frank Q

During the Day 2 broadcast, Donut spots Frank Q — the crawler who killed Rebecca W. — in this same safe room. Frank claims self-defense: his ICE-agent partner Maggie was killed by human traffickers he was investigating. He stalls Carl with an offer of ill-fitting looted pants while his actual partner, Maggie My, sneaks up to ambush them both. Carl, forewarned by Mordecai's tip about safe-zone violence penalties, has already told Donut over party chat not to react. Both attackers freeze mid-attack, penalized by the safe zone's rules. Carl rigs a corpse with live explosives as a parting gift, and they flee toward the Chopper just as a daily update announces patch notes and the removal of an overtuned mob that had killed 15,000 crawlers in a day.

Chapter 21 — The Trap and the Getaway

They ride the Chopper east for hours, fighting off raccoon-headed Scat Thugs during a bathroom stop, before finally finding a "Stairs + People" sign spray-painted by another group.

Chapter 22 — Team Meadow Lark

They meet an encampment of eldercare workers — Brandon An, his near-silent brother Chris Andrews 2, CNA Yolanda Martinez 13, and swordswoman Imani C — plus the strange homeless woman Agatha. Evacuated from a Wenatchee facility when a fire coincided with the dungeon's opening, only 38 of ~250 residents remain, mostly elderly and Level 1. The only way down is through a guarded spiral maze holding an unknown, dangerous creature. Carl proposes they train up and attack it together.

Chapter 23 — Covering the Signs

Worried other crawlers might exploit the vulnerable group, Carl quietly defaces the encampment's own directional signs. He and Donut grind through a neighborhood of Troglodytes before finding the area's boss room — a gym.

Chapter 24 — The Juicer

The Juicer (Level 9 Neighborhood Boss), a steroid-caricature bodybuilder, hurls flaming weight plates in a chaotic gym fight. Carl beats him down with a barbell; the boss nearly strangles Carl to death before Donut saves him by biting through his neck vein, taking a near-fatal hit herself in the process.

Chapter 25 — Debrief and the War Gauntlet

They loot the gym and hit Level 9. Mordecai debriefs the fight, confirming Carl's bare-knuckle damage now equals an unenchanted weapon, and reinforces the "find the weak point" lesson. Loot includes the Enchanted Shuriken of Bloodlust and Carl's signature weapon, the Enchanted War Gauntlet of the Exalted Grull.

Chapter 26 — The Spiral Maze

With the floor's timer running out, the group enters the spiral maze together. The escalated "B-B-B-Boss Battle!" announcement reveals The Ball of Swine (Level 15 Borough Boss) — dozens of Tuskling nobility fused into a rolling battle-ball. Using spike strips and terrain tricks to dodge its charges, they build a modular "redoubt" fortress designed to wedge the ball against the tunnel ceiling. The redoubt traps the ball; the party stabs it open, scattering dozens of disoriented, unarmed Tusklings who are slaughtered in the chaos.

Chapter 27 — Down the Ramp

With the last Tuskling dead, they win, level up across the board, and Carl agrees to scout Floor 2 alone with Donut first. At the bottom of the transformed stairwell-ramp, instead of stepping onto Floor 2, they're unexpectedly pulled into a production trailer — plucked for a televised interview.

Chapter 28 — Plucked for TV

Associate producer Lexis explains the rules: this is a private program, Dungeon Crawler After Hours with Odette, and Carl and Donut are the only real crawlers in an otherwise holographic set. Donut preps for the interview with practiced showbiz instinct while Carl warns her "these people aren't our friends." They meet Odette, one of the galaxy's most popular talk-show hosts — a bizarre crab-bodied, insect-headed alien with an exaggeratedly human torso.

Chapter 29 — Backstage with Odette

Backstage, Odette removes her elaborate costume to reveal a legless older human woman — gear from her own crawl, worn when she reached the stairwell to Floor 13 (she never descended, having struck an unspecified "deal"). She reveals she trained Mordecai generations ago, warns Carl about a slur to avoid, tells Donut never to change from her cute cat race, and admits the loot system is deliberately rigged to keep profitable crawlers alive and in danger for ratings.

Chapter 30 — Floor Two

Carl and Donut arrive on Floor 2 — structurally similar to Floor 1, but reinforced and cracked. They fight Brindle Grubs and Danger Dingoes, and Carl adopts a strict "destroy every corpse" policy once he learns how the grub-escalation mechanic works. They find a storm-shelter safe room with a mailbox that enrolls Donut in a spellbook-of-the-month club, netting her the necromancy spell Second Chance.

Chapter 31 — The First Collapse

Floor 1 officially collapses as episode two airs; the crawler count drops by roughly 700,000 in a single tick. More Waffle House refugees join the group; Agatha goes missing and is strangely edited out of the broadcast recap despite witnesses insisting she was present. A harsh new rule debuts: public urination now summons a punishment "Rage Elemental" — foreshadowing disaster. Donut gets her first follower and starts craving the attention.

Chapter 32 — Rev-Up Consultants

With their social numbers exploded after Odette's show aired, Carl and Donut scout toward Floor 2's stairwell and encounter gambling Clurichaun Rev-Up Consultants — hillbilly-goblin creatures who turn out to be the low rung of a moonshine-company pyramid scheme.

Chapter 33 — Plan Pied Piper

Using Puddle Jumper, they infiltrate the Rev-Up filling room. Unable to charm the rank-and-file workers, they lure the whole crowd (plus their two fairy managers) into an ambush hallway and firebomb them. They loot moonshine, an alchemy workstation, and a recipe for a "Rev-Up Immunity Smoothie." A "Live, Laugh, Love" door suggests the boss room may hold children — but the boss bursts straight through the walls into their room instead.

Chapter 34 — The Krakaren Clone

The Krakaren Clone (Level 10 Neighborhood Boss — an explicit clone; killing it just spawns two more) attacks with dozens of screaming tentacles and waves of reinforcements. Carl blends an Immunity Smoothie mid-fight (both he and Donut get visibly drunk from it) and sends a reanimated zombie in as an unwitting suicide bomber.

Chapter 35 — Six Percent Health

Carl survives the blast catastrophically injured — saved in part by a buff that redirected what should have been a fatal hit. They discover their looted crafting tables are seemingly indestructible (a bug Carl quietly decides to exploit) and find the Krakaren's actual corpse, confirming it died from the explosion, not direct combat. Mordecai, now in a new form, furiously refuses Odette's request to reconcile. Loot includes the Enchanted BigBoi Boxers, granting the Protective Shell spell.

Chapter 36 — Zev

A kua-tin Admin, Zev, becomes Carl and Donut's official PR agent. Carl explodes at her about being forced to perform for cameras; she surprisingly agrees, revealing she's just as trapped within the system as he is. Mordecai privately warns that the kua-tin's ruling party is pressuring Borant to end the season fast, meaning the dungeon is being made deliberately more dangerous.

Chapter 37 — The Grub Swarm

Mordecai explains the dungeon's "waste disposal" system: grub swarms scale directly with nearby corpse counts, capped per quadrant. They push through a massive swarm to link up with Team Meadow Lark, who've built an improvised "parade float" train to move all the residents at once. Mid-conversation, Zev breaks in with an urgent warning: an elderly resident has started urinating on a hallway wall.

Chapter 38 — The Rage Elemental

The bathroom-violation punishment triggers exactly as threatened: a Rage Elemental (Level 93) is summoned. It kills the offender, another elderly resident, and then Yolanda Martinez herself as she tries to hold it off. Carl's Protective Shell spell saves the rest of the group, buying time to reach a safe room. They seal the door with the elemental clawing outside — its only real counter now on a long cooldown.

Chapter 39 — Views and Consequences

The recap broadcasts the disaster to a massive new audience, treating one death as a crude joke and Yolanda's with real gravity. Loot includes risky scratch-off lottery items for both Carl and Donut. A system update announces safe rooms will now forcibly eject everyone one hour before every floor collapse, closing off their usual strategy.

Chapter 40 — Bomb Chicken

Rather than wait out his spell's cooldown, Carl devises a plan to kill the elemental outright, recalling that anything shoved down a stairwell without properly descending "dissolves." The group builds the "MOAB" — nicknamed "Bomb Chicken" — a bike-trailer bomb launcher, and lures the elemental on a chase down the hallway, tangling its legs with a magic chain and using an oil slick to make it slip. At the stairwell chamber, they abandon their burning chopper as a decoy and teleport to safety just as a final bomb shoves the wounded elemental into the hole, dissolving it — netting no combat experience since neither is credited with the kill.

Chapter 41 — Goodbye, Meadow Lark

Team Meadow Lark descends to Floor 3; Carl has a poignant goodbye with dementia-affected Elle McGibbons, who mistakes him for her late husband. Their friendly admin Zev is abruptly replaced by a hostile one, Mukta, who forces them onto a different show against their wishes.

Chapter 42 — Death Watch Extreme

They're transported to a sinister set for Death Watch Extreme Dungeon Mayhem, hosted by the Maestro — a cruel young orc prince — before an audience of jeering pre-teens. The show's format: two freshly-plucked crawlers must gamble on whether people in mortal danger live or die to earn rescue points. Disgusted, Carl physically breaks the illusion to refuse participation, then negotiates a compromise to keep speaking his mind without being killed for it.

Chapter 43 — Yvette

Carl talks the two trapped crawlers into using their earned points to save everyone rather than choosing one person, hijacking the Maestro's cruel narrative. Furious, the Maestro reveals he's a real prince of the powerful Skull Empire. The show then airs the true, horrifying backstory of Frank Q and Maggie My: their "daughter" Yvette was a captured teenager, and Maggie strangles the mortally wounded girl live rather than let her be saved. Maggie attacks Carl and only hits the trailer's invisible wall, vowing revenge.

Chapter 44 — The Skull Empire

Donut reveals she overheard Mordecai's private warning that Carl should abandon her before Floor 9's Blood Sultanate gauntlet. A patch closes their stairwell-dissolve exploit. Zev returns, cleared of a minor disciplinary mark, and explains the Maestro's family is a major galactic power. She reveals a mysteriously high-quality, anonymous "Pork Boy" deepfake of Carl and the Maestro has gone massively viral, humiliating the Skull Empire.

Chapter 45 — Ralph

Hunting the Kobold quadrant's boss, Carl and Donut find caged, abused Danger Dingoes used in an underground fighting pit and flip them neutral with pet biscuits. The boss fight begins against Ralph, a Level 11 Frenzied Gerbil — see Ralph's boss page for the full account, including the twist where a freed dingo swallows him mid-fight before he bursts back out for a final ambush.

Chapter 46 — Mongo

With Ralph dead, Carl loots a Master Pen Key that unlocks a pet reward room. Over Carl's objection, Donut insists on a strange, red-tagged chick-like baby dinosaur she names Mongo — who, unlike the tamed dingoes, stays hostile even after pet biscuits, kicking off a bonding-process arc.

Chapter 47 — Bonding

Carl and Donut spend the rest of Floor 2 training Mongo, eventually bonding him (title "Royal Steed") after Donut saves him from a Brindled Vespa. Both hit Level 13. In a strange twist, Carl finds a "History" tab listing three items he's never owned — Valtay Corporation tech, clearly tied to Agatha's mysterious shopping cart. Someone is approaching on the map as the chapter ends.

Epilogue — One Last Piece of Advice

Back on Odette's show, Carl and Donut discuss the Rage Elemental kill and introduce Mongo. Death Watch Extreme Dungeon Mayhem has gone on hiatus "to restructure," and the Skull Empire's request to stop calling the prince "Carl's Naughty Little Piggie" only makes it stick harder. Backstage, Odette warns Carl about the Valtay Corporation — a major rival power with a fleet parked outside the Borant system — all but confirming where the found tech (and possibly Agatha) came from. She leaves them with one last piece of advice as the book ends: during the upcoming race/class selection, look for a hidden, high-charisma-only option that would greatly help their survival — but picking it will make someone very angry.

Sourced from Book 1: The Apocalypse Will Be Televised.

docs.text:
Full narrative recaps, chapter by chapter. For the condensed version, see the Timeline; for standalone reference pages, see Characters, Bosses, and Spells.

Key Game Mechanics Introduced — click to expand
  • Race & Class Selection — the Floor 3 process, Earth Classes, Character Actor specialties
  • Wild Magic Bursts — the four-precursor-burst hazard
Table of Contents — click to expand

  • Chapter 2 — Primal
  • Chapter 3 — The Over City
  • Chapter 4 — Grimaldi's Traveling Circus

  • Chapter 7 — Elites
  • Chapter 8 — Water Lily
  • Chapter 9 — Heather the Bear
  • Chapter 10 — The Big Top
  • Chapter 11 — Papa Grimaldi
  • Chapter 12 — Street Urchins
  • Chapter 13 — The Freeballing Benefit
  • Chapter 14 — GumGum
  • Chapter 15 — The Desperado Club
  • Chapter 16 — Pustule
  • Chapter 17 — The Xistera
  • Chapter 18 — Miss Quill
  • Chapter 19 — Danger Zone
  • Chapter 20 — The Apito Education Center
  • Chapter 21 — Katia

  • Chapter 23 — Daniel Bautista
  • Chapter 24 — Remex's Story
  • Chapter 25 — Carl's Doomsday Scenario
  • Epilogue — The Leaderboard

Chapter 1 — Donut's Choice

Carl, Donut, and Mongo arrive on Floor 3 (the Over City) and meet Mordecai in his new Incubus form — his final shape before his guildhall permanently relocates. Donut keeps her Cat race outright. For class, Mordecai presents three AI-recommended options; Donut nearly picks the flashy NecroBard before Carl steers her toward Artist Alley Mogul — only for Donut to "accidentally" pick Former Child Actor instead, secretly following Odette's advice from Book 1 to trigger the hidden Manager Benefit without Mordecai suspecting it was planned. Mordecai is furious, realizing too late he's now bound to travel everywhere with them, losing his guildhall, television access, and privacy.

Chapter 2 — Primal

Carl works through his own race and class choices with Mordecai. He rejects the AI-recommended Hobgoblin and Sasquatch (too monstrous, would cost viewers) and instead picks the rare Primal race — a "blank slate" race tied to a mysterious, vanished precursor civilization, at the cost of -1 to all stats but with all higher-tier skills unlockable to level 20. For class, he picks Compensated Anarchist, an exclusive Monk/Rogue trapmaking-and-bomb-making class requiring 500 billion views and Explosives Handling 5, which comes with the Fear spell and access to the Desperado Club. Floor 2 collapses mid-selection; around 700,000 crawlers remain of the original 13 million.

Chapter 3 — The Over City

Mordecai formally presents Carl and Donut to the Over City, a themed urban floor built as a "stage set" around a fictional volcano-kingdom backstory. He explains that most NPCs are biologically engineered by Borant, memory-wiped and reused between seasons, and that city guards will kill on sight if provoked — but won't pursue into the ruins. Village signs act as a rough Pathfinder substitute, marking distances to settlements, stairwells, and saferooms. Mordecai warns Carl specifically to avoid "girls with horns on their heads" and to lean on his new Fear spell, then sends the party toward a larger settlement half a day's walk east.

Chapter 4 — Grimaldi's Traveling Circus

En route, the party is ambushed by knife-throwing Former Circus Lemurs and a stilt-legged Terror the Clown, remnants of a cataclysm-warped circus. Fighting through to a saferoom, they trigger their first-ever quest: The Show Must Go On, tasking them with investigating why the circus still terrorizes the ruins centuries later. Mordecai, meanwhile, gets catastrophically drunk on his first night out as manager (an Incubus weakness to alcohol he didn't know about) and passes out mid-sentence, leaving Carl and Donut to handle their first quest and boss-tier threat completely alone.

Chapter 5 — Clockwork Triplicate

While Mordecai sleeps it off, Carl and Donut open their Earth boxes: Donut gets a cat tree, a candle, and a mandatory Earth Hobby Potion that grants a random skill (hers is "Scutelliphily" — turtle-shell collecting); Carl's gives him "Cesta Punta," which turns out to be jai alai. Donut learns the new spell Clockwork Triplicate, which spawns two temporary illusory duplicates of a pet. That night the pair scout the circus perimeter, quietly killing sentry lemurs and getting their first look at Grimaldi's fortified encampment — including a defaced "Wanted: Traitor" poster of a horned elite named Tsarina Signet.

Chapter 6 — Tsarina Signet

Fleeing a mortar barrage from the circus's magical artillery, Carl and Donut fall through a collapsing floor into a hidden basement, only to be confronted outside by the poster's subject herself: Tsarina Signet, a half-Naiad, half-High-Elf Elite who tries to charm Carl before "helpfully" surrounding the party with six Mold Lions as unwitting blood sacrifices for her summoning magic. Carl breaks her charm effect by snapping his own finger (Mordecai's trick from chat) and uses Protective Shell to pin and kill the lions before her ritual can claim him, denying her the sacrifice she wanted.

Chapter 7 — Elites

With her sacrifice spell fizzled, Signet reveals her spells require a sacrificial death she can't personally cause, and admits she'd hoped Carl would die defending her. She invites the party back the next night to hear her and Grimaldi's backstory. Back at the saferoom, Mordecai — now recovered — explains what Elites really are: unique, AI-imprinted NPCs starring in scripted, producer-driven serial dramas that span the urban floors, protected by heavy "plot armor" and best avoided entirely. The recap show reveals Hekla's Amazonian/Shieldmaiden transformation and Lucia Mar's extreme Lajabless race and Black Inquisitor General class.

Chapter 8 — Water Lily

The next morning, Carl and Donut are ambushed and knocked unconscious for fifteen hours by an unseen, overwhelming spell. Carl wakes alone on a couch — Signet's captive — to learn Donut has been placed under her mother's heirloom Water Lily curse: if Signet dies, Donut dies with her, and moving her body drains her health. Signet reveals her true bargain: Carl must personally kill Heather, a captured, tortured circus bear, so Signet can use her blood for the sacrifice spell she couldn't cast on Carl the night before, since Signet herself is barred from directly influencing the fight.

Chapter 9 — Heather the Bear

Carl solo-fights Heather the Bear (Level 19 Neighborhood Boss), a parasite-infested former circus performer whose worm-covered claws speak directly into his mind. After a chaotic fight involving smoke bombs, a lottery-ticket custard blast that accidentally heals the worms off her, and a mercy kill, Carl frees the real Heather's spirit from the parasites just before finishing her. Her blood powers Signet's strongest Ink Marauder summoning yet — a towering army of animated, paper-thin "tattoo" monsters — and the two march on the circus together for the night's assault.

Chapter 10 — The Big Top

Signet's paper army tears through the circus's outer defenses in minutes, but an ancient protective ward stops them at the big top's canvas. Carl alone must enter with a stolen ticket, break the tent's three support poles, and confront the vine-thing at its center. Inside, he discovers the true final boss: Ringmaster Grimaldi, revealed as a Level 85 City Boss and Elite — a sentient Pestiferous Vine that reanimates his transformed "family" of circus monsters nightly. Using Mordecai's lore on poisoning vine-type mobs, Carl secretly poisons himself and bleeds onto Grimaldi's roots to try to kill him from within.

Chapter 11 — Papa Grimaldi

Realizing the producers of Vengeance of the Daughter are watching, Carl brazenly negotiates through Zev — threatening to spoil the drama's climax unless they let him resolve it his way, in exchange for future guest appearances. He then eats a parasite-laced "ice cream" to link minds with Grimaldi directly, using his temporary Wisp Armor spell to resist full mind control while begging Grimaldi to listen to Signet. Convinced, Grimaldi un-banishes her, ending their centuries-long war without a kill. The quest completes as The Show Must Go On — but Mordecai warns that Donut's health has dropped critically back at Signet's hideout.

Chapter 12 — Street Urchins

Carl races back to find Mongo, grown and battered, single-handedly holding off a swarm of spike-covered Street Urchins (Floor 3's "janitor" mob) to protect the still-cursed Donut. A jury-rigged potion recipe from Mordecai saves the badly wounded Mongo. Donut wakes at dawn as promised, having gained a huge share of Carl's quest experience. Passing the now-empty circus ruins, they find a new stairwell down to Floor 4 revealed at the site. Carl reflects on how much Donut has matured, and Zev reveals the mysterious production company behind Signet's drama: Sensation Entertainment, Incorporated.

Chapter 13 — The Freeballing Benefit

Back with Mordecai, the party opens a haul of quest rewards, including two "Hadji"-upgraded boxes. Donut receives Fang Caps (later given to Mongo) and a skill potion; Carl uses a rare Scroll of Upgrade on his Enchanted BigBoi Boxers, which comically grants +5 Dexterity, +5 Intelligence, +3 more Constitution, and the Freeballing Benefit — locking him out of ever wearing pants again. That night's recap show reveals a fellow crawler's pet goat transformed into a monstrous Hellspawn, and introduces a grieving orc NPC, GumGum, whom Mordecai flatly refuses to let the party help.

Chapter 14 — GumGum

Despite Mordecai's warning that "you can't save them all," Carl sneaks out that night to find GumGum and ask about her quest, but she's already gone. The next day, after a long shopping run through the settlement's general stores (with Donut's Charisma driving hard bargains), the party discovers GumGum again outside the town gate, piling up a mountain of murdered prostitutes' corpses — women who keep turning up dead and drained of blood in the alleys with no explanation. She begs for help, and the party accepts The Sex Workers Who Fell from the Heavens quest, against Mordecai's explicit advice.

Chapter 15 — The Desperado Club

Mordecai escorts Carl and Donut into the Desperado Club for the first time, explaining its layout — public bar, members-only main floor, and specialty rooms including a casino, a brothel, and a black market. They meet Quint, a floating Half-Djinn drug dealer and old friend of Mordecai's, and trade moonshine for a rare alchemy starter kit. Quint recounts a wild story from the night before: a crawler with one goat leg (clearly Lucia Mar) trashed the club's pet playroom and stole liquor after her rottweilers went berserk — the first hint of her escalating notoriety.

Chapter 16 — Pustule

At the Silk Road market, the party meets Pustule, an unnervingly cheerful, pus-covered hobgoblin explosives dealer who becomes a recurring supplier, and gets an appraisal on Carl's Jug O' Boom (worth 7,500 gold, mostly for the rare moonshine). Walking back to the inn that night, Mongo bolts into a dark alley and the party discovers GumGum's mutilated corpse alongside three horrifying flying-head Krasue and a deranged, self-proclaimed "final boss" city elf named Vicente, who dies instantly to a kick and a magic missile — but not before revealing he somehow already knew Carl and Donut's names.

Chapter 17 — The Xistera

Looting Vicente reveals a 201st Security Group military uniform; Mordecai explains city elves as a banished, doomsday-cult offshoot who worship the skyfowl as literal angels. GumGum's body yields a blood-soaked Mysterious Letter (written in necromancer's script) and a magistrate's Gate Pass. That night, fan boxes bring Donut a framed photo of Beatrice (which Carl finds no longer bothers him) and Carl a xistera — a jai alai scoop that instantly becomes his new primary ranged weapon, retiring his slingshot for good. A second dead prostitute is found the next morning with "No, you won't" carved into her back.

Chapter 18 — Miss Quill

Investigating the town hall, the party meets Miss Quill, the elderly, Beanie-Baby-obsessed receptionist who refuses them an audience with the reclusive Magistrate Featherfall (who, they're told, "only comes out at night now"). Carl dumps a corpse on her desk to force the point, to no avail. Later that day, hunting near a dead city boss's corpse, the party is ambushed in an unnatural, magic-resistant darkness by a group of towering, undead Shambling Berserkers. Carl's dynamite triggers the rotting boss corpse to detonate catastrophically, launching him unconscious — Donut and Mongo finish the fight alone.

Chapter 19 — Danger Zone

Carl and Donut appear on the round-table talk show Danger Zone with Ripper Wonton, meeting Hekla in person for the first time alongside Princess D'nadia, the Naga singer Manasa, and an obnoxious comedian named Tucker. Pressed on Skull Empire politics, Carl gives an impassioned "boil the frog" speech calling for the citizens to rise up. Minutes later, Prince Stalwart orders a assassination pulse-strike meant for Carl and Donut's trailer — but it hits Manasa's instead, killing her. The Valtay Corporation retaliates by destroying a Skull Empire royal yacht, killing Queen Consort Ugloo and the disgraced former Prince Maestro.

Chapter 20 — The Apito Education Center

Suspecting the city elves' "Apito Education Center" temple is tied to Featherfall's undead operation, Carl and Donut provoke a confrontation with nine armed cultist elves — only to accidentally aggro the town's guards in the chaos. Using their "Mic Drop" play (a mid-air boom jug), they incinerate the temple and most of the elves, but not before a pregnant dwarf named Eunice and her son Ricky Joe get caught in the crossfire — Mongo bites off the boy's arm mid-brawl. The elves reveal, under duress, that they tortured and killed GumGum for asking too many questions.

Chapter 21 — Katia

Hiding from the aggro'd guards, Carl questions the traumatized Ricky Joe about the temple before the party slips away. Back at the inn, they meet Katia Grim, a shy, poorly-sculpted Doppelganger sent by Hekla to level up with the party as a personal favor — she's a Level 9 Monster Truck Driver with absurdly high Constitution but far below Carl and Donut's level. The recap show airs a manufactured "feud" between Donut and Lucia Mar's rottweilers, with Lucia Mar coldly promising to hunt Donut and Carl down in the dungeon once given the chance.

Chapter 22 — The Krasue Nest

Using the bloodstained Mysterious Letter as bait — Mordecai deduces it's a scrying spell that lets the caster hear wherever it's removed from inventory — Carl and Donut lure their unseen enemy by planting explosives in Miss Quill's office and detonating remotely. The blast kills both Featherfall (already a centuries-old, mummified husk used as a magical prop) and, they hope, Miss Quill. Breaching the ruins, they find a nest of sleeping Krasue and, dying among them, a former receptionist named Burgundy, who reveals the truth: Miss Quill has secretly run the town for ages and was preparing an heirloom genocide spell to wipe out every non-flying resident.

Chapter 23 — Daniel Bautista

Leaving the collapsing building, Carl and Donut meet Daniel Bautista 2, a Tigran Swashbuckler whose entire family — the crawlers whose corpses yielded Donut's Fallen Oak anklet — was slaughtered by the circus lemurs back in Chapter 4. He thanks them for avenging his family and offers a favor in return before departing. Reflecting on how broken and lonely most of the crawlers and NPCs around them seem, Carl and Donut decide to finish the quest that night rather than wait, and head to the Swordsmen depot warehouse to confront the entity they now believe is a lich hiding above it.

Chapter 24 — Remex's Story

Braced for a lich, Carl instead finds Remex, a pitiful "Soul Leech Capacitor" — the resurrected husk of Miss Quill's dead husband, forcibly bound to power her spells. His rambling, digression-filled confession reveals the full plot: Quill, a disowned skyfowl royal, has spent generations building toward a three-part heirloom spell that would exterminate every flightless resident of the Over City and restore skyfowl rule. The quest The Sex Workers Who Fell from the Heavens completes — but instantly, a new event quest announces an uncontrollable magical explosion at Remex's location, giving everyone in a 45-kilometer radius seven minutes to escape or die. Unable to outrun it in time, Carl and Donut choose to stay and gamble on containing the blast, trapping the swelling soul crystal inside a rare Sheol Glass Reaper Case moments before detonation.

Chapter 25 — Carl's Doomsday Scenario

The case holds — barely — caging the silent explosion, and Carl manages to pull the now-transformed, unstable, un-inventoriable superweapon into his inventory anyway, naming it Carl's Doomsday Scenario. A series of magical "precursor bursts" strip the fleeing crowd of crawlers of their gear and stats before the real explosion; Carl strips down to nothing, Donut sacrifices her Sepsis Crown, and the party (now including Katia) narrowly escapes down a stairwell to Floor 4 alongside dozens of other survivors, ending Book 2's main floor storyline.

Epilogue — The Leaderboard

On Odette's show, Carl (still stuck in a toilet-paper loincloth) learns Borant used its one seasonal veto to strip the party of the Celestial-tier reward they'd earned — while a rival crawler exploited a loophole to claim one anyway, threatening Borant with a season-ending financial penalty. Despite losing the prize, the party's raw combat experience still rockets them up: Carl to Level 27, Donut to 26, Katia from 9 to 21. The current Floor 3 leaderboard reveals Carl and Donut sitting at 6th and 7th, behind Lucia Mar (1st) and Hekla (2nd) — and, astonishingly, Mrs. Elle McGibbons in 10th. Privately, Odette warns Carl that Hekla is quietly maneuvering to recruit Donut (and, through her, Mordecai) away from him, and that the Skull Empire may have purchased a deity sponsorship — likely Grull — aimed squarely at Carl heading into Floor 4.

Sourced from Book 2: Carl's Doomsday Scenario.

docs.text:
Full narrative recaps, chapter by chapter. For the condensed version, see the Timeline; for standalone reference pages, see Characters, Bosses, and Spells.

Key Game Mechanics Introduced — click to expand
  • Personal Spaces — whitelisting other parties into your own space
  • The 20% Buff Display Bug — the long-standing Good Rest/shower stat glitch
Table of Contents — click to expand

  • Chapter 9 — The Wheel of Fortune
  • Chapter 10 — Testing the Rails

  • Chapter 33 — Death Challenge
  • Chapter 34 — Air Quadrant
  • Epilogue — Choose Your Opponent

Chapter 1 — The Iron Tangle

Carl, Donut, Katia, and Mongo arrive on Floor 4 aboard a moving subway car — "the Iron Tangle," a sprawling train-and-tunnel maze with only 9,375 stairwells hidden among hundreds of thousands of stops. Donut picks the Football Hooligan class (gaining the party-buffing Mascot skill tied to Mongo's kills). Investigating a mysterious sealed car (#15), the party is swarmed by baby-like Drek at Sirin Station and ducks into a "Janitor's Lair" car, killing two Jikininki ghouls via a Magic Missile Double Shot and a Smush stomp. Trapped between hordes front and back, Carl sets an Alarm Module (accidentally blasting "Fergalicious") and a Spike Module as delays, then casts Protective Shell as an improvised plow, bulldozing the mobs the length of the train while the party sprints to the rear car.

Chapter 2 — Station 83

At transfer station 83, the party meets Non-Combatant shopkeeper Limp Richard (a Mole Man) and settles into a fast-food-themed safe room. Mordecai arrives in a new Grulke (toad) form, having lost daily-update access as a Manager. The crawler count has already dropped to 389,441. Opening Book 2's delayed quest loot, Carl gets the Necklace of the Haute Bourgeoisie (granting Talon Strike) and the Bang Bro spell tome; Donut gets the Tiara of Mana Genita and the Hole spell; Katia gets a shapeshiftable arm-shield. Using AI-granted "screw the sponsors" coupons, the party combines three level-3 personal spaces into a level-5 communal base with a 2-hour-sleep Ultra-Stabilized Bed and a Training Room, finally giving Mordecai his own room.

Chapter 3 — Brandon's Letter

After a full night of base-building, the party sleeps just two hours thanks to the new bed's Good Rest bonus. The recap show reveals the tentative Floor 4 leaderboard in full for the first time — Lucia Mar, Hekla, and a mysterious goat-person named Prepotente round out the top 3, with Carl and Donut at 6th and 7th. A system announcement declares bounty hunting officially open on the top 10. Then Carl finds a message in a new "Messages from Deceased Crawlers" folder: Brandon An died holding a line against Shade Gremlins as Floor 3 collapsed, and reveals he fought with his brother Chris just before dying, leaving an "I love you" he never got to say. Carl trains alone in grief, repeating his private mantra.

Chapter 4 — Formation One

The party settles into a routine: buffs, an hour of skill training, crafting, then grinding the rails. Carl crafts with new tools (the Goo-inator, earning the "Martha Stewart" achievement) and trades westerns for sci-fi novels with Limp Richard. Scouting the figure-eight Nightmare Express and the Yellow Line, they discover platform-sniping is safe against Cave Mudge Bonkers and Shock Chompers but reject it as an inefficient "time trap." Boarding a train, they drill Formation One — a V-shaped kill zone — against a wave of Bonkers, with Katia shapeshifting her arm into a weapon-catching limb.

Chapter 5 — Vernon

Fortified with crafted "Gangway Chock" barricades, the party survives a Pollyslog boarding attempt (severed by the closing doors) and reaches the Yellow Line conductor's break room, meeting Vernon, a dwarf trapped in an unexplained time loop — he blacks out at the end of the line and wakes at the yard, gold and mementos intact but wounds and hunger persisting. He reveals engineers are only ever seen after a derailment. The party finds the Porter reward room and picks numbered "prize" suitcases — Carl's holds an actual invisibility potion, but Donut's is trapped, unleashing Literal Fire Ants that burn the car and kill Vernon before the party barely escapes onto the platform.

Chapter 6 — The Control Sigil

At Banshee Station, Carl grapples with the horror of NPCs like Vernon believing in fabricated lives and memories. Investigating a side room, the party finds an inert pair of dwarven combat automatons guarded by a mysterious "control sigil" only Carl can see (via Escape Plan) — Mordecai explains it as sloppy, showrunner-controlled scripting, not standard AI mechanics. Meanwhile a PR call from Zev pressures Carl and Donut to make Katia "more interesting" for viewers, prompting an uncomfortable makeover conversation. The party demolishes the robots for fifteen tons of scrap metal. Daniel Bautista relays word that Imani C urgently needs to talk about Brandon and Chris, and warns of bounty hunters circling the leaderboard, before the party heads toward transfer station 131, home to a Desperado Club.

Chapter 7 — The Prize Carousel

Mongo hits level 15, maxing out his growth (now pony-sized) and gaining the Earthquake jump attack, as the party arrives at station 131. Mordecai crafts potions (including a two-use "immortality" brew and stat-buff potions) and Fragmenting Potion Balls. Fan boxes bring Donut the Enchanted Mongoliensis Saddle for riding Mongo, and Carl a live "Prize Carousel" segment hosted by an NPC named Chaco — whose mere presence enrages Mordecai into attacking him, triggering a 7-day manager suspension. Rattled, Carl picks a mysterious anarchy-symbol book as his prize: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook, revealed to be a secret, AI-invisible, edition-spanning guide to explosives, potions, and dungeon secrets passed between crawlers for generations.

Chapter 8 — Dirty Shirley

Carl skims the Cookbook's rules (contribute knowledge or lose access; secrecy is mandatory) and a few explosive recipes before forcing himself to stop. Without Mordecai, Carl and Donut visit the Desperado Club, hiring rock-monster bodyguards Bomo and The Sledge. They reunite with Elle McGibbons (now a foul-mouthed, floating Frost Maiden) and Imani C (an Obsidian Butterfly fire-support healer), who explain that Brandon's brother Chris Andrews underwent a personality-altering Igneous race change, split from the group after a fight, and is now hunting for Carl — around the same time a resident named Henry accidentally spawned an army of Shade Gremlins. The reunion is interrupted when an assassin knifes Donut in the back; her Cockroach skill barely saves her, and she kills him in self-defense, earning her first player-kill skull.

Chapter 9 — The Wheel of Fortune

Elle kills the assassin's female accomplice with an icicle before she can strike again. Club assistant manager Astrid, a Level 125 Bloodlust Sprite, smooths over the incident and grants Carl and Donut free security. Comparing notes with Imani and Elle, the group realizes all known transfer stations are prime numbers. At the casino, Carl learns the Hunting Grounds and a war-torn "Larracos" both lie below, then gambles his old comp chip on the Wheel of Fortune — narrowly dodging a "get stabbed" and "Nothing!" (a literal trapdoor to oblivion) before landing a Scroll of Upgrade that boosts his Toe Ring's Powerful Strike bonus significantly.

Chapter 10 — Testing the Rails

Back at base, Katia demonstrates a near-perfect Doppelganger disguise of Hekla using a new Makeup Table (paid for with her own upgrade coupons, to Carl's private dismay). After training and gear distribution, the party tests whether the third rail is truly electrified (confirmed, safely) and builds Jelly Bombs — improvised landmines adapted from the Cookbook — to attempt a train derailment. Elle's group reports discovering a Borough Boss version of Krakaren on another line.

Chapter 11 — Gore-Gore

The derailment succeeds spectacularly, earning the "Locomotive Breath" achievement. Amid the wreckage, the ochre line's engineer is finally forced out: Gore-Gore, a Level 40 Mantaur — a bizarre two-torsoed, four-armed creature bred for the grueling engineer role — emerges from the ruined engine car to confront the party. (See Gore-Gore the Mantaur for the full encounter.)

Chapter 12 — Sponsors

Looting Gore-Gore's corpse yields 498 gold, an Ochre Line Engineer's Key, a Rev-Up Magic Hair Restoration item, and a full neighborhood map of the entire Ochre line from station 11 to 435. Sponsor reveals finally land: Carl gets the Valtay Corporation, Donut gets Princess D'nadia of the Prism Kingdom, and Katia gets a mysterious "Princess Formidable of the Skull Empire." Katia realizes several of her fingers were permanently severed in the fight, a grim "losing myself" moment about her doppelganger flesh-as-clay nature. Studying the map, the party learns monsters walk the open track between stations to reach assigned stops, and that station spacing varies wildly — mere blocks apart early on, 40-50 miles apart further down the line. Katia plots a cross-line route using the Dismemberment Limited and the Nightmare Express to skip ahead quickly, while Imani and Elle report finding a Krakaren-run "drug den" system where Pooka hand out addictive, race-specific sedatives to keep mobs docile and cycling through the trains — with a warning that interrupting the supply triggers dangerous mob transformations.

Chapter 13 — The Ugly Ass Backpack

Zev books Carl and Donut for an upcoming "Planet Beautiful" pageant-and-pet-show narration segment. Riding the Dismemberment Limited, the party meets the tragic hybrid creature Levi the 7th and fights off Dismember the War Mage and his "Bereft Minions" Fleshers by choking a doorway and using a "Surprise Three" — reaching through a Hole spell puncture to rip off Dismember's head. Carl reads further Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook entries from crawlers Rosetta, Allister, Forkith, and the emotionally raw Drakea. Back at base, Carl engineers Katia an "Ugly Ass Backpack" using a discovered inventory trick — a container's contents can be selectively withdrawn independent of the container — letting her equip over a ton of dwarf-robot scrap as living mass, transforming into an eleven-foot armored giant with a strength bonus at the cost of dexterity. That night Carl receives a Bronze Benefactor Box from the sinister Valtay Corporation: a Neural Enhancer pill that grants him the ability to see and analyze subspace portals through doorways.

Chapter 14 — Stealing a Train

Waiting for the Nightmare Express at station 283, Carl builds an informal crawler information network by fist-bumping chat contacts at the Desperado Club. When the boarding plan (climbing the exposed, monster-filled car roofs) proves suicidal, Carl instead uses Protective Shell to smash through the train from the tunnel while Donut's mistimed Puddle Jumper leaves him exposed — he's clipped by the runaway train's cowcatcher and forced to climb into the engine car itself. There he meets Fire Brandy, a Lesser Demon MILF firewoman who births and burns her own stillborn young as boiler fuel ("Sheol Bricks"), and who talks him through driving the train after both human engineers are found dead. Carl's shield spell has killed every monster aboard, including three neighborhood bosses, netting him three levels (to 32), a Steam Engineer's Key, and the achievements "Kept a Rollin'" and "Three Cheers for Slaughter" plus a Platinum Big Daddy Box.

Chapter 15 — The Abyss

At the Ochre line's switching station, Carl discovers the mechanism behind the trains: colored-line cars drive through one-way portals and are dumped into a mile-wide, mile-deep pit called the Abyss, while only the engine cars teleport back to be rebuilt into new trains — explaining why NPC "loops" are really fresh builds, not time travel. Analyzing the portals reveals the key: any of three "marked" items (the Ochre Key, Steam Train Key, or the free souvenir conductor hat every crawler received) grants passage to the far-side trainyard. Carl broadcasts this to his growing contact network as one of several possible routes to the sealed-off early stations. Meanwhile Donut receives her first benefactor box from Princess D'nadia — the Prism Industries Capacitating and Focusing Goggles, which turn her Magic Missile into a multi-shot laser — and levels up to 30, unlocking the new Love Vampire ability.

Chapter 16 — Babababoons

Elle and Imani find the secret ghoul-cart tunnel out of the robot rooms. Donut discovers she finally has enough spell points to read her long-dormant Minion Army tome (a slow, situational mass-charm spell with a five-minute cast time). The party is then swarmed at the transit station by Babababoons — feral, drug-addicted baboon-men suffering "stage two DTs" from withdrawal on the Rev-Up Amazing Cure-All shot — and slaughters dozens with Powerful Strike, Banger Spheres, and Katia's new bone-spike grappling trick. Back at the switching station, Carl examines the "Pass-Through" portal gating trains into Station and Repair Hub E and watches Fire Brandy bond with Donut and Katia over motherhood before the party commits to driving the Nightmare through.

Chapter 17 — Widget

Trainyard E is being overrun by a ghoul infestation from a broken "excess citizen disposal" system. Grease Gremlin mechanic Widget offers to guide the party out via chain and turntable, but a "dead" ghoul reanimates and rips his head off mid-rescue, forcing Donut to fumble the turntable controls herself via chat. The party escapes with rescued NPC Madison (an Iron Tangle HR associate) aboard, passing station after station down the employee line. Interrogating Madison at station 24, Carl learns of six ravenous Station Mimics disguised as terminus stops and fires off a last-second warning to Bautista not to get off at one.

Chapter 18 — Human Resources

Bautista reports his crawler group trapped at a Station Mimic disguised as a boss-free stairwell chamber. Carl learns the Kravyad guarding station 435's employee portal are non-combatant NPCs who hypnotize dwarven workers into endless labor loops, and that the portal snaps shut the instant its Kravyad dies. Investigating the identical five-stairwell chamber atop station 24, Katia privately confesses she's grown a working third eye — and reveals she secretly recovered a PVP Coupon bearing Carl's name that Donut had buried and hidden on the tracks; Carl confirms with Imani that every party member who receives a first player-kill "Savage Box" gets one of these betrayal coupons, unsettling him about what Donut may still be hiding. Riding the line down through stations 36 through 60, the party finds every "employee town" hollow and unfurnished — proof the NPCs' entire home life is fabricated backstory with no real substance behind it. Madison, confronted with her nonexistent apartment and family, refuses to leave and is abandoned on the platform to await her ex-husband "Rod," while Donut connects Madison's cruelty to the memory of Miss Beatrice's callous mother.

Chapter 19 — Frank Q

Back at station 41, Carl gets updates: Imani's group survives a ghoul-swarmed Trainyard D conveyor landing, and Bautista's group neutralizes the Kravyad, only for her to kill herself and seal the portal, stranding over 150 hatless crawlers. At the Desperado Club, Carl finds Frank Q — Brandon's killer's ex-husband — a broken, drunk night elf assassin who reveals the horrifying truth of Book 2's ambush: he and ex-wife Maggie forced their teenage daughter Yvette to wear a cursed ring and mark Carl for death, and Maggie choked Yvette to keep the mark's pain from being healed once the attack failed. As an act of self-destructive "revenge," Frank gifts Carl the Ring of Divine Suffering itself, and its dangerous Marked for Death skill; Carl accepts the stat bonus but resolves never to use the skill.

Chapter 20 — Planet Beautiful

Zev teleports Carl and Donut to a luxury underwater production trailer piloted by the sardonic robot Mexx-6000 for a Planet Beautiful culture segment. Carl refuses to read a script full of degrading, AI-hallucinated "facts" about human beauty pageants, and producer Bin — venting about network pressure to make the show "more interesting" — swaps it for a videogame-history segment instead, while Donut happily narrates off-script about cocker spaniels. Word arrives that Chris Andrews murdered Frank Q at the Desperado Club before vanishing, and Carl finally clears the air with Donut over the PVP coupons, which she'd disposed of out of guilt. Returning home after looting the trailer's fridge shelves, makeup table, and couch, Carl finds their personal space suddenly full of unfamiliar women — Hekla's entire crew has arrived uninvited.

Chapter 21 — Brynhild's Daughters

Hekla and roughly thirty members of Brynhild's Daughters have used Carl's station-60 intel to reach the party's base directly, thanking Carl for training Katia and revealing they crossed via the employee portal after Sadie's Glass Prison spell neutralized their local Kravyad. Carl meets Eva Sigrid, Katia's half-nagini, half-orc friend — now carrying thirteen skulls, evidently serving as Hekla's dedicated enforcer — and immediately senses an uneasy hierarchy within the otherwise-welcoming all-women crew.

Chapter 22 — The Plow

To rescue a thousand crawlers trapped at station 101, Hekla's team commandeers a Vermillion-line subway car while Katia builds herself into a living cowcatcher — a spiked, rubber-insulated scoop bolted to the front windows, able to pull dead mobs into her inventory. As the train plows through a ghoul horde at stations 72 and 75, Katia's health mysteriously plummets despite the healer Silfa's inaction, and Donut — watching through her magic-catching goggles — spots Hekla firing invisible cursed bolts into Katia's scoop on purpose, blasting Hekla in the face with a Magic Missile the instant she confirms it.

Chapter 23 — Rush

Hekla flies back into the cab wall as chaos erupts, Eva and two mage "daughters" joining the fight. Cornered and accused, Hekla and Eva reveal nothing outright, but Eva's cruel taunting about Katia's failures at last triggers Katia's unpredictable Rush ability — and instead of hitting Eva, Katia's body veers off-target and kills Hekla outright, claiming the game's first top-10 bounty (500,000 gold) and rocketing from level 24 to 37 in one blow.

Chapter 24 — The Scavenger Mother of Mothers

Donut resurrects Hekla's corpse with Second Chance and Clockwork Triplicate to buy time while Katia loots the body — securing the Enchanted Repeating Crossbow of the Scavenger Mother of Mothers, a unique weapon that scales with the number of women in the party — before the trio seals themselves in the engine and reverses the train to safety. Carl pieces together Hekla's real plan: sacrifice Katia and healer Silfa to bait Carl into attacking a "daughter," giving Hekla cover to kill him and absorb Donut (and Mordecai) into her depleted, healer-heavy team. With Brynhild's Daughters shattered and Eva missing, Carl hands the rescued survivors and the second engine off to Li Jun, directing them to make a stand at station 36 alongside Imani and Elle's group.

Chapter 25 — Station 75

Carl and company collect over 700 souvenir hats and keys from grateful survivors to distribute to crawlers stranded at the Abyss, then explore the ruined workshop station 75 — a gnoll-and-hobgoblin depot wiped out in a ghoul war. Katia's bounty haul nets her a Club Vanquisher tattoo, the Wrestling Belt of the Great Gorgo, and a Find Crawler skill potion; the recap show frames Hekla's death as a tribute special and reveals Eva abandoned Katia on the third floor to join Hekla first. The new leaderboard puts Lucia Mar at #1 and Carl, Donut, and Katia all in the top eight. Zev visits with bad news: a Bloom-party rival named Loita is angling to take over as their representative, and something unspecified but serious has happened back at Borant headquarters.

Chapter 26 — Growler Gary

At the ruined station 75 depot, Carl finds an indestructible gnoll bartender, Growler Gary, who regenerates minutes after dying — a sign, per Cookbook lore, that an NPC holds something vital. Investigating the yard, the party discovers Interdiction Rapid-Response Railway Repair Carts: gnoll-only, dual-handed vehicles that project a mobile portal ahead of them, capable of scooping an entire track's worth of wreckage and monsters into either the Abyss or a trainyard. Devising a scheme to rescue three separated groups of crawlers trapped at the Abyss, Carl realizes the only way to activate the carts (which require two separated left-hand prints) is to repeatedly kill and loot Gary's regenerating hands — a grim, consent-eventually-given process that nets 14 severed hands and Carl's lasting guilt.

Chapter 27 — Physical

The rescue plan launches: paired carts (one tuned to the Abyss, one to a trainyard, each with a randomized Top-40 song as an audible warning) blast down three colored lines, funneling wreckage, ghouls, and stranded crawlers to safety. Carl also detonates a hobgoblin-dynamite train bomb to destroy a monster horde threatening a soul-crystal-generator team, netting a level and closing that line for good. Testing combat against a mutated, tentacled "stage-three DTs" monster, the party learns its true nature when it explodes into thousands of tiny Krakaren Crotch Dumplings — the Krakaren race's disturbing cloning method — forcing a scramble to burn them all before they mature. Word arrives that station 24 is now overrun with the things.

Chapter 28 — Yard H

A disguised railroad-crossing barrier turns out to be a tentacle of the station-433 Mimic Rex in disguise, and Carl's cart accidentally teleports the entire city-boss-tier mimic to trainyard E. Warned by Elle's manager that the mimic can only be killed by stripping over half its mass at once — and that the separated pieces then attack independently until it dies — Carl scraps the fight entirely and instead routes Bautista's roughly 1,400 stranded survivors straight through the main Abyss portal to a mimic-free yard, using the party's stockpiled souvenir hats. The rescued crowd showers Donut with tribute hats in gratitude.

Chapter 29 — The Bolt of Ophiotaurus

Bautista reveals his secret weapon: stuffed-animal figures looted from the dead Miss Quill's apartment that transform into true, temporary monster summons when their tags are pulled. Back at a safehouse, Katia's loot haul includes a riot shield and baton that upgrade her Rush into the area-effect Crowd Blast (usable every five minutes instead of once a day), an Auto Buckler she passes to Carl, and — from her mysterious sponsor Princess Formidable — a single, precious Bolt of Ophiotaurus, capable of pausing a god's invulnerability for fifteen seconds. The recap show reveals a hidden stairwell at the now-mimic-vacated station 433, and a jarring system announcement: private crawler chats are now sellable to viewers, and inventory can no longer hold loose liquids. Mordecai returns from his suspension just as Katia's stored gallons of ghoul blood — no longer inventory-legal — explode out of her across the room.

Chapter 30 — The Syndicate Logo

Mordecai forces Carl to remove the dangerous Ring of Divine Suffering, explaining that Marked for Death rings make their wearers priority targets for faction-war hunters on later floors. Studying Katia's map, Mordecai recognizes the Iron Tangle's overall shape as the Syndicate's own wormhole-network logo, and identifies the drug-den Krakaren/Pooka storyline as an in-universe political cartoon smearing a rival species, the Plenty, over their instant-communication technology. Katia, obsessing over the map, works out that each rail line is mirrored by an inverted twin line on the far side of a hidden chamber — and realizes the sealed five-stairwell rooms sit directly above those hidden spaces, meaning the province-boss ghoul masses gathering at station 36 and 48 may be positioned to flip up into the stairwell chambers themselves.

Chapter 31 — The Crane

Acting on Katia's mirrored-track theory, Carl's team rigs a captured interdiction cart into a makeshift crane above station 36's stairwell circle, aiming its scoop-portal straight down at the hidden chamber below. When the Iron Tangle's system "self-destructs" and the floor's center collapses, waves of now-human-sized Krakaren Juvenile Clonelings pour upward exactly as predicted — and the dangling portal swallows them by the thousands into the Abyss, saving the station. Amid the chaos, Carl learns dwarven and gremlin NPCs have lynched Madison in retaliation for the disaster, and a deliberately triggered soul-crystal chain reaction begins wiping out nearby ghoul generators — confirming Carl's suspicion that killing a province boss detonates every crystal in its blast radius.

Chapter 32 — Grull's Encore

Reinforced by Li Jun's terrifyingly competent sister Li Na (a chain-wielding Slave Driver) and Zhang, Carl's crew lures the mirrored-chamber province boss into the raised cart's portal and banishes it to the Abyss, then runs into the deranged, screaming goat-man Prepotente and his handler Miriam Dom mid-hunt for another boss. Retrieving their last interdiction cart from the trainyard, the group finds the employee-line entrance blocked by two mantaur neighborhood bosses — so Carl deliberately triggers an involuntary summon of the war god Grull through one mantaur's body, planning to hurl him at the rampaging Mimic Rex and then banish him to the Abyss before he can do more damage. The plan goes sideways instantly: as the first mantaur is thrown into the trainyard portal, its clawed hand locks onto Carl's numbed, invulnerable foot, dragging Carl through right along with it.

Chapter 33 — Death Challenge

Carl tumbles into trainyard E face-to-face with the Mimic Rex, and the broadcast reframes the moment as a live "Death Challenge" gambling event, revealing Grull's secret sponsor: Prince Maestro, previously presumed dead, now piloting the war god for his own on-air comeback. Carl survives by hiding, an invisibility potion, and Mordecai's near-invulnerability brew while Grull annihilates the mimic; Katia disguises herself as Carl to lure Grull away, and Li Na horrifically dismembers the second captive mantaur, keeping him alive with heals so the team can trigger a second involuntary summon and banish Grull to the Abyss with only a second left on the clock. (See Mimic Rex for the full Death Challenge and Grull encounter.)

Chapter 34 — Air Quadrant

With five hours left on the floor, Carl loots the Mimic Rex's Map of the Stars, and Fire Brandy and dwarf Tizquick — having each learned their "families" were never real — choose to ride the Nightmare into the Abyss as one final, willing bomb, triggering enough deaths to collapse the region's remaining ghoul generators and boosting Carl to level 41. The survivors finally descend the station 36 stairwell as the floor winds down, and a new admin, Loita of the Bloom party, announces she's taking over as primary handler while Zev is abruptly sent to a "reeducation retreat" for an unspecified personal tragedy.

Epilogue — Choose Your Opponent

At the post-floor interview, Loita imposes new restrictions (no inventory items, no snacks, tighter interview censorship) while Odette needles Carl about a viral "snick" video, reveals the Death Challenge had absurd 50-to-1 survival odds that cost Borant heavily, and gets abruptly muted by Loita whenever the topics of Eva or "something about Chris" come up — confirming both threads remain live dangers. Sent to the fifth floor, Donut spins the entry wheels for the party: they'll enter in the Air Quadrant, facing the Dirigible Gnome Wasteland Fortress.

Sourced from Book 3: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook.
