Chapter 1 — Collateral for the Gate

Floor 6, "the Hunting Grounds," opens with the Gate of the Feral Gods already a liability: hauled before the hooded, worm-headed Valtay liaison Orren, Carl learns the Syndicate can't legally confiscate the artifact but won't let him keep it either, given the danger it poses on a floor about to be flooded with hunters. Orren lays out three options — lock down every portal on the floor, "accelerate" (kill) Carl outright, or have him voluntarily surrender the gate for a receipt, redeemable on the ninth floor. Carl demands a lawyer, halting the meeting cold. Shunted into a stadium-sized staging arena for mandatory class specialization, he learns via chat that Donut has picked a new class, Legendary Diva (a singing bard subclass), over Mordecai's objections, and that Katia got a HAZMAT endorsement for her Monster Truck Driver class. Waiting in line, he meets an amputee crawler named Ajib and hears the floor's opening announcement: hunters, bumped to level 50, will be loosed in under 28 hours. A Bush Elf attendant, Ian, warns him in passing about a mantis hunter named Vrah who killed his brother and wears the heads of her kills — the first mention of the antagonist who will define the floor. The chapter ends with Carl specializing into Agent Provocateur, the bomb-focused class upgrade.

Chapter 2 — The Legendary Diva

Carl arrives at a dryad settlement outside Zockau and is immediately ambushed by an invisible pack of night weasels that paralyze two level-95 Funeral Bell guards in seconds. His new Ping spell and a thrown sack of gunpowder reveal the creatures just in time for Donut, Mongo, and Chris to drive them off before Carl himself is paralyzed and dragged into the personal space's saferoom. There, Mordecai's Floor 6 NPC form is revealed as "Pocket Kuma," a comically small and cuddly bear completely at odds with his usual gruffness, reducing Carl to helpless laughter. The chapter ends with an unexpected knock at the personal space door — the first delivery from the Gate negotiation.

Chapter 3 — Quasar's Condom Speech

Quasar, a foul-mouthed Nullian, introduces himself as Carl's court-appointed attorney, cutting Orren's meeting off cold with a memorable metaphor: he can't stop Carl from "getting fucked" by the Syndicate, but he's the condom. He warns Carl off "naked" (bodiless) Valtay like Orren and explains liaisons exist to manufacture leverage for the system. Together they settle on surrendering the gate as collateral rather than giving it up outright — Carl gets it back on the ninth floor. Back in the personal space, the mercenary package itself arrives: four cretin bodyguards (Bomo, the Sledge, Clay-ton, and Very Sullen) split across the party, plus two bonus spells taught to the mercenaries rather than to Carl directly — a Teleport to Stairwell spell for Bomo and a mysterious spell called Zerzura for the Sledge, Quasar's own suggestion. Katia returns from the previous floor's climax at level 52 with a new Steely Skin passive.

Chapter 4 — The Advanced Bomber's Studio

Carl buys the Advanced Bomber's Studio, a room that lets him simulate explosive yields on virtual targets and dissect ordnance he doesn't own. Donut's five new Legendary Diva spells are cataloged: Standing Ovation, Entourage, Encore, an offensive psionic song, an ice song, and a bonus spell, Laundry Day, that strips armor off a target — none of them useful yet, since her singing can't hold pitch. With the timer on the Hunting Grounds' 30-hour hunter grace period running down, Carl executes Predator, an invisibility-and-infrared recon move, and has Bomo cast the stairwell-teleport spell to jump himself and Donut directly into the hunter capital of Zockau before the hunters are even released.

Chapter 5 — The Zockau Raid

Carl's first strike against the hunters is a bloodbath. He mines the alleys around Zockau's Desperado Club entrance with barrel bombs, then uses the Ring of Divine Suffering — looted earlier, worn for the first time — to mark a drunk hunter, Chin'Dua, as living bomb-bait before beating him to death by hand. Spotting Vrah's flying sister Xindy overhead, he activates his toe ring's Super Spreader ability to copy his own Left to Fester mark onto her from a distance, then finishes her with a five-missile homing salvo that blows her out of the sky. The barrel bombs detonate, leveling a city block and trapping half the Desperado Club's occupants inside. Fleeing on foot, Carl and Donut are hit by a pursuing archer-hunter's crossbow bolts — one buries itself in his leg, another in his shoulder, both carrying a bleeding Blood Trail debuff. Carl collapses at the city border from blood loss and a Woozy-induced coma, saved only when Miriam Dom, Prepotente, and Bianca happen across them on the road outside.

Chapter 6 — Miriam and Bianca

Carl wakes in the back of Miriam Dom's cart, badly wounded but alive, having racked up 34 confirmed hunter kills from the raid. He meets Bianca Del Ciao, Miriam Dom's Hellspawn familiar — a formerly ordinary, formerly-asshole pet goat reborn as a horned, flame-wreathed demon after her soul was corrupted despite a protection spell — and learns only that Miriam herself is now a vampire, without yet learning how. Carl accidentally insults Prepotente (calling him by his hated nickname, "Pony," then telling him to "suck my dick"), who nearly attacks him in a rage before Miriam scolds them both into an awkward, forced hug.

Chapter 7 — The Belching Termite

Carl and Donut reach a bombed-out bugbear settlement and take refuge in a saferoom disguised as a Whataburger. Mordecai, furious over the reckless Zockau raid, tries to have "the talk" with Donut, who preempts him with a rehearsed speech: yes, Carl was reckless, no, she's not leaving him, and no, they are not doing a will-they-won't-they storyline on top of Katia's. Katia, Louis, Firas, and Britney are all gathered in the space; Mordecai instructs the group to open their boxes and settle in for the recap before the chapter ends.

Chapter 8 — The Butcher's Masquerade, Announced

Opening a Gold Junkie's Box from his first ring-kill lands Carl a second, much larger tattoo on his elbow — a sigil granting access to something called the Guild of Suffering, which Mordecai identifies as an obscure cult built around a "memorial crystal" and a demigod called the Night Wyrm, tied to anyone who uses a divine suffering artifact. Carl's 34 Hunter-Killer boxes turn out to contain severed hunter hands and escalating piles of gold (595,000 total) — revolting to Donut, who gets a single hand and a description explaining these are tickets to a prize counter at an end-of-floor event called the Butcher's Masquerade. That night's system message announces private crawler chats are no longer broadcast live (a lawsuit win Quasar had warned Carl not to get his hopes up about, since the hunters'-outside-intel problem is a separate, much shakier case), formally launches the guild system (parties capped at 30, guild charters starting at 500,000 gold), and reveals the Masquerade itself: an invite-only, top-50 party with a pet beauty contest, talent show, and hunter-trade prize booth. Donut immediately begins plotting Mongo's beauty-pageant campaign. The floor's top-10 list shows Carl at #1 with a bounty of 1,000,000 gold.

Chapter 9 — Bombs for the Bridges

With the hunters about to be released, Carl and Katia study the map: the Hunting Grounds spans roughly 100,000 square kilometers, bisected by a single winding river. Carl orders every bridge but one destroyed to funnel hunters into predictable chokepoints. Back at the sapper's table, he builds his largest bomb yet — a five-foot, egg-shaped thermobaric device nicknamed "Just Wait Until Your Daddy Gets Home" — designed for Bomo to wheel out as a suicide-and-respawn attack, over Donut's objections. Mordecai supplies Nitro Sludge, an oxygen-amplifying byproduct of his shield-potion research, as the payload.

Chapter 10 — Point Mongo

Carl and Donut cross into a large Ursine settlement and are turned away at the gate by a "no dinosaurs" town rule expressly written to keep Mongo out (along with bans on magic, dancing, singing, and naiads). Carl bribes the elderly mayor, Elmer, into stepping close enough to take payment, and Donut shoves him down the riverbank slope with Astral Paw; he dies from the fall itself, and a passing naiad drags his corpse into the water before they can loot it. The town falls to Donut, who renames it Point Mongo. Just before the hunter release deadline hits, a note arrives pinned to the personal-space door: Vrah, having somehow learned Carl's exact location despite the communication bans, promises a slow, ritual death in retaliation for her sister Xindy. Carl writes back "Come and get it, bitch" as the system announces the hunters are loose.

Chapter 11 — Mongo's People

Donut's new mayoral collar charm grants her the Snitch skill (summons town guards) alongside stat buffs, and she uses her new authority to strip Point Mongo of its more puritanical ordinances over the town cleric's objections — though Carl talks her out of also scrapping the "bugbears must bathe in the river" rule once he realizes it's a naiad death trap. A trap Carl left on the road nets a hunter kill and a Gold Trapmaster box (a pack of alarm-triggering Fail Safe mods). While arguing with the cleric about reinstating anti-dinosaur ordinances, a new quest, The Recital, appears — something is drawing escalating dinosaur attacks to Point Mongo — and Mongo suddenly bolts from town, drawn by instinct, straight into a semicircle of forty wild velociraptors led by the pack matriarch Kiwi. Carl and Donut nearly trigger a massacre trying to pull him free, until it becomes clear the standoff is a courtship ritual, not an attack — Mongo and Kiwi mate in front of the horrified party.

Chapter 12 — No Matter What

Back in town, Donut suffers a genuine panic attack after nearly losing Mongo, blurting out that she's terrified of being abandoned again (as Katia left, and as Carl keeps risking his life) before shutting down mid-confession about "the ninth floor." Zev interrupts with pointed small talk — an unsubtle warning to drop the subject before their scheduled visit to Odette later that day. Carl finally tells Donut directly, for the first time, that he will never leave her behind, no matter what, sidestepping for now the real problem underneath: the Crown of the Sepsis Whore curse still binding her to the Blood Sultanate's royal line on the ninth floor. The moment is interrupted by Mongo's triumphant, exhausted return from the jungle.

Chapter 13 — Bravvo in the Tree

Elite Signet reappears at Point Mongo's bridge with a new entourage: the ogre Areson the Wise and six were-creature warriors riding a giant caterpillar. They've found a hunter, the yenk Bravvo, immobilized in a tree after Point Mongo's guards shot him out of the sky, and offer him to Carl to finish off as a professional courtesy — the first hint of the "hunting rights" turf war developing between rival factions over Carl and Donut.

Chapter 14 — The Were-Castors

Carl marks and kills Bravvo with the Ring of Divine Suffering, leveling it up. Signet introduces her six warriors — were-castors (transformed beaver-people), survivors of a genocide by then-Princess Imogen decades before Scolopendra's attack — and their caterpillar guardian, Nadine, a transfigured schoolteacher. Signet's own backstory unfolds: a naiad princess's bastard daughter by the high elf king, exiled and cursed so water refuses to touch her, forced into circus life after her mother's murder in a naiad coup.

Chapter 15 — Vengeance of the Daughter

Areson delivers another hunter kill and a hand-drawn map, scrawled on the back of a kids' diner menu, revealing the hunter factions have divided the Hunting Grounds into claimed territories and drawn up a target list — Carl and Donut are double-claimed by both the Dark Hive and the Skull Empire, while the Dream has fixated obsessively on Louis for stealing a photo of their leader's mother to have Juice Box impersonate. Signet formally recruits Carl and Donut into her storyline, The Vengeance of the Daughter: help her retake her mother's naiad throne from the usurping Confederacy at their stronghold, Fort Freedom.

Chapter 16 — Clint and Holger

Two were-castors, bald Clint and mulleted Holger, escort Carl and Donut back toward Point Mongo, bickering and brawling constantly despite genuine affection, then fighting off a night-weasel pack with terrifying, teeth-and-claw efficiency once real danger arrives. Carl receives his third and final sponsor, the Apothecary, shared suspiciously with most of the current top-10 crawlers — a company Carl suspects is a front for Krakaren's collective-mind faction.

Chapter 17 — Samantha's Cousin

Back at base, Samantha throws a screaming fit on learning Donut and Carl are working with Signet, whom she claims (via a tangled royal lineage) is her third cousin and thus a possible source of a new physical body. Carl and Donut are then yanked to an orbital security checkpoint en route to Odette's show, tumbling in near-zero gravity as Earth spins beneath them, before a pair of shade-gnoll mercenaries pat them down and clear them for transfer.

Chapter 18 — Beatrice Is Alive

In Odette's production trailer, Odette drops the floor's first real bombshell: Beatrice survived the initial collection, was rescued by Odette from black-market bounty hunters intent on selling her to Borant as a repurposed country boss, and has been alive and hidden off-world this whole time. Odette wants to bring her onto the show as a ratings coup before a rival program can leak the story first. Carl is furious, suspecting Odette engineered the whole situation; Donut, shaking, insists on going through with the reveal on her own terms rather than let Carl shoulder it alone.

Chapter 19 — All Eyes on Bea

Beatrice appears on a pre-taped segment of Odette's show, thin, drugged, and hollow-eyed. Donut plays it cold through most of the segment before finally breaking character to deliver a devastating, unscripted monologue: she loved Bea unconditionally and was going to be given away anyway, and Bea doesn't deserve the closure of explaining herself. Carl backs her up and ends the reunion outright. Moments later, a system-wide broadcast announces the Valtay Corporation has forcibly acquired 51% of the Borant Corporation from the kua-tin government — a political earthquake Donut appears to have had a hand in, hinting at a secret alliance with Zev and a resistance cell.

Chapter 20 — Viva la Revolución

Aftermath of the Valtay takeover: Odette privately warns, via her assistant Lexis, that the incoming ownership will want to "wipe out and start fresh" with a top-10 of their own choosing — meaning Queen Imogen, the still-unrevealed Floor 6 country boss, is being positioned as a season-ending trap, and Carl and Donut should go down the stairs early rather than attend her looming party. Donut casually reveals she's been smuggling Valtay secret agents to Zev's resistance cell, the Borant Emancipation Front, without realizing the political fallout, leaving Carl (and Lexis) speechless.

Chapter 21 — CrawlCon Fan Box

The recap episode shows Vrah decapitating crawlers mid-hunt and mounting their heads, plus glimpses of Lucia Mar, Eva, and the Meadow Lark splinter team pursuing separate storylines across the floor. A fan box gives Carl a CrawlCon pass for three mandatory virtual appearances (an art-contest judging panel, a "Crawling Through the Ages" panel, and an autograph session) without Donut, sparking her indignation. The guild system launches properly; Katia's team forms Safehome Yolanda under guildmaster Imani. As the party discusses upgrades, a real attack begins: unseen elven artillery starts shelling Point Mongo with poison-gas boulders.

Chapter 22 — The Elven Catapult

Under bombardment from a hidden Dream-faction trebuchet, Carl improvises a guided missile out of Samantha, duct-taping seeking rockets to her head and lobbing her toward the artillery crew with a Major Charlie intelligence potion boosting his Ping range. The strike kills one elf outright, and a recall on Samantha's xistera drags a second, unconscious survivor back with her, clamped onto her teeth. Carl marks and interrogates the survivor, Akland, a self-described "accountant" drafted into the Dream's hunt for Louis, before deciding to kill him with the Ring of Divine Suffering regardless.

Chapter 23 — The Bomb Patch

Killing Akland levels the Ring of Divine Suffering up to two stat points per kill and earns Donut a looted Fireball bracelet, which she immediately equips and threatens to misuse indoors. Aftermath of the catapult fight: Samantha, now covered in gore and freely rolling around like a feral pinball, unsettles even Donut with how quickly her strength is growing beyond what a "harmless" withering spirit should have. Carl reflects on the Vengeance of the Daughter storyline's likely tragic ending and Herot's cookbook advice about surrounding himself with competent allies rather than dead weight.

Chapter 24 — The Rock Chucker

Doubling back to loot the first Dream elf's corpse — killed outright by Samantha's opening missile strike, and carrying a doctored photo of Louis — and to claim the abandoned trebuchet itself, Carl discovers the "Venomous Elven Rock Chucker" — a lightweight, poison-cloud-imbuing siege weapon built from magically-conjured bamboo and suspiciously high-tech metal plates, evidence the hunters are cheating with off-world tech disguised as enchantment. He claims it as siege equipment for later use. Signet's assault team gathers for the Fort Freedom raid; Carl reflects on the political dominoes still in motion — Sensation Entertainment's contested ninth-floor extension, and the growing certainty that the Vengeance storyline is building toward Signet's own death.

Chapter 25 — The Sacrifice

Elite Areson delivers a captured Skull Empire orc, "Future Huntress," for Signet's pre-battle blood sacrifice. Just before Carl marks her, word arrives that a hunter has claimed a top-10 bounty, killing Bogdon Ro along with archer Langley and the whole team who'd cornered him (later revealed to be Vrah's doing). Grief-stricken, Carl kills the sacrifice anyway, reasoning she never should have come. Signet's squad — paper-cutout tattoo monsters brought fully to life — wades into the naiad-held river toward Fort Freedom while Carl and Donut's ground team, plus Samantha thrown in as a distraction, hold the shore.

Chapter 26 — Into Fort Freedom

Samantha splashes into the water bearing a rigged alarm trap, triggers the castle's defenses on cue, and successfully draws the confederate guards toward the front gate while Signet's amphibious squad slips in from the rear. The castle assault initially goes smoothly, but a sudden lightning bolt and a wave of naiad and paper-warrior corpses floating to the surface signal that something has gone badly wrong deep inside.

Chapter 27 — Claude Sludgington the Fourth

Investigating the chaos, Carl accidentally teleports the fight's true obstacle — Claude Sludgington the Fourth, a Level 65 Eryops Borough Boss who's squatted in the throne room for years — directly onto the shore via Samantha, who'd bitten into the amphibian mid-rescue. The lizard-frog boss immediately kills Miss Nadine the caterpillar guardian with a lightning bolt aimed at her as she attacks it, narrowly missing Carl in the process. In the ensuing brawl, Carl's Protective Shell, cast too close, accidentally launches Claude straight into the sky instead of flipping him prone; Donut's first-ever Fireball spell burns a hole clean through his exposed belly as he falls back to earth, pinning him against the trees. Carl finishes the job by diving bare-fisted through the wound with Mongo, punching straight through the creature's body and out the other side as it explodes in gore around them. The fight costs Miss Nadine and, offscreen, the were-castor Clint, both killed in the chaos before Claude even fully manifested.

Chapter 28 — The Blood and Ink Tattoo

With Claude dead and the castle secured, Signet declares Fort Freedom liberated and the naiad Confederacy defeated, completing Vengeance of the Daughter, Part One. Part Two arrives immediately: kill Signet's half-sister, Queen Imogen, at the still-unnamed high elf party everyone already knows is coming. The camp mourns Miss Nadine and Clint in stunned silence as the were-castors search fruitlessly for Clint's body.

Chapter 29 — Miss Nadine's Memory

Signet's elder tortoise companion, Edgar, performs a ritual "blood and ink" tattooing on Signet's skin using Miss Nadine's remains, explaining that her fallen companions live on as sentient "blood and ink elementals" fused into her tattoos rather than true resurrections. The finished tattoo, unexpectedly, brings Clint's memory along with it — the caterpillar teacher had loved him enough that his form survives inside her portrait even without a body to draw from, giving the were-castors a bittersweet keepsake of both losses at once.

Chapter 30 — The Art Contest

Carl's first mandatory CrawlCon appearance is judging a children's art contest, seated alongside a jaded club designer, Hurk, and a barely-conscious camel playwright, G'valt. He fields a stream of unsettling submissions — including a depiction of his own gruesome hypothetical death and a trio of eerily red-eyed goat children from the Plenty faith — and strikes a bargain with Hurk to secure a good score for the head of security's granddaughter in exchange for a plug of the Desperado Club's interior design.

Chapter 31 — Judging Little Monsters

The contest wraps with word that the reigning champion — a slug-child whose portrait of Donut usually wins and took the previous day's round — is expected to riot when it loses this round. Hurk warns Carl, half-joking, half-not, to "be careful" before revealing the real headline event: Carl's upcoming panel will be moderated by the mother of the hunter he just killed, and fandom is buzzing over how badly it's expected to go.

Chapter 32 — The Ultimate Training Room

Zev debriefs Carl on the panel ahead, revealing Circe is a Dark Hive businesswoman rather than actual mantis royalty. Given a four-hour gap before the panel, Carl exploits the production facility's tier-four training room — far beyond anything available in the dungeon this early — to fast-track upgrades to his sapper's table and Powerful Strike skill, and briefly meets an NPC engineer, Dr. Ratchet, setting up his own demonstration table before being ushered toward the stage.

Chapter 33 — Circe Took's Panel

The "Crawling Through the Ages" panel goes exactly as badly as promised: Circe attacks the (illusory) table in front of Carl with her bladed arm, delivers a droning lecture nobody wants, and is repeatedly baited by Carl until, drugged without his knowledge, he hijacks the entire panel to crowdsource tactics against Vrah and the Dark Hive in front of a live galactic audience. A mysterious cloaked woman — a representative of Carl's new sponsor, the Apothecary — publicly intervenes to keep the mic on him before departing, further muddying who exactly is pulling strings on his behalf. Once the panel ends and the studio empties out, Carl finds Dr. Ratchet's level-5 Automaton crafting table and instruction manual left behind on the stage and claims both for himself.

Chapter 34 — Crowdsourcing a Mantis Kill

The panel audience volunteers a wealth of mantis-killing intelligence — vulnerable necks, antidote rings, the fact loud sounds hurt them, and the existence of the pacifist-but-fracturing Nebular Sin Patrol hunting faction, who've begun poaching the Dark Hive's claimed targets out of ancient rivalry. Rushing to prep before his return to the dungeon, Carl catches up on chat: Lucia Mar has trapped Donut in a guildhall standoff with hunters waiting outside for his return, and Samantha — tortured for his return coordinates — fed them a five-meter lie, buying a narrow window before a snitching dryad NPC gives them the truth.

Chapter 35 — The Battle of Alucarda

Carl teleports back into a warzone: Donut has already used decoy clockwork Sledges to spring Lucia Mar's own escape-teleport trap on a stand-in, sending Lucia and her dog away with a fake Donut while the second decoy detonates in the waiting hunter camp, sparking chaos between Dark Hive mantises and Nebular priests. Carl detonates a hob-lobber into the packed crowd, marks and kills several hunters with the ring, and watches an enraged, berserk mantis massacre her own allies before being cut down by one of her own sisters. Vrah finally arrives — bigger and stronger since Zockau, wearing her latest kills' heads as trophies, including the reanimated skulls of Langley and top-10 crawler Bogdon Ro. As Vrah closes in for the kill, the two zombie heads bite into her exposed neck on Carl's cue, and he seizes the opening to ram a looted Arrow of Enthusiastic Double Gonorrhea into her wound before she can shield and flee. Carl detonates the massive "Just Wait Until Your Daddy Gets Home" bomb at the saferoom door, leveling the block — a better outcome than his original plan, since it lets Vrah escape wounded and infected rather than dead, setting up the floor's next crisis.

Chapter 36 — The Apostate Box

With Vrah unable to cure her infection without mating (and mantis mating kills the male), Carl sends the mercenary Bomo into Zockau with a note demanding the Dark Hive's sole remaining sales representative defect for protection in exchange for his gear before Vrah can reach him and pass the disease along. Back in the saferoom, Carl works through weeks of backlogged loot: 14 Hunter-Killer boxes (bonus credit for mantises and nebs killed in the Alucarda chaos) push his trophy count to 52 and net 637,000 gold. A Gold Apostate Box — earned by accidentally shattering a desecrated temple's indestructible shrine when he fell through its roof — brands him with a third tattoo on his left arm: Enemy of the Church of Diwata, a minor nature goddess he must now avoid ever being seen by. Donut finally solves the mystery of her useless Book 3 hobby potion, Scutelliphily (the love of embroidered patches), while admiring his two new upgrade patches, and Carl crosses the 100-strength threshold, picking the passive stat-doubling perk Swole over Donut's favored kick-based option.

Chapter 37 — The Rainbow Bridge

The recap episode replays Donut's earlier fight against Lucia Mar in full: Lucia's dog Cici nearly kills Donut before Donut lures the rottweiler's head through a Hole spell and decapitates her from below, delivering the line "the only bridge you'll be crossing today is made out of rainbows." Lucia's fractured, childlike personality is on full display, oscillating between murderous rage and a confused, almost innocent grief for her dead pet. That night's announcement confirms attendance at the Butcher's Masquerade is mandatory for all top-50 crawlers (plus-ones optional). Bomo returns from Zockau with the Dark Hive's timid sales representative, Edict, in tow — terrified and pursued.

Chapter 38 — Edict, Cornered

Edict explains mantis mating law and honor culture — as a government-contracted merchant, coupling with Vrah (a for-profit hive's representative) would disgrace both families even though he's not directly forbidden from it — and reveals he's already handed off all the gear he was contracted to deliver to the Burrower mantis government to an undisclosed third party, leaving nothing for Carl to seize. Boxed in between mating with Vrah, defying her (inviting her family's revenge on his own), or surrendering the gear (financial ruin and dishonor), Edict picks a fourth option: he deliberately attacks Carl a third time — a violation the system automatically punishes by stripping and teleporting the offender to the nearest monster nest — choosing to die "in battle" with his honor intact rather than face any of the other outcomes. Vrah, already limping into the hallway with her lower body still smoking from the gonorrhea curse (and shedding her trophy heads to lighten herself), watches it happen in real time, shrieking in rage as Edict vanishes. Despite his claim of having nothing left, a small mountain of gold drops at Carl's feet the moment Edict disappears — an unintended parting gift.

Chapter 39 — Prepotente Town Number Four

Carl and Donut spend a stretch of downtime conquering small Ursine settlements and grinding levels, unsettled by lingering questions about Lucia Mar's fractured mind — her ravings about invisible companions, mysterious "points," and getting home to her "papa" suggesting something more complicated than simple insanity. They arrive at a town already claimed and mysteriously massacred by Big Tina, an out-of-control allosaurus tied to the still-unsolved "Recital" quest involving Kiwi's pack.

Chapter 40 — Meeting the Popovs

Carl's second CrawlCon obligation puts him face-to-face, physically, with Dmitri and Maxim Popov for the first time, sharing a cramped, spartan holding cell ahead of a joint autograph session. The brothers reveal genuine warmth beneath their bickering — Dmitri mourns a cat he'd just adopted before the collection — and their nodling race's true nature comes up: dying splits them into new, younger creatures inheriting a fraction of the original's memories.

Chapter 41 — Autographs and Nihit

The autograph session drags on for hours with cosplayers, an unsettling Society for the Eradication of Cocker Spaniels superfan with a possessive tentacle growing from her head, and endless questions about Beatrice and Vrah. The Plenty faction publicly reveals itself as Carl's new benefactor-box sponsor via an unnerving fifteen-second goat cameo. A hostile naga reporter, Nihit, accuses Carl of cheating and looms into his space; Carl stabs him in the neck with a magic autograph pen, ending the panel in chaos.

Chapter 42 — The Price of a Pen

Zev explains the Syndicate's warrant-and-franchise justice system — effectively legalized indentured labor for convicted criminals — and warns Nihit intends to press assault charges once Carl leaves the dungeon, though the odds of it ever mattering are slim given his wealth and notoriety. The looming, unsolved problem of Donut's Crown of the Sepsis Whore curse — binding her to the Blood Sultanate's royal line on the ninth floor — resurfaces as Carl privately worries about the near-impossible task of clearing an entire naga dynasty.

Chapter 43 — Miriam's Call

Back in the dungeon, sponsor gifts arrive in matching pairs for Carl and Donut — a bracelet for her, a jacket patch for him, both warding against vampirism and lycanthropy — hinting the Plenty and Apothecary are coordinating behind the scenes. A recipe for a Charm Animal potion requires a literal liter of Mongo's blood, appalling Donut, before the whole debate is cut short by an urgent message: Miriam Dom is trapped and dying, with only ten hours until sunrise will finish her off.

Chapter 44 — Prudence's Boys

Racing toward Miriam's location, Carl and Donut shelter in an unprotected (non-safe) pub with a terrified ursine barmaid, Prudence, and her two cubs, hiding from a rampaging Big Tina outside. Prudence recounts Tina's origin: she was once a bear cub named Tina, a gifted young dancer whose secret recital was violently broken up by her cleric father, moments before Scolopendra's nine-tier attack transformed the town's women into dinosaurs — Tina into the allosaurus monster, her mother into Kiwi, the pack leader Mongo has already mated with.

Chapter 45 — The Glamoured Fragments

Outside, the town's outskirts are a nightmare of animated body parts crawling toward each other, gradually reassembling into escalating-level "glamoured fragment" monstrosities — Big Tina's doing, feeding a vampirism-fueled undead army. Carl and Donut flee toward Miriam's coordinates, launching missiles into the reassembling pile to slow it down, as reports trickle in that the vampiric infection is spreading fast across the whole forest.

Chapter 46 — Sierra the Vampire Pterodactyl

En route, a levitating Carl is ambushed by a full boss battle against Sierra, a vampirized Northropi mount whose former rider, "Viscount Fog," had been hunting Miriam (for already being a vampire) before dying to his own reflected curse. Sierra crushes Carl in midair before Donut's dawn-lit Torch spell sets her ablaze; recoiling from the light, she flings Carl skyward and stumbles into the tree canopy. Free-falling back down on a health potion, Carl punches straight through her exposed chest — Superman-style — carving all the way through and out her back end, then finishes her off by stabbing her exposed heart with a broken branch. He survives with only bruises.

Chapter 47 — Miriam's Confession

Reaching Miriam and a paralyzed Prepotente, Carl learns the full story: Prepotente had tried to cure Miriam's vampirism with a rare scroll that swaps a curse's "prime" host, but Viscount Fog's countermagic bounced the spell back and forth until both were frozen in a mutual stun-lock, with Prepotente stuck Fragile — one hit from death — and freshly infected with Left to Fester from an accidentally-activated Ring of Divine Suffering that marked Miriam as his only eligible target. Miriam, exhausted and unable to heal Prepotente without killing herself first, quietly reveals a full life she gave up on Earth to care for aging parents and beloved goats, and asks Carl — as the only person who understands loving something the way she loves Prepotente — to be the one to end it. Rather than let her die anonymously, Carl privately puts on his own Ring of Divine Suffering and marks her himself just as dawn breaks, ensuring he — not a stranger — bears the weight of her death. Miriam turns to dust as the sun rises, thanking Prepotente one last time as "my beautiful boy."

Chapter 48 — Left to Fester

Miriam's death instantly cures every crawler and monster infected with vampirism across the floor, but triggers a mandatory world quest, The Creeping Apocalypse: fifty newly-created, uncontrolled "Odious Creeper" monsters, born from Big Tina's abandoned undead army, must be killed by nightfall or face unspecified, catastrophic consequences. Donut wakes Prepotente from his stun-lock; rather than discard his own Ring of Divine Suffering, he swallows it whole and collapses into raw, screaming grief over Miriam's ashes.

Chapter 49 — Kiwi's Pack

Kiwi's raptor pack surrounds the grieving group; Donut successfully tames Kiwi herself with the Charm Animal potion, gaining real influence over the rest of the pack — including, crucially, Tina's own mother — through their loyalty to their leader, though only Kiwi is truly her minion. Prepotente, using an emergency benefactor box and a temporary safe-space wand, pulls a legendary box containing a poison-mist applicator and a custom herbicide recipe that requires Carl's healing potions to brew, then mounts a rapidly-maturing Bianca and departs alone, vowing to kill everyone even remotely responsible for his mother's death, or die trying.

Chapter 50 — Uncle Morty's Weedkiller

Back at the saferoom, Mordecai can't explain why Prepotente swallowed his ring rather than discard it, while dinosaurs wreck the attached pub next door. Katia and Louis arrive with jugs of Mordecai's improvised anti-undead weedkiller, brewed from the recipe and applicator Prepotente received; Louis's Extermination Professional class turns out to have the perfect delivery method, an area-effect ability called Tent the House, usable from the Twister's deck. Louis heads back out to help chip away at the fifty-monster Odious Creeper quota as the kill counter ticks down.

Chapter 51 — Ferdinand's Lightning

Carl discovers the looted Dream-faction trebuchet can deliver poison straight through its sling cup, turning it into long-range artillery for sniping Odious Creepers a mile off with Donut spotting from the treetops — a discovery that hands Donut most of the kill credit and levels, to Carl's mild annoyance, while coordinated teams across the map (Katia's crew, Prepotente solo) chip away at the rest. Then Queen Imogen's honor guard makes its first physical appearance — two white stags and an armored rhino, Simoom, carrying the same unseen, curtained familiar — killing a Creeper before Carl can and confirming Carl and Donut are both guaranteed dance partners at the coming Masquerade. As it departs, the hidden familiar fires an unprovoked lightning bolt at Mongo; Donut dives in front of it and survives only by her Cockroach skill, while Kiwi is blasted and set ablaze attacking the rhino's shield. Recovering, Donut reveals what she saw when the litter's curtain briefly shifted: the familiar is Ferdinand — her real, pre-apocalypse first love, a cat she'd mentioned obliquely since Book 1, now memory-altered and transformed into Queen Imogen's cruel, self-aggrandizing familiar.

Chapter 52 — The Gehenna Bramble

Shaken, Carl privately resolves to take Donut down the stairs early rather than risk her at the Masquerade, but Katia, Imani, and Elle talk him out of abandoning both the guild and the changeling refugees counting on the eventual Zerzura plan; Donut, once she hears, refuses to run too, insisting she's already moved past Ferdinand. Katia hints at a private, unrelated problem she needs to discuss face-to-face, not over chat. As night falls, Big Tina finally appears in full — a bloodied tutu, a spent sparkle wand, and a battered tiara all grown into her hide — thrown into a raptor-restrained tantrum rather than attacking outright. The Creeping Apocalypse quest fails at sundown with two Odious Creepers left unreachable near Zockau, triggering brutal consequences: a new, retroactive "blood bar" mechanic locks crawlers and hunters out of saferooms unless they keep killing, and an uncounterable, exploding wall of thorns called the Gehenna Bramble begins spreading outward from the failure site. A hunter, ejected from his saferoom by the new rule, drops sobbing at their feet.

Chapter 53 — Iota, the Accountant

Carl and the felled hunter, Iota — a drunk, resigned "coin tinker" teleported directly into his path by the new blood-bar rule — trade information before Carl kills him. Iota reveals the crawl's controlling AI is rumored to be a cheap unit bought secondhand from the mantises' retired amusement-park stock, and that it's begun ignoring adverse court rulings entirely — the first confirmation that the AI itself, not just Borant's leadership, is destabilizing.

Chapter 54 — Taming Tina

Carl learns from cookbook lore that castles come in three distinct dungeon archetypes (ordinary buildings, conquerable governmental seats, or self-contained owned villages), foreshadowing the high elf castle's true nature. Realizing the Gehenna Bramble's path will converge on the elf castle right as the floor collapses, Carl and Katia agree to move the whole group toward that corner of the map together, racing to warn the hidden changelings in time. Kiwi walks Big Tina back into camp one last time, and — with Mongo and Donut's help — she's finally, peacefully tamed, resolving the "Recital" quest without a fight.

Chapter 55 — The Nipple Rings

Signet, Areson, and Holger briefly reunite with Carl and Donut to warn that the encroaching Gehenna bramble plague is spreading toward the elf border, and that the dryads' desperate summoning ritual may bring the forest-protector goddess Diwata into the world to intervene. A cryptic, coded benefactor note reveals Circe Took has personally sponsored Diwata — meaning she'd resolved to send a goddess after Carl regardless of how the Odious Creeper court case turned out. In a lighter beat, Carl and Donut both reluctantly pierce their own nipples to equip a set of looted magical rings (including a crucial fall-damage reducer), with Donut extracting a bribe and endless mockery in exchange for going along with it.

Chapter 56 — Zerzura, Fifteen Days Earlier

A flashback fills in the full mechanics of Zerzura, the Sledge's mercenary-installed spell: it teleports an entire town, buildings and NPCs, one floor down (or skips floors entirely on "Scolopendra levels"), but almost always lands in the worst possible location, killing everyone on impact and reanimating them as Children of Inpewt revenants that hunt the caster and every marked survivor until all are dead. Carl weighs this horror against simply abandoning his changeling allies to the collapsing floor and settles on using it as their best remaining option. Back in the present, a system announcement confirms the Masquerade's official rules — no violence, no magic, no weapons inside the ballrooms, all hunters and crawlers present under a guaranteed peace with safe passage promised by host Queen Imogen — and hands out plus-one tokens to the top 50. Donut's talent-show and pageant applications are both accepted, though her plan to make Big Tina's taming the act falls through since the rules require a crawler or hunter to headline. Poring over Edgar's detailed castle map with Katia, Imani, and Louis, Carl lays out the goodwill-ballroom layout (crawlers and hunters kept in separate, magically overlaid rooms) and resolves to whittle the roughly 600-strong hunter turnout down before the party. The chapter ends on an ominous note: Prepotente messages Donut that he has a "present" for her and is already on his way.

Chapter 57 — Katia and Bautista

With the party some 65 hours out, Carl confirms in an awkward, roundabout conversation that Katia and Bautista have quietly become a couple — apparently common knowledge to everyone but Donut, who marches off, delighted and scandalized in equal measure, to interrogate Katia directly. Amid Masquerade prep, Prepotente delivers a cold, curt visit to hand off a mysterious black potion (I Take It All Back, a cure for Scolopendra's transmutation curse) explicitly earmarked for Donut but "do NOT give to Tina" — one of several benefactor items now arriving through third parties rather than directly.

Chapter 58 — Clarabelle's Price

Carl and Donut visit the Desperado Club to reach the changeling contacts sheltering on the club's Hunting Grounds level, off-limits to crawlers since Carl's earlier raid split its floors apart. Bouncer Clarabelle initially refuses to bend the rules, until Donut produces meticulous records proving the club shorted them a security refund years earlier — leverage enough to secure a secret bathroom stairwell down to the restricted level. Sneaking through that level, Carl kills an unaffiliated Dreadnought hunter bare-handed in a restroom and makes contact with two changeling representatives, handing off evacuation plans, before club security corners them — Astrid, the club's level-125 Bloodlust Sprite assistant manager, sets Carl's blood boiling and hauls him off unconscious.

Chapter 59 — Orren's Warning

Carl wakes in liaison Orren's office, delivered there by Astrid after the confrontation, to learn Orren is departing his post permanently under the Valtay reorganization. Orren cryptically warns that not every liaison shares his restraint before finally connecting Carl to Quasar for a court-supervised legal call — during which a grieving superfan and her possessive head-tentacle, "Maggie," make an unsettling cameo pleading Princess Posse business.

Chapter 60 — The Automaton Table

Carl begins experimenting with his stolen Automaton crafting table, though most recipes need parts he doesn't have yet. Mordecai and Zev fill in the wider political fallout of the floor's unprecedented hunter body count — Borant is quietly profiting even as the Syndicate government hemorrhages money, and new legal rulings are barring further lawsuits against the AI itself in an attempt to slow its deterioration. As Donut wrangles pageant costumes, the group launches its first coordinated, cross-guild hunter raids; one already cost Carl a god's favor after he unknowingly killed an Emberus worshipper, earning a temporary Shunned penitence debuff, so on this next raid Donut handles the kill triggers on a suspected Emberus worshipper while Carl hangs back. The hunters, propped up by increasingly absurd sponsor-gifted tech (anti-air guns, portable pulse rifles restricted to their now-dead owners), are otherwise getting picked off in droves now that the brambles and the new blood-bar rule have forced them into the open.

Chapter 61 — The Coordinated Raids

Carl's group, now coordinating across multiple teams by chat, runs another string of hunter raids using seeker-spider automatons, Ping-and-Tripper combos, and Donut activating the kill triggers to bank experience for herself. The raid nets dozens more hunter-killer trophies before Carl's group turns toward a final, larger target — a church defended by mushroom guards — just as an unrelated, unexplained divine warning mark appears over Carl's head. The warning proves catastrophic: a hunter fleeing into the town temple is consumed by an explosive green transformation, and a minor nature goddess, Diwata — sponsored into physical form by Circe Took — bursts free from the wreckage as a squirrel-form deity before rocketing away within her five-minute window. Samantha's lore dump and the group's own math peg her true purpose: she's a shapeshifting fertility deity who mates with (and gives birth as) whatever she last "naffed," and she's here to cure Vrah's gonorrhea infection the same way — meaning Circe has bankrolled a literal god to personally save her daughter, and Vrah is now back in the hunt. Elsewhere, Big Tina wanders into town and casually devours an unconscious guard, unbothered by Kiwi's scolding.

Chapter 62 — The Number Seven

With the brambles closing on elf territory, Carl finds a weary Signet resting alone and privately convinces her to abandon her plan to attack Queen Imogen the instant the party starts, warning her (with a nudge from Zev) that the showrunners won't let a secondary elite's climax pre-empt the main event — he talks her into infiltrating the castle in secret and waiting for his signal instead. Back at camp, Mordecai and Carl notice an odd detail on two of Donut's mysteriously sponsor-gifted items — an enchanted stick and a small hammer, both otherwise inert — a hidden engraved "7" on each, hinting at a purpose tied to Floor 7 rather than anything usable now. With a stairwell sitting right outside camp, Carl briefly weighs abandoning the Masquerade entirely, recognizing the sponsors seem to be preparing Donut, specifically, to be the survivor of whatever's coming.

Chapter 63 — Queen Imogen's Twin

Carl circulates a written battle plan among the guild (goal: survive, with killing every last hunter dead last on the priority list) while the group loads into an escorted caravan for the castle. An elf footman, Theobold, lays out the Masquerade's protocol — goodwill ballrooms, no weapons, no magic, guaranteed peace under Queen Imogen — while the changeling Pearson rides disguised as Signet to gauge the guards' reaction. Mid-ride, Queen Imogen herself teleports directly into Carl's wagon to confront him over the decoy. She turns out to be a dead ringer not for Beatrice (as everyone feared) but for Ifechi, Florin's crawler girlfriend killed back in Book 4.

Chapter 64 — Entering Ballroom A

Katia quickly radios that Imogen isn't Ifechi at all but her previously-unmentioned twin sister. Imogen lingers in the wagon to recount the mythic origin of the Masquerade's non-violence spell and warn Carl explicitly: break the peace, and Apito's wrath, not hers, will be the one to punish him — confirming the group's entire plan to force a fight inside the ballroom is dead on arrival. At the castle, stablemaster Kibben separates the animal attendants, and Carl finalizes the goodwill-ballroom logistics with the guild by chat before the group is patted down and led into Ballroom A. Inside, Empress D'Nadia reveals she's judging both the pet and talent shows, and Vrah — crotch fire finally extinguished — charges straight at Carl the moment she spots him.

Chapter 65 — Britney's Butterfly

While Vrah threatens Carl in front of D'Nadia, Britney quietly disables the room's alarm-light system using a stuffed slate butterfly from her jacket, buying the group's covert plan crucial cover. Elsewhere, Katia has to be physically restrained from attacking the traitorous Eva, Florin nearly confronts a fragile, dissociative Lucia Mar, and Prepotente demands (and is refused) a spot in Carl's party for the remainder of the floor. As Theobold formally opens the party, Signet suddenly walks into the ballroom — not smuggled in by the party at all, but personally delivered by Apito herself as part of the goddess-curated guest list.

Chapter 66 — Signet Crashes the Party

Signet explains to a rattled Carl and Imani that Apito herself appeared and invited her directly, confirming the entire guest list — Signet included — was hand-picked by the goddess specifically to test Queen Imogen, who (per Signet) has never once actually won the boon a completed Masquerade is supposed to grant. Amused that her sister can't touch her without breaking the peace, Signet drifts off to chat up the three off-world celebrity judges instead, unnervingly aware that they aren't really "here" at all.

Chapter 67 — The Prize Counter

Carl visits the Masquerade's prize counter, run by Chaco, a wolf-headed bard with a painful shared history with Mordecai, to spend his stockpile of hunter hands, trading barbs along the way with a resigned alien hunter, Zabit, about the economics of the hunt. Among the catalog — potions, upgrade scrolls, a sold-out "Seventh Floor Pole Position" boon Prepotente already snapped up — sits a memorial crystal at the top tier: a storehouse of god-tier knowledge, revealed to belong to Queen Imogen's own necklace and rumored, impossibly, to have come from a dead god. Carl falls one hand short of affording it as the pet show begins.

Chapter 68 — Mongo's Moonwalk

Donut's pet-show entry — Mongo, hyped by Louis's over-the-top emcee routine and a blasted Nicki Minaj track — turns out to include a fully-trained moonwalk, stealing the room from every other entrant, including Tserendolgor's giggling, tank-like "tummy acher" pet. Backstage, Elle learns from a grieving hunter that Vrah's people tricked his own brother into the temple as Diwata's unwitting birthing vessel, and the group realizes the goddess is still trapped on the floor, indefinitely occupied giving birth to a swarm of mantis nymphs — Vrah's own children and half-siblings at once. Word arrives that mantis reinforcements are converging on the stairwells outside.

Chapter 69 — Ferdinand's Turban

Florin's attempt to intervene between Lucia Mar and the room takes a stranger turn: the crawler he catches comforting a sobbing, clinging Lucia briefly switches to a distinct personality — a ten-year-old Dutch girl named Jill, apparently one of several real children trapped inside Lucia's fractured mind and periodically able to surface, seemingly controlled from afar by "the dog." Before Carl can process it, Lucia snaps back to her usual murderous self, and Zev shuts down further questions. Ferdinand saunters onto Carl's shoulder wearing a ridiculous feathered turban to gloat, and Carl signals Samantha to make her move while he's distracted.

Chapter 70 — The Room Seals Shut

Donut, boosted to a god-tier 276 charisma by her benefactor tiara, works to charm Ferdinand mid-conversation while Katia confirms the stat math checks out even against a Province Boss. Outside, the plan unravels fast: Gideon reports elven cavalry pouring out to fight the changelings' airship, and the Twister is swarmed and overrun by mantis nymphs, forcing the Sledge to crash it into two of the castle's sentinel towers rather than lose it outright. Samantha, sent through the castle's cat-sized tunnels toward the security room, kills the five guards there without her sleep-gas potion (having stashed it with Clay-ton so it wouldn't clink) just as the talent show opens — and just as Queen Imogen materializes in the ballroom without warning, sealing the room shut for the rest of the party.

Chapter 71 — No Way Out

A bloodied Queen Imogen materializes in the ballroom — she'd been out fighting personally — and confirms the room's peace seal has locked everyone inside for good, herself included, at exactly the moment neither side can safely make a first move. Word arrives that Gideon's whole distraction team has been killed and the Twister destroyed, while Samantha discovers Vrah's own inside agent has already sabotaged the hunters' ballroom and is trying to do the same to theirs — the enemy's real plan, Carl realizes, is Circe Took herself, disguised among the mantis nymphs and coordinating with her daughter to collapse the goodwill system entirely. With every backup plan failing, Carl privately resolves to sacrifice himself and Eva to break the seal, only for Signet to insist on a better option: casting her tattoo-summoning spell using herself as caster, sacrifice, and executioner all at once.

Chapter 72 — Signet's Sacrifice

Donut's charm song All Eyes on Me and Big Tina's recital wand hold the entire ballroom transfixed as Sledge begins the five-minute Zerzura cast inside the besieged castle. Signet slits her own throat in front of her horrified sister, shattering Apito's protection and ending the Masquerade's non-violence spell for good — her final act framed explicitly as a message to the watching galaxy that her family, real or not, mattered. Carl marks Vrah with the ring, tosses smoke bombs, and gives the signal.

Chapter 73 — Sic 'Em

The seal breaks and everything erupts at once: Kiwi's disguised velociraptors leap off the stage into the hunters, Mongo and Samantha bring down Vrah for good, and Signet's animated tattoo-warriors materialize at full, terrifying scale to hold off Queen Imogen while mantis nymphs pour up through the shattered floor. Imogen retaliates with a room-wide lightning blast and nearly kills Carl with a bone-snapping telekinetic grab before Ferdinand — now genuinely loyal — tackles her and is savagely backhanded for his trouble. Donut's I Take It All Back potion cures Kiwi of her transformation mid-battle, but Tina, seeing her mother restored, can't follow — she remains locked in allosaurus form. Sledge finishes casting Zerzura in the nick of time, teleporting the surviving changelings and the still-half-destroyed castle straight to the ninth floor as everyone left behind freezes in midair.

Chapter 74 — Cage Fight Extreme

With the castle gone, everyone remaining — crawlers, hunters, Queen Imogen, and the newly-exposed, still-mid-birth Diwata — is rebranded by the AI as a four-way boss battle royale, plummeting together into the castle's exposed, mantis-choked basement pit as "Thunderstruck" blares. Donut's maxed Laundry Day spell strips Diwata's divine armor away, letting Circe Took's own newborn mantis children tear their mother apart in a berserk feeding frenzy. Imogen falls to a coordinated, beat-synced barrage of blunt-force attacks, finished off by Prepotente smashing a potion directly into her face.

Chapter 75 — We Are Goddamned Alive

The cost of the battle is brutal: Firas, Gwen, Horton, and both Popov brothers are killed outright (though the Popovs' nodling deaths split them into two rescued, ineligible infant crawlers who are immediately pulled from the dungeon), Tran loses both legs, and Britney's face is permanently scarred saving the group with her butterfly jacket. Katia finds and finishes off a buried, barely-alive Eva off-page, earning a second player-killer skull. In the shaky aftermath, Carl talks Donut through her guilt over not grieving hard enough, the group claims two open Faction Wars slots for The Princess Posse (Carl and Donut's own newly-sponsored team) and Princess D'Nadia's Prism Kingdom, and Carl uses his last moments on air to publicly shame the other faction-wars sponsors into a vote on removing the "safety protections" that keep non-crawler teams from real danger.

Epilogue — The Great Race

Floor 6 collapses into Floor 7, "The Great Race," dropping every crawler into an individual glass starting pod arranged in a spiraling stack of stairwell portals. Prepotente, having pieced the floor's true nature together from his late mother's item-lore boots and an overheard aside on a CrawlCon panel, deliberately shatters his own pod's reinforced glass with a hammer-and-rod combo — collapsing the entire level's Prince Rupert's Drop-style maze structure before it can properly begin, over the AI's own panicked, in-voice objections. Squads are capped at five and locked for the floor. Given ninety seconds to choose a starting location on a spinning globe of Earth, Donut — squad leader by default — picks the Caribbean instead of the intended Bahamas, to Carl's exasperation. Elsewhere, a shaken Katia hunts down and personally kills Eva, only for Eva's dying hand to trigger a Crown of the Sepsis Whore hidden on her own armor — the same crown Donut lost back on Floor 3 — which binds itself to Katia's bare head instead (the protective hat that would have stopped it is the one she'd handed off to Carl mid-battle), meaning only one of them will now be allowed to leave the ninth floor.

Sourced from Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade.
