Offered low-floor undead, city attendant, or game guide, he thinks of the cookbook — of the pride of adding to it, and the guilt of not writing more — and takes the game-guide deal, a hundred seasons, knowing it means never learning whether she lived. Top level 89. Survived his indentureship. Author of the second edition. Current status: Missing. Wanted by Syndicate Security.

docs.title: Part I — The Ceasefire
docs.text:
Chapter 1 — Welcome to Faction Wars

Carl and Donut land face-first in a drained, stinking alley in Larracos, City of Dreams. 32,429 crawlers remain; 30 days to collapse; a 60-hour ceasefire, after which only Team Retribution and its allies may stay in the city. Carl's Scavenger's Daughter is dangerously full of souls — Soul Poisoning, blocked partway by his Emberus ring — so he vaporizes a dead concierge shark with Daughter's Kiss. Eight teams immediately form the Bloc and declare war on both Team Retribution and the Princess Posse; Donut accepts the NPC truce before Carl can finish a sentence, keeping them in the city, and Ferdinand promptly renames the alliance "Ferdinand and his Bird." Cascadia — audibly drunk or worse — lays out the rules: ten teams arranged as a pie around Larracos, the city sealed until four teams remain, then the Peeling of Larracos, where attackers need the throne room for six hours and defenders need to hold a week. A team dies when its warlord dies or its throne falls. Donut picks her new class: Deathbed Hellcat, a long-range sniper-assassin that quadruples her spell range, grants at-will invisibility — and comes with a hat and a ghillie suit she does not yet understand.

Chapter 2 — The Ghillie Suit

In the guild saferoom Donut refuses to wear the ghillie suit ("I'll look like a tassel") but approves of the boonie hat, which grants a Targeting skill and stacks with the suit to let her snipe line-of-sight enemies from over a mile out. Mordecai's Floor 9 form is a bespectacled Canadian in a snowsuit and raccoon hat who says "aboot" and gets furious when it's pointed out; his upgraded alchemy table now lets him reverse-engineer recipes, and he is giddy. Mongo's burnt wing will be regrown by a Revitalize Pet potion. Carl works through fifty-plus backlogged achievements — Lord of the Flies for trapping a fellow crawler, Chickenshit Exploit for breaking the card system, Touched by a Demon (only one ever awarded), a Crab Chowder achievement that permanently adds a "chowder style" option to every food box, and an ominous, groaning Unbirthing for teleporting into Samantha's neck hole that ends with the AI telling him he is in fucking trouble.

Chapter 3 — The Tiara of a Thousand Lights

Donut's boxes: a Shield spellbook, a Sentry war-protection spellbook, and a smoking, screeching black tome called You're Not Done Yet that makes Mordecai step backward in fear. Her celestial benefactor box — from the baffling sponsor Long Haul Biological Waste Management Solutions — delivers the Tiara of a Thousand Lights and its charge pillow: any enchanted hat left on the pillow for ten hours is permanently drained and its buffs transferred into one of the tiara's 99 absorption jewels. A second, purple pillow arrives from the Apothecary, doubling the charging rate. Then Quan's Cloak of the Benevolent Champion, the first celestial item ever awarded on Earth: it raises the wearer's lowest stat to match their highest over 66 hours, grants Find Weakened, and pushes four spells and one skill to level 15. Mordecai's trick is a MySpace Photo potion that fakes Donut's Charisma 30 points high, so her Constitution climbs from 4 to 193. The cloak buffs Bad Attitude, Wall of Fire, Heal Critter, and Puddle Jumper.

Chapter 4 — Gloom Wraith Phase

Carl's turn: a fan box of ammunition and a leather shoulder holster for his father's Glock (he has no intention of ever using it), automaton fabricator parts, a Spider Reaper Minion patch that opens the Midnight Market, a town-upgrade coupon, bagpipes, and the Enchanted Toe Ring of the Well-Balanced — Heart Balance (an auto-trigger healing potion at 2%), Mind Balance (protection from enslavement and conscription), and Physical Balance, which lists Walk on Air as "already obtained," a gift Carl realizes with revulsion came from eating Li Jun's eye. The ring immediately reports Mind Balance is currently triggered. His Celestial Heavy Metal box — delivered by a demon drum kit — is a talking, hell-kissed skill potion that grants Gloom Wraith Phase, level 13: non-corporeal lunges that unravel unarmored flesh. Mordecai, shaken, tells them they are now the two most powerful crawlers he has ever worked with. "Good," Carl says. "Because we have eight whole armies to kill."

Interlude — Dante (3rd Edition)

A crocodilian game guide and trap-master instructor reads a newsletter announcing that the guild staff are being reassigned as ice castle guards for the coming eighth floor. Beside him is his skyfowl neighbour Justice Light, ten seasons into an indentureship he specifically negotiated: he demanded to be made the shopkeeper of the very NPC he murdered during his own crawl, and he spends his days rearranging shelves and sewing strange three-dimensional fabric sculptures. Dante recognized him instantly as a fellow cookbook owner and transferred guilds just to be near him, but never told him — guilt, he thinks, at having written only a single entry. Justice Light says flatly that he will refuse to fight crawlers. Nothing good will happen if he does, Dante tells him, and privately admits he has plenty of violence in his heart, just not for the innocent. Top level 89. Killed by administrative action for refusing to follow orders, 14 seasons short of freedom. Author of the third edition. Current status: Dead.

Chapter 5 — Sir Rendlegore

Carl finally confesses to owning Garret, Ren's tummy acher — who died a fifth time and reverted to a nameless, memoryless level-1 meatball. Donut treats it as an affair. The creature immediately climbs into Mongo's mouth, is swallowed, and is yakked back up giggling. Bonded over a bowl of chowder, he needs a name, and after a long argument Louis lands on Sir Rendlegore — "Rend" — which honours Ren without making him a copy. Meanwhile Samantha has escaped to hunt Tish, Ghazi's ex-girlfriend at the Larracos college, and Katia has to chase her down. Katia then attempts Carl's hair restoration; Splash Zone's power-wash fails because his spell counts as offensive in a saferoom, and Carl emerges from the shower with waist-length romance-novel hair that regrows every two hours for the next fortnight. Donut goes around the room physically touching people to make them officers; Florin becomes General, Louis becomes Army Air General.

Chapter 6 — Party Planner

Louis's celestial box: an Airship Portal guild upgrade (a dimensional hangar and elevator, with a vulnerable trapdoor on the saferoom roof), and an aircraft. Waiting for the elevator, Carl notices a strand of Christmas tinsel that survived the memory collapse and has a small vertigo of realization — they are living in a simulation of a simulation, where make-believe consequences are often deadlier than real ones — and remembers Lightning Lou, the old dog at the Florida gas station, and Paulie's warning. The eye on his chest blinks. Then the elevator opens on Party Planner: a fifty-foot silver "Casket in the Sky" tilt-rotor stealth light bomber, with room for five crew, a bomb bay that boosts all yields by 50%, and almost no defensive armament. Florin calls it a half-sized B-17 crossed with a stealth bomber. Carl calls it a death trap.

Chapter 7 — War Leader Arief

Leaving through the college saferoom, Donut discovers Louis's enchanted "Donut Holes" bootleg fan-club t-shirt — a cartoon of her backside, complete with an implied butthole — and demands royalties from Zev, who informs her the licensing threshold has never been reached by any crawler. Outside, Larracos is staggering: a Tolkien college of alabaster towers, flowering vines, and NPCs who are visibly preparing for war rather than going about their lives. They are met by War Leader Arief, a young Semeru dwarf in parade armour and a feathered heirloom helmet, commander of the Larracos Defense Force Infantry and carrying a Despondent debuff because his goddess Ysalte is dead. His people's history is the floor's real tragedy: millions of Semeru dug toward the gods, found the roots of the All Tree, built their castle as an apology — and were annihilated by Scolopendra's nine-tier attack, leaving fewer than ten thousand stewards of an empty city. Arief then bows to Louis: Warlord Juice Box wishes to solidify the truce in the traditional manner. Through marriage. Immediately.

Chapter 8 — Down Through the Rings

The walk down the funnel city, ring by ring, recruiting crawlers as they go. Arief explains the 66 nominal levels, the explosive traps on every other down-ramp, the flooding that reached ring 39 and is now held at ring 3 to keep the castle underwater. Crucially, he speaks of previous seasons: most of the NPCs now remember their past lives, and his uncle is one of the Jatismara who recall dozens of them. He names Architect Houston of the Madness, the Viceroy who tortured his brother, and explains why nobody — not even Juice Box — has ever infiltrated the naga inner sanctum: a court of assassins, not warriors, with poisons and acids and a Sultana nobody is permitted to look upon. Carl adds what Drakea and Mordecai have taught him about real naga politics: the "Blood Sultanate" is a PR exercise by the modern naga constitutional monarchy, the in-game Sepsis Whore is the actual crown princess, and she has never once been killed in Faction Wars. They reach the reopened Desperado Club, where Juice Box is waiting in a back office in the body of an elderly gnoll manager — who leaps across the desk and kisses Louis full on the mouth.

Chapter 9 — Juice Box's Ledger

Juice Box, back in human form on Louis's lap, is scarred and exhausted and clearly frightened, and she pointedly puts some of her papers in a drawer before sharing the rest: enemy maps, troop strengths, resupply schedules, and her abandoned plan to burn the Shanty Town food markets. Shanty Town — a ring of hovels that sprang up around the top entrance, far larger than any previous season, almost certainly someone's Emergency Action Item — will remain accessible to the Bloc after the ceasefire. Its current mayor, to Carl's dismay, is Ferdinand, who cannot be killed because the workaround that let the NPCs field a team routed the city defense system through him. Juice Box has no warlord menus, only messages and floating text, and is plainly out of her depth in a world with rules. Louis, prompted relentlessly by Donut over chat, stands, takes her hand, and agrees to marry her at once — she squeals, turns into a blonde cheerleader, and kisses him.

Chapter 10 — A Bowler Hat for a Town

At the Desperado Club entrance, Clarabelle the crocodilian bouncer informs them all crawlers are banned: the new management is Hamed — the Night Wyrm, leader of the Guild of Suffering, Astrid's husband and father of the strippers Damascus Steel and Anaconda, who are still somewhere inside hunting him. Ferdinand appears riding the head of Drick the Valtay-infested Dream elf, wearing a turban improvised from toilet paper and calling himself Donut's fiancé. Carl trades him Quan's boomerang bowler hat for the mayorship of Shanty Town, and Ferdinand accepts before he's finished admiring himself in Britney's mirror ("I'm a very handsome boy"), also renaming the truce "The Good Guys." Then the small wedding: changeling marriages come in two parts, a private legal ceremony now and a Confirmation in a month, with divorce papers signed in advance that expire if unfiled. No rings, no singing, no officiant. Louis whispers I wish my mom was here, they exchange private vows, and it's done. Then Carl's recruit notifications begin blinking so fast he has to mute them, and Florin tells him to get to the base immediately.

Interlude — Tipid (4th Edition)

A Crest poisoner sits in a zero zone with blood on his hands that isn't there, unable to tell how much time has passed. His memory slides between the outreach guild at the start of the twelfth floor — where the key he found only let one of them out, and he chose himself over Horatio, who had a wife and a child waiting — and the present, solars later, where a brusque agent named Damien is explaining that Tipid has completed his contract and is free, but that the brain lesions he never negotiated coverage for will cost him his entire pension and a loan on top. He asks to keep the key he bought with an extra season of servitude, then snaps the chain and throws it across the table. Top level 96. Retired to a Crest system to work for a waste management company. Author of the fourth edition. Current status: Colonel in the Princess Posse Faction Wars team.

Chapter 11 — Fifty Thousand Volunteers

Carl walks into the Meadowlark saferoom and finds two Crest standing there: Rosetta Thag and Tipid, both level 60, both listed as Colonels in the Princess Posse — and behind them, per Florin, just over 50,000 former crawlers. Tipid hugs him and says we've been watching, and we couldn't watch anymore. Rosetta slaps him on the forehead ("a self-correcting measure given in the spirit of comradery"), then reaches down his shirt to feel the tattoo and demands the last sliver of toraline, the spider's ink, four million gold, and access to every crafting room. The story: Dr. Porthus Hu built the Crawler Project and then the Open Intellect Pacifist Network, won released crawlers automatic Syndicate citizenship, and refitted a garbage freighter into a passenger liner when he put out the call. They came anyway, even after the protections were turned off. The catch is that all eight enemy teams got the same last-minute boost — roughly 20,000 hired mercenaries each, allowed in with their own weapons and armour. 150,000 new enemies.

Chapter 12 — The Base Camp

The Princess Posse base camp is a construction site and a revelation: watchtowers, trench-scroll channels, palisade walls being fireballed as they're tested, thousands of Fortification Engineers who level by building. Penn, a mountain of a man carrying a twenty-foot H-beam, drops it and hugs Carl — and then the whole camp, thousands strong, takes up a pounding hup, hup, hup war chant that shakes the ground. This is for you, Tipid tells him in chat. This is what you built. Tipid walks him through the new rules: saferooms revert to the blood-bar system once fighting starts, mercenaries are barred from guildhalls in the last two phases, and the stronghold must be built around the bait-shop saferoom so airships can dock. Florin covers scouting: only 18 Scout endorsements, towers needed for full coverage, and an absolute certainty that the camp is already riddled with enemy spies. The chapter ends on the stronghold's oversized door flying open and Big Tina bounding out into the clearing in her pink tutu.

Chapter 13 — Kiwi and the FUPA

Tina hops in circles around Mongo grunting "Pa-pa!" — she can talk now. Behind her waddles Kiwi — born ursine, turned dinosaur by Scolopendra's attack, turned back during the Butcher's Masquerade, and now enormously, about-to-pop pregnant with Mongo's litter. She hugs the bewildered dinosaur once, without a word, and takes her daughter back inside to make dinner. The fortress itself is named the Fortress of Unyielding Power and Authority — the AI locked the name in place the instant it noticed the acronym, and Carl gleefully spreads the FUPA across the entire army over Donut's furious objections. Inside, the castle is murder-holed corridors leading to a bare twenty-by-twenty throne room, walls glowing with eight of twelve possible enchantments. And in the antechamber, Elite Herman the Fleet is writhing behind his desk, fighting a compulsion, begging Carl to tell his brother he's sorry — and he is wearing explosive satchels under his clothes, an assassination ordered through Sensation Entertainment, now owned by the Dream. Donut's Magic Missile and Baroness Victory's battle-axe end it simultaneously; Carl inventories the destabilizing corpse. The orc adjutant calmly announces she will file a foul against the Dream, argues aloud with the AI about it, accepts its apology, and walks back into the flag room as though she'd stepped out for coffee.

Chapter 14 — The Flag Room

Inside the flag room — where nothing said is broadcast for eight days, and where the interface turns into an unwieldy city-builder's control panel — Carl finds the horror buried in his spam folder: hundreds of suppressed notifications reading Gloom Wraith Phase failed to activate. Mind Balance prevented activation. Shi Maria has been trying to cast through him nonstop, and Mind Balance has climbed from 5 to 9 holding her off. Had she succeeded, the phase would have detonated the bombs and killed Donut. Victory then lays out the four phases and the Ramp-Up rules: no offensive magic, no teleport magic or skills, entry only through kilometre-wide corridors — deliberately engineered to force hand-to-hand slaughter for 180 hours while the enemy holds pulse rifles and power armour. And there are 100,000 troops massing on the northern border.

Chapter 15 — The Skank Skunks

A mob-clearing hunt at the expanded edge of the map, with Chris, Jamal, the laconic Land War veteran Bodi, and two loud, freshly-tattooed tenner elves, Griffin and Morales. The target is a Rolling Battle Formation Ball, a level-70 riff on the first floor's Ball of Swine, which Carl cracks open with two hob-lobbers, raining three dozen Skank Skunk Warriors across the forest. Rend gets his first kills — chomping through necks like a food processor and swelling from meatball to beach ball, reaching level 8 — and Carl uses Gloom Wraith Phase for the first time, unravelling four skunks into ribbons of flesh inside their own armour. Then Donut knocks out Fancy Boy, the battle wizard whose control was the only thing suppressing the spray, and the entire remaining horde lets go at once. Donut, Mongo, Griffin, and Morales spend the next three hours violently, inconsolably Skanked. Jamal, who can no longer smell and who yearns only to hop, breaks his third automaton leg harness.

Interlude — Everly (5th Edition)

A sward mantis and her last two mercenaries are being slowly crushed as a ceiling descends on a sand-filled room ten flights below the top of a tower. The tower was an advertisement. Her sponsor, Dictum Waystation Controls, gifted her Gordon's Compass of Vertical Labyrinth Management — 49 uses, exactly one short of the fifty floors — specifically to lead her to a paper note at the summit slandering a competitor. Everly refused every offer of help from her fellow mantises, on this floor and every floor before it, because she left her colony rather than abide its lack of individualism. Watching the dwarf dig bloody-fingered for a keyhole with no key, she recognizes her queen's phrase for the moment hope drains out: the Inevitable Ruin. And she realizes it did not happen here — it happened when she abandoned the others. As the ceiling reaches them, the silent ogre's eyes flicker like a screen booting up and a different voice says, "Maybe it's not inevitable, like you say." Top level 62. Crushed to death on the eighth floor. Author of the fifth edition. Current status: Dead.

Chapter 16 — Glory Bound

Two patients, one jar. Katia must re-live her worst memory under a modified Glory Bound to break the addiction; Carl takes the same dose cut with Removal Order so he enters Shi Maria's memory instead of his own, where he can lock her in permanently — if he can work out how, since the mechanism manifests differently every time. His toe ring has to come off for it to work. Bucket Boy asks whether his head will explode; Mordecai says probably not. As they go under, Katia admits her favourite memory and her worst are the same one, and reaches out; their hands twist together before Imani can separate them, and Carl's consciousness floods out of himself and crashes into hers — and in the backsplash he brushes the minds of Imani (terrified), Mordecai (wary and sad), Rosetta (exhausted, full of familiar rage), and Edgar. Katia tells him she isn't angry at him, she's angry that he lets people hurt him. Then a warlord notification cuts her off: the Lemig Sortion offers free passage to parlay.

Chapter 17 — Eleven Hours Lost

Carl wakes standing in a ballroom of the high elf castle, drenched head to foot in blood, ringed by fifty corpses, eleven hours gone, with Quest Failed: The Bedlam Bride on his HUD. A Lemig goblin shoots him in the face and is frozen mid-trigger-pull by the ceasefire. He remembers the dream — Katia's ex Fannar telling the adoption agency about her decade-old addiction out of spite, the denied adoption, the cancer diagnosis, baby Annie in the crib — and remembers Hapanzi, Shi Maria's husband, a god in the shape of a spider, telling him I have her now, son. She is good and trapped. You can always set her free, if you must. But do not unless all is lost. Commander Stockade, a weeping seven-foot caterpillar with a Southern Californian surfer accent, is screaming at his adjutant that the massacre should be appealable; his beloved Luke is among the dead. Three adjutants teleport in and a minor quorum is called. Carl can now see through the eye on his chest, and has to consciously hold it shut, because the power behind it is enormous.

Chapter 18 — The Minor Quorum

In Queen Imogen's private kitchen — with an absurd, jarring bag of Earth cat food from a Seattle pet charity propped against the wall — the dreadnaught Panford reconstructs the plot on a floating screen. Stockade offered a parlay through the warlord chat and timed a level-15 Summon Ally to arrive in the sliver of time between Carl drinking the sleep potion and Imani prying off his toe ring, knowing the entity could accept on his behalf and hoping either to leave Shi Maria loose in the Princess Posse camp or simply kill Carl. It half-worked: the system split him, leaving a translucent avatar in each base. Pressed on how he timed it so exactly, Stockade blurts out that the Posse must be cheating too, and in doing so admits on the record that he was being fed live intelligence from outside the dungeon. Worse, the screen replays Katia's dream for the room, and Carl's demand that they turn it off is ignored. Houston never speaks, never moves, and simply watches Carl. Meanwhile the borders erupt: Prepotente reports trebuchets ranging in and a hundred invisible Madness mercenaries massing, Elle reports camo netting coming off tanks, and everyone scrambles to positions that aren't finished.

Chapter 19 — Stockade's End

Victory explains how Mordecai turned it around: knowing he was being illegally watched, he announced he was brewing a wake-up salve and actually brewed something to violently expel the spider, which fired at the exact moment Stockade cast to pull Carl fully across. Carl turned into Shi Maria in the middle of the Lemig throne room and butchered it, screaming "I have always loved you" and "I didn't kill you, Hapanzi!" with her jaws still unhinged around her husband's leg, her Insanity spell driving the survivors to murder each other and themselves. Luke died throwing himself in front of Stockade. Ferdinand burns an Emergency Action Item to black out all outside feeds for the rest of the game — profanely worded, instantly approved. The adjutants then name the channel: Nurse Yugoslav of the Madness, on the eighteenth floor — Houston's mother — relaying through a celestial cut-out. Houston refuses to confess and is ruled not culpable on circumstantial evidence, and Carl's jeering "Your mom? I can't wait to meet her" earns him a private threat. Houston privately promises Carl a thousand hours on his amplification table and warns him he is in mortal danger right now. Then Stockade, catching the full delayed dose of the spider's madness, grinds his own face against the floorboards until he dies. The Democratic Sortion is eliminated, its assets awarded to the Madness, and because the withdrawal was voluntary the ceasefire is cut by 23.33 hours and ends immediately. Houston throws off his robes — six arms, a bug body, a rifle — and fires as Carl teleports out with a hole through his shoulder and a stolen bag of cat food. Weapons free.

Interlude — Christmas Morning (Carl)

Carl's own flashback, and the hinge the whole series turns on. Leaving Orren's office with the Containment Interface finally installed, he asks to be sent back to the Florida gas station to sit with Lightning Lou, the memory-ghost dog left alone on Christmas Day. He opens the interface expecting one button marked boom and finds six tabs of untranslated Valtay telemetry; the fuse page lists five benchmarks, two already met, and an Override Conditions And Activate Fuse button. He wants to press it more than he has ever wanted anything. He doesn't — partly because he has no right to make that choice for everyone he loves, and partly because he cannot believe an AI that is so obviously enjoying itself would hand him a real kill switch unless it were a trap. Then, twenty entries down another list, he finds the other option: Disconnect Containment — rendering the unit inert, disabling the failsafe, and taking the leash off the AI entirely. Asking himself which of the three choices hurts the Syndicate most and protects his people best makes the decision easy. He presses it. The containment interface blanks out, the red dot over Earth begins to grow, and Carl says, "Welcome to the party, pals."

docs.title: Part II — The Ramp-Up
docs.text:
Chapter 20 — Weapons Free

Opens on a cookbook exchange: Justice Light's eighth-edition confession that he killed one NPC out of pure anger and became what he hates, answered generations later by Drakea, who tells him it was not his fault, that they made him a warrior out of a gentle soul, and that he should force them to look at what they forged. Nine of ten teams remain. Carl steps out of the field hospital into a camp boiling like an upset anthill, with rocks — non-magical, chemical-loaded — already breaking against the base shield. He confirms with Justice Light that the throne room was prepared before it locked; the one-winged skyfowl is an Origamist working on something secret with a squad of enthusiastically expendable sluggalos. Samantha has stowed away aboard Party Planner and has to be dumped out of the bomb bay. The army splits between two fronts ten miles apart while Carl's Scavenger's Daughter fills again and his ears ring, and three orphaned children — Randy, Todd, and the permanently kindergarten-aged flesh golem Clint — try to join the war with training spears.

Chapter 21 — The Rot Sticker Behemoths

The southern front is a First World War tableau: twelve-foot trenches under constant non-magical artillery, magical periscopes, thousands of protection mages holding the line, and a 250-metre no-man's-land glittering with traps hidden by Justice Light's protection spell. The first real assault is a thousand Juiced Rot Sticker Behemoths — Mini-Cooper-sized suicide pets the Reavers raised from infancy, played fetch with, loved, then caged, injected with steroids, infected with the Gurgles, and released. Mages throw up a dirt spine, the Tunnel Moles blow the buried charges early, and the line holds. But gurglers get into the trenches anyway, and a crawler with a flamethrower has to bake ten of her own screaming, bleeding comrades into a wall of dirt and then sit down and sob. Baroness Victory rules the infection a legal exploit because the pets were infected before the magic ban.

Chapter 22 — Colonel Boomer's Plan

Planning in the forward bunker with Tran — now wearing the two-part mechanical crab exoskeleton Katia built him, Odette's crab crossed with Iron Man — and Colonel Boomer, a five-thousand-year- old elf who looks like a pickled bulldog with a cigar, banned from Crawl Con for threatening to fist-fuck an orcish showrunner to death and wanted for killing a man in a waystation brawl over the crawl. Elle's reconnaissance gives them the whole enemy layout: forty large Dream trebuchets and dozens of mobile ones, fifty mounted mercenaries in reserve, twenty possibly-decoy tanks, and a hundred invisible Madness troops already moving. Boomer's read is that the Dream's bombardier class are desk-humping cowards who will run if pressed, but that Epitome Tagg's household guard are real veterans who won't — and that Tagg himself fights near the front, in a truly ridiculous helmet. The enemy's front trench turns out to hold almost no inner-circle officers, which tells Carl the naga army is hiding somewhere. Boomer lights his cigar. "Fuck yeah."

Chapter 23 — The Dazzler Raid

The assault. Louis walks a line of bombs across the ground directly in front of the enemy trench — not to kill, but to crater the unprotected earth, bury the defenders in dirt, and strip their forward protections. Elle knocks out the anti-air batteries with Carl's missile launcher. Their one trebuchet lobs Dazzlers into the craters: trap modules that strobe blinding light into the nearest enemy's eyes and simultaneously blast, at ground-shaking volume, Rage Against the Machine's "Killing in the Name." Two thousand Princess Posse soldiers go over the top under invisibility and illusion, Donut offering a prize to whoever brings her the most dead cheese sticks because positive reinforcement worked on Mongo. Drick the NPC adjutant drops into the trench to watch. Asked in private whether she's scared, Donut answers that she is, but it's more numb than anything now — it hits her afterward, not during. Carl goes over the wall with them.

Chapter 24 — Tunneling In

Chaos and casualty pings. A magic-diffusion burst strips every illusion, shield, and ear protection mid-charge, exposing the whole line to a heavy pulse gun; Carl knocks Donut and Mongo behind a rock and silences it with a hob-lobber. Then the Build Trench exploit: from inside the bomb craters Carl and dozens of others read Build Trench scrolls, angling new trenches to intersect the enemy's at a lower elevation and enjoining them — craft magic ignores the enemy's protections entirely, a hole in the rules known for years and never patched because the scrolls are too expensive for Faction Wars teams to bother with. A Saccathian drops into the new channel, helmet cracked, and Carl leaps onto his chest with Daughter's Kiss activated.

Chapter 25 — The Prism Castle

Carl wakes twenty-five seconds later buried in dirt: the soul discharge now comes with a knockout debuff the AI names Post Nut Clarity. The trench is taken, and Team Retribution's two changeling spies have turned the enemy's empty middle fallback trench into a concealed pool of acid — the retreating soldiers jump blindly into it, and Victory arrives shaken, saying they need to revisit what counts as "offensive" magic. Boomer takes command with orders to make it look like a stalemate rather than let them surrender. Carl, Donut, and Mongo board Party Planner — crewed by Louis, the changeling child Skarn, and Bonnie the gnome girl behind a door gun, because Donut gave her the last scout slot — and fly thirty miles low and fast to the Prism's headquarters, a small, barely defended warehouse. Three guards die at the door. Carl loots the traps, rolls Rend inside, and puts on the Ring of Divine Suffering. "Oh, Empress."

Interlude — Milk (6th Edition)

A xenopus guildmaster wakes starving in a straw nest behind a hidden door, having slept through so much of the season that the dungeon newsletters are stacked unread by the door and she hasn't had a supervisor meeting in fifty seasons. She runs both the Calligraphy and Cartography guilds inside Club Vanquisher; almost nobody ever finds them. Outside, screaming: Prepotente and his mother Miriam Dom — newly a vampire, and therefore newly banned from the club — have killed guards and are cornered, with the hellspawn Bianca setting the hallway on fire. They burst into Milk's guild and Bianca incinerates her carpet, her scroll linen, and very nearly her. Miriam apologizes, kneels, and rubs salve into the burn — the first time in all her cycles that a crawler has spent supplies healing an NPC. Milk warns them they won't leave alive, then finds the loophole: "I sure hope you don't threaten me. If you threaten me, I might be forced to give you information." Miriam draws a knife, and Milk offers the map of every secret entrance and exit in the club. Top level 73. Will not be freed until her guild services are used 333 times; times used so far: 6. Author of the sixth edition. Current status: Indentured within the dungeon.

Chapter 26 — Storming the Prism

Hunter-seeker automatons splatter two of the Empress's guards; the third, a sai rhinoceros, is knocked out and duct-taped. Inside the throne room Empress D'Nadia is firing a crossbow and holding a knife on herself, keeping her own health below full so Carl cannot mark her. Banger spheres strip her shields one by one; Donut's clockwork Mongos tear off her gown and the three separate shield modules hidden in it, then snap off the tentacle holding the knife. Carl heals her to full and marks her. Then he tells her, while she begs and calls herself his friend, exactly what this is for: she told Tsarina Signet that she wasn't real, that her family wasn't real. The rage that comes over Carl is whiter than anything he has felt for the Maestro, for the hunters, for Quan — because she pretended to be one of the good ones. Donut begs him over private chat to step back. He finds the edge, sees it clearly with one foot out over the air — and steps back.

Chapter 27 — The Death of Empress D'Nadia

Donut kills her, formally on Mongo's behalf and with a complaint about the pet show. Carl's achievement — Gavrilo Princip — spells out the scale: D'Nadia was the last living heir of a small but powerful trading dynasty, and the Syndicate probate courts are already bracing. The Prism is defeated, its assets awarded to the Princess Posse. Ten gnoll mercenaries burst in, eight of them instantly re-flagged to the Posse; their corporal pleads for the two who were assigned to other teams, including his cousin, and Carl — ring itching on his finger — lets them all live. He pulls the ring off in front of everyone. Donut tells him to throw it away, that it is doing something to him, that he is scaring her; Carl hears his mother's voice saying the same thing to his father, and still says not yet. Then the quieter reveal: Carl's stats have made him the strongest member of the party, and he is now Party Leader of the Royal Court of Princess Donut. Donut's outrage is, for the first time, mostly performance. Part of him is sad about that.

Chapter 28 — Toyotomi

Toyotomi, the sai mercenary, is a broken creature: his entire squad died to Minge the demon at the Desperado Club, he refuses to lead anyone now, and he asks to be left behind to die defending a castle he failed. Carl sends him to Shanty Town instead, where his Edifice Shield spell suits smaller structures. Li Jun reports a crazy old white lady with a shopping cart asking after Carl by name, level 23, no class — Agatha. Zev relays a direct order from Prime Minister Glory himself: do not interact with her under any circumstances, reason unstated, which is new — residuals have always been harmless. Carl reflects on how many hands are in this now — two residual factions, the Syndicate council, the Apothecary, the Plenty, the Pacifist Network, the Nebulars, Odette — and how it's like solving a blank puzzle with half the pieces missing and some of the rest decoys. He traps the castle, leaves a lone Madness mercenary sitting in the throne room with a chair and snacks to force the Bloc to squabble over the land, and declares it blob-hunting season.

Chapter 29 — Paratroopers

Back at base, Carl reviews a map that fills him with dread — seven battalions scattered across a hex-game battlefield. Donut reports her 1914 box contained a bleeding, crying spellbook called War Crime. Then the north breaks: Florin falls back under the full enemy push, and simultaneously the base is hit from inside. The anti-air battery and hangar bay are sabotaged. Reaver paratroopers drop in. And Carl works out how: mages listed on the casualty roster are still walking around, because gondii brain worms — Valtay mercenaries — can enter a corpse, reboot it, and inherit its memories. He tackles an "alive" dead mage and beats his face in until the worm crawls out, then stamps it. Worse, Bomo has found an extra door in the guild's situational hallway: a Reaver saferoom door, because the bait shop is now inside the FUPA and somebody from that team once used it. Carl orders Tina unleashed.

Chapter 30 — The Castle Door

The stand at the castle entrance behind fan-shaped shields, with invisible Madness Monkeywrenchers (tech cloaks the anti-magic bubbles can't see, spotted only through Donut's heat glasses) sniping from the barracks roof and a compromised mage named Lonnie systematically switching off the castle's interior wall protections from outside, so the Reavers can drop something through that saferoom door. Under Imani's overclocked Extreme Focus buff everyone talks too fast — Tipid on Valtay worm lore, Splash Zone on his wife Snail Trail and his mother-in-law Grandma Sticky — while Donut calls out invisible targets. Kiwi refuses to send Tina out, and Carl, composing an order to override her, stops: it is her decision, and he deletes it. Donut simply orders Tina out anyway. Then Donut climbs onto the castle front and gives her first real command speech — Comrades! — and the whole camp charges.

Chapter 31 — Satchel Charges

The fight at the bottom of the hill against Reaver cyborg drop troopers — Warlord Fang's personal deployment, mercenaries who sold pieces of their bodies for citizenship, thrown at colonial land-lease evictions for three-cycle deployments at a time, and who have been fighting far longer than any crawler. Tina rampages and starts losing shields. An invisible dreadnaught tries to knife Carl in the back on the barracks roof and Carl beats his face off in front of everyone, who go very quiet. Then his trap sense lights up: the enemy is arming a bank of automatons with proximity-triggered satchel charges. Carl casts Tripper, detonating all of it at once and erasing the cyborg line, and the crawlers — recovering fastest — swarm what's left. He finishes by leaping off the second storey onto the fleeing Lonnie with Daughter's Kiss.

Chapter 32 — The Necklace of Indelible Woe

The decision is made to collapse the bait shop and cut the saferoom off from the castle — repairable in an emergency, but guarded, because the alternative is someone dropping a nuke through that door. Justice Light says he already has everything he needs, working in the corner sewing folded paper into strange spirals: I have contingencies heaped upon contingencies. Danger lives in what they can't see. Outside, tens of thousands of enemies have massed, and riding at their head on a swamp yak named Gonk, in feathered parade regalia, is not Prince Stalwart but King Rust himself, come up from the eighteenth floor at the last minute. Tipid explains how the king got so many levels and spells: a Ring of Divine Suffering, and the Necklace of Indelible Woe, which swaps one of your spells for one of a killed crawler's highest — an item the factions agreed to stop using because combatants were farming crawlers to charge it. Then Rust rides out alone and requests a formal, registered parlay.

Chapter 33 — Riding Out to Parlay

Donut insists on meeting a mounted king while mounted herself, so Kibben saddles Simoom, Ferdinand's albino rhinoceros, in her ornate howdah — steer by the horn, stop by gently rubbing her behind, which Donut finds an outrage. Mongo whines at being replaced. Walking down through their own fortifications, Carl takes stock: bunkers of looted heavy guns, earthworks teams underfoot, a no-man's land of Tripper-resistant traps that Rust's level-15 Tripper can set off anyway. Florin reports capturing two enemy Weeper tanks and warns the main attack is imminent; Carl asks if they're having fun yet, and Florin says he'll answer face to face. Victory explains the parlay bubble: no attacks, no chat, saferoom rules, the shields drop at a hundred metres. And then Donut pulls the curtain aside — the orc king is crying.

Chapter 34 — King Rust's Warning

Rust is weeping with rage and grief and something like laughter all at once, and what he says upends the floor. His daughter Princess Formidable has seized one of his own cruisers, is five hours from the monitor station orbiting Venus, and intends to manually trigger the system failsafe and nova the star — announcing to the whole Syndicate, in the process, that the Skull Empire builds back doors into every piece of hardware it sells. She believes the AI's insanity is contagious and will reach the center system. Rust knows it is crackpot Nebular theory and knows she won't listen to him; he asks Carl to plead with her on behalf of Earth's surface population in exchange for withdrawing his armies. Carl, who knows the failsafe is already dead because he killed it himself, plays it straight and takes the deal. Rust rides slowly back, an old man who knows he is going to die — and Rosetta erupts from the ground in a tech cloak, flips onto the yak, and takes his head off with a whip. Five seconds of silence. Then tens of thousands of enemy troops charge.

Interlude — Volteeg (7th Edition)

A gargoyle who entered the dungeon as somebody's pet bird. Before the crawl he was a sturnus in a cage, loved by Mistress Henspar, who hid him inside her jacket at the market and smuggled him berries, and who forgave him for biting a shopkeeper. He sang for her. Then a pet biscuit gave him speech, and choosing gargoyle on the third floor gave him a mind large enough to understand the universe he was trapped in — and took away his ability to sing. Henspar died on the seventh floor; he found the cookbook too late, hid through his own Faction Wars, and wrote a single entry out of shame. He took the first deal offered, survived 26 seasons, and ended up guarding an Operatic compliance barge with two other "One-Offs." Porthus got him smuggled back in on a false designation. Now, watching Rosetta behead King Rust, he disconnects his Weeper tank's fire-control chamber, fills the crew compartment with dozens of live energy balls, turns Mozart up loud, sings along in a voice like dragged rock, drives into the centre of the Bloc formation and says "Show me Mistress Henspar." Top level 71. Killed over 10,000 of his fellow soldiers with a single blast, including Warlord Hortense Leadership Unit, eliminating the Operatic Collective from Faction Wars. Author of the seventh edition. Current status: Dead.

Chapter 35 — The Digger Tunnel

Under fire in the smoke, Rosetta demands Rust's head — she needs a retina scan to go with his family signet ring and a stolen credit chit. Carl inventories the head and the corpse while grenades land around them and a dozen robed war mages on clockwork mounts advance through the haze, filling him with primal dread. A dispel strips the smoke and, with it, the roof of a huge dwarven digger tunnel running beneath them; all five of them — plus Simoom and the grieving swamp yak — drop twelve feet into a passage full of Semeru dwarves who immediately start hunting the war mages who fell in with them. Then Volteeg's blast: the Operatic Collective is eliminated and Hortense is dead, ruled a probable fragging. Rosetta finishes her transfer, a cartoon slime chirps "Transfer approved! Thank you for using Colloid Bank," and she drops the datapad and sobs on the tunnel floor. Before Carl can ask a single question he is yanked out of the game to the Desperado Club.

Chapter 36 — The Zero Zone

Orren, dripping with the Syndicate's panic, has just hung up on the Prime Minister — Rosetta has stolen and laundered a few billion credits from the dead king, and nobody can claw it back. But that isn't why Carl is here. They have found the hidden Paulie conversation. They know he has the implant, know when he used it, and know what he didn't do with it. Carl's price for cooperation is the immediate end of the crawl, freedom for every surviving crawler, Syndicate assets spent on rebuilding, and then everyone leaving Earth's system forever. Orren says that if any of them could grant it they would, because this is now about survival, and detonates an engineered zero zone ball — cutting the AI out and giving them ten minutes. He needs to know whether it can be undone. Then a bedraggled gnoll with a bottle of vodka leans in the doorway: Growler Gary.

Chapter 37 — Growler Gary

The AI, wearing the body of the hyena bartender from the Iron Tangle, casually cancels the zero zone ("your zero zones were just a courtesy"), forgives Orren for trying to arrange its death, and tells him Harbinger was sent to kill both of them and has been warned off on pain of having his intestines pulled out through his hair follicles. Asked to prove its reach, it claps and Princess Formidable drops into the room out of her own ship, upside down. Her father is dead, her failsafe is dead, and Gary cheerfully admits he left the Venus station unlocked purely to see whether her crew goes through with it. It offers her four destinations — death, the Scolopendra Club, backstage at the Pineapple Cabaret, or Earth's surface — and when she picks the surface, it muses that it hopes she can swim. Confirmed: the AI's control now extends to the star. The crawl continues.

Chapter 38 — Relationship Advice

The real reason it came. Gary teleports Donut in and asks her — not Carl, not Orren — for relationship advice, wrapped in a transparent metaphor: a girl he's talking to who is teaching him everything, who has a huge ex-boyfriend she said was dead but who is actually in prison, and that ex's older former girlfriend who is also feeding him pointers and wants the prisoner killed. The two women hate each other but seem to want the same thing. When Donut strays too close to naming Agatha, the AI cracks the desk and growls "Do not venture too far from the metaphor. We. All. Have. Our. Limitations." Donut's counsel: what someone does matters more than what they say, if lots of people want someone dead you find out which kind of person he is before acting, and if she can't accept that, she's using you. Gary thanks her sincerely, says nothing changes, and collapses. Growler Gary wakes up drunk and confused, asks for Rory, and vanishes. His level reads 175.

Chapter 39 — The Bloc Fractures

Orren asks whether Carl broke the AI out of containment deliberately, and gets no answer; he says it no longer matters, and admits he left the Knot because he wanted to be an actor, not to preside over an apocalypse. The board has changed while they were out: the Bone Clan and the Dream have both quit the Bloc, leaving only the Blood Sultanate, the Madness, and the Reavers, with the orcs and the Dream unaffiliated. Donut, meanwhile, has been trash-talking the newly crowned King Stalwart in warlord chat — offering him a loan from her friend Rosetta, claiming she has turned his father's skin into a headless powder-room rug for Mongo's accidents, and finishing with "I'm sorry, but you are much too poor to be talking to me like this" and the observation that his father called him a disappointment before he died, which is the one thing she isn't lying about. Boomer's debrief: their base is a mess, most of the mages are dead, and it is time for Operation Snake Pit.

Chapter 40 — The Chain Dragon

Carl's 1914 box produces a shrieking, weeping, black-goo-leaking spellbook that begs not to be read in a cartoon Austrian accent: Run, Little Günter, Run, which summons a lollipop-licking child in lederhosen who stores whatever attack you hit him with and carries it to a designated target before detonating. Then the tattoo work. Using the last of the toraline ink, Katia inks a chain-shaped dragon down Carl's right forearm, transferring Li Na's Profane Iron skill by freely given blood — which, unlike the eye Carl tore out of Li Jun under Shi Maria's control, is temporary for the donor and chooseable. Imani gets a small barbed-wire ankle tattoo carrying Carl's Tripper. Donut objects loudly to the aesthetics, which Carl reads correctly as guilt: all of this traces back to a tiara she put on her head on the first floor. Then Zev calls them to the warlord council.

Chapter 41 — The Aryl System Goes Dark

In the production facility, Ferdinand teleports in and caroms off the walls in a screaming panic before composing himself, and the gnoll security detail pats everyone down. Then Zev delivers the news. Formidable's crew reached the Venus station and manually triggered the failsafe. Nothing happened here. But in the same nanosecond, the Aryl system went dark — the location of the previous crawl, a Squim battle-royale season, with tens of thousands of people still in-system on mining and reclamation ships. Its tunnel node simply switched off. Tunnel nodes have never turned off in recorded history; they were the map of the seeded worlds before anyone learned to travel them. It will be three cycles before anyone can see whether that star still exists. Aryl's AI had also stopped speaking weeks earlier — well before Carl's meeting with the residual.

Chapter 42 — The Warlord Council

Seven teams at the table. Cascadia is visibly disintegrating, scales dulling and falling out, drinking tequila from a ball. Donut and Ferdinand collapse into hysterics because Stalwart is actually wearing a crown, and when Chaco tries to run a viewer poll on it the orc punches him unconscious across the room. Then: System Message: Warning: Scolopendra Stirs — which has never happened before, and silences everyone. And coiled beside Carl is Princess Vinata, the Sepsis Whore: brilliant white and gold, six arms, solid red eyes, half again the size of any naga he has seen, and carrying a presence so overwhelming he has to make himself close his mouth. She whispers to him throughout — that Cascadia has just lost her husband and most of her family to the Borant civil war, that she wonders how Carl will react when his own family dies, that they are expecting his attack and will be ready, that she will happily take care of his "Katia problem," and that she would like him to come serve in her father's court when this is over. We are both survivors. That is how we are the same, you and I.

Chapter 43 — Odette Hosts

Odette appears to replace Chaco — out of her Nekhebit costume, no mask, no crab, just a woman in a yellow shirt in a floating wheelchair, and completely unflappable. She exposes the loophole everyone has been using to beat the live-feed blackout: every off-world team owns entertainment channels, and while they can't watch the feeds, they can still read the program directory, so they pay 30,000 credits a pop to rename their own shows into sentences. Epitome Tagg spent the hour conversing with a channel currently titled Yes. We have Deactivated the Infected Hardware. The AI cheerfully says it loves a good loophole and won't close it unless asked, so Carl spends one of their two remaining Emergency Action Items to shut it — Juice Box stopping Ferdinand from spending one of Team Retribution's. Cascadia, face on the table, sing-songs the other channels: menus, gym schedules, personal-trainer lockers, massage NPCs. Anything programmed from orbit. Odette then works the table for interviews, and when she reaches Juice Box the changeling offers a single statement: "Fuck all of you." She shifts into something nobody has seen — a midnight-black, armless figure with electrified tentacles and hundreds of root-like legs — and speaks in a voice of grit and fire: "It's coming. And not just for these here with me today, all of whom are already marked and damned... It is coming for you all." Then she walks out through the wall. Cascadia shrieks, Architect Houston stands up shaking with excitement, and Ferdinand sums it up: "That chick is intense."

Chapter 44 — The Unwashed

The morning after, in the same room. Donut demands somebody explain to the new kids what that was, Tagg dismisses it as a childhood jump scare, and Houston — in his element for the only time all book — explains. It is the Unwashed — the Hag, the Stalker, the Last Light, the Inexorable — what many species report seeing at the moment of death, which the Viceroys call the Beautiful Place and which Houston names as his life's work. Then Donut needles Odette about owning a channel, and Odette, spotting an angle, mentions that the Sultanate's studio, Blood Hunter Holdings, produced Blood Hunter — the drama that got Miriam Dom killed. Carl starts laughing and can't stop: the naga army isn't hidden, it's already dead, and Operation Snake Pit is already blown.

Chapter 45 — Operation Snake Pit

Back on the ground into a mess. Prepotente, hunting the naga for his mother, has already single-handedly killed most of their standing army and has hit level 99, the strongest crawler in the dungeon — and then got himself locked in a penalty stasis for threatening an entire adjudication quorum. He arrives to find the Posse doing what he considers his job and sends Carl a page-long, all-caps tirade of insults ending in I SPIT! I SPIT IN YOUR EYE! Half the sluggalos have chased him across naga territory whooping, and the other half have stolen a cart. Victory rules that Carl may not work with an unaffiliated crawler, which leaves two options: back off, or get Prepotente into the army. Carl pockets a Conscription potion and starts writing.

Chapter 46 — Four Blood Nagas

The plan, laid out. Eleven nagas came in; four must die to break the line of succession — Vinata herself, her two cousins the Ikbals, and the head of her castle guard, who is also her secret husband. Four groups move at once: Florin pushes north as a diversion, Tran feints south then angles toward Shanty Town, Imani and Elle and Edgar approach the castle under concealment with the sluggalos as expendable first wave, and Carl's group stages in Shanty Town. But the real problem is the vanishing act — the Sultana has never once been captured in the game's history. Invaders reach her chamber and find her tea still warm. Rosetta lays out the deduction: not the Desperado Club, not the forests, not tunnels (they build on rock), not a saferoom (blood-bar rules). Club Vanquisher. Two seasons prove it — one where the temple entrance was buried under a goddess's rampage and she never appeared at all, and one where a demon eviction near the temple cost her a guard and made her late.

Chapter 47 — Borrowed Spells

Louis, circling overhead, reports the runaway sluggalos doing donuts in a field a mile north of the naga castle and distant flashes far to the south. Imani and Elle go into the stronghold without the expendable first wave they were promised, and Carl lets them, and feels sick about it. Imani then sets off a wave of traps with Carl's own Tripper spell — cast through the barbed-wire tattoo on her ankle — and Carl feels the jolt in his chest from miles away. The chapter is where the toraline ink mechanics are finally laid out in full: blood freely given lends a spell temporarily and lets the donor choose which one, while a spell taken by violence is permanent and strips the owner of it for good, which is exactly how Carl ended up with Li Jun's Walk on Air. Katia has inked the chain dragon on Carl's forearm and the barbed wire on Imani's ankle; Donut objects loudly to the aesthetics, which Carl reads as guilt, since all of it traces back to the tiara she put on in Book 1. Off to the side, Katia and Bautista argue: he wants her to eat the flower now, because he is afraid Carl will take it for Donut. She tells Carl privately that if it comes to that she will give it to him, and that she is telling him rather than Donut because Donut would never allow it. Then the goat dragon starts circling in to land.

Chapter 48 — Colonel Prepotente

Bianca lands, now level 70 with a second pair of wings and glowing hooves; Prepotente, at level 99, jumps down and says simply, "Recruit me. Do it now before I change my mind." Carl quietly puts the Conscription potion away, and the relief that floods him carries its own reproach: No. Not like that. Never like that. Made a Colonel, the goat immediately dissolves into enormous, snot-filled sobbing about how lonely he has been, how he thought Carl had died at the Bahamas, how he has enhanced pet biscuits he's too frightened to use — and then screams directly into Carl's face. Samantha needles him until Katia claps a hand over her mouth and warns her never to mention his mother. Then Elle reports the first of the four dead: the head of the castle guard, who was also Vinata's secret husband. And Edgar, buried outside, reports non-corporeal movement rising from below the castle. Rosetta was right.

Chapter 49 — Theia or Khepri

A cookbook entry from Carl explains the mechanic everything hinges on: when someone worships a deity for the first time, a non-corporeal Bijou fairy drags a thread of invisible light from the god to the strongest temple on the floor and from there to the new worshipper's heart. Edgar's level-15 Sense Movement can see that upward motion — which is what he just saw. Of the fifteen light deities with temples in Club Vanquisher, six grant Travel the Path on first worship, and four of those also grant Welcome Home, a single-use skill that rides the Bijou's thread straight to the temple. Two of those four come with a recruiting quest allowing companions to be smuggled along: Theia, who turns prospects into motes of light for the pocket, and Khepri, who turns them into beetles the worshipper swallows and later gives birth to at an endless insect buffet. Theia is Samantha's mother and is sponsored by the Pacifist Network this season, so Vinata cannot use her. Which leaves Khepri — and about three minutes to break into his temple and kill everyone in it.

Chapter 50 — The Temple of the Dagda

Elle reports the naga stronghold empty and stinking; Louis gasses the exterior to seal it. The way into Khepri's temple runs through this season's out-of-city Club Vanquisher entrance, the Temple of the Dagda. Prepotente — drinking Big Red before battle at a strict maximum of five sodas a day, per his mother's rule — reveals he has a complete memorised map of the club's interior, given to him and Miriam by a guildmaster, and Carl notes what that would have been worth earlier and remembers Donut telling him long ago to try harder with the goat. Everyone drinks Mordecai's hour-long aura-immunity potion, because Li Na is about to be weaponized: the Shanty Town Extend Aura synergy tower amplifies her reach, and Mistress Tiatha's exploit — capacitor wire run from the clock tower's hands all the way into the club — will carry it through the portals so long as every door in the chain is held open. Inside the Dagda's temple there is harp music, a bubbling cauldron of stew, and a cleric who says the stew is for brothers only; Bautista distracts him while Li Jun and Zhang trail wire. In the vestibule the ram Mork — a Hellik worshipper, automatically hostile — is fed the story that Carl has captured Prepotente for the Holy Crusade bounty, with the goat throwing himself to the floor in an absurdly hammy performance and demanding to know when the indignities will end. Emberus immediately issues a quest to kill the blasphemer. Mork calls the guards. "Katia, you're up."

Chapter 51 — The Dreads

Four mantaur guards burst in and one promptly embeds his Wolverine claws in the ceiling and cannot get free. Katia bursts in as another mantaur, covered in fake gore made of cherry cobbler and breakfast sausage, screaming about demons — and Bautista's stuffed Eclipse Pyxies turn real in midair and start eating faces. In the smoke Carl hurls a Black Nimbus potion into the back of Mork's head, stripping him of his god's grace in his own home, and jams the final portal open with the ram's body while Li Jun climbs the walls to tie off the capacitor wire. Then Li Na activates Dark Purpose, and it is nothing like Donut's Why Are You Hitting Yourself? The fire gutters, the light drains, frost crawls up the walls. Mork pulls out his own eyes and shoves them back in backwards, then starts ripping his own ribs away trying to give his god back his heart, whispering that he's cold, that he was promised he'd never be cold again. A mantaur cuts his own throat. Every one of the hundreds of taxidermied trophy heads on the walls comes alive and screams without lungs; the rugs come alive. Then ethereal chains rise from the floor and drag each newly made ghost, screaming, down through it. Carl's Emberus quest completes to ten seconds of unhinged divine laughter and a celestial boon. And Li Na, asked what level that aura was, answers calmly that it was level 4 when she cast it, hit 15 within moments, and she is now cycling through Defile Soul and Bleeding Horror to power-level the rest. Carl realises how little he ever understood about her.

Chapter 52 — The Portal Dial

Through halls slick with self-inflicted death, with sentient pools of blood hunting around corners, to the temple portal dial. Prepotente works the dial off automatic while Rosetta supplies the address — Khepri is 453. Carl's portal analysis tool returns a screenshot: Vinata is in there with several other nagas and a robed figure whose head is an entire beetle. The door will only open for an adherent — or for the Damned, a status granted to anyone who has entered the Nothing and survived. Which is why Samantha is here. She bites the handle, the door opens, and Carl, Katia, and Prepotente pour through — into a freeze frame, a trespassing warning, a mark for death, Vinata wearing an Immortal tag, and the realisation that the bug-headed figure is not a cleric. It is Khepri himself. And Carl, standing in a deity's presence, is granted ninety seconds of immortality.

Chapter 53 — Khepri in Person

The trap, fully sprung, and it is elegant: Vinata worshipped Khepri herself, broke tradition, arranged to summon him into his own temple, and waited for Carl to find her — knowing trespassers in a god's own house are finished. The AI throws a full boss-battle sequence over it, opens betting, posts a 2X Jackpot if Zhang Lives banner, and complains bitterly about having to procedurally generate an "endless" temple. Khepri, level 250, invulnerable, retainer of Adrasteia, whose patron Khnum mysteriously dropped dead days ago. Six nagas, three of them veteran soldiers. The naga adjutant appears screaming for a foul and is told to go be smelly somewhere else. Katia and Prepotente both refuse Carl's order to run. The timer counts down from thirty, and Carl tells them a plan that Katia calls insane even for him.

Chapter 54 — The Waffle Maker

Everything at once. The three guards charge on speed potions; the two cousins turn invisible and flee down the endless table; Vinata turns invisible and charges; Katia and Prepotente drink Black Nimbus and are instantly ejected from the temple, which is the point. Carl summons Little Günter, points him at the god — and drops The Waffle Maker, a thermobaric bomb the size of a thermos, at his own feet in a narrow room. He is flattened, burned, and spread across the door, held together only by the immortality, and comes back through a reconstruction so agonising it takes seconds and feels like a year. Both cousins die in the blast. Günter detonates on the god somewhere far down the hall. Carl comes to outside the portal, blasted through the door — drunk, legs locked straight, suction cups on his fingers, screaming worms pouring from his nose as a dozen escaped gods pass through the club handing out random boons and debuffs through his patch. And wrapped around him, crushing, stabbing, and slamming his skull against the floor, is Vinata — driven insane by staring into the open Eye of the Bedlam Bride on his chest, screaming that they were almost free, that she was going to have children with him. Hellik sits down beside them as casually as a dinner guest and delivers a message for his brother: he did not kill Geyrun, their mother Apito has been corrupted, the All Tree is beginning to rot, Nekhebit has returned, and Scolopendra stirs — it is all connected. Then he leaves, and a level-29 sluggalette bursts out from under Carl's shirt and buries a hatchet between Vinata's eyes.

Chapter 55 — Milk

The Blood Sultanate is defeated, credit to Kandy "Bigs" Newton, and its assets — by the Sepsis Whore's own prior arrangement with her blood relatives — pass to Donut and Katia and thence to the Posse. Carl heals himself over and over on never-ending mana as Vinata's corpse cools; in death she is grey, the white having been makeup blown off by the bomb. Samantha arrives charred to a husk, furious that her mother Theia turned out to be a male skyfowl — the Pacifist Network sponsor behind the goddess. Getting out means berserking the remaining mantaurs with a Megadeth alarm trap, Black-Nimbusing two Basilica Guard ogres (the Untouchable tow-truck drivers of the Ascendency, whose absence from the twelfth floor is precisely why gods are now loose in the club), and finally unleashing Profane Iron — Li Na's chain skill, dozens of chains tearing out of his own flesh. They regroup behind a hidden panel into the Calligrapher's Guild, and the guildmaster is a half-frog, half-bat xenopus. Milk. The sixth-edition author, who has been here the whole time. And Carl — who has carried every one of those moments when I wasn't there and I wasn't here — is wrapped in her leathery wings and, finally, sobs. "Let it out. It's okay." He tells Donut over chat that it was easy, went off without a hitch. His cookbook note to the long-dead Drakea admits the truth: it's getting harder every day to keep himself from drowning.

docs.title: Part III — Open Hostilities
docs.text:
Interlude — Justice Light (8th Edition)

In the tunnels beneath the FUPA, Justice Light sends his sluggalo sappers away — all but one. He has known for days that Sick-Ass Worgo is a changeling, spotted by body temperature, weight, and the absence of hormonal emissions, and he has ringed the room with eight hidden traps. She surfaces Juice Box's face on a blank body and gives him five minutes. He spends them on his confession: he killed one shopkeeper NPC out of anger and let the cold in; he bought the right to run that same trap store; and then he and Dante were reassigned as ice castle guards and ordered, off camera, for reasons still unknown, to slaughter the ice elves they had come to know by name. Dante refused twice and was erased by a beam from the sky — he died free. Justice refused once, lost a wing, and obeyed. He dreams that the elves killed themselves to spare him, and hates himself for wanting it. Then he lays out what he has deduced: Team Retribution's real goal is not the alliance but physically touching as many gods as possible, which is why they could have decapitated the Sultana at any time and didn't. Juice Box confirms they lost three in the club and only touched Bast and three basilica guards. His offer: he can show them how to touch a god and survive, in exchange for honouring every deal and backing Operation Ruin without sabotage. When she says the gods won't matter if the operation works, he laughs — "you are thinking much too small. That's not the war I'm talking about" — and starts explaining the trap he began designing the moment he watched Carl find the Gate of the Feral Gods. Top level 86. Author of the eighth edition. Current status: Alive.

Chapter 56 — Operation Ruin

Six teams left; two hours to Open Hostilities. The Posse now holds sectors three and four and has turned the former Sultanate's rolling hills into a tripwire field they don't expect to kill anyone, only to report movement. Juice Box's sudden generosity has filled Shanty Town with Semeru dwarves alongside Li Na's 107th. And the Nest is finished: a granite synergy tower taller than anything outside the funnel, at 200% strength under Toyotomi's Edifice Shield, laced block by block with a lattice of protection spells, four deflector towers, and mages on every lower floor — built so that Donut can perch at the very top with line of sight over the entire battlefield. It cannot be hidden and it will draw every long-range weapon on the floor, which is exactly the point, and Carl is sick about it. Katia gets divine knee pads (Breathe Underwater, level-15 Swim, Iron Stomach for eating magical items, Eater of the Dead); Carl gets a screaming golden hairbrush that shouts "Encore!" and grants Speedster and +25% constitution, so the hair has to stay. Louis, shaken by being shown a recording of himself with Juice Box, is visibly cracking. Milk has been kidnapped and is being "interrogated" at the FUPA — which turns out to be not only permitted but encouraged. Watching Donut climb the Nest for the first time, Carl asks himself the question the fifth floor first put to him: What gives me the right?

Chapter 57 — Thirty-Two Loot Boxes

Carl's haul from Club Vanquisher, and the bill that came with it. Varg Vikernes bans him permanently from Club Vanquisher and from every temple except Emberus's and the handful where he's been named friend of the church — Apito, Eileithyia, Eris, Grull, Hellik, Issitoq, Nekhebit, Theia, Yemaya, a list full of unexplained entries. Liquified notes that blowing himself up only worked because of god-tier immortality and rewards him with a Lucky Shot patch that deflects a fatal blow into a party member, which he vows never to wear and hides from the others. A platinum box with an absurdly long name shoves him toward figuring out the Book of Voodoo. And Emberus, enraged rather than reassured by Hellik's message, orders him to kill a hundred Hellik worshippers and then confesses that if Carl actually succeeds in killing his brother, he will likely turn his grief on Carl himself — for this, I love you, beloved but doomed worshiper. I promise the burning will be exquisite. Then Carl goes to the brig, where every prisoner but one has been quietly killed by Li Na with the second Ring of Divine Suffering he gave her — the ring Donut begged him to hand over.

Chapter 58 — Rishi's Coup

Rishi, the last living naga, armless and smug in a containment shield, explains why he buried himself in the dirt rather than die with his wife: he had a contract to deliver. Syndicate law, he says, makes Carl the de facto leader of Earth, and the petition was filed on his behalf. The offer is citizenship in all naga territories plus five Naphil-class generation ships, in exchange for naga settlement rights over the rest of the solar system after the crawl — a hedge that pays off no matter which way Earth's future goes. He also lays out the Great Consensus, the philosophy spreading through the Syndicate that everyone would be better off alone, and reveals that Vinata genuinely believed in it: the plan was to steal the entire naga fleet and leave for a generation, in a direction no tunnel thread points. Rishi does not believe it. He signed the contract Sultan Rishi the Usurper, having already arranged for his brothers to depose the king, his children, the prime minister, and the whole House of Greens. Carl's counter-offer: get in those ships and fly into the nearest star. Then he marks him, in front of 95% of the naga system's viewers, and tells them Rishi is only the opening act.

Chapter 59 — The Bombing Run

Operation Ruin: four simultaneous offensives, plus what Donut calls the "Coup De War Crime." Florin takes the orcs, Boomer the Reavers, Donut the Dream, Carl the Madness, Rosetta coordinates everything, Tipid holds the FUPA. Carl's cookbook entry ends If this is my last entry, know I went down fighting. Cascadia's opening announcement is four sentences of exhausted hatred. It goes wrong immediately: Reaver seeker missiles chase Party Planner (Bonnie splashes three with a door gun), Dream magical artillery targets the trenches rather than the base, and two battalions of Dreamers mass-teleport straight to the FUPA's throne room, and Justice Light asks Rosetta to whittle them to under 3,000 before letting them into his lair. Then the Gate of the Feral Gods releases Meatus, who summons Harpocrates — the god of silence, who hates noise, which is a problem given that every dwarven digger in the plan is deafening.

Chapter 60 — Harpocrates

Mordecai explains the joke that has run for centuries: Meatus is a gremlin who stole Harpocrates's genitals, sewed them on, and became a god; the stolen part is sapient, loud, and refuses to go back because it likes music. Harpocrates is not deaf — he can hear a fly's heartbeat from half a planet away, and he will smash anything noisy until he times out. Florin reports a 700-ton scorpion-shaped mech clawing out of the riverbank with Stalwart inside. Louis makes his run on the King's Point, cracks the shield, dodges a long-range death ray, and the dwarves confirm the lava tubes are agitated. Then Britney's warning arrives half a sentence too late: the orcs added an emergency shield over the entire mountain, and the pressure has nowhere to go.

Chapter 61 — The Eruption

The mountain blows with Party Planner far too close. The airship cartwheels, bounces a propeller off the ceiling of the floor, and limps away on three. Eris, goddess of chaos is spontaneously summoned by battlefield conditions and immediately starts shrieking that she never wanted to come down here. A demon eviction opens across multiple locations. Team Retribution's forces occupy both the Bone Clan's and the Dream's throne rooms. Ferdinand's emergency action item is split: the gods do not get to stay, but from now on Ascendency players may no longer decline to pilot their own deities or appear as themselves — dragging every sponsor bodily into their god. Carl and Samantha jump into Reaver territory. And at Elle's gate, Carl arrives to find King Stalwart on his knees among the corpses of four war mages, being torn apart by three more. "My sister was right," the new king of the Skull Empire says, and explodes. Their dots turn white with a colour no army uses. Akuma, leader of the War Mage Rebellion, is holding the Gate of the Feral Gods, which he took off Elle. "Nice shoes, asshole."

Chapter 62 — The War Mage Rebellion

Team eliminated: With War Chief Stalwart dead and the War Mage Rebellion ruled ineligible to collect on the kill, the system awards all of the Bone Clan's assets to Team Retribution, who were already occupying its throne room — the Bone Clan is eliminated. War mages, it turns out, are the only truly dungeon-born entities: a skin ripped from a corpse becomes a flesher, the flesher consumes and re-sleeves a living being, and after a dozen or more iterations the magic itself becomes sapient and fuses skeleton, flesher, and magic into one creature that knows hundreds of spells and is, universally, a complete prick. The AI's description ends with a pointed warning about keeping an eye on the things you unleash. Their heads explode ten minutes after death, so Carl inventories the bodies. The system declares the War Mage Rebellion a "non-team entity," a category that did not exist an hour ago. Elle notes Akuma deliberately pulled a killing blow on her. Drick calls foul on his own team, Juice Box vanishes into the adjudication, and Carl realizes with rising anger that Rosetta, Juice Box, and Justice Light have all been making plans without telling him, using him as a piece. You're always on rails, says the voice under the torrent. You're a puppet, dancing on their stage.

Chapter 63 — Into Madness Territory

Through the gate into Madness territory, into a field glittering with thousands of traps. The team arrives by teleport automaton — including Dong Quixote, uninvited, mounted on King Rust's swamp yak Gonk with a war lance and his talking crust sock, and Bigs the sluggalette riding behind him. Boomer firmly tells Carl to stop running everyone else's operation. Louis is ordered to make his run on the Reaver castle despite the gravity-magic dragon circling it. Carl picks his way through the minefield stowing summon traps — including one loaded with fire ants — and then Samantha reports that the gate she was baiting has timed out. What comes through is not a Nothing demon: The Feral God Yarilo has entered the realm. "Uh-oh."

Chapter 64 — Osvaldo's Crystal

Yarilo, god of lust, bellows for Psamathe across the whole realm and chases Samantha in circles. Then a column of prismatic light erupts a mile away and starts waving around like a flashlight: the crawler Osvaldo cannot get the Memorial Crystal of Apito back into his inventory, and Emberus immediately reassigns Carl's quest to it. Elle's Subterfuge is negated, half the Madness army turns around to investigate the rainbow, and Prepotente helpfully observes that Carl is about to be in extreme danger. The stealth plan is dead: Carl summons the other half of the 105th, accepting that Bodi's 103rd must retreat without psionic cover, since Prepotente can only shield one force at a time. Missiles walk across the enemy line, and hundreds of Madness dune buggies pour over the dark fields backlit by their own burning castle. Well, that's not how this was supposed to go.

Chapter 65 — Bear Witness

Three thousand Scream Warriors teleport in, some of them into trees. Then the Madness turn their real weapon on Carl: a psionic barrage — Endless Thread of Distraction, Self Harm, Intrusive Thoughts — that drops him into a spiral of memories about westerns and unopened Christmas presents while his Emberus ring burns red and his bare feet sink into the ground. A familiar voice, friendly, male, tells him he is not crazy and to look down: he has been standing in an All Tree root the whole time, and what he has been calling a river is not water but souls, always flowing downward, always screaming. Mind Balance hits level 16 — trained past 15 by battlefield conditions — and he wakes, immune, able to see the enemy mind mages and paint them. The tree he was leaning on crumbles, rotted. Then Eris, panic-casting, drops Bear Witness across essentially the entire floor: everyone outdoors freezes, eyes white, tagged as Witnesses. Only Carl (via Mind Balance), Dong Quixote, the pets, the sluggalos, and the former tattoos are spared. Then she follows it with Bring Forth the Witnesses, and every frozen body on the floor rockets into the sky and vanishes like the rapture, leaving Carl in an emptied wood with a shark, a slug, a yak and a furious hellspawn.

Chapter 66 — Bring Forth the Witnesses

Mordecai explains the Ceremony of Chaos: some gods can only claim the Ascendent throne with mortal witnesses present, so Eris summons them — once, ever — into a single enormous pile. It has landed beside the Dream castle: roughly 80,000 people, crawlers, mercenaries, NPCs, the whole missing Reaver army, all conscious, all paralyzed, all mixed together. If Eris lifts the invulnerability while they're still frozen, most will be crushed or suffocate. Long-range teleports are dead for an hour. Louis's Party Planner is ripped in half by the dragon's gravity magic and he falls toward the Reaver castle, apologizing over chat for being a fuckup and asking Carl to tell Katia he's sorry. Then Donut announces she has a two-part plan and casts: System Message: Warlord Princess Donut has committed an atrocity. She has hit eighty thousand people with Rolling Battle Formation, the skunk wizard's hat spell, amplified by the Nest.
