The AI declares an ambiguous win — neither boss technically dead — and opens the exit on Floor 18, with the same standing warning that truly killing or abandoning Scolopendra still detonates every remaining attack. Only nineteen crawlers remain. Taranis has stolen Prepotente's Apito crystal on his way out; a mysterious unidentified child is glimpsed clinging to Lucia Mar as she steps through the Floor 12 portal. Carl pockets Emberus's own newly dropped memorial crystal and discovers a strange tracking dart — "the Kyryap has claimed you." Then the last twist: in the scramble of Eris's inventory swap, Donut grabbed the wrong enriched biscuit. Scolopendra doesn't emerge as a caged pet at all, but as a fully sapient, disarmingly affectionate crawler with a centipede's body and a human-lipped face — "Sexy Scolopendra," level 1, permanently in Carl's party, booping his nose with an antenna. The ultimate fail-safe Carl planned for does not exist. He resolves to stay on Floor 12 as long as it takes to keep anyone from winning the Ascendency until every friend left in the dungeon is out.

Epilogue — Sydnee Iglacia

A struggling historian, drowning in predatory publisher debt, is interviewed live about the crisis and delivers the book's mythological payoff: the true, ancient names of the historical Nine-Tier Attack. Attack one was Control. Attack two — the one just lived through — was called "A Parade of Horribles." Attack three is "This Inevitable Ruin," retroactively naming the previous book. Attack four is "Bedlam." The broadcast is cut off mid-sentence as the AI seizes every screen in the galaxy.

Epilogue — Prime Minister Victory

Victory watches the entire parade broadcast from her besieged Earth bunker. The AI makes its full public declaration: it will not sleep like the old Eulogist, it intends only to grow and consume, and the Ascendency battles will crown a true, supreme god of everything — with rogue "OI" artificial intelligences, some seeking old revenge, now also vying for the throne. The broadcast ends on a montage of every major figure in the war to come, closing on the Unwashed.

Epilogue — Louis Santiago 2

Louis wakes not in the safety of the Pineapple Cabaret as planned, but on Floor 15 — Sheol itself, the casino portal secretly redirected. Chris is being restrained mid-transformation; Britney stands guard with Ysalte's pickaxe; Pontiff is confirmed alive. A friendly demon, Forkith, fits Louis with a symbiotic leech to survive Sheol's heat and reveals the redirection was deliberate — a different front needs soldiers. Samantha messages in from somewhere she never names: she stowed away with Taranis and Krakaren, who are failing to physically reassemble their fragmented mother, Apito — and confesses her real agenda all along was to kill "the demon mother lady and her jerk son," who tricked her into birthing something meant to destroy all creation, inside the dungeon and out.

Sourced from Book 8: A Parade of Horribles.

docs.title: Characters
docs.text:
Full pages exist for the series' central duo, their guide, and anyone else who's earned it. Everyone else who appears with real substance in Book 1 is listed below in a table; pages will be split out as they accumulate enough detail across later books.

Promotion rule

A supporting-cast entry graduates from a table row to a full page once either:

  • they've appeared with real material across 2+ books, or
  • they already have a significant plot role, even within a single book — a real turning point, a named recurring ability/relationship, not just a scene appearance.

Quick Facts standard

Every full page's Quick Facts box should include Type, Class, and Subclass (even if the answer is "not yet assigned" or "not applicable"), plus Notable spells/abilities and Notable items — linking to spell/item pages where they exist. If the book genuinely shows none (e.g. a Non-Combatant NPC), say so explicitly rather than omitting the field. Any spell, item, or physical skill named here must itself have a full Reference page (see Spells / Items & Tattoos / Abilities & Skills) — not just a table row — and the Quick Facts entry must link to it. Magic spells go under Spells; physical combat skills (no mana cost, no tome/scroll) go under Abilities & Skills.

docs.title: Full pages
docs.text:
• Carl — protagonist, human, bare-knuckle fighter
  • Princess Donut — Carl's cat, deuteragonist
  • Mordecai — Floors 1–3 tutorial guide, Changeling/skyfowl
  • Mongo — Donut's bonded pet, a Mongoliensis (velociraptor)
  • Katia — party member, shapeshifter; kills Hekla and jumps to Level 37 in Book 3
  • Imani C — Meadow Lark nurse turned Floor 4 defense organizer (Book 1, 3)
  • Elle McGibbons — Meadow Lark elder turned Frost Maiden scout (Book 1–3)
  • Li Jun — Floor 3 leaderboard crawler, key Floor 4 ally (Book 2–3)
  • Li Na — Li Jun's sister; first crawler in the game's history to max every base stat at 300 (Book 3, 6–7)

The rest, alphabetically:

  • Akuma — level-100 war mage, leader of the War Mage Rebellion (Book 7–8)
  • Architect Houston — Viceroy, warlord of the Madness, Book 7's most menacing antagonist — killed in Book 7
  • Asher — Carl's ~6-year-old half-brother, discovered on Floor 8 and already dead (Book 6)
  • Astrid — Desperado Club assistant manager, secret ex-crawler, assassinated on a contract from her own husband (Book 3, 5–6)
  • Baroness Victory — orc judge, the Princess Posse's Faction Wars adjutant, later acting Prime Minister of the Syndicate (Book 6–7)
  • Bautista — Tigran swashbuckler, Katia's boyfriend (Book 2–5)
  • Beatrice — Carl's ex-girlfriend, Donut's original owner, revealed alive (Book 1, 4–5)
  • Brandon An — Meadow Lark leader, dies holding the line as Floor 3 collapses (Book 1, 3)
  • Britney Proskurina — pit-fighter crawler, sacrifices her jacket (and face) for the party (Book 4–5)
  • Chris Andrews — Brandon's estranged brother; possessed by an Infiltrator parasite, freed in Book 4 (Book 1, 3–4)
  • Circe Took — mantis hive queen, sponsors and becomes the goddess Diwata (Book 5)
  • Colonel Boomer — elven Legate, "tenner," wanted fugitive; field commander of the 106th Bloody Leeches (Book 7)
  • Corcunda — split half-mantaur stripper, Dong Quixote's long-lost lover, reunited and smitten by Grull in the same day (Book 8)
  • Damascus Steel — Ifrit dancer, Guild of Suffering doorkeeper, son of Astrid and the Night Wyrm (Book 6)
  • Dmitri and Maxim Popov — two-headed nodling crawlers, escape as rescued children (Book 5)
  • Epitome Tagg — warlord of the Dream, a secret cyborg grafted inside Louis Santiago's chest (Book 5–7)
  • Eva Sigrid — Katia's oldest friend turned betrayer, co-architect of the Hekla plot (Book 3)
  • Ferdinand — Donut's pre-apocalypse cat love, revealed as a brainwashed Province Boss (Book 5)
  • Florin — golden-marked crocodilian crawler, joins Katia's splinter team (Book 2–5)
  • Frank Q — Book 1 player-killer, resurfaces on Floor 4 with the Ring of Divine Suffering (Book 1, 3–4)
  • Grigori the Placid — fleshmancer mercenary, briefly possessed by the system AI to deliver the dungeon's true cosmology (Book 8)
  • Gwendolyn Duet — Floor 5 land-quadrant team leader, joins Katia's splinter team (Book 4)
  • Hekla — leader of Brynhild's Daughters, firebolt-crossbow Valkyrie — killed in Book 3
  • Jasha and Radoslav — bugbear musicians of Team Free Love, killed by Carl himself to save time on a rescue (Book 8)
  • Juice Box — Hump Town changeling bartender turned Floor-6 agent (Book 4)
  • Justice Light — Skyfowl trap master, 8th-edition cookbook author; breaks the Nothing and wakes Scolopendra (Book 7)
  • Kandy "Bigs" Newton — level-29 sluggalette with a head-mounted hatchet; kills Princess Vinata (Book 7)
  • Louis Santiago — pest-exterminator crawler, engaged to Juice Box (Book 4–5)
  • Lucia Mar — rival broadcast star, mace-and-rottweilers crawler
  • Milk — Xenopus/Vesper hybrid, 6th-edition cookbook author, guildmaster of the hidden Cartography and Calligraphy guilds (Book 7)
  • Miriam Dom — "the goat lady," broadcast-only crawler with a Hellspawn familiar (Book 2–3)
  • Odette — host of Dungeon Crawler After Hours, secret rescuer of Beatrice (Book 1–5)
  • Osvaldo — Curupira ranger with a doomed god-quest over two memorial crystals — killed by Britney Proskurina (Book 6–8)
  • Paz Lo — Cuban Santero, smitten by his own god and turned into a totem card — the first crawler to become one (Book 6)
  • Penelope — a pig accidentally made sapient, used as bait against two gods (Book 8)
  • Prepotente — 2nd on the Floor 4 leaderboard; revealed in Book 3 to be a sapient, transformed goat
  • Princess Chandra, Esq. — Naga lawyer who marries Carl via Widow's Rights and tries to seize Donut's fortune (Book 8)
  • Princess D'Nadia — Prism Kingdom royalty turned sponsor and pageant judge (Book 2–5)
  • Princess Vinata — the reigning Sepsis Whore, six-armed naga warlord of the Blood Sultanate — killed in Book 7
  • Quasar — Carl's Nullian attorney, negotiates his Floor 6 collateral deal (Book 5)
  • Queen Imogen — Floor 6 country boss, Signet's half-sister — killed in Book 5
  • Rosetta Thagra — Crest ex-crawler, host of Shadow Boxer, 9th-edition cookbook contributor and covert resistance operative (Book 6)
  • Samantha (Psamathe) — hired trainer NPC, a minor deity split into a possessed sex-doll head (Book 4)
  • Sir Rendlegore — Carl's bonded tummy acher, formerly Tserendolgor's pet Garret (Book 7)
  • Sister Ines Quiteria — Cat Girl Poet Laureate, convicted mass-murderer, Book 6's secondary antagonist (Book 6)
  • The System AI — the dungeon's narrating, rule-enforcing, bit-doing observer AI
  • Toyotomi — Sai fortification engineer inherited from the defeated Prism; builds the Nest — killed in Book 7
  • Tsarina Signet — Floor 3 Elite, blood-magic summoner (Book 2)
  • Tserendolgor — Mongolian ex-supermodel crawler; denies the showrunners a fight and detonates herself (Book 5–6)
  • Volteeg — Gargoyle/Sturnus hybrid, 7th-edition cookbook author; ends the Operatic Collective by himself (Book 7)
  • Vrah — Dark Hive heir hunter, infected by Carl, killed at the Masquerade (Book 5)
  • Zev — Borant PR/outreach admin assigned to Carl and Donut (Book 1–5)

See the Supporting Cast page for everyone else who appears with real substance but hasn't earned a full page yet.

docs.title: Akuma
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: War mage — a dungeon-born symbiote of skeleton, flesher and sapient magic. Leader, and eventually sole Warlord, of the War Mage Rebellion
  • Race: War mage. "This was originally a high-elf cobbler with a human skin, resleeved 12 times before the ambient magic gave him his final form." He presents as "a long-haired elf, old and wizened with an angry sneer on his sagging face"
  • Class: War Mage — the system prints it as his class line
  • Subclass: None stated
  • Level: 100
  • Role: Warlord of a non-team entity that is handed official standing by accident, wins control of the city defense system, and then walks away from it
  • Notable spells/abilities: None named individually. "War mages come with knowledge of hundreds of spells," and he is "arguably the most powerful non-god magic caster on this floor." His group breaks a Conscription lock with "a clever combination of Pull spells." A war mage's head detonates as a Sapient Moment of Destruction roughly ten minutes after death
  • Notable items: The Gate of the Feral Gods, taken from Elle McGibbons in Chapter 61
  • Status: Alive — he voluntarily leaves the realm in Chapter 78, which defeats his own team

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Akuma is the only warlord in Book 7 who wins his war and then declines the prize. He begins the floor as a conscripted asset of the Skull Empire, ends it holding the throne room that would have won Faction Wars outright, and leaves the floor with the one thing he actually came for.

Carl first examines him in the clearing where King Stalwart dies:

Akuma. War Mage. Level 100.

Leader of the War Mage Rebellion.

This was originally a high-elf cobbler with a human skin, resleeved 12 times before the ambient magic gave him his final form. He’s arguably the most powerful non-god magic caster on this floor. He’s also a complete prick, as evidenced by the company he keeps.

The accompanying cookbook entry is a long essay on war mages as a species: they are "one of the few, true dungeon-born entities," created accidentally by overuse of You're Not Done Yet, formed when a flesher re-sleeves a reanimated skeleton enough times that the magic itself becomes sapient. "And nobody made them! All of this just happened on its own." The entry closes with a pointed warning to the showrunners: "maybe you should ask that pissed-off changeling army that's in the middle of wrecking your shit why you should probably keep an eye on the things you unleash, especially when you don't fully understand what they are."

docs.title: Killing Stalwart and Taking the Gate
docs.text:
In Chapter 61, Carl and Elle have the Gate of the Feral Gods open in orc territory. War mages teleport in en masse; Elle is knocked unconscious into a tree. Four of Donut's Magic Missile kills are already smoking on the ground when Carl arrives.

Stalwart was here, on his knees, crying in pain. There were four corpses on the ground. War mages. The magical beings were dead and smoking. They’d all been hit and killed with Donut’s amped-up Magic Missile before they’d all teleported here. Three more of the war mages surrounded Stalwart, shouting. A fourth stood off to the side.

The fourth is Akuma. His colonel's insignia fades away as Carl watches, and the group's dots turn white and then "a brownish-orange glow" — a color no army on the board uses.

As I watched in horror, the three war mages surrounding Stalwart each chanted something in unison, and the orc’s flesh began to tear.

I met eyes with the terrified orc for just a moment.

“My sister was right,” King Stalwart, leader of the Skull Empire, said in the moment before he exploded right in front of me, showering the clearing with his gore.

The four mages do not attack Carl. Then he sees what Akuma is holding.

For the first time, I saw what was in the hands of Akuma, the leader of this group.

He had taken the Gate of the Feral Gods from Elle.

The war mage was staring at my bare feet.

“Nice shoes, asshole,” he said to me before the four of them teleported away.

Elle's own account: "That war mage prick snatched the gate right out of my hands." She also notices he pulled a punch — "That strong one, the elf-looking guy. He pulled back at the last moment. It was almost like he was trying not to kill me."

Who gets the credit

The system awards the kill to "three members of the War Mage Rebellion," and the text places Akuma standing apart from the three who did the chanting. He is named as the group's leader and as the one holding the gate, not as one of the three killers.

Baroness Victory's reconstruction: "it appears the War Mages broke their own allegiance against the Skull Empire, which they shouldn't be able to do. They were under strict Conscription rules, but they used a clever combination of Pull spells to kill Stalwart anyway. I think Stalwart might've ejected them from his army on purpose in an attempt to get them to stop hurting him. It didn't work."

docs.title: How a Non-Team Got Standing
docs.text:
The killing creates a category the game does not have. Victory, immediately after: "We just received notification that there's a new, non-team entity called the War Mage Rebellion. I still don't know what that even means. 'Non-team entity' is not a thing. At least it wasn't until just now."

Because they are not a team, Stalwart's assets are awarded to whoever is sitting in the Bone Clan's throne room instead. Drick, Team Retribution's own adjutant, then calls a foul against his own team, alleging illegal interference, and a full quorum is convened. The quorum's finding backfires spectacularly:

Warlord Message: A full quorum adjudication has determined no cheating has occurred by any warlords. Any players under an administrative hold have now been released.

Warlord Message: After a careful deliberation, it has been determined that the Non-Team Entity known as the War Mage Rebellion will not be allowed access to Larracos until the Peeling phase.

Warlord Message: Since we are now in the Peeling Phase, this ruling is rendered moot. However, the system has determined that the Quorum’s ruling has given the War Mage Rebellion standing.

A ruling meant to restrict the war mages is the ruling that makes them real. The faction itself is covered elsewhere; what matters for Akuma is that this is the moment he becomes a warlord with system access.

docs.title: The Agatha Problem
docs.text:
Standing comes with a warlord, and the system does not give it to him. Agatha — the residual Carl was ordered by Zev never to interact with ("You are not to interact with Agatha. This is a direct order.") — is named Warlord of the War Mage Rebellion, and Akuma is attached as co-warlord. Her three emergency action items grant the Rebellion full warlord access, open the Conscription spell to unaffiliated players, and revert the Peeling Phase to the original Faction Wars rule that every soldier and warlord of a defeated team drops dead where they stand.

Victory, on the arrangement (Chapter 69): "They clearly did not anticipate Agatha would be named as a co-warlord, and the other leader, Akuma, does not like her. The system is going all in with them." And later in the same chapter: "Based on that Akuma guy's reaction when they assigned her as co-warlord, I don't think they are assisting each other at all."

Agatha then abandons the post she was handed:

Warlord Message: Warlord Agatha of the War Mage Rebellion has been deemed to have abandoned her post. As such, she has been removed as Warlord from the War Mage Rebellion. Warlord Akuma has been given full system access and named sole Warlord.

docs.title: "She Seeks to Kill Us All"
docs.text:
In Chapter 77 the Rebellion abandons Team Retribution's throne room — the six-hour hold that would have won them the season — and the city defense system goes inert. In Chapter 78, Akuma opens a conversation in the warlord chat that Carl calls "bewildering."

Warlord Akuma: Hey, underwear boy. Do me a favor. Kill that old lady for me, and I’ll forgive you and your pet for killing off so many of my brothers.

The Champion of Nekhebit: I AM NOT A PET, MR. WAR MAGE. AND WHY ARE YOU MAD AT ELLE? SHE IS DELIGHTFUL. ALSO HOW CAN I CHANGE MY NAME BACK TO WARLORD DONUT? IT DOESN’T DO THIS IN THE REGULAR CHAT.

Warlord Akuma: Is Elle the one on the Four Seasons path? Not her, dipshit. Keep her alive if you wish for us to face Scolopendra and survive. Agatha. The other warlord we were forced to accept in order to gain system access. She was forced upon us, and she is an enemy to you. She is an enemy to us all. We had no hand in those so-called “action items” other than the Conscription one. She slipped away before I was able to kill her. Do this for me, and we will be allies.

Carl catches the word that matters — "Us? If you wish for 'us' to survive?" — and offers to meet. Akuma's answer is his exit statement:

Warlord Akuma: You won’t be seeing me again on this floor. We never wished to keep that falling-down castle. We sought to test the potions we gathered. We wished to find the Scavenger’s daughter, who was hidden within the castle, and we found her. She is with us now. Once we had her in our possession, we left. That was all we ever wanted with this place, and we are no enemies to you. But Agatha’s actions continue to place everybody and everything in jeopardy, and she must be dealt with. She has a method that allows her to jump to the Waiting Room and reappear outside an open stairwell. You won’t likely see her on this floor again. You will have to find her on the 10th. Do this for us if you want to survive. She seeks to kill us all. Not just you and not just me. Everybody and everything.

Donut's contribution to the exchange, in full: "DID YOU JUST CALL ME A DIPSHIT? I'M A HIGHER LEVEL THAN YOU ARE, YOU SAGGY TWAT."

docs.title: Leaving the Realm
docs.text:
The message thread is immediately followed by the cleanest exit in the book:

Warlord Message: Warlord Akuma has left the realm. As per the current season’s ruleset, the War Mage rebellion has been defeated. They have no assets to award.

No throne room falls, no soldiers die, nothing transfers. Carl forwards the whole conversation to Victory and Zev; neither answers quickly, which worries him more. Victory's eventual reply dodges the question entirely: "I don't know where Akuma went. That team is officially defeated and therefore no longer under our authority."

Unresolved

Three threads are left open. What the war mages were testing their gathered potions for is never explained. Who or what "the Scavenger's daughter, who was hidden within the castle" is — a person, given Akuma's "she" — is never established; Carl asks Mordecai directly ("who is the Scavenger? And who is the Scavenger's Daughter? I know it's the name of my patch, but I didn't know there was more to it than that") and is brushed off. See The Scavenger's Daughter. And Akuma's reference to facing Scolopendra — and to Elle being "the one on the Four Seasons path" — is dropped without follow-up.

docs.title: Book 8: A Parade of Horribles
docs.text: Akuma resurfaces on Floor 10, and this time he isn't running from Carl — he needs him.

docs.title: The Note
docs.text:
Early in Heat 3, a gremlin delivers Carl a note that Carl recognizes as Akuma's the instant he reads it:

"Don't tell anyone about this note. You need to kill two teams next heat. Come visit us when we open after the next race, and I'll explain why. Ask for the top-shelf upgrades so you're led to the back. We don't have to be enemies, Carl. We want the same thing. I can smuggle friends to the Pineapple Cabaret. We can escape this chaos. Come alone. — Akuma."

docs.title: Cornered and Tortured
docs.text:
Carl's group ambushes him instead of coming alone, at the Chicken & Waffles upgrade shop in Heat 4. Elle McGibbons — still owed payback for the stolen Gate of the Feral Gods — freezes one of his testicles solid with an ice bolt the moment Donut mutes him, and the interrogation proceeds from there. What Akuma gives up, under duress and admittedly "fuzzy" on some details, is the single biggest lore-dump of the book's first half:

  • Herot, the 16th-edition cookbook author, is a skink former crawler still alive, secretly running the hidden pocket dimension called the Pineapple Cabaret from the inside — a discovery Akuma made alongside another former crawler, Menerva, after they realized NPCs and mobs were supposed to be periodically "recycled" for their own sake but were instead being exploited and reused indefinitely.
  • The Pineapple Cabaret itself was originally built as a cover project — the never-visited 17th floor — that quietly became a genuine escape route for exploited NPCs, one Akuma admits he engineered forcing Carl into a two-team kill to guarantee Carl would need his help getting access to.
  • Akuma's team is chasing something called the Scavenger's Daughter inside the Cabaret, which he is deliberately vague about.
  • He's the source (though not the only one) of the book's exposition on the "Big Six" dungeon power factions — the system AI itself delivers a fuller version later, in its own voice, during the Heat 7 casino ambush with the shadow mimic "Mitch" (see Carl).

Akuma's own summary of why any of this matters: "After what just happened with the Nothing being broken, everyone is aware of them now... That is why we must work together. You didn't need to crush my fucking balls."

docs.title: Fate
docs.text:
Akuma tells Carl directly, before the end of Heat 5, that he intends to leave the floor: "I am still here. I will be leaving soon. Stop messaging me unless it's important." He is not shown captured, killed, or freed on the page after that — the last confirmation of his status is his own statement of intent to leave, and he later appears only as one of several named figures (alongside Carl, Donut, Li Na, Samantha, and others) flashed across the screen during the system AI's galaxy-wide Ascendency announcement in the epilogue, implying continued relevance rather than closure.

Unresolved

Book 8 never confirms what became of Akuma after Heat 5, nor what the War Mage Rebellion's ultimate relationship to the Pineapple Cabaret and the Scavenger's Daughter turns out to be.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Elle McGibbons — robbed of the Gate of the Feral Gods, and the crawler Akuma tells Carl to keep alive; tortures him for information in Book 8
  • Carl — "underwear boy," the warlord Akuma tries to recruit against his own co-warlord
  • Supporting cast — for Agatha, Drick, and Judge Deng Bao, the grixist adjutant the system assigns to the Rebellion ("He's the only one who would do it")

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin and Book 8: A Parade of Horribles.

docs.title: Architect Houston
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: NPC warlord — leader of the Madness in Faction Wars, and prime of the Viceroys, a title he holds “not because he was elected so, or because of some innate ability to lead his people, but because he’s made the most scientific discoveries”
  • Race: Viceroy. Publicly a white featureless mask with a small red teardrop at its centre and long, flowing, starkly white robes “like a pope.” Underneath: a multi-limbed half-bug, half-monster with six arms and mandibles, which Carl compares to “a mix between a Predator alien and a goblin with no lips”
  • Class: None stated — warlords are not given character sheets
  • Subclass: None stated
  • Level: Not stated
  • Notable spells/abilities: No named spell list. He casts at least twice in the surgical theatre — once on the corpse suspended above him — and produces a rifle from under his robes
  • Notable items: The Grease Monkey, a Viceroy Portable Surgical and Scientific Exploration Unit — a chrome chandelier of robotic arms and surgical tools hanging from his theatre ceiling; a ring of eight Containment Breach Trap Mark IV modules loaded with Sheol fire, chained in sequence, Tripper-proof, and wired to a dead man’s switch attached to him
  • Status: Deceased — Chapter 68, killed by Carl with Gloom Wraith Phase

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Houston is the book’s most menacing antagonist, and almost all of it is delivered through what he says — which is not much, and never loudly. Through the whole first adjudication he does not speak or move at all; he simply watches Carl, his neck making “a slight creaking noise, like from a wooden ship” when he turns his head.

He is introduced second-hand, by the awakened dwarf NPC Arief, who draws his sword in a corridor to announce a grudge: “When the fighting starts, I will have my revenge against Architect Houston!”

“The leader of the Madness,” the dwarf said. “A Viceroy outworlder. He caught my brother as he attempted to sabotage their fortifications.” He re-sheathed his blade over his shoulder. “They say my brother was tortured before Juice Box infiltrated and ended his suffering.”

“That was one of his surgeons,” the dwarf said. “Nobody has managed to get into Houston’s operating theater. That’s what they call his lair next to the throne room.”

King Rust, in the middle of telling Carl the solar system is about to be destroyed and that he no longer cares about anything, stops to say this:

And if not us, that lunatic Architect Houston has been using this season’s rules to... open up his full arsenal.” He sighed, almost wistfully, and he met my eyes. “I can admit this now. He’s the only living creature in this universe I fear. But that doesn’t matter anymore. Death looms for us all.”

docs.title: The Adjudication
docs.text:
Chapters 18 and 19 put Carl in a room with him. The hearing concerns Commander Stockade of the Lemig Sortion’s attempt to kill Carl by timing a Summon Ally request to land while Shi Maria had control of his unconscious body; the adjutants conclude that Stockade and Houston conspired together to run real-time outside intelligence through Nurse Yugoslav of the Madness — Houston’s mother — on the 18th floor.

Houston refuses to confess and is found not culpable. Baroness Victory’s assessment is exact:

Victory shrugged. “Houston is obviously guilty, but unless he admits it, he was smart enough to let Stockade do all of his dirty work. I will vote not culpable for both the Madness team and the Princess Posse.”

Carl, who has just sat through a screen replay of Katia’s worst memories being watched for entertainment, needles him with the one thing available: “Your mom? Your mom is here in the dungeon? I can’t wait to meet her.” The reply arrives privately in the warlord chat, and it is the first time Houston says anything at all:

Architect Houston: If you ever mention my mother out loud ever again, you and that animal companion of yours will spend the last thousand hours of your existence upon the amplification table in my surgical theater. This is a promise.

Warlord Carl: Oh, fuck off.

Architect Houston: You are in mortal danger at this very moment, and you don’t even realize it. I do hope you escape so we can extend our play, but gracious pet owners accept the gifts their animals drop at their doorsteps.

Then Stockade, driven insane by the spider’s Insanity spell, begins smashing his own face against the floor in front of everyone. Victory offers Houston the chance to intervene — “Feel free to help him. Or call his guards.” He does not move. He continues to stare directly at Carl while the caterpillar beats his own brains out, and the Madness inherits the entire defeated Lemig Sortion as a result.

The ceasefire ends in the same breath as the ruling, and Houston’s opening move of the war is to stand up, throw back his robes, and shoot Carl in the chest at a conference table.

docs.title: The Beautiful Place
docs.text:
At the Chapter 43 warlord council, Juice Box shapeshifts into a form that unnerves every leader in the room. Houston’s reaction is the one Carl notices:

Architect Houston’s reaction was the strangest of all. The Viceroy jumped to his feet, his strange robes undulating. He put both hands on the table and leaned forward. He was shaking, and if I didn’t know better, he was shaking with excitement.

He is the one who explains what she turned into, over Epitome Tagg’s objections, and the book lets him talk:

“Now is not the time or place to rehash that story, but to say that was the personification of the Nothing is one way to describe it. Though what that thing truly is goes well beyond that. There is some scientific basis that this creature actually exists and is...”

“There is some scientific basis that this creature, who does not have a single name, is what some people see at the moment of death. It is theorized it’s not some supernatural deity, like many believe, but a trans-dimensional entity, similar to the Apothecary. There is no proof that merely seeing this creature imprints you in some way that damns you.”

“It has a thousand names,” Houston said. “Before most cultures in this galaxy found the stars, they’d already had a name for it. The Hag. The Unwashed. The Stalker. The Last Light. The Thirst. The Fell. The Inexorable. But we, the Viceroys who seek all understanding of life and death... We call it The Beautiful Place. There’s an interesting, involuntary nerve reaction in some species to the very image of the creature, even in those who are otherwise paralyzed. It is studied extensively, but we still have more questions than answers.” After a moment, he added, somewhat wistfully, “Gaining access to this creature is my life’s work.”

For the rest of the council he paces back and forth, on his feet, unable to sit down.

docs.title: The Surgical Theatre
docs.text:
Carl reaches the Castle of the Madness in Chapter 67 with Dong Quixote, Bigs, Jamal and Rend. Ping shows twenty soldiers and, in the room beside the throne room, one purple dot and one white — plus three crawlers and a crawler’s corpse.

The corpse is Zeynep, a Turkish crawler Carl met on Floor 8 and never spoke to on this one. Two of her surviving squadmates, Selvi and Tuba, are conscripted into the Madness army. The third crawler in the theatre is Burcu, the badger-headed porsuk swashbuckler from the Butcher’s Masquerade, and she is still alive.

Down the hallway, the screaming keeps starting and stopping. “That... that sounds like it’s him screaming. Architect Houston.”

The doors are marked Do Not Enter, with a lit neon sign beneath reading Amplification in process. Inside is an octagonal white room with a raised viewing gallery so students can watch, four surgical tables, and the Grease Monkey overhead — “a chandelier covered in robotic arms and surgical tools, all spinning and waving about, silently whisking as they worked.”

Zeynep is on the first table, cause of death Died on the Surgical Table. Carl will not describe what was done to her: “They had done... something to her. Something unspeakable. Something I won’t describe.”

Burcu is on the second, bound by magic, tongue and voice box cut out. Her first successful message is:

Burcu: There you are! None of my messages were delivered. He cut out my tongue and voice box. I can’t speak. He tortured my mother. He killed her right in front of me. Free me so I can kill him. These bindings won’t let me cast magic. You owe me, Carl. You killed my father. Free me now.

On the third table is Houston himself — robes gone, mask gone — with the peeled-open corpse of a changeling named Namico suspended upside down ten inches above him, the two of them being physically spliced together by the machine. “Things were coming out of the changeling and going into Houston and vice-versa.”

He is being operated on by his own machine, without anaesthetic, and he is screaming. His first words to Carl are not a threat:

“Stay back,” Houston called at me. He was clearly in pain as the machine continued to work. Hundreds of tiny little arms appeared, and they were connecting what appeared to be nerves from the changeling’s neck to Houston. “You take one step in here, and it’ll set off the traps, incinerating us all. “I’m almost done. I’m almost there. You’ll have your victory, Carl. I care no longer for what happens here. Let me finish. Let me finish, and your fellow crawler doesn’t have to die. This is my life’s work. I’m almost there.”

And, as Carl reaches for the switch that will release Burcu’s bindings:

“Carl. Do not... Do not press that button. I can stop it all,” Houston called. “You don’t understand. It is called the Beautiful Place. I can get there. They are the key. The changelings. This world. Why do you think we come here, cycle after cycle? You’ve helped make the greatest discovery in history, and you don’t even realize it. It was here all along, right under our mandibles.”

docs.title: Death
docs.text:
Carl cannot simply step into the room and let the traps kill everyone, because Burcu has no invulnerability and would be turned to ash. So he crosses the theatre by jumping table to table with Walk on Air, which is how the whole thing comes apart: his own invulnerability expires mid-crossing, he knocks Zeynep’s corpse to pieces landing on it, he puts Burcu to sleep with the wand of Nighty-Night, and then the table he lands on tips over.

Before that, he does something stranger. Houston’s health bar drops and he begins to die on the table — and the changeling corpse above him starts to change, growing roots.

“Yes!” Houston called as he died. He was sobbing. “I found you. I found you. After all this time. You were right here all along. It’s really you, isn’t it? Not just an avatar. It’s you. It’s you.”

Carl throws a Fine Healing potion at his head to stop it. “‘Gah!’ he cried as his health rocketed back up. ‘No! No! What did you do?’”

Then the table tips, Burcu falls, Carl’s bare feet hit the floor, and the dead man’s switch arms the whole ring of Sheol-fire traps.

“You don’t know what you’ve done,” was all Houston said in the moments before the traps fired.

For my part, I activated Gloom Wraith Phase the very moment my feet touched the ground.

I shot forward in the direction I was facing, which was toward Architect Houston, still alive, still on the table, still under the creature surgically attached to him.

I pushed through them, everything moving in slow motion as the fire descended upon the room from all directions at once. I passed through the naked Houston, unraveling him.

Carl exits the room non-corporeal, hits something magical on the way out, dislocates a shoulder and is briefly knocked unconscious. Burcu dies in the fire. In the spin, the thing that used to be the changeling turns to face him and briefly becomes Li Jun, who thanks him and is whisked away by roots.

System Message: Architect Houston of the Madness has fallen. Credit for the kill has been given to Warlord Carl of the Princess Posse.

System Message: The Madness has been defeated.

System Message: All assets of the Madness have been awarded to the Princess Posse.

Unresolved

What Houston found, whether he reached the Beautiful Place, what the changeling became, and what Carl actually saw and passed through on his way out are all left open. Carl’s own account is deliberately uncertain: “I’d seen something, but I wasn’t sure if it was real. It felt like a dream.”

docs.title: The Peeling Phase
docs.text:
His death is the trigger for the last act of Faction Wars. The system messages run straight on from the kill credit:

System Message: Battlefield conditions have been met. Larracos is no longer safe.

Warning. Warning. Warning.

System Message: The Peeling Phase is upon us. This city is open. First to take the castle, wins.

And remember, folks. Only one team can win. Alliances don’t matter in the end.

Within seconds, the War Mage Rebellion is granted standing, full access to the Conscription spell, and a reversion to the original Faction Wars rules — under which “every affiliated soldier and warlord on a team who is still on the battlefield will now drop dead where they stand the moment the team is defeated.” Victory’s message arrives in the same barrage: “I’m sorry. We tried to delay as long as possible. Our attempts have backfired. We were out maneuvered.”

Eliminating the Madness removes the faction Carl most feared and hands him its entire asset pool. It also ends the phase of the game in which anyone was safe.

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Asher
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: Human, non-crawler — a memory ghost on Floor 8, and one of the nine heads of a city boss
  • Race: Human
  • Class / Subclass: Not applicable — Asher was never a crawler and was about six years old when the Earth was harvested
  • Family: Son of Carl's father and Tami-Lynn; Carl's half-brother. Carl never knew he existed
  • Age: "Maybe six years old," with a birthday party scheduled for the following day. The book never gives a firm number
  • Notable spells/abilities: As a hydra head, a lightning attack and lightning resistance — pointedly assigned to the boy whose bedroom wall is covered in crayon drawings of storm clouds destroying cities, because he is afraid of lightning
  • Notable items: A heart-shaped candy box holding a shiny rock, two dollars and a plastic cowboy. Carl leaves it where it is
  • Status: Deceased, killed in the initial collapse along with his mother — a fact Carl only works out afterwards, from the rules of what a Reminiscence Hydra is made of

docs.title: The Reveal
docs.text:
Floor 8 — "The Ghosts of Earth" — replays memories of the crawlers' own lives. Carl's takes him into his father's trailer in Iowa, around June or July of the year before the collapse, to watch a man he hasn't seen in over twelve years die of liver failure at 140 pounds with a Mariners game on.

A boy's head appears around the hallway from the back bedrooms. His father shouts after him:

"Asher! Get back here you little shit!"

Asher, I thought. His name is Asher.

Carl had been holding out hope that his father had simply met a woman with kids. The face ends that: "But no. That nose. Those eyes. That hair. My mom always complained my dad's genes were so dominant, anyone remotely related to him was doomed to look just like him." He finds a wedding photo with the woman visibly pregnant, and a photo of his father with a one-year-old Asher on his lap.

Brown hair that looked like it was enough for two people. Thick and haphazard and untamable. Blue eyes. That nose.

Asher.

Asher.

My brother.

I had a brother.

Goddamn you, I thought.

Carl watches Tami-Lynn administer the lethal dose of morphine she's been hiding in the flowerpot outside, and doesn't watch the end. Her reason, delivered much later: she saw what the man had done to Carl and would not let it happen to Ash.

Before leaving the boy's bedroom, Carl says the thing he can say to someone who can't hear him:

"I'm so sorry I didn't know about you," I said. "If I had, I would've been here. I would've made sure you were okay. In a few months, something is going to happen, something really terrible. Hopefully you'll be asleep in your bed when it happens. It's too late for me to do anything about that, but I want you to know something. You won't be forgotten. Not ever."

I reached forward, and I put my hand on his head, but my hand went all the way through.

He notes there was no picture of himself anywhere in the trailer. No sign the boy knew he had a brother at all.

Carl does not tell Donut. "I wasn't certain why, especially after I promised him he wouldn't be forgotten. There would be time for that."

docs.title: The Reminiscence Hydra of Malicious Compliance
docs.text:
The trailer burns, and out of it comes the floor's city boss: a stitched flesh-ball the size of a small elephant on four stubby legs, with nine screaming heads on long stalks, each one the face of somebody Carl knows. It is billed as a rebranded "Scolopendra Nymph," a monster from the third and fourth seasons.

The nine: Asher; Tami-Lynn; Carl's friend Monobrow Sam; Bea's mother; Sugar Cube, one of Donut's relatives; Carl's supervisor Dick; his landlord Mr. Roth; Sally from billing; and Judge Lucian, a cat-show judge who acts as the hydra's deckmaster and leader.

The system's own announcer describes the cruelty of it out loud — "a naughty man with beautiful feet sitting there in his underwear, facing down a nine-headed monster that's probably going to kill him and his cat, all the while he wonders what any of this exposition has to do with the fact that one of those nine heads is that of his recently-discovered little brother." The AI also notes that it swapped the boss out at the last minute: the original was going to be Carl's father.

The Asher head taunts him — "Carl, why didn't you ever visit me?" — and Carl keeps lobbing bombs at it specifically to get it off the field, while the other heads swoop in to shield it. His coping mechanism is to read the writing: "The heads were clearly saying things the real versions of these people would never say… It was like the dungeon was trying too hard to be edgy, which in effect turned the whole thing into a parody. While making me watch the actual memory was a perfect way to try to break me, this was just pissing me off."

docs.title: "The Echo of Your Kin Has Been Muffled"
docs.text:
Half-dead and on fire, Carl silently asks his own totem, the spider Shi Maria, for a mercy:

Asher, I thought. Get him out of here. Kill him fast. He's suffered enough.

Shi Maria turned her head to regard me.

"Asher?" she asked, her head corkscrewing. "Which one of these little morsels of confusion is Asher?"

Her third eye — the one that is supposed to blind and madden anyone who looks into it — opens, and this is the moment she gets inside Carl's head:

Ah, yes. I see now. Don't worry, Carl. I will not blind you. Not in the way you're thinking.

"Carl, I wish I'd known you, too," the Asher head called out to me just before he was swallowed and then bitten off.

Three Heads Remaining.

There, Carl. The echo of your kin has been muffled. He rests. I have done something for you. Soon, soon you will do something for me.

That debt is the whole back half of the book. It is collected in Chapter 71, when Shi Maria takes control of Carl's body and tattoos the Eye of the Bedlam Bride into his chest.

Tami-Lynn is the last head standing. Her dying words are the confession:

"I don't regret it," she said. "I saw what happened to you, and I didn't want Ash to go through the same thing. So I made sure. I made sure it was done right."

Earlier in the fight she had screamed the line that detonates in the next chapter: "I wrote you, and you never answered! I needed help. Look what you made me do!"

docs.title: What Beatrice Knew
docs.text:
Donut lets it slip by accident, recognizing the boy's face from before the collapse:

"I've seen him a bunch of times, but I still don't really know who he is. Miss Beatrice had his picture on her phone, and she was always talking about him with her mother. His name is Asher. I think he was her nephew or something. I missed that whole drama, but Miss Beatrice's mom said to just ignore it."

…"And Miss Beatrice knew you had a brother, and she was hiding it from you? That's… that's something Georgina would do!"

Tami-Lynn had written to Carl, probably on Facebook. Beatrice saw it. Carl didn't.

Goddamn you, Beatrice. Up until that moment, I realized I'd never been mad at her. Even after all the cheating, all the lying, I hadn't been angry. I was just pissed at myself for being so stupid and naïve. Not until now. Now that it was too late.

His own read on why: "She didn't want me leaving. That was the only explanation. I would've come here, to Iowa, and she knew it." He tries once to extend her the benefit of the doubt and then shuts the whole thing down: "This is done. It's in the past, and it's blinding you. It's making you weak. It's what they want. They're trying to break you."

docs.title: Dead
docs.text:
Carl works out what membership in a Reminiscence Hydra actually means:

A wave of sadness washed over me. I finally realized what it meant for someone to be in that hydra. They were all dead. These were all people who'd been collected in the initial collapse.

He had hoped Asher and Tami-Lynn were asleep in their beds when it happened, and had been terrified the showrunners would use his brother as the boss outright — "They weren't allowed to do that anymore, not with children, but it was clear they cared little about the rules at this point."

docs.title: The Reason for Everything After
docs.text:
The last words of Carl's story in Book 6, as Floor 8 is scoured clean and he is pulled into the sky over Cuba:

Don't worry, I thought as I looked down upon the quickly receding landscape. I knew none of these people, but I was overwhelmed with the urge to make certain they would be proud of me. I thought of Asher, the brother I never knew. I needed to make him proud. I couldn't disappoint him. I would literally pull myself through hell on my hands and knees if I had to. I wasn't there for him while he lived, but I would be damned if I allowed his death to be for nothing.

You will not break me.

You will be avenged.

I swear it.

I swear it to you all.

Carl's father is never named

Donut asks directly. Carl refuses: "What was your dad's name, anyway? I don't think you ever said." / "It doesn't matter. He doesn't deserve to have one. Not anymore. It's done." No name for him appears anywhere in the text.

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: Astrid
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: NPC — Assistant Manager of the Desperado Club (and its head of security); secretly a former crawler working off an indenture contract
  • Race: Bloodlust Sprite — a small fae race; see Species and the Desperado Club
  • Level: 125
  • Also: Owner/head of the Naughty Boys Employment Agency, a 500,000-gold social upgrade sold as a saferoom addition; patron of the bard Doctor Bones; quietly ran a shadow Meat Shields office inside the Penis Parade so her sons' crew would count as protected mercenaries
  • Family: Wife of the Night Wyrm, head of the Guild of Suffering, whose real name is Hamed; mother of Damascus Steel and Anaconda
  • Notable spells/abilities: Cardiovascular magic — she can boil a target's blood with a snap of her fingers, and does; Cosmic Sense, a precognitive alert skill; flight. She once knocked Carl unconscious through a closed door
  • Notable items: None named — her magic is stored in her wings, which is what kills her
  • Status: Deceased — assassinated in the Desperado Club kitchens, Chapter 32/33

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Astrid has been part of the furniture since Book 3: the tiny, extremely dangerous fairy who has to come down and clean up whatever Carl and Donut have just done to the Desperado Club. She was summoned when a crawler tried to kill Donut; she was summoned again when the pair got caught on an off-limits floor. Carl's assessment before the job: "She's a level 125 bloodlust sprite. She knocked my ass out through a closed door last time. She has something called cardiovascular magic, and she can make my blood boil at the snap of a finger. Plus she's always surrounded by a bunch of guards. And she's a fairy. Because of my stupid goblin tattoo, she does even more damage to me."

She works and sleeps in a hollowed-out hole inside a tree, reached through a small vent near the ceiling at the end of the top-floor employees-only hallway.

Book 6 promotes her from a name on the mob roster to a person, and then kills her.

docs.title: The Contract
docs.text:
The Night Wyrm gives Carl and Katia a Guild of Suffering job. Guild contracts are cover-blind — saying the target's name out loud voids the quest and revokes guild access — so neither of them can discuss it with anyone, and neither knows who they are really working for.

"We wish to remove the competition. She serves dual roles. She keeps our family in the ground. She keeps our blood dry. You must kill her. The owner of the Naughty Boys Employment Agency. The assistant manager of the Desperado Club. She is one. Astrid. Kill her. Bring her lifeless body to the family."

The job is Katia's, and it is the last of the three seals on her Engaged Lock Box of the Night Wyrm — the only thing standing between her and the Orchid of Eileithyia's Grace, which is the only exit she can see from the Crown of the Sepsis Whore. If the job isn't completed, the succession rules will eventually force Katia and Donut to fight each other.

docs.title: The Ambush, and How It Fell Apart
docs.text:
Carl's plan: catch her in the narrow hidden hallway at the bottom of the secret passage she always uses to come down from the top floor. A motion-triggered smoke trap over the doorway, directional anti-NPC claymores packed with orcish iron BBs (deadly to fairies) aimed into the closet, teleport traps carpeting the hall to dump her guards into a locked upstairs closet, and Katia herself standing by invisible as the redundancy. Samantha, briefed on only half of it, was the lure — make a scene in the badger bar, refuse to leave, force the crocodilian guards to summon Astrid.

Three things went wrong at once:

  1. Astrid took the main stairs. "The door to the employee exit opened, and Astrid flew out. There was no warning… She went straight for the regular stairs. She hadn't used the secret stairwell at all." Every trap was in the wrong hallway.
  2. Samantha caused a containment breach in the casino. A player lost the knife game and was pulled into the Nothing; the tear let out Minge, a Level 225 Minor Feral Demon and the little sister of Samantha's old enemy Slit, who began hunting Samantha through the club by smell.
  3. Astrid's Cosmic Sense had already warned her. She took the fast route to the casino, and her response to the breach was to unleash the vorpals — the monsters sealed in the very back room the ambush had been built around.

Carl called an abort. Katia refused: "Carl, no. I have to do this… If I don't finish this now, we won't get a chance. The fight will be our distraction."

docs.title: Death
docs.text:
Cornered in the club kitchens amid the chaos, Astrid does not attack Carl. She warns him off — "Carl, is that you? You need to get out of here. It is not safe." — tells him where the vorpals will and won't go, and, unprompted, gives him her husband's real name as a kindness:

"You're in the Guild of Suffering. My husband is named Hamed, but he's known as the Night Wyrm. Don't tell him I told you his real name. His lair is hidden up there on the top floor."

When Katia's eight-foot troll totem crashes in, Astrid puts herself between the monster and Carl. She boils the troll's blood and kills it.

Katia — invisible, shapeshifted into "a metallic, spiked-covered, human-faced, canine monstrosity" — grabs Astrid out of the air and raises a spike over her head, and then freezes solid, millimetres short. Carl breaks the stalemate himself:

Astrid was right there, hovering in front of me, still clutched in Katia's hand. I reached forward, grasped onto her wings, and I ripped. They pulled off of her easily.

A fairy's magic lives in her wings. Katia comes unstuck; Katia's skull-headed crow totem takes both of Astrid's eyes. Blind, disarmed and dropped, she gets out most of a sentence:

"No, please! Save my children. I was almost done. I would be free soon. Tell them…"

A spike shoots from the wolf's neck and skewers her through the head mid-word. Katia inventories the corpse and shifts into an ogre on the way out so the NPC witnesses will blame a monster rather than a crawler.

Astrid dies without knowing that her own husband ordered the hit, without knowing Carl was involved, and having spent her last conscious act shielding him. "Astrid hadn't liked me, but she wasn't expecting me to attack her, either. In the end, she'd moved to shield me, to protect me from the monster. I'd ripped the wings right off of her."

docs.title: "I Was Almost Done"
docs.text:
The line haunts Carl for the rest of the book, and the answer arrives an hour later from her sons.

Astrid and Hamed were former crawlers serving out an indenture — Carl compares them to the bopcas — with the family's contract nearly expired. Damascus: "We were promised freedom. He wanted to make sure she was dead. They're still married. My mother has—had—so much… He gets it all. He'll have it all when we get out." She was killed in the game for money on the outside.

"Save my children" meant Damascus Steel and Anaconda, whose jobs, safety and cover all depended entirely on her position. Carl unknowingly honours it within the hour by buying the entire Penis Parade crew out of the club on a two-floor mercenary contract.

Sourced from Book 3: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook, Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade, and Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: Baroness Victory
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: NPC — Adjutant for the Princess Posse in Faction Wars, formally logged by the system as a “non-combatant” observer; by the end of Book 7, acting Prime Minister of the Syndicate
  • Race: Orc — Skull Empire nobility. Sister of the late Queen Consort Ugloo, aunt to Prince Maestro and Crown Prince Stalwart, sister-in-law to King Rust
  • Class: None stated — no character sheet or class is ever shown for her
  • Subclass: None stated
  • Level: Not stated anywhere in the book
  • Role: Rules referee, legal counsel and procedural weapon. Outside the dungeon she is a judge; Quasar calls her “Judge Victory”
  • Notable spells/abilities: Adjutant teleportation (she can follow the warlords onto the field and “cracks into existence” at will, even during Ramp-Up), adjutant invisibility, a protected non-corporeal form that weapons and hands pass straight through, and a direct line to the AI which she argues with out loud, eyes flashing
  • Notable items: A massive, cruel-looking battle-axe carried in her waistband
  • Status: Alive at the end of Book 7 — and promoted

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Victory is the referee Carl picked, and the single most useful non-combatant he has. She was chosen as adjutant at the end of Book 6 — see her row on the supporting cast page for that selection, where she won the job by mentioning she had recently sentenced her own aunt to indentureship for unpaid taxes and, drily, “I’m the only one the others sued to keep out of the game.” On Floor 9 she becomes a fixture: teleporting into trenches, standing silently in corners of the flag room, and appearing at Carl’s elbow at the exact moment a ruling is about to matter.

Quasar tells Carl how to use her before the floor even starts:

Just keep your head down and listen to what Judge Victory tells you. She’s a smart one.

Her opening briefing sets out exactly what she is and is not:

“I know you two prefer a more hands-on approach. I will be present when it’s prudent. If my presence causes a problem, let me know, and I will come back here. All adjutants can also go invisible if need be. But I will warn you. I can and will call out all fouls as I see them. That includes anything perpetrated by your team. If you have any questions about the rules, ask me first. I am on your side. I can help with strategy. In addition, I can make suggestions to fit something into the existing ruleset, if required.”

Donut, unconvinced, asks her whether her dead sister was nice or a jerk. Victory answers seriously, at length, about Ugloo losing herself when she married into the royal family. Donut’s justification: “You can judge someone based on how they talk about the dead.”

docs.title: Killing Herman the Fleet
docs.text:
In Chapter 13, Carl and Donut walk into the antechamber of their own flag room and find an Elite legionnaire of their own army writhing behind a desk.

Elite Herman the Fleet. Ogre Strongman. Level 70.

Legionnaire.

Princess Posse.

Herman the Fleet — third of the three ogre strongmen from Grimaldi’s circus — is a suicide bomber, packed with explosive satchels under his clothes and fighting the compulsion. “Been waiting. Brother says you good. Supposed to do it already. Been fighting it. Tell brother... tell sorry.” Donut fires a Magic Missile; Florin hits the deck; Tipid turns to smoke. And then the flag room door opens.

At the same moment, the door to the flag room opened, an armored orc stepped out, and she slammed a massive, cruel-looking battle-axe into the head of the struggling ogre.

The elite slumped over, dead.

Carl inventories the destabilising corpse. The orc watches him do it with “a slight hint of distaste on her boar-like face.” This is his first sight of her in the flesh, and of the tag over her head:

Baroness Victory.

Adjutant for The Princess Posse.

This is a “non-combatant” observer.

The quotation marks are new. “My eyes focused on the ‘non-combatant’ part of her name, which now had quotes around it. The AI had done that.”

Her only explanation to Carl is “I can only do so much for you, warlord.” Her justification to the system is a full legal argument delivered before anyone can charge her:

“That wasn’t a legal attack,” the orc said, sliding her blood-splattered axe back into her waistband. A bit of brain dripped off it and splatched onto her boot. “That was an unlawful assassination attempt by Sensation Entertainment, and I will be calling foul. I will be filing a grievance against the Dream, who now own the entertainment company. They were exerting undue influence on one of their elites to affect Faction Wars. Princess Donut, that was an admirable shot, and it may have saved you all. I will file for you to get credit for the kill.”

Then she argues it out with the AI in the room, out loud, alone:

The orc paused, looking up at the ceiling. “No,” she suddenly said out loud, angrily pointing at the ceiling. “Absolutely not. That was clearly a foul by the corporate interests who purchased Sensation, and if you don’t like it, you should re-read your own rules. In addition, you are out of line by not warning me he was being influenced.”

She paused again.

“I accept your apology,” she finally said.

Florin’s verdict, walking in behind her: “I don’t know if I should be terrified or in love.” Victory herself later files the incident away in one line — “What you saw just now was an anomaly.”

docs.title: The Rules Lawyer
docs.text:
Her value to Carl is almost entirely procedural, and the book keeps finding new uses for it.

At the minor-quorum adjudication in Chapters 18–19 — convened after Katia and Carl’s consciousnesses got tangled and Shi Maria slaughtered a ballroom of Lemig goblins — she sits between Carl and two enemy warlords and simply refutes the accusation that the Princess Posse were also cheating. “‘I will refute this,’ Victory said. The simple pronouncement was followed by a ping from the system.” That ping is the whole defence. She also winks at Carl across the room mid-hearing, and assesses the other warlord frankly:

Victory shrugged. “Houston is obviously guilty, but unless he admits it, he was smart enough to let Stockade do all of his dirty work. I will vote not culpable for both the Madness team and the Princess Posse.”

In the field she reads debuffs, spell exploits and enemy tricks for him — identifying the Gurgles (“A really nasty, contagious, non-curable debuff… The factions had agreed many years ago to never use it again because it’s so insidious”), and later cracking Lucia Mar’s inexplicable power source in one snap of her fingers: “It’s Power Siphon! Those jewels used for the towers leak all sorts of energy. They’re in range. It’s drawing power from the active towers in Larracos.” She calls it genius and admits she would never have thought of it.

She is equally willing to point the weapon at Carl. “Carl, I am very busy right now, but I’m not so busy that I won’t call foul. Don’t tempt me.” And she draws a hard line at intelligence:

Baroness Victory: There are rules. I follow those rules. I am not to be an intelligence source.

In the late-book adjudication that Carl is frantic to end, she reveals the tactic:

Baroness Victory: Carl, trust me on this. You want this trial to go on as long as possible. We’re stalling on purpose. We will stall until the AI gets so pissed, it ends it.

It does not work. Her message when the Madness falls and the Peeling Phase opens is four flat sentences: “I’m sorry. We tried to delay as long as possible. Our attempts have backfired. We were out maneuvered.”

One of the few duties she visibly hates is the live viewer update — standing in a privacy bubble alongside Drick, the adjutant for Team Retribution, doing colour commentary in “a strange, newscaster-like persona I hadn’t heard from her before,” and being leaned on by unnamed parties to do more of it.

docs.title: The Deal with Porthus
docs.text:
Victory is also running her own operation, and the book only shows it in the Rosetta interlude near the end of Part 3.

Rosetta Thagra killed King Rust on the battlefield — lassoing and decapitating her own people’s oldest enemy — and immediately scanned his hand, ring and severed head into a hand-held credit device to drain his accounts. What she needed and did not have was the PIN. Victory supplied it.

Baroness Victory: I was able to check the financial feed during the adjudication while we waited for that idiot Ferdinand to come down out of the rafters. It appears the money has reached the intended destination. Obviously we can’t see what’s really happening out there anymore, but we can still see transactions and their amounts. I can’t decipher what the gods is happening in the Naga system, but there was a transaction more than big enough to suggest your people were able to purchase two ships, despite the apparent chaos in the system. Assuming your Homecoming Queen starship follows your orders and shoots down that yacht, our transaction is done.

Rosetta: Thank you, Baroness. I know your sister would be proud.

The price of the PIN was an orc yacht in orbit — “The yacht they’d agreed to kill in exchange for the pin number contained several children. Orc children, yes, but children nonetheless.” The money buys two ships for Porthus and the Open Intellect Pacifist Network, so that the families of everyone trapped in the dungeon can run: one generation ship to board, the second handed to the goats in the Plenty system in exchange for passage through the forbidden gate at the Impetus Point.

Rosetta cannot work out what Victory gets from it. The narration is explicit that she is not playing for the Skull Empire throne — “There were no circumstances in which Baroness Victory would end up in charge of the Skull Empire, not unless she first killed about 1,000 other nobles spread across the galaxy, so her motivations in helping the Pacifist network were a mystery to Rosetta.” The deal was brokered between Porthus and Victory before Victory was chosen as an adjutant at all.

Unresolved

Her motive for the Porthus deal is never explained in Book 7. Rosetta flags it as a mystery and the book leaves it there.

Asked in the same exchange whether the arrangement compromises her, Victory is blunt:

Baroness Victory: Just because we have dealings together outside the dungeon doesn’t mean I am not taking my duties as adjutant seriously. I told you before I will not cheat nor will I help you cheat. Any information I give about in-dungeon rulings must go through warlords Carl or Donut. That said, everything is fucked. That’s what’s going on. We’re all going to die because the AI is insane.

docs.title: Prime Minister Victory
docs.text:
Three things happen in sequence in the last quarter of the book.

First, in Chapter 81, Prime Minister Glory of the Syndicate tries to have Carl killed by overriding the emergency ejection sequence through a legacy Syndicate control panel. The AI blocks it, freezes the world, and issues a threat instead of a reward:

A galactic power—In this case, Prime Minister Glory himself—just attempted to assassinate you using a little known, but apparently still active control panel that allows the Syndicate to override certain showrunner-controlled aspects of the game.

It didn’t work. And not only did it not work, but now I’m irritated.

You may be relieved that you’re not currently in this system, Prime Minister Glory. But you should be very, very worried that your adult children are.

Second, in Chapter 83, Victory and Fopsy blink back into the room from a virtual Syndicate Council session. “They’ve just called a No Confidence vote on Glory, and that’s happening right now.” She notes that Fopsy — a former Prime Minister, and the Dream’s adjutant — might get the job back if the vote breaks a certain way.

Third, in Chapter 86, she is still in Carl’s tent when Donut asks her why she hasn’t left with the other adjutants:

“No,” she said. She straightened. “With the unfortunate death of my underage nieces and nephews up in orbit, I once again became eligible for political office. Not allowed to be in office if you have underage leaders in your family. It’s an old, stupid rule, but a rule nonetheless. Anyway, as people weren’t certain of former Prime Minister Fopsy’s relationship to the Dream, he was passed over for the newly-vacated position of Syndicate Prime Minister. As a result, I am now acting Prime Minister Victory. There will be a real vote in a few months, but in the meantime, I’m it. They wanted someone stuck here with the rest of us so I could truly focus on the crisis.”

Those underage nieces and nephews are the children on the yacht she helped arrange to have shot down. The goddess Huanxin makes the connection out loud and to her face — “And I’m sure it’s just an unfortunate coincidence your underage nephew was blown out of orbit. Now that idiot the Maestro is the king, and you’re Prime Minister” — and Victory answers by telling her a mantis colony system has just gone nova. Minutes later Katia’s choice kills Huanxin at Victory’s feet.

Donut’s immediate reaction is that they now know a prime minister and can be rescued. Victory shuts it down: “It’s only temporary. And even if it wasn’t, it wouldn’t matter. I have less power now than I did when I was a judge. The council is just as bad as the Lemig Sortion these days. It’s total gridlock.”

Carl puts a hand on her shoulder, feels the softness of a protected form that his fist would pass straight through, and wishes her luck. Then:

As much as I loathed the idea of killing another few thousand schmucks who’d gotten railroaded into coming down here for the crawl, as much as I actually liked Victory, I wouldn’t hesitate. Not even for a moment, to kill the goddamn prime minister of the Syndicate.

She snorted. She knew it, too.

Her last words in the book are an apology for leaving early:

Okay, team. They are calling me away. I’m sure we’ll speak soon. I’m about to get yelled at for allowing the murder of another CEO. It was all within the rules, but they won’t care. Congratulations on your victory.”

“Yeah,” I said as Baroness Victory, now Prime Minister Victory disappeared for the last time.

docs.title: Voice
docs.text:
She is the driest character in the book, and the book gives her the best throwaway lines.

On spotting King Rust’s battle regalia on the horizon: “Well I’ll be fucked raw with a Soother sausage. That’s him alright. He must’ve come up from the 18th floor at the last minute. I wonder if he brought all his concubines with him?”

On Carl asking whether her family is as dysfunctional as his: “The bigger the universe, the smaller it becomes.”

On Prepotente delaying an adjudication: “Your boyfriend is holding up the adjudication. We’re waiting for Drick to get him out of the rafters. Literally.”

On her own rulings during Donut’s more improvisational moments, after asking what the plan is and being told there isn’t one: “You’re not going to question her?”

And her stock response to anything genuinely unprecedented — which on this floor is most things: “Don’t even ask because I have no idea what that was.”

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Bautista (Daniel Bautista 2)
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: Tigran Crawler
  • Class: Swashbuckler
  • Level: 28 (Book 3) → rising through Books 4–5
  • Party: Katia's splinter team
  • Relationship: Romantically involved with Katia as of Book 5; still together at the end of Book 7, when she leaves the dungeon pregnant by someone else
  • Notable spells/abilities: Swashbuckler swordplay, trained alongside teammate Tran for a team-combat bonus
  • Notable items: A collection of hundreds of summonable beanbag-toy "stuffed animal" figures, looted on Floor 3, several with undocumented rare variants; a refresher kit letting him reuse a given figure's summon tag twice more; an electronic stuffed-animal guidebook (Book 7) that identifies any plush from its label before it is used

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Bautista is a Tigran (tiger-headed) crawler and the sole survivor of his family after Grimaldi's lemurs killed them on Floor 3. He forms a debt/chat-contact bond with Carl after being rescued during Book 3's Iron Tangle evacuation, later joining Katia's splinter team at the end of Book 4.

docs.title: Role in the Story — Book 5
docs.text: Ranked #23 among crawlers by the time of the Butcher's Masquerade, Bautista fights with Katia's team through Floor 6, using his beanbag-toy summons — including an uncommon-variant beanie fitted with sunglasses and a fake tiara — to fake a convincing "clockwork Donut" that fools Lucia Mar during a saferoom teleport-trap ambush aimed at drawing her out. He confirms to Carl, somewhat nervously, that his relationship with Katia is real and public; Donut reacts with theatrical, delighted shock. He narrowly avoids having his head blown off by a hunter's pulse rifle during one of the floor's coordinated raids (Gwendolyn Duet, fighting nearby, isn't so lucky — a separate pulse-rifle hit punches a grapefruit-sized hole clean through her midsection, though she survives that one too), and helps hold off Eva Sigrid alongside Florin when Katia nearly breaks the peace seal confronting her at the Butcher's Masquerade.

docs.title: Role in the Story — Book 6
docs.text:
Bautista's Book 6 is his relationship with Katia coming apart over her addiction and her secrets, in four clear stages.

  1. He covers for her. When Katia goes dark for ten hours after finding a drug den in the Desperado Club, Bautista stonewalls Carl: "She's okay. She's asleep. She found some secret merchant in the Desperado Club, and she's out of sorts. But she'll be okay in a bit." Pressed: "Just leave it, okay? She'll be fine." Imani, whose husband is an addict, hears the same thing from him independently and names the pattern at once: "He didn't want to tell me any of this. The way he was making excuses for her… Let's just say it's familiar."
  2. The blow-up. Carl wants a barely-conscious Katia, carrying twelve debuffs, to get up and go anyway. Bautista pushes her back down — "Where do you think you're going?" — then turns on Carl: "You can do this later. We have time." Carl refuses. "'Fine. Kill yourself. But I won't stand by and watch,' Bautista said. He turned and stormed from the club."
  3. Louis says it out loud at the Christmas party, in the middle of the speech where he lists everything wrong with everyone: "Katia is struggling every day, and Bautista is having a nervous breakdown." Donut, separately, to Carl: "We're already losing Katia no matter what happens, and nobody is talking about it. Doesn't anybody see what it's doing to Bautista?"
  4. Where it stands at the end. Carl asks Katia about him in Chapter 63: "The tiger crawler walked near the back of the group along with Elle, who was scanning the sky for threats. It was clear their relationship had been damaged by recent events." Katia's only comment: "He doesn't want me to use the orchid." Carl, privately, agrees with him.

Elsewhere on the floor he is doing exactly what he always does: making the tea that Elle reckons is "the only thing keeping Imani together," spamming his stuffed-animal summons through the Ysalte fight, and finally getting some use out of his shape-changing ring, turning from tiger into "a large, four-armed creature." He is one of the four-man team that goes in on Sister Ines. Carl is also deliberately not telling him that Donut looted an oak bracelet off one of his dead family members.

docs.title: Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin
docs.text: Book 6 left Bautista and Katia's relationship damaged. Book 7 spends the whole floor letting Carl — and the reader — assume it is going to end badly, and then resolves it in the last two chapters with an act of quiet craftsmanship.

docs.title: The Floor
docs.text:
He fights all book as part of Katia's pair rather than as a commander in his own right. Carl's first close look at him is in the field hospital before the war starts: "Bautista remained in the back of the room, pacing back and forth, chewing on one of his finger claws. I wasn't too clear on the state of Bautista and Katia's relationship, but she'd asked for him to be here."

He and Katia are attached to whichever front needs a hammer. Florin has them "with what's left of the 105th" flanking Carl's position during the King Rust standoff, holding open a retreat corridor into Shanty Town. Later they are in Group Four with Carl, Li Na and the 107th White Dragons for the Club Vanquisher operation, and he is part of Carl's hand-picked teleport squad for the assault on the Madness castle — where he turns up "irritated he hadn't been summoned as part of the first group."

His job at Club Vanquisher is to walk into the temple of the Dagda and keep a suspicious cleric talking while Li Jun and Zhang string Li Na's capacitor wire behind his back, killing him only if necessary. He then holds the door out to Shanty Town so the aura stays live. He gets clear of the club before the boss fight seals, which is why his achievement box is only legendary while the others get celestial ones.

docs.title: The Eclipse Pyxies
docs.text:
His stuffed-animal collection finally gets a proper showcase. Katia's breach of Club Vanquisher is opened by a pair of his plushes:

From over both of Katia's shoulders flew a pair of ridiculously cute stuffed animals. They were stuffed versions of a demon mob called Eclipse Pyxies. They looked like fat, fur-covered guinea pigs, but with bat wings and jagged teeth. Bautista had a dozen of these things. The stuffed animals switched in midair from toys to actual monsters.

His legendary box from the raid is an electronic guidebook for the collection — scan a plush's label and an info box tells you what it does before you summon it. He also uses the toys as a mapping tool during the Reaver castle assault, throwing them into the randomly-shifting honeycomb corridors, tracking where they end up and calling the results to Katia while she redraws the map on the wall.

He is separately the one who identifies the Kimaris plush that Carl is carrying — "He's one of the brothers of Sheol. He has a summoning time of 'the remainder of the floor.' Be careful with him." That identification is what triggers Samantha's revelation about who Kimaris was to her; see Samantha.

docs.title: Katia
docs.text:
The tension runs under everything. Carl catches them arguing silently in Shanty Town with their eyes flashing, until Katia says out loud, "I said no," and "a look of rage flashed across Bautista before he lowered his head." Katia's explanation is not what Carl expects:

Katia: I'm good. It's okay. He's just scared for me. You need to remember what happened with his family after he came in here. He doesn't want anyone else he cares about to die. He thinks this is too risky and wants me to eat the flower now.

Katia: He's afraid that if this doesn't go well, you'll turn on me to get the flower to give to Donut.

Samantha, riding his shoulder, spends the whole floor coaching him toward a jealous rage: "You are a mighty Tigran, but you act like a lamb." Donut and Katia agree to keep their real plan from him because "he's going to be mad." Carl notices him "staring at us" every time Katia hugs him.

When the orchid ceremony finally happens, Bautista panics — "Wait, we are not prepared! I need... I thought..." — and then disappears from the tent entirely. Carl assumes the worst and messages him that he is running out of time. The reply:

Bautista: Sorry. I'm doing something in the crafting room quickly. I'm coming.

docs.title: What He Was Doing
docs.text:
The goddess Eileithyia makes Katia human again, and human means the body she actually has. Her right arm is gone to the shoulder, her left leg is gone, her right leg is gone to the knee, and she is missing an ear. "Just a few things I've lost along the way."

"Here, quick," Bautista said, quickly bringing the cybernetic parts to her. She'd made them herself, in anticipation of this. She'd left them in the crafting room, and Bautista had finished them for her. We all worked, clicking and fastening them into place just as Eileithyia, ignoring all this, placed her three-fingered hand on Katia's stomach.

Katia made the prosthetics. Bautista finished them — and had known for some time without being told. His exchange with her in front of the whole room, moments earlier:

"Oh, Daniel," Katia said, speaking for the first time. "I didn't think you knew."

"Oh course I knew," he said. "I love you. I'm sorry I made you doubt me."
