The last thing Katia does before she vanishes is raise the cybernetic arm and wave. Bautista's last words to Carl, on his way to the stairwell:

"I know you think I was going to do something horrible or jealous. I want you to know I almost did. I keep losing family, Carl. It makes me scared, and it makes me angry. And I know I am not considered human anymore, and that is my great shame, especially today. But I would never do anything to hurt a brother like you."

Sourced from Book 2: Carl's Doomsday Scenario, Book 3: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook, Book 4: The Gate of the Feral Gods, Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade, Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride, and Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Beatrice
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Role: Carl's ex-girlfriend; Princess Donut's original owner
  • Type: Human survivor, never a crawler — remained on Earth's surface, then in Syndicate custody
  • Status: Alive as of Book 5, confirmed for the first time since the Book 1 collapse
  • Notable items/relationships: Donut's owner on the pre-collapse Persian-cat show circuit (Bea's family raised and showed the cats); the poorly-drawn tattoo of Donut's grandmother, Princess Chonkalot, on her lower back; her ever-present Aries anklet

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
Before the collapse, Beatrice ("Bea") was Carl's girlfriend, living with him in Seattle. Days before the world was harvested into the dungeon, Carl learned she'd cheated on him with a man named Brad while on a Bahamas vacation, and their relationship had ended. Bea was traveling at the moment the dungeon opened, leaving Carl looking after her champion show cat, Donut — which is why Carl, not Bea, ended up inside the dungeon holding her.

Book 4's epilogue first revealed Bea survived the collapse on Earth's surface, living among a native human settlement with Brad for months, before being captured (unharmed) by an operative working for the talk-show host Odette — see Supporting Cast for that book's account.

docs.title: Book 5: Alive, and Cast Aside
docs.text:
Odette reveals to Carl and Donut, moments before a live broadcast, that Bea is not only alive but was being hunted by bounty hunters intending to illegally sell her to Borant so she could be forcibly transformed into a country boss — a fate Odette says she extracted Bea off-world to prevent, framing it as protecting her own investment in Carl and Donut — and to keep a rival production from using Bea's survival as a hostile ambush story. Bea appears on Odette's talk show as a surprise guest, broadcast in remotely from off-planet: thin, aged, drugged into a hollow, unresponsive state, and dressed for the broadcast in a revealing gown that exposes Donut's grandmother's tattoo on her back. She spots Carl first and rushes to hug him, her arms passing harmlessly through him since she isn't physically present in the room; she then reaches for Donut and passes through her the same way.

Donut, who has spent the whole series privately grieving Bea's presumed death, delivers a raw, unscripted rejection live on air — accusing Bea of planning to abandon her, of treating her as little more than a way to win more ribbons than Bea's own mother, and declaring that Carl is her person now, and always has been. Carl backs her up, coldly wishing Bea well and asking Odette to end the segment. The confrontation closes the loop on a plot thread the series has carried since Book 1 without offering Bea any further redemption or explanation.

The interview is filmed the same day Borant announces, in a real-time system message (not a broadcast), that the Valtay Corporation has acquired 51% ownership of the Borant Corporation — but Odette insists the Bea segment itself won't actually air until two recap episodes later. Odette does use Bea's rescue as leverage for a higher revenue-share contract with Borant — but that is a separate deal from the Valtay takeover itself, which Donut cryptically takes credit for moments later ("Viva la revolución, Carl"), tied to her own undisclosed dealings with Zev and the Borant Emancipation Front.

Sourced from Book 1: The Apocalypse Will Be Televised, Book 4: The Gate of the Feral Gods, and Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade.

docs.title: Brandon An
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Role: Leader of the "Meadow Lark" evacuee group (Book 1); maintenance worker at an eldercare facility before the collapse
  • Status: Killed in action, end of Floor 3 — dies holding a line against Shade Gremlins so the rest of his group can reach the stairwell in time
  • Notable weapon: A giant hammer
  • Family: Older brother of Chris Andrews

docs.title: Book 1: Leading Meadow Lark
docs.text: Brandon leads a group of eldercare-facility residents and staff (the "Meadow Lark" evacuees) that Carl and Donut encounter and help protect on Floors 1–2, wielding a giant hammer in their defense and making the hard calls to keep the mostly-elderly group moving toward each floor's exit. He and Carl form a real, if understated, bond over the course of the evacuation.

docs.title: Book 3: The Last Message
docs.text:
Brandon and his brother Chris have a falling-out on Floor 3, sparked by a disagreement over strategy — Chris wants to leave the stairwell area to hunt and reconnect with Carl and Donut, while Brandon insists on staying close to the exit and training safely. The argument escalates into Chris leaving the party with several other men, all of whom are later confirmed dead except Chris himself.

As Floor 3 collapses, Brandon and a resident named Henry hold the line against advancing Shade Gremlins so Imani, Elle McGibbons, and the rest of the group can reach the stairwell in time. Knowing he won't make it, Brandon sends a final message — to Carl, Imani, and Elle simultaneously — that only reaches Carl after a delay, arriving in a new "Messages from deceased Crawlers" folder just as Floor 4 opens:

"Look, man. I got into a fight with my brother Chris, and he left the party... I said something stupid, and he got mad. He left, and now it's too late to tell him I love him. I never said it. I'm about to die, and it's all I can think about... tell him I said I was sorry, and that he was right. He'll know about what... And tell him I love him. That's the most important part."

Carl never manages to pass the message along directly — Chris disappears from contact shortly after, resurfacing only through secondhand reports (see Chris Andrews).

Sourced from Book 1: The Apocalypse Will Be Televised and Book 3: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook.

docs.title: Britney Proskurina
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: Human Crawler
  • Class: Pit Fighter → Pit Champion (Book 5, Floor 6 specialization — upgrade details not fully described)
  • Level: Reaches the top-50 leaderboard independently by Book 5
  • Party: Katia's splinter team; Princess Posse officer and Team Retribution liaison (Book 7)
  • Notable spells/abilities: A powerful, thirty-second Shield spell blocking both magic and physical attacks (four-hour cooldown); berserking skills (Book 7)
  • Notable items: A jacket made entirely of stuffed slate butterfly figures (Book 5, sourced from Bautista's beanbag-toy collection) — capable of summoning a live slate butterfly that seeks out and extinguishes the nearest light source; enchanted underwear featuring a pin-up of Elle and the caption "Stay frosty, boys," which gives +10% dexterity and enhances all berserking skills (Book 7 — she has not told Elle about them)
  • Status: Alive at the end of Book 7; enters the Floor 10 stairwell "contemplating a deal," afraid, and expecting to be back

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Britney Proskurina, a Ukrainian former pit fighter, is one of two survivors of Floor 5's water quadrant original crawler team. She joins Firas's group by the end of Book 4, having refused to go back underwater ever again, and remains a quiet, perpetually irritated presence around the party for most of Book 5.

docs.title: Role in the Story — Book 5
docs.text:
Britney unexpectedly earns her own top-50 leaderboard spot by the Butcher's Masquerade, entitling her to attend independently rather than as anyone's plus-one; she attends anyway as Donut's guest and guitarist for the talent competition, revealing hidden musical skill Carl and Donut hadn't known about. During the masquerade, she uses one of her stuffed slate-butterfly summons to covertly short out a warning light monitoring the ballroom's guards — a small, high-stakes sabotage she describes afterward as leaving her "heart in her throat."

At the battle's climax, Carl shouts for Britney to trigger her entire jacket at once, sending the whole swarm of slate butterflies airborne to help swamp a near-dead Queen Imogen — but Imogen's own last, desperate lightning attack strikes the dense, light-seeking swarm by accident instead of its intended target, and the resulting explosion permanently, visibly burns Britney's face even after healing and kills her close friend Firas outright.

docs.title: Role in the Story — Book 6
docs.text: Britney enters Floor 8 at level 55, having risen significantly up the ranks, and in the worst state of anyone in the guild: the burn from the Butcher's Masquerade covers the left side of her face, and at the start of the floor she is "just sitting there, clutching onto Louis," unable to stop crying.

docs.title: The Extinction Sigil
docs.text: She arrives at the Desperado Club already wearing a new tattoo under her eye — an extinction sigil, awarded for wiping out an entire species. The book never says which species, or when she earned it. (Carl has one too, from a lizard race; the sigil grants a charm effect that removes the hostility of the extinct species' natural enemies, and can cut the other way — some creatures do extra damage to a sigil-bearer. See Game Mechanics.)

docs.title: Tserendolgor
docs.text:
The friendship that gets her through the floor is with Tserendolgor, who had a similar facial scar before the crawl. Donut is in the middle of clumsily consoling her — "scars are beautiful. It goes well with the whole barbarian aesthetic you're going for" — when Britney cuts her off:

"I'm not worried about it anymore," Britney said. "I have been talking to Tserendolgor, who once had a similar scar upon her face."

Carl physically restrains Donut from saying anything nasty about her.

docs.title: The Smile
docs.text:
Tserendolgor dies in Chapter 60, detonating herself rather than fight Donut for a key. Three chapters later, when the rescue party finally reaches Cuba, Carl catches this:

Tran, too, was smiling as he reached over and pet Donut. Britney was on the ground, on her back as Mongo snuffled against her. She was laughing as well. It was the first time I'd seen either of those two, Tran or Britney, so much as smile since the end of the Butcher's Masquerade.

Actually, come to think of it, it was the first I'd seen Britney smile. Ever.

The trigger is Mongo, not Ren — but Carl's next thought in the same passage is of Ren, "and of the hopelessness that had broken her," and of everyone forced to confront their own personal nightmares on this floor. His conclusion: "It was loneliness. It had always been loneliness… It was isolation that would break us."

She also dances with the stripper Author Steve Rowland at Louis's Christmas party, tells Louis to turn the music back on, and is one of the last crawlers holding the stairwell during the Ysalte fight.

docs.title: Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin
docs.text:
Britney spends Floor 9 in a job nobody assigned her and everybody comes to depend on: she becomes the Princess Posse's diplomatic channel to Juice Box and the NPC faction, Team Retribution. Carl's own summary:

I wasn't exactly sure when and how this happened, but Britney had pretty much become our main liaison with the NPCs.

And later, in the briefing for the four simultaneous offensives:

Britney will coordinate all of our communication with Team Retribution. It seems she's become quite close with Juice Box. She's gotten very good at being a go-between, working multiple lines of communication with the skill of a seasoned police dispatcher.

docs.title: The First Third
docs.text:
She is at Carl's shoulder for most of the opening act. She ties his hair back for him in the guild hall — "Keep it tucked in or monsters will grab it, believe me" — and the burn down the side of her face has finally stopped registering to him as a wound: "It fit her hard visage."

She is on the Party Planner unveiling, on the recruiting tour into Larracos, and in the room for the Donut Holes t-shirt argument, where she is both the person who warned Louis not to let Donut see it and the person he immediately sells out ("No, she has panties with a picture of Elle on them"). On the tour, while everyone else is gossiping about Louis's wedding, she is the one who asks the NPC Arief the question that matters — "Does your uncle remember dying?" — and who tells him flatly that "the 'outworlders' aren't immortal anymore."

At the Juice Box briefing she reads the paperwork while everyone else argues. She notices Juice Box has quietly withheld some of the documents, studies the fortification maps, and is the one who spots the item that ends up deciding the whole floor: "How big are these diggers?" She then stays behind at the Desperado Club to be taught the Larracos city defence system in person. At Louis and Juice Box's wedding she is physically present and completely checked out — "Britney clutched onto a pile of automaton plans and hadn't been paying attention."

docs.title: The War
docs.text:
Through the fighting she runs the Special Operations Forces in Shanty Town and works the changeling spy channel — the Naga infiltration goes Carl to Britney to Juice Box or Arief, because Carl cannot talk to the NPC operatives directly.

Carl: Britney. We're almost ready. Are your guys in place?

Britney: They're ready. Waiting on you.

During the four-front offensive she is effectively the theatre's radio: relaying dwarven confirmation that the lava tubes have been agitated, calling the abort when a digger is about to surface next to a god, reporting the Dream castle's shields down, and — when the war mages seize the Gate of the Feral Gods and Juice Box vanishes mid-battle — holding the line with nothing: "I don't know! Juice Box teleported away!"

When the Peeling Phase begins she is deep inside Larracos and has to run for her life. She resurfaces in a column of Team Retribution changelings led by a ten-foot armoured beetle, with the warlord cat Ferdinand poofed out and screaming on top of her head, still wearing his bowler hat. From then on she commands from the college with Jamal and the others, coordinates the raid on the castle of Larracos, calls the acid drain and the Bounce House catch, and afterwards stays behind with Florin and Rosetta to repair the top defensive ring. She is also in the room for Kiwi's labour, rubbing the bear's head with a wet cloth while Florin holds her hand.

docs.title: Eris's Claim
docs.text:
Near the end of the book the chaos goddess Eris, freshly unsponsored and free, freezes time, tells Carl several things she says are true, and finishes with one that isn't explained at all:

"Also, Britney picked that axe off the ground and is now possessed."

She disappeared with a crack.

Already married? I thought as I downed a healing potion. Axe? What axe? Possessed? By who?

Carl has Imani and Juice Box check her without telling her, and they find nothing.

Imani: Her health is 100%. I don't see any sign that there's anything wrong with her. She doesn't have an axe, Carl. Or if she does, it's in her inventory.

Juice Box: If she has a presence about her, it's deep. It's not anything I can feel. And believe me, I can feel most everything.

Juice Box cannot feel anything on Carl either, who is definitely carrying a presence, and suggests the goddess may simply have lied. Elle wants to just ask Britney; Carl refuses — "If it's a presence like mine, we don't want it to hurt her if it suspects we know it's there."

Unresolved

The book never confirms or disproves Eris's claim. No axe is ever found, no possession is ever demonstrated, Britney is never told, and the thread is not picked up again before the floor ends. The description box for Eris says she is All Knowing and that "If she gives you information, it's probably true" — while also noting she is able to lie. Nothing in Book 7 settles it either way.

docs.title: Exit
docs.text:
At the stairwell she does not commit either way:

Britney said she was contemplating a deal, but was afraid and would probably be back. She went in with Chris.

docs.title: Book 8: A Parade of Horribles
docs.text: Britney's Book 7 exit thread — "contemplating a deal, but afraid" — resolves into the book's clearest statement yet that whatever is or isn't riding inside her, she is now actively pursuing an agenda of her own.

docs.title: Killing Osvaldo
docs.text:
In Heat 7 of Floor 10, Britney jumps into the same heat as Osvaldo and kills him outright as he flees, stunned, toward a portal:

A champion has fallen. A bounty has been claimed.

Crawler Osvaldo has been killed by Crawler Britney Proskurina.

She lands directly on his corpse as the kill lands, earning a golden player-killer skull. What she takes from the body isn't the Apito crystal already in Prepotente's hands — it's Osvaldo's other, long-useless memorial crystal, tied to the dead goddess Ysalte:

"I saw her," I said, watching Britney, my paws up on the dash. "She has the memorial crystal from Ysalte now."

docs.title: The Vulgar Temple
docs.text:
Samantha immediately identifies what the crystal is for, and where Britney needs to take it:

"She needs to get to the Basilica or the Vulgar Temple and place the gem in the plinth, and she'll be back for good. I'll be curious to see if that actually works."

Carl's own gloss adds the stakes: "All I'm saying is Britney needs to get to either the Halls of the Ascendency or Sheol if she wants to get that crazy Ysalte bitch out of her" — which reads the goal as freeing/restoring Ysalte specifically, not merely charging the crystal. Britney disappears through a portal shortly afterward without confronting anyone about it; Elle's frustration afterward is the book's clearest statement that the party never actually addressed the Book 7 possession question before losing the chance to: "I said from the start we should've confronted Britney, and we never did, and now she's gone where we can't help her."

docs.title: Sheol
docs.text:
By the book's epilogue, Britney has reached Sheol itself — the Louis Santiago interlude finds her there already, armed with a pickaxe, alongside a Taurin named Pontiff and the demon Forkith. Whatever she's doing with the Ysalte crystal there is not shown on the page.

Still unconfirmed

Book 7 left open, via the goddess Eris's own unverified claim, whether Britney is possessed or influenced by Ysalte. Book 8 does not resolve this either way — it only confirms Britney is now pursuing Ysalte's revival on purpose, with a specific object and a specific destination. Whether that pursuit is her own will or something else's is not settled by anything in this book.

Sourced from Book 4: The Gate of the Feral Gods, Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade, Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride, Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin, and Book 8: A Parade of Horribles.

docs.title: Carl
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Crawler title (Book 1): Royal Bodyguard Carl
  • Type: Human Crawler (Book 1) → Primal Crawler (Book 2)
  • Race: Human (Book 1) → Primal (Book 2) — a blank-slate race (-1 to all base stats) that unlocks training skills past level 15 and exclusive Earth-based classes
  • Class: Not yet assigned (Book 1) → Compensated Anarchist (Book 2) — a Monk/Rogue hybrid Earth Class requiring level-5 Explosives Handling and 500 billion views
  • Subclass: Agent Provocateur (Book 5, Floor 6 specialization — chosen over Revolutionary and Guerilla) — grants +1 Intelligence per level, +1 to his Sapper's Table level, +2 to Dangerous Explosives Handling, and access to an Advanced Bomb Maker's Workshop
  • Level: 27 (end of Book 2) → 41 (end of Book 3) → 47 (end of Book 4) → 63 (end of Book 5) → 73 (end of Book 6) → 81 (Book 7, last level stated in the text) — entered Book 5 ranked #1 on the dungeon leaderboard, but ends it ranked #3 on the Floor 7 leaderboard; Donut claims the #1 spot for herself instead. He is still ranked #3 (behind Prepotente and Donut) at the start of Book 6, with a 2,000,000-gold bounty; no end-of-Floor-8 leaderboard rank is given. He is the #1-ranked crawler for all of Book 7, though Donut (135) and Li Na (87, with all base stats maxed at 300) both far outstrip him by the end of it
  • Party: The Royal Court of Princess Donut — Katia remains nominally attached but has been operating independently since Book 4; Book 5 ends with just Carl and Donut squadded together as the floor changes, plus a brief, ended-by-mutual-insult party of convenience with Prepotente. Party leader from Book 7 ch. 27 (highest combined base stats, taken from Donut) until she reclaims it in ch. 77
  • Faction Wars (Books 5–7): Co-Warlord of The Princess Posse with Donut; Mayor of Shanty Town from Book 7 ch. 10, traded out of Sir Ferdinand. The Princess Posse wins Faction Wars at the end of Book 7
  • Marriage (Book 7–8): Revealed in the Book 7 epilogue to be married, without explanation, to Donut's newly assigned attorney Princess Chandra, Esq. — Book 8 explains it: Chandra invoked Widow's Rights, a Naga custom letting a royal widow claim her husband's killer as a replacement husband. The marriage is legally contested and unresolved at the end of Book 8
  • Religion: Devotee of Emberus (Book 6–7) → publicly renounces his faith at the Floor 11 climax (Book 8), removing the Enchanted Pauper's Ring of the Steadfast Emberus and falsely confessing on the record to killing Emberus's son Geyrun himself (a lie, told to enrage the god; the real killer is still unknown) — bound, prior to that, by two standing church quests (find Geyrun's killer, tied to a stolen Memorial Crystal: Apito; kill the god Hellik before Floor 12); Book 5 added a daily blood tithe, a Shunned/Penitence status for accidentally killing a fellow worshipper, and an unhelpful "boon" system; Book 6 raised the tithe from 5% to 10% and added a 990,000-gold church debt that barred him from renouncing the religion while it was outstanding — a debt evidently overridden by the renunciation
  • Notable trait: Bare-knuckle fighter; per Mordecai, his unarmed strikes hit as hard as an unenchanted weapon by the end of Book 1; Book 5: crosses base Strength 100 and permanently doubles all future Strength level-up points via the Swole milestone upgrade
  • Notable spells/abilities: Pugilism, Unarmed Combat, Foot Soldier, Iron Punch, Powerful Strike, Smush, Fear (Compensated Anarchist), Bomb Surgeon, Trap Engineer, Hide in Shadows, Backfire, Escape Plan (grants access to the hidden Dungeon Locator), Talon Strike (Book 3, necklace-granted), Bang Bro (Book 3), Wisp Armor (read/cast for the first time in Book 2), Ping (Book 4, tome), Tripper (Book 5, sets off every trap he's placed in range at once), the item-granted Protective Shell, and Self-Immolation (Book 6, granted at Devotee rank — a once-a-day sphere of Sheol fire centred on himself), plus the Book 6 patch skills Soul Reaper / The Daughter's Kiss; Book 7 adds Walk on Air (taken permanently from Li Jun at the end of Book 6, noticed only in Book 7), Gloom Wraith Phase (level 13, celestial-box potion), Profane Iron (a once-a-day chain skill borrowed from Li Na via a toraline-ink tattoo inked by Katia), Heathen Scald (level 15, an Emberus Celestial Boon), Pied Piper (level 15, a Harpocrates proximity effect made permanent by an Eris coin flip), the thirty-hour Speedster benefit (hairbrush-granted, not permanent), and Mind Balance — toe-ring-granted at level 5 and trained to level 16, the first skill in the series pushed past 15 by battlefield conditions rather than potions; Book 8 adds Oozy Form, a slime/ooze travel and infiltration spell that becomes indefinite-duration at level 15
  • Notable items: Arrow of Enthusiastic Double Gonorrhea (Book 5, looted, later used as a weapon against Vrah); Carl's Doomsday Scenario; Drakea's Enchanted Kerchief of Disorder; The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook; Enchanted Anarchist's Battle Rattle (Book 5: gains an arrow patch, a bomb patch, and an anti-vampirism "Midnight Epicure" patch); Enchanted Auto Buckler of the Peach Pit; Enchanted BigBoi Boxers; Enchanted Hairbrush of the Beefmaster (Book 7, celestial — four thirty-hour benefits including Speedster, and it screams); Enchanted Necklace of the Haute Bourgeoisie; ~~Enchanted Night Wyrm's Ring of Divine Suffering~~ (Book 5: finally worn in earnest, upgraded to 5 stat points per kill; destroyed in Book 7 — Carl fed it to Donut, who swallowed it); Enchanted Nightgaunt Cloak of Stoutness; Enchanted Pauper's Ring of the Steadfast Emberus (Book 6, bought on a 990,000-gold church loan); an Enchanted Prison Tattoo Kit; Enchanted Toe Ring of the Well-Balanced (Book 7, source of Mind Balance, Heart Balance and Physical Balance); Enchanted Trollskin Shirt of Pummeling; Enchanted War Gauntlet of the Exalted Grull; The Eye of the Bedlam Bride (Book 6, a chest tattoo inked into him by Shi Maria while she was controlling his body); The Filthy Little Crawler's Book of Voodoo; The Gate of the Feral Gods; Goblin Pass and Desperado Pass tattoos; a Reaper Spider Minion upgrade patch granting access to the Midnight Market (Book 7); Rockard's Ring of Sniping; The Scavenger's Daughter (Book 6, a divine back patch for the Battle Rattle — doubles all patch stat bonuses and adds the Soul Essence bar and the one-shot Mysterious Bone Key); Stayfast Ink and an Adept's fountain pen (Book 7, gifts from Milk); Velma, Tserendolgor's flamethrower; a Wand of Nighty-Night; a Xistera
  • Pet (Book 7): Rend, the meatball inherited from Tserendolgor at the end of Book 6
  • New tattoos (Book 8): Mark of the Damned — permanent, raised scar-tattoos on the backs of both hands, replacing the sun-shaped Emberus marks the instant he renounces the god. The system gives the tattoos a name and nothing else: no stated mechanical effect is given anywhere in Book 8

docs.title: Background
docs.text: Carl enters the dungeon in the same clothes he was standing in when the Earth was harvested — including a pair of ill-fitting Crocs, which he's self-conscious about ("painfully aware that I was wearing Crocs that didn't fit"). He's accompanied by his ex-girlfriend's cat, Princess Donut, whom he's holding when the apocalypse hits.

docs.title: Class Situation
docs.text:
Unlike most crawlers, Carl does not get a class assigned right away. His character sheet reads:

Class: Not yet assigned.

This persists across multiple checks early in Book 1, which becomes a running point of tension — other crawlers and NPCs comment on it, and Carl compensates by leaning entirely on unarmed combat. Mordecai notes that Carl's bare-hand attack has scaled to the point that it's "just as good right now as any unenchanted weapon."

docs.title: Relationship with Princess Donut
docs.text:
Carl and Donut form a party very early on — The Royal Court of Princess Donut — with titles assigned by Donut herself:

  • Donut: Grand Champion Best in Dungeon
  • Carl: Royal Bodyguard

Donut is characterized as vain and status-obsessed (insisting on her full title, "GC, BWR, NW Princess Donut the Queen Anne Chonk"), while Carl treats her partly as a responsibility he didn't ask for and partly as his only real connection to his old life. Their dynamic — bickering, protective, occasionally very funny — is a throughline of the early books.

docs.title: Background (continued)
docs.text: Before the collapse, Carl was 27. After a stint in the US Coast Guard as an MK (machinery technician) aboard a cutter, he'd left the service and was working as a civilian marine tech, fixing electrical systems on rich people's party boats. He lived with his girlfriend Beatrice ("Bea") in Seattle; they'd broken up days earlier after he learned she'd cheated on him in the Bahamas, and he was looking after her show cat, Donut, when the apocalypse hit. His Coast Guard background explains his above-average hand-to-hand combat training and why his starting skill sheet already listed Unarmed Combat: 3 alongside firearms proficiencies he can't use (he entered with no weapons).

docs.title: Signature Fighting Style
docs.text: Carl never picks up a real weapon for long. His build centers on bare-knuckle combat, reinforced by a stack of unarmed-combat skills (see Quick Facts above for the full list). By the end of Book 1 these skills, combined with gear like the War Gauntlet, make his fists hit as hard as an enchanted weapon.

docs.title: Personal Rules
docs.text: Carl adopts "You will not break me" as a private mantra after being forced to kill goblin infants in a boss room (Book 1's darkest moment). He also insists — even when it costs time and safety — on destroying corpses left behind on the second floor once he learns corpses spawn endless waves of Brindle Grubs, and on trying to protect Meadow Lark's group of elderly evacuees even though it's tactically costly.

docs.title: Notable Book 1 Achievements/Reputation
docs.text:
• Credited inventor of Carl's Jug O' Boom, a moonshine-and-goblin-oil incendiary that earns him a permanent (if heavily taxed) gold-per-kill royalty in the Accounts tab (see item page)
  • Becomes the subject of a viral, non-consensual "snick" (fan-made deepfake video) mocking Prince Maestro of the Skull Empire after publicly challenging him to single combat — nicknames the prince "Pork Boy" / "Carl's Naughty Little Piggie," an insult that goes intergalactically viral
  • Ends Book 1 about to descend to Floor 3, where he and Donut will choose a race and class for the first time

docs.title: Timeline Notes (Book 1)
docs.text:
• Enters the dungeon holding Donut at the moment of the announcement (see Level 1)
  • Forms the Royal Court of Princess Donut party
  • Fights a floor-one neighborhood boss before progressing to the stairs down
  • Reaches the second floor, at which point his and Donut's stats become visible to live viewers
  • Helps evacuate a group of elderly crawlers ("Team Meadow Lark") down to Floor 3, losing nurse Yolanda Martinez to a Rage Elemental in the process
  • Tricks and kills a level-93 Rage Elemental by luring it into a collapsing stairwell (denies XP, but saves the group)
  • Ends the book about to pick a race/class on Floor 3

docs.title: Book 2: Race, Class, and the Manager Scheme
docs.text:
On Floor 3, Carl picks Primal as his race — a species so rare and mysterious even Mordecai doesn't fully understand it; legend holds Primals were the first civilization to conquer the galaxy before vanishing entirely. He picks it specifically because it's the only race/human option that unlocks training skills past their normal level-15 cap, at the cost of starting five effective levels behind (-1 to all stats, missing the +10 human bonus).

For class, he takes Compensated Anarchist — an explosives/trap/social-media hybrid class described in-game as "the Agent Provocateur" — over the AI-recommended Bomb Squad Tech and Prizefighter, largely because it comes with the hidden Escape Plan skill, which unlocks access to a secret Dungeon Locator system Donut's own build had flagged as available.

Per Odette's advance coaching, Carl and Donut deliberately engineer Mordecai into choosing the hidden Manager benefit (tied to Donut's Former Child Actor class) by making it look like an accident — Donut "misclicks" her floor specialty in a way that locks it in. Carl goes along with the deception despite real guilt about it, since a manager who can personally accompany the party (rather than being confined to a guildhall) is too valuable to pass up. Mordecai remains furious about it through most of Book 2 without learning it was deliberate.

docs.title: Book 2 Notable Events
docs.text:
• Reaches Floor 3 (the "Over City," an urban level type recurring every 3 floors) and helps Donut/Mordecai through race and class selection
  • Gets drawn into a quest involving Tsarina Signet, an Elite who kidnaps and magically comas Donut to force Carl into fighting her rivals — defeats the circus boss Heather the Bear, breaking her free of mind-control in the process, then talks down the possessed Ringmaster Grimaldi and negotiates a truce between him and Signet rather than killing either
  • His Enchanted BigBoi Boxers are upgraded via a Scroll of Upgrade, becoming his most valuable item; also receives a Xistera from a fan box, replacing his slingshot as his primary ranged weapon
  • Takes on a second quest, "The Sex Workers Who Fell from the Heavens," after NPC GumGum asks for help investigating serial krasue killings — the trail leads through the cult-like 201st Security Group, briefly makes Carl the town's "Magistrate" after killing a decoy, and ends with the death of the settlement's true ruler, Miss Quill
  • While cornering Miss Quill's undead husband Remex, an overloaded soul crystal forces Carl to contain a catastrophic magical explosion, creating Carl's Doomsday Scenario — an item he can never safely remove from his inventory — and permanently welcomes new party member Katia into the group in the process
  • Appears on the talk show Danger Zone with Ripper Wonton alongside Hekla; publicly criticizes the Skull Empire's King Rust, prompting Crown Prince Stalwart to order a botched assassination attempt that instead kills the singer Manasa and escalates into a Valtay/Skull Empire crisis
  • The Doomsday Scenario event triggers a Syndicate legal fight over withheld Celestial loot boxes — Carl, Donut, and Katia are denied the reward they earned on a technicality, while an uninvolved bystander gets one instead
  • Ends Floor 3 ranked 6th on the leaderboard (Level 27), just above Donut
  • Mordecai's indentureship requirement is fulfilled the moment the party reaches Floor 4 — after this, he's free to leave crawler service, though he chooses to stay on as manager

docs.title: Book 3: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook
docs.text: Carl's Floor 3 "joke" prize from a fan-vote prize carousel turns out to be the single most valuable item he's ever received: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook, a living, editable record of survival knowledge left behind by 24 prior crawlers to have owned it. Carl becomes its 25th author, using it (and a hidden mental "scratchpad" feature that lets him add notes without physically opening the book) as his primary source of dungeon knowledge for the entire floor — including power-supply mechanics, portal theory, deity-summoning rules, and crafting recipes he passes off to Mordecai as his own deductions.

docs.title: The Iron Tangle Collapses
docs.text:
Floor 4 is an underground subway-and-trainyard superstructure called the Iron Tangle, run by gnoll/hobgoblin NPC staff and infested by a "Krakaren" ghoul-generator system. When a group of crawlers destroys a soul crystal at a ghoul generator, it triggers a cascading, franchise-wide system failure: the Krakaren (a real, license-parodied alien "Apothecary" species per Mordecai) floods the Tangle with monsters, hundreds of thousands of crawlers are stranded across the railway, and the level's collapse timer accelerates. Carl becomes the de facto architect of the floor-wide rescue effort:

  • Reverse-engineers hobgoblin interdiction carts (rail vehicles with built-in, dial-a-destination portal "scoops" meant for clearing wrecks) into weapons and rescue vehicles, using them to teleport entire crowds of stranded crawlers directly to safety and to funnel Krakaren monster waves into the abyss
  • Farms severed hands from an indestructible, self-resurrecting gnoll bartender NPC named Growler Gary — 14 hands total — to bypass a two-person security lock on the carts — a plan he narrates with open self-disgust. The first several hands are taken while Gary is frightened and resisting; Carl stops partway through to explain the full reasoning, after which Gary gives resigned consent to the remaining ten
  • Builds and detonates a hobgoblin-dynamite train bomb by sending the salvaged Vermillion engine backward down a monster-choked line, timed to a hob-lobber trigger pole — his explosives handling skill hits 11 and he levels to 35 off the resulting kill credit
  • Rigs a rapid-response cart into a suspended, upside-down portal directly over a stairwell station's collapsing floor — correctly guessing, with Katia, that the Iron Tangle's track layout mirrors a hidden, upside-down duplicate level connected by a "noodle" of interior escape tunnels — plugging the hole the Krakaren pour through and saving the entire station

docs.title: The Ring of Divine Suffering
docs.text: Carl inherits the Enchanted Night Wyrm's Ring of Divine Suffering from Frank Q's corpse and wears it briefly for its passive +5% stat bonus. Mordecai reacts with genuine alarm bordering on violence — smacking Carl for the first time since his own father used to — explaining that faction-war armies on Floor 9 always include a Divine Suffering ring-bearer, that the item exists specifically to lure crawlers into becoming farmable power sources for the factions, and that its owner becomes an immediate, universally-known target the moment word gets out. Carl removes the ring and agrees to sell it before Floor 6, though he keeps it in inventory for now.

docs.title: The Grull Gambit and the Death Challenge
docs.text: Cornered by the floor's city-boss mimic while trying to clear a path for stranded ally Bautista, Carl exploits his War Gauntlet's involuntary-summon mechanic on purpose for the first time: he beats a captured mantaur neighborhood boss into "vessel" status, drops the transforming body through a portal to summon the war god Grull — unknowingly piloted, live, by the supposedly-dead Prince Maestro as a sponsored guest deity — directly in front of the mimic. The confrontation is broadcast as a full Death Challenge gambling event (50-to-1 odds against Carl's survival). Carl survives by hiding, decoying Grull with a Katia-disguised body double, and re-summoning a second captured mantaur at the last second to yank Grull (and Maestro) out of the arena and into the abyss — winning without landing a single hit on either monster. He ends the floor at Level 41, having also helped orchestrate the deaths of Hekla (indirectly, via Katia) and dozens of soul-crystal ghoul generators floor-wide.

docs.title: Other Book 3 Notes
docs.text:
• Formally welcomes Katia as a full, permanent party member (already informally the case since Book 2) and gives her his own Enchanted Auto Buckler of the Peach Pit after she outgrows it via a fan-box shield upgrade
  • Publicly and repeatedly needles the resurrected Maestro on-air, continuing the "Carl's Naughty Little Piggie" humiliation arc from Book 1 with a new viral "snick"
  • Loses his usual PR contact Zev to an unexplained "reeducation retreat" back home just before the floor ends, replaced by a colder, more adversarial admin named Loita
  • Ends the floor with a written vow, appended to the Cookbook: to start actively working to free — not just kill — the dungeon's enslaved NPCs, a marked escalation from his Book 1 "You will not break me" survival mantra

docs.title: Book 4: The Gate of the Feral Gods
docs.text: Floor 5 traps roughly 1,172 crawlers each inside a self-contained "bubble" world with four quadrants (Land/Sea/Air/Subterranean), each hiding a castle that must fall before the bubble's stairwell unlocks. Carl and Donut's bubble is a desert bowl ruled by a dromedarian/changeling refugee town (Hump Town) under siege by an airborne dirigible-gnome dreadnaught, the Wasteland.

docs.title: The Air Quadrant and the Fall of the Wasteland
docs.text: Carl builds increasingly refined guided rockets (with Mordecai's help) to fight the floor's aerial threats, killing the borough boss Ruckus (a cyborg chicken hawk) for its buzzsaw weapon, then engineers an elaborate hostage-swap con — disguising Katia as a corpse, a chair, and a resurrected zombie gnome simultaneously — to hijack a gnomish ambassador's balloon mid-negotiation and detonate the Wasteland from the inside with smuggled missiles, saving Hump Town from bombardment ("Squeeze out the Juice Box" quest). The strike enrages the System AI for reasons Carl doesn't understand at first (it wanted him to personally stomp a frenzied gerbil, per its long-running fixation from Floor 2's Ralph fight) and nearly triggers a punitive "acceleration" before Carl relents and kills one by hand. He and Donut go on to finish the air quadrant by defeating the indestructible Denise the Feral Goose Mother in a no-magic, no-physical-damage boss fight (solved by shoving her head into a garbage disposal), rescuing the orphaned NPC child Bonnie in the process.

docs.title: Chris, Maggie, and the Infiltrator
docs.text: Carl encounters a changed Chris Andrews, who turns out to be puppeted by Maggie My — revealed to have taken an Infiltrator (Scree) race, a full-body brain parasite that locks its host out of their own actions entirely. Unable to save Chris without killing him, Carl has Donut portal him into a sealed, flooding chamber rather than let him be executed on the spot. At the very end of the floor, using a Mordecai-brewed Phase Lava Rock potion, Carl reaches directly into Chris's skull mid-battle to extract the worm; it burrows into Carl's own arm before Mordecai's double-healing potion forces it out through his neck, and Mongo finishes it off. Chris is freed and joins the party for the trip down to Floor 6, in Brandon An's memory.

docs.title: Killing Administrator Loita
docs.text: After Donut's merchandising deal repeatedly humiliates her, and PR admin Loita threatens to have Mongo fed to a mob if Donut talks back again, Carl engineers Loita's death disguised as an accident: rigging a defective RealPet-toy's tamper-proof self-destruct panel to fail at the exact moment Loita stands up from a couch, using residue from an infused "Hobgoblin Disco Ball" smoke bomb (learned from the Cookbook) to corrode the panel's seal. A Syndicate liaison, Orren, interrogates Carl and Donut afterward but cannot prove intent and is overruled by an unnamed kua-tin faction that intervenes on Carl's behalf — Carl learns fifteen admins have already died to crawlers this season, all with known methods, making his the season's only unsolved case.

docs.title: The Gate of the Feral Gods
docs.text: Carl assembles all three pieces of a celestial-tier artifact — two enchanted pocket watches and a winding box, together called the Gate of the Feral Gods — capable of opening a one-way portal to any dialed coordinate, at the cost of also opening a temporary two-way gate to "the Nothing" that releases an imprisoned feral god. He uses it twice: first, repeatedly, to evacuate roughly 2,300 stranded crawlers out of sealed, doomed bubbles (intentionally unleashing a feral god into each abandoned bubble as the price); second, to send a gnomish/changeling ally, Juice Box, safely through to Floor 6's city of Larracos while flooding its ninth-floor faction-war marketplace with sharks, explosives, and seawater instead of a god — deliberately crippling the resupply capability of seven factions who'd sued to stop him. He keeps the artifact rather than destroying it, over Mordecai's objections.

docs.title: Becoming a God's Acolyte
docs.text: Cornered mid-air-battle by the rival crawler Quan Ch — who is trying to kill an innocent, Celestial-tier puppy named Orthrus for a bounty — Carl throws a sponsor-gifted celestial grenade without realizing he has no deity to summon, is prompted to pick one, and accidentally becomes a worshipper of Emberus, the fire god whose lost pet the puppy turns out to be. The resulting Divine Intervention buff saves him and Donut from the ensuing god-fight; afterward he rips Quan Ch's arm off in a separate confrontation and loots two enchanted rings from it. He ends the book publicly declaring his intent to hunt down every bounty hunter sent after him on Floor 6, having just become the dungeon's #1-ranked crawler.

docs.title: Other Book 4 Notes
docs.text:
• Gains a mysterious, extravagantly well-funded second sponsor, The Open Intellect Pacifist Action Network, Intergalactic NFC, who sends a custom-made xistera attachment (head-throwing extension) just in time to save Carl, Donut, and hired NPC Samantha from a rampaging demon — the epilogue reveals the sponsor is run by a "Dr. P. Hu," almost certainly Cookbook author Porthus
  • Loses Katia as a day-to-day party member (though not formally out of the group) at the floor's end — she splits off to protect Eva Sigrid's scattered former "daughters" before Eva can pick them off one by one
  • Ends the book with Chris Andrews as a new party member and Katia operating independently

docs.title: Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade
docs.text: Floor 6, the Hunting Grounds, is a jungle Over-City variant where sponsored bounty hunters are released to hunt the top crawlers by name — 360 were registered as of the pre-release broadcast, with the announcement itself warning that number was expected to double or triple by the actual release. Carl treats it as the war he promised at the end of Book 4.

docs.title: The River
docs.text: Book 5 introduces a recurring internal motif: Carl repeatedly hears/feels "a river" or a running tap at the back of his mind, growing louder under stress and only quieted by rest or violence. It is tied, obliquely, to a childhood memory of hearing running water, going down to the basement, and finding a note shortly before his mother arrived — the text never states outright what happened to her, but the implication (and Carl's private mantra shift to "I will break you all") suggests her suicide is the source of both his numbness around death and his growing willingness to escalate.

docs.title: Opening the Hunt
docs.text:
Forced to surrender the Gate of the Feral Gods as collateral (returnable on reaching Floor 9) in a negotiation with Syndicate liaison Orren, Carl gains an attorney, the Nullian lawyer Quasar, and four mercenary "cretin" bodyguards (Bomo, the Sledge, Clay-ton, Very Sullen). Before the hunt officially opens, he teleports solo into Zockau with Donut via Bomo's Teleport to Stairwell spell and runs a "Predator"-style invisibility raid — barrel bombs packed with gunpowder and hobgoblin dynamite planted by hand along the club district's alleyways, plus a volley of rocket missiles — that kills roughly 35 hunters (earning a separate "Mass Casualty Event" achievement for over 250 additional non-hunter NPC casualties from the blast), including hive matriarch Circe Took's mantis daughter Xindy (Vrah's sister, finished off by missile fire).

The raid nearly gets him killed by crossbow fire and is what first draws Vrah — Circe's remaining daughter and heir — into a personal vendetta. Carl then builds a second, far larger thermobaric bomb — nicknamed by the system Just Wait Until Your Daddy Gets Home — and he and Donut plan to use her Clockwork Triplicate spell to send a copy of Bomo out to wheel it back into Zockau's streets for a second strike, but they scrap that plan after finding a taunting note from Vrah warning him off further explosives. The bomb itself doesn't see use until much later, when Carl kicks it out a saferoom door to blow apart the hunters and mantises chasing him and Donut out of Alucarda, a village that Lucia Mar had separately seized and slaughtered earlier in the floor.

docs.title: Conquering Towns, Killing Hunters
docs.text: Carl and Donut spend the floor taking over a string of small Ursine settlements (Point Mongo, Ferdinand Peak, Nipton) as forward bases, training the local guards to fight off hunters with missile launchers, and running coordinated raids with Katia's splinter team using seeker-spider automatons, siege weaponry, and Carl's expanding trap network. He personally kills or marks dozens of hunters using the newly-worn Ring of Divine Suffering. By the Butcher's Masquerade prize counter, he's collected roughly 66 trophy hands — 34 short of the 100 needed for the counter's priciest item, a Memorial Crystal: Apito (Queen Imogen's own necklace, offered as the party's prize). Nobody affords it at the counter, so it reverts to Imogen — but when she dies in the floor's final battle, a ranger crawler named Osvaldo (his race, Curupira, is drawn from Brazilian folklore) loots it straight off her corpse, immediately triggering an update to Prepotente's own "Find Out Who Killed My Son" quest and setting the two of them up for a dispute over it. Separately, at the 50-hand tier, he's one hand short of buying both a skill upgrade and a case of potions in the same trip and has to choose.

docs.title: Vrah, the Arrow, and Diwata
docs.text: After Vrah nearly kills him in single combat, Carl improvises a weapon out of a looted Arrow of Enthusiastic Double Gonorrhea, jamming it into her neck moments before she can flee — deliberately choosing infection over an outright kill to keep her out of the fight without killing a would-be hive queen outright. The gambit backfires spectacularly: Circe Took turns out to have sponsored the shapeshifting fertility deity Diwata into the realm to cure her daughter — Diwata first manifests through a sacrificed hunter used, unknowingly, as a birthing vessel, then shapeshifts into a male mantis to personally cure Vrah by mating with her before turning female and birthing an endless wave of mantis nymphs into the Hunting Grounds. Carl marks Vrah for real during the climactic battle at the Butcher's Masquerade; Mongo and Kiwi — a raptor pack leader Mongo mated with earlier on the floor, later revealed to be a cursed, transformed Ursine woman — tear off her limbs together before Carl sends Kiwi back to the stage and has Mongo finish her off.

docs.title: The Miriam Dom Mercy Kill
docs.text: Summoned by an endangered Miriam Dom, Carl secretly marks her with his own Ring of Divine Suffering and lets her burn to death in the sunrise rather than intervene — the only way to cure the floor-wide vampirism curse she'd unknowingly spread and to free her paralyzed adoptive son, Prepotente, from a magical stalemate. Only Donut is told the details firsthand, though a floor-wide world-quest announcement publicly flags the suspicious timing of Carl's resulting stat boost to everyone else on the floor. He also quietly pockets a couple of Miriam's abandoned potion scrolls for himself before honoring the rest of his promise to hand her remaining stockpile over to Prepotente.

docs.title: The Butcher's Masquerade
docs.text: Invited to Queen Imogen's mandatory top-50 party inside the High Elf castle, Carl helps engineer a multi-front plan — smuggling disguised changelings through a secret underground tunnel to seize the castle's four sentinel towers on foot, charming Queen Imogen's cat familiar Ferdinand through Donut, and infiltrating the security control room via Samantha — that has to be reworked on the fly the moment the party turns out to be sealed under an unbreakable, Apito-enforced peace ward that traps everyone inside, including Imogen herself, until someone breaks it. When the plan falls apart, Carl privately resolves to kill fellow crawler Eva Sigrid and break the seal himself as a last resort, sparing his friends the choice — before Tsarina Signet volunteers to sacrifice herself instead, casting a one-person Ink Marauder spell that shatters the peace seal and triggers the floor's final, catastrophic battle. In the ensuing "Cage Fight Extreme" boss battle against Queen Imogen and Diwata simultaneously, Carl leads the assault on Diwata, using Donut's Laundry Day spell (boosted past level 15 with a Pawna's Tears potion) to strip away Diwata's divine "armor" — which, since Diwata is inhabiting Circe Took's own mantis body as her vessel, exposes the ordinary, mortal Circe Took underneath, stripped of her god-tier protection and immediately torn apart by her own mantis children. Separately, the Sledge — trapped inside the castle with the gnome Bonnie and two rescued ursine cubs as everything collapses — casts the long-planned Zerzura spell at the last possible second, teleporting the entire castle (and everyone still inside it, including Ferdinand) straight down to the ninth floor.

docs.title: Losses
docs.text: The final battle kills Signet, Gwendolyn Duet, Firas, Horton the mushroom bard, and roughly thirty crawlers who'd stayed behind to help sow chaos outside the castle, among many others. Carl privately tells a shell-shocked Donut, holding her as she realizes she isn't grieving properly, that she's wearing an emotional "mask" that will protect her until it's safe to take it off — a rare moment of him comforting her rather than the reverse.

docs.title: Faction Wars and the Ending
docs.text: In the wreckage after the battle, Carl and Katia dig two unconscious baby nodlings out of a pile of corpses and gore, and Carl and Donut discover that the "Ineligible" ruling protecting pregnant/child crawlers has been quietly used to smuggle the Popov brothers to safety as newborn nodling yearlings. At the floor's close, Carl publicly reveals that the Princess Posse — the crowd-funded fan organization Donut had been building since Book 4 — has bought a Floor 9 Faction Wars seat, making the pair Co-Warlords, and uses the broadcast to publicly pressure the other eight factions into voting to remove Faction Wars' sponsor-safety protections. He also learns, via a surprise, staged reunion on Odette's show, that Beatrice — his ex and Donut's original owner — survived the Earth's collapse and was secretly rescued by Odette; both he and Donut coldly reject her on-air. Floor 7's entire maze is then instantly destroyed by Prepotente before Carl and Donut so much as see it properly, and the two of them are already choosing their Floor 8 starting location (a globe-spinning mishap lands them in the Caribbean instead of the Bahamas Carl wanted) when the book closes on a rare private point-of-view scene revealing that Katia has separately hunted down and killed Eva Sigrid — and that the reforming Crown of the Sepsis Whore has passed from Eva's dying grip onto Katia's own head, a secret Carl and Donut do not learn before the book ends.

docs.title: Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride
docs.text: Floor 8, "The Ghosts of Earth," is the floor where Carl's entire past is put on public record and then rebuilt into a boss monster and pointed at him. He enters it ranked #3 with a 2,000,000-gold bounty, at level 64/65, and leaves it at level 73 with another consciousness living in his chest.

docs.title: The Shadow Boxer Interview
docs.text:
Zev books Carl and Donut onto Shadow Boxer, an interview show about crawlers' pre-crawl lives, hosted by the former crawler Rosetta Thagra. Her opening line to him is "So, comrade. Let's talk about your dead mother."

What comes out — most of it for the first time, in front of the entire galaxy and in front of Donut:

  • On Carl's fifteenth birthday, his mother poisoned his father, left him for dead, went down to the basement and hanged herself from the pipes. Carl found her. His father survived, barely injured. She left a note; it was a letter to Carl, and its contents have never been made public.
  • A few months later his father walked out and never came back. Carl lived alone in the house, eating whatever was left, until the power went out and someone noticed. He spent a night in an interrogation room being asked whether he'd killed his father, took his first cigarette from the detective, and — he admits to himself — wanted to be suspected: "I was here, goddamnit. I was real." Then his father turned up alive and drunk in Wisconsin and the interest evaporated. "I was just another sad, abandoned kid. A victim. I was not their problem. I was nothing."
  • Two years at the Anacortes Boys' Ranch, a high school equivalency certificate, a month on a couch in Seattle, and a recruitment centre where the Coast Guard desk was the only one manned over lunch.

Donut had been told, for years, only that his mother "left." Her reaction is one of her best moments in the book: she gets on his lap, asks one question, decides not to push, and leans her head against his. Carl's closing line on it: "It's in the past. I don't want to be defined by things I have no control over."

The interview is also a delivery mechanism. Rosetta plants a coded "milk and potatoes" message pointing Carl at Crawler Milk's 6th-edition cookbook notes on magic ink, and the Valtay liaison Harbinger cuts the broadcast mid-word, recalls Carl's attorney, bans Rosetta from all future crawler interviews, and tells Carl to his face: "I am actively working to have both you and the caprid disposed, and I will eventually succeed."

docs.title: The Father, and Asher
docs.text:
Floor 8 replays the crawlers' own memories. Carl's takes him into his father's trailer in Iowa to watch a man he hadn't seen in over twelve years die of liver failure, 140 pounds and yellow, with a Mariners game on. He finds a small boy in the hallway.

His half-brother Asher, about six, son of his father and his stepmother Tami-Lynn. Carl never knew he existed. Beatrice did — Tami-Lynn had written asking for help, and Beatrice buried the message, a fact Donut reveals by accident two chapters later. It is the first time Carl has ever actually been angry at Beatrice.

Carl talks at his unhearing father for a while — "You're broken, you're alone, and you're a nobody. My only regret is that you lived long enough to inflict yourself onto my poor brother" — and leaves before the end, because "You don't deserve for anybody to watch you die." Tami-Lynn kills the man with a lethal dose of morphine she'd been hiding in the flowerpot outside, after sending Asher to a neighbour's house.

Carl's father is never named

Donut asks directly: "What was your dad's name, anyway? I don't think you ever said." Carl: "It doesn't matter. He doesn't deserve to have one. Not anymore. It's done." No name for him appears anywhere in the text.

Tami-Lynn's motive is implied, not stated

The book shows the morphine and shows her protecting Asher from the scene; Carl says outright that he doesn't know what her plan was. Her later line as a hydra head — "I wrote you, and you never answered! I needed help. Look what you made me do!" — is the strongest evidence, but the text never states the motive directly.

Among the things Carl loots out of the trailer before setting the curtains on fire: his father's Glock, his motorcycle keys, three packs of Marlboro Reds, court documents, and an arcade cabinet. "It wasn't Frogger, but Centipede."

docs.title: The Reminiscence Hydra of Malicious Compliance
docs.text:
The burning trailer produces the floor's boss: a stitched flesh-ball with nine screaming heads, each one the face of somebody Carl knew, all of them dead in the collapse. Asher, Tami-Lynn, Monobrow Sam, Bea's mother, Donut's cousin Sugar Cube, Carl's boss Dick, his landlord Mr. Roth, Sally from billing, and the cat-show judge Judge Lucian as the deckmaster. The AI admits on air that it swapped the boss at the last minute — the original was going to be Carl's father — and that these things used to be called Scolopendra Nymphs.

Carl gets through it by refusing to take the writing seriously: "The heads were clearly saying things the real versions of these people would never say… the dungeon was trying too hard to be edgy, which in effect turned the whole thing into a parody."

The consequential moment is silent. Half-dead and on fire, Carl asks his own totem for a mercy — Asher. Get him out of here. Kill him fast. He's suffered enough — and Shi Maria grants it, and opens her third eye on him doing it:

Ah, yes. I see now. Don't worry, Carl. I will not blind you. Not in the way you're thinking.

There, Carl. The echo of your kin has been muffled. He rests. I have done something for you. Soon, soon you will do something for me.

Also in the hydra's deck: Leveled-Up Frank, a level-90 Blood Assassin Night Elf — the resurrected Frank Q. Carl's immediate reaction is not to the fight but to the precedent: "The existence of Frank as a card opened up a new, horrific possibility I hadn't even considered… There were a lot of people who wouldn't be able to handle that."

docs.title: Devotee of Emberus
docs.text:
Carl came into the book already worshipping Emberus. The hydra fight promotes him:

Baptism by Fire.

You have grown closer to your god, Emberus. He is pleased by your suffering.

Your new rank: Devotee.

Warning: because you are not a Cleric or a Paladin, this is the highest rank you may obtain.

It upgrades his Burn immunity so that heat and lava environments (Sheol included) do no environmental damage, grants a once-a-day level-10 Self-Immolation — a sphere of Sheol fire 1.5 metres in every direction, including down — and raises his tithe from 5% to 10%. Self-Immolation is the spell Shi Maria fires off inside a crowded room in Chapter 71.

Later, in Club Vanquisher, the high cleric Pater Coal and a satyr jeweller sell him an Enchanted Pauper's Ring of the Steadfast Emberus to survive slugpox — a million gold, 10,000 down, no interest "to our martyrs," financed by the church:

You have taken an interest-free* loan of 990,000 gold from the Temple of Emberus. You will no longer be allowed to renounce your religion while you are under debt.

Carl: "Uh… What the hell does that asterisk part mean?" The jeweller: "I don't understand." The achievement is called Columbia House! and the collateral is the strength ring Carl has worn since Floor 1.

docs.title: Quan Ch
docs.text:
Quan Ch — level 70, still one-armed, sixty-plus player-killer skulls — holds both of the region's exit keys. Carl teleports into the Capitol stairwell chamber on a spider automaton and takes him apart. Quan, blind and dying, asks for something back: not his stolen cloak, but a plain gold ring reading "For Daddy" on the inside, still attached to the severed arm in Carl's inventory. Carl digs it out and puts it in his hand.

He took in a deep, rattling breath. "She'd be ashamed of what I've become."

I didn't answer. I formed a fist, but before I could finish him off, he died.

The system gives the kill, the bounty, both keys and a golden player-killer skull to Donut.

docs.title: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride
docs.text:
In the last fight, Carl is temporarily combined with a totem — and the totem drives.

Shi Maria takes his body, rifles his inventory, finds the cookbook and the toraline root and the tattoo kit, and starts building something. She casts his Self-Immolation to burn through a floor, maiming Mongo's wing and Katia's arm in the process. When Li Jun slides down a chain to help, she uses Carl's hand to drive the tattoo stick into his eye, and makes Carl eat it, for ink.

If you won't bring this card to the next floor, I will have to attach myself to something you can't discard so easily.

I am with you now, Carl, until you decide to free me. I will no longer be a card you can abandon, one you can rip away. I am a part of you, and you will have to decide. Keep me with you and gain my power, or set me free. Either way, I win.**

A second, male voice intervenes during all this and is shouted down — "You killed me, and now I am here" / "That is a lie!" — and gets one warning out to Carl: "Don't trust her, boy. Get her out of you as soon as you can. Don't ever trust her." The book never identifies the speaker.

The result, in the middle of his chest, is a tattoo of an eye that blinks once and then closes and vanishes into his skin:

Tattoo. The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

That's all it said. It gave no other description.

Donut rips Shi Maria's card the moment the battle ends — "She's not going to hurt Mongo ever again" — and it changes nothing. The escort quest to deliver Shi Maria to Larracos is still in Carl's log, and Shi Maria is still in Carl's head.

docs.title: The Ending, and the Centipede
docs.text:
Carl talks the AI into scouring the entire planet with a hell portal, which lets every surviving crawler ride a stairwell chamber into the sky rather than be hunted through the last four days. The crawler count goes from 38,532 at the start of the floor to 33,804 — a number Carl calls, with wonder, "shockingly low."

He burns his first Emergency Action Item to hand all remaining Faction Wars votes to the audience. The audience passes Remove Safety Protections For Faction Sponsors at 98%, and a tenth, NPC-populated team — the Home Team, based in Larracos, co-warlorded by Juice Box and Sir Ferdinand — at 52%. His speech at the ceiling:

"We are coming. There is nowhere for you to hide. It is going to be a bloodbath the likes of which has never been seen."

And then, in the last seconds before the floor collapses, a mistake he didn't notice making.

The Scavenger's Daughter, a divine back patch he won early and sewed onto his Battle Rattle, charges a Soul Essence bar off every melee kill and is supposed to be drained after every fill via the Daughter's Kiss. Mordecai's instruction was explicit: "Just make sure you drain the essence bar each time it fills up… Just don't store the stuff for too long." The patch's own warning compared carrying it around to asbestos, then told him to forget it said anything.

"Carl, your jacket is glowing! It's not an aardvark like I thought. It's a giant centipede! The image is of a centipede crawling through all the skulls! It's disgusting!"

At the same moment, a voice spoke in my mind.

You did not diffuse your soul power from the Scavenger's Daughter. That was a mistake. You should never allow it to linger within you. I need you alive, Carl. I need you reasonably sane. We have so much work to do.**

Unresolved — the Scolopendra hook

The book never explains the centipede image and never says the word "Scolopendra" at this moment. What it has established elsewhere: Scolopendra is the final boss of the whole dungeon; the Reminiscence Hydra is a rebranded "Scolopendra Nymph"; a cookbook note speculates that Shi Maria is the great centipede's daughter, or sister, or mother; the galaxy's wealth is gathered in something called the Scolopendra Club; and the arcade cabinet in Carl's father's trailer was Centipede. None of this is resolved in Book 6.

Carl's last thought as Cuba is stripped off the face of the Earth beneath him:

I thought of Asher, the brother I never knew. I needed to make him proud… I wasn't there for him while he lived, but I would be damned if I allowed his death to be for nothing.

You will not break me. You will be avenged. I swear it. I swear it to you all.

docs.title: Other Book 6 Notes
docs.text:
• New gear: the Scavenger's Daughter back patch (divine, unique, fleeting — doubles all patch stat bonuses, +25 Strength, +25 Dexterity, deity-proximity alerts, Climb, Soul Reaper, and a one-shot Mysterious Bone Key that opens any lock in the dungeon at the cost of the jacket and one of Carl's own bones); an Enchanted Prison Tattoo Kit; the Pauper's Ring of the Steadfast Emberus; The Filthy Little Crawler's Book of Voodoo; a Wand of Nighty-Night; a shrink wand; Quan Ch's cloak and roughly five million gold; Velma, Tserendolgor's flamethrower.
  • He never uses the bone key. Per Tipid in the epilogue, it would only have let one of them through — Carl would have had to choose between himself and Donut.
  • He loses all his hair and both eyebrows to Samantha's stomach acid, and has a hair tonic he is choosing not to think about yet.
  • He hasn't yet apologised to Li Jun.

docs.title: Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin
docs.text:
Floor 9 is Faction Wars, fought across the plains outside — and down inside — the funnel city of Larracos. Carl enters it as the dungeon's number-one-ranked crawler and Co-Warlord of The Princess Posse, and spends most of the book running an army instead of a party: nine rival factions, a ten-team alliance board, four named offensives and a staff of officers. It is also the book in which he quietly does the single most consequential thing any crawler has done in the series, and never tells anyone he meant to.

Level endpoints

The book prints only two hard levels for Carl. At the Club Vanquisher raid (Ch. 51) the mantaur guards are "ranging from 75 to 80, which was a little worrying as I was only level 75." At Chapter 77 he notes "even I had leveled a few times—up to level 81—despite me not doing anything." 81 is the last level stated for him in the book; no start-of-floor or end-of-floor figure is given, and he ended Book 6 at 73.

docs.title: Mayor of Shanty Town
docs.text:
In Chapter 10, negotiating with Queen Imogen's cat familiar Sir Ferdinand — now co-warlord of the NPC Home Team, renamed Team Retribution — Carl trades Quan Ch's looted black bowler hat (plus gold the system demands to complete the transfer) for the mayorship of Shanty Town, the shanty ring built around the lip of Larracos:

"I want to be mayor of that town. Shanty Town. You'll have to transfer your mayorship to us, which means that jewel on your necklace will go away. You'll get this hat, and we'll trade it back for your turban in a day or so. ..."

The trade also renames the two factions' truce to "The Good Guys." Shanty Town becomes the Posse's third front, the site of the Nest sniper tower Donut fights from, and the ground over which her third Atrocity is cast.

docs.title: Christmas Morning, and the button he actually pressed
docs.text:
The book's biggest secret is buried in two matching interludes set on Floor 8 — the Prologue and the Christmas Morning interlude that closes Part One, just before Chapter 20. Both are memories replayed on the eighth floor's Ghosts of Earth, and in both Carl can move and act while the memory around him stays frozen.

In the Prologue, a homeless man named Paulie — a gondii residual wearing a human — speaks to Carl through a frozen moment and talks him into drinking a doctored cup of coffee. It installs an illegal Valtay-built Containment Interface in Carl's head. Paulie explains what it is for: the system AI's containment carries a "fuse," a failsafe that turns the system's star nova if five or six conditions trip. Paulie's people want Carl to blow it on purpose.

"Good. This controller in your interface will allow you to pop the fuse. You will, unfortunately, die. But the good news is you'll kill everyone else on the way out."

Paulie then breaks his own mission to add a warning: "If you make this decision. Be sure. Be sure it's your only option. This is more than just a failsafe. It's the end of everything."

The Christmas Morning interlude is the other half. The handshake completes — Containment Interface is now available for use — and Carl asks the liaison Orren to transfer him back to a gas station he had passed, so he can sit with the memory ghost of a sleeping dog, Lightning Lou, and think. There is no single "Boom" button. There are six tabs of untranslated menus. It takes him about ten minutes to find the Fuse page, which lists five benchmarks with only two marked Conditions Met, and one control: Override Conditions And Activate Fuse. Warning. Warning.

He wants to press it. The interlude is explicit that he wants to press it "more than anything in the world." He does not, for two reasons: he does not believe the AI would have permitted him the power if it actually wanted to die, and he cannot make the choice for everyone else.

I did want to hit the button. I wanted it more than anything in the world. My anger at the powers that made this happen were bright. So bright.

I miss you, too, Donut.

...

But not bright enough.

He keeps reading, and at the very end of a list of twenty status notifications he finds the only other control in the interface:

Disconnect Containment. Warning. This will disengage all metrics and controls, including the fuse system. It will render the Containment Unit inert. The failsafe will no longer function. Most controls will cease to function.

He weighs three options — do nothing, blow the fuse and die, or switch the whole apparatus off — and frames the decision as "Which of those three options would hurt the Syndicate the most? And which of those three options would protect my people the most?"

We already were under the thumb of the psychotic AI.

I pressed the Disconnect Containment button. The entire new interface blanked out, leaving nothing but the map. Already, the little red dot over Earth started to grow.

"Welcome to the party, pals," I said.

The consequences land in Chapters 34–39. Skull Empire King Rust reveals his daughter Princess Formidable has hijacked a cruiser and intends to manually trigger the failsafe from an orbital monitor station, killing everyone in the system. Carl already knows it will not work:

I knew it wasn't going to work because I knew the failsafe was already deactivated. I knew the failsafe was deactivated because I was the one who had turned it off.

Orren interrogates him about the implant with ten minutes on the clock, and by the end of the scene the System AI has demonstrated reach out past the star. Orren, defeated: "All right. You've gone fully primal, and we can't stop you. But beyond that, you have broken free of your containment." Afterwards he asks Carl directly:

"Carl," Orren said after a few moments. "Is that what you did? You helped break the AI from its containment? Did you do it deliberately?"

"What?" Donut asked. "What's this?"

I just looked at him. I didn't answer.

Orcs at the monitor station later pull the trigger themselves and nothing happens. The showrunner Cascadia spends the rest of the book managing a season with an AI that has officially "gone primal" and a system with no off switch — which is also the premise Rishi builds his treaty offer on, and the reason the galaxy's tunnel node to the Aryl system went dark.

docs.title: Party leader of the Royal Court
docs.text:
In Chapter 27, immediately after Empress D'Nadia dies, the system reassigns the party:

Due to your recent upgrades, your total base stat count has made you the strongest member of your party. As a result, you have been designated as the new Party Leader of the Royal Court of Princess Donut.

Donut has held the role since Book 2 on combined base stats. Her objection is entirely for the cameras, which Carl notices and is sad about:

"This is not acceptable," she said with a harumph. She jumped onto my shoulder. "If you change the name of the party, I swear I will leave, Carl. Is that what you want? Mongo to come from a broken home?"

He keeps the party name and the titles. The arrangement lasts about fifty chapters: when Donut jumps to level 135 in Chapter 77 she takes it straight back — "At least I'm back in my rightful spot as leader of the party."

docs.title: The Ring of Divine Suffering
docs.text:
Carl wears the Ring of Divine Suffering through the whole of Faction Wars, and the book treats it as an addiction rather than an item. He also loots a second ring off King Rust's corpse, which he eventually gives to Li Na.

The worst moment comes in Chapter 26, standing over a dying D'Nadia. The anger is explicitly unprecedented — "The anger that washed over me was so brilliantly white, all three of my eyes burned. I'd never felt anything like this" — and the river in his head comes back with it. Donut talks him down over party chat while stalling out loud:

Carl: Donut, I changed my mind. I want to do it. Step aside.

Donut: No, Carl. Please, no. I need you to step back. I need you to calm down right now. I got this. It's okay.

He steps back. The book gives the moment its own paragraph — "I saw it, clear as can be. Right there. I stood upon it, one foot stretched out over open air... You can find clarity when you need it most." — and he lets Donut call the kill instead, which Mongo takes. Afterwards she presses him again:

Donut: You do know what came over you. I want you to throw that ring away, Carl. It's not worth it. It's doing something to you. You're scaring me.

You're scaring me lands on him as "How many times had my mother said that to my father?" He still refuses: "Not yet. I need it for just a little longer."

He finally lets it go in Chapter 85, in the rebuilt ruins of Larracos with Faction Wars already won. The temptation is specific — he could mark and kill the surrendered enemy mercenaries and max his base stats at 300 the way Li Na just had:

One look at Li Na, and I knew that path, that slope was too steep. Survival had more than one meaning.

Still, I didn't want to let it go.

So he destroys it in the only way that guarantees he cannot change his mind. He holds the ring up in front of Donut's nose, she asks "Are you sure, Carl?", and she swallows it.

"I almost choked to death, Carl. That would've been quite ironic, don't you think?"

docs.title: New skills, boons and borrowed magic
docs.text:
Every acquisition on this floor comes from somewhere other than a level-up. (Ability and spell pages carry the mechanics; this page records only how each was obtained.)

  • Walk on Air — already in his skill list when the book opens, which he only notices when a toe ring's description says "(already obtained.)" It is Li Jun's skill, taken permanently when Shi Maria used Carl's hand to tear out Li Jun's eye at the end of Book 6 and made him eat it. Rosetta later confirms the rule: "Spells and skills taken against the owner's will were much more powerful and resulted in the owner losing them permanently."
  • Gloom Wraith Phase — level 13, from a Sheol-flavoured potion out of one of his Floor 8 celestial boxes, identified and handed over by Mordecai in Chapter 6. It is the skill he kills Architect Houston with.
  • Profane Iron — a once-a-day chain skill borrowed from Li Na by Rosetta's toraline-ink method: Li Na gives blood freely, temporarily losing five levels, and Katia inks the resulting chain-dragon tattoo across Carl's right forearm (his first tattoo on that arm; the system rates it expert quality). He reciprocates, giving Imani a borrowed Tripper via a small barbed-wire ankle tattoo of her own.
  • Heathen Scald — level 15, a Celestial Boon from Emberus for completing the church quest Kill the Blasphemer in Chapter 51, announced after "a good ten seconds of uncontrolled, absolutely unhinged, shrieking laughter in Emberus's voice." Adds its damage to any punch attack, for the remainder of the floor.
  • Speedster — not permanent and not from Eris. It is one of four thirty-hour buffs granted by the Enchanted Hairbrush of the Beefmaster, a celestial item from the Club Vanquisher raid haul, which requires 25cm of hair and screams while in use. Mordecai has never seen the benefit awarded that way.
  • Pied Piper — level 15, a proximity effect from the god Harpocrates in Chapter 70. It becomes permanent by coin flip. In Chapter 76 the chaos goddess Eris, newly freed of her sponsor, spins a two-item wheel in front of him: Dick will fall off! (from the feral god Meatus) and Level-15 Pied Piper! It lands on the first, "hovered for a second, then ticked over" to the second. It is also, as Carl has to explain to Donut, nothing to do with rodents — "the skill allows me to play musical instruments."

docs.title: Mind Balance, trained to 16
docs.text:
The Legendary Enchanted Toe Ring of the Well-Balanced (left pinky toe, non-negotiable) gives him Mind Balance at level 5, protection from Enslavement and Conscription. It immediately reports itself currently triggered — Shi Maria, tattooed into his sternum, is trying to cast through him, and the log fills with hundreds of identical entries:
