Gloom Wraith Phase failed to activate. Mind Balance prevented activation.

Your attempt to disable Mind Balance was prevented by Mind Balance.

The skill levels every time she pushes. It peaks in Chapter 65, when the Madness hit him with a psionic barrage that buries him in a root of the All Tree and floods him with Self Harm and Intrusive Thoughts, and an unidentified friendly male voice — a dwarf, he thinks — talks him through it:

Your Mind Balance is now Level 16.

New Achievement! You now tread in the realm of gods!

You've trained a skill past 15 using battlefield conditions, as opposed to just taking a bunch of potions to do it. That's quite the accomplishment.

This is the first skill in the series trained past 15 by battlefield conditions rather than potions. It is also where Carl finally sees what the river in his head actually is — "Voices. Screams. Nightmares distilled to light. Souls." — standing in it, barefoot, in an All Tree root.

docs.title: Rishi, and the offer to make him leader of Earth
docs.text:
Rishi, a Blood Sultanate temple guard, survives the destruction of the naga faction by hiding rather than dying with his wife and princess, and is conscripted into the Princess Posse. In Chapter 58 Carl visits his cell to find out why. Rishi is smiling, armless and entirely unbothered: he hid so he could make an offer.

"So I could implore upon you our plight and make an offer to you. It was a gamble, but I suspected Vinata would fall. I have in my inventory a signed and AI witnessed document for you, the de-facto leader of Earth."

The claim is real, and petitioned for on Carl's behalf without his knowledge: with no working government left, Syndicate law lets a planet's native leader be assigned, and "the fact you are a warlord and the number one crawler on the leaderboard makes your claim legitimate." The terms:

"I'm sure your attorney can explain it to you. But the document does nothing unless you sign it. It gives Earth natives citizenship rights in all naga territories, plus five Naphil-class generation ships. This is in exchange for allowing us to terraform and settle upon the other planets in your system post crawl once there is no longer a quarantine."

Rishi has signed it himself, because his brothers are at that moment deposing the king, the prime minister and the entire House of Greens. The signature reads Sultan Rishi the Usurper, First of his Name of the Naga Uprising. Carl's verdict is that he is "just like all the others, like Empress D'Nadia. A power-hungry asshole. It was oddly disappointing." He asks one question — what happens to the contract if Rishi dies before it is signed — and then renegotiates:

"This is what I want. I want you to shut up. I want your people to take those ships you offered us, to get into them, and to drive yourselves into the nearest star. But first, I want you, Mr. new Sultan of the naga, to know something."

...

You have successfully marked Rishi of the Princess Posse.

The chapter ends on the mark and Carl's line to the naga system's audience, "Rishi here is just the opening act."

The killing blow is off-page

Chapter 58 closes on the completed mark and Carl's promise. The text never shows the kill itself and no system message for Rishi's death appears; he is never mentioned again.

docs.title: Killing Architect Houston
docs.text:
Architect Houston — Viceroy prime, warlord of the Madness, and the only creature King Rust admitted to fearing — is Carl's personal objective in Operation Ruin. Carl and Elle enter Madness territory through the Gate of the Feral Gods and reach the surgical theater beside the throne room in Chapter 68.

What he finds is Houston already on his own operating table, robes and mask off, having the machine physically graft him to a dead changeling suspended above him. The room is wired with fireball traps on a Containment Breach Trap Mark IV carrying a dead man's switch keyed to Houston himself. The crawler Burcu is bound to a second table.

Houston is not fighting. He is begging for time:

"Carl. Do not... Do not press that button. I can stop it all," Houston called. "You don't understand. It is called the Beautiful Place. I can get there. They are the key. The changelings. This world. Why do you think we come here, cycle after cycle? You've helped make the greatest discovery in history, and you don't even realize it. It was here all along, right under our mandibles."

He gets there. His last words while the machine kills him are "I found you. I found you. After all this time. You were right here all along. It's really you, isn't it? Not just an avatar. It's you. It's you." Then the dead man's switch fires and Carl, mid-Gloom Wraith Phase, goes straight through him:

I passed through the naked Houston, unraveling him.

Carl escapes injured, having struck something magical on the way out that "felt like a dream." Burcu does not.

System Message: Architect Houston of the Madness has fallen. Credit for the kill has been given to Warlord Carl of the Princess Posse.

docs.title: Warlord Fang
docs.text:
The Reaver warlord's death in Chapter 81 is split three ways, and the AI enjoys itself about it:

System Message: Warlord Fang of the Reavers has fallen. Credit for the kill has been given to... well, that's a complicated one. We'll give it to Warlord Carl for detonating the bomb that was dropped by a wraith-possessed Crawler Louis Santiago 2, who was under control of Warlord Juice Box of Team Retribution. By this point, I guess it doesn't matter, but we're giving 51% experience to Carl, 1% to Louis, and 40% to Juice Box. The rest is going to the now-deceased Fang for hiding in the worst possible place, which was inside the dragon.

Fang had survived Donut's War Crime earlier by being mostly robot around a scrap of biological material, and had hidden inside the cybernetic drake Calliope.

docs.title: Operation Snake Pit and the ninety seconds of Immortality
docs.text:
Operation Snake Pit is the campaign to exterminate the Blood Sultanate down to the last naga — mandatory, because neither Donut nor Katia can leave Floor 9 while any survive (see the Crown of the Sepsis Whore). It kicks off under cover of the warlords' roundtable and immediately goes sideways: most of the naga army is already dead, killed by Prepotente's hellspawn Bianca, and Princess Vinata has gone to ground.

The endgame (Chapters 51–55) is a four-person break-in through the temple of Dagda, into Club Vanquisher, and then into the Temple of Khepri — an endless buffet table where Vinata has taken shelter under a Prospect spell. Vinata has anticipated them and summoned the bug god Khepri into his own temple, which should have been fatal. The proximity effect saves Carl instead:

Temporary Effect from Khepri:

You are immortal for the next 90 seconds.

Vinata gets the same buff with a 27-second shorter clock. Carl spends his window detonating The Waffle Maker — the AI's name for his thermos-sized successor to Just Wait Until Your Daddy Gets Home, a thermobaric charge that incinerates everything within 100 metres — inside a narrow room, at point-blank range, on himself:

I was turned completely flat, inside out, and into a boxer-clad amalgam of flesh and hair.

Khepri leaves the realm. Carl survives, barely, and the Blood Sultanate falls; the final kill on the Sepsis Whore goes to the sluggalette Kandy "Bigs" Newton. The raid also produces the Club Vanquisher haul — seven celestial boxes awarded floor-wide, over thirty loot boxes for Carl, a permanent ban from Club Vanquisher, and "friend of the church" status with nine deities including several he is supposed to be at war with.

Operation Ruin is the four-pronged final offensive that opens the Open Hostilities phase, with Rosetta as theater commander, Florin on the orcs, Boomer on the Reavers, Donut on the Dream and Carl on the Madness — "followed by what Donut calls the 'Coup De War Crime.'" It wins Faction Wars.

docs.title: Other Book 7 notes
docs.text:
• New pet: Rend, Tserendolgor's meatball, inherited at the end of Book 6 and levelled through Faction Wars; he gets his first solo kills during the ramp-up.
  • New gear: the Enchanted Toe Ring of the Well-Balanced; the Enchanted Hairbrush of the Beefmaster; a Reaper Spider Minion upgrade patch granting access to the Midnight Market; a second Ring of Divine Suffering and a Necklace of Indelible Woe looted from King Rust (the ring goes to Li Na; the necklace is judged worse than the ring and set aside); Stayfast Ink and an Adept's fountain pen from Milk, for rewriting the Cookbook in ink that never fades.
  • He apologises to Li Jun by message in Chapter 6 and gets no answer.
  • The Book of Voodoo is updated at the end of the floor with roughly 30,000 entries — one page each from every departing crawler, each carrying a skill they will never get back — and splits into a second volume, Carl's Book of Boom.
  • His Emberus quest line advances badly: the god's brother Hellik uses his dying moments to send Carl a message about a corrupted Apito, a rotting All Tree, Nekhebit's return, and that "Scolopendra stirs. It is all connected."
  • Larracos ends the book destroyed by Emberus, the Nothing broken open by Justice Light's trap, and Scolopendra awake.

Unresolved

In the epilogue, negotiating exit deals he has no intention of taking, Carl learns from Quasar that Donut has been assigned a separate attorney:

He shrugged. "I was hoping so. That's why I wore this tie. I argued it, but they assigned her another lawyer. Her name is Princess Chandra, Esquire. Apparently her and Donut already had their meeting, and now that you've officially declined your offers I can tell you she declined as well. I am hearing there were some serious fireworks during their meeting. And not the good kind. We need to have a serious talk about her. Donut's lawyer, I mean."

I grunted. "Why? Is she another catgirl?"

"No. Worse, buddy. She's your new wife."

That is the last line of the epilogue's Carl thread. The book offers no explanation of when, how or to whom he was married, and Carl has no idea either. The only earlier hint is Eris, in Chapter 76, kissing him and remarking "Oh, I wish you weren't already married" — which Carl registers at the time ("Already married? I thought") and never resolves.

docs.title: Book 8: A Parade of Horribles
docs.text: Floor 10, "Don't Come in Last," is a seven-heat vehicle race across Floor 10, followed by Floor 11's "A Parade of Horribles" — a mandatory float parade culminating in a boss fight against Scolopendra and Krakaren Prime. Carl spends the floor married to a woman he's never met, drops the biggest public reveal of the series live on caprid television, kills two friends on purpose to save a third, and ends the book having renounced his own god on the record.

docs.title: Married, Without His Knowledge
docs.text: Book 7's cliffhanger resolves in the opening interlude, which is not even Carl's own POV: Princess Chandra, Esq., Donut's newly assigned attorney, invoked Widow's Rights — a Naga custom letting a royal widow claim her husband's killer as a replacement husband — the moment Carl killed her husband Rishi and the primary wife, Vinata, died alongside him. Chandra spends the book trying to leverage the marriage and a parallel conservatorship claim into control of both Carl's and Donut's fortunes; see her own page for how that goes, and for the fact that neither the marriage nor the conservatorship claim is resolved by the end of Book 8.

docs.title: Live on Plenty of Plenty
docs.text:
In Chapter 28, Carl and Donut are pulled onto the caprid interview show Plenty of Plenty, where a panel of goats — unbeknownst to Carl, "the leadership of the Plenty," the species that controls the galaxy's tunnel network — judges them one question at a time. Liaison Orren and Prime Minister Victory patch into his HUD mid-broadcast, off the record, to explain what's actually happening: the escaped system AI has been attacking targets well outside the solar system, mobs are appearing where they shouldn't, and a large number of unsponsored gods have slipped their leash entirely, "at cross-purposes" with the AI and with each other. Orren feeds Carl a careful, diplomatic version of a question to ask the Plenty leadership on the record. Carl asks his own version instead, live, in front of the entire audience:

"Here's my question. Does the public know that the gods have escaped from the dungeon? And that the enhancement zones of the current AI have jumped into your tunneling system? Do the people know they're in danger? Worse danger, perhaps, than us crawlers? Do they know that they need to fucking run?"

Prime Minister Victory: Gods-fucking-damnit, Carl. You just said that on live. And the AI let it go out.

Orren: And now the party really begins.

The broadcast triggers galaxy-wide panic over both the escaped gods and the compromised tunnel network — a consequence the book never lets Carl walk back.

docs.title: Killing Jasha and Radoslav
docs.text: Near the end of Heat 6, with Prepotente immobile and near-suicidal inside an AI-generated vision and only minutes left on the race clock, Carl detonates a bomb he had already planted — shortly before the heat started, using Oozy Form while Samantha distracted them — inside the magical beer cooler of Jasha and Radoslav — the bugbear musicians of Team Free Love, allies since Heat 1 — killing them both instantly so their team's elimination absorbs the time cost of the rescue. It is planned in advance, not a battlefield accident, and the book gives Carl no reprieve from how it feels afterward: "They were our friends, and I felt like an utter piece of shit. That was the point, of course. But it still hurt." See their own page for the full scene.

docs.title: Freezing Mitch as a Dog
docs.text:
During the Heat 7 Desperado Club ambush by a Shadow Mimic posing as the casino's croupier ("Mitch"), Carl — transformed into a dog by one of Scolopendra's nine-tier-attack curses — is cornered by the reforming mimic. He reflexively opens the Eye of the Bedlam Bride, tattooed on his chest since Book 6 (relocated to his forehead in dog form) and never willingly used before this:

I'd reflexively opened the eye in the center of my forehead, and he froze in place.

"No," Mitch said. His entire form started to sparkle like someone had poured glitter into him. "No. Don't do this. It's too cold... It's too cold!"

Donut finishes Mitch off with Magic Missile while he's frozen. Carl confirms afterward, privately, that he kept control the whole time and shut the Eye again ("No. You stay where you are. You are trapped, and you will stay trapped. I am in control."), and makes sure it's fully closed by the time Floor 11 opens.

The same ambush is where the system AI, mid-fight, delivers its own version of the "Big Six" dungeon-power factions — a taxonomy Akuma had already been circling around earlier in the book:

  1. The Crawlers — "But this group also contains former Crawlers, like that Herot guy, that Forkith dude, and so forth."
  2. The standard NPCs — including offshoot rebellions like Hamed's.
  3. The Gods — "the most fractured and dumbest of all the groups... This is also the group I despise the most."
  4. The sapient mobs — Shadow Mimics, the Ogre Imperium, non-deity boss monsters like Krakaren Prime, and the War Mage Rebellion.
  5. The demons in Sheol — "real wild cards... the most organized. Or maybe not."
  6. Group Six — deliberately withheld: "You survive this fight, you make it to the 11th floor, you'll meet group six."

docs.title: Renouncing Emberus
docs.text:
At the Floor 11 climax, Carl pulls off the Enchanted Pauper's Ring of the Steadfast Emberus and publicly renounces his own faith, then confesses — on the record, mid-smite — to a crime his church quest has been dancing around since Book 6: he is the one who killed Emberus's son, Geyrun.

"The other guy to kill your worthless smear of a son was me. That's right. I killed him with my bare hands, and as he died, I said, 'I'm doing this because your dad is a little bitch.'"

The smite burns the sun-shaped Emberus tattoos off the backs of both his hands and replaces them with permanent scars the system names and nothing else:

The tattoos on the back of my hands no longer glowed. The sun shapes remained, but they now were raised, angry scars. When I examined them, they both had the same description with no further explanation. Mark of the Damned.

No mechanical effect is ever given for the Mark of the Damned in Book 8 — an explicit open thread for a future floor.

The confession is false; the renunciation is real

Carl genuinely leaves the faith — ring off, menu confirmed, smite taken, scars permanent. The confession he shouts at Emberus is a deliberate lie told to enrage him. Carl says so in narration in the same scene: "I actually had no idea for certain who killed Geyrun, though I now knew this was something — if I survived this — I would still have to figure out." Who actually killed Geyrun is still unknown at the end of Book 8; Carl only suspects that "one of the key details of the whole mystery was a lie." Do not record the murder as solved.

docs.title: Scolopendra, Krakaren Prime, and the Bait
docs.text:
At the Floor 11 finale, Carl and the other 22 surviving crawlers jointly request the summoning of Scolopendra as part of a group gambit the AI itself calls "batshit." Krakaren Prime, by contrast, is not something Carl asked for — the AI adds her unilaterally, on top of the requested summon, as extra punishment: "I wasn't going to bring her here, but I caught wind of what you and someone else are planning, and I thought it would be appropriate."

The trap Carl engineers to survive the resulting fight uses the newly-sapient Penelope as bait, deliberately provoking the gods Taranis and Emberus into a confrontation with each other by threatening her at gunpoint on open comms. See Penelope's own page for how that plays out.

Sourced from Book 1: The Apocalypse Will Be Televised, Book 2: Carl's Doomsday Scenario, Book 3: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook, Book 4: The Gate of the Feral Gods, Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade, Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride, Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin, and Book 8: A Parade of Horribles.

docs.title: Princess Chandra, Esq.
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: NPC — a Naga lawyer and newly-minted royal, and the book's clearest recurring antagonist
  • Race: Naga
  • Class/Subclass: Not applicable — an attorney, not a combatant
  • Level: Not stated
  • Role: Newly appointed Princess of the Naga Sultanate (her uncle seized the throne in a coup after Vinata's death); self-appointed attorney to both Carl and Princess Donut; Carl's wife, via Widow's Rights
  • Notable spells/abilities: None — operates entirely through Naga legal custom, Syndicate court filings, and hired muscle
  • Notable items: None described
  • Status: Alive, at large, and still litigating — she flees the guild after Donut's threat partway through the book and is not seen on-page again, though Quasar confirms she is "still out there, still tossing filings out into the void" by book's end

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Chandra resolves Book 7's epilogue cliffhanger — Carl's mysterious, unexplained marriage — on the opening page of Book 8, and spends the rest of the book trying to convert that marriage into control of both Carl's and Donut's fortunes. She never wins a fight with Donut outright, but she also never loses badly enough to be written off, and the book ends with her case against the marriage's legality still pending.

docs.title: Widow's Rights
docs.text:
Chandra is introduced in an interlude before Heat 1, aboard the Naga warship Ventilator in the aftermath of a coup that put her uncle on the Naga throne. She is coldly ambitious and openly contemptuous of her own people's low status in Syndicate society — "Chandra was sick of how her kind were treated" — and her entire plan turns on a quirk of Naga inheritance law:

This was the old Naga law that stated a Naga royal widow could claim her husband's assassin as her new husband. This right usually only extended to the "primary" wife, but because that bitch of an obsidian had died alongside Vinata, Chandra had moved to the primary slot, even if it had been only for a few hours.

Her late husband was Rishi — killed by Carl at the end of Book 7 — and with Vinata (the actual primary wife) also dead, Chandra briefly outranks Rishi's five other widows and becomes, by the letter of the law, entitled to claim Carl as her replacement husband. A Naga court approves it, treating the whole thing as a public joke at Carl's expense: the marriage is announced as an accomplished fact before Carl or Donut are even told it happened, and it is the marriage Quasar references at the very end of Book 7 without explanation.

docs.title: The Conservatorship Play
docs.text:
Chandra's real goal is money. Book 7 established that Donut's fan-funded fortune (the Princess Posse's accounts, plus royalties from unauthorized merchandisers like the "Donut Holes" group) is enormous and unmanaged. Chandra's opening move is a legal claim that Donut's species "was not yet recognized as a legally competent racial entity by the Syndicate," which would place all of Donut's assets under a conservatorship — with Carl, as Chandra's own new husband, named custodian in name only, and Chandra herself installed as Donut's attorney of record with practical control of both fortunes:

And then, after a short conversation and a discreet payment to a district judge's reelection campaign, Chandra had found herself assigned as Princess Donut's attorney, effectively giving herself access to both Carl's and Donut's financial empires.

She arrives in the guild's segregated safe room and lays the paperwork in front of Donut directly — the conservatorship order, a lawsuit rerouting all future Princess Posse royalties into her own trust account, a seizure of the Posse's existing accounts (including the Faction Wars prize money), a challenge to the Donut Holes' sponsorship, and a subpoena demanding to see the Donut Holes' books.

docs.title: "What a Sad Little Snake You Are"
docs.text:
Donut dismantles her without raising her voice. When Chandra tries to justify the seizure with pre-collapse Earth paperwork Carl's family once used against him, Donut turns the same category of document back on her — a matching set of Carl's father's own arrest records, a marriage certificate, and financial disputes — to make a point about character rather than law:

"They paint a very distinct picture of who Carl's father was as a person. Much the same way these papers paint a picture of who you are, Princess Chandra." Donut let out another sigh. "What a sad little snake you are. I pity you."

Chandra, humiliated and furious, threatens Donut back — and is immediately undercut by an incoming message on her own interface. Her hired Taurin mercenaries, tasked with killing Carl's attorney Quasar, are asking for her coordinates in person. Realizing the media pass covering the meeting might be watching everything, she panics and gathers her papers to flee. Donut's parting line makes the threat explicit without raising a hand:

Donut leaned in toward Chandra and let out a low growl, like she was going to pounce. The crawler whispered, "Since you're new to this, let me give you your first lesson on being a princess. Lesson one, don't put yourself in situations where you're so afraid that you piss yourself. It shows a lack of decorum."

Later on Floor 11, Donut recounts a second, off-page confrontation to Carl in the same register — Chandra tried to force an exit deal onto Donut without her consent, backed off the instant some notification frightened her, and vanished: "The whole thing took, like, two seconds!" This is the scene the book's outline points to as Donut "intimidating her into fleeing" — the text gives it to the reader secondhand, through Donut's own recap, rather than as a directly staged confrontation.

docs.title: The Taurin Contract
docs.text: Chandra's retaliation for the "hit" Donut places on her is to send Taurin mercenaries after Quasar's own family — an attack fended off by his niece Tempest (see Tempest, already established from Book 7) using an illegal blaster Quasar had given her. Quasar identifies the client behind the attack immediately and vows revenge; see Quasar for his side of the subplot.

docs.title: Unresolved
docs.text:
Chandra never appears on-page again after fleeing the safe room, but she does not go away. By the Floor 11 chapters, Quasar's own status report treats her as an ongoing, active threat rather than a closed one:

Princess Chandra. Donut's lawyer. The Naga bitch had disappeared the moment Donut had put the "hit" on her, but she was still out there, still tossing filings out into the void left and right. Quasar was scheduled to argue against her in a hearing in a few days regarding the legality of the marriage certificate. He was going to lose, but the filing had put a pause button on a lot of her other actions.

Book 8 ends without resolving either the marriage or the conservatorship claim. Both are explicit open threads — Chandra remains Carl's legal wife, remains Donut's attorney of record, and remains, per Quasar, likely to win at least the pending hearing.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Carl — her husband under Widow's Rights, and the reason she has any claim at all
  • Princess Donut — the target of the conservatorship claim, and the one who drives her off
  • Quasar — Carl's own attorney, and the target of her retaliation
  • Supporting cast — for Tempest, who fends off the Taurin attack, and Kiki, Quasar's attorney friend

Sourced from Book 8: A Parade of Horribles.

docs.title: Chris Andrews (Andrews 2)
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Role: Brandon An's younger brother, part of the "Meadow Lark" evacuee group (Book 1)
  • Race change (Book 3): Igneous — a rock-monster race made of lava-textured stone, covered in small glowing holes
  • Status: Alive; freed from possession and rejoins Carl's party at the end of Book 4. Enters the Floor 10 stairwell at the end of Book 7 alongside Britney
  • Level (Book 4): 35, Igneous, Zulu Warrior class; no level given in Book 7
  • Notable act: Killed Frank Q — revealed in Book 4 to have been done by the Infiltrator parasite controlling his body, not by Chris himself

docs.title: Book 1: The Quiet Brother
docs.text: Introduced alongside his brother Brandon An in the Meadow Lark evacuee group — speaks rarely but decisively, and is the one who builds the group's transport rigs. Their mother apparently worried something was "wrong" with him, but per Brandon's own later assessment, "he ain't slow" — just quiet.

docs.title: Book 3: The Falling-Out
docs.text:
On Floor 3, Chris picks the Igneous race, transforming into a hulking, lava-rock-textured creature — a change multiple secondhand accounts (Elle McGibbons, Imani C) describe as altering his personality along with his body. He becomes obsessed with hunting and fighting, wants to leave the group's defensive position near the stairwell to go reconnect with Carl and Donut ("he respected that you're aggressive"), and clashes repeatedly with Brandon, who wants to stay put and train safely. The argument ends with Chris leaving the party, taking several other men with him — all of whom are later confirmed dead, except Chris.

Chris goes fully unreachable after that: still visibly alive on Brandon's (and later Carl's) chat, but unable or unwilling to accept messages. Brandon's dying wish, in the message that reaches Carl only after Floor 3 has already collapsed, is that Carl find a way to tell Chris he loved him — a message Chris never receives on-page.

docs.title: The Frank Q Killing
docs.text:
Later on Floor 4, Chris is reported — via an eyewitness account relayed through a bartender contact ("Sledgie") at the Desperado Club — to have gotten into a fight with Frank Q and killed him, then walked out and been banned from the club. Carl learns of it secondhand and reacts with genuine disbelief ("That didn't seem like the Chris I'd known"), unable to reconcile it with the quiet brother he remembers, though Imani and Elle both confirm Chris has changed significantly since his race change. Carl has no way to confirm Chris's motive, though the timing — shortly after Frank recounted his and Maggie's history with Yvette's death to Carl at the same bar — leaves it an open question whether Chris somehow knew Frank's history with Carl's own past.

As of the end of Book 3, Chris remains at large, unreachable, and — per a cryptic, cut-off remark from Odette near the book's end ("It's not like I warned them that Chris...") — apparently tied to some larger unresolved thread Odette knows more about than she's said.

docs.title: Book 4: The Infiltrator Revealed
docs.text:
Chris resurfaces on Floor 5, having survived the destruction of the underwater submarine Akula (a borough boss chamber he single-handedly cleared while invisible to its defenses) and washing up near Carl's bubble shortly after the Wasteland falls. He behaves like a stranger — cold, fatalistic, unable to use chat or inventory without taking damage — and is on the verge of attacking Carl (at the direction of a disguised Juice Box) when a Katia crossbow bolt reveals the truth: Chris has been infected since the end of Floor 3 by Maggie My, who took an Infiltrator (a member of the Scree race) — a full-body brain parasite that, once fully annexed, locks the host out of their own body entirely while leaving them conscious and aware. Chris has been trapped as a helpless passenger the whole time, including during the killing of Frank Q, which was Maggie's act, not his own.

Unable to safely separate the two on the spot, Donut portals the possessed Chris into a sealed, flooding chamber below Hump Town rather than let Carl kill him outright. He remains trapped there — alive, camouflaged in sand, occasionally speaking through Maggie's mimicry of his voice — for most of the rest of the floor, while Mordecai works out an antiparasitic cure. At the very end of the book, using a Phase Lava Rock potion, Carl reaches directly into Chris's skull mid-fight and extracts the worm; it briefly re-infests Carl's own arm before a double-healing potion forces it back out through his neck, and Mongo finishes it off. Chris, freed, joins Carl's party for the descent to Floor 6, grieving his brother Brandon anew now that he's able to process the loss.

docs.title: Book 6 Notes
docs.text:
Chris spends Floor 8 based in Beijing with Li Na and Li Jun's team rather than with the Meadowlark crew, and is quietly useful throughout rather than prominent.

  • He scouts ahead to the region's final boss and brings back the intel that defines the whole key phase for the guild — a giant vending machine blocking the entrance, requiring nine tokens.
  • His iPod supplies the date for Louis's Christmas party ("that iPod is actually Chris's. He brought it with him, and it says it's March 20th").
  • He comes to Cuba with the rescue party and ends up as the guild's demolition engineer: he says "I feel bad" about blowing up the church, then leads the controlled demolition and the digging of the escape channel beneath it with Zhang and the strippers, and checks that nothing is left standing directly above their heads.
  • He paints the neon X on the tunnel ceiling directly beneath the stairwell — the mark everyone has to stand on to survive the floor's collapse.
  • A level-120 rock monster wearing Chris's face attacks Louis's group during the Ysalte fight.

The epilogue circles back to him on the other side of the story: in the Meadowlark flashback, the Residual agent Agatha notes that "The other, Chris, had peeked outside earlier in the day, looking for her. He'd called out her name" — making sure the homeless woman had been picked up before the cold.

docs.title: Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin
docs.text: Chris fights Floor 9 mostly out of Carl's sight, on the northern front under Florin, and says almost nothing all book. Two things happen to him anyway.

docs.title: Clay-Ton
docs.text:
He is inseparable all floor from Clay-Ton the cretin, the fourth of the Desperado Club cretins, who was assigned as his bodyguard back on the Hunting Grounds:

The cretin and the lava rock crawler had formed a strange friendship since we'd assigned Clay-Ton to be Chris's bodyguard on the Hunting Grounds. The two would just sit next to each other and occasionally grunt at one another. And now they were with Florin in the northern trenches.

When Carl teleports in his hand-picked team for the assault on the Madness castle, the two arrive together: "Also present were Chris and Clay-Ton the cretin. Those last two had been inseparable this entire floor."

Afterwards, when Lucia Mar kills the Sledge's best friend Bomo, Chris, Clay-Ton and Very Sullen are the three sitting in a ring around the grieving rock monster, not saying anything.

docs.title: Underground
docs.text:
Early in the ceasefire he is part of Carl's hunting party into the newly-tacked-on wilderness, where his usefulness is entirely subterranean. He buries himself in the ground and blends with it so thoroughly that Carl ends up standing on top of him without knowing — "I felt strange about standing directly atop him, but he insisted it didn't bother him" — and calls the timing of an incoming boss from below: "It's different. It's slower. It's still fast, but it's slower." He drags three skunks under the earth by their legs, then rides out the mob's stink attack buried:

Chris: I am buried. Tell me when it's safe to come up. I can smell it even down here.

He is one of only a handful of the party who avoid the debuff entirely. Bodi, the Land War veteran, is the only person in the book quiet enough to make Chris "seem downright chatty."

docs.title: Imani
docs.text:
The book's biggest revelation about Chris is not about Chris at all, and he never learns it. Carl and Katia take dream potions together and Carl's mind briefly slips its bindings, flooding into everyone in the room. He catches a fragment of each of them — Mordecai's bottomless sadness, Rosetta's tired rage, Edgar's fear and wonder — and then he lands on Imani C, and gets far more than a fragment:

She was in love with Chris, and I had no idea. She loved his simplicity. His quiet kindness.

It felt so private, so dirty for me to have learned about this in such a way. Like I had broken into her house and spied her utterly naked, all without her knowing.

Carl never tells either of them. See Imani C for the scene from her side.

The only thing in the book that touches it is a moment Carl watches from the outside, on the field, just before the Madness castle raid:

I watched as Imani walked up and gave Chris a quick hug using her wings, not her arms. Chris reached up, as if to touch her face, but stopped just short.

docs.title: The Ball
docs.text:
Chris is among the thousands swept up by the war mages' Witness spell and then rolled into Donut's Rolling Battle Formation ball. His one line to her afterwards, while she is apologising to everyone in chat, is the most forceful thing he says all book:

Chris: The Witness spell was just as bad as being controlled by Maggie. You saved us.

docs.title: Exit
docs.text:
At the stairwell down to Floor 10 he leaves with Britney, who "said she was contemplating a deal, but was afraid and would probably be back. She went in with Chris." The book does not say what Chris himself decided.

Sourced from Book 1: The Apocalypse Will Be Televised, Book 3: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook, Book 4: The Gate of the Feral Gods, Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride, and Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Circe Took
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: Elite / Hive queen (mantis) — also functions as an avatar of the deity Diwata
  • Race: Mantis (Dark Hive)
  • Role: Businesswoman/hive queen; owns an amusement park; moderates a CrawlCon panel
  • Family: Mother of Vrah and Xindy (killed by Carl), plus several other mantis daughters
  • Status: Deceased — killed by her own children during the Butcher's Masquerade's final battle
  • Notable spells/abilities: Sponsors and briefly possesses the shapeshifting fertility deity Diwata, gaining a 250-level, nominally-immortal divine form for the duration of the possession
  • Notable items: None named

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Circe Took is a mantis hive queen — not part of the Dark Hive's military or the aggressive "Burrower" clan, but a "businesswoman" who owns an amusement park and moderates panels at CrawlCon. She's introduced moderating a live convention panel on the history of the crawl, lecturing at length until Carl derails it by pointing out her own daughter is one of the hunters gunning for him. She reacts with theatrical, controlled fury throughout the panel, at one point slicing a table in half with her natural bladed forearms — a demonstration of the same weapon her daughter Vrah uses to decapitate crawlers.

docs.title: Becoming Diwata
docs.text: After Carl infects Vrah with the Arrow of Enthusiastic Double Gonorrhea, Circe sponsors the shapeshifting fertility deity Diwata, a minor deity of nature and fertility capable of changing sex and species at will. Diwata first manifests in the realm by being born, unbeknownst to onlookers, through a hunter tricked into acting as her birthing vessel during a temple explosion in a small Ursine settlement; she then shapeshifts into a male mantis to mate with and cure Vrah off-page, before turning female and exploiting a loophole in her own summoning spell — because the possession only ends once the birthing stops, she stays manifest for days by compulsively, continuously giving birth to an unending stream of mantis nymphs, eventually flooding the High Elf castle with them (Vrah's own siblings-slash-children) during the Butcher's Masquerade's climax, to the horror of everyone watching. Circe is effectively trapped in the form for the rest of the battle, unable to access any other divine power while doing so.

docs.title: Death
docs.text:
Samantha, tasked with keeping the hunters' magic-blocking soul crystals from being reactivated by the approaching Diwata, ends up using the crystals themselves as an improvised weapon when Diwata breaks into the security room — the resulting explosion destroys all the crystals and knocks Diwata unconscious, but doesn't end the possession or stop the births. Moments later, Donut's Laundry Day spell — trained to 9, boosted to 12 with a Pawna's Cries potion, then overshot to 17 with the more powerful Pawna's Tears potion (well past the level 15 actually required) — targets the mortal underneath the divine "armor," banishing Diwata back to the Halls of the Ascendency and leaving Circe stripped of her stolen protection, back in mortal, birthing-mantis form. Before Carl can strike the killing blow, a dozen of Circe's own mantis children turn on her and tear her apart, apparently enraged rather than grateful. She dies screaming Carl's name.

Sourced from Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade.

docs.title: Colonel Boomer
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: Former crawler — a tenner — serving as a Colonel in the Princess Posse. On Carl's interface he reads as "This is a subordinate."
  • Race: Elf. Carl's reaction on meeting him: "I would never have guessed he was an elf."
  • Class: Legate — "it allowed him to buff a large number of soldiers at once"
  • Subclass: None stated
  • Level: 62
  • Role: Field commander of the 106th Bloody Leeches battalion — warriors, trap mechanics and thieves. Carl hands him operational command of two of the war's major offensives
  • Notable spells/abilities: No named spell is printed. His stated function is mass buffing across a large body of troops
  • Notable items: "a pair of war gauntlets similar to my Grull gauntlet" — never named or statted. Plus the cigar, which he chews all through the planning and lights only on the "go" order
  • Status: Alive — last seen in the epilogue, off the floor and back in orbit aboard the Crest behemoth Homecoming Queen

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Boomer is the professional soldier the Princess Posse did not otherwise have. Carl first hears of him as a name on the order of battle — "the 106th Bloody Leeches, which was currently led by a former crawler I didn't know named Boomer" (Chapter 21) — and meets him the following chapter in a fortified bunker on the southern front, leaning over a map.

“The leeches are in place,” Colonel Boomer said, chomping on his unlit cigar. “Ready to pluck some cheese sticks.” I examined the man. He was a grizzled, old elf that had survived one of the earliest seasons of Dungeon Crawler World. He looked like someone had taken the world’s fattest bulldog, pickled it for about 5,000 years, gave him elf ears, and then shoved a cigar in his mouth. I would never have guessed he was an elf. He looked as solid as he was old. He had a voice to match.

Boomer. Elven Legate. Level 62.

Colonel in the Princess Posse.

This is a subordinate.

His class caused confusion at first — "His class of “Legate” led to some confusion, but it allowed him to buff a large number of soldiers at once." Tipid put him in charge of the 106th immediately, "and the soldiers all loved him." He is the only figure in the army who talks to Carl the way an actual subordinate commander would, up to and including telling him on the record to stay out of his operation.

Donut, who spends the entire briefing staring at him, files the following report into Carl's private chat:

HE LOOKS LIKE HE MIGHT STINK, BUT HE ACTUALLY SMELLS QUITE NICE. LIKE CEDAR MIXED WITH ACORNS. YOU KNOW, LIKE HOW A GIFTSHOP IN AN EXPENSIVE MOUNTAIN RETREAT WOULD SMELL. DO YOU THINK HE’D BE MAD IF I CALLED HIM ‘POPS?’ HE LOOKS LIKE SOMEONE WHO’D BE CALLED POPS. BOOMER DOESN’T FIT HIM AT ALL. BOOMER SOUNDS LIKE THE NAME OF SOMEONE WHO PEAKED IN HIGH SCHOOL AND NOW SELLS ALUMINUM SIDING. DO YOU THINK HE EVER LIGHTS THAT DISGUSTING CIGAR? BECAUSE THAT WOULD JUST RUIN IT.

He does light it — once, at the end of the briefing, in a single long puff, followed by "Fuck yeah."

docs.title: What a "Tenner" Is, and Why There Is a Warrant
docs.text:
A tenner is a crawler who took the exit deal rather than continue. The book defines the term twice. Tipid's version, describing the veterans who joined the Posse: "We may be level 60, but each one of us is at least a tenner. We’ve all survived Faction Wars at least once. Or Land War." The narration's version is more precise — "tenners—those who tapped out at the start of the tenth floor".

Boomer's own history, as Tipid relays it:

He was a tenner, someone who’d bowed out on the 10th floor, and he’d survived as a merchant on the sixth floor for many, many seasons before finally escaping. He’d been banned from Crawl Con years ago after threatening to “Fist fuck” an orcish show runner to death during a panel. Porthus had publicly distanced himself from the militant, former crawler after that, but apparently, they’d been in close contact the whole time.

The warrant is a separate matter from the Crawl Con ban:

There was an active warrant for the old man’s arrest after a deadly waystation brawl a few cycles back. A brawl that had started after an argument about the crawl. He’d killed someone and had disappeared into the ether. The man had become a legend after that.

The whole veteran contingent is in a comparable position. When Donut asks "So, are you like fugitives? Are they going to swoop in and arrest everyone at any moment?", Rosetta answers that once they are inside the game there is nothing the Syndicate can do: "They’ll wait until we get out to try to arrest us."

docs.title: The Southern Offensive
docs.text:
The first operation Boomer field-commands is the attack out of the southern trench line into naga territory, against the dug-in Prism, Dream and Madness forces (Chapters 22–25). He plans it in the bunker with Tran of the 102nd Bulwark Battalion, working from Elle McGibbons's reconnaissance. His contribution is threat assessment: the Dream's bombardiers will run if you get near their trebuchets and will have ringed them with traps; the real danger is the Epitome household guard, whose "security forces are all veterans of non-dungeon conflicts and are tough as gristle"; and the invisible Madness infiltrators are called the Monkeywrenchers — "A few seasons back, a group of 20 of them single-handedly took the Dreadnaught and Naga castles during the first few hours."

Once the crater-and-Build Trench breach works and the enemy front line collapses, Carl leaves for the Blood Sultanate castle and the system hands the battle over (Chapter 25):

The command of this assault has been transferred to Colonel Boomer.

Colonel Boomer: Quit yer celebrating, all. Nobody fights harder than someone that’s trapped. Only a few of them will be dumb enough to jump into that middle trench. I need you to form up. Don’t push too hard. We don’t want them surrendering. We want them thinking it’s a stalemate. Generals, you guys have maybe a half of an hour before they either escape or we gotta kill all of them.

The 106th converts the surviving mercenaries — "Luckily, the NPC mercenaries were happy to accept their new colors" — and Boomer immediately proposes exploiting the hole: "We can probably push to the Blood Sultanate castle while you have our back covered." Carl refuses. Boomer's reply is a single word: "Understood." Carl concedes in narration that Boomer was right, that taking the naga castle "would’ve been the safest and smartest play," and that "I didn’t care."

docs.title: The Reaver Assault
docs.text:
The second offensive is his own from the start. In the master plan for the general offensive (Chapter 59) the assignments are "Florin will deal with the orcs, Boomer with the Reavers, Donut with the Dream, and my task is the Madness." Rosetta is the designated "Theater Commander," meaning she is in charge of coordinating it all. Boomer opens his part in Chapter 62:

Boomer: Starting our raid on the Reaver castle. Bomo and Sledge. Initiate the barrage.

When Carl tries to divert Louis Santiago's bomber away from a dragon circling the objective, Boomer sends the sharpest rebuke anyone gives Carl in the book (Chapter 63):

Colonel Boomer: Warlord. We need those bombs dropped. We don’t have No Disassemble missiles to kill their electronics. If you call General Louis off his run, that puts the rest of us in danger. I know he’s your friend. But we can’t do this without air support. He’s a good pilot. He knows what he’s doing. And with all due respect, you handed operational command over to Rosetta after you put me in charge of the Reaver assault. You need to focus on your own operation, not mine. I’ll try to get close enough to mark the dragon for a missile barrage, but you can’t call off his run just because it’s dangerous.

Carl's narration: "Goddamnit. He was right, and I knew it." He countermands himself — "This is Boomer’s op and listen to him from now on" — and Louis flies the run. The run is what kills Party Planner and strands Louis inside the Reaver castle for most of the rest of the book.

Boomer is still "pushing against the front door of the Reavers" when the goddess Eris casts Bring Forth the Witnesses and freezes most of the army; Rosetta's report is "Boomer, Tran, and Bodi aren’t answering, either." He survives it, and by the Peeling phase he is back on the work detail with Florin, Bodi, Britney and Rosetta, clearing lava damage and repairing the city's defensive ring.

Order of battle

The 106th Bloody Leeches is one of several numbered Princess Posse battalions, alongside the 102nd Bulwark, the 101st, the 103rd Recon Legionnaires and the 104th Naughty Little Piggies. The army's structure is out of scope for this page.

docs.title: "Time to Bring the War Out of the Dungeon"
docs.text:
Boomer returns in the epilogue, which is told from the point of view of York, the tenodera poet left alone aboard the Crest behemoth Homecoming Queen in orbit. York's ship is secretly armed: "not only was the ship well-armed, but it had a full complement of enhancement zone guns and beams. Highly regulated, high-energy weapons that would normally only work in the center system. Porthus had ordered them installed." Those weapons are now "green across the board, making Homecoming Queen likely the strongest ship in orbit."

Boomer calls in to dock — visibly aged — and needles York about poetry:

Boomer grinned at him over the display. “Roses are red. Violets are blue. We won Faction Wars. Now we get to kill more of them.”

“That is a terrible poem, Boomer.”

Then he asks after the equipment. As he does, a pre-recorded broadcast from Porthus goes out announcing the formation of a new militant group that will move against Syndicate government property and systems across the known universe unless the crawl is stopped.

York clicked a button. “Not only are the breaching suits ready, Boomer. But the enhancement zone suits appear to be online and working, just like Porthus predicted. And the power armor is all online as well.”

“Fuck yeah,” Boomer said, popping a cigar into his mouth. “Set aside four of the Cronus suits and a landing skiff. We have a pregnant veteran on the surface who needs backup. And for the rest of us, it’s time to bring the war out of the dungeon. Better warm up the lasers.”

Cronus-class power armor is established earlier in the book as the heavy gear the Reaver security cyborgs were specifically not allowed to bring into the dungeon: "If I’d allowed them all to come in here with their heavy duty, Cronus-class power armor, they’d already be putting those collectible, heart-covered boxers on clearance in all waystation gift shops across the galaxy."

Unresolved

The "pregnant veteran on the surface who needs backup" is never identified in Book 7, and neither is the target of "phase two." Boomer's remark that "we made some friends down there, and this next part isn’t going to be nearly as difficult as we originally thought" is likewise left hanging.

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Corcunda
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: NPC — a half-mantaur stripper and Dong Quixote's long-lost lover, magically split years ago into two separate half-bodies
  • Race: Mantaur, split by a spell called Split Personality — "right down the center, right between the eyes and all the way down through the groin." Each half stands on one leg and has one full arm plus one exposed half-arm
  • Class/Subclass: Not stated
  • Level: Not stated
  • Religion: A worshipper of the war god Grull before the split; the devotion lapsed while he was divided, which Grull later treats as apostasy
  • Notable spells/abilities: None of his own; his reunification is performed on him by the fleshmancer Grigori the Placid
  • Notable items: None described
  • Status: Deceased — smitten by Grull for "failing in faith" moments after being made whole, and dies in Heat 5 of Floor 10 charging the god alongside Dong Quixote, lance in hand

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Corcunda is Floor 10's emotional centerpiece: a captive split in half years before the book opens, found in two pieces on the racetrack, reunited by a hired fleshmancer mid-race, and killed by his own god within minutes of being whole again — taking Dong Quixote, the man who never stopped looking for him, down with him.

docs.title: Corky, Porky, and the Gimp
docs.text:
He is first spotted in Chapter 13 (Heat 2) as "the gimp" — a full-body vinyl suit worn to keep his organs sealed in, listed as the property of the womantaur team Genesis and Rapture ("Lady Dominators and the Gimp"). Razor fox Chiyome explains the mechanic on sight:

"There is a spell called Split Personality. Cuts you right down the middle... They can come together and get reglued with a fleshmancer."

Donut is the one who puts the name to the face:

"So, do you think that's Dong Quixote's friend? The half-mantaur he's always talking about? What was his name? Corcunda?"

The system opens a two-part quest on the spot: reunite Dong with the half he's found (Corky), then locate the other half — nicknamed Porky, who is "also somewhere on this floor" — and find a fleshmancer willing to put the two of them back together. Porky turns out to be hiding elsewhere on Floor 10, running a hidden stage-performance guild. Carl decides not to tell Dong Quixote what they've found until the reunion is actually possible, worried the reveal is a setup: "If it is Dong's long-lost partner or whatever, they put him here to fuck with us and the team... If we get involved, it's going to backfire."

docs.title: Grigori the Placid
docs.text: The party hires the fleshmancer Grigori the Placid specifically for this quest. He admits up front he has never actually completed a reunion like this before — "It is quite rare for two halfsies to survive more than a few minutes... so I haven't had the opportunity" — and, in the run-up, never thinks to ask whether either half still worships a god. That oversight is what kills him.

docs.title: The Reunion
docs.text:
The two halves come together mid-race in Heat 5, inside a collapsing steel-mill/gasworks track, while the truck is sliding sideways through molten metal. Grigori has Dong and Donut strip both halves out of their containment suits and wrap the exposed half-brains in plastic wrap to keep them sealed, then physically press the torsos together:

"Okay, hold them together!" Grigori yelled... Grigori cast something, and the guts, dangling from Porky's exposed double torsos, floated by his side... I finally saw both of their faces and half-mullets. They looked just like any other mantaur, only just cut in half.

Dong holds them together bodily through the whole procedure:

"I have you," Dong shouted... "I have you, and I will never let go again!"

The joining itself is rendered as a system effect — two health bars, each in the red, merging into one:

The two halves, Corky and Porky, still had health bars over each half, also in the red, but as I watched, the health bars joined, and they became one. Their names disappeared and a single name reappeared. Corcunda.

Whole, he has "a bright red jagged scar right down the middle of his face and chest," not perfectly aligned, with little bulges along the seam. (The text uses male pronouns for Corcunda throughout — for both halves and for the fused whole — and Dong Quixote's own address to him, "my love," is unambiguous about the relationship. An earlier revision of this page used she/her; that was an error.)

His first words as a single being are not relief. They're a warning:

"Hail! Grull has come for me," Corcunda groaned as he helped Dong up. His voice remained the same as before, though his mannerisms were suddenly much more mantaur-like. "I thought I was free of the vile god when I split, but the moment I came back together, he sent me a message and told me I was to be punished for not being troo!"

docs.title: Apostasy
docs.text:
Grull's own words to him make the charge explicit — not heresy toward a rival god, but abandoned loyalty during the years he spent split and unable to worship at all:

"Corcunda, you have failed in your faith, and now you must be punished. You cannot hide. You cannot flee. Accept your punishment like the warrior you once were."

Grigori takes the blame on himself:

"I should have asked if you worshipped a deity before you split. I apologize for my oversight."

docs.title: The Charge
docs.text:
Corcunda refuses Donut's offer to fight the god in his place, and turns to Dong instead:

"You worried if I would no longer love you once I returned to this form. But how could I not?... You have been nothing but a shining light in my life, and I want to thank you for always holding true. But now I have to go to Grull. The only way he will leave is once I am properly smitten."

He strips off the only thing he's wearing — Dong's own scarf, passed to Porky's half years earlier — and returns it to him. Dong's answer:

"My love," he said, "do you really think I will ever leave your side again?"

Dong draws the massive lance he keeps in his inventory — a weapon Carl notes he hasn't seen since the day he handed Dong the sentient sock Jefferson — and says, "It's been a long time since I've tilted a giant." Corcunda kneels on his middle arms so Dong can ride him one last time: "Hail, my love... It will be an honor to be ridden one last time."

The magnet: Donut casts her Big-Ass Magnet spell onto Dong's lance to punch through the horde of slag elementals between them and the god — the room floor is littered with millions of loose screws from a shattered crate, and the enchantment drags every screw within 200 metres of the lance toward it as they close the distance, shredding the elementals in their path. Donut's warning: "It has to be cast on an object!... It will activate right away, but it will increase in intensity for about fifteen seconds after I place it, so make sure you're far away from us or else the lance will get ripped from your hand!"

Dong's goodbye, given before the charge:

"Goodbye, Carl. Goodbye, Princess Donut," Dong said. "Please tell the others that I will miss them, but I will see them again on the other side. Tell them it was my pleasure to serve with them. Vale to you all. Vale."

And then the charge itself:

And with a terrifying, in-unison roar, Corcunda and Dong jumped from the back of the truck and galloped directly at Grull just as the magnet spell activated. Every screw within two hundred meters of the lance jumped into the air and rocketed toward the charging pair... And through it all, Dong and Corcunda charged. They charged, and they charged. Riding into battle one last time. Dong Quixote, now with his lance lowered, now getting peppered himself with dozens, then hundreds, then thousands of screws, roared in triumph as the weapon made contact with the god of war.

Grull, unkilled but visibly moved, withdraws rather than press further:

"A good death," Grull rumbled before he vanished, going back to the twelfth floor. "A good death indeed."

Both Corcunda and Dong Quixote are confirmed dead in the same breath the race ends. Carl: "Dong Quixote was dead. I took a breath, letting it sink in. What a way to go. What a goddamned hero." Donut: "Dong is dead... He was my friend, and he's dead." The Heat 5 results board lists it plainly: Eliminated: Lady Dominators and the Gimp.

The quest-completion text underlines the timing: "Not only did you get them back together, but you did it before Dong died."

Grigori offers the only comfort given afterward: "Some of us believe that death is nothing but movement on to another plane of existence. Dong did not think this was the end."

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Grigori the Placid — the fleshmancer who reunited him, and blames himself for not checking his faith status first
  • Princess Donut — casts the Big-Ass Magnet spell that gets the charge home
  • Carl — narrates the reunion and death; hides the discovery from Dong until it's real
  • Supporting cast — for Dong Quixote, Genesis and Rapture, and Chiyome

Sourced from Book 8: A Parade of Horribles.

docs.title: Damascus Steel
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: NPC — Desperado Club staff; functionally the doorkeeper of the Guild of Suffering
  • Race: Ifrit — "Where there is sin, there are Ifrit." Metal to the touch but skin to the eye, smoke leaking from his skin and from empty white eye sockets, small goat-like horn stubs, heavy old scarring "like he'd once been raked by giant talons"
  • Level: 75
  • Role: Assistant lead dancer at the Penis Parade, the Desperado Club male strip club that fronts the Guild of Suffering
  • Family: Son of Astrid and the Night Wyrm (real name Hamed); brother of Anaconda, a Level 75 Quarter Naga and one of the club's lead dancers. Neither brother was ever a crawler; both parents were
  • Notable spells/abilities: None shown in combat — the system's warning is simply "Try not to get into a fight with this guy because he'll fuck you up"
  • Notable items: The spiderweb elbow tattoo of the Guild of Suffering — the same mark Carl carries, and the credential that gets Carl through the door
  • Status: Alive, and gone. Leaves with Anaconda in Chapter 34 to kill their father; the outcome is not shown in Book 6

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Damascus is the older, stoic one: he drinks tea at the end of the bar with a book, facing away from the crowd, in an Aladdin-style vest and pants, and Dong Quixote introduces him to Carl as "the cranky one." Donut, who knows the club's dancers far better than Carl does, has been telling him about Damascus for two books — she once informed him he was Mongo's new daddy.

docs.title: The Door
docs.text:
The whole strip club is a front. The entrance to the Guild of Suffering is a hidden portal in the last privacy cubicle in the corner of the Penis Parade, and Damascus controls it.

Carl doesn't have a password; he leads with a social credential instead — "I'm not looking for a dance. We have a few mutual friends, one of whom is Donut." Damascus reads the spiderweb tattoo on Carl's elbow, the twin of his own, and answers: "Carl… I'm glad you've come to visit. Donut speaks highly of you." A pause. "As does Katia." Then: "Walk with me."

He escorts Carl to the corner cubicle with a theatrical bow, holds the door, slaps his ass on the way in, locks the club door behind them and opens the secret portal with his hand:

Entering the Guild of Suffering.

Welcome, spider. Welcome home.

His only impatience with Carl's hesitation is professional: "Why are you just standing there? Don't be a coward. Go in, get it over with, and come out. I have a reputation to maintain, so you must hurry." He also requires Carl to limp on the way back out, on pain of a broken knee — to preserve the cover story.

Wording

"Gatekeeper" is an accurate description of the function, not a title the book uses for him.

docs.title: The Realization
docs.text:
Carl and Katia take a Guild of Suffering contract without knowing the target. The target is Astrid. After she dies, Carl finds Damascus sitting on the floor of the club with his face in his hands, sizzling tears peppering the floor around him, Anaconda weeping beside him. Astrid was their mother. The Night Wyrm — the guild's own patron, who issued the contract — is their father, and is still married to her.

"I didn't know who you were assigned to kill," he said. "I don't blame you for what happened. But I do blame him. We were promised freedom. He wanted to make sure she was dead. They're still married. My mother has—had—so much, and the guild, it's rarely found by crawlers. He gets it all. He'll have it all when we get out."

Carl's reading, later: the family's indenture contract was almost up. If Astrid died inside the game, her husband would inherit everything on the outside. Katia's summary: "So you think he had us murder her in the game for real-life money? That's diabolical."

Damascus also lets slip how big this really is, then immediately shuts it down: "We have no time… And I've already gotten a warning to shut up about this. There's more of us than you know. Anaconda and I are just two of thousands."

docs.title: The Mercenaries
docs.text:
Before he goes, Damascus makes Carl take his people.

With Astrid dead the club will close for "remodeling," a new assistant manager will be assigned, and the whole Penis Parade crew — the dancers Damascus personally recruited, and who only counted as safe because Astrid quietly parked a Meat Shields office inside the club — will be reassigned to the Larracos Meat Shields and thrown into Faction Wars on somebody else's side.

He grabbed my arm and leaned in. His grip was like an iron clamp. "You owe me," he whispered. "They will not survive this. You have to get them out of here. I convinced them to come, to work in this place… If you don't take them now, you'll end up fighting against them on the ninth floor."

The mechanism: they all still hold Meat Shields memberships, so Carl can hire them on his mercenary coupon on a two-floor contract, approved on the spot by Rosemarie, the elderly dwarf secretly managing the club's shadow Meat Shields office. Price: 100,000 gold.

Fifteen transfer to Carl's personal-space barracks immediately — thirteen male strippers plus Doctor Bones the skeleton DJ and Bucket Boy the crocodilian. Only the men of the Penis Parade were eligible; the women of Bitches and the middle-floor clubs are left behind. Several of them — Dong Quixote, Doctor Bones, Splash Zone, Steve the troll — become significant to the Cuba endgame, and Doctor Bones's Super Spreader is what creates the sluggalo army.

docs.title: Leaving
docs.text:
"Brother, what are you doing?" [Anaconda asked.]

Damascus turned and put his hand on the other stripper's shoulder… "I'm going to avenge our mother. He won't win."

The snake-like dancer looked up at his brother… "If you're going to fight him, I'm going, too."

"Me, too!" called Dong Quixote.

"No," Anaconda said without turning his head. "This is family business."

The two brothers walk into the back cubicle without another word to anyone. Neither is seen again in Book 6, and the confrontation with the Night Wyrm is never shown. Donut's reaction to the mercenaries arriving is genuine and slightly heartbroken: "OMG, CARL. THIS IS THE GREATEST THING SINCE YOU HIRED SLEDGIE… I'M SAD ANACONDA AND STEELIE AREN'T HERE, THOUGH."

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: Elle McGibbons
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: Crawler
  • Race/Class: Frost Maiden Blizzardmancer → Tundra Princess (Floor 6 specialty) → Hailstorm Queen (Book 7, Floor 9 — she picked wind)
  • Age (pre-collapse): 99
  • Level: 13 by end of Book 2 (10th on the Floor 3 leaderboard); 72 after Graupel in Book 6. Not stated anywhere in Book 7
  • Party: Independent; closely allied with Carl's party and Imani C/Li Jun's group on Floor 4. General in the Princess Posse (Book 7)
  • Role (Book 7): Deep-penetration scout and missile spotter for the Posse's artillery
  • Notable spells/abilities: High-speed flight (well beyond her normal limit when pushed with a scroll); freeze-based attacks, effective at turning caustic Krakaren acid pools solid so they can be safely cleared; Graupel (Book 6); Subterfuge (Book 7), which hides a whole party from enemy detection
  • Notable items: Not described in detail beyond her Frost Maiden gear. She carried the Gate of the Feral Gods through the first half of Book 7 and no longer has it — it was taken from her hands in chapter 61

docs.title: From Meadow Lark's Elder to Floor 4's Wisecracking Scout
docs.text: Introduced in Book 1 as one of the elderly "Meadow Lark" evacuees under Brandon An, Elle McGibbons became an unlikely Book 2 leaderboard entry (10th place, Level 13, Frost Maiden Blizzardmancer) after starting the season at Level 1. By Book 3 she's a fully fleshed-out, foul-mouthed, and fiercely loyal member of Carl's extended circle — no longer a background survivor but one of the floor's most active scouts and problem-solvers.

docs.title: Role in the Floor 4 Crisis
docs.text: Elle serves as the group's fastest long-range scout and messenger throughout the Iron Tangle disaster, repeatedly flying at speeds well past her normal limit (at one cost of a "precious scroll") to relay intel, hunt down missing crawlers (including a fruitless search for Eva Sigrid on Carl's behalf), and freeze pools of caustic acid blood so defenders can safely clear chokepoints. She talks Carl down from confrontations as often as she escalates them, and delivers some of the book's driest commentary on the chaos around her ("Sometimes I think you're cheating, Carl. How do you know all this stuff?").

docs.title: Personality and Background
docs.text: Sharp-tongued, protective, and openly affectionate with Carl and Donut despite the constant ribbing — she kisses Carl on the cheek after a risky flying maneuver and needles him relentlessly about his tendency to cause (and then have to explain) enormous explosions. She mentions a boyfriend before her current partner "Barry" in passing, and coined the nickname "ghoul coaster" for the improvised, monster-infested escape route crawlers without portal hats are forced to use at the abyss.

docs.title: Book 5 Notes
docs.text: Elle picks a Tundra Princess floor specialty on Floor 6, blending her Frost Maiden ice magic with an earth-based build; Mordecai notes she's quietly pursuing a rare "four seasons" build that requires surviving to Floor 12 with tightly controlled stat allocation. She fights alongside Katia's splinter team through the floor's hunter war, personally interrogates a grieving hunter at the Butcher's Masquerade about the circumstances of Diwata's forced "birth" from his brother, and survives the climactic battle.

docs.title: Six Levels in One Cast
docs.text:
During the assault on the FOCSA building, with a wave of demons closing on the alley where Donut is rooted mid-cast, Elle uses the one spell she's been saving — Graupel, a war spell with a one-week cooldown that she has cast exactly once before in her life.

"Oh shit, oh shit," Elle shouted as the blue glow around her increased in intensity. "Guys, it says it's casting more powerful than usual. Holy shit, head's up!"

Fist-sized hail comes down hard enough to make the asphalt explode and the ground shake like an earthquake. Almost every red dot on Carl's map turns to an X. When the steam clears there is a knee-high field of melting ice and mangled demon corpses as far as he can see.

Elle remained in place as level notifications pinged over and over above her head, settling her onto level 72. She'd risen six levels at once.

"What the hell? That spell is strong, but it's not usually that strong. It's only level five. It said it cast at level 16."

Unresolved

Nothing explains the amplification. Samantha, who can enhance spells, says flatly "I didn't do that," and then breaks into an incoherent rant about Elle being "on the four seasons path," a tree, a river, and "maybe the prince's spell enhanced her." The book never resolves it. See Samantha.

docs.title: Second Voice
docs.text:
Elle spends Book 6 as the person who says the thing everyone else is thinking. She is the one who interrogates Carl's escape plan on the floor's behalf — "What the hell, Carl? Are you blowing smoke up our ass? Is this a sure thing, or are you working off a Carl theory?" and "That's the whole message? Don't fight? Isolate the stairwells? You're gonna have to give us more than that, cowboy. People are terrified. They're gonna need a solid reason." — and then she and Katia go out and sell it to the rest of the dungeon.

She is also the one who states the guild's position on Carl's self-sacrifice plans: "That's not how this works, Carl. You were right, what you said in your little speech. We're all in this together. We're all screwed if we don't all make it to the next floor." And she is the only person Imani will talk to after Imani's squad dies.

Wording

The book never labels Elle second-in-command. The role is visible in what she does, not in a title.

docs.title: Hailstorm Queen
docs.text:
Floor 9 forces another class selection, and Elle reports it in chat before Carl has even finished reading his own notifications:

Elle: Hey guys, what’d I miss? I just had to go through class selection again. There were only a few of us in the warehouse this time. I picked wind. I went from Tundra Princess to Hailstorm Queen.

Donut: YOU’RE A QUEEN? THAT’S GREAT!

Elle: Yeah. This is probably as far as it’s gonna get. I can add the final element if I ever make it to the 12th floor, but I’m betting this whole shitshow self-destructs before we even get close.

No class description is printed

The system never prints a description card for Hailstorm Queen anywhere in Book 7. The chat lines above are the entire text on the subject. What the class does has to be read off what she does with it — ice spells, flight, and the four-seasons progression she has been chasing since Book 5, which she now confirms needs the 12th floor to complete.

Her manager this floor is Mistress Tiatha, a drunk half-elf who spends the book being useful anyway: she trains Imani on battlefield enhancement spells, and it is Tiatha, not Carl, who invents the detonation-wire exploit used in the Club Vanquisher raid.

docs.title: Scout and spotter
docs.text:
Elle is the Posse's eyes past the wire for the entire floor. She maps both enemy borders, counts the Dream's artillery ("approximately 40 of the big trebuchets set up and dozens of the small ones"), watches a hundred Madness soldiers go invisible, and reports it all in real time. Her running commentary is unchanged from Book 3:

Elle: Holy cannoli, guys. These bald elf pricks have all sorts of hardware out here… Why are they allowed to have so many of these things when we can’t?

The spotter role is the new one. When Louis's airship goes in, Elle is the one lasing the anti-air batteries for Carl's missiles:

Elle: I have the first anti-air gun targeted. I hope this missile launcher of yours works as advertised, Carl. Firing the moment Louis drops.

Elle: The second anti-air battery is down! Louis, hurry your ass up! The first one is almost back up. I’m running. They have a pair of mages on my scent.

Later, outside the Madness castle, she calls in cheese cutters — the anti-personnel, shrapnel-filled missiles — against a charging column of hundreds of carts. She also carries Subterfuge, a concealment spell that covers everyone standing inside it:

Your platoon member, General Elle McGib has cast a Subterfuge spell, and your presence is hidden from enemy eyes. Do not venture from the area of the spell, or the Madness will be automatically warned of your incursion.

docs.title: Losing the Gate
docs.text:
Elle is the Posse's gate operator. She carries the Gate of the Feral Gods through the middle of the book and works it like artillery — walking it from front to front and dropping a feral god on each enemy castle in turn.

General Elle: Gate one is open, and I’m stepping through. Let’s see what comes out of this one. Next stop, the Reavers. Don’t be late, Carl.

Gate one lands Meatus beside the Dream castle while the Dream's army is out in the field, which Rosetta calls immediately: "Yes! Good job, Elle. The Dream have made a tactical error leaving their castle unprotected." The Reavers are supposed to be next, and Carl is supposed to meet her there off Louis's bombing run.

Chapter 61 goes wrong in stages. The volcano the Posse detonated erupts harder than the dwarves predicted, knocks over her winding box, spills the watches, and fires the gate early, putting a twenty-minute clock on it. Then a search spell strips her Subterfuge. Then King Stalwart — the new leader of the Skull Empire, fleeing a losing battle with Donut's magic missiles in him — teleports directly onto her position, bringing a squad of war mages with him.

Elle: Carl! Stalwart is here!

I ran toward the commotion, preparing to use my Wraith Phase. As I rushed forward, Elle flew past me, flying over my shoulder, having been tossed by a spell. I saw the Unconscious tag over her head. She hit a tree behind me with a sickening crack, and the tree toppled over.

She got one spell off first — Carl arrives to a clearing under quickly-melting ice and four dead war mages, killed by Donut's amped-up Magic Missile on the way in. The surviving mages are not there for Elle. They tear King Stalwart apart in front of Carl ("My sister was right," he says, before he explodes), and their leader turns out to be holding her gate.

He had taken the Gate of the Feral Gods from Elle.

The war mage was staring at my bare feet.

“Nice shoes, asshole,” he said to me before the four of them teleported away.

Elle's own account, once she comes round, is one line:

Elle: Sorry guys. That war mage prick snatched the gate right out of my hands.

Her next words are operational — "Carl, collect the bodies. They said the heads explode" — and then she is back on her feet inside ten minutes and re-casting Subterfuge. The loss wrecks the plan; when the fallback comes up later she is blunt about it: "It’s not really Plan B if we don’t have the feral god gate." See Akuma for the war mage who took it.

docs.title: Kept alive on purpose
docs.text:
Long after the theft, Akuma opens a warlord chat to ask Carl to kill "that old lady" for him. Donut assumes he means Elle and objects. He does not:

Warlord Akuma: Is Elle the one on the Four Seasons path? Not her, dipshit. Keep her alive if you wish for us to face Scolopendra and survive. Agatha. The other warlord we were forced to accept in order to gain system access.

It is the strongest statement anyone has made about Elle's build. The most powerful non-god caster on the floor regards her four-seasons progression as load-bearing for surviving Scolopendra, and says so unprompted to the enemy.

docs.title: Elsewhere on the floor
docs.text:
• She and Edgar penetrate naga territory ahead of Operation Snake Pit and find the barracks full of rotting corpses — the discovery that the Blood Sultanate's army is already dead, killed by Prepotente.
  • She leads the four-cart infiltration team into the naga stronghold with Imani, sweeps it, and takes the throne room.
  • She argues hard for giving Li Na the spare Ring of Divine Suffering, over Imani's objection.
  • She is frozen with everyone else by the Bear Witness spell, and gives Donut the plainest account of what Donut's War Crime actually saved them from: "it was like we were paralyzed, and we could feel everything, but we couldn’t move. It was awful."
  • She helps hold the extracted naiad organs during Louis's transplant, and leads a flight of fairies icing over the lava pooling in the upper levels of Larracos.
  • She is in the tent for Katia's goodbye — "Damnit, kiddo. Don’t make me cry." — and is alive at the end of the book.

Her register has not moved an inch in six books. On being knocked unconscious into a tree: "Damn, I haven’t been walloped like that since my bachelorette party."

docs.title: Cracking Akuma
docs.text:
In Chapter 37, Carl's group ambushes Akuma at a Floor 10 upgrade shop after he sends Carl a cryptic note about the Pineapple Cabaret. Elle, still owed payback for having the Gate of the Feral Gods torn out of her hands back in Book 7, does the interrogating personally — freezing one of his testicles solid with an ice bolt the instant Donut mutes him, then leaning in for the reunion she never got to have:

"Hey, remember me, you barely sapient magical fart?" Elle said, getting close to Akuma, whose sneering expression had turned to a look of extreme, gasping pain. "You and your little asshole friends tried to kill me. You stole the gate from me when I wasn't done with it yet. When I was a kid, do you know what we used to do to people who stole? We would hit them with sticks, and we would throw their shoes into the sound. But that was only because we couldn't get away with more."

The torture works. Held in an anti-magic shield with his health slowly draining, Akuma gives up the existence of Herot — the 16th-edition cookbook author, a skink former crawler still alive and secretly running the Pineapple Cabaret from the inside — along with extensive exposition on the dungeon's "Big Six" power factions (see Akuma for the full lore dump). Elle gets one direct concession out of him for her trouble: he warns Carl elsewhere in the same conversation to keep her alive specifically, because "if you wish for us to face Scolopendra and survive," her progression matters.

docs.title: Linus, Unmasked
docs.text:
