It was just a glimpse, but it was so, so much. She’d fled her home in Detroit, and her older brothers and sisters blamed her for leaving the family. But she had to. She had to get away. She’d earned her nursing certificate and found a job in what she considered the middle of nowhere. A relatively small, beautiful town where drugs and violence and despair were just something one saw on the news. She was always chasing peace despite the overwhelming guilt she carried, like a heavy sack she couldn’t put down. She was sick of being looked at as the one in charge, the one who had to make the tough decisions. She didn’t want that responsibility, yet it always fell to her, despite her always being the youngest one in the room.

She was in love with Chris, and I had no idea. She loved his simplicity. His quiet kindness.

Carl knows immediately that he has done something he cannot undo:

It felt so private, so dirty for me to have learned about this in such a way. Like I had broken into her house and spied her utterly naked, all without her knowing.

She hadn’t invited me into her mind, and I should have looked away. But I couldn’t. I didn’t know how. My only solace was that I knew—somehow I knew—I’d forget much of this when I finally woke up.

He never tells her, and neither of them ever raises it. See Chris Andrews.

Unresolved

Nothing comes of it in Book 7. The closest the two of them get on-page is a single moment before the Madness assault, with both of them expecting to die: "I watched as Imani walked up and gave Chris a quick hug using her wings, not her arms. Chris reached up, as if to touch her face, but stopped just short."

docs.title: Elsewhere on the floor
docs.text:
• She and Elle run the Posse's recruiting for most of the ceasefire.
  • She takes the four-cart infiltration team into the naga stronghold with Elle, sweeping traps by hand because Prepotente scattered the expendable sluggalos that were supposed to go in first.
  • She is the only officer who argues against giving Li Na the spare Ring of Divine Suffering.
  • She is frozen with everyone else by the Bear Witness spell and freed by Donut's War Crime.
  • In the Reaver castle she throws a wing-cast shield none of the party had seen before, covering Elle, Holger and the strippers through a blast, and then wakes Louis from a paralytic.
  • She and Rosetta open Princess Lunette to extract the donor heart and lungs for Louis's transplant, and Imani is the one who places them in his chest: "Organs incoming!"
  • She delivers Kiwi's babies in a tent in the middle of the siege, shouting Bucket Boy out of the room for nearly vomiting.
  • She is in the tent for Katia's goodbye, and alive at the end of the book.

docs.title: Jacobus, Permanently
docs.text:
Imani's tooth-fairy T'Ghee card Jacobus — a Danish-speaking "Reverse Tooth Fairy," level 90, established in Book 7 — is caught in the chaos goddess Eris's Floor 10 visit. One of Eris's random effects makes a nearby temporary condition permanent, and it lands on him:

"I just received a notification that he is now permanently summoned and can no longer be used as a card."

From that point on Jacobus simply follows Imani around as a standing companion rather than a card she can hold in reserve — squirting water in reaction to conversations, delighting openly in Akuma's torture, and no longer something she can put away.

docs.title: A Target
docs.text:
Imani is confirmed as one of the two named targets of the Syndicate assassin Minus, posing as Elle's superfan "Linus" — see Elle McGibbons and Supporting cast for the reveal and unmasking. Carl's own retrospective judgment, once the assassination plot is exposed: "That alien had been correct to target her for assassination... it'd become clear that Imani and Katia were the true bedrocks of our ability to stay organized."

Sourced from Book 1: The Apocalypse Will Be Televised, Book 3: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook, Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade, Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride, Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin, and Book 8: A Parade of Horribles.

docs.title: Jasha and Radoslav
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: NPCs — bugbear musicians, the recurring heart of Team Free Love on Floor 10
  • Race: Bugbear
  • Class/Subclass: Not applicable — non-combatant racers, not crawlers
  • Level: Not stated
  • Team: Team Free Love, a "hippie" van team (tie-dye aesthetic, Pan flute, bongos, tambourine, violin) that races alongside Carl and Donut across every heat of Floor 10; their third original member, Alevtina, dies in a crash during Heat 1
  • Notable spells/abilities: None described — comic-relief racers, not fighters
  • Notable items: A modified van with a floating/hover upgrade
  • Status: Deceased — killed together near the end of Heat 6, by Carl, via a hidden bomb planted in their own beer cooler

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Jasha and Radoslav are Floor 10's longest-running running joke — a pair of tie-dyed bugbear musicians Carl and Donut rescue in the very first heat and keep bumping into, garage to garage, race to race, all the way through Heat 6. Then Carl kills them both on purpose, in cold blood, to buy time for a rescue that has nothing to do with them, and the book asks the reader to sit with exactly how ugly that decision is.

docs.title: Team Free Love
docs.text:
They're introduced in Heat 1 (Chapters 3–4), rescued by Carl and Donut after their minivan crashes; their bandmate and third member, Alevtina, dies in the wreck. Donut's read on them at first glance is "undercover cops" dressed as hippies — bugbears playing Pan flute, bongos, tambourine, and violin, entirely earnest about it. They're heavily implied to be reincarnated or "awakened" NPCs carrying fragmented memories from past lives across other floors, racing purely for the shot at freedom that winning would represent.

From Heat 2 on they're a fixture of the cul-de-sac — beer on the garage lawn chairs, comic sideline commentary on every other team's disasters, a running presence through the alliance that forms around the Heat 2 boss fight. They pitch in without being asked: at the end of Heat 5 they're the ones who find the unconscious, "cheating" unicorn Dwight spinning in circles outside the exit and physically drag him back in, over their own objection ("You really think we should save him? He's the worst one!").

docs.title: The Bomb
docs.text:
The kill happens in Chapter 76, near the end of Heat 6 — a race through a shrunk-down human apartment building, collecting seven hidden gates floor by floor. Carl's team has just cleared its final gate with minutes left on the clock when an ally radios that Prepotente has gone near-suicidal, immobile inside an AI-generated "what-if" vision of his own lonely mother, and someone has to physically go get him (see Prepotente). Carl is the only one who can. Doing it costs time his team does not have — and coming in last, on this heat, is fatal.

This is not a fight, and it is not an accident. It's premeditated triage, planned before the race even started:

"How many NPCs had we killed at this point? What were two more?"

Carl had already infiltrated Team Free Love's cooler on the cul-de-sac before the heat started, using his Oozy Form spell for the first time while Samantha distracted the two bugbears as cover, and swapped one of their peach-flavoured Busch Lights — the flavour nobody ever drinks — for a drilled-out, identical can built in his own "bomber's studio," undetectable without a level-12+ Find Traps skill. An enchanted cooler that automatically returns to their van after every race guarantees the bomb is always in position as a fail-safe. He carries the detonator in his own interface the whole heat, dreading it:

They did not wave, and I did not wave back. We all knew what had to happen next. I felt a chill, looking at them. I had been afraid that the dungeon wouldn't allow me to use my Oozy Form spell in the cul-de-sac, but it had let me. I almost wished it hadn't. Fuck everything about this place.

He detonates it from a distance, mid-crisis, with a single line of narration standing in for everything he doesn't let himself feel in the moment:

I pulled up my explosives menu, scrolled to the Primed subtab, and found the detonator I was looking for. Fuck everything about this place. "Forgive me, friends," I whispered. I clicked Detonate.

The system confirms the kill flatly, folding two names into a bracket update:

Team Free Love has been eliminated due to the death of both racers. Three teams remain in the current heat.

Neither Jasha nor Radoslav gets any final words on the page. There's no cutaway to their side of it — Carl narrates the act retrospectively, analytically, immediately followed by the one line that gives away how little the tactical logic actually helps him:

That was the logic, but it wasn't reality. They were our friends, and I felt like an utter piece of shit. That was the point, of course. But it still hurt. At least it's not another crawler, I thought.

docs.title: Afterward
docs.text:
The reaction is muted rather than confrontational — no one in the party calls Carl out over it on-page. Passing the wreckage of the van on the way out, the only response shown is wordless:

On the way there, in the hallway, we passed the wreckage of team Free Love's van. We'd killed them just before they'd hit the finish line. Donut jumped from the seat and into my lap upon seeing that, and I held her tight as we approached the exit.

Heat 6's final standings list the consequence in the same clinical register as the kill itself: Eliminated: Team Free Love.

A joint page, by design

Jasha and Radoslav are treated here as a single entry rather than two, matching how the text itself handles them — as an inseparable pair, killed in the same instant, credited and mourned as one unit ("both racers"). No distinguishing personality traits or individual dialogue are given to either bugbear separately anywhere in Book 8.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Carl — plans and detonates the bomb; carries the guilt of it silently for the rest of the book
  • Prepotente — the rescue that makes the bomb "necessary"
  • Supporting cast — for Dwight and Lucienne, the unicorn team Jasha and Radoslav rescue earlier in Heat 5

Sourced from Book 8: A Parade of Horribles.

docs.title: Juice Box
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Role: Changeling prostitute/bartender NPC, Hump Town (Floor 5, Book 4)
  • Species: Changeling — one of a refugee population of shapeshifters displaced from their original home, "the Hunting Grounds" (Floor 6)
  • True form: Not physically shown — changelings shift into a generic race-form (human by default here) with cosmetic adjustment, gaining minor real abilities of the mimicked race
  • Type: Dungeon-born NPC (never a crawler); warlord as of Book 6
  • Class: None stated — changelings in the text have forms and a library, not a class
  • Subclass: None stated
  • Level: Unreliable by design — displays 17 (Book 4), 35 in human form and 120 in her blank form (Book 7). Mordecai says there is no way to read a high-level changeling's real level, even in blank form. She claims to have lived "at least 400 different lives"
  • Notable spells/abilities: Changeling shapeshifting into anything she or her line has physically touched, including forms nobody else has — the Unwashed / The Beautiful Place (the personification of the Nothing), a hunter wraith (which can possess and puppet a body, and carries the Inevitable Ruin truth-curse), and a Fleshmancer capable of grafting transplanted organs
  • Notable items: None named
  • Status: Alive as far as the text shows. Sent through the Gate of the Feral Gods to Floor 9's Larracos at the end of Book 4; co-warlord of the Home Team in Book 6, Faction Wars' tenth, NPC-populated team, alongside Sir Ferdinand; the team arrives on Floor 9 in Book 7 renamed Team Retribution. Leaves the ninth floor at the very end of Book 7 by jumping into the Nothing, bound for the 12th floor "the long way" — what she becomes is never shown
  • Relationship: Engaged to Louis by the end of Book 4; marries him in Book 7 in a changeling small wedding and divorces him on the same floor

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: Introduced as a ditzy, cheerfully transactional bartender at Hump Town's saferoom tavern, handing out juice boxes to the town's children and running a cosmetic-persona side hustle for paying crawlers. Carl initially treats her as comic relief — until she reveals a much sharper political and personal awareness than she lets on.

docs.title: What She's Hiding
docs.text: Juice Box is the sister of Henrik, the leader of Hump Town's hidden changeling "principals" — a faction secretly using the town's dromedarian collateral arrangement to try to obtain a resurrection spell for the necropolis's ghost queen, Quetzalcoatlus, in hopes of finding a cure for compression sickness, a birth defect increasingly common among changeling children born in this world (one in four births, by her account). She initially disapproves of her brother's methods — particularly his torture of the gnome hostage Wynne — but ultimately helps Carl's plans once she comes to trust him.

docs.title: Awakening
docs.text: Like Fire Brandy and Tizquick before her (Floor 4), Juice Box begins remembering fragments of a past life once exposed to Earth media (movies playing in Carl's personal space) and to enough honest conversation from Louis and Carl about the nature of her world. She recalls a dream/memory of being a schoolteacher forced to help kill infected students during some past outbreak, and recognizes the significance of "the Hunting Grounds" (Floor 6) as her people's true, lost home.

docs.title: Role in the Story — Book 4
docs.text:
• Helps shelter dozens of Hump Town's children (both dromedarian and changeling) in Carl's personal space during the Wasteland bombardment, in exchange for a promise from Carl to try to bring her people down through the floors with him wherever possible
  • Reveals the existence and mechanics of the Gate of the Feral Gods' three-piece structure and the changelings' true goal, once Carl proves himself by saving the town
  • Discovers her brother Henrik is dead (killed by the ghost Quetzalcoatlus while trying a desperate backup plan inside the flooded necropolis) and processes the loss while continuing to help Carl
  • Sacrifices her own safety to walk into Carl's confrontation with Chris Andrews (possessed by Maggie My), correctly identifying the threat as "worse" than a simple changeling
  • Adopts the orphaned gnome girl Bonnie into Hump Town's changeling/dromedarian community at the book's end, promising Carl's group she'll always have a home there
  • At Carl's request, becomes the sole carrier sent through the Gate of the Feral Gods to Floor 6's city of Larracos in the book's climax — tasked with quietly telling other changeling survivors the truth about what they are, ahead of Carl and Donut's own eventual arrival

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Henrik — her brother, leader of the changeling principals; dies in Book 4
  • Louis — reveals at the very end of the book that the two are engaged to be married, to Carl's open astonishment
  • Carl — a trust built slowly over the book; extracts and receives a genuine promise that he'll try to bring changeling survivors down through the floors with him

docs.title: Book 6: The Home Team
docs.text: Juice Box survived the trip to Floor 9 at the end of Book 4, and Book 6 reveals what she has been doing down there. She has been running an insurrection.

docs.title: Wearing the Enemy's Face
docs.text:
She crashes the Faction Wars preproduction meeting by beheading the viceroy of the Madness mid-session and taking his seat — wearing the face of Epitome Noflex, mother of the Dream's representative Epitome Tagg, and the bald elf whose photograph caused all of Louis's problems.

"You. My men told me they found you and killed you."

"Obviously not."

Tagg had ordered his own mother killed. The executive producer Cascadia rules that nobody can touch her: "The rules haven't changed. She's an NPC. The AI won't let us touch this." Tagg's conclusion, and the book's: "They're becoming self-aware. All of them. It's going to be impossible for anybody to win."

She also reminds Crown Prince Stalwart of the arrow she once put through his eye, shifting into his form with the arrow still in it — "Do you remember this one? I bet it hurt. Next time, I'll get your other eye." Stalwart does take a second arrow through the eye and die at that table, though Carl notes it wasn't her: "It hadn't been Juice Box unless she'd learned how to teleport."

docs.title: The Demand
docs.text:
"If you want us to stop knocking down all of your pretty structures and killing your army folks, or to let you finish draining Larracos, there's only one way to do it. I want you guys to make a new rule… I want you to add my people as their own team, afforded all the safeties as the rest of you. I want regeneration for all of us."

And, when Carl formally proposes it: "And with full voting rights." Her self-assessment in the same scene is the whole point of her arc: "I am my own team, thank you very much… I know how this works now. I know what I am."

docs.title: Winning
docs.text:
The proposal sits unvoted for most of the book because the other warlords have stopped participating entirely. In the last minutes of Floor 8, Carl burns the first of his three Emergency Action Items to hand all outstanding votes to the audience — and the audience decides it:

Pending Action Item, originally proposed by the Princess Posse: A tenth team populated with NPCs, afforded the same protections as the rest.

This item has been passed by a 52% audience vote.

This team will be designated as Home Team with the city of Larracos as their base… This team's assigned co-warlords are the NPCs Juice Box and Sir Ferdinand.

Her co-warlord is Sir Ferdinand — Donut's pre-apocalypse cat love, now titled. Donut gasps at the mention of "Gravy Boat."

docs.title: Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin
docs.text: Book 6 won her people a team. Book 7 reveals what she wanted it for, and it was never the team.

docs.title: Team Retribution
docs.text:
The tenth team the audience voted into existence at the end of Book 6 arrives on Floor 9 under a name of the NPCs' own choosing: Team Retribution, the defending team, headquartered in Larracos, with Juice Box and Sir Ferdinand as co-warlords. Carl's summary early in the book: "there are ten teams total. Nine attacking teams and one defending team, the NPCs, who have decided to call themselves Team Retribution."

The partnership is lopsided in a way that infuriates her. Ferdinand — "Warlord on High, Sir Ferdinand. Cat. Level 100" — holds the warlord menus, the mayorship of Shanty Town and control of the city defense system, because the system classes him as crawler stock rather than dungeon-born. Juice Box has no menus at all, only the mental messaging and the floating words.

"This cat has done nothing but cause problems, and now he has been given control of my people… If he dies, we lose control, so he must be kept safe."

That, she admits, is the only reason he is still breathing.

She has changed since Floor 5. When she takes her human form for Carl in Chapter 9 she has scars she didn't have before, and her left ear doesn't form with the rest of her — it appears ten seconds late, "almost like an afterthought." Her displayed level is useless as a measure: 17 on Floor 5, 35 in human form here, 120 in her blank form at the wedding. Mordecai says there is no way to read the real number off a high-level changeling.

docs.title: Married, Then Not
docs.text:
She marries Louis in Chapter 10, in the entrance bar of the Desperado Club, in the private "small wedding" that is the legally binding half of a changeling marriage. She wants the houses bonded; Louis agrees mostly because the alliance needs it. What she actually feels she tells Carl much later, watching over Louis's unconscious body:

"There is so much chaos and death in this world, and I needed an anchor… When you see someone like that, and it is so free of the rot of cynicism, so free of corruption, it's like the most alluring, beautiful thing in the world… He is to me like Donut is to you."

Then she saves his life by taking the form of a hunter wraith and possessing him — and the form carries a curse called the Inevitable Ruin, which the book also takes its title from. It shows the possessor the truth of what they possessed.

"But for me, when I had Louis possessed in order to save him, the curse showed me the truth. And the truth is that he's terrified of me. The truth is he's not in love with me. He thinks he has a special ability that causes NPCs to fall in love with him… It doesn't matter that it's not true. He doesn't trust what I feel, and he never will."

She files the divorce papers inside the month. The same conversation carries the first hint of what she is really carrying:

"I have something inside me, Carl. Something very, very powerful, and I've been afraid of it for a long time. But the thought of using it, really using it has been unthinkable because there are people like him out there."

docs.title: The Prophecy
docs.text:
At the warlord council (end of Chapter 43), Odette presses her for a statement in front of the galaxy. Juice Box gives one — "Fuck all of you… You had no right to do what you did to my people" — and then changes into something nobody at the table has ever seen in the flesh: a midnight-black, thin alien with no arms and electrified tentacles waving from its shoulders. Cascadia shrieks and drops her drink. Ferdinand bolts for Carl's shoulder. Architect Houston stands up shaking with excitement.

Her voice changes with the form — "Gone was that trailer park girl drawl, replaced with the voice of a demon."

"It's coming. And not just for these here with me today, all of whom are already marked and damned. Those of you at home, safe with the knowledge everything you've ever known is real, true. Those of you watching this, riveted to your screens, waiting to see what happens next. It is coming. It is coming for you all."

Odette tentatively floated closer. "What's coming?" she asked.

She doesn't answer. She walks out through the wall on hundreds of root-like legs.

Chapter 44 is the table trying to work out what she was. Houston calls it "the personification of the Nothing," and says it has a thousand names — "The Hag. The Unwashed. The Stalker. The Last Light. The Thirst. The Fell. The Inexorable" — and that the Viceroys call it The Beautiful Place. Cascadia: "We're banned from using the Unwashed as a mob." Carl's chill is the obvious follow-up question: a changeling can only take a form it has physically touched, so how does she have this one?

docs.title: What She Actually Wants
docs.text:
The Justice Light interlude is where the floor's real plot gets stated out loud. Justice, building the trap system beneath the castle, works out that one of his sluggalo assistants has been swapped for a changeling spy named Jessica, and uses her to open a channel to Juice Box. Along the way she casually revises her own age: not a hundred lives, but "at least 400 different lives up until this point."

He lays out what her alliance with the crawlers is actually subordinate to:

"The gods. It's all about the gods. It has been about them the whole time. You're risking it all so you and your kind can physically touch as many of them as possible."

She does not deny it. Her accounting of the Club Vanquisher incident is a status report on the programme:

"We lost three. We did not cause the gods to appear, but we were in position just in case. One of us managed to touch Bast—the panther god—but she died before she could escape. At this point, only one of us has touched a deity, and that one is... wrong."

This is her brother Henrik's project from Floor 5, scaled up to the divine: changelings can only become what they have touched, and every god touched is a god added to the library. Justice Light's offer — a way to touch a god and survive — is what buys the crawlers her full cooperation for the rest of the war. He also notes she was never as boxed in as she let on: "You could've killed the Sultana and her entire court quite easily. Hell, I believe you could end all this right now."

Her spies are everywhere, in every base, including Carl's.

docs.title: The Rest of the War
docs.text: She keeps her side of it. Her changelings hold the Dream's throne room; she pulls them out on request to keep Tagg from killing Louis, and puts them back when it's time. She takes the hunter wraith form to extract Louis from the Reaver castle. She is the one who identifies Tagg inside his chest. And in the surgery that frees him she shifts into a Fleshmancer — a tall, dark-skinned male figure — and casts the spell that makes the transplanted naiad organs take: "Casting now," Juice Box said, her male voice calm.

docs.title: Into the Nothing
docs.text:
With Emberus burning the floor, the crawlers take the stairwell and the NPCs transfer to the 12th. Juice Box doesn't take the transfer.

Juice Box: I will be leaving approximately 10 seconds after everyone else.

Carl: Wait, what the fuck? Where are you? Where are you going? You're not transferring to the 12th?

Juice Box: Oh, I'm going to the 12th floor all right. But Justice Light and I are taking the long way. It's okay, Carl. Trust me. You'll like this one.

The long way is the Nothing, through a permanent portal made from the broken winding box of the Gate of the Feral Gods. Her departure and Ferdinand's are logged as abandoning their posts — Team Retribution is defeated, and the Princess Posse wins Faction Wars.

Justice Light told her he was coming with her. He lied; he stayed behind to spring his trap, which breaks the Nothing open and drains it into the Halls of the Ascendency, Sheol and Scolopendra's lair. His last thought about her is the last thing the book says on the subject:

Juice Box would be fine, if her short time in the Nothing didn't drive her mad. She had a journey ahead of her, but like he told her, if she managed to survive this next part, she would be reborn as the ultimate weapon to end this madness. This war.

Unresolved

What Juice Box becomes is never shown. The line above is Justice Light's belief, relayed in his own point of view in the book's final chapter, and it is conditional on her surviving and on her sanity holding. She does not appear again before the end of the book, nothing confirms she reached the 12th floor, and the text gives no description of the "ultimate weapon" she is supposed to be reborn as.

Sourced from Book 4: The Gate of the Feral Gods, Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride, and Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Justice Light
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: NPC / former crawler — a returned cookbook author fighting for the Princess Posse on Floor 9
  • Race: Skyfowl — birth race also Skyfowl. A one-winged eagle, “shorter and stockier than most,” black feathers tinged with gray, with a twin tuft on his head that makes him look horned
  • Class: Trap Master, per his own status card. In Book 7 the system shows his class title as Origamist — Carl notes he has “no idea what the hell that even meant”
  • Subclass: None stated
  • Level: 65 during Faction Wars (Chapter 32), earned mostly from partial credit on his own traps. Top level during his original crawl: 86
  • Role: Trap master for the Princess Posse; author of the 8th edition of The Dungeon Anarchist’s Cookbook
  • Notable spells/abilities: A trap-concealment spell he worked out long ago (previously believed to work only on alarm traps); a presence-hiding spell used in the final chapter; built-in neural implants including seismic sensors sensitive enough to track a dwarven digger idling underground and to read a body’s temperature, weight and hormonal emissions
  • Notable items: None personally worn or wielded. His final trap is assembled from a bijou fairy trap, a demon trap, and the broken winding box of the Gate of the Feral Gods used as a permanent portal
  • Status: Deceased — stayed behind alone on the burning Floor 9 in Chapter 87, triggered his trans-dimensional trap, and died in the fire as Emberus melted the floor

Status card vs. the ending

The status card at the end of his interlude — which opens Part 3, between Chapters 55 and 56 — reads “Current status: Alive.” That card is written as of the interlude, thirty-odd chapters before he dies.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Justice Light comes to Floor 9 with the mercenary waves Porthus arranged — Carl calls him “the third, and the last I believed, of the cookbook authors who had come with the mercenaries.” Tipid introduces him to Carl in Chapter 11 with a straight promise:

“And wait until you see what my friend Justice Light can do. That eagle knows more about traps than anyone else who ever set foot in the dungeon.”

In person he is unnerving. He stands in the corner of the guildhall muttering, head jerking back and forth “like he was hearing things that weren’t really there,” sewing folded scraps of coloured paper into three-dimensional sculptures — which Tipid says is how he calms himself. When Carl worries aloud that losing a saferoom entrance will cost him his workbenches, Justice answers without looking up: “It’s safer and faster to use your table, but there’s nothing left I can’t do on my own.” Pressed on whether captured gondii brain worms might have learned the party’s secrets, he pulls a thread and all the scattered paper pieces snap together into a spiral:

“It doesn’t matter,” Justice Light said… “I have contingencies heaped upon contingencies. Have faith in the process. Danger lives in what they can’t see.”

Donut is not reassured.

Donut: ARE WE SURE WE TRUST THIS GUY? HE’S OBVIOUSLY UNSTABLE.

Carl: I trust him with my life.

Donut: OKAY. BUT YOU’RE TRUSTING HIM WITH MORE THAN THAT. IT’S WITH ALL OF OUR LIVES.

Both Tipid and Rosetta Thagra are described as fiercely protective of him. Rosetta vetoes his request to be deliberately infected with slugpox so he can breed more sluggalo assistants, warning that the skyfowl “had a tendency to hyperfixate on his projects, and he’d end up killing himself in the process.”

docs.title: The Shopkeeper
docs.text:
His entry in the 8th edition, reprinted at the head of Chapter 20, is about one killing out of thousands:

I think about him all the time. I have killed many NPCs since I arrived in this horror, but I have only killed one out of anger. He did not deserve that, and it haunts me. I keep going over it. It’s the manifestation of how I’ve changed, all boiled down to a single incident. The old me wouldn’t have done that. Snapped and just killed someone.

The memory is abhorrent to me. I have become what I hate.

The victim was a lizard-like NPC who ran the only trap store on the level; with the store gone, “dozens of my fellow crawlers were unable to find the supplies they needed to complete the level, and they died.” On taking his exit deal, Justice asked for and was granted an indentureship as the shopkeeper he had killed, accepting extra time on his contract for the privilege — something Dante notes was not normally allowed.

Crawler Drakea, 22nd edition, answers him directly in the book:

Listen to me, brother. We all make mistakes… But in this case... it was not your fault. No. They put you here. I remember your passage about how you would hunt and give food to the flightless elders of your world. You were once a good, gentle soul. They turned you into a warrior. They are the engineers of this all.

docs.title: Dante, the Ice Elves, and the Wing
docs.text:
The Dante interlude (between Chapters 4 and 5) shows the two of them as neighbours in indentureship — Dante a crocodilian thief, author of the 3rd edition, who had transferred to the trap master guild specifically to be near Justice without ever telling him they were brothers in the book. Both are reassigned off their posts to guard an ice castle on the eighth floor. Dante’s card records the outcome: “Was killed by administrative action for refusing to follow orders.”

Justice finally tells the rest of it himself, to a changeling, in his own interlude. The castle was staffed by ice elves — “More fairy than anything… They are gentle, simple creatures. Innocent… They would play in the snow, like children. This was all off camera.” He knew all their names. They loved puzzles, as he does.

“All this time later, and I still don’t understand why they ordered us to kill them all.”

Dante refused twice. There was no third warning.

“He’d already passed the point of no return, or so I thought. But in the end, I was wrong. He stood his ground, and he died. And by the gods, he died free.”

Justice refused once, was given a warning, and was ordered again. A beam took his wing, and then he did as he was told.

Justice held out the stump of his wing. “I, too, refused. But I only did so once, and unlike Dante, I was given a warning. They ordered me a second time.” He lowered his head… “I am still not free.”

He adds the part he has never told anyone, not even Porthus: a recurring dream in which the elves, having overheard, kill themselves to spare him the act. “Even that would’ve been the coward’s solution, so why do I yearn for it?… what difference is there between anger and cowardice?”

“They didn’t even fight back. They loved puzzles and the snow. I was already done. It was all off camera. I still don’t understand why.”

His personal proverb, repeated twice in the interlude, is his answer to all of it: “Wishing for favorable air currents does not manifest them. You ride the currents you have, or you don’t fly.”

docs.title: The Changeling in the Tunnel
docs.text:
Justice never trusted the NPC team, and said so to Tipid and Rosetta. He picked sluggalos as his work crew partly because he assumed procedurally generated mobs could not be copied by changelings. He was wrong — and his implants caught the substitution the moment it happened, from a change in body temperature, weight, and the absence of hormonal emissions.

He sends the rest of the crew up, then quietly arms eight hidden traps and addresses the last slug in line by her real employer’s name.

“Your real boss,” Justice repeated. “Juice Box. Tell her we need to talk.”

…”Damn, man,” the slug finally said, sighing. “I’m supposed to kill you if you figure it out.”

The changeling — an old, powerful one named Jessica — counts six of his traps, and takes a humanoid form with Juice Box’s head so Juice Box can speak through her over chat. A dwarven digger idles beneath them the whole conversation, ready to surge up and kill him.

The moment that lands hardest is not his: when he describes the ice elves, Jessica switches to one.

“Juice Box does not have these creatures in her library, but I do. I lived amongst them many lifetimes ago. They are indeed simple, gentle creatures.”

docs.title: Reading Juice Box
docs.text:
Justice lays out the case that Team Retribution’s alliance with the crawlers is real but secondary. His evidence is the Blood Sultanate: their security was worse than the Madness’s, yet Juice Box claimed she could not reach them, “an obvious lie,” after having decapitated multiple Viceroys before the ceasefire. He concludes she could kill every faction leader on the floor at any moment and has chosen not to.

“The gods. It’s all about the gods. It has been about them the whole time. You’re risking it all so you and your kind can physically touch as many of them as possible.”

He is right. Changelings can only take the form of something they have personally touched — Carl works through the same logic separately in Chapter 44 while thinking about Juice Box’s dead brother, whose quest was “to touch as many rare creatures as he could.” Juice Box’s reply gives away the tally:

“We lost three. We did not cause the gods to appear, but we were in position just in case. One of us managed to touch Bast—the panther god—but she died before she could escape. At this point, only one of us has touched a deity, and that one is... wrong.”

His offer is a trade: he shows them how to touch a god and survive; they stop the subterfuge and back Operation Ruin in full. She points out that if Operation Ruin works, the gods stop mattering.

Justice Light finally did chuckle. “Oh, my dear. You are thinking much too small. That’s not the war I’m talking about.”

He then explains what he has actually been building under the castle — a trap he says he started designing “the very moment he watched Carl discover the Gate of the Feral Gods.” The digger engine comes fully on, and then moves away.

docs.title: Building It in the Open
docs.text:
Everything Justice does for the Posse during Faction Wars doubles as cover. He wires the throne room, teaches Carl the alarm-trap upgrades reprinted in the 25th edition (recordings, playlists, a wider music database — still no volume control), hides the minefields with his concealment spell, supplies the teleport-trap trick that lets a mount and all its riders through at once, and holds the tunnel network under the castle as the last line of defence. His attitude to the last of those is not defensive:

Justice Light: That’s too many. Chop ‘em up a little first for me, Rosie. Get ‘em down to under 3,000, then we can let them in. I will welcome any and all guests into my lair. Would prefer it be Reaver, but I’ll take what I can get.

The one thing he cannot hide is how badly he needs the Gate of the Feral Gods back after the war mages steal it. He will not say why.

Justice Light: GODSDAMNIT, WHY ISN’T ANYONE LISTENING TO ME? GET THE GATE BACK, AND IT WON’T MATTER.

Carl tells him where it is — in the stomach of a merchant named Paca in the Midnight Market — against Tipid and Rosetta’s hesitation, on the grounds that “Who was I to stand between a brother and his revenge, whatever it may be?” Justice retrieves it in Chapter 81: “We have retrieved the Gate of the Feral Gods, and we are back in our location. Juice Box, it is ready.”

By the time Emberus is announced, it is already live.

Carl: In 65 minutes, Emberus will melt this entire floor.

Justice Light: Oh. Is that all?

Carl: Set your trap or whatever the hell you’re doing and get to Larracos.

Justice Light: The trap is already turned on. It has been turned on for days now.

Baroness Victory is the one who finally names the thing, after Rosetta reports him missing:

“Perhaps you should have watched him better,” Victory said. “He built a trans-dimensional trap right underneath your castle, and you didn’t even notice because he decorated it with regular traps.”

Carl’s working definition, when Donut asks: “It’s a trap that affects more than one place at a time. At least here in the dungeon.”

docs.title: Breaking the Nothing
docs.text:
He told Juice Box he was jumping into the Nothing with her. He lied; he needed to be on the crawler side of the veil to fire the trap. Everyone else has transferred. Only he and Emberus remain on the floor.

Justice Light: I am not sorry. Peace to you all, brothers and sisters.

He took his talon, and he snapped a piece of twine.

System Message: A Legendary Trap has been triggered.

The mechanism is deliberately small. Snapping the twine topples one tiny trap, which drops two items into the permanent portal below it — a portal made from the broken, blood-soaked winding box of the Gate of the Feral Gods, the same one Juice Box had just used to flee. The two items are a bijou fairy trap, carrying the thousands of threads tying the bijou to the 12th floor, and a demon trap, carrying thousands of evicted demons “with the power to open a portal back to Sheol, if only they could find something to latch onto.”

System Message: The Nothing has been broken.

System Message: The Nothing is currently draining into The Halls of the Ascendency.

System Message: The Nothing is currently draining into Sheol.

System Message: The Nothing is currently draining into Scolopendra’s Lair.

System Message: Scolopendra stirs.

…

System Message: Scolopendra has awakened.

He does not see any of it. “Still, his last moments were spent envisioning what was happening. Four separate planes—all jumbled and confused—folded and moved together as the unbreakable lines of the bijou fairies tightened, creating a flower pattern before the darkness in the center of it all broke apart.”

As the fire engulfed him, finally giving rest to a soul that had been so tired for such a very long time, Justice Light cawed into the air.

The narration, not a character, supplies the framing for how much this matters: he turns his attention to “the single, small trap that was about to change the course of all history.” On the text’s own terms it is the most consequential act in the book — it wakes the dungeon’s final boss years ahead of schedule, at the end of the ninth floor rather than the eighteenth.

On 'self-immolation'

The book never uses that word for him. What it shows is a deliberate choice to stay behind on a floor he knew Emberus was about to melt, in order to trigger the trap by hand; the fire that kills him is Emberus’s, not the trap’s. He also knowingly accepts the cost to everyone else — “All his friends left in the dungeon could possibly suffer because of what he was about to do.”

Unresolved

Justice told Juice Box that if she survived her passage through the Nothing “she would be reborn as the ultimate weapon to end this madness. This war.” What that means, and what he actually promised her about touching gods safely, is not explained before the book ends.

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Kandy “Bigs” Newton
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: NPC — a sluggalette, the female form of the sluggalo; a member of the Princess Posse
  • Race: Sluggalo. She is the size of a bulldog, slimy, and leaves orange goo behind her
  • Class: None stated
  • Subclass: None stated
  • Level: 29 at her introduction in chapter 54 — “She was only level 29, and she’d killed Vinata”
  • Role: Carl’s improvised bodyguard out of Club Vanquisher, later a permanent hanger-on of the Princess Posse column
  • Notable spells/abilities: None shown. She fights entirely with the hatchet, and she is immune to the Witness spell because the system classes sluggalos as a different kind of NPC
  • Notable items: None named — “A single hatchet grew straight up from the center of her head.” It is part of her body, not equipment
  • Status: Alive as of her last appearance in chapter 82. The text does not say what becomes of her at the end of the floor, though most of the surviving sluggalos stay with the Posse

docs.title: What a Sluggalette Is
docs.text:
The sluggalos are Carl’s own disease weaponised. SlugPox — “a nasty, old spell,” per Pater Coal — is what Carl caught on Floor 8 in Book 6 when he flagged the dying boss Asojano (“Warning: You have been infected with SlugPox.”). Boils grow on the infected, and out of each boil comes a fully formed slug person, each one higher level than the last. Carl can pass it on with his Super Spreader skill. His own summary, from Book 6:

Carl: They’re not punk rock. They’re Sluggalos. And I only infected one of them. Doctor Bones. He has the same Super Spreader spell as I do, but his is better. I can only do it on one person once per hour. He infected the others all at the same time, and then he cast a spell on the slugs so they’re not so hostile after they come out.

Doctor Bones mass-infected the Penis Parade strippers with that improved variant, which is where the sluggalo army comes from. They carry into Book 7 as Princess Posse troops — loud, obscene, suicidally enthusiastic, devoted to Imani, and used by Carl’s commanders as shock infantry precisely because they “swarm the castle face-first, inexpertly killing and getting themselves splattered like a bunch of idiots.” The system treats them, along with the former tattoos, as a separate category of NPC, which is why they are unaffected by several floor-wide effects that hit everyone else.

Carl never had his own slugpox cured, and by chapter 54 he is carrying an untreated boil on his back with the slug level somewhere around twenty or thirty. Bigs is what comes out of it. The mob type itself is covered separately.

docs.title: Killing the Sepsis Whore
docs.text:
The end of chapter 54 is the worst moment of Carl’s floor. He has blown himself up inside Club Vanquisher, and Princess Vinata — the Sepsis Whore, warlord of the Blood Sultanate — has survived the blast wrapped around him, driven insane by staring into the Eye of the Bedlam Bride on his chest. She is crushing him, stabbing him, and beating his head against the floor while gods walk past and ignore them both. Carl is drunk, cannot bend his knees, has screaming worms coming out of his nose, and is counting down his own immortality timer against hers.

I was about to drop the next bomb when I felt the sluggalo burst out of my back. He—actually, a she—slipped out from under my shirt, whooped loudly, and planted a hatchet right between Vinata’s eyes, killing her.

“Yeah, bitch! Right in the nugget!” the sluggalo woman shouted. She looked down at me as Vinata’s lifeless body slipped off of me and to the side. “I wish I had feet. I’d make me some snakeskin boots!”

Chapter 55 opens on the system messages, which is how Carl learns her name at the same time the rest of the party does:

System Message: The Sepsis Whore of the Blood Sultanate has fallen. Credit for the kill has been given to Kandy “Bigs” Newton of the Princess Posse.

System Message: The Blood Sultanate has been defeated.

System Message: All assets of the Blood Sultanate, as per prior arrangement, have been split evenly with the surviving blood relatives of the Sepsis Whore, Warlord Princess Donut and General Katia Grim, both of the Princess Posse. As per prior arrangement, all assets have been forfeited to the Princess Posse.

Katia: Who the hell is Kandy Newton, and where the hell are you, Carl?

That is a level-29 spontaneously generated slug eliminating an entire Faction Wars team, at the exact moment the operation had collapsed, by hitting the warlord in the head with the axe she was born with. A full page here rests on that single kill and nothing else needs to be added to justify it.

Carl gets his first proper look at her a moment later:

“Oh, daddy, you don’t look so good,” the sluggalette said, looking down at me. She was only level 29, and she’d killed Vinata. The naga must not have fully healed herself before the immortality expired. The slug was the size of a bulldog. She had little wisps of pink-dyed hair, monk-style, circling around her round head. Piercings ran down the slide of her slimy head, reminding me of that goblin shamanka from so long ago. A single hatchet grew straight up from the center of her head. It dripped with blood.

She names herself in the same chapter, while Carl is trying to give her orders:

“Okay, Kandy is it?” I asked the sluggalette… “Stay with me. Kill anyone who gets in my way. I have some friends we’re meeting halfway. Don’t hurt them. But I want you to sink a hatchet into anyone else. Things are about to get loud.”

“Call me Bigs,” the sluggalette said. She swung her head hatchet which flecked naga blood everywhere. “Is this ogre dude our friend or is he getting kneecapped?”

She also, undeterred by the fact that she is a bulldog-sized slug, repeatedly tries to bury the hatchet in Baroness Victory, who is not physically present and whose leg it passes straight through.

docs.title: After the Club
docs.text:
Bigs never leaves. She turns up mounted on Gonk the swamp yak alongside Dong Quixote in chapter 63, having got there because a sluggalo told her that if a mount takes a teleport trap, all its riders go through with it. Her mourning paint has been updated:

Since I’d last seen her, her face/eye paint had changed. She now had a massive teardrop built into the stalk of her right eye alongside the row of piercings. The hatchet protruding from her head gleamed. She leapt off the back of Gonk and splotched into the woods with a loud whoop. She waved the axe. “Imma get my chop on today. Where the bad guys at?”

She is one of the handful immune to the Witness spell in chapter 65 — the mass effect that sweeps everyone caught outdoors into a single rolling ball of bodies — along with Rend, Gonk, Jamal and Dong, because the system does not count sluggalos and former tattoos as the same sort of NPC.

On the Madness castle raid she scouts the front door, ties up two conscripted crawlers Carl has just rescued, and requires supervision about it:

“Can I kill one of them?” Bigs asked. “That one is already bleeding pretty good.”

“Holy shit, Bigs. She’s a friend. One of us. A good guy. Keep them safe.”

“I’ll wait until he’s gone,” Bigs whispered loudly at the two women. “Then one of you is getting the chop.”

Her other recurring notes are a running propositioning of anything that holds still — she offers an outraged antlered alien ten gold to lick her tail, and gets seduction coaching from Samantha while riding on her head — and a hard, unexplained animosity toward Li Na:

“No, she’s a bad guy,” Bigs said. “You know what she did to Sneaky Tyler C?”

“Uh...” I said. I was assuming Tyler C was another sluggalo. “No?”

“She tied a potion to him and then ordered him to run right into the god. He blew up the moment he touched the thing. That’s what I heard. It was a bitch-ass move. I don’t like her.”

Sneaky Tyler C was the lead sluggalo on Justice Light’s underground project. It is the only time in the book that a sluggalo holds a grudge.

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Katia
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Full designation: Crawler #9,077,265, "Katia Grim" — ranked General of the Princess Posse in Book 7; the epilogue of her arc gives her full name as Katia Grimmsdottir
  • Type: Human Crawler (in appearance only — see Race below). No longer a crawler as of Book 7 — reverted to human and ejected from the dungeon (see Status)
  • Race: Doppelganger — can reshape her own body/gear (of equal mass) at will, but must consciously "sculpt" the result herself; her true, resting appearance is black-haired, pale, mid-30s, with light, wide-set eyes
  • Class: Monster Truck Driver, a combined Earth/Staunch Barrier + Jouster "Juggernaut" tank class — massive Constitution that scales further the faster she's moving
  • Subclass: Not yet revealed
  • Level: 9 when introduced, jumping to 21 during the Doomsday Scenario event, then 24 and, after killing Hekla, a single-event jump to 37 — briefly the highest-level member of her own party and 8th on the Floor 4 top-10 leaderboard → 44 by the end of Book 4 → 60 by the end of Book 5 → never stated again in Books 6 or 7
  • Party: Joins The Royal Court of Princess Donut at the end of Book 2, at Hekla's request; remains a party member on paper but operates as leader of her own splinter team (Bautista, Gwen, Tran, Louis, Firas, Florin, Li Jun, Li Na, Zhang) through Books 4–5
  • Relationship: Romantically involved with Bautista as of Book 5; still together, if badly strained, when she leaves in Book 7
  • Succession status: Inherits the reforming Crown of the Sepsis Whore at the very end of Book 5, placed on her head by Eva Sigrid's dying hand — putting her in direct succession conflict with Donut over which of them may descend from Floor 9 to Floor 10. Resolved in Book 7 by the death of Princess Vinata and by Katia removing herself from the succession entirely
  • Status (Book 7): Alive, and out of the dungeon. Eats the Orchid of Eileithyia's Grace in Chapter 84 and chooses the pregnancy boon over the Celestial Attendant post — made human again, fitted with her own cybernetic prosthetics, impregnated with Louis Santiago's son, flagged Ineligible and exported to the Earth-surface "kinder facility" holding roughly 120,000 children and pregnant women. No longer a crawler; Donut is freed to descend
  • Notable spells/abilities: Rush (once-daily active skill; propels her body forward like a battering ram — upgraded in Book 3 to Crowd Blast, a five-minute-cooldown cone attack), Second Fuel Tank (random damage-absorb-and-reflect proc, once per fight), Pathfinder (helps locate stairwells; also a factor in Book 4's submarine expedition), immunity to wind-spell damage, plus her shapeshifting/"sculpting" ability — refined in Book 3 into a full combat form (a tripod "sentinel gun" mount for her looted crossbow) and near-perfect gnoll mimicry, and in Book 4 into a full-sized diving-bell/elevator shape and a working camouflage-skinned lookout form. Book 7 adds Hamzo (stuns and summons a single enemy to her location) and, on the non-combat side, the automaton-table engineering that produces Tran's exo-suit, Jamal's spider legs and her own prosthetics, plus the transfer-tattoo work she does on Carl and Imani
  • Notable items: A ring granting +15 Constitution (her main stat-stacking piece); Enchanted Repeating Crossbow of the Scavenger Mother of Mothers (Book 3, looted from Hekla; Book 4: fires Petrify Rock Class bolts — briefly petrifies rock-type creatures rather than killing them, and a fan-box bolt adding armor-piercing plus level-scaled damage in place of her unlimited free ammo); Enchanted Wrestling Belt of the Great Gorgo (Book 3); Enchanted Shade Gnoll Riot Forces Crowd Control Shield and matching Telescoping Crowd Control Baton (Book 3); The Bolt of Ophiotaurus (Book 3, sponsor gift, 1-of-100 anti-deity ammunition); an adjustable mass-storage backpack with retractable stilts (Book 4, a boss-box upgrade of her Book 3 "Ugly Ass Backpack" exploit); The Left Fang of the Green Sultan (looted from Eva in Book 3; returned to Carl in Book 4, then used to kill Eva outright in Book 5); a knit Apothecary beanie (Book 5, +3% to all stats and the party-wide knockback spell I Need My Personal Space — given away to Carl mid-battle at the Butcher's Masquerade); the Orchid of Eileithyia's Grace (carried uneaten out of Book 6, consumed in Book 7); the Enchanted Spiked Knee pads the Munificent Goddess Kina (Book 7, a divine item from the Club Vanquisher raid — used to eat twenty levels' worth of Intelligence via its Iron Stomach skill, then unequipped and given to Donut); a set of cybernetic prosthetics she built for herself and Bautista finished (Book 7)

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: Katia is a member of Hekla's group, Brynhild's Daughters, who gets separated from the team after they scatter entering Floor 3. Too far away to share in the group's experience gains, Hekla personally asks Carl and Donut (as a favor) to take Katia in and help her level up, introducing her by chat before the two parties meet in person.

docs.title: What She Actually Is
docs.text:
Katia is a Doppelganger — a notoriously difficult race that her own game guide, Bannon, talked her into picking without properly warning her what it entailed. Unlike Mordecai's Changeling race (which grants the actual non-physical abilities of whatever it copies), a Doppelganger only looks like whatever shape it sculpts — she has to physically "chisel" her own appearance by will alone, and doing so hurts. Before Mordecai helped her practice, her race literally displayed as "What the f-word?" in her info box. She can only see her true, unsculpted face when asleep or in the bathroom (and can't reshape herself in either state), reduced early on to using the reflection off a health potion as a mirror — until Carl gives her a shard of broken glass looted back on Floor 1. Equipped gear disappears into her body mass once worn; only her weapon stays visibly separate.

Before the collapse, Katia was an art teacher — a fact she finds ironic given how poorly she can initially sculpt her own face ("Those who can't do, teach").

docs.title: Class & Combat Role
docs.text: Her class, Monster Truck Driver, is Mordecai's best guess at a combined "Juggernaut" build — a Staunch Barrier/Jouster hybrid that grants an escalating Constitution bonus the faster she moves. Her Book 2 stats: Strength 11, Intelligence 8, Constitution 51, Dexterity 30, Charisma 8. Mordecai notes she's an extremely tanky wall that's still vulnerable if an enemy can simply pick her up and remove her from a fight, rather than trying to out-damage her directly.

docs.title: The Doomsday Scenario
docs.text: Katia fights alongside Carl and Donut during the climax of the Miss Quill/Remex quest chain (see Carl's Doomsday Scenario), using her Rush skill to save herself from one of the event's escalating "precursor bursts" — the impact visibly breaks her nose, which she doesn't seem to notice. As a designated co-host of the resulting emergency group quest, she can't retreat to a safe room and has to help evacuate NPCs instead while Carl and Donut gamble on containing the blast. She survives, jumping from Level 9 to 21 in the process — the largest single-event jump of anyone involved.

docs.title: Joining the Party
docs.text:
At the end of the Floor 3 event, Katia formally joins The Royal Court of Princess Donut as a new permanent member, appearing alongside Carl, Donut, and Mongo on Odette's talk show as "the newest member" of the group. Her placement in the party makes her subject to the same Manager arrangement with Mordecai, who "really likes her" per Carl's own observation.

Odette privately warns Carl that Katia is likely not a willing participant in Hekla's separate scheme to recruit Donut away from the party — implying Katia may be more entangled in outside plots than she currently lets on.

docs.title: Book 3: The Hekla Betrayal
docs.text:
Katia becomes the emotional center of Floor 4. After the party discovers Hekla is manipulating events to have Carl killed and Donut isolated into joining Brynhild's Daughters (see Hekla for the full plot), a multi-way brawl breaks out aboard a moving train. Hekla shoots Katia with two invisible, untraceable bolts meant to kill her slowly; Eva Sigrid, Katia's oldest friend and the actual architect of the scheme, cruelly reveals the full plot to Katia's face as a final cut. Katia's Rush — canonically unreliable in both distance and aim — goes off while she's aiming for Eva and instead slams Hekla into the train wall, killing her outright. Katia becomes the first crawler to claim a top-10 bounty (500,000 gold, Hekla having been ranked 2nd), jumping from Level 24 to 37 in a single event and earning a permanent player-killer skull and Club Vanquisher access.

She spends most of the rest of the floor visibly suppressing the trauma of both the kill and Eva's betrayal, throwing herself into engineering problems instead — most notably discovering that the Iron Tangle's rail network is a physical, "double-sided noodle" recreation of the Syndicate's own corporate logo (see Mordecai), a breakthrough that directly enables the party's endgame plan to blow the floor's ghoul-generator network.

docs.title: The Backpack and the Blood Exploit
docs.text: Katia develops a signature Book 3 technique: mass-storing liquid (blood, mostly, from acting as a literal human cowcatcher on the front of a train — her own idea) directly in her inventory to keep her "scoop" form clean, later re-manifesting it in an "Ugly Ass Backpack" of mass she carries in humanoid form. A Book 3 patch that bans storing unContained liquids in inventory catastrophically and comedically backfires this exploit, causing her to violently discharge weeks of stored gore across the party's personal space the moment Mordecai returns from his ban.

docs.title: Other Book 3 Notes
docs.text:
• Reaches 98% accuracy sculpting a convincing gnoll disguise, closing in on being able to pass Iron Tangle security checks in gnoll form
  • Picks up the Find Crawler and Gear Head skill/knowledge potions, the latter proving essential to salvaging and rebuilding hobgoblin cart engines
  • Loots The Left Fang of the Green Sultan — Eva's dropped saber, non-magical without its matched twin — denying Eva her main weapon
  • Gives Carl her Enchanted Auto Buckler of the Peach Pit after a fan box renders it redundant with her new riot shield

docs.title: Book 4: Growth, Command, and Departure
docs.text:
On Floor 5, Katia spends five days effectively running the party alone after Carl and Donut are detained off-page by a Syndicate liaison following Admin Loita's death — coordinating with a new ally, Gwendolyn Duet, to breach the land quadrant's castle walls, storing an entire flying house (balloon included) in her own inventory, and generally proving to herself (and to Carl) that she doesn't need his presence to function. She engineers the elaborate hostage-swap con against the Wasteland's gnomish ambassador almost entirely with her own body — simultaneously playing a fake corpse, a chair, and the "body" of a resurrected zombie gnome — and separately builds a working facsimile of the Gate's winding box from memory, swapping it for the real one during a goodbye hug so Carl can use the genuine artifact.

She also personally forms a "diving bell" elevator shape to ferry Carl and two other crawlers 500 meters down to the drowned submarine Akula, fighting off a city boss (Lusca the octo-shark) at point-blank range using a repurposed giant buzzsaw as an improvised melee weapon.

docs.title: Leaving the Core Party
docs.text: Having spent the floor talking with survivors of Hekla's old group, Brynhild's Daughters, Katia learns that Eva Sigrid — Katia's former friend and Hekla's actual co-conspirator — has been picking off the group's scattered "daughters" one by one, including healer Silfa and her two children. Katia decides she can't keep letting this happen and, at the end of the book, splits off from Carl and Donut's day-to-day party (though not formally out of the group) to lead a new team — Gwen, Tran, Louis and Firas, Bautista, and Florin among them — dedicated to gathering and protecting the surviving daughters before Eva (or someone else) gets to them. Carl gives her back The Left Fang of the Green Sultan to return to Eva as a parting gesture.

docs.title: Book 5: Killing Eva
docs.text:
Katia spends Floor 6 running her own splinter team's manhunt for Eva Sigrid, who has been running solo, killing repeatedly, and wielding a poisoned rapier prosthetic on the wrist where she lost a hand back in Book 3. During the book she also begins a relationship with Bautista, confirmed publicly to Donut's shock. In a private, Katia-only point-of-view passage at the very end of the book — not something she confides to Carl, who remains unaware of it — she's revealed to be secretly addicted to Blitz Sticks, using them to relive a false memory of stopping Eva sooner and of the daughter, Annie, she never got to raise back on Earth.

At the Butcher's Masquerade, Katia is nearly goaded into breaking the party's peace seal confronting Eva directly, and is only barely held back by Bautista and Florin. After the seal is broken by Signet's sacrifice, Katia hands off her Apothecary-gifted beanie to Carl instead so he can use its knockback spell to clear a path to Donut — leaving her own head bare. The text is explicit that it's the bare head, not the missing spell, that costs her: with any headgear occupying that equipment slot, the reforming Crown of the Sepsis Whore would not have had anywhere to land.

In the battle's aftermath, Katia and Li Na dig out a buried, unconscious Eva; Li Na casts a spell to stop her from healing, and Katia hacks off Eva's remaining hand-with-a-ring (her means of escape) and the poisoned rapier prosthetic, leaving her only her two lower hands. Once Eva wakes and begs to be spared, Katia executes her with The Left Fang of the Green Sultan, finally closing the loop from Book 3's betrayal. As she dies — but before she's fully dead — Eva uses one of her two remaining hands to pull a hidden item from her own armor: the reforming Crown of the Sepsis Whore. It flies to Katia's bare head, and by the time it finishes equipping, Eva has already died. The book ends with Katia realizing this puts her in direct succession conflict with Donut — only one of them will be permitted to descend from Floor 9 to Floor 10.

docs.title: Book 6: The Crown, the Orchid, and the Drugs
docs.text: Book 6 is Katia's heaviest arc. She spends it working a single problem — the Crown of the Sepsis Whore, and the fact that only one of her or Donut will be permitted to descend from Floor 9 — and comes apart doing it.

docs.title: The Crown, Confessed
docs.text:
She tells Carl mid-floor by chat, then tells Donut properly at the top of Chapter 19. The Crown came off Eva Sigrid's dying hand at the very end of Book 5, and she blames herself for it:

"It was Eva. She did it at the last minute, right before she died. It was my fault. I'd talked when I should've just killed her."

"You were monologuing? You know we don't monologue, Katia."

Donut goes straight to the arithmetic — "But what are we going to do? Only one of us can leave the next floor." Katia's answer:

"They want us to fight. That's not going to happen. I love you, Donut. And I will never fight you. I will die before I let that happen."

docs.title: The Lock Box and the Orchid
docs.text:
She has been carrying a second secret since the start of Floor 6: an Engaged Lock Box of the Night Wyrm, won in a celestial prize box for opening the Gate of the Feral Gods and flooding Larracos. Dark wood carved with spiderweb patterns, three purple jewels (one lit, two burnt out), and slats showing a pink orchid bud inside.

The box is attuned to her personally; if she dies, it destroys the prize. Three seals:

  • ✅ Kill someone you are currently or formerly partied with — Eva Sigrid
  • ✅ Kill a country or level boss — Queen Imogen
  • ⬜ Find a Guild of Suffering and complete an assassination quest

Inside is the Orchid of Eileithyia's Grace. Eating it knocks the user unconscious for an hour at 1% health with no healing possible; survive, and Eileithyia grants one of three permanent boons, at the goddess's discretion:

  1. Base Constitution tripled — "pretty much indestructible to physical damage," but it lapses if Eileithyia dies or the user passes Floor 12.
  2. Celestial Attendant — immediate transfer to the twelfth floor as a temporary non-combatant NPC, out of every party, progress frozen.
  3. Reversion to her birth race and immediate pregnancy, father of her choice — which disqualifies her from the game entirely and exports her to the Kinder Facility in former Mumbai.

Two of the three solve the Crown problem by removing Katia from the succession. Only the first leaves it live.

She worships Eileithyia off a scroll of worship that arrived in an emergency sponsor box from Princess Formidable of the Skull Empire. She read it and worshipped on the spot, and only afterwards discovered that Eileithyia's sponsor is Huanxin Jinx — who promptly messaged her with terms. Get Carl to repair Yemaya's shrine, and Huanxin will steer the boon so that both Katia and Donut survive.

docs.title: The Drugs
docs.text:
Katia finds a drug den in the Desperado Club — "set up like one of those frozen yogurt places, where you get a bowl, and you self-serve stuff into it and add toppings" — because Carl told her where it was. She goes under for ten hours. Bautista covers for her: "She's asleep… Just leave it, okay? She'll be fine." Imani, whose husband is an addict, recognises the pattern immediately.

Four drugs, per Mordecai:

  • Travis Priest — a very strong, very addictive painkiller (cured first; the source of the vomiting)
  • Creamsicle Charm — ground-up fairy wings, "a bit like shrooms, but it also makes you forget your worries"; not very addictive
  • Blitz sticks — "like weed plus a hallucinogen that shows you non-existent memories, which is why they're so damn addictive." She has been on these for a while
  • Glory Bound — taken once. "That's the bad one and is the most addictive. By far. It puts her in a coma and allows her to relive a memory… She basically would've just gone back in time and fully re-experienced something"

The Glory Bound cure is itself a dose of Glory Bound: "she'll have to re-live one of her worst memories. It's pretty fucked up." She never completes that final treatment in Book 6.

The damage is permanent. Mordecai's summary:

"The problem is she's already jacked up her stats. It's not good. Everything is scrambled. Her intelligence took a hit, though it's actually still higher than I thought it was from before thanks to the blitz… Her highest stat, constitution, has taken a big hit. Her strength is higher. Her Charisma took a hit. She'll be permanently susceptible to any sort of addictive spells from now on. She's probably forgotten a spell or two. And she's probably lowered a few skill points."

No system block

The stat damage is reported only through Mordecai's chat message. No numbers are given anywhere, and the system never prints a debuff block for it.

docs.title: Killing Astrid
docs.text:
The third seal on the lock box is a Guild of Suffering contract. Guild jobs are cover-blind — saying the target's name aloud voids the quest — so neither Katia nor Carl knows they have been hired by the target's own husband.

The mark is Astrid, level 125 Bloodlust Sprite, assistant manager of the Desperado Club. The ambush fails on every axis: Astrid's Cosmic Sense warns her, she takes the wrong staircase, and Samantha simultaneously tears open the Nothing in the casino and releases a level-225 feral demon. Carl calls an abort. Katia refuses:

"Carl, no. I have to do this… If I don't finish this now, we won't get a chance. The fight will be our distraction." … "Carl, this is all my fault. I have to fix it."

In the kitchens, Katia — invisible and shapeshifted into "a metallic, spiked-covered, human-faced, canine monstrosity" — grabs Astrid out of the air and then freezes solid mid-strike, spike millimetres short. Carl breaks the paralysis by tearing Astrid's wings off with his own hands. Her crow totem takes Astrid's eyes. A spike from the wolf's neck finishes her, cutting off her last words.

Katia stores the body and shifts into an ogre on the way out so the witnesses will blame a monster rather than a crawler: "We don't want them knowing a crawler did this." Then: "Carl, we did it. I have the orchid."

docs.title: Bautista
docs.text:
The relationship does not survive the floor intact. He covers for her, then blocks her — physically — from going on the Astrid job while she has twelve active debuffs:

"Where do you think you're going?" … "Don't touch me like that. Don't ever touch me like that."

"Fine. Kill yourself. But I won't stand by and watch," Bautista said. He turned and stormed from the club.

Louis names it out loud at the Christmas party — "Katia is struggling every day, and Bautista is having a nervous breakdown" — and Donut names it to Carl: "We're already losing Katia no matter what happens, and nobody is talking about it. Doesn't anybody see what it's doing to Bautista?" By the book's end they are walking at opposite ends of the group, and Katia's summary is one line: "He doesn't want me to use the orchid."

docs.title: Unresolved
docs.text:
Katia ends Book 6 holding the Orchid, uneaten. Carl doesn't want her to use it either — "The more I think about it, the more scared I get it's a death sentence" — and her answer is that not using it is also a death sentence. The calculus got worse once Odette announced she was personally entering the Ascendency as a goddess, because the only version of the plan that saves both Katia and Donut depends on trusting Huanxin Jinx, whose entire motive was revenge on Odette.

Carl's closing thought on it: "The call was ultimately Katia's to make, but there had to be another way. There had to be."

She also, at the climax, hands Paz Lo the reused Bolt of Ophiotaurus that kills the goddess Ysalte, loses an arm to Carl's hijacked Self-Immolation and simply regrows it, and is the first to say what should be done with Paz's card: "We rip it. That's what he wanted."

Not stated in the text

Katia's level is never given anywhere in Book 6. Early in the book she sits around #6 on the top-ten list; no end-of-floor level or rank appears.

docs.title: Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin
docs.text: Book 7 finishes everything Book 6 left open. Katia gets clean, spends the floor building machines for other people, and then eats the Orchid — and the choice she makes with it takes her out of the dungeon and out of the story.

docs.title: Getting Clean
docs.text:
The Glory Bound cure Mordecai couldn't finish on Floor 8 happens in Chapter 16, in a field hospital outside the base rather than in a saferoom. The dose is a jar of fizzing green slime: "basically two hits of Glory Bound, but compounded with a subdermal gel and mixed with a potion called 'Tough Love.'" Mordecai puts Katia under for eight to ten hours. Carl takes the same drug at the same time, his dose cut with Removal Order so he'll walk Shi Maria's memory instead of his own.

Edgar's warning is that once Katia is under she is alone, and waking her early could kill her. She goes under anyway, and tells Carl one thing first:

"My favorite memory and my worst memory are the same thing. I'm going to the same place I was last time. I hope that doesn't mess this up."

They reach for each other's hands as the potion takes hold. Imani separates them physically, but the connection through Carl's river holds, and Carl ends up inside Katia's dream with her — the only reason the reader ever sees it.

The memory is Reykjavík, about a year before the crawl. Katia is trying to adopt a nine-month-old girl named Annie, hospitalised with brain cancer. Fannar — a fellow professor, the man she was originally going to adopt with, whom Katia reported after he slept with a student — walks into the adoption office ahead of her to tell them about her decade-old addiction history. "I can take a test," the memory ghost pleads. "I haven't touched anything in ten years. It was so long ago." The application is denied. Katia locks herself in a bathroom stall, puts her fist in her mouth, and screams silently. Then she goes upstairs and holds the baby for the last time.

"And here is the worst moment of my life because I know it's the last time I will ever see her," Katia said. A moment passed. "It's also my favorite memory, and it is where I keep coming back to."

Annie died alone weeks later; Katia only found out by running into a nurse at a park. The crow-totem card she has carried since Floor 8 — a bird with the skull of an infant — is named Annie for her.

What Carl also sees is what she thinks of herself: that she is a burden, that she is ashamed everyone is doing this for her, and that she is angry — including, briefly, at Carl. Her explanation:

"It's not that I'm angry with you," she said… "I'm just mad that you let people hurt you. You meet someone, you start to care for them, and then it becomes…"

She does not overstate the result afterward:

Katia: I think so. It's not like a switch that one flips on and off. We won't really know right away. But, yes. I think it worked.

Not stated in the text

Book 7 never prints a system block confirming the addiction cleared, and never revisits the permanent stat damage Mordecai described in Book 6. It also never gives Katia's level anywhere in the book.

docs.title: The Engineer
docs.text:
Katia spends most of the floor at Carl's automaton table rather than in the line. Three builds matter.

Tran's conveyance. Tran lost his magical wheelchair between floors. Katia repurposes a recipe from Carl's automaton manual into a two-part rig: a mechanical crab body he can climb walls and sprint on, plus a battle mode where "a secondary exo-skeleton covered the crab legs, crawling up his body, encasing him in full-plate armor and a helmet." Carl's summary — "as if Odette and Iron Man had a baby." So much of Tran is metal that he can't carry ranged weapons without the system reclassifying him as Armor.

Jamal's legs. Jamal the hammerhead shark flesh golem breathes air, can't swim, and can only flop. Carl builds three voice-controlled prototypes and Jamal breaks all three by hopping; Katia's version is the real one — eight double-jointed legs and a harness, thought-driven rather than voice-driven, and strong enough that he outruns most of the party. Rosetta's crafting team bolts Tserendolgor's flamethrower Velma to the underside of the harness. A No Disassemble blast later fries the cybernetics, and Katia simply hands over the spare set she'd already built.

Her own prosthetics. She builds these quietly, in the crafting room, and tells nobody what they're for. Bautista finishes them for her while she's unconscious under the Orchid.

docs.title: The Transfer Tattoos
docs.text:
The toraline-yam ink that Shi Maria brewed lets a willing crawler lend a spell or skill to another in the form of a permanent tattoo. Edgar is the party's actual tattoo artist, but he's off scouting naga territory, so the work falls to Katia, who admits she has never done a real tattoo before. (The mechanic itself belongs with the toraline ink and the Enchanted Prison Tattoo Kit; this is her part in it.)

She does two:

  • Carl's chain dragon, a large piece on his right arm, carrying Li Na's level-13 Daughter's Kiss. Li Na gave her blood freely, so she loses five levels of the skill temporarily rather than permanently — the opposite of what happened to her brother Li Jun when Shi Maria took Walk on Air by force.
  • Imani's barbed wire, a small band around her ankle, carrying Carl's Tripper. Donut objects loudly to the style on aesthetic grounds; Katia's answer: "Donut, didn't we agree you were going to stop complaining about the tattoos? It's not a disfigurement."

She also did Samantha's neck lettering, which she declines to count.

docs.title: General Katia Grim
docs.text:
She holds the rank of General in the Princess Posse and runs the northern front alongside Florin for most of the fighting. For Operation: Snake Pit — the raid on Club Vanquisher to wipe out the Blood Sultanate's line of succession — she shapeshifts into a mantaur, covers herself in fake gore (cherry cobbler from Carl's broken food box), and talks her way through the temple door with an improvised battle cry: "Fight to the death!… Kill all the heathens! The demons come! Uh, steel and heavy metal!"

The raid kills Princess Vinata and settles the succession on the crown's side of the ledger; see Crown of the Sepsis Whore for the mechanics. The system names Katia in the payout:

System Message: All assets of the Blood Sultanate, as per prior arrangement, have been split evenly with the surviving blood relatives of the Sepsis Whore, Warlord Princess Donut and General Katia Grim, both of the Princess Posse.

Her celestial box from the raid is the Enchanted Spiked Knee pads the Munificent Goddess Kina, a divine item. Drick calls it on air as a gift intended to be handed to Carl, since she's leaving either way. She eats twenty levels' worth of throwaway magic items with its Iron Stomach skill to pump her Intelligence, then unequips the knee pads and gives them to Donut — who uses their Eileithyia boon to kill Huanxin Jinx with them on.

Privately, she tells Carl something she never tells Bautista: if the plan collapses, the Orchid goes to Donut.

Katia: I know. But I want you to know something. I haven't told Daniel this, but I'm telling you now. If it comes to that, I will give you the flower. That Huanxin bitch will rage, but I'm certain she'll take Donut to the 12th floor.

docs.title: Eating the Orchid
docs.text:
