Chapter 84. Samantha's confession summons Emberus, who gives the floor 66 minutes before he burns it. The Orchid takes exactly 60 minutes to work, so the goodbye everyone had planned for days later happens in about ninety seconds.

"Katia!" I called… "Eat the orchid. You have to do it now. Now, now, now!"

"But…" she began.

"Carl, we haven't had the chance to say goodbye to her!" Donut cried. "I thought we had days left!"

She hasn't finished transferring her inventory, and there's gear she needs still sitting in the saferoom. She eats it anyway.

"I love you," Katia said. She raised her voice. "I love all of you."

Donut leaps for the table and lands too late. Katia is at 1% health with Waiting for the Goddess over her head before the cat touches down.

docs.title: The Choice
docs.text:
She wakes in Chapter 86 with eight minutes left on the world. Eileithyia arrives in her true form — and wearing Huanxin Jinx, who immediately starts hurrying her along. The book never prints a system block for the three boons here; the narration is all the reader gets:

Right now Katia had three choices floating in her vision. The first would cause her constitution to get extremely powerful. The second would allow her to become a celestial attendant. The third would cause her to get pregnant. Ultimately the choice was up to the goddess, but Katia had to pick one before Eileithyia could whisk her away.

Huanxin's own framing of it: "Damnit, Katia. I can't take you until you make a choice. It doesn't matter what you pick. Just pick one." Donut then casts Laundry Day, rips the heiress out of the goddess's soul armor, and kills her with Mordecai's ashes-tipped bolt fired from Katia's own crossbow — the deal with Huanxin dies with her, and Katia chooses free.

She hugs everyone, kisses Donut on the forehead — "You keep him safe. And now I have to press the button" — and picks the third option.

"Please, goddess. Please." She took a breath.

"I wish to be made pregnant."

Eileithyia offers her the safe option one more time, explicitly:

"Are you certain? This is a hard, cruel world you have found yourself in, and as a woman with gift, your challenges will be even greater. If you come to assist me and Yemaya in my court, I promise you will be kept safe. I sense the strength in you, and you would be welcome."

Katia turns down the Celestial Attendant post, and the reason is not her own safety:

"The rules of this world are strange," Katia said. "If I am pregnant, I get sent somewhere else. There are no children or pregnant women allowed here in this place. At least not of my kind. But there are several children, up there," Katia said, pointing upward. "And they are mostly alone. I think they're in trouble. They all need help, and this is the only way I can get to them."

She means the kinder facility on the surface of Earth, where Zev has admitted roughly 120,000 children and pregnant women are being held — the ones who tried to enter the dungeon and were routed somewhere else instead. Eileithyia, who is a goddess of childbirth, can suddenly sense them and cannot reach them. Donut closes it: "You can't get there. But Katia can, and she can protect them for you."

docs.title: What She'd Been Hiding
docs.text:
The goddess makes her human again first, and the shapeshifting stops covering for her.

Her entire right arm was gone, all the way to the shoulder. Her left leg was gone. Her right leg was gone up to the knee. She was missing an ear as well.

Katia smiled sadly from the bed. "Just a few things I've lost along the way."

I remembered when she'd lost the ends of her fingers on her hand, all the way back on the Iron Tangle.

"I had no idea," I said.

"How could you? We've all become experts at hiding what we've really lost."

Bautista bursts in with the cybernetic limbs, which she had built herself in advance and left in the crafting room for him to finish. The party clicks them into place while the goddess works.

Not stated in the text

The text does not say when each limb was lost, beyond Carl's memory of her fingertips on the Iron Tangle (Book 3). The wording — "accumulated over seven floors" — is Carl's inference from the scene, not a system statement, and nothing identifies which floor cost her the arm, the legs or the ear. Nor does the text call the replacements Bautista's work: "She'd made them herself, in anticipation of this. She'd left them in the crafting room, and Bautista had finished them for her."

docs.title: Leaving
docs.text:
Eileithyia rules that the father must be human, and that it cannot be Carl — "I see who you wish for it to be, but it cannot be so," with Bautista standing right there. Katia asks Louis, fresh out of surgery and worried he may not count as human any more. Eileithyia takes his hand: "Of course you are. And a good soul at that."

"It is done. It will be a boy."

"Spoilers," Louis muttered.

Ineligible appears over her head.

And then, just like that, Katia Grimmsdottir… Art Professor. Crawler. Hero. Human. Friend.

Mother.

…disappeared in a puff of smoke.

She leaves two things on the table: the Annie card, which Donut takes, and a joke bra with Carl's face on one cup and "Time to pay the daddy tax!" on the other.

With Katia out of the dungeon, Donut is free to descend. The succession crisis that had run since the end of Book 5 ends not in a fight but in Katia removing herself from it.

Sourced from Book 2: Carl's Doomsday Scenario, Book 3: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook, Book 4: The Gate of the Feral Gods, Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade, Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride, and Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Li Jun
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: Crawler
  • Class: Street Monk (Book 2)
  • Level: Ranked 9th on the Floor 3 leaderboard (Book 2)
  • Party: Independent; travels with his best friend Zhang and his sister Li Na on Floor 4
  • Notable spells/abilities: Acrobatic melee combat — flips, tentacle grabs, and throws; a red-glowing unarmed buff; Walk on Air (lost permanently to Carl at the end of Book 6, later re-bought from a book)
  • Notable items: The Engine of Tomorrow (Book 7) — a celestial-tier robotic eye replacing the one Carl ate
  • Status: Deceased — killed by the god Harpocrates in Chapter 68 of Book 7, drawing the god away from Donut's tower

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: First introduced in Book 2 as a fellow guest on Death Watch Extreme Dungeon Mayhem, whom Carl recognizes as someone he'd previously helped save from troglodytes and Brindle Grubs during that same abusive broadcast appearance. He ranks 9th on the Floor 3 leaderboard as a Street Monk.

docs.title: Floor 4: Leading From the Front
docs.text:
By Book 3, Li Jun has become a key ally in the fight to hold station 36 against the Iron Tangle's collapsing ghoul-generator network, personally volunteering (along with his best friend Zhang, an Earth Mover mage-tank, and his sister Li Na) to help Carl retrieve a stranded interdiction cart through monster-infested tunnels. His fighting style is acrobatic and improvisational — flipping through the air, grabbing tentacles, and throwing full-grown Krakaren monsters — and his quiet competence contrasts sharply with his sister's blunter, more intimidating presence.

Li Jun and Zhang are instrumental in the operation to bait and capture two mantaur neighborhood bosses as "vessels" for Carl's involuntary deity-summon gambit against the floor's mimic city boss (see Carl); Zhang's one-charge shrinking wand is also what makes it physically possible to move a full-size interdiction cart through the Tangle's narrow service tunnels.

docs.title: Family
docs.text:
• Zhang — Li Jun's best friend, an Earth Mover mage-tank in segmented black-and-gold armor, quietly in love with Li Na without her brother's knowledge
  • Li Na — Li Jun's sister, a Level 30 Changbi Slave Driver whose disturbing, demon-like appearance belies a sharp tactical mind; she's the one who proposes using the Def Leppard interdiction cart to bait and portal away a province boss, and who dispassionately amputates and repeatedly heals a captured mantaur to make it easier to manage as a summoning vessel

docs.title: Book 5 Notes
docs.text: Li Jun is secretly infected with vampirism on Floor 6, telling only his sister Li Na and Zhang, and is cured floor-wide when Miriam Dom dies. He continues fighting alongside Katia's splinter team through the hunter war and the Butcher's Masquerade, visibly shaken afterward by the scale of the final battle's losses.

docs.title: Book 6 Notes
docs.text: Li Jun spends most of Floor 8 in Beijing with his sister Li Na and Chris Andrews, and comes to Cuba with the rescue party. He is also the one who brings Carl the news of the Battle of Beijing and the five Tier-3 Doggie Door upgrades Lucia Mar left behind — including her parting threat against Donut and Mongo, which Li Jun passes on privately.

docs.title: The Eye
docs.text:
In the last fight, Carl is hijacked by his own totem, Shi Maria, who needs ink for a tattoo. Li Na fires a chain down through a burning apartment and Li Jun slides down it to help his friend.

"Carl, what can I do?" It was Li Jun, looking at me worriedly. All around him, the walls continued to burn.

I warned him, Shi Maria said in my mind.

No, I thought. No. He's my friend.

I took the stick from the tattoo kit, and I jabbed it directly into Li Jun's eye. He cried and fell back. I pulled the stick to my mouth, and I licked. Oh god, oh god. His eye. His eye was at the end of the stick. I crunched down and ate it.

Shi Maria, still wearing Carl, then threatens Li Na to keep her from healing him: "Do not approach, demon, or your brother will lose more than an eye, and Carl will lose his own heart… Do not attempt to heal him."

The eye does not come back. Carl's own verdict — "I'd eaten his eye. I'd eaten his goddamn eye. It was gone. It wouldn't come back." — and Louis's casualty report afterwards confirms it. Carl does not get the chance to apologise before the floor collapses. "I hadn't had time yet to apologize for what I'd done to Li Jun's eye. I hoped he was okay."

docs.title: Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin
docs.text:
Li Jun enters Floor 9 wearing an eyepatch. He and Li Na skip the officer ceremony in the guild hall entirely because they are out "seeking out a healer who might be able to regrow Li Jun's eye" — a search that never succeeds. Carl opens the book by trying to apologise:

Carl: Hey, Li Jun. I didn't have a chance to talk to you at the end of the last floor. I wanted to apologize about what happened, and I was hoping we could talk.

He didn't answer.

Carl is meanwhile stuck carrying the evidence. The Walk on Air skill that Shi Maria tore out of Li Jun is now permanently Carl's, and he uses it repeatedly through the book, each time with the taste of the eye in his mouth. Katia's verdict on why Li Na has gone silent on Carl: "She's not mad at you. She's mad at herself for not protecting her brother." (Li Jun does get Walk on Air back, but only because they bought the skill book.)

docs.title: Shanty Town and Club Vanquisher
docs.text:
He spends the ceasefire and the first war phase in Shanty Town with Li Na and the 107th White Dragon Urban Defense battalion, reporting tower construction progress into the war chat — and he is the one who spots Lucia Mar drinking at the Possum Envy and passes it to Florin.

In the assault on Club Vanquisher he is one of the wire team. He and Zhang trail the capacitor wire from Li Na's clock tower into the club so her Dreads will reach inside, with Li Jun "hanging impossibly off the wall" to loop a wire around the mounted dragon's head over the fireplace, then holding the interior door open so the aura stays live. He also sits out in the open watching his sister's dread levels and telling her when to switch.

docs.title: The Engine of Tomorrow
docs.text:
The raid earns five crawlers a Celestial, Who-Let-The-Gods-Out Box. Li Jun's is a celestial-tier robotic eye, discussed on the broadcast the day before Carl and Katia's own interview:

"Yesterday we talked to Li Jun about his celestial tier robotic eye and Zhang's new cape with the target on the back."

Carl's closer look at it:

His new eye, which at the moment was a swirling orb of black, unnerved me. When it was working, the black changed to look like a miniature, clockwork engine, all contained in the round eye. Even the name of the thing was a little freaky. The Engine of Tomorrow.

It lets him see muscles tensing and slows his own perception of time in short bursts — "Like Bullet Time from the Matrix movies." He and Li Na train with it nonstop. It is also the last thing he notices about Carl before his death: he corners him outside the brig, asks "How are you doing?", refuses the deflection, and presses — "Yes, but what about you?"

docs.title: Death
docs.text:
In Chapter 68, Donut has the entire allied army rolled up inside her Rolling Battle Formation ball and cannot leave the Nest tower until the ball reaches the corpse field. The god Harpocrates — who she has just spent several minutes insulting over a public address system — has marked her for death and is closing on the tower.

Li Jun: He's going to get to you before the ball reaches the other field. I have an idea. Speaker number 11 is still on the back of a cart. Mute all the speakers except that one. Play the song I just sent you.

Li Na: Jun, no. No!

Li Jun: Sorry, little sister. I'll jump before he catches me.

Carl, elbow-deep in the Madness castle at the time: "Li Jun was distracting the angry god so Donut could finish her plan, and it was all I could do to not scream."

His last message is to his sister:

Li Jun: Sister. Tell Zhang I'm sorry I didn't get to say goodbye to his face. Tell him I won our bet. And you. Protect him. I want you to be kind to the others. This was my decision. I had to do it. I know you get angry. If you must, be angry with me. I love you with all I have. I love you with the moon and the sun and all the stars in the sky. I will see you soon, and I will tell mama you said hello.

The death itself happens off-page. What Carl gets instead is a vision, in the half-second he spends non-corporeal inside Architect Houston's trap room — the thing surgically attached to Houston turns, leans in as if to kiss him, and briefly wears Li Jun's face:

"Thank you for giving me more time with my sister and my best friend," Li Jun said as roots wrapped around him and suddenly whisked him away.

Then, in the wreckage:

Li Jun: Thank you for giving me more time with my sister and my best friend.

This message is from a deceased crawler.

"No, no, Li Jun. No," I whispered, my voice hoarse. I thought of that moment when we'd been face to face. Was that real? What did that mean?

Unresolved

The book never explains the vision. Carl himself cannot tell whether it was real, and nobody else saw it. The creature was a dead changeling that Houston had been surgically operating on while raving about something he called the Beautiful Place; no connection between that and Li Jun's appearance is ever drawn.

docs.title: Afterwards
docs.text:
Li Jun's sacrifice buys Donut the time she needs, and the guilt lands on everybody. Li Na tells Donut, to her face, that her brother's death is her fault; Donut repeats it to Carl and then adds, "But she's not wrong, either." Carl has no time to grieve — he registers, mid-battle, that "Li Jun had been in charge of these towers" and has to take manual control of them from a menu, then notes flatly: "There wasn't time to grieve the loss of Li Jun."

Zhang, who never got his goodbye, is the one who lets Donut off the hook:

Zhang: Donut. Jun was always afraid he wouldn't do anything important. He was afraid his sister would be lost without him. You helped her get strong enough to protect herself. That would've made him proud, and it makes me proud to have you as a friend.

His sister's response is the rest of the book. She gouges out her own eye and installs his celestial eye in the socket, takes Carl's spare Ring of Divine Suffering to its logical end, and becomes the first crawler ever to max out every base stat — see Li Na.

Sourced from Book 2: Carl's Doomsday Scenario, Book 3: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook, Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade, Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride, and Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Li Na
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: Human Crawler; sister of Li Jun, partied with Zhang
  • Race: A demon-like race — Carl describes "the woman's demonic face," and her passive aura makes her physically untouchable; nobody in the guild can shake her hand without a potion. (Book 3 names the race Changbi; Book 7 never restates it)
  • Class: Not restated in Book 7. (Book 3 gives her class as Slave Driver)
  • Subclass: None stated
  • Level: 84 at the time of the Club Vanquisher broadcast — "number two on the top ten list, passing Prepotente" — and 87 by the end of the book
  • Role: Commander of the 107th White Dragon Urban Defense battalion; runs the Extend Aura synergy tower in Shanty Town; the Princess Posse's builder and jailer
  • Notable spells/abilities: Her Dreads — at-will auras, not counted as offensive magic — including Dark Purpose, Defile Soul, Bleeding Horror and Succulent Decay; ethereal chains, including a once-a-day multi-chain skill she loans Carl by tattoo; flight and new hunting skills after the ball; the Damned status, which lets her enter any temple
  • Notable items: Carl's second Ring of Divine Suffering, looted from King Rust; her dead brother's celestial-tier eye, The Engine of Tomorrow
  • Status: Alive — walks into the stairwell to Floor 10 alone and silent, permanently unable to heal

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Li Na had been a background figure for four books: her brother's blunt, unsettling sister, the one who kept a mantaur alive by cutting it down to a torso on the Iron Tangle. Book 7 puts her at the centre of the floor and then takes her brother away, and what is left is the most powerful crawler in the dungeon and the one Carl uses, at the very end, as the argument against becoming her.

She starts the floor barely speaking to Carl at all — he ate her brother's eye on Floor 8. Katia diagnoses it for him:

"She's not mad at you," Katia said. "She's mad at herself for not protecting her brother. She knows you didn't do it on purpose."

She cannot be recruited into the army normally, because nobody can touch her; Mordecai has to brew a potion that negates aura effects first. The moment she joins, she asks for a job: she and her squad want to build the defences in and around Shanty Town. Carl agrees, and the 107th White Dragons become the Posse's engineers, jailers and urban-defence battalion, with the Prism sergeant Toyotomi running her builder squad.

docs.title: The Dreads
docs.text:
Carl's own aura magic comes from Imani. Li Na's is a different mechanic entirely:

The other crawler who used auras was Li Na.

Hers were very, very different.

The ones she could activate at will were called Dreads.

Dreads normally only affect someone physically touching her, and they do not count as offensive magic — which matters enormously during the ceasefire's magic ban. For the assault on Club Vanquisher, Elle's manager Mistress Tiatha supplies the exploit: Li Na mans an Extend Aura synergy tower in the Shanty Town clock tower, dozens of capacitor wires are strung from the clock arms, and Li Jun and Zhang trail those wires into the club. Anyone within about 20 metres of the wire catches the full effect.

  • Dark Purpose — the one they planned on. Li Na compares it to Donut's Why Are You Hitting Yourself?; Mordecai has never heard of it. Amplified, it is a massacre. Guards tear their own throats open; a mantaur is found with "his own claws buried up through his chin, eyes open with surprise"; ghostly chains drag shrieking apparitions down through the floor. Carl, watching: "Hey, uh, Li Na. That spell isn't exactly what I was expecting."
  • Defile Soul — cycled in next. Its effect is never described on-page.
  • Bleeding Horror — "if someone with bloody hands gets near me, and I have the dread active, it's supposed to turn their blood against them. And then the blood would turn on my enemies." She has never previously got it past level 2 because victims die too fast. Carl runs through a corridor where a ram's own blood is pouring back into his mouth and nose "like liquid mercury."
  • Succulent Decay — "I am turning on the last of my dreads, and I do not know how it will react." The text never shows what it does.

She was never really casting them for Carl. She was power-levelling:

Li Na: Dark Purpose was level 4 when I cast. It is not meant to be used like this, and it leveled even more rapidly than we anticipated. It hit level 15, and I moved to a different dread. I am cycling my dreads and rapidly leveling them all. Right now I am using Defile Soul. Next I will train Bleeding Horror.

Carl asks her to switch back to save his own approach and she refuses on the spot — "I will if I have to, Carl. I need to train, and I can't give up this opportunity" — then gives him a tactically correct reason why her plan is better. Donut yells at her in chat. It does not work.

Her simple, matter-of-fact, almost emotionless delivery was chilling. Christ, I thought. It was like she was a sociopath. She was always so calm. How was it I'd never noticed this before?

The collateral runs on for days: a cleric in the neighbouring Dagda temple boiled himself alive in his own stew.

Naming

The source calls the blood dread Bleeding Horror when Li Na announces her training order, and Blood Horror when she reports it hitting level 15. Both spellings are in the book.

docs.title: Rishi's Arms
docs.text:
Li Na's White Dragons hold the prisoners. When Carl finally goes to the brig to see Rishi — the one captive he had explicitly ordered left alone — the cells are otherwise empty, and Rishi has been mutilated:

Still, someone—clearly Li Na—thought it would be best to take extra precautions and had his four arms removed, which was especially barbaric.

Carl does not confront her about it.

docs.title: The Second Ring
docs.text:
Carl loots a second Ring of Divine Suffering from King Rust's corpse. Li Na asks for it.

When Li Na first approached me and asked if she could have my extra Ring of Divine Suffering, my initial reaction had been fuck no. She was quite possibly the most powerful crawler in the dungeon already, and I'd worried that while it would make her stronger, it'd also drive her to do something crazy.

Only Imani objects. Elle is emphatic the other way — "She can handle it better than you certainly can. And if she can't, at least it'll be the ring that kills her. She's a scary psycho, but at least she's our scary psycho, Carl" — and it is Donut, out loud and without giving a reason, who settles it: "Please, Carl. Please give it to her. Do it as soon as you can." Carl works out why the moment he sees Rishi's cell.

Li Na also asks about the Necklace of Indelible Woe and turns it down, because using it might cost her the level-15 dreads.

docs.title: Her Brother
docs.text:
Li Jun dies in Chapter 68, drawing the god Harpocrates away from Donut's tower with a single unmuted speaker on the back of a cart. Li Na's last words to him are "Jun, no. No!" His last message is to her.

Rosetta's status report an hour later: "I've ordered Li Na to assist the NPCs, but she is currently in a fit of hysterics over the death of her brother." Then she goes dark — off her synergy tower, unreachable, not answering Carl's messages.

She resurfaces in the stairwell of the Nest tower, and Carl finally understands what she meant when she said she was "installing" her brother's eye:

"Holy shit," I exclaimed upon seeing her face. I'd heard her say she was "installing" Li Jun's fake eye into herself, but the meaning hadn't really hit me until that moment.

The front of the woman's demonic face was covered with blood. She'd gouged her own eye out and replaced it with Li Jun's celestial-quality eye. The eye would allow her to slow down time and move with incredible speed.

She has also looted and duplicated the war mage's Hell-Kissed Potion of Conscription, hands Carl the copy, and states her intentions in a flat monotone before walking out:

"I used Jun's scroll of potion duplication on it," Li Na said. She spoke with a dead, chilling calm. "I am going to use the original now on Harpocrates and then I will save Zhang, Elle, Katia, and the others before they, too, fall victim to your chaos."

Carl shouts a warning after her that the level discrepancy could kill her, as it killed the war mage. She does not wait. She uses it correctly, conscripts a god, and spends the next stretch of the book riding Harpocrates like a mount, with Juice Box's changelings climbing on to help hold him.

She also blames Donut for the death, to Donut's face. Donut repeats it to Carl and then defends her: "But she's not wrong, either. I've made a lot of mistakes already today… He was her brother."

docs.title: Three Hundred
docs.text:
Donut's War Crime spell is the endgame: the entire enemy army, thousands of them, welded into a rolling ball. Li Na's contribution is the anvil. She builds a lattice of ethereal chains across the wreckage of Shanty Town — "There were more chains than I thought possible" — anchored to the Nest, and tells Donut to slam the ball into it:

Li Na: Donut, this is all I can build. Do it.

The chains broke one by one. But as they broke, Li Na grew more. With each slam, the survivors who remained stuck to the paw were slammed down again. And again. And each time they pushed through chains, they were cut to pieces.

She had already marked every one of them with the Ring of Divine Suffering — which is why Carl, trying to use his own ring, found he could not.

System message. A crawler has maxed out her base strength. Crawler Li Na now has 300 strength.

System message. A crawler has maxed out her base intelligence. Crawler Li Na now has 300 intelligence.

System message... yeah, I can keep doing this, but she maxed them all. Even Charisma, which is a hard one.

System Message. So, this has never happened before, but a crawler has reached max base stats. She can still raise her stats beyond that with equipment and bonuses and spells, but we don't actually have a plan to deal with this, so I'm gonna have to come up with something.

Carl's reaction is one line: "I felt a deep, deep chill." Donut's is outrage that Li Na did it at level 87 while Donut had to reach 135 to be the strongest crawler in the dungeon.

docs.title: The Debt
docs.text:
The ring's price comes due immediately. Marks that are not cashed in do not expire quietly.

"She used the Ring of Divine Suffering," I said. "But she has a problem. I'm pretty sure she'd marked both Tagg and Fang, but we didn't kill them. They both got away somehow. More might have gotten away, too."

"Uh, oh," Donut said. "Doesn't that mean she can't heal?"

"Yes. And every time she uses her chains, she loses just a little health."

She tears through the Larracos castle looking for them, glowing, not speaking to anyone, and then takes to the woods. Prepotente reports her flying — "She appears to have some new hunting skills along with the ability to fly" — and unable to find the ones she marked. Eighteen of them existed; three survived.

They were King Rust's harem, non-combatants he had negotiated into the dungeon under a private deal with the AI, and they reached the Cosmic Lounge in the Desperado Club and went back to the 18th floor.

"They are gone, and they are forever out of Li Na's reach. She now has a condition that will never allow her to heal. Luckily for her, her health is still several times that of all of us combined. But she will need to be very careful, despite her massively increased stats."

Donut, unable to resist: "I TOLD YOU THE RING WAS BAD NEWS, CARL."

What Book 7 actually says

The permanent no-healing condition is a Ring of Divine Suffering penalty, not a side effect of the transplanted eye — it applies because three crawlers she marked escaped the floor alive. Book 7 states the condition itself as permanent ("forever out of Li Na's reach," "a condition that will never allow her to heal") and says nothing further about it.

docs.title: Bigs
docs.text:
Not everyone accepts the grief as an excuse. When Li Na hangs in the air over the column, twenty feet up, glaring down at Louis — the last person still carrying one of her marks — the sluggalette Kandy "Bigs" Newton growls at her:

"She's not a bad guy," I said. "She's just going through some shit. Her brother died."

"No, she's a bad guy," Bigs said. "You know what she did to Sneaky Tyler C?"

"Uh..." I said. I was assuming Tyler C was another sluggalo. "No?"

"She tied a potion to him and then ordered him to run right into the god. He blew up the moment he touched the thing. That's what I heard. It was a bitch-ass move. I don't like her."

docs.title: What Carl Takes From It
docs.text:
In the last chapter, with twenty thousand surrendered mercenaries milling around Larracos and the Ring of Divine Suffering still in his inventory, Carl works through the same maths Li Na did:

My initial instinct was to kill them. I could mark them like Li Na had, and I could kill them all, raising my stats to 300 across the board just like she had. I knew a lot of people following my progress would be enraged at me not doing exactly that. They would call me stupid. They would be disappointed in the lack of blood I shed, and they would angrily unfollow my feed because I was not the monster they hoped I would be.

Fuck you all, I thought. Fuck you all.

One look at Li Na, and I knew that path, that slope was too steep. Survival had more than one meaning.

He holds the ring up to Donut, and she eats it.

docs.title: Exit
docs.text:
Li Na goes down to Floor 10 by herself. Zhang, still partied with her, goes in alone too.

Tran went into the stairwell, as did so many others, including Zhang, who went in alone. I'd asked him if he was going to take a deal, and he said he didn't know. Li Na remained partied with him, but she hadn't spoken to him at all. She, too, had gone into the stairwell without saying a word.

See also Li Jun, Carl, and the Zhang entry in Supporting Cast.

docs.title: Book 8: A Parade of Horribles
docs.text: Li Na's permanent no-healing condition from Book 7 — the price of marking eighteen crawlers with her Ring of Divine Suffering and losing three of them off the floor alive — becomes the engine of one of Book 8's central subplots: an escape attempt built entirely around her.

docs.title: The Cleaner-Bot Plan
docs.text:
The party engineers Li Na's escape through a "cleaner-bot exploit" into a hidden pocket dimension called the Pineapple Cabaret, hoping that leaving the dungeon entirely might stop her condition from worsening, or possibly cure it outright — though the text is explicit that this is only a theory, never a confirmed fix. Li Na goes first, alone, as the test case: if she signals back that it's safe, the rest of a much larger group of volunteers will follow the same route.

Mordecai rigs a signal system for exactly this purpose — a potted cactus in the guildhall, tied to her life and her location, that only he can read:

Mordecai: Okay, guys. A single flower just bloomed on the cactus.

It had worked. A single flower was the code meaning that Li Na had made it to the Pineapple Cabaret and that it was safe to bring the others.

The system's own caution, delivered in the same message where it hands Carl the choice: "Beware exits that seem too good to be true."

docs.title: 227 More
docs.text:
Li Na's confirmed safe arrival opens the floodgates. Using the same method — and a second, larger cleaner bot recruited from another crawler — the guild sends a mass wave of volunteers after her:

Imani: It went smoothly. Your cleaner bot could only fit forty people, but the one from Bobby Montague, the Illusionist guy with the tall hair, managed to fit 105. The total number sent to the Pineapple Cabaret is 227, not including Na. Zhang, Tran, Daniel, Archie, Randall 3. All gone.

Mordecai builds a "Garden of Deliverance" — a terrarium of over two hundred individually-tied potted plants, one per volunteer, so the guild has some way of tracking who lives, dies, or gets out even though "even the showrunners can't see what's going on in there." Li Na's own cactus remains distinct from the rest, "the only one with the complicated messaging system," since she was the proof of concept the whole plan was staked on.

Confirmed: safe arrival, not a cure

Book 8 confirms only that Li Na (and, after her, 227 more volunteers) reached the Pineapple Cabaret alive. Nothing in the text confirms her permanent no-healing condition is cured, reduced, or otherwise changed by leaving the dungeon — that remains an open, unconfirmed hope, not a resolved fact.

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin and Book 8: A Parade of Horribles.

docs.title: Louis Santiago
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: Human Crawler. Still human as of Book 7, per Eileithyia's own ruling — despite a transplanted naiad heart and lungs and a permanent set of gills
  • Class: Pest Exterminator → Extermination Professional (Book 5, Floor 6 specialization) — grants a 0.5% insta-kill chance on same-level-or-lower mobs
  • Subclass: None stated
  • Level: 22ish (Book 4) → 42 (Book 5); not stated in Book 7
  • Rank (Book 7): Army Air General of the Princess Posse — a rank unique to him
  • Marital status: Engaged to Juice Box from Book 4; married to her in a changeling "small wedding" in Book 7 and divorced by her before the floor ends. Becomes the father of Katia's son as part of her exit from the dungeon
  • Party: Katia's splinter team
  • Notable spells/abilities: Tent the House — an area-of-effect potion-delivery spell, castable once every six hours, expanded further when cast from an airborne platform; a poison cloud attack used repeatedly in Book 7
  • Notable items: A trap-module boombox rig (rigged from Carl's own trap modules); the airship Party Planner, a Casket in the Sky-class tilt-rotor stealth light bomber (Book 7, from a celestial box — destroyed in Chapter 66), plus the Airship Portal guild upgrade that hangars it
  • Status: Alive. Five player-killer skulls from Book 6; vivisected by the Reavers and rebuilt by Mordecai in Book 7; descends to Floor 10 with the party

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Louis is a comic-relief lieutenant who becomes one of Carl and Donut's most consistently loyal allies from Book 4 onward, alongside his best friend Firas. Both become the party's dedicated pilots for the flying house (the Twister) on Floor 5, and Louis proposes to Juice Box by the end of that book.

docs.title: Role in the Story — Book 5
docs.text:
Louis fights with Katia's splinter team through Floor 6's hunter war, using his Tent the House spell to deliver Mordecai's anti-undead herbicide against the floor's world-quest "Odious Creepers." He co-produces (with Donut) the Butcher's Masquerade's viral pet-show entrance for Mongo — complete with a smuggled trap-module boombox and a full moonwalking reveal — and, while stuck at the party, coordinates by chat with the Sledge during the desperate effort to smuggle a refugee changeling community (disguised as elves) into the High Elf castle's sentinel towers. The operation goes badly: the Twister itself is boarded and overrun by mantis nymphs, and the changelings aboard it shape-shift into birds and flee under their own power rather than escaping with it. It's the Sledge alone — along with the gnome Bonnie and two rescued Ursine cubs, who never make it aboard the Twister at all — who ends up riding the High Elf castle itself down to Floor 9 once he casts Zerzura on it in the battle's final moments.

He's devastated when the Sledge, forced to abandon the doomed Twister, instead crashes the airship into the last two active castle turrets still firing on him, Bonnie, and the cubs on the castle roof — and again when his best friend Firas dies in the battle's climax, having secretly been planning to be Louis's best man at Louis and Juice Box's eventual wedding (and had asked Katia to secretly sew the tuxedoes as a surprise).

docs.title: Role in the Story — Book 6
docs.text: Book 6 gives Louis the best supporting arc in the book.

docs.title: Christmas
docs.text:
Two hours after fighting a hydra head wearing his own mother's face, Louis throws a Christmas party in the guild hall. He dates it off Chris's iPod (March 20th), wears "an idiotic Christmas sweater featuring a mooning Santa Clause," and bribes Mordecai's changeling kids with Vietnamese candy the strippers helped wrap.

Carl asks whether this isn't all a little inappropriate, and Louis — for the first and only time in the series — gets angry at him:

"Oh my god. Look, man," he said, suddenly serious. There was something else there, something I'd never seen from the large man. Anger. He had tears in his eyes… "You think I don't know? That last party sucked, man. My best friend died. And after today… Imani's squad doesn't have a key. Tserendolgor doesn't have a key. Lots of squads don't. I'm not stupid. None of us are. We all know what happens next. It's going to be terrible, and some of us are going to die. And if we survive? We go down to the next floor, and we do it all over again. I have a whole, entire army of elves who want to kill me on the ninth floor. Britney can't stop crying. Tran just watched a memory of his own mother tell him he's not welcome home anymore. Katia is struggling every day, and Bautista is having a nervous breakdown. And every time I look at you, I get scared that you're going to go insane and kill everybody in the room because your eyes are getting wilder and wilder by the day."

He lifted a shaking finger and pointed it into my chest. "But not tonight. None of that is going to matter tonight. I don't care what you say or what you think. I don't care what day it really is. Tonight it's fucking Christmas, and we are going to have fun and drink some goddamned eggnog and open presents."

Carl folds, in the only way he knows how:

"This isn't Christmas," I said, turning to face Louis. He swallowed as he met my eyes. I pulled a turkey corpse from my inventory and held it out. "Not until we eat one of these."

Carl and Imani are both still carrying their unopened presents from Santa when the floor collapses.

docs.title: Five Skulls, and a Sixth
docs.text:
Louis gets his first player-killer skulls on Floor 8 — five of them, all from one attack — and, per Katia, is not handling it well.

Which is why, when Carl drops Sister Ines unconscious with a Nighty-Night wand and the party has to finish her, Louis shoulders him out of the way:

"I'll do it," Louis said, pushing me aside. "I already have five player skulls and none of you guys do. Trust me. You want to put that off as long as possible." Before I could object, he pulled a dagger from his inventory. "Sorry cat lady. I never met you, but you need to go if we want to save everybody else." He took the knife and plunged it directly into her chest.

A marked-for-death indicator — a spinning squiggle like a tornado — appears over his head the instant the knife lands, and music starts to play.

"Uh-oh," Louis said.

The death of the bard has angered her celestial Patron. She is coming to seek revenge.

The Goddess Ysalte has entered the realm.

Ysalte hunts him personally through the rest of the battle — "Find that one with my mark upon him, and kill him!" — and he survives her. Paz Lo kills the goddess, and Louis collects on the curse:

Louis: Dude! I got a Celestial box for outliving a goddess who has a marked for death curse on me!

He finishes the book carrying an unconscious Carl through the burning city in his arms.

docs.title: Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin
docs.text: Louis gets married, gets divorced, gets shot down, gets cut open, gets a naiad's heart and lungs, and ends the book as the father of Katia's child. It is the most that happens to anyone in the book who is not a warlord.

docs.title: Army Air General
docs.text:
The Princess Posse's warlord menu gives him a rank nobody else has: Army Air General. His celestial box from Floor 8 pays out in two pieces — a tier-three guild upgrade called an Airship Portal, an elevator from the guild hall to a dimensional hangar, and the airship itself.

Casket in the Sky. Party Planner. Tilt Rotor Stealth Light Bomber.

This aircraft is owned by crawler Army Air General Louis Santiago 2.

Casket in the Sky is the model name; Party Planner is what Louis calls his. The system describes it as "a lighter-than-air, long-range death delivery system" and is candid about the tradeoff: forward and aft anti-air guns, rudimentary shields, and nothing else. "Seriously. It would take a pilot with gonads the size of bowling balls to fly this thing into a heavily fortified area." Every bomb dropped from it gains 50% yield. Donut's verdict on the name is a flat "Casket in the Sky?"; Carl's is "Jesus, Louis. This thing looks like a death trap."

He flies it low and fast on bomb runs across every front of the war, carrying fifty of Carl's thermobaric charges at one point, and using it to deliver the opening barrage that cracks the southern trench line — bombing the ground in front of the enemy trenches rather than the trenches themselves, to strip their traps and bury their mages in dirt.

docs.title: The Small Wedding
docs.text:
Chapter 10, in the grimy entrance bar of the Desperado Club, after Clarabelle has banned every crawler in the dungeon from the club proper.

Changeling weddings come in two parts. The small wedding is the legally binding one: no rings, no officiant, no singing, no ring bearer, to Donut's considerable disgust. The Confirmation a month later is the party. Mordecai explains the catch — part of the small wedding is signing divorce papers, which expire in a month if unfiled. For that month either party can walk away with no consequence.

Louis is not exactly swept up in it. He agrees because the marriage "bonds the houses" and keeps the NPC team on side:

Louis: She thinks it's important. We need them on our side, and if this helps, I'll do it. If they turn against us, we're screwed. This will help. We need each other.

Donut coaches him into the proposal by chat ("DON'T BE ALL CARL ABOUT IT. BE ROMANTIC"), and he manages it, after asking Juice Box to change into someone else first. The ceremony itself takes almost no time; the vows are whispered in each other's ears, to be repeated aloud at the Confirmation that never happens.

"I wish my mom was here," he whispered.

docs.title: Shot Down
docs.text:
Chapter 66. On his second sortie of the general offensive, a gravity-magic dragon over Reaver territory tears Party Planner in half. Louis reports it himself, mid-fall, in the chat:

Louis: A little busy now, Carl. Feather falling... Party Planner is dead. Ripped in half... Hit the dragon with missiles, and it just pissed it off... It cast a spell, and I tried to dodge. It ripped Party Planner down the middle. Dropped the bombs before they were armed. I'm sorry... They didn't go off. I'm falling through the air right now. Gonna land right on the Reaver castle... I think my door gunners are dead... Glad Bonnie and Skarn weren't here... He was right... That cop's husband. I'm sorry... The feral god is still there a mile west of the castle. I see him just sitting there. Dragon still flying above... I'm going to hit the castle by myself. Tell Katia when she wakes up that I'm sorry to be such a fuckup...

"That cop's husband" is a Book 7 reveal, delivered second-hand by Katia: as a child, Louis was protected by a police officer who was shot and killed doing it, and at her funeral her husband said something cruel enough to Louis that he has carried it his whole life.

docs.title: What the Reavers Did
docs.text:
He lands in the middle of the Reaver castle, is tracked by its security, and disappears into a cell for the better part of the floor — unconscious, health bar untouched, because he is hooked to a machine keeping him alive. Juice Box, reaching him first, describes what she found:

"They were doing surgery on him. He was... cut open. His heart has been replaced. His lungs have been replaced. It looked like they were getting ready to replace his brain, but we got to him in time. I had to heal him, but when I did it, it didn't regrow his heart or lungs."

The replacement organs are mechanical with biological threads woven through them, and the biology isn't his:

"It's not Louis. It's... It's pieces of Tagg."

Epitome Tagg, warlord of the Dream, has grafted himself into Louis's chest cavity and controls his vital organs from inside them — the same trick Warlord Fang used to survive inside the dragon. Tagg's leverage is stated plainly in the warlord chat: "Fuck off. I control his vital organs. You try to remove me, and I will shut him down." See Tagg's own page for the cyborg reveal and how it resolves.

Juice Box gets him out by taking a hunter wraith form, possessing his unconscious body, walking it to a teleport, and dumping his No Disassemble charges behind her; the detonation kills Warlord Fang and finishes the Reavers.

docs.title: Heart, Lungs, and Gills
docs.text:
Chapter 84, with Emberus counting down the floor's last hour, the party performs open-chest surgery on Louis in a field tent — thirty minutes they do not have.

The donor organs come from Princess Lunette, the naiad flesh golem in Carl's inventory: Signet's mother, originally one of Edgar's tattoos, handed to Carl at the end of the Butcher's Masquerade as the body Samantha was eventually going to inhabit. It is Samantha who proposes spending it, knowing exactly what it costs her:

"If we do this, that means you won't get your body back. At least not for a while."

She nodded solemnly. "I know. It's okay. Louis deserves it more than I do."

Mordecai cuts and sews. Edgar directs. Donut pours the healing potion and Mordecai's Special Brew. Carl and Tipid hold the ribcage open against the healing trying to close it. Imani, Rosetta and Elle extract the naiad organs. Juice Box, shifted into a Fleshmancer form, casts the spell that makes them take. Bucket Boy yanks the old organs free — Mordecai can't, without it counting as an attack. Mongo eats the discarded plastic heart and lungs, and the system credits him with killing Tagg.

The complication is that Lunette was a full naiad, so the organs are water-only. Mordecai's fix is a tiny device from Carl's inventory:

"It was the kua-tin rebreather I'd taken from Loita's body after I'd assassinated her."

He slits the bronchial, sews the rebreather inside it, casts Water Breathing from a scroll, and grows Louis a set of gills, tubed directly to the transplanted organs and held open with stops until they set. They are permanent. Louis spends the rest of the book with a hand around his own throat, coughing water.

The Loita reference is the same Loita

This is the Borant administrator Carl assassinated on Floor 5 with the rigged Veriluxx toy in Book 4 — not a namesake. Book 7 states it twice: "Loita the kua-tin I'd assassinated on the fifth floor," and, at the surgery, "the kua-tin rebreather I'd taken from Loita's body after I'd assassinated her." Carl looted her rebreather off her corpse at the time and has carried it since. Loita was kua-tin and wore the rebreather because kua-tin are aquatic, which is why it fits a naiad's lungs.

docs.title: Divorced, and a Father
docs.text:
Juice Box files the divorce papers inside the month, and she does it because of what the wraith form showed her while she was saving him. The Inevitable Ruin is a curse laid on hunter wraiths: when they possess someone, it tells them the truth about what they possessed. What it told her about Louis was that "he's terrified of me. The truth is he's not in love with me," and that he believes he has a special ability that makes NPCs fall for him, so he will never trust what she feels. She leaves rather than be another monster in his life. Louis's account of it is three sentences:

"Juice Box left me," Louis said, coming to sit down in the tent… "She gave me divorce papers."

Minutes later, Eileithyia tells Katia she must name a human father for the child that will carry her out of the dungeon, and that it cannot be Carl. Katia asks Louis. His first concern is whether the gills disqualify him.

"Uh," Louis said. He reached up and touched his neck. "Am I still human?"

"That's actually a good question," Donut muttered. "The last thing Katia needs is a baby with flippers."

Eileithyia smiled, and she put her hand on Louis's hand. "Of course you are. And a good soul at that."

"Then sure, I guess. I mean, if she'll have me."

The goddess confirms it will be a boy. Louis's reply: "Spoilers."

He walks into the Floor 10 stairwell mourning his airship — "I really wish I could've kept Party Planner" — and Carl tells him Florin stole a plane.

Sourced from Book 4: The Gate of the Feral Gods, Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade, Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride, and Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Lucia Mar
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Age: About 13
  • Likely origin: South America (broadcast context, unconfirmed)
  • Signature gear: A mace and a full set of glowing silver armor, worn under her original yellow-and-blue soccer jersey as a tabard
  • Pets: Two rottweilers, Cici and Gustavo 3 — both dead by the end of Book 7 (Cici decapitated by Donut's Hole in Book 5; Gustavo 3 killed by Carl's pet Sir Rendlegore in Book 7)
  • Notable stat: Very high Dexterity (wall-running, flips, acrobatic combat); over 200 player-killer skulls plus 20 dead hunters by Book 7
  • Status (Book 7): Alive. Captured and conscripted by Carl on Floor 9, then released when the floor ends; she descends to Floor 10 partied with Florin. She is also a dead-man's switch for roughly 120,000 children held on the Earth surface, and by her own account an ally of "the Eulogist"
  • Type/Class/Subclass: Not shown in Book 1 → Lajabless race / Black Inquisitor General class (cleric/mage/warrior triple class), revealed Book 2
  • Level: 29 — 1st on the Floor 3 leaderboard, the highest-ranked crawler shown
  • Notable spells/abilities: No named spells shown; a personal magical shield noticed late in Book 1; her Lajabless race halves her strength but doubles spell power in human form, and the reverse in her skeletal "goat-leg" form
  • Notable items: A mace; a full set of glowing silver armor; a personal magical shield

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Lucia Mar is never met directly by Carl — she exists entirely as a recurring figure on the in-universe broadcast, one of the season's breakout stars and a running benchmark Carl measures his own progress against. She's first shown in an early recap tearing through a cow-sized spider with her two rottweilers before graduating to a mace and full magical armor, still worn over her original soccer jersey.

docs.title: Cici & Gustavo 3
docs.text: Her two rottweilers are dungeon "familiars" rather than standard pet-class mobs, which is why she can have two of them at once (Mordecai later explains this exception applies to certain classes, races, or unusually high-Charisma crawlers). Cici wears a chainmail sweater; Gustavo 3 develops the ability to shoot lightning when he barks. Per Carl's naming-convention guess, "3" indicates he's the third dog named Gustavo (without a surname) to enter the dungeon.

docs.title: Recurring Broadcast Presence
docs.text:
Lucia Mar reappears across multiple recap episodes throughout Book 1:

  • Shown obliterating a nest of monsters before descending a stairwell, then whisked away for a guest appearance on Dungeon Crawler After Hours with Odette immediately before Carl and Donut's own appearance — one of her dogs attacks a producer backstage.
  • By roughly the book's midpoint, she has four player-killer skulls by her name, with the circumstances never explained on-air.
  • After Carl's "Pork Boy" incident goes viral, his appearance fee is reported to have doubled to the point of equaling hers — used as an explicit measure of how famous he's become.
  • Later shown smashing a Brindled Vespa with a personal magical shield Carl hadn't previously noticed her have.

docs.title: Role in the Story
docs.text: Lucia Mar never interacts with Carl directly, but functions as his constant point of comparison for how a "successful" crawler is supposed to look — decked out in flashy magical gear, high Dexterity, camera-ready — which Carl explicitly contrasts with his own scrappy, unarmed, improvised approach.

docs.title: Book 2: Race/Class Reveal
docs.text: On Floor 3, the recap show reveals Lucia Mar's choices: race Lajabless, one of the most extreme options shown — she spends half the day as a beautiful adult woman (double spell power, half strength) and the other half with a skull face and a transformed goat leg (double strength, half spell power, and a permanent limp that ends her wall-running). Her class, a triple cleric/mage/warrior hybrid called Black Inquisitor General, is described by Mordecai as making her likely "the most powerful crawler in this game." By the time Floor 3 collapses, she's ranked 1st on the leaderboard at Level 29, ahead of every other named crawler including Hekla and Carl. Donut, jealous, calls her "awful" and "ugly" on-air.

docs.title: Book 2: Desperado Club Incident & the Feud
docs.text: Lucia Mar's dogs go berserk inside the Desperado Club's pet playroom, killing two attendants and another pet before breaking loose onto the dance floor; while the room is frozen by one of her spells, she steals liquor and kills an elite gnoll with her mace, getting her club membership permanently revoked. The incident (and Donut's own drunken, overheard insult of the dogs — "bitch-ass rottweilers") is spun by the broadcast into a manufactured rivalry, "Princess Donut Versus Cici and Gustavo 3." Confronted about it on the arena show Knuckle Cracking, Lucia Mar — in her skull-faced Lajabless form — threatens to kill Donut and "rip Carl to pieces" for his gear; Mordecai confirms the two parties will eventually be forced together for a televised confrontation, but not before Floor 6 at the earliest.

docs.title: Book 5: The Fight with Donut, and the Voices in Her Head
docs.text:
Lucia Mar finally collides with Carl and Donut directly on Floor 6, seizing an entire village (already named "Alucarda" — much to Donut's annoyance that she didn't get to name it herself) and setting a network of saferoom teleport traps as an ambush. While Carl is pulled away to a mandatory intergalactic fan convention, Donut faces her — and her rottweilers, Cici and Gustavo 3 — alone. Caught by a snare trap in Lucia's own treehouse pub, she survives Cici's lunge behind a stacked Entourage illusion (with an invisibility potion layered onto her own "copy"), then casts a single Hole beneath her own feet to drop straight through the floor to the ground below and break the snare. When Cici sticks her head down through that same hole hunting for her, Donut simply snaps the spell off from below — decapitating the dog with the closing hole rather than a second, separate cast. The recap footage of the fight becomes one of the season's biggest broadcast moments.

The fight reveals something new and unsettling: Lucia's personality visibly flips mid-conversation between a genuinely scared, homesick child (in one aside, speaking with a Dutch accent and naming herself "Jill," a name Florin later confirms belongs to a real, ten-year-old crawler) and her usual violent, "Lajabless kid warlord" persona — implying multiple people, possibly children, are somehow sharing or fighting over control of her body via her dogs. Florin, confronting her at the Butcher's Masquerade, concludes the dog Gustavo is the one truly "in charge" and that the real Lucia/Jill can only surface in short bursts. She escapes the masquerade's final battle using a pre-set teleport trap before the boss fight even begins, avoiding the "Cage Fight Extreme" that kills several other crawlers.

docs.title: Book 6: The Battle of Beijing, and a Threat
docs.text: Lucia Mar spends Book 6 entirely offstage and is one of its most consequential figures anyway. She sits at #4 on the leaderboard and, per Florin, buys up every teleport trap and stairwell-chamber item that appears on the market: "Teleport traps and alcohol are the only things she purchases." Florin's read on her, before the phases split: "She has good days and bad days, and it's been more bad than good lately."

docs.title: The Battle of Beijing
docs.text:
It happens off-page. The only direct glimpse is an announcer's aside — "We are interrupting that one-sided Lucia Mar slaughter in Beijing to bring you whatever this is" — and Li Jun's account of the aftermath:

"It was Lucia Mar." He swallowed. "They're calling it the Battle of Beijing. Lucia, she never really collected any cards. She refused to play it. She got the six totems they automatically gave her, but they were all low-level monsters. And whenever a battle started, she discarded the first one, and she played the rest until her hand was empty which allowed her to use her spells and magic and inventory. She and her dog went in and killed everything."

"She killed so many people. She set up a teleport trap, and Fang's team got caught up in it. He had a key. She killed him and his wife and took it. After that, we thought she'd already gone down the stairs, but when we got there, she was waiting for us. She can hide her presence now."

docs.title: The Doggie Doors
docs.text:
Before going down the stairs she drops five Tier-3 Doggie Door personal-space upgrades on the ground and leaves them for Carl's guild. Li Jun: "She said Florin had messaged her before he'd gone down the stairs and told her to help us."

Nobody can work out where she got them. Katia: "She shouldn't have had one, let alone five of them. It's a tier-3. Mordecai says these shouldn't be available until the ninth floor. He thinks Lucia stole them when she went on a show or something." Imani prices a guild-wide rollout at twenty-five million gold; they install one in Imani's room and hold the other four. Elle, on what it means: "It would've changed everything… We've been chasing a fast travel system since the whole guild system opened."

docs.title: The Threat
docs.text:
Li Jun holds one detail back for Carl alone:

Li Jun: This is just for you, Carl. There's more. Lucia dropped the upgrades, and she said she was helping us because Florin had asked, but before she went down the stairs, she went from really friendly to mean again, and she said she was saving something special for herself because she had a score to settle with Donut and that she would be seeing her on the next floor. She said she was going to kill both Donut and her pet dinosaur. That's why my sister wanted to fight her.

Reported, not quoted

The threat reaches Carl — and the reader — only through Li Jun's paraphrase. Lucia herself never appears on the page in Book 6.

docs.title: Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin
docs.text:
Book 7 finally pays off the threat Li Jun carried down from Floor 8. Lucia comes for Donut and Mongo, she gets close, and the encounter ends with her losing her last dog, losing her autonomy, and handing Carl the worst piece of information in the book.

She spends the ceasefire drinking. Li Jun’s early sighting: “She’s here in Shanty Town right now with her dog, drinking at the Possum Envy right on the edge of the border with the robot team. The Reavers. One of the new guys tried to recruit her, and she almost ripped his head off.” She refuses every recruiter, hides her position from the Find Crawler skill, and joins no army. Zev will not even try to warn her: “Lucia doesn’t respond to messages anymore. She was never my client, thank goodness.”

docs.title: The Nest Tower
docs.text:
Chapter 70. Donut is alone at the top of the Nest, the Princess Posse’s tallest synergy tower in Shanty Town, sniping the Larracos defence towers while two gods fight below. Lucia walks in through the front door. The garrison dies in the time it takes to send three messages:

Toyotomi: No. It is a crawler. A woman with a dog. She’s coming in.

This message is from a deceased mercenary.

Sergeant Bret S: We need backup! Backup!

Bomo: Will stop her now.

This message is from a deceased mercenary.

Bomo — one of the four cretin mercenaries Quasar negotiated out of the Syndicate back in Book 5 — and the Sai sergeant Toyotomi are both killed, along with a squad of mages. Carl finds them on his way up: “I spared a quick, sad glance for Toyotomi, Bomo, and the defending mages, all of whom were cleaved right in half with a spell.” Toyotomi is dead for good; Bomo would regenerate on the 10th floor, but the guild no longer holds his contract.

Lucia also drops a net over the tower so Donut cannot teleport out, then starts climbing. What she wants is stated plainly: “Give me your dinosaur, and I will leave. It is justice I seek. Nothing more.” Donut answers by activating Donkey Kong — a last-ditch defence that turns the tower’s stairs into a ramp and rolls barrels down it — and holds her off for several minutes while Carl levitates, bombs a theatre, accidentally triggers the entire Larracos city defence system, and fights his way in behind her.

docs.title: Conscripted
docs.text:
The fight ends by accident. Donut throws Gustavo 3 down the ramp, Lucia goes with him, and the two of them bowl into Carl halfway up, along with Raul — the crab from Donut’s Floor 8 card deck, now mythic-rarity and level 110, who pins Lucia in the entrance hall while announcing his own magnificence.

Carl uses the potion Li Na had just duplicated for him: a Hell-Kissed Potion of Conscription, level 18, looted from a dead war mage and brewed in the Nothing by Krakaren Prime. The item text notes it “will work against pretty much any non-affiliated entities, regardless of their protections, including most deities.”

I smashed the screaming, Hell-kissed Conscription potion against Lucia’s head.

The potion worked. A pink glow appeared around Lucia’s dot.

Under Orders appears over her head, her terrified act drops instantly, and she spends the next several minutes trying and failing to attack him. He orders her protections down — a list the warlord menu shows as astonishingly long — and sits with her on the floor. His observation, examining her: “Through the stench of burned hair, I could smell sweat and alcohol. But there was something else, too. A faint perfume. A sweet one. The kind a child would pick.”

docs.title: Diah
docs.text:
Carl is about to mark her for death when the thing Florin has been warning about for two books surfaces and speaks:

“Sir,” she said. Her eyes had changed. Her voice had taken on a raspy quality. “My name is Diah. Lucia is with Alexandro. And Alexandro is only here when the dogs are close. My name is Diah. We are in the dark. You need to wait until the dog is close, and Lucia will be back. Wait until she is back. Please, sir. Please.”

Under a direct order to tell the truth, she confirms it, and describes where “we” are:

“I... I. Yes. Sir. Please. We are in the dark, and it’s so cold. Sometimes we can hear them talk. We can hear them whispering. It’s like there’s a river running through our room, and if we touch it, it hurts. They say such sad things. When the dog wanders off, Lucia fades, and one of us takes over, and we can see again. We take turns. Sometimes it’s day, and we can see the light.”

Carl cancels the death mark. He never gets to ask a follow-up question.

docs.title: Rend Kills the Last Dog
docs.text:
Gustavo 3 gets to Mongo. Carl, pinned by a gale-strike tower with a shattered arm, watching the dog and the dinosaur between him and safety, thinks: She’s never going to forgive me. This is what will break her.

Then the meatball arrives.

A terrible, deep giggling filled the night.

The dark, round silhouette appeared above the ridge. Rend.

Carl casts Hi-Yo Silver to yank his pet toward him, and Rend uses the only skill he has on the way past:

The back half of Gustavo 3, the second of Lucia Mar’s two rottweilers, terror of the dungeon, exploded in a red mist as Rend rushed right up to me, stopping inches from my face.

“Good boy,” I gasped at Rend.

Mongo’s throat is torn open and his health is at a sliver. Lucia — still conscripted, and for a moment genuinely herself — drops to her knees and pours a pet healing potion into him, sobbing “You did it. You did it.” Donut’s thanks, later: “Thank you, Rend. I still think you’re disgusting, but you saved my boy’s life, and I will never forget that.” Rend belches in her face.

docs.title: “Now You Can’t Kill Me”
docs.text:
Seconds after saving Mongo, her posture changes, and she delivers the book’s parting shot:

“You should’ve killed us both when there was still a connection,” the girl said to me. “Now it’s too late. Now the Eulogist has another ally in the dungeon, and now you can’t kill me. Not unless you want all the children of Earth to die.” She shook her head and walked off.

Zev fills in the rest, badly and reluctantly. Lucia’s presence in the crawl was originally a glitch; Borant chose to leave her in once she started earning, and the AI now says it is “unable to extract her.” What nobody understood until Gustavo 3 died is what is tied to her:

Zev: It’s complicated, Carl. It’s not all the children. Just the ones that tried to get into the dungeon. And it’s only half of those. All the ones who were in a specific wing. They’re on the surface in the kinder facility.

Carl: So what happens if she dies?

Zev: As of about five minutes ago, we thought the glitch would self-correct and release everyone. That’s what’s supposed to happen. Now? We don’t know for certain. The Eulogist is another name for the AI in the center system. We don’t know how it’s all connected for certain. But now we think... we think if she goes, they all go.

Carl: How many is it?

Zev: I shouldn’t be telling you any of this.

Carl: How many fucking children is it?

Zev: About 120,000. Give or take a few.

Carl’s response: “I almost killed her, Zev. You almost let me kill her.” And then: “She’s a goddamn dead man’s switch. A psychotic one. And she just lost her bodyguard. Don’t let her leave. Keep her safe.” Zev’s answer: “It’s out of my control, Carl.”

Unresolved

“The Eulogist” is the name for the AI of the centre system, and it runs through the whole book attached to the residual Agatha, the Nebular cult and the Open Intellect — see Game Mechanics. What Lucia’s alliance with it consists of, who “Diah” and “Alexandro” are, how children came to be inside her head, and why the dogs govern which of them is driving are all raised and none are answered.

docs.title: Afterwards
docs.text:
The conscription only runs to the end of the floor. Lucia spends the rest of the book in an interview room with the liaisons — Florin, who has appointed himself her keeper, hopes “they talk her into taking a deal at the beginning of the 10th. If not, I will volunteer to keep her safe.” Jurgen the barbarian, whose pregnant wife Heidi is in the same kinder facility, attaches himself to the same job: “if Lucia’s fate is tied to that kinder facility where they’re keeping all the kids and the pregnant women, he’ll die protecting the girl.”

The last sight of her on the ninth floor is in the rubble of Larracos:

Lucia Mar was here, sitting on the ground, sobbing. Florin, Jurgen, and Imani surrounded her, talking.

They were trying to convince her to take a deal. I hoped it would work.

It does not, quite:

Florin had talked Lucia Mar into partying with him. He said she’d agreed to take a deal, but she’d been sketchy.

None of us believed she actually would. And as a result, he would not take one, either.

Sourced from Book 1: The Apocalypse Will Be Televised, Book 2: Carl’s Doomsday Scenario, Book 5: The Butcher’s Masquerade, Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride, and Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Milk
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: NPC — an indentured former crawler, guildmaster inside Club Vanquisher
  • Race: Xenopus — a winged clawed-frog race chosen in the dungeon. Birth race: Vesper (a bat). Carl reads her on sight as “half frog, half bat”
  • Class: Cartographer
  • Subclass: None stated
  • Level: Top level 73 during her own crawl. No current level is shown
  • Role: Guildmaster of both hidden guilds on the club’s second floor — the Cartography (Map-Making) Guild and the Calligrapher’s Guild; author of the 6th edition of The Dungeon Anarchist’s Cookbook
  • Notable spells/abilities: Words of Power — calligraphy magic, written onto skin or objects. She scrawls a power word on her own wrist to survive a demon’s fire, etches one on her own throat to magically amplify her voice, and writes them over a tattoo to boost a spell’s level. She can glide on her wings, and long ago wrote a scroll that mutes the dungeon’s announcements to her
  • Notable items: None worn. She gives Carl 825 ml of Stayfast Ink and an Adept’s Fountain Pen, and keeps the maps of Club Vanquisher’s hidden entrances and exits
  • Status: Alive and, by the end of Book 7, free — “I fulfilled my contract. I still have to live out the season, but I can leave after this.” She stays behind on Floor 9 rather than transferring to the 12th

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Milk is the cookbook author who was in reach the entire time. Her contract, per her status card, holds her until “her services are used at least 333 times in the dungeon” — and at the point of her interlude, across an indefinite number of seasons, the counter reads 6. Nobody comes to the calligraphy guild. Nobody comes to the cartography guild next door. Both doors are hidden, and she has not had a one-on-one with a floor supervisor in over fifty seasons.

So she sleeps. Her own interlude opens with her waking up starving in a dusty nest of straw, her wings sore and atrophied from disuse, unsure what season it is:

Warning. Your health levels are low due to starvation. You are not allowed to self-terminate, and if you expire due to starvation, you will be saved and time will be added to your indentureship contract.

“Oh, fuck off,” she muttered.

The self-assessment she cannot get away from:

You were a crawler. You fought. You were part of something, once. And now, look at you. All you do is sleep. You’ve missed entire seasons more times than you can count. You’re a coward, that’s what you are. When was the last time you even tried to help someone? Your family would be ashamed.

docs.title: The Door Opens
docs.text:
Her interlude is set during Book 4, on Floor 5, and the crawlers who kick her awake are Miriam Dom and Prepotente, on the run after Miriam’s vampirism got her club access revoked. Prepotente’s hellspawn familiar Bianca sets fire to Milk’s carpet, her newsletters and her scroll linen, and tries to incinerate Milk herself — who survives by scribbling a power word onto her own skin in the half-second she has.

Miriam then does something Milk says she has never seen a crawler do in all her cycles: she stops to heal an NPC, rubbing salve into the burn on Milk’s arm while apologising for her son.

Milk warns them they will not be allowed out of the club alive — and gets a system warning for it — then finds the loophole that lets her help anyway:

“I sure hope you don’t threaten me,” she said to the pair. “If you threaten me, I might be forced to give you information.”

Miriam pulls a knife and asks what sort of information.

Milk grinned. “Information on the many secret entrances and exits from Club Vanquisher, including the one in the back of this very room. I have a map, and I hope you don’t steal it from me.”

docs.title: “Milk?”
docs.text:
Carl finds her by accident at the end of Chapter 55, half-dead and stiff-legged, fleeing the Sepsis Whore fight through Club Vanquisher with Katia, Prepotente, Li Jun, Zhang and the sluggalette Bigs. Prepotente presses a wall panel, and the party falls through into the Calligrapher’s Guild.

He recognises her from her own pages before he reads her name — she had written extensively about the difference between Xenopus wings and Vesper wings.

“Milk?” I asked.

And even though she didn’t know who I was before this, in that moment, she did. I could see it. I could feel it. This was my sister, and I was her brother, and we now both knew it.

It breaks him open. This is the chapter immediately after Carl detonated a bomb at his own feet to kill Vinata, and he has been holding the aftermath of being torn apart and reassembled entirely inside himself:

And up until that moment, I’d been holding it all back. Those moments when I wasn’t there and I wasn’t here. Those horrific seconds as I’d reformed. It was like all the pain anyone had ever felt, all shoved into a single moment. I had borne it because what other choice did I have?…

I didn’t break. No. I wasn’t broken. I will not be broken.

“Milk,” I whispered a second time. This time, it wasn’t a question.

“Child, come here,” the strange creature said, wrapping me in leathery wings. She held on me as I pretended like I wasn’t, finally, sobbing.

“It’s not over yet,” I managed to whisper. “Not even close.”

“I know. Don’t you worry. It’s okay,” she said, stroking me with her wings…

“Let it out,” she whispered. “It’s okay. It’s okay.”

The rest of the party watches this “absolutely bewildered.” Katia, Li Jun and Zhang all clearly want to ask and are all smart enough not to.

docs.title: Kidnapped, Technically
docs.text:
She refuses to leave with them, and the system will not let them hire her. Rosetta’s advice is blunt: kidnap her. Tying up and “torturing” a guildmaster for their information turns out to be not merely legal but encouraged. So Milk is bound, carried out through the temple bathroom, and held in the FUPA — with everyone involved keeping up the pretence for the rest of the book. By Chapter 74 her wrists are “loosely bound” and she is untying herself to help right a tipped-over tortoise.

Her maps immediately become part of the war effort. Katia, mid-operation: “Thank Milk. Her maps are insanely accurate.”

docs.title: Words of Power
docs.text:
The magic system arrives with her. In Chapter 74, Edgar the tortoise tattoos Donut with a Dinner Bell variant spell that has to be pushed above level eight to work, and Rosetta explains how: “It’s gotta be a tattoo, and Milk here is going to etch words of power over it to increase the spell’s level.”

“Not quite yet, child. We must get it temporarily above level eight. This may sting a little,” Milk said. She came forward and produced a pen, dripping with black ink. Her hands were no longer bound. She wrote some words atop the tattoo with a flourish as Donut hissed with pain. I didn’t recognize the script, but when I examined the characters, the system simply said, Words of Power.

She then dips the pen into her shirt and it comes out purple.

“It’s a magic style that I haven’t seen used often in the dungeon. The calligraphy guild teaches it.”

The effect fades as the ink fades: “As the ink fades, the power will decrease, but if you practice using the spell at that high of a level, it will assist greatly with training.”

Asked how many magic systems there are, she gives the fullest statement of her craft in the book:

“There’s more than you can imagine. Even with just ink and calligraphy and maps, there are dozens of different methods. It is dangerous, though, attempting to learn too much. There’s a lot the right kind of ink can do. But, over the turns, I’ve learned the danger of using recipes I don’t quite understand. Inks and letters that shine the brightest burn out the fastest.”

And then the confession underneath it, delivered with a webbed hand on Carl’s cheek:

“I had a book once, and I wrote several of my recipes in it. But later, I switched to a different type of ink. It was an attempt to share my knowledge with a wider group, and it wasn’t until recently did I learn all that I wrote after I changed methods faded and disappeared.”… “Some of my best recipes were lost, and it wasn’t until they were needed the most did I learn they were gone. It is my fault that I didn’t write them properly.”

That is why Carl found nothing in her entries about the fifth-floor yam gift when he looked, three times, in Chapter 47. It is also why she hands him Stayfast Ink — 825 ml of it, “Enough ink for several chonky books,” ink that nothing will ever make fade — and an Adept’s Fountain Pen, with a pointed nudge toward The Filthy Little Crawler’s Book of Voodoo:

“He also has another book. One that all of you have. The Book of Voodoo, I believe it is called. Anything he writes in it will be given to everybody who already has the book. Best of luck to you.”

Her people’s saying, offered as the lesson: “‘No single recipe is a feast in itself.’ Meaning there’s always another way.”

Not the party's tattooist

The tattoo work in Book 7 is Edgar the tortoise’s. Milk’s contribution is the calligraphy written over a finished tattoo, and the ink formulation advice that let Edgar work without toraline. Katia is present for several of these scenes but is not involved in the tattooing.

docs.title: The Last Meal
docs.text:
By Chapter 82 she has stopped hiding entirely — Carl spots her floating above the third ring of Larracos, lecturing a large crowd of crawlers. In the final chapter it becomes clear what the lecture was.

She amplifies her voice with a word etched on her own throat and presents the departing crawlers’ gift: every crawler taking a deal has painted three skills or spells onto pages — one for Carl, one for Donut, one left open in the Book of Voodoo for anyone. The book is updated “with a metric fuckton of entries” and splits into two volumes, the second titled Carl’s Book of Boom.

“They’re leaving the dungeon, so I taught them how to remove a skill or spell and paint it onto a page.”

And of the former crawlers, who cannot transfer anything:

“They already gave what they could. And some gave everything they had.”

That act is the one that finishes her sentence, 333 services rendered:

“I did it,” she said. “I fulfilled my contract. I still have to live out the season, but I can leave after this.” She grinned at me. “I am glad I was given the chance to cook one final meal.”

She does not transfer to the 12th floor. She goes back to her guild.

“Goodbye, Carl,” Milk said. “If you can sneak back into Club Vanquisher, come say hello. But if not, that’s okay. You have given me something I didn’t think I had anymore. Burn it all to the ground.”

I gave my sister a hug.

In the epilogue, Quasar reviews Carl’s own exit offers and dismisses one for having “a contingent exit clause that’s almost as bad as that clause your bizarre friend Milk had.”

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Miriam Dom
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Race: Human → Vampire (turned off-page sometime before Book 5, after going looking for a panicked Prepotente while separated from him). Book 7's MILK interlude, a flashback to Floor 5, shows her already reading as race Vampire on an NPC's examine at that point
  • Class: Shepherd (a mage-class build, per the Floor 3 leaderboard)
  • Level: 27 (Book 2) — ranked 5th on the Floor 3 leaderboard; 52 as of Book 5
  • Status: Deceased — dies by voluntary sunrise exposure at the start of Book 5's second act, to lift a vampirism curse she'd unknowingly spread and to free Prepotente
  • Signature trait: Entered the dungeon with 15 pet goats
