  • Notable pet: A Hellspawn familiar ("Bianca Del Ciao"), transformed from one of her goats via an Enhanced Pet Biscuit — Level 32 as of Book 5, one of ten surviving goat children she keeps in inventory pet carriers

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Miriam Dom is a broadcast-only figure, nicknamed "the goat lady" by Carl and Donut — Mordecai mentions her before they ever see footage of her firsthand. She entered the dungeon with 15 pet goats and, remarkably, managed to keep most of them alive well into Floor 3.

docs.title: The Goat Menagerie
docs.text:
By the point a recap episode shows her, she's down to 5 of her original 15 goats. Three (Boer goats — a meat breed Carl recognizes from a childhood farm job) remain physically unchanged. The other two were altered by Enhanced Pet Biscuits:

  • One transformed into a bipedal, armored goat warrior wielding a double-headed axe, seemingly granted a Donut-like intelligence upgrade
  • The other — after what Mordecai calls a biscuit that "didn't go so well for her, or several of her goats" — became a Hellspawn familiar: a horse-sized, multi-breasted, jet-black goat monster with glowing red eyes and constant steam rising off its body

Mordecai identifies the Hellspawn as one of the most powerful pet types in the game: "if she can keep that thing alive, she's gotten it early enough that it'll level pretty high. It'll eventually grow wings and will be the size of a damn dragon." It's shown trampling a group of hyena-faced monsters to death on-air.

docs.title: Leaderboard
docs.text: Ranked 5th on the tentative Floor 3 leaderboard Odette reveals late in Book 2, at Level 27 with a bounty of 200,000 — see Level 3: Leaderboard for the full table.

docs.title: Book 3: Revealed as Prepotente's Keeper
docs.text: Miriam Dom reappears on Floor 4 as the caretaker and apparent romantic partner of Prepotente — the sapient, aerialist Caprid crawler who turns out to be one of her own transformed goats. She manages his theatrical, murder-threat-prone personality with unbothered affection, using her shepherd's crook to smack him when he's rude to strangers (Carl and Imani among them) and rewarding good behavior with a kiss on the head, addressing him as "Pony." She and Prepotente depart together to hunt a different province boss after their first target is accidentally teleported away by Carl's group.

docs.title: Book 5: Cursed, and a Final Kindness
docs.text:
Miriam Dom and Prepotente reappear early on Floor 6 already having survived a run-in with Big Tina (an allosaurus boss) — and Miriam is already a vampire by this point, having turned off-page some time before, after Prepotente panicked and ran off during a separation and she went looking for him and "somehow ended up a vampire." That existing vampirism, and her position as the "Prime" carrier of a floor-wide infection spreading through the local wildlife, is what draws the attention of an elite vampire hunter, Viscount Fog, star of a rival broadcast called Blood Hunter — his mount, Sierra, does not curse her; he hunts her because she's already a vampire. It's actually Miriam and Prepotente who come to Carl and Donut's aid first, not the other way around: they find and heal a badly-injured Carl (hit by crossbow bolts during his own opening raid on Zockau) and drive him to safety in their cart, and it's during that ride that Miriam confides her full backstory to him: a farm outside Parma, Italy, twenty years spent caring for aging parents and her goats rather than pursuing her own life, and a bone-deep devotion to Prepotente ("my stubborn little boy") that predates his transformation.

Fog attacks Miriam and Prepotente directly on two separate occasions — the first while they're fighting the allosaurus Big Tina, which they survive. The second time, Prepotente attempts to cure Miriam by transferring her curse to Fog using a scroll of Community Pool — but Fog's countering ring bounces the spell back and forth between them several times, leaving Prepotente Stunned, then Fragile (one hit point, unable to heal). In the chaos, Prepotente's own newly-acquired Ring of Divine Suffering activates on its own and marks Miriam — the only eligible target in range — meaning Prepotente himself now carries Left to Fester and cannot heal until his own mark, his mother, dies. Fog eventually dies of his own reflected curse at sunset; Miriam spends the night fighting off infected wildlife to protect Prepotente's frozen body, then summons Carl and Donut at dawn — not to save her, but to keep watch and, implicitly, to end her life before Prepotente can wake and try to stop her himself.

Carl secretly marks her with his own Ring of Divine Suffering just before sunrise and lets her burn to death in the light, curing every crawler and creature infected with her strain of vampirism floor-wide and lifting the Left to Fester debuff so Prepotente can finally be woken. She dies asking Carl to explain her choice to Prepotente "one day" and leaves her entire inventory behind for him, save two scrolls Carl quietly keeps for himself. Her death triggers a world quest (The Creeping Apocalypse) forcing every crawler and hunter on the floor to hunt down the newly-created, uncontrolled undead "Odious Creepers" her infected wildlife left behind before sunset, or face unspecified consequences.

docs.title: Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin
docs.text: Miriam has been dead since Book 5, and she does not appear in Book 7's present day. Her only real scene is a flashback, and the rest of her presence in the book is other people remembering her.

docs.title: The MILK Interlude: Thrown Out of Club Vanquisher
docs.text:
The interlude before chapter 26 is told from the point of view of Milk, the xenopus guildmaster of the calligraphy and cartography guilds in Club Vanquisher. It is set on the fifth floor — during Book 4, well before Miriam's death — not in Book 7's present.

Milk wakes to sirens and screaming, and finds Miriam and Prepotente fighting their way through the club's mantaur guards with the hellspawn familiar Bianca. Prepotente is the one shouting:

"They can't do this, mother. I won't stand for it!" came the screech. "It wasn't your fault! Bianca, melt the guards!"

"Prepotente Lorenzo De La Rosa! Stop that this instant!" came the woman's voice again, stern. "Stop. More guards are coming. They will kill us. We must flee."

When the pair burst into her hidden guild, Milk examines them and works out what the fight is about:

Milk examined the pair of crawlers plus their giant pet standing there, and she instantly knew what the problem was. The older, female crawler was originally a human, but her race was Vampire, which wasn't a race someone could voluntarily choose. That meant it was likely a recent thing, and upon noticing this, they had likely just told her that her access to Club Vanquisher was being revoked. Her child, who'd apparently taken a caprid race, was upset about this.

Two things worth being precise about. First, this is the passage that confirms Miriam's vampirism on the page — the system's own race field reads Vampire — and it dates it to Floor 5 at the latest, earlier than Book 5's account established. Second, the club expulsion is Milk's inference, not a stated ruling: the narration says "they had likely just told her," and the word banned is never used of Miriam anywhere in the book. (In Book 7 that word belongs to Prepotente, who carries a Holy Crusade Bounty.)

What the scene is really about is Miriam's kindness. Bianca sets the guild on fire and tries to incinerate Milk; Miriam's response is to rush over and treat the burn with her own salve.

Milk just looked at the woman, open-mouthed. In all of her cycles in the dungeon, she'd never known of a crawler giving up supplies to heal an NPC.

She then apologises for her son — "he still hasn't learned how to politely wield it" — and, when Milk hints that she can only give information if she is threatened, plays along by drawing a knife so Milk can hand over the map of the club's secret exits without being punished for it. Miriam's sad smile, "revealing sharp teeth," and a hand on Milk's shoulder are the thanks. It is the encounter that eventually pulls Milk out of fifty seasons of hiding.

docs.title: Remembered
docs.text:
• Volteeg, the cookbook author driving a tank for the Operatics, listens to Mozart before his last battle and wonders "if it was similar to the music Prepotente's owner, Miriam Dom, would've played for the goat before he'd taken his pet biscuit."
  • At the warlord council, Donut recognises the naga Princess Vinata's broadcast, Blood Hunter, as Viscount Fog's show: "The one who killed Miriam Dom, she didn't say." She then tells Vinata, "Oh, honey. And I thought I was going to be the one who killed you."
  • Before the Club Vanquisher assault, Prepotente steadies himself with a muttered litany of names. Carl recognises Miriam and Bianca in it, along with several others, ending on "Ragazzaccia," a word he doesn't know.

Prepotente himself is a major Book 7 character and one of the strongest crawlers left; see Prepotente.

Sourced from Book 2: Carl's Doomsday Scenario, Book 3: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook, Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade, and Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Mongo
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Species: Mongoliensis — actually a velociraptor (see below)
  • Sex: Male
  • Owner: Princess Donut (pet-class mob, bonded)
  • Title: Royal Steed
  • Obtained: Floor 2 pet reward room, from a locked, red-tagged cage
  • Full-grown danger level: Level 15 ("especially powerful, fast, and vicious")
  • Type/Class/Subclass: Not applicable — pet-class mob, not a crawler
  • Level: 6+ by mid-Book 2, rising to 13+ by the end of the Floor 3 quests, then 26 by the end of Book 3 → 33 by the end of Book 4 → 34+ by the end of Book 5 — grows from turkey-sized to pony-sized to full adult size (roughly pony-height, about 13 feet long including tail) over the series so far. No level is stated for him anywhere in Book 7, and no evolution or upgrade notification is printed for him in that book
  • Notable spells/abilities: No named spells; combat is physical — biting, clawing, pack-hunting instinct (confirmed useful against Brindle Grubs); leaps nearly 10 feet vertically by Book 2, later able to clear a full building story in a single jump; immune to acid-blood splash damage from Book 3's Krakaren monsters; Book 4: destroys at least four defective "Robot Donut" toys on sight, and delivers the killing bite/crunch on the Scree parasite (Maggie My) after it's forced out of Chris Andrews and Carl's own body; Book 5: has a rarely-used Earthquake attack that damages and reveals invisible foes over an area (used against a pack of invisible Night Weasels), and is trained by Donut to moonwalk for the Butcher's Masquerade pet showcase; Book 7: Donut's new Muscle Mommy benefit boosts his Strength by 25% of her own, and her Clockwork Triplicate spell splits him into two clockwork duplicates plus the original
  • Notable items: A magical tracking collar (Book 2, from a Gold Pet Box) that keeps his dot visible on the minimap at all times; Enchanted Fang Caps of the Expectorating Tizheruk (Book 2, transferred from Donut; Book 4: a second pair adds +15% movement speed and +15% Strength)
  • Offspring (Book 7): Twin Ursensus daughters by Kiwi, born mid-book in Bucket Boy's clinic — Legendary Creature, "Part raptor, part bear, part Scolopendra magic"

docs.title: Book 2 Growth
docs.text: Mongo grows visibly with almost every fight on Floor 3, gaining size, adult plumage, and strength at a pace that surprises even Donut ("They grow up so fast"). He remains prone to breaking training the moment he gets excited near a kill, but grows steadily more useful — including helping fend off Grimaldi's circus lemurs and mold lions alongside Carl and Donut. He single- handedly holds off a room full of spike-throwing Street Urchins to protect an unconscious Donut, earning him fang caps as a reward for his own inventory, and later helps clear the krasue nest in Miss Quill's lair, using his enchanted bite to kill the ghost-class monsters outright.

docs.title: Origin
docs.text:
Mongo is found caged in a Floor 2 pet reward room alongside other red-tagged (dangerous) pet-class options. His in-game description reads:

"The stubborn and hot-headed Mongoliensis is not the type of pet to ever be 'tamed.' The best one can hope for is mutual respect. And even then they still might try to eat you if the fancy strikes them. While especially powerful, fast, and vicious when they are fully grown at level 15, getting them to level 15 is about as likely as a cheerleader from West Virginia reaching her 18th birthday as a virgin."

Donut names him on sight, before even confirming his sex: "If it's a boy I'm gonna call him Mongo... If it's a girl I'm naming her Sissy."

docs.title: What He Actually Is
docs.text: Mongo is described and pictured as a small, feathered, beaked creature — Carl repeatedly calls him "the little chicken" or "the little dinosaur." Late in the book, talk-show host Odette reveals the translation gap behind his species name: "Mongoliensis" is the scientific name for what humans call velociraptors. Carl hadn't put it together because of the pink feathers and beak.

docs.title: Pet-Class Mechanics
docs.text:
Per Mordecai, pet-class mobs behave differently from normal mobs:

"Mobs that start out as a pet class will always be level one regardless of what they usually are when you find them in the dungeon. And they'll stay level one until they're bonded. Only then will they start to level."

Mongo starts fully hostile (a red status dot) and has to be carried in a gerbil cage to avoid biting Carl or teleporting away. Bonding happens in stages:

  1. Remove auto-hostility — achieved by letting Mongo kill (and eat) live Brindle Grubs, after Carl learns from a recap broadcast that Mongoliensis are pack hunters. His status dot turns from red to white.
  2. Obedience training — Donut spends a full day training him with pet biscuits until he'll hold an attack until she gives the command (which evolves from "attack" to "sic 'em").
  3. Full bond — triggered when Mongo is nearly killed by a hornet-type monster in the stairwell hallway (the same hallway where the Rage Elemental fight happened) and Donut saves him. His dot turns from white to orange, and the system announces:

"Mongo the Mongoliensis Level One (Pet of Grand Champion Best in Dungeon Princess Donut) has joined the party."

"Mongo's title has been changed to Royal Steed."

docs.title: Timeline Notes (Book 1)
docs.text:
• Found and caged in a Floor 2 pet reward room
  • Named by Donut before his sex or species were confirmed
  • Bonding process consumes most of the party's remaining time on Floor 2
  • Saved by Donut from a hornet-type mob in the stairwell hallway, completing the bond
  • Revealed by Odette, during a broadcast interview, to be a velociraptor rather than an unfamiliar alien species
  • Descends to Floor 3 with Carl and Donut at the end of the book

docs.title: Book 3 Notes
docs.text: Mongo reaches Level 23 mid-floor and finishes at Level 26, having grown into what Carl and Donut agree is his full adult size — he "won't get any bigger." He plays a recurring, dark-comic role in the floor's Growler Gary hand-farming plan (see Carl), efficiently and repeatedly killing and dismembering the self-resurrecting gnoll on command, and proves immune to the caustic acid blood of the floor's Krakaren monsters, letting him fight them in melee without the protective measures the rest of the party needs. He's kept caged for a stretch around the remnants of Brynhild's Daughters following Hekla's death, for safety on both sides.

docs.title: Book 4 Notes
docs.text: Mongo hits Level 33 on Floor 5, gaining three levels in a single fan-box-fueled battle (the airship heist) despite not doing anything himself, to Donut's mock outrage. He's temporarily released from his pet carrier to make room for Clockwork Triplicate duplicates during the Wasteland assault, terrifying him with the height. He develops a habit of instantly destroying every defective "Robot Donut" merchandising toy Veriluxx sends the party (several detonate harmlessly after he bites through their heads), and picks up a stuffed pink rabbit from the gnomish floating house that he carries around for the rest of the floor. At the climax, he lands the finishing bite on the Scree parasite (Maggie My) after Carl forces it out of both Chris Andrews's skull and his own neck.

docs.title: Book 5 Notes
docs.text: On Floor 6, Mongo encounters what appears to be a matriarchal pack of wild Mongoliensis led by a scarred, level-60 female named Kiwi, and mates with her almost immediately, to Donut's horrified running commentary — Carl jokes on the spot that Kiwi is now "most definitely" pregnant by Mongo, a claim the book bears out shortly afterward: when the High Elf castle is yanked away to Floor 9 mid-battle, the narration lists everything lost with it, including "Kiwi, who'd turned into a bear—a very pregnant bear—was gone" (the on-stage transformation scene itself, moments earlier, doesn't mention it). Kiwi is not actually his own species at all — she's later revealed to be an Ursine woman transformed into raptor form by one of Scolopendra's curses, and her "daughter" Big Tina (a deranged allosaurus terrorizing the region) is the same curse's other victim. Donut tames only Kiwi herself as an actual bonded minion (a potion keyed to Mongo's own blood as the special ingredient); the rest of the pack merely goes non-hostile in step with their leader and is never personally bonded. Donut later cures Kiwi with a sponsor-sent potion during the Butcher's Masquerade climax — reverting her, mid-battle, back into her Ursine form — while the rest of her raptor pack immediately turns hostile again the instant Kiwi's control lapses. Tina, tragically, is never cured and remains trapped as a dinosaur, crying out for her mother as the transformation happens. Mongo survives a lightning bolt meant for him — cast from a concealed litter later revealed to be carrying Queen Imogen's cat familiar, Ferdinand — only because Donut throws herself in the way; helps Kiwi tear Vrah apart, then delivers the actual finishing bite alone after Carl sends Kiwi back to the stage ("Kiwi... back onto the stage. Quick. Mongo. Finish her off for me."); and is trained by Donut to moonwalk on stage during the masquerade's pet showcase, drawing applause even from some of the watching hunters.

docs.title: Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin
docs.text: Floor 9, the Faction Wars floor, is the biggest book Mongo has had. He is credited with killing two of the ten enemy warlords, is reunited with Kiwi, becomes a father, and very nearly dies. The book never states his level and never prints an evolution or upgrade notification for him.

docs.title: Getting His Wing Back
docs.text:
He enters the book maimed. Carl, controlled by Shi Maria at the end of Book 6, had burned off his feathers and taken his right wing, and Carl can't look at him without flinching. Donut has already used a Heal Severe Injury potion on the burns; the wing needs a rare Heal Pet potion, which Mordecai insists on reverse-engineering on his upgraded crafting table first.

"These are super rare, and expensive, but with my newest table upgrade, I can figure out the recipe without ruining it. So let me look at it first, and we can give it to Mongo after. It'll grow his wing back in aboot an hour or so." He patted Mongo on the head. "You'll be as good as new. Well, almost. You'll probably still have some scars."

Carl administers it by smashing the vial on Mongo's backside — Mordecai's potion-ball trick, and "a hell of a lot safer than trying to pour it down his throat."

docs.title: Rend
docs.text: In chapter 5 Carl re-bonds the tummy acher he inherited from Tserendolgor, who is renamed Sir Rendlegore — "Rend." Mongo's first reaction is to try to eat him; the meatball hops into his open mouth on purpose, and Mongo swallows him, then yaks him back up on the table. They are inseparable from that point on. Rend rides on Mongo's back (he has no arms and works out how to climb up unaided), gnaws on him constantly, licks gore off his neck after fights, and steals his bacon. Donut's verdict on Rend, twice over, is "He's a bad influence on Mongo" and later "He's a terrible influence on Mongo."

docs.title: Killing Empress D'Nadia
docs.text:
In chapter 26 Carl and Donut assault the Prism throne room to kill Empress D'Nadia. Donut casts Clockwork Triplicate on Mongo, and it is the two clockwork copies — not the real one — that do the work of stripping the Empress's three layered tech shields and tearing her armour and gown off her. The real Mongo is held back the whole time:

The clockwork Mongos went back to work, tearing at her. The real Mongo held back, hopping from one foot to the next, his arm feathers rustling with anticipation.

Carl nearly takes the kill himself, and Donut talks him down from it. Then she settles an older score — the pet show Tserendolgor admitted cheating at in Book 6:

"Empress, Darling," Donut said. "Mongo would like to express his utmost disappointment at how you judged him during the pet show."

The chapter ends there. Chapter 27 opens with the system's ruling:

System Message: Warlord D'Nadia of the Prism has fallen. Credit for the kill has been given to pet Mongo of the Princess Posse.

Afterwards Mongo and Rend are found licking blue Saccathian gore off the throne room wall, and Mongo squawks agreement when Donut demands Carl not rename the party now that he's outranked her: "Is that what you want? Mongo to come from a broken home?"

docs.title: Muscle Mommy
docs.text: Once Donut becomes the strongest crawler in the dungeon again, her new Muscle Mommy benefit boosts Mongo's Strength by 25% of her own. Carl notes he is "decidedly more buff" afterwards. Combined with Donut's Twinkle Toes he becomes the party's fastest ground mount.

docs.title: The Nest, and Nearly Dying
docs.text:
Late in the siege of Larracos (end of chapter 72) Mongo and his clockwork duplicates are knocked down a chute out of the Nest tower, and Donut is locked in the room above, screaming for him. Outside, they land in front of Gustavo 3, the last of Lucia Mar's rottweilers. Gustavo's lightning destroys both clockworks; when the real Mongo bites down on him, the dog's Porcupine Defense erupts steel quills up through Mongo's mouth from the inside out, then electrifies them. Gustavo takes the unconscious dinosaur by the throat and starts shaking.

Mongo is saved by Rend. Carl casts Hi-Yo Silver to summon him, and Rend's Wrecking Ball does the rest:

The back half of Gustavo 3, the second of Lucia Mar's two rottweilers, terror of the dungeon, exploded in a red mist as Rend rushed right up to me, stopping inches from my face.

Lucia Mar herself, sobbing, pours a pet healing potion on Mongo, whose health is down to "the barest sliver of red," his throat ripped open. He survives, blood-soaked around the collar, missing neck feathers.

docs.title: Kiwi
docs.text:
Mongo is reunited with Kiwi in chapter 13, on Carl and Donut's first walk around their new headquarters base (shortly before it is christened the FUPA), and the scene plays out almost entirely without dialogue. Big Tina — the allosaurus, Kiwi's daughter, now able to talk — greets him as "Pa-pa," to Donut's outrage. Then Kiwi comes out of the house in an apron, one-eyed and heavily pregnant. She is now an Ursine again, cured at the Butcher's Masquerade; Carl's narration is blunt about the arithmetic: "before she'd turned, she'd had... relations with Mongo when they were both dinosaurs."

"Mongo?" Kiwi asked.

Mongo gave a single, quiet roar. He pushed past Tina and moved, head low to the ground as everybody watched, all of us holding our breath, all of us wondering what was going to happen next. Mongo sniffed at Kiwi and gave an uncertain peep.

Kiwi stepped forward, wrapped her arms around Mongo's neck, and she hugged him. Mongo just stood there. They hugged for a few moments, and then Kiwi turned away.

She goes back inside to make dinner. Mongo is left standing there "a confused look upon the dinosaur's face, like he didn't know what had just happened," and Carl tells him, "Sometimes people change, and that's all there is to it." Her personality has changed completely — from the scarred, murderous pack leader of Book 5 to a soft-spoken woman who cooks for the troops. Mongo keeps at it anyway; Samantha reports that while Carl and Donut are in the planning room, "Mongo goes in the kitchens and sniffs Kiwi's butt so much she has to swat him away."

docs.title: The Twins
docs.text:
Kiwi goes into labour mid-book while Carl's group is away; Florin messages that she is in Bucket Boy's new clinic "in active labor and is asking for Mongo." Mongo's response to Donut telling him he's about to be a father is to cock his head, then start backing up and screeching "like he did when he didn't want to get zapped away into his cage."

He goes in anyway. Kiwi puts a hand on his side through the delivery; he squeals in concern each time she pushes. The birth runs through the end of chapter 82, intercut with Carl's conversation with Juice Box about the Inevitable Ruin:

A second cry filled the tent as Mongo squawked in confusion and fear and perhaps a tiny bit of joy.

"Oh my god, oh my god," Donut called from my shoulder. "Mongo... Mongo... you're a daddy!"

Twin girls. Carl's description is unsparing — "They weren't bears. They weren't raptors. They were something in-between," four-legged, stub-winged, covered in wet brown fur, with distinctly Mongo-like heads but no feathers, beaks, mammal-like cries, and badly mismatched, unfocused pug eyes. He privately calls them "goddamn abominations." Then the system card lands:

Newborn Ursensus. Female. Level 0.

Legendary Creature.

I just love it when I'm allowed to create new monsters within the confines of the game rules. Part raptor, part bear, part Scolopendra magic. All adorable. These fuzzy little meat-eaters are going to be quite the handful when they grow up.

Because of this mob's intelligence level they cannot be used as pets.

Ursensus is a brand-new mob type, created by the AI on the spot. Donut: "Mongo, you made a legendary creature!" Carl's own contribution is to pat him on the back — "If I had a cigar, I'd give it to you, buddy."

docs.title: Killing Epitome Tagg
docs.text:
Mongo's second warlord kill, in chapter 84, is an accident. Epitome Tagg of the Dream has hidden himself inside the biomechanical heart and lungs surgically installed in Louis Santiago's chest. The team's fix is to cut the organs out and replace them with a flesh golem's, on a rapid-healing clock. Bucket Boy yanks the heart and lungs free and throws them over his shoulder onto the tent floor — where, unnoticed, Mongo eats them.

Mongo popped up and let out an angry screech. He had blood on his beak, and he spit out the chewed-to-hell plastic heart and lungs onto the ground of the tent with disgust.

System Message: Warlord Epitome Tagg of the Dream has fallen. Credit for the kill has been given... Well, this one is just as complicated as the last one, but imma give it to pet Mongo of the Princess Posse. I almost called it a suicide, and I almost gave it to that Bucket Boy kid, but it's going to Mongo. Consider it a present for the baby shower.

The Dream is eliminated and all its assets go to the Princess Posse, leaving two enemy teams.

docs.title: End of the Floor
docs.text:
At the going-away party Mongo sniffs at the babies while Rend tries to catch streamers in his mouth. Kiwi, Tina and the twins go down to the 12th floor with the other children; Mongo and Rend stay with Carl and Donut. Mongo "freaked out when Tina and Kiwi and the new babies had disappeared," and has to be coaxed into his carrier.

Sourced from Book 1: The Apocalypse Will Be Televised, Book 3: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook, Book 4: The Gate of the Feral Gods, Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade, and Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Mordecai
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Role: Tutorial guide (Floors 1-3), then personal Manager (Book 2 onward)
  • Species: Skyfowl (true form) — currently a Changeling
  • Race/form (Floor 1): Rat Hooligan, level 50
  • Race/form (Floor 2): Bugaboo, level 50
  • Race/form (Floor 3): Incubus, level 50 ("Gigachad of the Over City")
  • Race/form (Floor 4): Grulke Infantry, level 50 — a militaristic toad-warrior race
  • Race/form (Floor 5): Still Grulke Infantry — coincidentally, a Bautista-supplied distraction beanbag toy Carl uses on Floor 5 summons an unrelated level-15 grulke toad mob that Carl notes looks just like Mordecai's own Floor-4 form
  • Race/form (Floor 6): Pocket Kuma, level 50 — a magic-infused, half-fairy creature (small bear crossbred with a capybara spirit and a sugar glider) originally bred as a pet for the High Elf royal court; knee-height, fuzzy, huge-eyed, buck-toothed, and "disgustingly cute," but can barely walk or fight
  • Race/form (Floor 8): Hills Cyclops, level 50 — the weakest and dumbest of the cyclops types
  • Race/form (Floor 9): Human, level 50 (Book 7) — specifically "something called a Canadian," per the system's examine text, snowsuit and raccoon hat included. His level does not change; the book never shows or explains the transition, and he is never described as reclassing
  • Status: Non-Combatant NPC; indentureship requirement fulfilled at the end of Book 2; served a Book 3 seven-day system ban after attacking a game-show host. Alive at the end of Book 7, still on Floor 9 with Carl and Donut
  • Type/Class/Subclass: Not applicable — Non-Combatant NPCs don't carry a crawler class
  • Notable spells/abilities: None described — as a Non-Combatant NPC, he cannot be attacked and isn't shown fighting. In Book 7 his upgraded alchemy table lets him reverse-engineer any potion he is handed and mass-produce the result
  • Notable items: None described beyond personal mementos (a photo of his brother, his mother's ashes) kept on a shelf in his guildhall. In Book 7 some of those ashes are built into a crossbow bolt (see below)

docs.title: What He Is
docs.text:
Mordecai is a Changeling — a race that reshapes into a new form (always a type of mob native to the current floor) every time his guildhall relocates to a new level. His true species is the skyfowl, an eagle-like race; he keeps a framed photo of his brother (also a skyfowl) as one of the only possessions he was allowed to bring across dungeon moves. On Floor 1 he appears as a Rat Hooligan (a "smartest, fastest, ugliest" Rat-Kin variant); on Floor 2, after the guildhall relocates, he shapeshifts into a hulking, owl-eyed Bugaboo.

Mordecai was a crawler himself, centuries ago, on his own now-mined homeworld. He made it to Floor 11 before deciding to stop, later telling Carl the deepest anyone has ever gotten in the game's history is Floor 13 — a human crawler from a different Earth-like world, who died within thirty minutes of arriving.

docs.title: Role in the Story
docs.text:
As tutorial guide, Mordecai:

  • Grants Carl and Donut access to their inventory and menu systems
  • Explains core mechanics: loot box tiers (Bronze → Silver → Gold → Platinum → Legendary → Celestial), the Views/Followers/Favorites/Patrons system, safe zones, and boss types (Neighborhood → Borough → City → Province → Country → Floor)
  • Gives tactical advice after boss fights, generally in the form of "look for the clue" (e.g., pointing out that both the Bad Llama and the Juicer boss had an exploitable throat/vein weak point)
  • Is restricted from revealing certain information directly (spoilers about the current floor, deeper floors, or living admins) but often finds loophole ways to hint at it — telling Carl to "ask directly" or communicating through pointed non-answers

docs.title: The Odette Connection
docs.text: Mordecai was trained by Odette during his own crawl, generations ago. He reacts with immediate, visceral anger when Carl relays her request that he "seek her out" once his indentureship ends, saying he'd rather commit unspeakable acts than be in the same solar system as her. The full history between them is left unresolved in Book 1 — Odette only says she "pushed him too hard, and he paid dearly for it."

docs.title: What He Reveals (Under Pressure)
docs.text:
Mordecai is more forthcoming than most NPCs seem to be allowed to be, especially once cameras aren't recording him talking (viewers can see/hear crawlers, but not NPCs, unless the NPC has press credentials):

  • His indentureship doesn't count toward completion unless one of his crawlers reaches Floor 4 — a fact Odette reveals, not him
  • Borant is being pressured by the kua-tin government (the Bloom, aka "the Party") to end the season as fast as possible due to a looming bankruptcy/debt-collection crisis
  • The Skull Empire, Orcish Supremacy, and Blood Sultanate are separate, rival political/factional entities that matter more from Floor 9 onward
  • Floors 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, and 18 are linked "settings" that exist and progress independently of the crawlers

docs.title: Personality
docs.text: Grumpy, self-interested, but ultimately protective of his charges within the limits the system allows him. He's visibly weary from centuries of running tutorials, drinks, and keeps a shrine-like shelf of personal mementos (his mother's ashes, his brother's photo) that Donut repeatedly disturbs, to his great irritation.

docs.title: Book 2: The Manager
docs.text:
Carl and Donut deliberately trick Mordecai into activating the hidden Manager benefit tied to Donut's Former Child Actor class (see Carl for how) — he doesn't learn it was intentional in Book 2. As Manager, he can physically accompany the party (including outside guildhalls, on urban floors) but can never engage in direct combat; in exchange he loses his own room, guild access, the information codex, and television access, relying only on memory to help them. His Incubus form comes with a built-in weakness to alcohol, leading to a memorable early-Book-2 bender that leaves Carl and Donut without guidance during a dangerous first night on Floor 3.

He also secretly steals a physical newsletter (meant for NPC shopkeepers without feed access) to warn Carl and Donut about a coming "major battle event" — explicitly telling them that as Manager, "we can't engage in direct battle with mobs. Everything else is fair game."

His indentureship requirement — reaching Floor 4 with a crawler — is fulfilled at the very end of Book 2. He is now technically free to leave crawler service, though the book ends with him still accompanying the party.

docs.title: Book 3: The Chaco Incident and a Seven-Day Absence
docs.text:
Early on Floor 4, Mordecai attacks talk-show host Chaco — tongue-whipping a chair at him during a live segment — and is hit with a system-enforced seven-day ban/timeout, vanishing from the story for nearly the entire floor at the worst possible time. Chaco's on-air needling implies Mordecai did something under orders from "his manager" that hurt Mordecai personally and caused the pair to "lose Odette" — a specific accusation Mordecai refuses to discuss when he returns, only promising "it won't happen again." The full backstory behind it, and its connection to the still-unexplained rift between Mordecai and Odette, remains unresolved.

He reappears in his new, Floor-4-mandated Grulke Infantry form — a squat, toad-headed warrior race — just as the floor's crisis is winding down, and is immediately confronted with a room soaked in blood, two new player-killer skulls, and a floor's worth of catching up to do.

docs.title: Book 3: The Ring Lecture
docs.text: On learning Carl has looted and worn the Enchanted Night Wyrm's Ring of Divine Suffering, Mordecai reacts more violently than at any prior point in the series — physically smacking Carl and threatening to bar Donut from associating with him past Floor 6 if he doesn't get rid of it. He explains that Divine Suffering rings are seeded every season specifically to bait crawlers into becoming farmable power sources for the Floor 9 faction wars, that every winning faction army historically includes a ring-bearer, and that simply possessing one paints an enormous target on its owner. Carl agrees to sell it before Floor 6.

docs.title: Book 3: The Iron Tangle as a Map of the Galaxy
docs.text: Using Katia's obsessively detailed hand-drawn map of the floor's subway system, Mordecai identifies the Iron Tangle's track layout as a disguised recreation of the Syndicate's own corporate logo — a schematic of real interstellar wormhole routes converging on a galactic core (the floor's central "abyss"). He connects the floor's Krakaren-vs-Pooka ghoul/drug plotline to real, ugly interstellar politics: a xenophobic caricature of an actual alien collective mind (the "Krakaren," more accurately translated as "the Apothecary") and the Plenty, the real species behind the dungeon's faster-than-light communication network, whom Borant-aligned factions (including the kua-tin Bloom) publicly demonize as a existential threat. He also lays out the dungeon's full deity-summoning rules for Carl (celestial boon, indentured summoning, and involuntary summoning; duration, size, and re-summoning mechanics) — directly enabling Carl's Grull gambit against the floor's mimic boss (see Carl).

docs.title: Book 4 Notes
docs.text:
Mordecai plays a quieter, more support-focused role on Floor 5, spending much of the book at his alchemy and sapper's tables. Notable contributions:

  • Brews the Dolores Doesn't Splat potion (a rock-buffalo-mating-derived, five-application fall-cushioning potion with a signature side effect Carl and Katia never forget) and the Phase Lava Rock potion, the latter essential to freeing Chris Andrews from the Scree parasite possessing him
  • Correctly identifies the Infiltrator/Scree parasite controlling Chris on sight, and lays out the full shapeshifter taxonomy relevant to the floor: Doppelgangers (Katia's race) vs. Changelings (his own) vs. Mimics vs. Illusionists vs. Gondii/Valtay brain-worms vs. Infiltrators
  • Explains the dungeon's full deity-worship and celestial-grenade mechanics just in time for Carl to accidentally join Emberus's faith
  • Reacts to Carl's assassination of Admin Loita with open alarm ("You don't know the forces you're dealing with"), repeatedly urging him to sell off dangerous, high-profile loot (the Ring of Divine Suffering, the Gate itself) rather than keep provoking the season's producers
  • Eventually determines a use for a mysterious sponsor-gifted root vegetable (the "yam") with help from the hired NPC Samantha, producing the Phase Lava Rock potions in time

docs.title: Book 5 Notes
docs.text:
Mordecai's guildhall relocation this floor turns him into a Pocket Kuma — a fuzzy, knee-high, buck-toothed, monkey-tailed creature so absurdly adorable that both Carl and Katia burst out laughing at him on sight, to his fury.

He finally solves a Charm Animal potion recipe he's been chasing for 50 cycles — keyed to the mongoliensis species via a full liter of Mongo's own blood as the special ingredient (drained over three cut-and-heal cycles, to Donut's horror) — after a sponsor mails Carl the missing recipe step alongside a drawing (not a photo, despite Donut calling it one) of Mongo. Donut uses the finished potion to tame the velociraptor pack leader Kiwi. Mordecai also brews Uncle Morty's Insta Lawn-Kill and Undead Repellant, Extra-Strength Edition (an anti-plant-monster weedkiller laced with anti-undead boosts, used against the floor's Odious Creeper world-quest monsters) and a pair of Holy Gooper potion balls (blessed shrine water plus a healing potion and a coagulant, effective against vampires) with almost no notice. He talks Carl into taking the "Swole" strength milestone upgrade over "Prison Bitch" or "Stepson," and reacts to Carl's account of the Ring of Divine Suffering being marked onto Miriam Dom, and of Prepotente swallowing his own copy of the ring whole, with equal parts horror and professional curiosity.

Mordecai also mentions, in an aside to Carl, that he once testified against Odette in an official trial — but is careful to clarify this happened when she was his manager, not back when she was a fellow crawler ("It was when she was my manager"), adding one more piece to the still-unresolved rift between them. He continues managing the party's rapidly growing collection of hired NPCs and rescued children from his post inside the guildhall.

docs.title: Book 6: The Prologue — How Uzzi Died
docs.text:
Book 6 opens with the thing Mordecai has never talked about. The prologue is his own crawl, on the tenth floor, with a level collapse imminent.

His party: Mordecai, his brother Uzzi (a skyfowl Storm Commander), the wolf-headed bard Chaco, and a skyfowl named Hold Steady. Their manager, non-corporeal and watching from outside, is Odette. The exit puzzle needs nine assembled pieces and will only open if it physically touches a storm god or is hit with god-tier storm magic. If Mordecai reaches the eleventh floor, Odette gets a bonus big enough to buy her way out of her own indentureship — nine seasons knocked off, and a residency berth in the inner system.

The scheme was Odette's friend Armita's idea: use Armita, then working as a demigod attendant, as a cutout to reach Huanxin Jinx, the grixist heiress who sponsored the storm goddess Dodola every season, and pay her to drive Dodola into hitting the puzzle. The text is blunt about what this is: "Once money became involved, it clearly became cheating… It was cheating, and it was fraud."

Huanxin escalates — ten percent, then a third, then half, then a threat to zero out the whole party. Odette breaks the deal: "Armita, tell her we don't have a deal."

Mordecai offers to kill himself with his Final Blow skill instead. Odette has a better idea. She orders Chaco — a crawler in her own party, not a subordinate, and a worshipper of Dodola — to put the Dart of Ophiotaurus into Uzzi. Chaco refuses: "You want me to kill Uzzi? It's not going to happen." She coerces him with a promise of protection and a lie about the Outreach Guild.

He throws the dart. Crawler Uzzi has fallen. Dodola is force-summoned into the shell of Uzzi's body inside a Circle of Containment; her own lightning ricochets and kills her in the immunity gap. A deity has fallen. The heavens tremble with rage. Chaco jumps ten levels and takes the godkill credit. The stairwell opens.

Mordecai tackles Chaco into it, and then sends Odette a message:

Mordecai: I am going to kill you, Odette. I am going to get free of this place, I am going to find where you are, and I am going to kill you.

This retroactively explains the Book 3 incident in which Mordecai threw a chair at Chaco's head on live television and served a seven-day system ban for it.

docs.title: Form
docs.text: Hills Cyclops, level 50 — per the system, the weakest and dumbest of the cyclops types, shepherds by trade, and unable to see their own reflections. Mordecai's running complaint: "I hate it when I'm a cyclops. No depth perception plus I can't see my own reflection."

docs.title: The Children
docs.text:
Carl and Donut catch him wearing a face full of children's makeup — "dragged face first through the makeup aisle at the dollar store" — and find a custom split hand-controller on the floor next to a pillow, built for a child with no arms. He has been quietly fostering six changeling orphans, using his own attendant slot plus all five of Carl's:

"It's all the system would let me."

"Combined, it's a little more than 1,000 gold a day. I've been paying myself with the money you've been giving me for supplies."

Donut calls it embezzlement. They are specifically the children with compression sickness, a birth defect caused by their parents' malnutrition on a new world, which means their shapeshifted forms are always missing parts — including a girl named Ruby, who in human form has no arms and a sunken-in head. He took them because he judged they wouldn't survive the end of Floor 7.

He can be criminally charged for the theft. Zev's response to the story is to try to monetise it — the AI refuses to let viewers watch it, so Borant licenses the story to a documentarian, Titan, who is preparing a vid about it with virtual characters. Donut isn't in it ("They didn't want to pay the extra licensing fee"). Mongo is. Mordecai is "especially grumpy" about the whole business.

docs.title: The Advice He Gives Once
docs.text:
In Chapter 30, privately, he says the thing nobody else will say about Katia's succession problem — that the safe answer is to let her go.

Mordecai: I'm helping Katia with this because she's become my friend. No, more than that. She's part of my family… You, Carl, you're helping her for the same reason. That, plus you have this sense of honor that's going to get you killed. I know you love Katia… But I also know you love Donut more.

Carl: No. We're not doing this. Not now.

Mordecai: Son. I can't have this conversation with Donut, but this needs to be said. The right thing to do is to help Katia. Yes. But the smart thing, and the safe thing is to step back and let her self-destruct… It's either her or Donut… It's not your fault. It's not Donut's fault. And honestly, it's not Katia's fault. Some breaks aren't clean.

Carl: No. We're not giving up on her, and I don't want you to bring it up again.

Carl's narration closes it: "Mordecai didn't answer. I knew he thought I was being stubborn. Stupid. Suicidal, even. He was right. I didn't care."

He never raises it again.

docs.title: Canadian
docs.text:
The Floor 9 guildhall relocation turns him human. Carl examines him in chapter 2:

Mordecai. Human. Level 50.

Manager of Princess Donut.

This is a non-combatant NPC.

This is a human. This one is something called a Canadian. Part French. Part maple syrup. He’s weirdly obsessed with ice hockey and snowmobiles and semi-erotic lumberjack fan fiction. Has a well-worn Tim Hortons loyalty card in his Velcro wallet. He says “aboot” instead of “about” and gets really, really upset when you point it out, claiming you’re hearing things and that it’s a harmful stereotype. It’s not a stereotype, and that’s exactly how it sounds. He has a relative who was trampled to death by a moose. You get the idea.

He arrives in a snowsuit, a raccoon hat and glasses, and takes the reaction badly:

“You make fun of me when I’m something stupid, and when I’m the most normal thing possible, at least to you, you also laugh? Fuck both of you.”

The "aboot" is not a one-off gag — it survives into his serious dialogue for the rest of the book.

No reclass is described

The book never narrates the change, never names a mechanic, and never uses the word "reclass." He simply walks out of the crafting room human in chapter 2. His level is unchanged at 50, and he is still flagged a Non-Combatant NPC, so nothing about his class or role moves — only the racial form, which is what the Changeling relocation mechanic has always done to him. Floor 9's playing field is populated largely by the crawlers themselves, which fits, but the text does not say so.

docs.title: The alchemy table
docs.text:
The single biggest change to what he can do. His table came out of Floor 8 upgraded past anything he has ever had:

He was in the crafting room, excitedly working on something on his newly-upgraded alchemy table. His table was now leveled up higher than he’d ever gotten it, and he was excitedly sending me messages about this potion and that. He now, apparently, had the ability to examine potions and see how they were made. This was the first time he’d had access to this ability, and his excitement was palpable.

Reverse-engineering does not consume the sample — "with my newest table upgrade, I can figure out the recipe without ruining it" — which means any rare potion the party loots becomes a recipe he can then mass-produce. Over the course of the floor that yields the hour-long aura potion used in the Club Vanquisher raid (the ones Prepotente had before "only lasted for two minutes"), gallons of a privacy-bubble potion, mass-manufactured Black Nimbus potions, and Mordecai's Special Brew, the potion that holds Louis's chest open during surgery. Donut's read on his mood is that he is excitable because he is Canadian now; Carl's is closer:

“He’s spent literally hundreds and hundreds of years wondering about some of these potions, and now he finally has the chance to learn all their ingredients and secrets. It’s gotta be exciting for him.”

docs.title: Surgeon
docs.text:
In chapter 84 Mordecai performs the heart-and-lung transplant that saves Louis Santiago, whose organs have been colonised by the Reaver CEO Epitome Tagg. Edgar the tortoise directs; Mordecai cuts. The donor is the flesh golem Princess Lunette, whose naiad heart and pulmonary system are extracted by Rosetta, Imani and Elle while Carl and Tipid hold Louis's ribcage open against the constant healing trying to close it. They have a thirty-second window.

The non-combatant rule holds even here — "Mordecai couldn’t be the one to remove the organs, lest it constitute an attack," so Bucket Boy does the pulling. Mordecai does the graft, slits the bronchial for a rebreather, and plumbs the new organs into a set of gills grown with a Water Breathing scroll.

Donut: DID YOU KNOW MORDECAI KNEW HOW TO DO THIS STUFF?

Carl: There’s still so much about all of them we don’t know.

docs.title: Uzzi's bolt
docs.text:
The Book 6 prologue debt comes due in chapter 86. Donut has Huanxin Jinx — the grixist heiress who extorted Odette's party on the tenth floor, and whose demand is the reason Uzzi was killed — pinned inside a circle of power words, stripped out of her goddess's soul armor, unable to teleport. Katia's crossbow is mounted on Donut's back, unloaded. And then Donut says they have a mutual friend outside.

“You’re a non-combatant NPC,” Huanxin hissed at Mordecai as she pulled herself up. She held her arm, which dripped blood. “You can’t touch me. You can’t fucking touch me.”

“No, I can’t. Not directly,” Mordecai said. He held something up. It was a simple crossbow bolt. There was nothing magical about it. “You see this?” He flicked the tip. “My brother died because of you and because of Odette and because of Chaco. But mostly because of you. Some of my mother’s ashes are built into the tip of this bolt. It’s a funeral rite in my culture. To make a weapon with the ashes of those you lost. My mother died before the crawl came to my world, and I’m grateful for the opportunity to allow her to avenge her son.”

Mordecai turned his attention to Katia. “Goodbye, Katia. Be safe, kid.”

He loaded the bolt into the crossbow on Donut’s back, turned, and he walked from the tent.

He does not stay to watch. Donut fires it between Huanxin's eyes a page later. The ashes are the same mementos he has kept on a shelf in his guildhall since Book 1, and the funeral rite is the first time the text explains what they were for.

docs.title: Ruby, and losing the children
docs.text:
The six changeling orphans with compression sickness that he took in on Floor 8 come down to Floor 9 with him, along with the gnome girl Bonnie and the flesh-golem children. They are a constant low presence through the book — he plays them war movies (Hamburger Hill, Platoon, Saving Private Ryan) hoping to talk them out of wanting to fight, which backfires completely and leaves the kids louder than ever about being allowed to join up.

The quiet scene is chapter 70. Carl bursts into the saferoom mid-crisis and finds him reading Anne of Green Gables to Ruby, the armless girl with the sunken-in head:

I almost said something, but I held back, seeing how young Ruby clutched onto Mordecai, how she had her misshapen head on his shoulder. I had a sudden memory of Katia and Annie from the dream, and I realized this was the same thing. He thinks it’s over, and this is how he’s choosing to spend his last few hours. If Donut died, he’d be done. I wasn’t sure exactly what would happen to him with the quarantine, but I knew he’d be out of the dungeon, and he would never see Ruby or any of the other kids again.

At the end of the book, Zerzura — the spell that lifts the entire city of Larracos and everyone in it to the 12th floor — takes them. Mordecai does not go; the text states it flatly and does not say why.

I gave one last cursory glance around me. Mordecai was here, too. He would not transfer with the Zerzura, and he held little Ruby in his arms, who would.

“It’s for the best, little one,” he said.

That is the whole goodbye. The book gives it two lines and moves on.

Zerzura, as far as the text supports it

Zerzura is a spell, cast at the end of Book 7, which transfers the city of Larracos — thousands of mercenaries, the NPC army, the children, Kiwi and the babies, and Edgar — to the 12th floor. Epitome Tagg names it: "the Zerzura spell, which will take the city of Larracos to the 12th floor." A handful of NPCs choose to stay behind with Carl instead. The mechanics beyond that are a Locations/Mechanics topic, not settled here.

docs.title: One more glimpse
docs.text:
During the shared-dream accident in the Several Days Earlier interlude, Carl's mind floods over everyone in the room. What he catches of Mordecai is one clause:

Of Mordecai and that deep, bottomless well of sadness within.

docs.title: Book 8: A Glitching New Form
docs.text: Floor 10's guildhall relocation gives Mordecai his strangest form yet — and the first one the book frames as an actual malfunction rather than just an unflattering species.

docs.title: Form
docs.text:
Carl finds him floating in the safe room "like a grim-reaper-style monster, but with really long arms," desiccated undead-like hands, and a black hood that hides everything but the occasional glint underneath:

Mordecai. Level 50. Moon Reaper.

From a dark, terrifying corner of Sheol, Moon Reapers are one of several different types of janitor mobs that occupy the 15th floor... Their gaze attack can come in many forms. That includes inflicting the dreaded Jaunt sickness.

He isn't actually a Moon Reaper, and he corrects the misconception himself once he stops malfunctioning: "I'm actually not a Moon Reaper, but a—" is interrupted by his own hood falling back to reveal a flaming eyeball, then a brief, unwilled prophetic trance in which he delivers cryptic doom pronouncements to Carl and Donut in a voice not his own ("Death awaits you at every turn... You should remember that, Oak Fell Champion of Nekhebit"). He downplays it immediately afterward as harmless theater rather than real prediction: "It's always vague bullshit that can be twisted to fit whatever happens... This stuff is designed to be scary, not true." He then glitches through several more shapes in quick succession — the Canadian form from Book 7, a black-and-white cat, an otter, a massive slug — before settling back into the reaper shape.

His own explanation for the instability: "I'm a shadow mimic. Mimics only take on the shape of the creature. Changelings can get some of the powers, though. That's why it's glitching, I think." He lays out why the combination is unstable at all — "shadow mimics and changelings are mortal enemies... shadow mimics think changelings are delicious" — which becomes load-bearing information later in the floor, when a real Adolescent Shadow Mimic turns out to be posing as a Desperado Club croupier (see Carl).

docs.title: Kept Away From the Others
docs.text:
Rosetta, watching him glitch every time an unfamiliar race gets near him for the first time — he nearly loses himself entirely when the sluggalette Bigs first wanders in — recommends isolating him for the floor: "We should probably keep you sequestered from the others for this floor." Later, when the party heads out for the finale, "only Mordecai remained inside the safe room" while everyone else, including non-combatant NPCs like Bucket Boy, went along.

No stated floor rule

Book 8 never states an official rule confining Mordecai to the safe room this floor. What the text actually gives is a practical, self-inflicted limitation — his glitching around unfamiliar races — and Rosetta's resulting recommendation to keep him isolated. Whether there is a system-level restriction behind it as well is not confirmed either way.

Sourced from Book 1: The Apocalypse Will Be Televised, Book 2: Carl's Doomsday Scenario, Book 3: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook, Book 4: The Gate of the Feral Gods, Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade, Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride, Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin, and Book 8: A Parade of Horribles.

docs.title: Odette
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Role: Host of Dungeon Crawler After Hours with Odette
  • Type: NPC / former crawler, now corporate figure
  • Race: Human ex-crawler; broadcasts using a bug-helmet, crab-body holographic persona
  • Status: Alive, married to the president of the corporation that bought out her prior criminal warrant (confirmed by Odette herself in Book 6). As of Book 6 she has put her show on hiatus and entered the dungeon personally, sponsoring the resurrected goddess Nekhebit in the Celestial Ascendency. In Book 7 she is on the 12th floor piloting Nekhebit in person, and names Princess Donut her Champion
  • Notable spells/abilities: None described — hosts remotely via hologram/avatar. From Book 7 she wields Nekhebit's divine powers by piloting the goddess directly, and Nekhebit's "Court" hands out spells to worshippers (Book 7)
  • Notable items: None described

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Odette is a human ex-crawler who made it to the stairs of Floor 13 before striking an unexplained "deal" and stepping away from the crawl. She's hosted Dungeon Crawler After Hours for generations, trained Mordecai during his own crawl, and has run a secret off-the-books rescue operation since at least Book 4 — extracting surviving Earth humans from the "Walk-On List" bounty market before rival hunters can capture and sell them.

docs.title: Role in the Story — Book 5
docs.text:
Odette reveals to Carl and Donut, just before airtime, that Beatrice — Carl's ex and Donut's original owner — is alive, and that Odette personally arranged her rescue in order to protect her own investment in the pair (and to pre-empt a rival production planning to ambush Carl with the same reveal). She stages the reunion as a serious, non-comedic segment, framing Bea's survival through a false "Borant heroically intervened" cover story in exchange for a higher revenue share on the remainder of the crawl's broadcast rights — a deal Odette insists was "an afterthought" next to protecting her investment in Carl and Donut, though Carl remains openly skeptical of that claim.

Odette also warns Carl and Donut, through her assistant Lexis, about the sixth floor's Butcher's Masquerade and its coming corporate upheaval — feeding them dangerous advance information (including that Queen Imogen is a repurposed human and that the party is being engineered to end in a mass battle) indirectly through Lexis rather than risk saying it herself. She confirms she personally caused something significant enough to Mordecai in the past that he still refuses to name it, telling Carl to "get the story from him." Separately, Mordecai reveals he once testified against Odette at her own criminal trial, from back when Odette was serving as his manager (not during her own crawl) — though the underlying incident is left unstated. Odette does not attend the masquerade itself; during the party it is a different sponsor-aligned celebrity, Empress D'Nadia, who taunts the elite Signet about the crawlers' odds of survival.

docs.title: Role in the Story — Book 6
docs.text: Odette stops being a talk-show host in Book 6 and becomes a player. The book opens with her worst act, told from Mordecai's point of view, and Chapters 35–37 are her explaining it.

docs.title: The Prologue
docs.text: Book 6's prologue is Odette as Mordecai's manager, generations ago, on the tenth floor. See Mordecai for the full account. In short: she bribed the grixist heiress Huanxin Jinx through her friend Armita to have the storm goddess Dodola open a stairwell puzzle; Huanxin kept escalating her price; Odette broke the deal at the last minute and instead had the crawler Chaco put a Dart of Ophiotaurus into Mordecai's brother Uzzi, force-summoning Dodola into the corpse inside a containment circle so she could be killed there. It worked. Mordecai reached the eleventh floor. Uzzi did not.

docs.title: On Air
docs.text:
Her final show before hiatus is not a confession — it is a press conference. Asked why she can't be the Princess Posse's Faction Wars adjutant:

"Oh, believe me, I was going to ask to do it, but I received an opportunity I can't pass up… That's right folks. The rumors are true. My show will soon be put on hiatus as I step into the dungeon. I have sponsored a deity, and I will be attempting my hand at the Celestial Ascendency."

The deity is Nekhebit, a massive Egyptian vulture goddess just resurrected on-floor by four unrelated crawlers hatching a speckled egg — slender human body, red dress, yellow vulture head, oak bow, and covered in healed wounds "almost like she'd been a corpse that had been exhumed."

"The origin story of Nekhebit is one of betrayal and revenge. She has earned every one of those scars. Whether she is considered a villain or a hero depends on one's perspective."

"Unlike all the other resurrected gods and goddesses on this floor, Nekhebit is not a retainer to any existing gods or goddesses. And yes, she will have a retainer of her own."

Carl reads it correctly: Huanxin was planning something, and Odette is refusing to let her have the advantage. She is going into the dungeon on equal footing.

The adjutant refusal has a second reason, which she gives him privately: adjutants stand physically on the battlefield, and Huanxin wanted her there "so she could legally exact her revenge." Her line to Carl: "Oh, I'm sorry. I didn't allow you to set me up for an assassination?" Carl picks Baroness Victory instead.

docs.title: The Confession
docs.text:
Chapter 37 is a private, off-the-record conversation engineered by having a Syndicate probe shot out of orbit to trigger an all-hands and pull Zev away. Fifteen minutes, her assistant Lexis the only witness.

Her stated motive for everything: "You think my motivations are money. Or fame. They're not. It's about Mordecai. It always has been."

  • Pieter and Armita. Her cousin Pieter, about thirteen, and her lifelong friend Armita, about seventeen, were taken into the dungeon with her. "Eventually, they forced me to choose. Pieter or Armita. I picked my friend. Simple as that. It was the right choice. Still, I think sometimes, I wonder… I had pushed them all. One more floor, I'd said… They'd all died because of it."
  • Why she became a game guide rather than a Celestial Attendant, which is what Armita took: "I didn't want to have anything to do with them. Those rich assholes running it all." She became Mordecai's manager and promised to get him out. "He reminded me so much of Pieter, the way he looked up to his brother. Once, he'd transformed into a human, and he even looked like him."
  • The bribe, in her own words: "I made an illegal deal with Huanxin to rig the game in exchange for credits. It was facilitated by Armita… But it went bad. She was driving a goddess named Dodola, and she'd asked for more money, and I was so tired of it. I felt just like you feel right now, Carl. I broke the deal at the last minute. I tricked her. We trapped the goddess in a containment, and Chaco killed her, causing her to lose the Ascendency game before it even started. Mordecai made it to the next floor, but Uzzi, Mordecai's brother, died."
  • Armita's death, the arrest, the warrant. Out of guilt, she filled out a voluntary crime-admission form after her release — "I was sure Armita would've turned me in, but she hadn't… she remained my friend while I betrayed her." Nobody read it in time. "The very first thing Huanxin did when she returned to the dungeon the following season was kill Armita. It was like it was nothing. After all, it was the dungeon. Perfectly legal. But then some bureaucrat finally read my statement, and I was arrested. Huanxin was given nothing more than a token punishment… my warrant was purchased by the man who'd eventually become my husband." She has also never had her legs fixed: "It felt wrong."
  • Watching Mordecai. "I watch him every day… drinking himself into oblivion. Crying over his brother… I did that. I killed Pieter. I killed Armita. And this one. This one I broke."
  • The title of the book comes from her. "We had a saying, my people. Never stare into the blinding eye of the Bedlam Bride. What it means is don't become obsessed with something, lest you're blinded to everything else. When it shows itself, it's all you can see. And that's exactly what I'd done."

She has set aside a large trust for Mordecai and for Chaco. Her plan against Huanxin, she says, is "going to kill me, most likely. But that's okay. It'll kill her, too."

Carl is not moved: "You're a part of it… You are the highest paid cheerleader for all of this. We die, and you applaud." Her exit line: "See you on the inside, Carl."

docs.title: What the Crawls Are For
docs.text:
Also in Chapter 37, almost in passing, Odette gives away the largest piece of worldbuilding in the book. See Game Mechanics for the mechanic itself; this is her delivery of it:

"This whole machine exists for a reason beyond what you see. The mantises mine and resurrect the AIs and then graft them into the planetary engines for a reason. The elements they mine, what do you think they're for?"

"All planets used for a crawl or any other game, such as Battle Royale or Land War are used to collect fuel. The elements. The byproduct of the biological overgrowth of the seeded systems. The entertainment aspect of it all came along later, but it's necessary in its own way. It's expensive, what they do. But without it, it all gets shut off. All of it. We need to shut the crawl down, but we have to do it in a responsible way. Lest we kill half the known universe. If we do this right, future collections will be humane. It will be done in a way that removes all the suffering. What I did to Mordecai. To Armita. To Pieter. What is happening to you. It will never happen again. And it's all coming together this season. This is our chance. Finally, after all these centuries. It's our chance."

Carl's entire response is "What the hell are you talking about?" Lexis cuts the conversation off seconds later, and the reveal is never elaborated on again in Book 6.

docs.title: Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin
docs.text: Odette is off-screen for most of Floor 9 and her fingerprints are on a great deal of it. She is on the 12th floor, inside the Celestial Ascendency, and everything she does reaches Larracos secondhand — through a goddess, through a title dumped onto Donut without warning, and through a trail of dead gods.

docs.title: Piloting Nekhebit
docs.text:
Book 6 had her “sponsoring” Nekhebit. Book 7 makes clear what that means in practice: an Ascendency player does not stand behind their deity, they get inside it and drive it. The text uses “piloting” and “driving” interchangeably. Carl’s running tally of who is inside whom: “Eileithyia, who was being driven by Huanxin Jinx, wasn’t a surprise... Odette was driving Nekhebit, and the Open Intellect’s agent, Rectrix, was driving Theia.”

The mechanic has a physical layer called soul armor. When Donut’s Laundry Day strips the divine armor off a summoned goddess, the pilot is “violently ripped from the soul armor of the goddess” and dumped on the floor as their ordinary, mortal self — which is exactly how Huanxin Jinx dies at the end of the book. The same thing had already happened to the influencer Nami, whose ejection left her a helpless human in the middle of a battlefield.

Piloting was optional until Ferdinand, prompted by Juice Box, burned a Team Retribution emergency action item that made it mandatory:

The second action item has been approved. Effective immediately, the following ascendency rules are applied. Ascendency players may no longer choose whether to pilot their sponsored deities should they be summoned off the 12th floor. Attendance is now mandatory. In addition, during gameplay summons, ascendency players may no longer choose to appear as themselves. All deities will appear as designed, and all sponsored deities will be piloted by their sponsors. Any summons currently in progress where the pilot stayed back because she was being a cowardly little chicken have been corrected.

docs.title: Hosting the Warlord Council in Person
docs.text:
The Faction Wars warlord council (Chapter 42) collapses before it starts: King Stalwart punches the correspondent, the former crawler Chaco, hard enough to knock him out of the room. Roughly two minutes later, Odette appears in his place — and not as the crab-bodied, bug-masked persona, but as herself.

There was a flash, and to everybody’s surprise, a new figure appeared in the room. It was Odette, but she wasn’t in her usual costume. She was without her mask, her breastplate, and her crab body. It was just her floating in her wheelchair. She wore a simple, yellow shirt, and she had her normally bigger-than-life hair back in a bun. Her long fingernails were gone. She, too, was holding a microphone.

“Hello, everyone,” Odette said, talking into the microphone. “I’m Odette. Yes, this is me out of gear if you haven’t seen me like this before. I just onboarded into the Ascendency where I am playing Nekhebit. They asked me if I would fill in for my very old friend Chaco, who is feeling a little...” she paused and gave Stalwart a look, “punched in the face right now.”

She runs the meeting flawlessly — an ad read for the Ultima Corporation, a read on the unprecedented Scolopendra Stirs warning, and a brutal interview of the drunk, disintegrating showrunner Cascadia. Her one genuine slip is a twitch of the eye when Epitome Tagg mentions the Skull Empire’s finances: “Odette, I realized, wasn’t used to having to hide her real reactions because she was usually behind a bug mask.”

The council’s substantive item is hers: she is the one who explains how the off-world teams are still talking to their home systems despite Team Retribution’s live-feed blackout, by paying to rename their own news programmes in the feed directory over and over. Carl burns an emergency action item to close the loophole, and notes that Odette looked “kind of irritated” about it.

His read on her presence:

The fact Odette was even here right now was a sign she was a master at this game. Was it possible she’d colluded with Chaco to get to this meeting? And how did she know so much about the activities outside the 12th floor? She was hosting this meeting like she’d never entered the dungeon. Was she getting prompted in real time?

docs.title: Champion of Nekhebit
docs.text:
Donut casts her third Atrocity in Chapter 76 and is immediately handed a new class and a title she did not ask for:

System Message: Warlord Princess Donut has received a new class.

System Message: Warlord Princess Donut will now be referred to as The Oak Fell.

System Message: The Oak Fell has been named Champion of Nekhebit.

Milk’s read: “it’s likely a side effect of some posturing that’s currently happening on the 12th. The fact she was also named Champion means it was something that was set in motion by Nekhebit.” Rosetta’s read on what the title actually costs:

“It’s similar to worshiping the deity. Enemies of Nekhebit will receive a bounty if they kill her.” She’d lowered her voice, making certain Donut wasn’t in earshot. “Honestly, it’s not too unlike Conscription, but with a lot more autonomy for Donut. Should the goddess want her to do something, she can order her to do it or face a smite.”

Carl’s reaction, in full: Fucking Odette. Rosetta guesses the mechanism was a standing spell — “something along the lines, ‘the first crawler to cast three atrocities on the next floor gets the title and class.’”

Donut is delighted rather than alarmed. Earlier, having picked up a spell from a god called Wepwawet, she had already worked out the connection: “Carl, Carl, it says he’s in the ‘Court of Nekhebit!’ and I can worship Odette now, too!” She keeps the title to the end of the book, and the goddess Eileithyia signs off on it: “That is wisdom, champion of Nekhebit, harbinger of doom.”

docs.title: Clearing Out a Sub-Pantheon
docs.text:
The thread runs under the whole book. Carl kills the bug-headed god Khepri on the ninth floor, and Khepri’s own description had already flagged the pattern — he “was a retainer of the god Khnum, but like several of the other deities in this particular sub-pantheon, Khnum mysteriously dropped dead a few days back,” leaving Khepri scrambling for a new patron.

Carl puts it together afterwards:

Khepri’s original description had given me a pretty big hint about some things that were currently going down on the 12th floor. He and Odette’s Nekhebit were in the same sub-pantheon. Someone was going through and killing off all the gods in that group. I figured it was either Odette for some reason or possibly Huanxin Jinx. I didn’t know enough to form a proper guess.

Two other pieces point the same way. The dying god Hellik, passing a message to his brother Emberus through Carl, names her directly: “Tell him the All Tree is beginning to rot. Tell him Nekhebit has returned, and I believe she is behind it all.” And Huanxin Jinx, arriving in the last chapter, confirms at least one kill in passing while complaining about the mess Larracos has made of the 12th floor:

“The whole court is in a tizzy about that city you fools just teleported in. It splattered an entire convent of Resheph’s nuns, and he is losing his mind. And now all those zombies are wandering all over the place and fucking Odette has taken control of them because she’s already taken out Inpewt, and it’s a big mess and the games haven’t even started yet.”

Unresolved

The campaign is established but never narrated. No scene shows Odette killing a god, and no count is given. Her Book 6 stated aim was Huanxin Jinx — “It’s going to kill me, most likely. But that’s okay. It’ll kill her, too.” — and Book 7 kills Huanxin without Odette present, by Donut’s Laundry Day and a crossbow bolt packed with Mordecai’s mother’s ashes. Whether the sub-pantheon purge was aimed at Huanxin, at the Ascendent throne, or at something else is not answered on the page.

docs.title: Still Unforgiven
docs.text:
Nothing has thawed between her and Mordecai. Standing over Huanxin Jinx in the last chapter, he lays out who he holds responsible: “My brother died because of you and because of Odette and because of Chaco. But mostly because of you.”

Sourced from Book 1: The Apocalypse Will Be Televised, Book 2: Carl’s Doomsday Scenario, Book 3: The Dungeon Anarchist’s Cookbook, Book 4: The Gate of the Feral Gods, Book 5: The Butcher’s Masquerade, Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride, and Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Osvaldo
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: Human Crawler
  • Race: Curupira (drawn from Brazilian folklore) — small-framed, red-haired (not his natural color), with backward-facing feet hidden under large boots
  • Class: Ranger
  • Level: 60 (Book 6) → 72 (Book 8)
  • Religion: Worships Tupa, alongside teammate Filipe L
  • Team: Team Flamengo — unaffiliated through Faction Wars, then racing solo on Floor 10 with Filipe L driving
  • Notable spells/abilities: Not described in detail beyond ranger fundamentals
  • Notable items: Two separate, non-functional memorial crystals tied to a standing quest from Tupa (see below); previously owned the pet hawk Gimli, killed at the end of the Butcher's Masquerade
  • Status: Deceased — killed in Heat 7 of Floor 10 by Britney Proskurina, who claims his memorial crystal from Ysalte and vanishes toward Sheol

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Osvaldo is a Brazilian ranger who spends three books circling the edges of Carl's story — a leaderboard name, then a looter, then a quiet holdout — before Book 8 finally gives him both a real arc and a real death. He never joins Carl's guild and never really likes Carl, but the two of them share more history than either particularly wants: two crossed memorial-crystal quests, a shared loss to the same crawler's carelessness, and, in the end, the same god's mercenary as his killer.

docs.title: Books 6–7: The Crystal Nobody Can Use
docs.text: Osvaldo first appears in Book 6 at #8 on the leaderboard, Level 60, owner of the pet hawk Gimli — killed at the end of the Butcher's Masquerade, likely by Prepotente or his familiar Bianca fighting over Queen Imogen's corpse. Osvaldo is the one who loots Queen Imogen's Memorial Crystal off her body in the chaos, which puts him directly in the path of both Carl's own standing Emberus quest (find whoever killed the god's son, Geyrun) and Prepotente's parallel private quest. Book 7 shows him teaming with a crawler named Jurgen and, off-page, losing the crystal to Prepotente during the chaos at the end of Faction Wars — the theft that finally moves Carl's long-stalled Emberus quest forward. Osvaldo and Team Flamengo sit out most of Faction Wars in the woods, a choice neither Donut nor Elle forgives, and then decline the Outreach Guild exit deal and continue on to Floor 10 anyway.

docs.title: Book 8: A Second Crystal, and a Shared God-Quest
docs.text:
Osvaldo reappears on Floor 10 riding the giant slaughter gnu Bruna, with teammate Filipe L (a level-63 human Strongman) holding the reins. He's still a prickly, standoffish presence — "he only talked to me when terrible stuff was happening" — but opens up to Carl in a rare direct message about the crystal business, revealing it was never resolved:

"I had a quest to collect a memorial crystal for Tupa. I didn't get it until right at the moment that Imogen died, and my entire party would have gotten smitten if I didn't collect it, so I did. But then after I got it, he said that one was corrupted, wrong. Then I had a lead on a second one in the forest during Faction Wars, and we hunted it down, and then the god said that one was wrong, too, and now I have a new quest to find out why the memorial crystals aren't working right."

He gave the first (Imogen's) crystal to Prepotente not out of generosity but exhaustion and spite — he'd meant to smash it in front of the goat as payback for Gimli's death, then simply handed it over instead, only for Prepotente to be ungrateful about the timing. Osvaldo's closing line on the whole chain of crossed quests doubles as the book's bleakest joke about Carl himself:

"Ysalte. The Vinegar Bitch. The one Paz killed. He was my friend, you know. Paz and Anton and even Sister Ines. It's like everyone who ever comes in contact with you dies. Now it's our turn, I suppose."

docs.title: Racing Floor 10
docs.text:
Osvaldo and Filipe race independently through every heat, occasionally overlapping with Carl's team or Jasha and Radoslav's Team Free Love in the garage row, trading beer-and-gossip banter about the other teams (Dwight's cheating win, the Corcunda situation) without ever joining Carl's alliance outright. Carl repeatedly urges him not to take unnecessary risks and to consider an exit deal, without success:
