Carl: Osvaldo, you're in the same heat as us. Don't do anything too rash. We have plans in motion to get as many people out as possible. Don't kill any of the other racers.

Osvaldo: Fuck off, Carl. I'm not talking to you. I won't attack you during the race unless it's you or us, but I don't give a shit about any of the other teams.

docs.title: Death
docs.text:
Osvaldo and Filipe reach Heat 7 — the last heat of Floor 10 — still unaffiliated and still refusing to commit to an exit deal, which puts them in the same heat as Carl's team and forces a crawler-vs-crawler outcome. During the race, cornered and stunned against a portal wall while fleeing, he is killed outright by Britney Proskurina, who has jumped into the same heat and claims the kill for a bounty:

A champion has fallen. A bounty has been claimed.

Crawler Osvaldo has been killed by Crawler Britney Proskurina.

Team Three, Team Flamengo, has been eliminated due to the death of their last racer.

Britney lands directly on his corpse as the kill lands, a golden player-killer skull forming over her head. Carl's only reaction is a private, helpless one: "You stubborn idiot... Why did it have to come to this?"

What Britney takes from the body is not the crystal Prepotente already has — it's the other memorial crystal Osvaldo had been chasing all book, the one tied to the long-dead goddess Ysalte:

"I saw her," I said, watching Britney, my paws up on the dash. The barbarian crawler casually sauntered back toward the gecko and Louis. "She has the memorial crystal from Ysalte now."

Samantha immediately flags what that means: "She needs to get to the Basilica or the Vulgar Temple and place the gem in the plinth, and she'll be back for good." Britney disappears through a portal shortly after, taking the crystal with her; see Britney Proskurina for where that leads.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Britney Proskurina — kills Osvaldo and inherits his last quest object
  • Prepotente — holds Osvaldo's first memorial crystal, from Queen Imogen
  • Carl — the crawler Osvaldo blames, not entirely wrongly, for everyone around him dying

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride, Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin, and Book 8: A Parade of Horribles.

docs.title: Paz Lo
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Full designation: Crawler #8,199,454, "Paz Lo"
  • Type: Human Crawler (Cuban); a prison guard, not an inmate
  • Race: Human
  • Class: Santero — per Sister Ines, "a necromancer cleric. He also has a lot of healing and protection spells." Carl reads him as a warrior cleric. His mere presence agitates the undead: "Warning: The presence of a Santero has aggravated the already-unsettled dead."
  • Subclass: None printed — his character sheet shows race, class and deity only
  • Level: 45 at introduction → 101 as a totem card after killing a goddess
  • Religion: Worshipper of the god Ogun (palm-frond symbol), until Ogun smites him
  • Notable spells/abilities: Turtle — a temporary, very strong shield that draws aggro but roots him in place, unable to move or attack, and cannot be cancelled once cast; Self-Destruct — a suicide blast he can aim magically at a single target, which Carl covets for its precision; plus healing, protection and necromancy
  • Notable items: Full glowing silver plate armor with platform boots, worn with a backwards baseball cap; a mace "twice as long as he was with a diamond-shaped head the size of a beer keg" that he summons into his hands
  • Status: Deceased, twice over — killed by Ogun's unhealable smite in Chapter 16, flagged into a T'Ghee totem card at the instant of death, then freed when Carl and Donut ripped the card in Chapter 72

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Paz is one of three Cuban crawlers Carl and Donut meet on Floor 8, with his cousin Anton Lopez and Sister Ines Quiteria. Carl initially assumes the two heavily-tattooed men are convicts; Paz corrects him flatly: "we weren't prisoners. We were guards. It was a women's prison. We were outside, walking them to the med building when it happened."

He is enormous, armored head to toe, and disarmingly gentle. His self-description of his combat role: "Mostly I just curl up on the ground and let the bad guys hit me." Mongo, on meeting him, immediately shoves his face into Paz's mirror-polished breastplate to look at himself and knocks Paz flat on his back "like an upset turtle." Paz howls with laughter.

He and Anton both took up Ogun on a priest's advice that the god would protect them from being controlled — a precaution against Ines's Toxoplasma racial skill. It did not work, and the skill made them forget why they had done it within minutes.

docs.title: The Smiting
docs.text:
The Cuba storyline requires the party to repair a set of god-shrines. Anton, charmed by the goddess Oshun, hurls the Ogun shrine piece out the door, and the system warns that the two Ogun worshippers will take a smite for it. Ogun — God of Blacksmithery and Armor, Level 250 — turns up in person, because "Ogun strongly believes all punishments should be handed out in person."

Carl casts Black Nimbus on Anton to try to strip him out of the god's targeting. Ogun's reply: "That was a good attempt. But all you have done is removed this man from my protection. From my mercy. Not from my wrath." He then takes a step backward, steps on Anton's head, and crushes it — "Just like that, as if he was nothing."

Paz gets worse. Ogun heals him completely first, so that he can take something away:

"Paz, you are no longer under my grace. For your failure, I am taking your ability to heal this condition you now suffer. Go in darkness, and when you pierce the veil, you will find yourself alone and without armor."

The condition is a permanent, unstoppable bleed. Ines can top his health up but cannot slow the drain. The smite leaves a hand-shaped burn across his face that strips the skin away, showing red muscle and the white of his teeth. Paz calls the affliction the Inevitable debuff:

"I remember it all," Paz said. "Ogun, he cured me of everything. Everything except the Inevitable debuff. I don't worship him anymore." He let out a groan. "He promised he would fix it, and he did. But only at the end."

Not in the system text

"The Inevitable" is Paz's own word for the condition. No system debuff block for it appears anywhere in the book. (Unrelatedly, a T'Ghee card called The Inevitable is mentioned in the cookbook as representing the goddess Ysalte — the text draws no link between the two.)

docs.title: Becoming a Card
docs.text:
Paz spends his last minutes saying goodbye. Sister Ines refuses to let him:

"No," Sister Ines shouted, her voice suddenly angry. "No! You're not leaving."

"No, no, no. Please. You're not leaving me. Everyone leaves me."

She produces a squad flag and jabs it into his neck. Whoom. Paz becomes a card — green, the common tier. Even Ines seems stunned it worked. It is the first time in the series a crawler is turned into a T'Ghee totem, and it establishes that dead crawlers can be pressed back into service as summons.

Carl carries the guilt for the rest of the book.

docs.title: "Please. No More."
docs.text:
Ines summons him in the eight-way FOCSA card battle in Chapter 56. He comes out of the card with the burn still across his face:

"Sister," Paz called up to the nun. "Please. No more. I can't take… gah!"

"Paz," she called. "Accept your suffering! Use your self-destruct skill the moment this false god…"

She never finishes the order — Quan Ch plays a Force Play card that burns her Flee, ends her fight and loses her the key. Paz dissipates into dust in the snake's mouth.

docs.title: The God Predator
docs.text:
After Louis kills Ines, her celestial patron Ysalte — Goddess of Hopelessness and Insanity, Level 250, invulnerable on this floor — enters the realm and inherits an enhanced version of Ines's deck. Which includes Paz.

Carl is head-first inside Samantha's neck when it happens, so the only eyewitness account is Donut's:

KATIA GAVE PAZ AN ARROW THING, AND HE STUCK IT INTO THE DWARF LADY'S EYE, AND THEN HE BLEW HIMSELF UP, BUT THE EXPLOSION WAS ALL CONCENTRATED ON THE GODDESS'S NECK. HER HEAD FELL OFF! WE ALL FELL DOWN SEVERAL STORIES. THEY GAVE HIM CREDIT FOR IT EVEN THOUGH HE WENT AWAY WHEN SHE DIED.

The arrow is Katia's Bolt of Ophiotaurus, the anti-deity bolt Princess Formidable sent her back on Floor 4 for use on Prince Maestro; Katia had already fired it once and recovered it, because magical bolts can be reused as long as they don't break. Paz's Self-Destruct — a suicide blast he can aim at a single target — does the rest, concentrated entirely on the goddess's neck.

A deity has fallen. The heavens tremble with rage.

System Message. Crawler Paz Lo has slain the goddess, Ysalte. He has been marked for death by all deities except sworn enemies of the late goddess.

Ysalte's equipment is awarded to Paz, upgrading his armor. Carl's reaction on hearing it: "Paz had killed the goddess. But how? How was it possible? He was her own totem."

His card description has changed:

Paz Lo. The God Predator. Level 101 Former Crawler.

docs.title: Release
docs.text:
Katia hands the card to Donut as soon as the goddess falls. In the last chapter, with the option of keeping a single card down to Floor 9, Donut suggests keeping Paz — "Maybe there's a way to set him free." Katia has already decided: "We rip it. That's what he wanted." Imani and Elle agree.

Carl refuses to keep him, remembering the look on his face when Ines summoned him:

Please, he'd said. No more.

"We can't," I said… "We should never have let the Sister turn him into one in the first place. It was my fault. It's not right."

Donut asks whether she'll get another player-killer skull for it. Carl: "No. It calls him a former crawler now. I don't know what that really means, and I don't want to find out."

And then, without any additional fanfare, Donut put one corner of the card in her mouth. She held the other corner down against my shoulder, and she ripped. Just like that. The card disappeared in a puff of smoke. She did not get a player killer skull.

"Goodbye, Paz," I said.

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: Penelope ("Penny")
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: Transformed pet → fully sapient crawler ally
  • Race: Yorkshire pig
  • Class/Subclass: Not applicable — enters the party too late in the book to select one; appears with no assigned class
  • Level: 10 (as Crawler #12,953,454, "Penelope 3")
  • Prior status: Belonged to Nico and Dario's "One Fine Pig" team (see Supporting cast), and was already the target of a stray love-spell (Touch of Maw-Loo / the Snowdrop Curse) that made certain NPCs — including the god Taranis — fall for her on sight, with Taranis magically protecting her from harm
  • Notable spells/abilities: None of her own; communicates over chat rather than speech
  • Notable items: A movement/oxygen harness, a collar with a trap module, and Katia's old Enchanted Spiked Kneepads of the Munificent Goddess Kina (passed down through Donut), which also grant temporary deity-proximity effects like Carl's Scavenger's Daughter patch
  • Status: Alive — ends the book with Carl's party rather than with Taranis

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Penny is a literal farm pig, mixed up with a mythic engine-of-war centipede, and turned into a person entirely by accident. Once sapient, she becomes central to the endgame's most dangerous gambit — deliberately provoking two gods into a fight — and comes out the other side both wiser and, apparently, single.

docs.title: Made Sapient
docs.text:
Penny was already caught up in the plot before her transformation: as a pet of Nico and Dario's team, she carries a curse that makes certain NPCs — most consequentially the god Taranis — compulsively infatuated with her, with Taranis personally protecting her from harm on pain of death. Carl takes custody of her after Nico and Dario die and he uses the winner's key to open their abandoned garage.

Penny's transformation is not the biscuit mix-up

An easy error, and one this page previously made: Penny is not the victim of the famous mixed-up biscuit. Carl feeds her deliberately, with the correct item, during Floor 11's ninety-minute float-building phase — before the parade, before the arena, and before Eris ever scrambles anyone's inventory. The mix-up belongs entirely to Scolopendra, later, mid-fight. The two events use the same family of item, which is what makes them easy to conflate.

The feeding itself happens off-page; the last the reader sees is Carl calling her over in the garage ("Penny, come here. I got a snack for you") as the parade timer runs out. Carl's own retrospective account, in the arena, names both the item and the intent — and is characteristically uneasy about what he has done to her:

We'd fed her the enriched pet biscuit. The Nothing Special Party Companion one... it didn't give her the ability to talk out loud.

Penny communicates over party chat rather than speech from that point on, and because Carl is the one who fed her the biscuit, she is automatically placed in a party with him. The system assigns her a new identity outright:

Crawler #12,953,454. Penelope 3. Yorkshire Pig. Level 10.

docs.title: Bait
docs.text:
Carl is explicit that Penny's transformation immediately becomes tactical: "Especially since I was planning on using this poor woman as bait." The plan is to use her — and Taranis's obsession with her — to lure both Taranis and the fire god Emberus into the same place at the same time and provoke them into fighting each other, buying the party room to work.

The execution is blunt and uncomfortable even by the book's standards. Carl straps Penny into a movement backpack, doses her repeatedly with "splooge" (a running gag drug/potion — Penny's repeating in-scene line is "GIVE ME MORE SPLOOGE. I CRAVE SPLOOGE"), fits a magic ring through her nipple for underwater oxygen (an item called Petey Motteux's Little Secret), and finally holds a gun to her head to force the confrontation into the open:

"Taranis, if you don't want me to shoot this fucking pig in the fucking head, show yourself!"

Both Taranis and Emberus answer the summons. Taranis's reaction on seeing her in danger is immediate and genuine: "Penelope! My sweet love! Hold on! I will protect you." When she is nearly killed during the fight that follows, he personally revives her.

docs.title: The Breakup
docs.text:
Book 8 does not end with Taranis taking Penny away with him — a natural assumption given how hard he falls for her, but not what the text shows. After the confrontation, Taranis sets Penny down safely beside Carl and Donut, and Penny herself ends things, over a much smaller betrayal than anything else that happened that day:

"HE LIED ABOUT THE SPLOOGE, SO WE BROKE UP. I HAD NO IDEA HE WAS MARRIED."

Taranis leaves the realm afterward, but not with Penny — he departs with Samantha, who slips away from the party to hitch a ride with him and Krakaren Prime on her own private mission (see Samantha). Penny stays behind with Carl's group, folded into the party alongside the newly-sapient "Sexy Scolopendra."

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Carl — engineers the trap that transforms Penny into bait
  • Princess Donut — grabs the wrong biscuit for Scolopendra in the same climax
  • Sexy Scolopendra — the transformation that actually was a mistake
  • Samantha — leaves with Taranis instead of Penny
  • Supporting cast — for Nico and Dario, Penny's original owners

Sourced from Book 8: A Parade of Horribles.

docs.title: Dmitri and Maxim Popov
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: Two crawlers sharing one body
  • Race: Nodling — a two-to-six-headed race; splitting apart on death spawns a new toddler-then-adult creature per head
  • Class: Dmitri: Illusionist → Visionary (Book 5 specialization). Maxim: Bogatyr (melee)
  • Level: Ranked 5th on the Floor 6 leaderboard as a combined entity
  • Status: Ineligible — both are pre-collapse children, rescued from the dungeon as newborn nodling yearlings after their shared adult body dies in Book 5
  • Notable spells/abilities: A shared, flaming meteor-hammer melee weapon
  • Notable items: None named individually

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Dmitri and Maxim Popov are fraternal twin brothers whose game guide steered them into the Nodling race specifically because it grants an "extra life" on death — not warning them that doing so would fuse the two into a single, permanently shared two-headed body. Dmitri is the gentler, rounder-faced half (an Illusionist/Visionary mage); Maxim is the more chiseled, blunt melee half (a Bogatyr). Both are minors: Dmitri had just adopted a kitten, Kapitan Whiskers, the day before the collapse.

docs.title: Role in the Story — Book 5
docs.text:
The Popov brothers rank 5th on the Floor 6 leaderboard and share an autograph table with Carl at CrawlCon, where Dmitri repeatedly expresses a wish to meet Donut in person. They fight alongside Carl and the rest of the top-50 at the Butcher's Masquerade, and are killed instantly during the climactic battle when a flaming, magically hurled elf mount skewers their shared body.

Per Nodling racial mechanics, their death splits them apart into two separate infant bodies — newborn nodling yearlings. Carl and Katia dig the pair out of the battlefield's wreckage before anyone can loot them; their status flashes to Ineligible and they're automatically teleported to a kinder facility on Earth's surface, revealed by Zev to have been engineered deliberately: their original game guide chose the race specifically to guarantee this escape route, using the dungeon's ban on pregnant or child crawlers as a loophole to free them.

Sourced from Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade.

docs.title: Prepotente
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Race: Caprid
  • Class: Forsaken Aerialist → Profane Vitiate (Book 5, Floor 6 specialization)
  • Level: 27 (Book 2) → 34 (Book 3) → 57 → 71 (end of Book 5) → #1 on the leaderboard (Book 6) → 99 → 100 (Book 7). At level 99 he is "by far—the strongest crawler in the dungeon," and stays that way until Donut passes him late in Book 7
  • Sapience: Confirmed in Book 3 — one of only two Earth-origin creatures (alongside Princess Donut) known to have gained true human-level sapience
  • Party: Solo, alongside his familiar Miriam Dom — deceased as of Book 5; briefly parties with Carl and Donut at the very end of Book 5, for convenience, then leaves
  • Affiliation (Book 7): Colonel in the Princess Posse — he asks Carl to recruit him in chapter 48, ending six books of operating alone
  • Notable items: Enchanted Night Wyrm's Ring of Divine Suffering (Book 5, a second copy of Carl's — swallowed whole after Miriam Dom's death); "Memorial Crystal: Apito" (Book 7, acquired off-page from the crawler Osvaldo); a complete memorised interior map of Club Vanquisher

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Prepotente is, as of Book 2, a complete mystery — a name and a rank with no attached scene, backstory, or physical description anywhere in the text. Prepotente appears exactly once: as an entry on the tentative Floor 3 leaderboard Odette reveals near the end of the book. Even Carl, reading down the list in real time, has no idea who this is:

"Who is Prepotente?" I asked, reading down the list. I knew Florin was the crocodile-headed dude with the shotgun. Miriam Dom was the goat lady. I didn't know Ifechi.

Nobody answers him. Unlike Florin, Miriam Dom, or Li Jun — all of whom Carl can immediately place from prior broadcast appearances — Prepotente gets no follow-up identification at all in Book 2.

docs.title: Leaderboard
docs.text: Ranked 3rd, at Level 27 with a bounty of 400,000 — see Level 3: Leaderboard for the full table.

docs.title: Book 3: The Mystery Solved
docs.text: Prepotente turns out to be exactly what his class name suggests: a former goat belonging to Miriam Dom, transformed into a sapient, aerialist crawler by the same Enhanced Pet Biscuit mechanic that turned Donut into a person. Carl meets him directly on Floor 4, mid-battle, through a portal connecting their two locations — Prepotente is condescending, theatrical, prone to shrieking mid-sentence for no apparent reason, and openly proud of being one of only two Earth creatures (himself and Donut) to have achieved true sapience. He was in the middle of a slow, days-long assassination of a province boss (via cardiac arrest, entranced) when Carl's group accidentally teleports the target away, souring the encounter considerably. He threatens to kill several people over the course of the conversation, none of it apparently sincere; Miriam Dom manages him with a shepherd's crook and casual affection, whacking him with it when he's rude and kissing him on the head as a reward for good behavior. He expresses a genuine, long-standing wish to share a drink with Donut and discuss their shared, singular circumstances.

docs.title: Book 5: Mother's Death and a Vow of Extinction
docs.text:
Prepotente and Miriam Dom are hunted across Floor 6 by an elite vampire hunter, Viscount Fog, and his cursed mount. A botched scroll of Community Pool — meant to transfer Miriam's new vampirism curse onto Fog — backfires when Fog's counter-ring bounces the spell back and forth between them, leaving Prepotente Stunned and then Fragile (one hit point, unhealable) at the exact moment his own newly-acquired Ring of Divine Suffering activates on its own and marks Miriam — the only eligible target in range — leaving Prepotente himself afflicted with Left to Fester, unable to heal until his own mark, his mother, dies. Fog dies of his own reflected curse at sunset; Prepotente is left paralyzed, aware, and unable to move or speak while his mother spends the night defending his body from infected wildlife, then asks Carl and Donut to watch over them both until dawn.

At sunrise, Miriam Dom burns to death by choice — Carl having secretly marked her to break the curse — and Prepotente, freed the moment she dies, collects every item she'd left behind, then takes his own Ring of Divine Suffering off, picks it back up off the ground, and eats it whole rather than continuing to wear or loot it normally. He declares, screaming to the sky, that he intends to kill everyone even remotely responsible for her death "or perish trying," then mounts his mother's now-flight-capable Hellspawn familiar, Bianca Del Ciao, and spends the rest of the floor grinding levels almost exclusively by killing the world-quest "Odious Creeper" undead monsters Miriam's death unleashed — racking up ten solo kills, gaining ten levels and roughly eighty stat points in a single day, funded by an emergency benefactor box from his sponsor, the Plenty.

docs.title: The Butcher's Masquerade
docs.text: At the masquerade, Prepotente corners Carl and insists on temporarily joining his and Donut's party — not out of any interest in the changeling-evacuation plot happening around him, but purely to get his hands on a pair of sponsor-gifted items in Donut's possession, an Enchanted Hammer of Fast Forward and an Enchanted Stick of Cascadia's Screams (both benefactor-box items whose notes specified they be given to Donut). He'd also used his new wealth to purchase a Seventh Floor Pole Position boon at the prize counter, and separately deduces (correctly) that Floor 7 is built around the fairy tale of a boy trapped in an inescapable, resurrection-looped maze — intelligence he pieces together from an overheard interview and from the unusually long item description on his mother's looted boots, which he refuses to fully explain to Carl. At the battle's climax, he personally delivers the killing blow to Queen Imogen, smashing a potion into her face moments after Carl's disco-ball attack disorients her — and pursues his own quest for the Memorial Crystal: Apito (its exact nature undisclosed to Carl) — which turns out to double as a lead in Carl's own, separate, preexisting Emberus quest to find whoever killed a figure named Geyrun. Neither thread gets resolved: the crystal is looted by a third crawler, Osvaldo, before either Prepotente or Carl can claim it. He briefly, grudgingly parties with Carl and Donut as Floor 7 begins (strictly for Donut's help, per him — "Carl is not necessary") just long enough to borrow the hammer and stick back from her, then leaves the party and uses them, together with the knowledge from his mother's boots, to shatter the level's opening puzzle chamber outright — ending the floor's intended maze mechanic for every crawler simultaneously, to the AI's audible fury ("Godsdamnit, Prepotente. Don't do it. Please. I worked so hard to make this floor happen.").

docs.title: Book 6: The Stairwell Theory, and a Grudging Pardon
docs.text: Prepotente spends Floor 8 alone in the Bahamas with Bianca, sitting at #1 on the leaderboard, lonely enough that he keeps asking Carl to read him the region's lore book.

docs.title: "A Carl and Pony Theory"
docs.text:
Carl works out that a hell portal could be made to scour the entire planet, and that a crawler standing directly beneath an enclosed stairwell chamber would be carried up with it and could strike the stairwell on the way. He then takes the idea to the smartest crawler he knows to have it broken:

"Actually, you're the smartest guy I know. Let me run something by you really fast. Here's the thing. I don't want it to be local. I want it to spread over the whole world. I need ideas."

Carl credits the finished plan jointly — "It's a theory. It's a Carl and Pony theory, though, if that means anything" — and it is Prepotente's endorsement that gets the rest of the dungeon to actually risk their lives on it:

"Everyone. As much as it pains me to say this, I believe Carl is correct. We have seen gated stairwell encasements break before. I once watched Lucia Mar attempt to teleport a stairwell to another location, and I witnessed what happened to both the stairwell itself and the surrounding structure. This portal is of a particular type, and I believe Carl's theory is sound. I'm certainly not going to risk it myself. I am going to make my way down the stairwell using my key in just a moment, but I am reasonably certain there's at least a fifty percent chance this will work. Maybe forty percent."

He then revises it downward twice more within the hour: "Remember, I amended it to 40 percent, Carl… So maybe I should have said 35 percent."

He also warns Carl to read the quest's winning conditions carefully, because the crawlers in Indonesia — the landmass furthest from Havana — will be the ones who die if the demon isn't buffed enough.

docs.title: The Forgiveness
docs.text:
His actual goodbye is warm, by his standards:

"For what it's worth, Carl. I do hope you and Princess Donut survive this foolish endeavor. You are an oafish brute, and it's a miracle you have made it this far, but the dungeon would not be the same without you."

And then, as an afterthought, he lets Carl off for Miriam Dom:

Prepotente: I've decided to not kill you for letting my mother hurt herself. I have been contemplating it for some time now. I've decided you were too stupid to have done anything about it anyway. Your penance will be to assist me in exacting my revenge on the true culprits.

The running argument is intact to the end: "How many times must I tell you not to call me by that name?"

docs.title: Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin
docs.text:
For most of Book 7 Prepotente is simply the strongest thing on the floor. He enters at level 99, unaffiliated, hiding his position from everyone, riding a Bianca Del Ciao who has grown to level 70 and full size with a second set of wings. He announces his intentions in chapter 18 and then goes and does exactly what he said:

Prepotente: …Once the festivities begin, I have a very specific score to settle with the lead producer of the Blood Hunter program, and after that is complete, only then will I come to your aid and join in your military. If you’re still alive.

docs.title: He kills the Blood Sultanate's army by himself
docs.text:
The naga — the Blood Sultanate — own Blood Hunter, the program that sent Viscount Fog after his mother. The Posse spends the opening of Open Hostilities unable to work out why the naga seem to have no troops. The answer, found by Elle and Edgar scanning the stronghold, is that the barracks are full of corpses.

They were dead. The Blood Sultanate was almost defeated already, and they were trying to hide it.

Elle's report when she runs into him is the first anyone hears of it:

Elle: …the moment we moved into position that goddamned goat friend of yours appeared out of nowhere and went absolutely apeshit on us. He's the one who took out most of their army! I don’t know how he did it, especially without magic, but that goddamned thing is level 99 now.

He did it alone, and he did it before Operation: Snake Pit — Carl's own plan to kill the naga line of succession — could reach them. Carl only learns of it after Snake Pit has already launched, which means the entire operation was aimed at an enemy that no longer had an army. The method is never explained: "Prepotente did something—the details of which were still unclear—that killed off a huge chunk of their army."

Unresolved

Carl asks him directly how he did it and never gets an answer. The book never returns to it.

He did not get to finish. The naga called foul, claiming he was an unofficial agent of the Princess Posse. He won the hearing, then threatened the entire quorum — including Baroness Victory — and was put in penalty stasis. His furious message to Carl, delivered in chat, is his best rant in the series:

Prepotente: Carl, you idiotic, bumbling, feckless imbecile. You cad. You fool. You ruiner… I have already defeated their standing army, and just as I was about to finish off my vengeance, I was stopped because they claimed I am unofficially part of YOUR silly fighting force… SHE WAS MY MOTHER, AND IT IS MY RIGHT TO EXACT VENGEANCE AGAINST THE NAGA… THERE WILL BE NO MORE WARM HUGS FROM ME. YOU ARE BANNED! SO HELP ME IF SHE GETS AWAY, I WILL HOLD YOU ACCOUNTABLE. I SPIT! I SPIT IN YOUR EYE!

Carl's read is that the naga complaint accidentally saved everyone: Prepotente did not know the Sultana could vanish at will, and had he pressed on, he would have spooked her into hiding and damned both Donut and Katia.

docs.title: Joining the Princess Posse
docs.text:
Chapter 48 is the status change. Adjudication rules mean Carl cannot so much as coordinate with an unaffiliated crawler, and Prepotente has worked that out before Carl opens his mouth.

I held up a hand at Prepotente. “Look. We can’t talk at all unless you’re in the army. I know you don’t want...”

“I know, Carl. I am not an imbecile. Recruit me.”

I paused. “Are you sure?”

“Do it now before I change my mind. If this is the only way I may salvage this utter fuckup on your end, then make it so.”

Carl had a potion of Conscription in his other hand, behind his back, and stows it — a small private moment about how close he came to doing this the ugly way. He makes Prepotente a Colonel instead of the Legionnaire his first instinct suggested.

What follows is not what anyone in the clearing expected.

The goat rushed forward and pulled me into a tight hug. He started to uncontrollably sob. “You’re my best friend, Carl. I’ve been so lonely. When you didn’t show up at the Bahamas on the last floor, I thought...” He didn’t finish the sentence. He was letting out these huge, wet, snot-filled sobs. It had come so suddenly and unexpectedly, and he was clutching onto me like I was a life raft. Everyone around us just stopped what they were doing to look at us. Even Bianca appeared embarrassed.

He continued to sob, and he spoke between the gasps. “Let us put our differences aside... I’m ready for the emptiness to be filled. I have several enhanced pet biscuits ... but after what happened last time, I’ve been so afraid... And now I’m afraid it’s too late. Bianca is fine company, but she doesn’t speak. You are absolutely right. ... We need to keep communicating. I need to come to terms with you being an idiot and be grateful for what I have. ... You can’t help how stupid you are.”

And then, the moment Carl relaxes:

You’d think I’d be ready for what happened next by now, but it still caught me off guard.

He screamed right in my damn face.

docs.title: The Club Vanquisher map
docs.text:
On the walk to the Club Vanquisher raid, he mentions in passing that he has the layout of the entire place.

I stopped dead, my hand on the door to the temple. I turned to look at Prepotente, incredulous. “You have an interior map of Club Vanquisher?”

“Oh, yes. My mother, Bianca, and I made friends with a delightful guildmaster inside the club, and she gave us the map. We used a secret exit, and we came out of a bathroom stall inside of the entrance temple.”

He tapped the side of his head. “It’s all right here. Perfect recall, Carl.”

Carl's reaction is regret rather than relief: "That would’ve been really useful. I was once again reminded of Donut’s advice long ago that I should’ve tried harder to speak with him."

docs.title: Miriam Dom, vampire, and the ban
docs.text:
The Milk interlude supplies the other half of that story, and confirms something Book 5 left implicit. Milk, the xenopus cartography guildmaster, is woken by screaming outside her hidden guild and examines the two crawlers who burst in:

The older, female crawler was originally a human, but her race was Vampire, which wasn’t a race someone could voluntarily choose. That meant it was likely a recent thing, and upon noticing this, they had likely just told her that her access to Club Vanquisher was being revoked. Her child, who’d apparently taken a caprid race, was upset about this.

"Upset" is Prepotente melting the mantaur guards with Bianca while Miriam Dom tries to drag him out — "Prepotente Lorenzo De La Rosa! Stop that this instant!" Milk hands them the map, and the secret exits, under the fig leaf of being threatened into it. It is also where Miriam's kindness to an NPC — healing Milk's burned arm with her own salve, for nothing — starts the chain of events that eventually brings Milk into Faction Wars.

docs.title: The crystal
docs.text:
Carl's standing Emberus quest and Prepotente's own private quest have been chasing the same object since Book 5. In Book 7 it surfaces in the hands of the crawler Osvaldo, a holdout hiding in the woods with a group called Team Flamengo, and it starts glowing hard enough to light up the sky in the middle of Carl's raid on the Madness castle. Neither Carl nor Prepotente can go for it at the time.

Then it simply changes hands:

Memorial Crystal: Apito has fallen from Crawler Osvaldo’s hands and is now in possession of Crawler Prepotente. Retrieve it from him before he cracks the secrets and gives them to the Epicure.

I had no idea how the memorial crystal had gotten from Osvaldo to Prepotente without a fight.

Unresolved

The transfer happens entirely off-page. Carl decides to sit Prepotente down and explain the whole Emberus business when things calm down, expecting him to be "an ass about it," and never gets the chance inside Book 7. The wider Emberus/Apito material is a Mechanics topic; what matters here is that the crystal is now Prepotente's and that it is the live thread in Carl's quest.

docs.title: Around the floor
docs.text:
• He rides in to shield Carl's whole force against the Madness's mass psionic attack outside their castle — "I will be to you in moments, Carl, and I will shield you and the rest of the force" — and warns of a third enemy column coming up from under the castle.
  • He drinks soda pop before battle — Big Red, sarsaparilla, Diet 7-Up, "I can only drink up to five soda pops a day. It’s a hard rule my mother gave me. She says... she said if I drink too many, I get hyper." The tense correction is the whole character in one line.
  • He plays the prisoner to get past the Club Vanquisher door guard, throwing himself on the floor in fuzzy unlocked handcuffs: "I have been caught! My goose has been cooked! Oh woe! Oh woe!"
  • Before the temple assault he mutters a litany of names to himself — Miriam, Bianca, several others, ending on "Ragazzaccia," which Carl does not recognise.
  • He is level 100 by the end, and no longer the strongest crawler in the dungeon: Donut passes him after War Crime, and Carl notes he is "getting left behind" by Donut, Li Na and Prepotente alike.

docs.title: Book 8: A Parade of Horribles
docs.text: Floor 10 gives Prepotente the book's biggest emotional arc outside of Carl and Donut themselves — a temptation he talks himself out of, a devastating vision he's talked out of, a surprise musical triumph, a stolen relic, and a rescue that costs two other people their lives.

docs.title: The Paramour Biscuit
docs.text:
Early in Heat 2, Prepotente shows Carl and Donut a celestial-box Enriched Pet Biscuit called "The Paramour" and asks for advice — the only time in the series he's shown asking anyone for help with a personal decision. Feeding it to a pet grants full sapience and transformation plus an incurable charm that makes the pet fall hopelessly in love with whoever fed it to them. He wants to use it on Ragazzaccia, a goat who was his girlfriend before the dungeon began, whom he still has in a pet carrier:

"So . . ." Prepotente said. "Her name is Ragazzaccia, and before the dungeon began, she was—"

"Absolutely not," Donut said. "You will not be turning anyone into a sex slave, Prepotente. How is this even a conversation? My goodness."

Donut talks him down entirely on her own authority, walking him through what the biscuit would actually do to Ragazzaccia (make her a level-1 crawler, exposed to real danger, permanently compelled to love him rather than choosing to) rather than simply forbidding it:

"Nobody will like you if you use that pet biscuit on anything. Can you imagine if that's what had happened to me? Do you really think I could be a proper girlfriend for Carl? It's a crime against nature. Don't use it. Ever. Ever, ever, ever."

Prepotente accepts it, and admits the loneliness underneath the request: "I don't have anybody to ask these things. Sometimes I imagine my mother and me having these conversations... but I don't have that." Donut agrees to talk to him daily going forward. This is the same biscuit family later used, deliberately, on Penelope — and, by accident, on Scolopendra herself (see Princess Donut).

docs.title: The Vision of His Mother
docs.text:
During the Heat 6 apartment-building sequence — a floor-wide, unauthorized AI event called "Ad Infinitum," in which the unstable system AI generates "what-if" simulations of crawlers' loved ones — Prepotente freezes inside an apartment showing his mother, Miriam Dom, as a professional concert pianist who never stayed home to raise him:

"This is my mother if she had never stayed to take care of her parents," Prepotente said... "She would've become a professional concert pianist. She wouldn't ever have known me... She would've had everything she had ever dreamed of."

He reads the vision as proof he doesn't belong anywhere — "Nobody wants me around... I don't fit in anywhere... I wish I'd never taken the pet biscuit" — and comes close to giving up entirely. Carl, not Donut, is the one who talks him back from it in person, arguing that the vision is a toxic hypothetical and that the real Miriam had him, not loneliness:

"This what-if bullshit is insidious. It's like a goddamned toxic virus on your brain... Look, buddy. We don't have time. I'm sorry if we didn't get to see you sing. But you are always welcome with us... you and I and Donut and everyone else, we are a herd, and—"

Prepotente tackles him into a hug and sobs, then tells him afterward: "You can call me Pony if you like."

docs.title: The Cost of the Rescue
docs.text: Getting to Prepotente in time costs Carl minutes he doesn't have — and those minutes are why he detonates a bomb, planned days in advance, that kills Jasha and Radoslav of Team Free Love outright. Prepotente never learns, on the page, that his rescue was the reason.

docs.title: The Song He Never Got to Sing
docs.text:
At the Floor 11 finale's parade, Prepotente is supposed to deliver a scripted vengeance line about the downtrodden rising up. Instead, riding the tapir Sweety, he abandons the script and sings — "In the Air Tonight" by Phil Collins, the same song he never got to perform back at the Heat 5 bar before the fight there interrupted him — accompanied by nothing but Sweety stamping out the beat:

Not only was he singing it, but he was singing it well. I was absolutely floored. It was strong, it was steady, and it was goddamned beautiful.

Even Elle is stunned: "Holy shit, guys. How does that voice come out of him?"

docs.title: The Stolen Crystal
docs.text:
Prepotente's Memorial Crystal: Apito — his standing personal quest object since Book 5, and the same crystal Carl's own Emberus quest is tangled up in — protects everyone riding with him from Scolopendra's attacks for most of the Floor 11 finale, charging as the fight goes on. In the chaos of the boss fight's end it's pulled from around his neck:

Prepotente: I will recover. Tend to Jurgen. I was electrocuted, but I am now fine. The deity stole my memorial crystal! The thief pulled it right off my neck! I have filed a formal complaint with the Epicure!

Which deity — a correction

Prepotente never names the thief on the page, and Carl's own follow-up guess points not at Eris but at the god who is confirmed to leave the realm carrying off both Krakaren Prime and Samantha at the same moment — implied, though not stated outright, to be Taranis: "I think Krakaren has something to do with Apito. So does Samantha. And he took the memorial crystal because it contains all her memories and spells." Treat the identity of the thief as unconfirmed rather than settled either way.

He is left, by the book's end, both without his crystal and without the protection it provided — and Carl's only promise is "I'll see what we can do."

Sourced from Book 2: Carl's Doomsday Scenario, Book 3: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook, Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade, Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride, Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin, and Book 8: A Parade of Horribles.

docs.title: Princess D'Nadia
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: NPC royalty / broadcast panelist, later a Carl and Donut sponsor
  • Race: Saccathian ("Sac") — tentacle-faced
  • Title: Princess of the Prism Kingdom (Book 2–4) → Empress D'Nadia (Book 5, after her father's retirement) → Warlord Empress D'Nadia of the Prism, holding Spot 5 on Floor 9 (Book 7)
  • Class / Subclass: Not stated anywhere — she is an NPC head of state and is never statted out as a crawler, even as a Faction Wars warlord
  • Status: Deceased — killed in her own throne room in Larracos at the end of chapter 26 of Book 7; the system credits the kill to Mongo, Donut's pet, on Donut's order
  • Notable spells/abilities: None described through Book 5 — a diplomat/broadcast figure, not a combatant. Book 7: Donut's pre-raid briefing lists "A BUNCH OF ICE AND WATER SPELLS" plus a crown carrying water spells, but she casts none of them on-page
  • Notable items: None described through Book 5. Book 7: three separate tech shields built into the fabric of her gown, a teleport-to-safety ring (useless inside Faction Wars), a magical crossbow, a small concealed pulse gun, and a knife she uses on herself to stay injured and so block Carl's Ring of Divine Suffering

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Princess D'Nadia is a recurring, friendly saccathian panelist on the talk-show circuit since Book 2, gifting Donut the Prism Industries goggles that expose Hekla's plot in Book 3. Her father's retirement makes her Empress of the Prism Kingdom by Book 5.

docs.title: Role in the Story — Book 5
docs.text: D'Nadia serves as one of three celebrity judges for the Butcher's Masquerade's pet show and talent competition, alongside an unnamed, tall, thin soother and an unnamed jello-mold blob alien — not the gleener and camel-alien pair (Hurk and G'valt) who separately judge Carl's earlier CrawlCon art contest; the two judging panels are distinct. She reveals she's become one of Donut's sponsors — via a corporate buy-in bid Carl's new legal entity nearly derailed without meaning to — and needles Signet during the party, dismissively telling her that Signet's dead mother and fallen tattoo-warriors were "never real," a comment that directly motivates Signet's decision to sacrifice herself and prove otherwise by resummoning them all one final time. She survives the ensuing battle, having been present only as a remote broadcast avatar throughout.

docs.title: Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin
docs.text: The Faction Wars seat she spent Books 2 through 5 buying is the thing that kills her. D'Nadia enters Floor 9 as Warlord Empress of the Prism, holding Spot 5 — the territory directly south of the Naga Blood Sultanate and adjacent to the Princess Posse's southern front. She is the second faction leader eliminated in the war, and the first killed by Carl and Donut personally.

docs.title: Before the Assault
docs.text:
The Prism signs the opening ceasefire along with everyone else. D'Nadia's position deteriorates from there. Her broadcast-era relationship with Donut has already curdled: she has sold Donut's sponsorship on, and Donut is "still mad at Empress D'Nadia for trying to get us deleted," to the point that Carl has to stop her sending a message into the Prism chat about "her betrayal."

Her people fight dirty and badly. A Prism scout — not a mercenary, but "a Saccathian prince of some kind, one of D'Nadia's actual relatives" — infiltrates the Princess Posse's southern trenches and unleashes an Instant River scroll that drowns soldiers in an escape tunnel; he is blown apart by a landmine while fleeing. Almost the entire enemy first trench line on that front turns out to be flying Prism banners, which Carl reads correctly as her committing nearly everything she has between his army and her headquarters. After the trench battle, most of it is dead.

docs.title: The Throne Room
docs.text:
In chapter 26 Carl walks into the Prism headquarters — a castle Carl later notes was a fraction of the size of his own — announcing himself: "Oh, Empress. You have visitors." He puts the Ring of Divine Suffering on his finger before he goes in.

Her guards are already dead or unconscious. She fights alone, and briefly: a crossbow bolt off Carl's shield, a concealed pulse shot at Donut that goes wide. Carl works her over with banger spheres while Donut casts Clockwork Triplicate on Mongo and sets the two duplicates on her to strip her three layered tech shields, her gown, and the knife she has been using to keep herself at less than full health — because the Ring of Divine Suffering can only mark a target at 100%. Carl heals her with a scroll and marks her anyway.

You have successfully marked Warlord Empress D'Nadia of the Prism. Her highest stat is Intelligence.

What follows is less an interrogation than a sentencing. Carl brings up Tsarina Signet, and the thing D'Nadia said to her at the Butcher's Masquerade:

"You told her that she wasn't real. That her family wasn't real."

"I'm sorry none of the golems are here right now. That's just how it works out sometimes. But that's okay. I think, in the end, she considered me as part of her family as well."

She pleads her old friendship and her old sponsorship — "Donut, I was your sponsor. I got you your glasses. Don't you like your glasses?" — and then her motive: "I did it for my people." Carl: "No, D'Nadia. You did it for you. And now your people are going to suffer because of it."

docs.title: Carl at the Edge
docs.text:
This is the scene where the Ring of Divine Suffering nearly takes Carl. He remembers meeting her on Ripper Wonton's show, when she held his hand and cried over Manassa's assassination, and thinking "perhaps she was one of the good ones" — before learning she had been trying for years to buy her way into the dungeon to hunt people like him.

The anger that washed over me was so brilliantly white, all three of my eyes burned. I'd never felt anything like this. Not with Maggie My. Not with Quan Ch.

Not as I sat there, in that gas station with the button that would end it all.

I hated her.

It is Donut who stops him:

Carl: Donut, I changed my mind. I want to do it. Step aside.

Donut: No, Carl. Please, no. I need you to step back. I need you to calm down right now. I got this. It's okay.

And there it was.

The edge.

I saw it, clear as can be. Right there. I stood upon it, one foot stretched out over open air.

You can do that, sometimes. You can find clarity when you need it most.

I took a step back.

Minutes later, with ten captured gnoll mercenaries standing in front of him and the ring telling him he could mark all of them at once, Carl pulls the ring off his finger in front of the whole room. Donut asks him to throw it away — "It's doing something to you. You're scaring me." Carl recognises the words as ones his mother used to say to his father, and still refuses: "Not yet. I need it for just a little longer." See Carl.

docs.title: The Kill and What It Cost the Galaxy
docs.text:
Donut takes the kill, and takes it on Mongo's behalf, closing out the Book 6 pet-show grudge:

"Empress, Darling," Donut said. "Mongo would like to express his utmost disappointment at how you judged him during the pet show."

System Message: Warlord D'Nadia of the Prism has fallen. Credit for the kill has been given to pet Mongo of the Princess Posse.

System Message: The Prism has been defeated.

System Message: All assets of the Prism have been awarded to the Princess Posse.

Donut loots the body and then takes the corpse itself. The system AI's achievement — Gavrilo Princip — treats her death as the only politically consequential one of the day:

Empress D'Nadia is a whole different cookie, my friends. You just killed—and, by the way, bankrupted—the last living heir of a small but powerful trading dynasty. The Syndicate probate courts are already girding themselves for the endless court battles that are about to ensue. Even if this is the only system leader you manage to slaughter during the next few weeks, you have made an impact, my boy. A big one.

The reward is a Legendary 1914 box — the box that later produces Donut's War Crime spell and Carl's Run, Little Günter, Run.

Carl's own reaction is not triumph. "All the anger I'd just been feeling was gone, drained out of me like all my rage had been ejected out of an airlock... An unexpected sense of mourning hit me, all at once, and it was confusing and strange and completely bewildering." He later reflects, "I'd seen my father in myself at that moment."

Her castle cannot be held, since it does not adjoin Posse land. Carl leaves a lone Madness mercenary sitting in it deliberately, to make the surviving warlords fight over the scrap; it changes hands three times and eventually goes to the Dream.

Sourced from Book 2: Carl's Doomsday Scenario, Book 3: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook, Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade, and Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Princess Donut
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Full title: GC, BWR, NW Princess Donut the Queen Anne Chonk (self-insists on "Princess Donut," or "Princess" in polite company)
  • Crawler title (Book 1): Grand Champion Best in Dungeon
  • Type: Cat Crawler
  • Race: Cat (tortoiseshell/Persian mix)
  • Class: Not yet assigned (Book 1) → Former Child Actor (Book 2) — a rare Earth Class requiring the "Cut!" achievement and 1 trillion+ views — plus, from Book 7, a second permanent class, The Oak Fell, awarded for casting three Atrocity-tier spells on one floor and stacked on top of Former Child Actor rather than replacing it; Mordecai and Rosetta have never seen a class granted that way
  • Subclass: Not applicable — instead has the Character Actor skill, letting her re-pick a temporary "floor specialty" class each floor (picked Artist Alley Mogul on Floor 3; a Hooligan specialty on Floor 4; Glass Cannon on Floor 5; Legendary Diva — a Bard floor-specialty — on Floor 6, unlocking a whole singing-based spell kit; Master Telephone Psychic — a psionic specialty — on Floor 8, granting greatly improved mapping, +5 Intelligence, and three charm/debuff spells; Deathbed Hellcat — a long-range sniper/assassin specialty — on Floor 9, quadrupling the range of every spell she has, raising her Dexterity and instakill odds, granting invisibility at will, and coming with a ghillie suit and boonie hat)
  • Title (Book 7): Champion of Nekhebit — awarded alongside The Oak Fell by the goddess Nekhebit, currently driven by Odette. She need not worship Nekhebit but may worship no deity outside her court, enemies of Nekhebit collect a bounty for killing her, and per Rosetta it is "not too unlike Conscription, but with a lot more autonomy" — the goddess can order her to act or smite her
  • Level: 26 (end of Book 2) → 33 (end of Book 3) → 39 (end of Book 4) → 55 (end of Book 5) → 63 (end of Book 6) → 135 (Book 7, last level stated in the text) — enters Book 6 ranked #2, having just lost the top spot to Prepotente. In Book 7 she is level 65 entering the Nest tower, 74 after hours of sniping, and jumps to 135 the moment her third Atrocity lands, making her the highest-levelled crawler in the dungeon and, per Mordecai, "the most powerful crawler in the history of this game"
  • Stats (Book 7): base Charisma over 200 (well over 300 with gear, though not at base); base Intelligence and Strength both over 100. Natural benefits taken: Brain Trust (Intelligence), Muscle Mommy (Strength — also adds 25% of her Strength to Mongo's), Wholesale Discount (Charisma), and Monologue, a fear-based charisma skill that pays experience in proportion to how terrified the enemy is, received when her boosted stats topped 300
  • Party: The Royal Court of Princess Donut (party leader — highest combined stats) — briefly designated Squad Leader as Floor 7 begins; loses the leader slot to Carl in Book 7 ch. 27 and reclaims it in ch. 77
  • Buff: Enhanced Growth — gains +1 Strength, +1 Intelligence, +2 Charisma automatically every level, with no free stat points to distribute; Charisma passes 100 during Book 3, and reaches base 138 (temporarily doubled to 276+ by a benefactor tiara) by Book 5
  • Faction Wars: Co-Warlord (with Carl) of The Princess Posse, sponsored by The Society for the Eradication of Cocker Spaniels — the fan-funded advocacy group Donut has been quietly building since Book 4 buys a Floor 9 Faction Wars seat at the end of Book 5. The Princess Posse wins Faction Wars at the end of Book 7
  • Succession status: Formerly enrolled in the Blood Sultanate's line of succession via the (now-destroyed) Crown of the Sepsis Whore — Book 5 confirms losing the physical crown never lifted the obligation; the crown itself resurfaces and is forced onto Katia's head at the very end of the book
  • Notable spells/abilities: Magic Missile, Fireball (Book 5, item-granted), Torch (Book 5: reaches level 14+, strong enough to ignite vampires), Second Chance, Puddle Jumper, Heal Critter, Clockwork Triplicate, Minion Army (uncastable), Hole (Book 5: used to decapitate the Rottweiler Cici; also cast through the ceiling connecting the attendant ballroom to the main hunters' stage during Mongo's pet-show number, letting extra "girlfriend" raptors briefly appear on stage from the room below — confirmed by Donut's own after-the-fact explanation to Tserendolgor), Wall of Fire, Twinkle Toes, Standing Ovation, Entourage, All Eyes on Me (all Book 5, Legendary Diva songs), Laundry Day (Book 5, a separate floor-spellbook gift, not part of the Diva kit), Slice Attack/Back Claw (melee), Night Vision, Cat-like Reflexes, 9 Lives (cat racial benefits), Love Vampire (Book 5: finally works at scale, charming multiple enemy elves at once during the final battle), Deflection, Brain Freeze, Bad Attitude and Why Are You Hitting Yourself? (all Book 6, Master Telephone Psychic), Legionnaires of the Damned and Mute (Book 6, tomes), Bitch, What? (Book 6, item-granted berserking spell), and a level-10 Hover skill (Book 6, tiara-granted); Book 7 adds the three Atrocity-tier spells Rolling Battle Formation, You're Not Done Yet and War Crime (the last castable only three times, ever, and only on Scolopendra levels), plus Flak, Shield and Sentry from floor and quest boxes, Bijanbi (tattoo-granted, from the god Wepwawet), Astral Paw, the druidic Oak Fell deity spells Raise Forest, Gather Ye, Vermin and a water-to-salt-water spell, and a Claw racial skill trained from level 4 toward 15 by her champion shawl — note: the Wisp Armor tome, once considered for her, ends up read and cast by Carl instead
  • Notable items: a Belt of Buoyancy; a cat-sized ghillie suit and boonie hat (Book 7, Deathbed Hellcat kit — Blend into the Background, Cone of Silence, Targeting); celestial knee pads passed on by Katia (Book 7, a 500% Eileithyia damage bonus against enemies); Enchanted Anklet of the Fallen Oak; Enchanted Collar Charm of the Effete Bourgeoisie (Book 5, tracks conquered settlements, matching Carl's necklace); ~~Enchanted Crown of the Sepsis Whore~~ (destroyed in Book 2, obligation persists); Enchanted Fae Scale Quadruped Crupper of the Fleet; Enchanted Fur Brush of the Ecclesiastic; Enchanted Mongoliensis Saddle; Enchanted Nipple Ring of the Superior Fire Demon's Hand Maiden (Book 6, fire immunity and Bitch, What?); Enchanted Obsidian Bracelet of the Raggle Rouser (Book 5, grants Fireball); Enchanted Silver Bracelet of the Ab-solar (Book 5, anti-vampirism); Enchanted Tiara of Mana Genita; Enchanted Tiara of the Inebriated Dragonfly (Book 6, grants Hover); her champion shawl (Book 7, trains Claw); Prism Industries Capacitating and Focusing Goggles; a Quadruped weapon mount — "The scorpion's bite" (Book 7, a non-magical bandolier from the Apothecary, used to fire Katia's crossbow off her own back); ~~Talisman of the Slate Butterfly~~ (Book 5: retired, replaced as her collar-charm slot by the leadership charm below); The Tiara of a Thousand Lights and Accompanying Charge Pillow (Book 7, unique — 99 absorption jewels that permanently drain any enchanted hat's buffs into the tiara; +10 Charisma on its own)
  • Sponsors: Princess D'Nadia (Books 2–6, until she sells the contract mid-Book 6) → Long Haul Biological Waste Management Solutions (Book 6 — revealed in the epilogue to be a front for the freighter Homecoming Queen)

docs.title: Background
docs.text: Before the collapse, Donut was a champion show cat owned by Carl's ex-girlfriend Beatrice, with a room in their apartment devoted to her competition trophies and ribbons. She was with Carl (not Beatrice) when the dungeon opened because Beatrice was traveling and Carl had been asked to cat-sit. Donut initially enters the dungeon classified as a pet, not a full crawler — a status that changes when Carl force-feeds her an Enhanced Pet Biscuit from a Legendary Pet Box.

docs.title: The Transformation
docs.text:
The enhanced biscuit dissolves Donut into a puddle of goo for several minutes before she reforms — physically almost unchanged, but now able to speak and reason at a human level. Her stats before the transformation were all 1 (except Dexterity at 8, Charisma at 5); the biscuit boosted four random stats and applied the permanent Enhanced Growth buff. Post-transformation stats climb fast — by the tuskling "Ball of Swine" fight she's already at Strength 18, Intelligence in the 20s, and a Charisma so high (37–43 through most of Book 1) that she can casually charm sapient mobs (goblins, fairies) into compliance, provided their aggro is already neutral.

Once she can speak, Donut immediately renames the party The Royal Court of Princess Donut, appoints herself Grand Champion Best in Dungeon, and demotes Carl from "manservant" to Royal Bodyguard.

docs.title: Personality
docs.text:
Vain, status-obsessed, and initially dismissive of Carl, Donut nonetheless refuses to abandon him when he tries to split up early on, admitting she doesn't want to be alone and that she'd noticed him quietly looking at apartments that allowed cats (i.e., planning to keep her) before the world ended. Over Book 1 she becomes a genuinely loyal partner — dragging Carl to safety twice after near-fatal injuries — while never losing the diva affect, especially once cameras get involved.

She develops a visible addiction to audience attention after her first talk-show appearance (on Dungeon Crawler After Hours with Odette), obsessively tracking her Views/Followers/Favorites counts, to the point Carl has to repeatedly talk her down from playing for the camera during actual combat.

docs.title: Combat Role
docs.text:
Donut is the party's ranged/magic damage dealer, though she's reluctant to use her claws (calling melee "inelegant") until circumstances force her to (see Quick Facts above for her spell/ability list). Her physical stats eventually let her one-shot low-level mobs with her claws, but her Constitution stays crippingly low (as low as 2, raised to 4 with gear) because Enhanced Growth never lets her allocate points there — making her fast and hard-hitting but fragile.

The Crown of the Sepsis Whore (see Quick Facts) is worth calling out specifically: a Legendary, cursed tiara she puts on without reading the full warning. It's a Fleeting + Unique item that permanently enrolls her in the royal line of succession for the Blood Sultanate on Floor 9, meaning she (and by extension Carl) will eventually be required to kill the Sultan and the entire royal family to descend past that floor.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Carl — bodyguard, "manservant," and, increasingly, genuine found family
  • Mordecai — mutual affection; he's forbidden from telling her much but clearly likes her
  • Zev — the pair bond quickly over shared taste in Earth television (Gossip Girl, Riverdale)
  • Mongo — adopts a baby Mongoliensis (a velociraptor, per Odette) from a Floor 2 pet reward room and spends the rest of the book getting bitten on the nose while training him
  • "Ferdinand" — repeatedly mentioned by Donut as someone she loves, described dramatically as a forbidden lover; revealed live on air in Book 2 to actually be Gravy Boat, a neighborhood tomcat belonging to a woman named Marjory back on Earth
  • Katia — a new party member recruited in Book 2 (see Katia)

docs.title: Book 2: Race and Class
docs.text:
On Floor 3, Donut refuses every race option and stays Cat — but confirming the choice (rather than leaving it a non-choice) unlocks new racial benefits: Night Vision, Slash Attack, Cat-like Reflexes, and 9 Lives (halves damage from her first nine physical hits per day).

For class, she's shown only 34 options (the fewest Mordecai has ever seen, due to her Desperado Pass and her Crown) and picks Former Child Actor — a rare Charisma/Chance Earth Class built around the Character Actor skill: each floor, she re-rolls a temporary "specialty" class for that floor only, with the AI randomly determining how many of that specialty's skills/spells she actually receives. Her hidden Manager benefit (see Carl for how it was obtained) makes Mordecai personally accompany the party instead of being guildhall-bound.

docs.title: Book 2 Notable Events
docs.text:
• Kidnapped and placed under a magical sleep (Water Lily) by the Elite Tsarina Signet as leverage to force Carl into a fight
  • Learns Clockwork Triplicate, a spell that creates two temporary clockwork duplicates of a bonded pet/minion
  • Insists on pursuing NPC GumGum's "Sex Workers" quest after GumGum is killed, reasoning "she died because of us" — pushes Carl to keep going with the investigation multiple times when he's ready to drop it
  • Loses the Crown of the Sepsis Whore — forced to remove it during the Doomsday Scenario wild-magic event to avoid a worse stat penalty; being Fleeting, it disintegrates the instant it comes off (the succession curse it created remains regardless, per that item's own page)
  • Appears alongside Carl and Hekla on Danger Zone with Ripper Wonton; publicly reveals, live on air, that her long-mentioned love "Ferdinand" was actually a neighborhood tomcat named Gravy Boat
  • Welcomes Katia into the party as a new permanent member, insisting on protecting her during the Doomsday Scenario's evacuation even at cost to their own safety
  • Ends Floor 3 ranked 7th on the leaderboard (Level 26), just behind Carl

docs.title: Book 3 Notable Events
docs.text:
• Receives the Prism Industries Capacitating and Focusing Goggles from Princess D'Nadia — their hidden vision mode lets her spot the two invisible "Dirty Little Phased Bolts" Hekla fires at Katia, exposing the plot that gets Hekla killed
  • Reaches 100 Charisma and unlocks Love Vampire, a passive that reflects damage back onto lower-level attackers; kept carefully unused for most of the floor since the party avoids letting her get hit
  • Casts Second Chance on Hekla's corpse mid-battle, then Clockwork Triplicates the reanimated result into three bodies to hold off the rest of Brynhild's Daughters while Carl and Katia loot the remains — reuses the same combo later on exploded Krakaren clone corpses
  • Picks up a Hooligan floor specialty via Character Actor, gaining minor Guinness and Mascot skills for the duration of Floor 4
  • Champions collecting and freely redistributing roughly 700 escape-portal "train hats" to stranded crawlers rather than selling them, over her own vocal objections about the lost gold — ends up gifted dozens back in gratitude by the survivors she helped
  • Publicly reveals, on Odette's show, that she was present for — and inadvertently starred in — a new viral "snick" mocking the resurrected Maestro, continuing Carl's Book 1 humiliation arc
  • Grows close to Katia as a full-time party member, repeatedly insisting on protecting her (and covering for her) through the trauma of killing Hekla
  • Ends Floor 4 at Level 33, having spun the wheel that sends the party into the Air Quadrant of Floor 5, against the Dirigible Gnome Wasteland Fortress

docs.title: Book 4 Notable Events
docs.text:
• Picks Glass Cannon as her Floor 5 specialty on Mordecai's advice — the buff proves genuine, visibly strengthening every spell she casts for the floor, though she never receives the specialty's usual Constitution bonus
  • Cast as the "healer" in Carl's gnome-hostage con, using a fake-corpse Second Chance resurrection of a dead dirigible gnome to bluff a Wasteland ambassador into ferrying the party aboard his balloon
  • Becomes the unwilling face of Veriluxx RealPet Companions, a sponsor selling a cheap, repeatedly-exploding "Princess Donut the Queen Anne Chonk" toy alongside a bootlegged Garfield personality; goes on the toy's infomercial anyway, where Carl's needling about the sponsor's slavery-linked parent company (Veritan Linkage) triggers the toy's rigged detonation and kills admin Loita
  • Loses her PR contact Zev for a second time when Loita takes over, then celebrates her return after Loita's death; develops a visible, Carl-noted addiction to her newly-purchased social media board
  • Portals Chris Andrews to safety rather than let Carl mercy-kill him while possessed, overriding Carl's judgment in the moment ("You're not a killer, Carl")
  • Casts Meat Hooks to lure the celestial-tier puppy Orthrus out of bubble 543 and to safety, then helps heal him mid-air-battle against Quan Ch and the god Emberus
  • Ends the book newly obsessed with hiring "staff" for the personal space, having personally championed keeping the possessed doll head Samantha as a hired trainer

docs.title: Book 5 Notable Events
docs.text:
• Picks Legendary Diva (Bard) as her Floor 6 specialty, gaining a starting kit of five songs — the party-support Standing Ovation, Entourage, and Encore (a heal-party/cleanse spell), plus two offensive numbers she never gets much use out of — and separately picks up Laundry Day as a bonus regular spell from her floor's spellbook club (not part of the Diva kit itself). She's blocked from casting any bard song reliably until she trains her singing enough to hold pitch "in key," a running joke and a real mechanical bottleneck for most of the floor. All Eyes on Me is the name given to one of her Diva songs only when she finally performs it at the Masquerade
  • Tames the pack-leader velociraptor Kiwi using a sponsor-supplied Charm Mongoliensis potion brewed from a full liter of Mongo's own blood, gaining Kiwi's entire raptor pack as loyal (if unpredictable) minions for the back half of the floor, and later magically charms Queen Imogen's cat familiar Ferdinand into betraying his mistress at the Butcher's Masquerade using a second charm potion that the group's planning notes say requires "a liter of cat blood" — with Donut, as the only cat on hand, the implied "ready source" (she jokingly balks at being drained a second time, "I don't have a liter of blood in me. I am very petite," and the book never shows the actual collection on-page, so treat the exact blood source as strongly implied rather than explicitly confirmed)
  • Wins Point Mongo's conquest outright by pushing its bear mayor into a naiad-infested river, then renames and redecorates the town over Carl's objections; separately conquers a second and third settlement (Ferdinand Peak, Nipton)
  • Fights and nearly loses to child crawler Lucia Mar solo while Carl is pulled away to a mandatory intergalactic fan convention — decapitates Cici, one of Lucia's two rottweilers, using Hole, and out-maneuvers Lucia with an Entourage illusion stack before escaping (her Cockroach passive doesn't trigger here; it does trigger twice later in the book — once when she throws herself in front of a lightning bolt meant for Mongo during a roadside encounter with Queen Imogen's familiar Ferdinand, and again during the Butcher's Masquerade's final battle when a mass debuff wave zeroes out her health)
  • Publicly, coldly rejects her original owner Beatrice, who reappears alive on Odette's talk show — delivering the emotional gut-punch of the book ("You're not my person anymore. Carl is. He's always been.") before privately admitting to Carl she isn't sure why she doesn't feel the grief she expects to over the friends they lose at the Butcher's Masquerade
  • Headlines the Masquerade's talent competition, singing her mother's (Beatrice's) old drunken lullaby, "All Eyes on Me," to unknowingly charm the entire ballroom — including Queen Imogen — moments before Signet breaks the peace seal
  • Cures Kiwi of Scolopendra's centuries-old Transmutation curse using a sponsor-gifted "I Take It All Back" potion mid-battle (a Prepotente benefactor-box item passed to Donut), turning the velociraptor back into her original Ursine form on the spot; Kiwi was never a vampire — the floor's vampirism plague had already been cured earlier when Miriam Dom died
  • Ends the book as Co-Warlord of the Princess Posse in Floor 9's Faction Wars, alongside Carl

docs.title: Book 6 Notable Events
docs.text: Floor 8 is Donut's most competent book. She starts it at level 56/57 and ends it at 63, and she spends the whole of it as squad leader — which on this floor means deckmaster, the only person who can hold, draw, play or flee with T'Ghee cards. Carl is legally a minion for the duration of every card battle.

docs.title: New class: Master Telephone Psychic
docs.text:
Her Character Actor floor specialty. Mordecai offers her a choice between Agony Urchin (safer) and Master Telephone Psychic (better mapping, offensive charm spells); she refuses the Urchin on sight because it would change how she looks — "I HAVE AN IMPORTANT IMAGE TO MAINTAIN."

What the psionic kit gives her:

  • Enormously improved mapping — "IT'S ALMOST LIKE WE ALREADY HAVE THE MAP FROM A NEIGHBORHOOD BOSS… IT'S EVEN BETTER THAN THAT PATHFINDER SKILL"
  • +5 Intelligence
  • Brain Freeze — single-target, drains health and lowers resistances, and blinds at level 10 or above. It starts at level 8.
  • Bad Attitude — per Mordecai, "similar to Carl's Fear spell, but it'll be a lot more potent in your hands… Fear tends to affect dexterity while Bad Attitude drains intelligence and lowers resistances"
  • Why Are You Hitting Yourself? — "IT MAKES PEOPLE STAB THEMSELVES IN THE FACE!" She eventually lands it on a level-250 demon prince: I CAST WHY ARE YOU HITTING YOURSELF ON SATAN!

The class grants no fire spells — her fire magic (Fireball, Magic Missile, Wall of Fire) is all gear-granted and is separately amplified by her new nipple ring. She also keeps her Viper Queen venom spit (level 3) and her Bard songs, minus a couple she's forgotten.

No system text

Master Telephone Psychic has no printed class-description block, and none of the three spells has a printed spell block. Everything known about them comes from dialogue.

docs.title: Deckmaster
docs.text:
Donut builds an eighteen-card deck off crowdsourced chat math (roughly an 80% chance of pulling a totem in the opening spread) and learns to run it well. Her final active deck is six totems — Shi Maria, Jola the Yule Cat (a gift from Katia), Lazarus A-Bang-Bang, Skylar Spinach, Geraldo the monk seal and Raul the crab — plus utility, snare and mystic cards.

The real skill turns out to be personnel management: refereeing Raul against Geraldo, shouting the orisha Asojano into line, coaching Raul out of grovelling, and negotiating with Shi Maria, who demands to see her hand and offers tactical advice. Carl deliberately stays out of it — "I was trying not to be a backseat deckmaster. When the real fights started, I wouldn't be able to sit there and help her."

Her best plays include stealing a summon out of an enemy deckmaster's hand mid-cast with a Thief card, and permanently fusing Lazarus with Skylar Spinach using a Golden Combo followed by the Glow-Up consumable Tserendolgor gave them — building the best possible single card, since only one may be carried down to Floor 9.

She does not enjoy it. "I don't like being in charge of the deck. You're usually in charge of the important stuff."

docs.title: The Golden Skull
docs.text:
Carl brings Quan Ch down, but Quan dies a beat before the finishing blow lands and the system credits the kill — plus the bounty and both exit keys — to Donut. She gets her first golden player-killer skull for it.

Donut sported a new, golden player killer skull. She hadn't commented on it, and neither did I. That felt important, the nonchalance of it all. We were losing more of ourselves every day.

docs.title: Losing D'Nadia, Gaining the Garbage Truck People
docs.text:
Mid-card-battle, Donut gets a notification that Empress D'Nadia — now warlord of the Prism Kingdom Clan, and therefore an opposing Faction Wars faction — has sold her sponsorship contract to someone else.

"I'm not a trading card to be collected and discarded, Carl." … "Carl, I thought she liked me."

Carl's read is that it was partly conflict of interest and mostly money: "Selling Donut's sponsorship had to have made her a lot of money. I'd actually been expecting this for a while now." D'Nadia subsequently files emergency action items to delete the Princess Posse from Faction Wars, and to delete Carl and Donut.

The replacement sponsor is Long Haul Biological Waste Management Solutions.

MY NEW SPONSOR IS NAMED LONG HAUL BIOLOGICAL WASTE MANAGEMENT SOLUTIONS, AND I JUST CAN'T WITH THAT. I KNOW I'M SUPPOSED TO APPEAR GRATEFUL, BUT THAT SOUNDS ABSOLUTELY DISGUSTING. CARL, ARE THEY GOING TO SHOW COMMERCIALS FOR GARBAGE TRUCKS ON MY FEED? THIS IS NOT ACCEPTABLE.

Long Haul are the galaxy's corpse-disposal contractors — they normally don't arrive until after the last crawler has died. The epilogue reveals what the sponsorship actually is: their freighter Homecoming Queen, parked in Earth orbit, is crewed by Rosetta Thagra and Tipid and loaded with fifty thousand former crawlers who have just been cleared to enter the dungeon as troopers for the Princess Posse.

In the last minute before the floor collapses, she gets her first celestial box from them. It is still unopened when the book ends.

"It's a celestial box! My first celestial box, and it's from the garbage truck company? The posse is going to be scandalized."

docs.title: Ripping Shi Maria's Card
docs.text:
After Shi Maria hijacks Carl's body, burns Mongo's wing off and tattoos herself into Carl's chest, Donut ends the argument the moment the battle does:

"I ripped her card," Donut said after a moment. "Shi Maria. As soon as the battle ended, I ripped it. She's not going to hurt Mongo ever again."

It doesn't work the way she hoped. The escort quest to deliver Shi Maria to Larracos survives the rip, and so does Shi Maria — in Carl. Donut also holds, and at Carl's insistence rips, Paz Lo's card. She does not get a skull for that one.

docs.title: Other Book 6 Notes
docs.text:
• She picks Cuba as their Floor 8 region, against advice, on the grounds that it's near the Bahamas and Miss Beatrice. The entire floor follows from that choice.
  • New tiara: the Enchanted Tiara of the Inebriated Dragonfly — a blank silver tiara plus a 25,000-gold flawless citrine — granting a 50% potion cooldown reduction, +10 Intelligence, poison protection, negation of the inebriation dexterity penalty, and a level-10 Hover skill. "I can fly now. Carl, I can fly! I'm like Wonder Woman!" / "Wonder Woman can't fly." / "She has an invisible jet, Carl. Don't ruin this for me." She never gets to use Hover in a real fight.
  • New nipple ring: the Enchanted Nipple Ring of the Superior Fire Demon's Hand Maiden — cursed-item removal, immunity to natural fire and lava, no health loss inside Sheol, fire spells scaling with Intelligence, and a once-daily berserking spell, Bitch, What?, which Mordecai tells her to only ever cast alone.
  • New spells: Legionnaires of the Damned and Mute, in addition to the psychic kit.
  • Mongo reaches level 40, is tripled by Clockwork Triplicate in almost every fight, and has his right wing burned off by Carl's body under Shi Maria's control. A potion Carl upgraded will regrow it.
  • She hears Carl's whole childhood for the first time on Shadow Boxer, and the most striking thing she does with it is decide not to push.

docs.title: Book 7 Notable Events
docs.text:
Floor 9 — Faction Wars, fought over the funnel city of Larracos — is Donut's book. She enters it as Co-Warlord of the Princess Posse and the party's ranged damage dealer, and leaves it as the highest-levelled crawler in the dungeon, holding two classes, a goddess's title, and the only spell in the game the system files under Atrocity. It costs her more than any previous floor, and the book is unusually direct about the cost.

Level endpoints

She finished Book 6 at 63. The text's first Book 7 figure is 65, the level at which she climbs into the Nest tower around Chapter 70. Hours of sniping take her to 74 by Chapter 74. Then her third Atrocity, in Chapter 76, jumps her straight to 135 — "Her level had grown to 135." That is the last level stated for her in the book, and Mordecai's read is blunt: "I think you're now the most powerful crawler in the history of this game."

docs.title: New class: Deathbed Hellcat
docs.text:
Her Character Actor floor specialty for Floor 9, picked off-page while Carl is distracted. It turns her from an artillery piece into a sniper:

"Great, isn't it? It's a long-range sniper and assassin class. It doesn't come with many new spells, but the range on all my existing spells is quadrupled, and my dexterity is much higher.
