  • Current form: A decapitated half-naiad sex-doll head, modeled on a fictional character named Lika from the stage play Troubadour's Bounty. By the end of Book 7 she is burned black — "nothing but a scorched, round head" with a single surviving white curl, and after a second trip into a volcano, worse than that
  • Status: Hired staff — trainer in Carl and Donut's personal space, as of Book 4. Alive and still with the party at the end of Book 7; she gives up the promised flesh-golem body to save Louis Santiago and goes down to Floor 10 with the rest of them
  • Type/Class: Withering Spirit — a soul split between two vessels during a botched escape from the Nothing; not fully alive, extremely difficult to kill, effectively powerless outside her vessel

docs.title: What She Is
docs.text:
Psamathe tricked the Mad Dune Mage Ghazi into opening a portal to the Nothing on his behalf (claiming to be Yarilo, the banished god of Lust, whom Ghazi wanted to trade with) as her own escape attempt. The escape went wrong: her essence split in two. One half fled into the necropolis and possessed the ghost of the emperor's wife, Quetzalcoatlus; the other half — unable to find any better vessel in time — took up residence in a sex-doll head modeled after Ghazi's obsession, Lika, moments before Ghazi's own botched containment spell turned the whole castle (doll included) to glass. She spends years frozen and aware, unable to move or speak, while Ghazi unknowingly keeps her within arm's reach.

Mordecai identifies her condition as a withering spirit — a soul-split creature that isn't alive or dead, nearly impossible to kill, but with very little independent power. He compares her (unfavorably, in terms of danger) to Remex, the deliberately-weaponized soul leech capacitor from Floor 4.

docs.title: Recovery and Personality
docs.text: Freed when Mongo accidentally knocks over and shatters her glass-encased doll body, Samantha (named by Carl, since he refuses to use "Psamathe") is foul-mouthed, unfiltered, prone to non-stop declarations that she's "going to kill your mother," and entirely without a body below the neck for most of the book. Despite this, she proves genuinely useful — walking Carl through monster weaknesses she's picked up over her long, strange unlife, and helping Mordecai finally identify a use for a mysterious sponsor-gifted root vegetable ("the yam"), which becomes essential to the Phase Lava Rock potion that frees Chris Andrews.

docs.title: Role in the Story — Book 4
docs.text:
• Refuses Carl's offer to send her back into the Nothing, and instead is hired as a hidden personal-space trainer (on Donut's insistence) so she can be kept both useful and contained
  • Is chased by her aunt/cousin — a feral, banished demon named Slit, hunting for her on another demon's behalf — after being thrown fifty-plus kilometers as a distraction/weapon via a custom xistera attachment; Slit is killed moments later by an unrelated god before she can catch up
  • Reveals that the demon that killed Slit was her own mother — one of several harem-demons who hate her — deepening the sense that Samantha's family history is as dysfunctional and dangerous as the gods and demons hunting Carl's own party
  • Helps talk Chris Andrews's captor, Maggie My, into a final confrontation stance alongside Carl at the book's climax (indirectly, via her earlier knowledge-sharing with Mordecai)

docs.title: Book 5: A God's Cousin
docs.text:
Samantha travels with Carl and Donut through Floor 6 as an expendable, indestructible scout and distraction weapon — thrown, duct-taped to missiles, and used repeatedly to lure or infiltrate hostile positions since a killing blow simply can't land on her. She reveals she's a blood relation (calling herself Signet's "third cousin thrice removed," "by marriage if you're being super technical" — the connection runs through Signet's own great-grandfather, "Tsar Guggenheim," though Carl cuts her off before she can finish explaining exactly how) of the elite Tsarina Signet, and briefly tries to convince Signet to sacrifice her own body so Samantha can finally have a physical form again — Signet deflects with a vague future promise the narration explicitly calls a lie. Well before Signet's death, Donut already notices Samantha is growing stronger and rolling faster than Mordecai's original "withering spirit" assessment predicted, comparing her to the creatures from the movie Critters and worrying about what she's turning into. Her demand for a body is never fulfilled by Signet; after Signet's death, one of Signet's tattoo companions, Miss Nadine, instead hands Carl the inert body of Signet's own late mother — an "Incomplete Flesh Golem" — suggesting Samantha might use it with the help of "a Pulpmancer," but this thread is left hanging at the end of the book.

Samantha's decisive contribution comes at the Butcher's Masquerade: infiltrating the castle's hidden control room through a network of cat-sized tunnels (built, unbeknownst to her, by Queen Imogen's own familiar, Ferdinand), finding the elf guards already dead there — decapitated by mantises sent ahead of Circe Took/Diwata. The room holds two pairs of soul crystals: one pair frees the crawlers' own ballroom from its magic/inventory block when Samantha pulls it, while the other pair (controlling the hunters' ballroom) turns out to have already been pulled by the same mantis infiltrators — so, on Carl's order, Samantha instead pushes that second pair back into place, keeping the hunters locked out of their own magic and gear. When the goddess Diwata (Circe Took, mid-mantis-birth) breaks into the room to retake it, Samantha, unable to hold the room, instead grabs multiple soul crystals in her mouth and bites down on them right next to Diwata, deliberately triggering a massive overload explosion to try to force the goddess to stop giving birth and leave. It works — the blast blows a hole through the floor and ceiling between the two ballrooms and knocks Diwata out cold — though it does not kill her; Circe Took's actual death comes later, on the battlefield, when her own mantis children turn on her once Donut's Laundry Day strips away her divine "armor." After the seal breaks and the "Cage Fight Extreme" battle erupts, Samantha reappears in the crawlers' ballroom (surfing in on a wave of bug gore from above), helps finish off Vrah, and hands off Signet's mother's inert "flesh golem" body to Carl — then, rather than agree to reunite with him on the ninth floor, declares "Fuck that!" and is last seen firing off toward parts unknown, rocketing down through a hole in the floor. Carl tries and fails to summon any further help from her afterward ("We weren't able to coax any sort of spells or buffs out of Samantha. She was gone anyway to god knew where") — her fate at the end of Book 5 is left unresolved.

docs.title: Book 6: Spell Enhancement, Acid, and the Nothing
She Can Enhance Spells After All
docs.text:
Book 5 ended with an unexplained note from Carl's missing sponsor suggesting he use Samantha to boost Donut's Laundry Day. Samantha claimed to have no idea what they were talking about and acted like they were crazy, and they had to burn a Pawna's Tears potion instead. Book 6 confirms the note was right:

As it turned out, Samantha actually did have the power to enhance spells. In fact, she could enhance them quite a bit.

Her own account of it:

"I can help spells. I can make them more powerful. But it doesn't always do what I want. Like, sometimes it's a lot stronger than I thought it would be. And sometimes it doesn't work too good… And sometimes my magic does stuff without me asking."

The proof event is Carl's xistera recall of Sister Ines, amplified by Samantha, which drags back not just the nun but a level-125 sea snake, roughly a thousand zombie baby seals, five thousand zombie crabs, five hundred adult zombie seals and most of the region's fish. She also enhances Donut's Minion Army, and is at least partly responsible for Elle's level-5 Graupel casting at level 16.

docs.title: She Keeps Getting Stronger
docs.text:
She was barely able to roll at the start of the floor, and by the end she is a serious combatant — noticeably heavier, with a faint vibration to her that wasn't there before. Nobody knows why. Carl's hypothesis, formed right after her ex-boyfriend the badger bartender dies:

"I'm starting to think maybe Samantha gets more powerful every time somebody dies… If that's the case, we really need to be careful of her on the next floor. If we let her inhabit the body of Signet's mom, I'm afraid she's going to end up stronger than we can handle."

Unresolved

The death hypothesis is Carl's speculation. Neither the system nor Samantha ever confirms it, and Book 6 offers no other explanation. Carl's earlier worry stands: "Nobody knows why or how you're getting all these new powers, and it kinda freaks me out because we don't know where it's going to stop."

docs.title: The Neck Hole
docs.text:
Samantha's ragged neck hole turns out not to be a hole at all but a deep, pliable, acid-filled storage cavity. It is discovered the hard way, during the Desperado Club disaster, when the bartender Charles ends up shoulder-deep in it — "there was a deepness there that hadn't been present before." (Samantha's explanation: "Oh, him? We're on a date. His arm got stuck. I'm practicing my Kegels.") What comes out of her later has had the flesh burned off it.

Carl immediately weaponises it. Teleport-trap anchors can't be pre-placed by anyone else, so he loads spider automatons carrying anchors into her and has her fly them wherever he needs to jump to. Samantha's offer: "I can take anything you got." Carl's condition: "just make sure you pop them out the moment you land."

In Chapter 69 he uses it on himself. He needs to be under 5% health to trigger his Emberus boon The Martyr's Path — which would set fire to every footprint he's left outdoors, and since his fire is currently Sheol fire, would bathe the demon prince Amayon in it — and he needs to be back at the battle at the same moment. So he teleports into the trap he left inside her.

I landed headfirst inside of Samantha's neck hole.

Head-first, suffocating, wedged, being slammed repeatedly against something, his hair burning off and "the acid literally melting my face off," while Samantha shrieks and tries to push him out and he holds her down onto himself. The timer runs out at 7%, which he thinks is failure; he keeps dropping, hits the button anyway, and the Path fires. He bottoms out at 2% health with a blinking red line of debuffs.

Her verdict afterwards, hovering next to him in the demon's palm:

"Carl, that was the second weirdest sex I ever had. You gotta warn a girl if you're going to just pop in like that." She looked me up and down. "We are going to have to do something about your hair before we announce that we're dating now."

She breaks up with him at the end of the book anyway: "Carl. We need to break up. I've been thinking about it, and I've decided to go back to my king."

docs.title: Sheol and the Nothing
docs.text:
Samantha supplies most of the book's cosmology, in her usual register.

  • The Nothing is a mixing prison, and she was in it: "Before I was banished to the Nothing when I had my original body, I would get more powerful when someone prayed to me or bought a charm with my likeness." Her fellow inmates include a crocodile-headed goddess who "makes sushi rolls out of her own innards. They keep growing back, and she keeps making more and selling it. She has a little stand and everything. She's quite the entrepreneur."
  • Sheol is separate, and its royalty don't get sent to the Nothing: "You know the four crown princes of Sheol? The oldest brother calls himself the King even though his mommy is in charge?… Amayon is that guy's brother. He's the youngest one I think… We all mixed together in the Nothing, but he wasn't in there. He likes to set things on fire. Kinda like Emberus, actually. They don't like each other."
  • On Amayon's escape spell: "He is casting a spell to get home. It's a portal. They try casting it a lot in the Nothing, but it doesn't work there because he needs to suck a lot of souls in for it to work. It'll probably work here, though." And on scale: "he's a big boy and big boys need big doors and lots of souls."
  • She is also personally responsible for the Desperado Club catastrophe: a knife-game loser was pulled into the Nothing, "and when it opened, it tore," letting out Minge, a level-225 minor feral demon and one of a group of sisters who hate Samantha for insulting their king.

docs.title: The Elle Rant
docs.text:
Immediately after Elle's Graupel fires six times stronger than it should, Samantha loses coherence completely — the only time in the book she looks frightened:

"Elle is part earth, part water mage," she said, floating past, talking to herself as she continued to rotate. "She's on the four seasons path. I… but how did that happen? I am stronger too. I didn't do that. It's the tree, I think. Or maybe. It's all there. He's opening a path through the river, the water, and the tree, the earth. It's good she's not fire yet, but maybe the prince's spell enhanced her. No. No. Gotta kill her. No, not Elle. Her mother. No, not her mother." She shook her head like a dog. She turned to look at me. "What just happened? Carl, did you roofie me again?"

Carl asks her directly what she just said and gets "You need to stop gaslighting me, Carl."

Unresolved

"The four seasons path" appears exactly once in the book. Nothing in this rant — the tree, the river, "the prince's spell," the mother — is ever picked up or explained. It rhymes with Carl's own recurring "river" motif, but the text never connects them.

docs.title: Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin
docs.text: Samantha spends most of Floor 9 in the register she has always been in — a foul-mouthed, indestructible nuisance who is also, repeatedly, the only asset that fits the job. Then, in Chapter 83, she says one sentence out loud and destroys the floor.

docs.title: Battlefield Asset and God Bait
docs.text:
Carl’s opening achievement haul includes a Stretching! achievement “for shoving all those traps in Samantha’s neck hole,” which is a fair summary of how she gets used. She is thrown, she is loaded with gear, she scouts, and she is deliberately parked next to danger.

The most deliberate use is as bait at the Gate of the Feral Gods. Both previous feral demons to come out of the Nothing — Slit on the bubble floor and Minge at the Desperado Club — locked onto her instantly, so the plan is to stand her next to the gate and drag the resulting monster across the battlefield “like a kite.” What comes out instead is a god:

Samantha: YOU DON’T HAVE TO TELL ME TWICE. THIS IS A GOD, NOT A DEMON. IT’S YARILO, AND HE DOESN’T LIKE ME! HE’S MAD BECAUSE HE THINKS I HELPED GET HIM TOSSED IN THE NOTHING IN THE FIRST PLACE. IT’S NOT MY FAULT HE’S SEXUALLY ATTRACTED TO ANIMALS. NO OFFENSE, KATIA.

Yarilo is the god she impersonated to trick Ghazi into opening her escape route in the first place, so the hatred is earned. He spends the rest of the sequence bellowing “PSAMATHE! Are you here? We need to talk! Quick! Wait, don’t run!” across the realm.

She also picks a fight of her own. Ghazi’s letters to the Larracos college revealed that his ex-girlfriend Tish still works there, and Samantha breaks out of the guild early in the floor to go kill her — “I went out the door, Carl. I went looking for my child, but then Louis told me he was at the college, and I went to kill her before she could steal him from me like she tried to do to Ghazi.” Donut’s ruling: “Samantha, you shouldn’t hold Tish accountable for what happened. That was 100% Ghazi’s fault.”

Later, alone inside the Reaver castle hunting for the captured Louis, she befriends the castle’s robot guard dogs, names one Buster, removes its “explodey part,” and keeps the resulting nuke. She gets Louis out of the castle blast personally, arriving back at the party as a falling comet:

A flaming, screaming comet fell from the heavens and embedded itself into the ground nearby. Samantha. She was nothing but a scorched, round head. The word “Fuck” remained emblazoned on her forehead. A single, white curl of hair had somehow survived and remained on the top of her head.

She floated upward and shook herself off. She floated up to us standing over Louis.

“I saved him,” she said. “You’re welcome. Now where’s my new doggie?”

She stays burned for the rest of the book — Donut: “Samantha, you look like a piece of popcorn shrimp that has been stuck at the bottom of the oven for two years straight.”

docs.title: The Daughter
docs.text:
Samantha comes onto the floor looking for her child, the sand-ooze daughter she used to trick Ghazi back on the bubble floor, and early on she is certain she has found her: “She’s here! I can feel her, but she’s in the castle of the stinky dwarves! She’s still in the water.” By Chapter 83 she has concluded the child is dead — killed, she believes, in the acid of the flooded Reaver castle, and she blames Tish for it:

“Carl,” she said, sounding serious and morose. “I think my child is dead. I think she died in the acid. I felt her, and now I don’t feel her anymore, and it is my fault. I should have gone to save her sooner, but I did not. I was too caught up in my own lust and anger, and now I have lost my only child. I have failed as a mother.”

Carl, trying to console her, has a thought he never gets to chase down. The war-mage warlord Akuma had just announced that his team’s entire reason for being in the Reaver castle was to retrieve “the Scavenger’s daughter, who was hidden within the castle, and we found her. She is with us now.”

I had a sudden thought. What was it that War Mage had said? They’d found and taken the Scavenger’s Daughter. Could that possibly be Samantha’s daughter? And if so, did that mean Samantha was really the scavenger? I still didn’t know who that was.

Unresolved

The text never answers this. Carl asks Mordecai directly — “who is the Scavenger? And who is the Scavenger’s Daughter? I know it’s the name of my patch, but I didn’t know there was more to it than that” — and Mordecai deflects with “Are you talking about the in-dungeon one or the fairy tale? Either way, that’s a conversation that’s not going to matter if you don’t figure out how to find and kill those two warlords.” The connection between Samantha, the item the Scavenger’s Daughter (see the item page), and whatever Akuma’s team carried out of the castle is raised and then dropped. Nothing confirms Samantha is the Scavenger.

docs.title: Giving Up the Body
docs.text:
With Louis dying — his heart and lungs replaced by the machinery of the possessing warlord Epitome Tagg — Samantha is the one who finds the answer, and the answer costs her everything she has been chasing since Book 5:

Samantha sniffed. “The flesh golem body you have in your inventory. Of Princess Lunette. She has a good heart and lungs. If you swap them out fast enough, you can save Louis.”

Princess Lunette is Signet’s mother, the “Incomplete Flesh Golem” handed to Carl at the end of the Butcher’s Masquerade and earmarked for Samantha ever since. Carl spells out the price — “If we do this, that means you won’t get your body back. At least not for a while” — and she takes it anyway:

She nodded solemnly. “I know. It’s okay. Louis deserves it more than I do.”

Carl’s reply: “That’s... very brave and strong of you. That makes you a hero, Samantha. And I’m very proud of you.” Her answer is the closest the series has come to her explaining herself — “I don’t always mess things up, right? I’d like to think maybe I can be a good influence sometimes and not someone who ruins everything, which is what King Blaine said to me and what my father said to me and what my mother said to me before they all cast me out... I used her, my daughter, to get what I wanted. I ruined everything.”

The transplant works. Louis lives, with naiad gills and a kua-tin rebreather sewn into his bronchial tube. Samantha’s verdict: “We’re cousins now,” followed by kissing him on the lips.

docs.title: “You Did Not Just Fucking Say That Out Loud”
docs.text:
In the same conversation, minutes earlier, she adds a footnote to her own apology. Geyrun is the murdered son of the god Emberus — Carl’s own patron deity, and the subject of Carl’s long-running personal quest Find Out Who Killed My Son:

She nodded. “I may be a neglectful mother. I may have had an indirect, possibly direct hand in the death of Geyrun, but a girl can find forgiveness, right?”

I sighed.

“You did not just fucking say that out loud.”

“What?”

System Message: Emberus has entered the realm.

Chapter 84 opens on a clock:

66 Minutes Until the destruction of the 9th Floor.

And on Carl’s quest updating in the worst possible direction:

Quest Update: Find Out Who Killed My Son.

This so-called Psamathe claims she was part of my son’s death. Capture her for me, and I will personally handle the interrogation. Once I have finished grilling her, I will cleanse this world in fire to remove the stink of this murderer’s presence.

If she is not within my presence in 66 minutes, this world will be destroyed in fire and lava and wrath.

Fly, martyr. Bring my enemy to me.

The system then issues a floor-wide, no-opt-out team quest, This is How the Gristle Grinds:

Here’s the problem. A very angry god that many of you are familiar with has just entered the realm. His name is Emberus. His son, Geyrun, was murdered. It’s a big mystery that probably isn’t going to be solved today, even if any of you bastards do survive this. But a demigod named “Samantha” has just admitted to having taken part in the crime. Emberus, being the loving father he is, has come to the realm to question this demigod. Regardless of what Samantha says to him, Emberus is going to turn the entirety of the 9th floor into a cremation chamber.

This will happen in at least 66 minutes, but your cremation may be delayed slightly if Samantha actually shows up to the interrogation.

Regardless, everything and everybody on this floor is going to die. This is not something that can be stopped.

That is, unless you manage to kill Emberus, which as we all know is possible, but unlikely.

Samantha’s reaction is to be offended: “Wow. I wouldn’t have opened my heart if I’d known you were going to be all dramatic about this.” When Elle suggests “a solid positives and negatives analysis of letting you keep that pet sex doll of yours,” Samantha mutters, “Like you never accidentally triggered an apocalyptic event, Elle.”

Everything that follows — Katia eating the Orchid early and losing her goodbyes, the rushed end of Faction Wars, the evacuation — runs on that 66-minute clock. Carl’s assessment to Katia, who had joked he was about to “Carl it up”: “Yeah, this one is on Samantha.”

In the final minutes he fires her out of the city with the head-thrower xistera attachment, streamers tied round her, to stall the god in person. Her reports from inside Emberus’s hand are in character throughout:

Samantha: HE’S JUST HOLDING ME AND CRYING. YOUR GOD IS A LITTLE BITCH, CARL. MAYBE IT’S GOOD I HELPED KILL OFF HIS BLOODLINE.

Samantha: MAN, THIS GUY DOES NOT HANDLE BAD NEWS VERY WELL.

Carl recalls her at the last moment, “heavy and smoking” and barely recognisable. Her summary: “Okay, that was pretty wild. He was going to eat me, but I had him throw me in a volcano like you said. He’s blowing up the world now, so, yeah we should probably go.”

docs.title: Kimaris
docs.text:
On the stairwell at the very end, Bautista — who received an electronic guidebook to his stuffed animals as a Book 7 achievement reward — finally looks up a plush figure Carl has been carrying: “I looked up the Kimaris figure you have. He’s one of the brothers of Sheol. He has a summoning time of ‘the remainder of the floor.’ Be careful with him.”

Samantha abandons Louis mid-flirt:

“Kimaris!” Samantha asked, zipping away from Louis, who took the opportunity to also dive into the stairwell. “You have Kimmy as a stuffed animal? Give him to me. Give him now!”

Asked who he is to her, she produces the book’s last piece of her own backstory, and hits a hole in her memory doing it:

“He’s one of my best friends. I met him when...” She paused. “Huh,” she said. “That’s weird. Why couldn’t I remember that? He’s... He’s the one who gave me the potion that would put my baby in me when I couldn’t get pregnant. We were friends. He’d give me advice on who to date, who to see and who to...” She floated off, muttering. She gasped. “His mother! I will kill his mother!”

Earlier in the book she had tried to name Carl’s new pet “Kimmy” — “Kimmy the second. I don’t care what you call him, he will always be Kimmy to me” — which nobody understood at the time. The pet was named Sir Rendlegore instead.

Correction on the plush's owner

The Kimaris figure belongs to Carl, not to Bautista. Bautista’s Book 7 prize was the scanning guidebook for plush toys, which he had promised to lend Carl so Carl could identify the figure he already had. Bautista’s own stuffed animals are the Eclipse Pyxies he throws in combat.

docs.title: Book 8: A Parade of Horribles
docs.text: Samantha continues in her established register — indestructible, foul-mouthed, useful in spite of herself — but ends the book on the single most consequential line she's ever delivered about her own past.

docs.title: Chachi
docs.text:
In Chapter 52, unprompted and mostly to gossip, Samantha identifies the mysterious presence Lucia Mar's alter Azra had mentioned hiding among the trapped children inside Lucia's mind: a goddess named Chalchiuhtlicue, whom Samantha calls "Chachi." Her introduction of the goddess is characteristically callous about the actual horror underneath it:

"She's always so high and mighty, always talking about how she's protecting them, but the second something bad or inconvenient happens, she's like 'We need to sacrifice a seven-year-old to make things right.' She even did it once at a Yarilo party because the meatballs had cilantro in them... She sent out an emergency prayer request and had her worshippers kill a whole village day care in the hopes the next waiter would bring her something that didn't taste like soap."

Rosetta confirms Chachi is a minor, unsponsored goddess of childbirth, water, fire and harvests — never powerful enough to matter in the Ascendency game — and Prepotente supplies the Earth-myth parallel, the Aztec goddess of the same name, "considered benevolent" despite a culture that practiced human sacrifice. Carl's private takeaway is the one that matters: whatever Chachi actually is, she is real, dangerous to children, and already inside Lucia Mar's head.

docs.title: Examined by Grigori
docs.text: Samantha spends much of the floor trying to get the fleshmancer Grigori the Placid to examine her own withering-spirit condition, at one point catching him trying to avoid her entirely: "I knew it! You've been hiding him from me!" She succeeds in dragging him off for a private examination, but the book never shows what he finds or says.

docs.title: Saying Goodbye to Louis
docs.text:
Samantha spends most of Floor 10 loudly courting Louis Santiago, and takes his departure through the Desperado Club's casino portal harder than anyone — sobbing on his shoulder, proposing they simply shove Florin and Lucia Mar through instead, and cataloguing, at length, why nobody left in the party is an acceptable replacement affair ("Elle is too much woman for me to handle... Donut is too star-crossed with that orange kitty"). She offers to go with him and he tells her no.

She turns up in his story once more, in the book's closing interlude, but only as a voice: with Louis disoriented in Sheol after his jump is secretly redirected, Samantha messages him over chat. She is not physically present with him, and the text never says where she actually is — only that Taranis and Krakaren are "at the temple" and that she "slipped away."

docs.title: Leaving With Taranis
docs.text:
At the Floor 11 climax, after the god Taranis is lured into the open by Carl's use of Penelope as bait, Samantha slips away with him and the newly-departing Krakaren Prime rather than staying with the party. Her explanation, delivered in the book's final pages via chat to Louis, doubles as its last and biggest open thread:

"I JUST HITCHED A RIDE WITH TARANIS AND KRAKAREN. THEY'RE AT THE TEMPLE, TRYING TO COMBINE A BUNCH OF THINGS TO MAKE WHOLE HIS MOM WIFE, BUT IT'S NOT GOING TO WORK BECAUSE THEY'RE MISSING A PIECE. I SLIPPED AWAY. IT'S ALL PART OF MY PLAN. I'M REALLY HERE TO KILL THE DEMON MOTHER LADY AND HER JERK SON, WHO I THOUGHT WAS MY FRIEND BUT HE TRICKED ME INTO GIVING BIRTH TO A MONSTER THAT WILL DESTROY ALL OF CREATION BOTH INSIDE AND OUTSIDE THE DUNGEON."

Open Book 9 thread — do not resolve

This is the book's own words, not an inference: Samantha states outright that she was tricked by someone she considered a friend into "giving birth to a monster" capable of destroying all of creation. Nothing about who the "jerk son" is, what the monster actually is, or how any of this connects to her established backstory (the sand-ooze daughter from Book 4, the possible Scavenger's Daughter connection raised and dropped in Book 7) is explained anywhere in Book 8. Treat this as an explicitly open thread for a future book, not something to speculate past.

Sourced from Book 4: The Gate of the Feral Gods, Book 5: The Butcher’s Masquerade, Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride, Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin, and Book 8: A Parade of Horribles.

docs.title: Sir Rendlegore ("Rend")
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: Pet — "This is a pet-class mob." Bonded to Carl, and inseparable from Mongo, who is bonded to Donut
  • Race: Tummy Acher, "also known as Belly Achers, also known as Colon Worms" — armless, two-legged, round, with a single upward-pointing tooth and a permanent giggle
  • Class: Not applicable — pets do not take a class
  • Subclass: Not applicable
  • Level: 1 at bonding (Chapter 5) → 8 after his first training run (Chapter 15) → 10 by the base defense (Chapter 30). No level is printed for him after that
  • Role: Tank. "They have multiple tank-based special abilities and are generally resistant to most types of damage."
  • Notable spells/abilities: Wrecking Ball — "the only skill he had," a mass-and-speed special attack
  • Notable items: The Enchanted Tooth Cap of Hi-Yo Silver, a mount-grade tooth cap that lets Carl summon him from up to five kilometers away
  • Status: Alive at the end of Book 7
  • Previously: Garret, pet of Tserendolgor ("Ren") in Book 6

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Rend is the same creature as Garret, and legally he is not. Tummy achers regenerate on death, and on every fifth death they revert to level 1, lose their memories, drop their bond and must be renamed. Ren killed Garret deliberately with the Knife of Frozen Tears in Book 6 so that exactly this would happen and Carl could take him — "You’re going to go live with Carl. He’s going to take care of you because I can’t do it anymore."

Carl arrives on Floor 9 with a level-1 meatball in his inventory and a promise attached to it. The first thing Donut does is accuse him of an affair.

“In all of my life, I have never felt a sense of betrayal this profound,” Donut said. “Are Mongo and I being replaced? Is that what’s happening here? You’re replacing us?”

Carl zaps him out onto the table. He is half the size of Carl's fist, with "a spattering of black hairs atop his not-quite-perfectly-round head, reminding me of Linus from the Peanuts comic," and Garret's old pronounced underbite with "his single, round tooth sticking straight up." Mongo swallows him within a minute, and then throws him back up; Rend's response is to try to climb back in. The two are inseparable for the rest of the book.

docs.title: The Card
docs.text:
The only status card the book ever prints for him is the pre-bond examination in Chapter 5:

Male Tummy Acher – Level 1

This is a pet-class mob.

This pet is not bonded with a crawler.

This pet has died five times. As such, this pet’s stats are all buffed by 125%.

This pet has five weaknesses. Weaknesses may only be examined if you are bonded with this pet or if you have him contained within a carrier.

Tummy Achers, also known as Belly Achers, also known as Colon Worms, are named such because they were originally parasites, living in the intestinal tracts of Jotan-class Titans. They are generally good-natured, though infants can be a little... difficult to control. They are voracious eaters, and when they reach full size can swallow just about anything. They have multiple tank-based special abilities and are generally resistant to most types of damage. They can survive in almost any environment. In addition, while not necessarily known for their offensive skills, their Wrecking Ball attack is considered a terror on any battlefield.

They may be dumb, they may smell a little like expired chorizo, but holy shit are they adorable.

At its current regeneration level, this Tummy Acher will reach full size upon ascending to level 25.

The regeneration rules follow in the same block, and they are what make him unusual:

This particular pet is unique in that it will regenerate upon death as long as their body has not been destroyed. After each regeneration, they will be stronger than before, their overall stats getting buffed by an additional 25%. They will retain their size and strength upon regeneration except upon every five deaths, wherein they will revert to level 1 and lose their memories. Bonded pets will have to be re-bonded at this time. You must change their name as well. After 10 deaths, their full potential size doubles.

Warning: This pet will not regenerate if it dies before it hits level 5.

Warning: Upon death, they will receive a new, random weakness. This weakness generally results in insta-death. The more deaths, the higher the chance the weakness will be something common, like contact with water. It’s considered quite rare for a Tummy Acher to survive past 10 deaths, thus it’s not advisable to deliberately allow your pet to die in order to increase its strength.

Donut’s summary — "Five weaknesses?… So it’s stupid and defective?" Only one of the five is ever named in the text: eating undead flesh (Chapter 15), which is why the party has to confirm a mob is not undead before letting him into a fight.

docs.title: Bonding and Naming
docs.text:
Ren told Carl the bond would take several feedings. It takes one bowl of accidental chowder.

“Too late,” I said. “Man, that was a lot easier than getting Mongo to bond. Ren said we had to feed him a few times, but it only took one bowl.”

Congratulations. You have bonded with Tummy Acher, level-one. A new tab is available in your interface. Bonded Pets. Please see this tab for more information.

Your guild has a pet stable installed. New options are available in your Bonded Pets tab.

Your Tummy Acher requires a name. Please choose a name now.

Donut's ruling on the name is that it cannot be "Garret two" — "being known as a second edition, like a photocopy? Can you imagine?" — and that it must "honor the past but make it clear they're not a copy of someone." Rejected suggestions include Cousin Oliver, Scrappy, Meatball, Balzac, Sherman, Tugboat and Kimmy the Second. The naming happens with the Name Your New Pet box still open and Katia about to pour hair tonic on Carl's head, and it is Louis who lands it:

He held the meatball up with two hands, like that monkey in The Lion King. “Sir Rendlegore. You know, Sir, S-I-R like a knight. And then Rendlegore. You can call him Rend. Sir Rendlegore. It fits with the royal court theme, and it still honors the past. Plus, Ren would’ve loved it. Nobody could ever pronounce her name. She pretended it made her mad, but I think she kinda liked it.”

“Okay, that is a good name,” Samantha agreed.

“Done,” I said before anybody else could respond. “It’s a good name.” I typed it into the box and hit enter.

Your pet has been named Sir Rendlegore!

docs.title: Growing Up
docs.text:
Pet training is accelerated on this floor, and Carl grinds him on a colony of oversized skunk mobs in Chapter 15, initially by holding him in one hand and using him as a weapon.

“Go!” I cried as I retracted my scoop. I moved Rend into my left hand and thrust him toward the dazed creature.

“Chomp, Rend! Chomp!”

It was like I was holding the business end of a food processor in my hand. Blood sprayed from the point of contact as Rend gurgled with glee.

He goes from meatball-sized to softball-sized on the first kill and finishes the session at level 8 and "about the size of a large beach ball" — "Level eight was a decent start because it meant he'd regenerate if he died, but it still wasn't good enough." By Chapter 30 he is a level-10 tank who takes two direct pulse-rifle hits and only falls over and squeals. By Chapter 56 he is "about ¾'s the size of his former self," measured against Garret.

The old high elf Kibben, minding him and Mongo during the King Rust parley, recognizes him: "I got a bit of experience with belly achers." Asked what separates a tummy acher from a belly acher, his answer also settles Rend's pedigree:

“No real difference,” he said. “They tend to call ‘em bellies when they get extra big, but it’s not written down anywhere or anything like that. I remember this fellow from his last incarnation, and even though he was on his first run, he was still pretty big. He’s a special one.”

docs.title: The Tooth Cap and Wrecking Ball
docs.text:
Before the general offensive (Chapter 65), Rend is fitted with a donated item.

Someone had donated a tooth cap, similar to the ones Mongo had for his sharp teeth, but this was designed for mounts. It was called The Enchanted Tooth Cap of Hi-Yo Silver. We installed it over his single, round tooth, making the tooth gleam silver. It allowed me to summon Rend to my position. It wasn’t a teleport spell, but it had about a five kilometer range. The cooldown was only three minutes. When I summoned him, he’d get inexorably pulled toward me at great speed. If there was a wall in the way, he’d—possibly—smash through the wall.

Donut refuses to put one on Mongo because the skill is dangerous. On Rend it is a feature: whatever is between him and Carl when the summon fires gets hit, and it pairs with Wrecking Ball, the special attack that "increased his mass and speed, and it did exactly what the name implied."

Both the item and the ability are covered by other pages.

docs.title: Saving Mongo
docs.text:
The payoff comes at the end of Chapter 72, under the guns of Larracos. Lucia Mar's rottweiler Gustavo 3 has already killed Raul the crab and two clockwork duplicates. It fires Porcupine Defense — steel quills that erupt through Mongo's mouth from the inside — electrifies them, then takes the unconscious dinosaur by the throat. Carl is folded in half by a gale tower, his arm shattered, his sleep wand exploded in his hand.

No, I thought as I struggled to my feet. No. Not Mongo.

She’s never going to forgive me, I thought. This is what will break her.

A terrible, deep giggling filled the night.

The dark, round silhouette appeared above the ridge. Rend.

He’d gotten bigger. Much bigger.

The dog and the dinosaur stood directly between Rend and myself.

“Wrecking Ball!” I wheezed as I cast Hi-Yo Silver a second time. Another gale hit me, and I spun head over heels landing on my stomach.

I watched, as if in slow motion, as Rend started rolling toward me. And as he was magically pulled in my direction, he activated the only skill he had. Wrecking Ball. The special attack increased his mass and speed, and it did exactly what the name implied.

The back half of Gustavo 3, the second of Lucia Mar’s two rottweilers, terror of the dungeon, exploded in a red mist as Rend rushed right up to me, stopping inches from my face.

“Good boy,” I gasped at Rend. I downed a healing potion.

A gale tower bolt hits him immediately afterward. "He barely moved, but he did giggle."

Lucia, still in her hag form and sobbing, pours a pet healing potion on Mongo, whose health "held just the barest sliver of red." Carl's report to the chat is four sentences: "It’s okay. He’s okay. Gustavo is dead. Lucia is conscripted. Rend saved him."

Donut, who has spent the entire book calling him a replacement and an imbecile, settles it in the next chapter:

She jumped from my shoulder, to Mongo’s back, to the ground next to Rend.

“Thank you, Rend. I still think you’re disgusting, but you saved my boy’s life, and I will never forget that.”

Rend belched loudly in her face.

Chapter numbering

The kill itself falls in the closing pages of Chapter 72; Donut's thanks and the aftermath are in Chapter 73.

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin, with background from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: Sister Ines Quiteria
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Full designation: Crawler #8,199,462, "Sister Ines Quiteria"
  • Type: Human Crawler (Cuban) — the secondary antagonist of Book 6
  • Race: Cat Girl — a bipedal humanoid cat with the long, thin face of a Siamese, coffee-dark fur and rounded ears; Donut identifies the look as a Havana brown and loathes her on sight for it. Ines did not pick the coloring ("I didn't get to choose… Maybe it's because I'm Cuban")
  • Class: Poet Laureate — a bard class that requires the crawler take a patron. She calls herself "a bard healer": she buffs allies, hits mobs with afflictions, and fights in melee with a glowing trident
  • Subclass: None printed — her character sheet shows race and class only
  • Level: 47 at introduction; the book never restates it
  • Nickname: El Segador de La Habana — "The Reaper of Havana," the name the Cuban papers gave her after she poisoned every nun in her own convent
  • Order: A Discalced Carmelite nun. She refuses to worship any dungeon deity — "I cannot bring myself to worship a false god"
  • Sponsor and patron: the Nebulars, a religious faction that preaches shutting down the crawl and eradicating every world that can host one. Her celestial Patron by the end is the goddess Ysalte, herself sponsored by Pontifex Shine of the Nebular Balance
  • Notable spells/abilities: Word Weaver (her charisma-scaling charm spell, raised to level 15 by the Nebulars); the Toxoplasma racial skill (see below); a level-15 Book of Rhymes bard skill granted by her patron, used to amplify Word Weaver
  • Notable items: A glowing trident; a cloak and arm bracers
  • Status: Deceased — stabbed through the chest by Louis Santiago while unconscious, Chapter 65

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Ines enters the book as one of three Cuban crawlers Carl and Donut meet on Floor 8, alongside Paz Lo and his cousin Anton Lopez. All three worked at the same women's prison in Havana — the two men as guards, Ines as an inmate. She was serving time for murdering every sister in her convent by poison.

She is soft-spoken, funny, devout, and completely insane. Paz's summary: "She's insane. She's obsessed with the idea of sin. But compared to how she was before? She is so much better." She had been medicated before the collapse; the party assumed the pills were unnecessary inside the dungeon.

She picked Cat Girl deliberately: "it was the only race that gave me a charisma boost for my Word Weaver spell, amongst others, and our game guide insisted it would allow me to choose the Poet Laureate class, which it did. Plus, I always liked cats. We had several at the prison."

Carl likes her. After she stands between her party and a level-250 god with nothing but a trident and a "You're not a real god," he concludes: "She'd been willing to die for her party members, and that said more about her than anything that had happened in the before times. She was one of us… I liked her." Donut wants her dead from the first minute ("Mongo, eat the nun").

docs.title: Toxoplasma
docs.text:
Her race carries a passive charm skill that Paz can only half-remember the name of, because the skill itself keeps eating the memory:

"It's her race. It comes with a skill called Toxo… Toxo plasma something. It makes people like her, want to protect her. You don't even realize it's happening. The effects are mild at first, but they get stronger and stronger as time goes on. And then eventually you'll do anything to protect her. My cousin and I, we didn't learn about it until it was too late. You don't even know it's happening. When you find out, you forget a minute later. That's how it works."

Paz and Anton took up the god Ogun specifically because a priest said he'd keep them from being controlled — and then forgot why they had done it, minutes later. It didn't work anyway. Carl feels the skill land on him in real time, catches himself thinking We can party with her. It wouldn't be so bad, and gets a chill. He chooses to separate from her and warn the other crawlers rather than kill her.

Not in the system text

The word "Toxoplasma" is never printed in full and the skill has no system description block anywhere in the book — Paz's stumbling paraphrase above is the only source for it. See Abilities & Skills.

docs.title: The Card
docs.text:
Paz is smitten by his own god, Ogun, for failing a shrine quest — given an unhealable, permanently draining condition Paz calls "the Inevitable debuff." As he finishes saying goodbye, Ines breaks:

"No," Sister Ines shouted, her voice suddenly angry. "No! You're not leaving."

"No, no, no. Please. You're not leaving me. Everyone leaves me."

She produces a squad flag and jabs it into his neck. Whoom. Paz turns into a card — a common green one. Even Ines looks stunned that it worked. It is the first time in the book a crawler is turned into a T'Ghee totem, and Carl never stops feeling responsible for allowing it.

She then loots Anton's corpse and walks out without a word.

docs.title: The Chowder War
docs.text:
Floor 8's Cuba region carries a quest called The Chowder War — a conflict between the Monk Seals and the Red Maníseros Land Crabs, which the crabs intended to end with a single sneak attack. Ines negotiates with the Monk Seal Abbot instead and warns him of the crabs' treachery.

The system's verdict is that she has turned a quick, survivable rout into a genocide:

Instead of a quick attack and surrender, it has become a war of attrition, with both sides losing devastating numbers in only a matter of days… the only hope of survival from either side is for them to completely wipe out their enemy.

The Chowder War quest fails. The mass death it generates is what floods the underworld and triggers the floor's Demon Eviction event — the chain of consequences that produces "Hell Comes to Crawler Town," Amayon, and the burning of Cuba.

docs.title: Madre de Aguas and Amayon
docs.text:
With Word Weaver boosted to 15 by the Nebulars and further amplified by her patron-granted, level-15 Book of Rhymes skill, Ines glamours the Madre de Aguas — a level 125 city boss, a whale-sized sea serpent she had earlier failed to flag and kill. Because the boss can command every creature in its region, charming it hands her the region: the zombies, the beasts, even the fish start dragging themselves out of the ocean to get closer to the poem.

Controlling the snake allowed her to in turn control pretty much every creature within shouting distance. It was a brilliant plan until the spell got broken prematurely.

Samantha bites her mid-recitation and breaks it. When the Demon Eviction arrives, the demon prince Amayon — one of the four princes of Sheol, level 250 — is forced into the realm inside the zombified snake's body. Ines enslaves him too. Demons across the city are tagged in Carl's interface as "minions of Sister Ines," and the snake is visibly forced to speak Carl's name against its will. Amayon screams at her constantly. Her grip on him is measurably slipping by the endgame.

docs.title: Her Endgame
docs.text:
Ines holds the church that contains the last door Carl needs, and she will not open it. Her chat messages to him are lucid and completely deranged:

"I am filled with power, Carl. With each demon who appears, I grow stronger. They come, they keep coming, and I am the last rampart protecting us all. It is because of my faith. I can save you. I must free you from this place before your soul is dragged into hell. I can't save the cat, of course, as she is nothing but a rank beast."

"But I can save you, Carl. Come to me, and I will show you the way. I showed my sisters, and I can show you. It's not too late."

Carl's reading is that her sponsors deliberately pushed her back over the edge: "Whatever imbalance she had, it's been deliberately kicked back into place." Mordecai's is colder — the Nebulars "likely sponsored her because she's religious, and they either want to convert her or make an example of her."

docs.title: Death
docs.text:
Carl's assault team climbs thirty-two floors of the FOCSA building to reach her. She has to die before Amayon is freed, or the full-strength demon will torch the building in revenge for her. Carl opens the door to find her already sprinting down the hall at him, glowing, screaming "Sinner!" He drops her with a Nighty-Night wand. She is unconscious on the floor at his feet.

"I'll do it," Louis said, pushing me aside. "I already have five player skulls and none of you guys do. Trust me. You want to put that off as long as possible." Before I could object, he pulled a dagger from his inventory. "Sorry cat lady. I never met you, but you need to go if we want to save everybody else." He took the knife and plunged it directly into her chest.

Sister Ines Quiteria, The Reaper of Havana, finally died.

A god's marked-for-death indicator appears over Louis's head:

The death of the bard has angered her celestial Patron. She is coming to seek revenge.

The Goddess Ysalte has entered the realm.

Ysalte — Goddess of Hopelessness and Insanity, level 250, "The Downward Spiral, The Vinegar Bitch" — materializes out of Ines's dissolving corpse, inherits a slightly enhanced version of her deck, and tells Louis: "She was asleep, and you killed her. Her mind is finally at ease, which is a blessing, but I was not done with her yet, and for that you must suffer."

The goddess is then killed by Paz Lo, the card Ines made.

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: Supporting Cast
docs.text:
Characters who appear with real substance but haven't yet earned a full page. See the Characters overview for the promotion rule that moves someone from here to a full page.

Name Role Notes 150-Soldier AK-47 Group Broadcast-only crawler group Never given individual names/leader; shown moonwalking through the dungeon well ahead of schedule, then reduced to melee and improvised weapons after running out of ammunition Admiral Corinne Whimpleshin Dromedarian camel; adjutant for the Blood Sultanate (Book 7) A single-humped camel in a sundress holding "an honest-to-goodness martini," and a little heavyset for a camel. Teleports into the middle of Carl's Operation Snake Pit raid on the naga castle mid-slaughter, spraying her drink, shouting "I am calling foul! I am calling for an end to this immediately!" Like Baroness Victory, she is not frozen by the effect that has stopped everyone else in the room Agatha Homeless woman; revealed in Book 6 to be Residual Agent number 22 Survives events she shouldn't; carries unexplained high-tech items (Valtay Corporation weapon/shield/comms) later found in her cart. Still alive and pushing her cart on Floor 4 (Book 3); briefly glimpsed on Floor 5 (Book 4), now Level 12. Book 6's epilogue is her POV and explains everything: she is a member of a rare, ancient species that "peeled away from the collective" ten years before the collapse, wearing a human shell she took by hunting down and killing one of the Apothecary's own residuals — which is how she has access to both feeds. She spent those ten years in Wenatchee, Washington, and liked it. At the emergency collapse order she is in the alley behind the Meadowlark Elder Care facility, planning to light a barrel fire at exactly the right moment to draw staff and police outside so a dungeon entrance will generate near them — i.e. she is why the Meadowlark crawlers got in at all. She was fond of Brandon, who shared his lunch with her. Her faction's goal is recruiting the system AI; her private view is that "this entire universe would be swept clean of biological life". Book 7: Zev relays a direct order from Prime Minister Glory that Carl is not to interact with her. She is then named co-warlord of the War Mage Rebellion alongside Akuma, who plainly does not want her there. Fopsy the Dream's adjutant theorises her aim is not to win Faction Wars at all but to end the Celestial Ascendency early — because once the ascendency is finished with no crawlers left, the system's hard-coded shutdown-and-hibernation sequence triggers, an alternative to the failsafe — and that she now believes the local AI is "a threat to the Eulogist." Akuma's own warning to Carl is that she "seeks to kill us all" Allister Cookbook author, 13th edition; T'Ghee practitioner (Books 3, 5–7) Contributes recurring marginal notes to The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook on explosives stability, vampire lore, and protection spells, all filtered through his home culture's T'Ghee card-and-meditation tradition — his own T'Ghee deck holds cards like the Plague Bearer and the Open Wound. For him, T'Ghee is a genuine religion, not the card-battle totem game Ren later runs, and Carl leans on that distinction when he first encounters totem combat in Book 6. Confirms Batbilge's death was likely his final entry Anaconda Level 75 Quarter Naga, lead dancer at the Penis Parade (Book 6) Brother of Damascus Steel and second son of Astrid and the Night Wyrm, though the brothers "weren't even remotely the same species" — evidence that the family's in-game races aren't their birth races. One of Donut's two favourite dancers. Found weeping beside Damascus when word of their mother's assassination reaches the club, and insists on going with him to confront their father: "If you're going to fight him, I'm going, too… This is family business." Does not join Carl's mercenaries; neither brother is seen again in Book 6 Anton Lopez Level 47 human crawler, class Fugitive (Book 6) Cousin of Paz Lo, fellow Havana prison guard, and the third member of Sister Ines's Cuban squad. Bald, caped, covered in real prison tattoos including his face; carries a crossbow with a monkey's open mouth on the front; two player-killer skulls, earned killing two of his own party on an early floor for trying to kill Sister Ines. Worships Ogun. Charmed by the goddess Oshun into throwing the Ogun shrine piece out the door, which triggers the smiting of both men; when Carl casts Black Nimbus to pull him out of the god's targeting, Ogun simply steps backward onto his head and crushes it — "Just like that, as if he was nothing" Areson the Wise Ogre strongman, one of the three brothers from Grimaldi's circus (Book 6–7) Brother of Herman the Fleet and of Apollon, who was left behind on the third floor; all three were once part of a single three-headed nodling that died and split long ago. Fights on Carl's side through Book 7 and is one of the soldiers teleported in for the assault on the Madness castle Arief Level 80 Semeru dwarf; War Leader and commander of the Larracos Defense Force Infantry (Book 7) Team Retribution's senior soldier and Carl's guide to Larracos — he is the one who walks the party down through the city's rings and explains its layout, its defences and the explosives rigged on every other down-ramp. Carries a Despondent warning because his goddess is dead: he cannot worship another deity, all his stats take a 15% hit, and worshippers of other gods do 10% more damage to him. Personally wants revenge on Architect Houston. On NPC mortality: "We believe that for most of us, if one dies, they are dead forever. We are not immortal like the outworlders." Guards the door at Louis and Juice Box's wedding Big Tina Allosaurus; daughter of Kiwi, raised in the FUPA (Book 5–7) The "ballerina dinosaur," still carrying her magical self-repairing feather boa and her dead magic wand. Kiwi refuses to let Carl use her in the castle defence — "She's just a child" — and Carl nearly overrules her before deciding it is Kiwi's call; Donut overrules them both, and Tina comes out roaring. Later single-handedly takes out one of Larracos's fire lance towers and shields dozens of crawlers from being burned alive. Inseparable from Simoom the albino rhino, who she treats as a pet Bobby, Low Thi, and Morris Sp The Tomb Raiders — a subterranean-quadrant crawler team (Book 4) Bobby D.J. (Spy, trap disarmer), Low Thi (D-Bag Geek), and Morris Sp (Arachnid Freelance Psychiatrist) survive a chaotic, trap-filled slog through the Necropolis of Anser's subterranean quadrant, aided by Katia's hand-drawn maps. All three die completing the quadrant's final task — disconnecting/reconnecting the necropolis's lightning-conduction wiring under fire from the ghost boss Quetzalcoatlus — earning the quadrant's liberation posthumously; teammates Tyler Storm, Mike Barnes 3, and Janice die earlier in the same questline Bodi Level 60 Big Game Spear Hunter; veteran of Land War, a different game inflicted on his own home planet (Book 7) Tall, tan-skinned, and almost silent — "He'd said maybe three words since I'd met him, making Chris seem downright chatty." Elected a battalion commander on experience alone, and everyone treats him as someone famous without ever saying why. Carries a boomerang-enhanced spear that returns to his hand. Takes over the 103rd Recon Legionnaires and runs the feint that pulls the Madness defenders off Carl's infiltration route Bomo and the Sledge Two of the four cretins (rock monsters) freed on Floor 6; members of Carl and Donut's 15-strong Personal Guard platoon (Book 6–7) In Book 7 they run the Princess Posse's entire missile battery from Shanty Town, firing over 1,500 missiles at the Madness and Reaver castles through Trollish Portable Control Rooms modified to look like the oversized game controllers they already knew how to use. Sledge's contribution to the war effort: "Robots go boom." Bomo is killed in Chapter 70 defending Donut in the lower levels of the Nest tower against Lucia Mar, alongside Toyotomi and the defending mages — his last message, "Will stop her now," is followed by This message is from a deceased mercenary Bonnie Young dirigible-gnome NPC, daughter of Commandant Kane (Book 4) About ten years old; witnesses her pet pig Sausage taken hostage and killed, then her father's death (mauled by the boss Denise, whom he'd raised as a replacement pet). Kept calm afterwards only by a mind-altering potion her father gave her before dying. Rescued by Carl and Donut, gifted the family's soul-crystal power source, and adopted into Hump Town's dromedarian/changeling community under Juice Box's care. Book 5: rescued a second time from Floor 6, using her ballista skills against attacking mantises during the Twister's destruction. Book 7: crews the airship Party Planner alongside Louis and Skarn, having swapped her Dallas Cowboys jersey for an oversized 105th Scream Warriors shirt ("We bleed when the job's done"). Carl repeatedly orders both children off the ship and they repeatedly stow away; she is calm and chewing gum while manning the door gun through the dragon attack. Transfers to Floor 12 with Kiwi and the other children Brad Bea's affair partner (Book 1, 4) Present at the original Seattle collapse; survives on the surface with Bea for months in Book 4's epilogue, quietly resentful and fantasizing about having entered the dungeon instead. Shot (non-fatally, left to bleed) by Odette's operative Lexis after reaching for a dropped weapon during Bea's capture Brother Widespread Tempest Level 125 Ogre Basilica Cleric Guard, Club Vanquisher (Book 7) A worshipper of Taranis standing guard over the temple district during Operation Snake Pit. One line in the system text and nothing more Bucket Boy Young crocodilian NPC, former Penis Parade attendant and low-tier healer (Book 6–7) Hired with the rest of the club crew as one of Carl's mercenaries. In Book 7 he is Imani's assistant and runs the Princess Posse's field hospital, and later a clinic by the castle — where Kiwi gives birth. Scales notwithstanding, he visibly pales when Mordecai proposes a Removal Order on Carl: "Like, won't his head explode if it doesn't work right?" Burcu Level 59 Porsuk (badger-headed) Swashbuckler, Turkish crawler (Book 6–7) A newcomer at #10 on the leaderboard, same class as Tran and Bautista. One of the three who brawled over Queen Imogen's memorial crystal at the end of Floor 7. Carl knows her only as "very serious, reminding me of Hekla." Her drunk teammate Emir threatens Carl with "My Burcu is going to kill you." Killed in Book 7 on a table in Architect Houston's surgical theatre. Houston cut out her tongue and voice box and tortured her mother to death in front of her; she gets a message to Carl through his Book of Voodoo with a map of the room and its fireball traps. Her last words to him, and the reason she is one of the book's cruellest loose ends: "He tortured my mother. He killed her right in front of me. Free me so I can kill him… You owe me, Carl. You killed my father. Free me now." Carl never learns what she meant about her father. His attempt to carry her out tips the table and sets off the traps; she dies, and he barely escapes Calliope Level 130 Cybernetic Bleached Drake; pet of Warlord Fang (Book 7) The gravity-magic dragon that shoots down the Party Planner and then circles the abandoned Reaver castle, ignoring the battle underneath it. Fang is hiding inside her. When Carl detonates the No Disassemble device she spirals out of the sky screaming and explodes, showering the party in blood — and taking her owner with her Captain Fresh Syndicate security officer, handler for the assassin Minus (Book 8) Preps Minus for his undercover mission posing as his own dead brother "Linus," supplying five hundred hours of injected memory footage and a cover story built on the real Linus's finances: "If the AI so much as suspects you're anything other than a simple tourist, it's going to pop you like a boil." Never appears again after the briefing Cascadia Kua-tin lead engineer and executive producer of Dungeon Crawler World: Earth; the "kill, kill, kill" announcer (Books 1–6) The voice that opens every floor. Book 6 shows her in the flesh for the first time: at the Faction Wars preproduction meeting Carl needles her about Administrator Loita's death, she blinks out — and then reappears physically in the room, splashing water across the table, rebreather strapped over her gills. "I'm really here now, Carl… You want to hurt me? Now's your chance… I fucking dare you. It would be the end of the both of us. I would godsdamned welcome it." She also warns she is "one crisis shy of pulling the failsafe, which would kill us all." The instant the other warlords arrive she snaps on a fake smile and her announcer voice — a change Carl finds "instantaneous and unnerving." Recently divorced. Book 7: she disintegrates in public. Her floor-opening announcement is slurred and "a little too chipper"; by the warlord council her scales are falling out and the ones left have "a dull, sickly sheen," and she drinks tequila out of a softball-sized potion ball through her rebreather while Odette tries to interview her. Princess Vinata supplies the reason, whispering it to Carl: the Borant civil war has killed Cascadia's former husband and most of her family — rebels hired the Valtay against the Bloom, and a derelict warship hit the liquid habitation ring around Borant Three, killing millions. The news is not public, and Vinata will not say how she knows it. Cascadia's last word in the meeting is a laugh with "a hint of madness to it": "Well, why not? Why the fuck not?" Chaco Wolf-headed skyfowl/pterolykos Bard, prize-counter attendant (Book 3, 5–6) Mordecai's former party-mate. Book 6's prologue finally explains the Book 3 on-air attack: on the tenth floor, Odette — their manager — coerced Chaco, a worshipper of Dodola, into throwing the Dart of Ophiotaurus into Mordecai's brother Uzzi, force-summoning Dodola into the corpse inside a containment circle so the goddess could be killed and the stairwell opened. He refused at first — "You want me to kill Uzzi? It's not going to happen" — and she bought him with a promise of protection and a lie about the Outreach Guild. He jumped ten levels and took the godkill credit. In Book 5 he runs the Butcher's Masquerade's prize counter and apologizes to Carl again without explaining why. Odette has set aside a trust for him. Book 7: drafted as the warlord council's field correspondent because Magnificent Troy refuses to come down to the surface, and spends the meeting narrating over people's shoulders with a microphone and a lint roller. He asks the room to vote on whether the newly-crowned King Stalwart looks stupid in his crown, and Stalwart — who is physically in the same room — punches him unconscious across the floor. Odette takes over the broadcast in his place: "my very old friend Chaco, who is feeling a little… punched in the face right now" Chiyome Razor fox, "Mistress of Nunchaku," Team Wild Hunt (Book 8) Introduced performing a group Size Up scouting spell on Carl and Donut with two silent, flipping ninja-style teammates; relaxes into a genuine tactical ally once alone, drinking beer and explaining the "Split Personality" spell that created Corcunda's two halves. Loses a teammate, Ito, to the Heat 2 kangaroo-demon boss Chuluuna and Khulan The last two members of Tserendolgor's squad (Book 6) Human, Mongolian, married, from the same village as Ren. Chuluuna is her tank — a strongman who turns his skin to stone and casts Chain Lightning, and the only one who could stand inside her flamethrower. He is killed by Ren's own Mongolian Death Worm totem after Quan Ch flips totem allegiance mid-card-battle, then eaten and vomited back out by it. Khulan, tiny and weathered, paralyses targets so Ren can burn them; she was teleport-trapped away and arrives after the fight, and will not leave her husband's body. She had also lost a little girl in the collapse. Ren states she will kill herself as soon as she stops crying, dumps her own gear on Carl, and is inside the dome when Ren detonates it — but Khulan's death is never confirmed on the page; only Tserendolgor's name enters the deceased-crawlers folder Clarabelle Crocodilian Desperado Club door bouncer (Book 4–5) Runs security at the Desperado Club's entrance; still on good terms with Carl and Donut in Book 5 despite past incidents, and reluctantly reveals the club's secret bathroom stairwell down to the Hunting Grounds level after Donut extorts her over a decade-old refund discrepancy Clint, Randy, and Todd Three child NPCs living in the Princess Posse's guild hall (Book 7) Clint was a chee kindergartner on Floor 6 until Scolopendra's nine-tier attack turned his whole class into were-castors; he grew up, fought the high elves for centuries, died, was turned into a tattoo on Tsarina Signet by Edgar, reverted to his pre-attack child form, and became a flesh golem when Signet died — so he is a kindergartner again, permanently. "Edgar says I might never grow up because I'm a flesh golem now." Randy and Todd are orphaned ursine bear cubs whose father was killed by Kiwi before she changed back from a velociraptor; Todd is disconcertingly pious ("We're going to bathe in apostate blood"). All three turn up in metal skull caps with training spears demanding to fight, and are sent back inside. Transfer to Floor 12 at the end Commander Stockade Level 76 Phase Sorcerer; warlord of the Lemig / Democratic Sortion (Book 6–7) A seven-foot upright caterpillar who talks like an aged Southern California surfer — the leader whose proxy Luke stood in for him in Book 6. His one gambit is the book's first faction-ending disaster: he uses a level-15 Summon Ally invitation, precisely timed by an illegal outside observer, to teleport Carl to his throne room while Carl is unconscious and infested, intending to strand the Shi Maria spider there to massacre the room. It half-works, the spider gets loose on his side anyway, and it kills half his family and Luke. He spends the entire adjudication that follows on the floor, undulating and sobbing "Luke, oh gods, Luke is dead. My beautiful, beautiful Luke," admitting his guilt on the record by accident, and pulling his own fur out in a ring around himself. Kills himself the moment the panel begins reading out his penalty Corporal Pillbox Gnoll mercenary, originally in Empress D'Nadia's employ (Book 7) Talks his squad into surrendering when the Prism castle falls and negotiates for the lives of mercenaries on other teams: "Lockjaw and Mange are our mates… Mange is my cousin, and my ma would never forgive me." Survives the entire floor. In the last chapters he is one of the mercenaries Carl consciously declines to kill, even though killing them would have maxed his stats at 300 the way Li Na did: "They would be disappointed in the lack of blood I shed… because I was not the monster they hoped I would be." Pillbox is crying when Carl says goodbye Dante Crocodilian Thief; cookbook author, 3rd edition (Book 7) Neighbor and confidant to fellow cookbook author Justice Light during their shared indentureship as merchants and, later, castle guards. When both are ordered to kill the gentle ice-elf NPCs of the settlement they'd been guarding, Dante refuses twice and is executed on the spot by an AI beam — "no third warning... the light simply erased him, as if he'd never existed." His status card: "Was killed by administrative action for refusing to follow orders." Justice Light later credits him with teaching that "there is no such thing as the point of no return." See The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook Doctor Bones Level 90 Skin Skellie Bard; the Penis Parade's announcer/DJ (Book 6–7) Hired with the rest of the club's crew as one of Carl's mercenaries. Turns out to be the crowd-control lynchpin of the Cuba endgame: he has a better version of Carl's Super Spreader, which he uses to mass-infect the strippers and create the sluggalo army, and a Conscript spell that flips a percentage of enemy forces. Astrid was his bard's patron until her assassination — "She was Astrid. Now it's you," he tells Carl. Book 7: one of the Penis Parade crew who stay on and are made officers in the Princess Posse's army — the strippers are all commissioned Sergeant First Class, which lets them recruit and command the base troops, including the sluggalo Legionnaires. Holds the castle entrance during the Monkeywrencher assault and teleporting in for the attack on the Madness castle Dong Quixote Level 45 human, elderly stripper at the Penis Parade (Book 6) Spanish-accented, fond of shouting "Thou hast seen nothing yet!", and insists on fighting with a lance despite having no mount. Points Carl at Damascus Steel ("the cranky one"). Carl gives him the sentient nickel sock — Jefferson, the life force of a cursed miser bound into a tube sock once owned by a kid named Tanner, looted off Quan Ch — and Dong takes it "reverently," calling it "a mythical weapon." He uses it to knock a demon crab off the FOCSA building after the crab drags his friend Author Steve Rowland into hell, and barely speaks afterwards. Book 7: finally gets his mount — Gonk, the dead King Rust's swamp yak — and rides her through the back half of the book with the sock Jefferson still giving him advice. Substitutes himself for Holger on Carl's infiltration team and so ends up on the raid into Architect Houston's castle. One of Carl and Donut's Personal Guard Dorota Donut's rival pet-chair AI companion, built into the Floor 10 racing vehicles (Book 8) A whining, obsequious enchanted seat forever fishing for Donut's approval ("My breathtaking princess, you should sit here... Without you, I have no purpose") and constantly needled by Dr. Metcalf, who resents its existence. Briefly disabled mid-race by an enemy attack: "I just initiated Dorota's diagnostics mode. I think she might be defective" Dr. Metcalf The Floor 10 truck's sardonic GPS/AI navigation unit (Book 8) A holdover joke from the "Miss Beatrice" fake AI therapist gag of earlier books — Donut clarifies "It's not really her. I asked." Voices every race briefing in a deadpan, doom-laden register ("I thought a cat driving was a 50/50 death sentence, but now... a prepubescent crocodile behind the wheel...") and visibly resents rival seat-AI Dorota's existence throughout Drakea A bune; cookbook author, 22nd edition, namesake of Drakea's Enchanted Kerchief of Disorder (Books 3–7) The cookbook's most prolific recent annotator and a survivor of the final naga-controlled season, "both emotional and verbose," dripping with hatred for the Naga and the Syndicate. Theorizes the system AI is "moving into the minds" of dying monsters, trying and failing to know what it's like to lose everything, and repeatedly urges future authors to record exactly how they die. Died, per Mordecai's uncertain memory, on the 11th or 12th floor, not before helping bankrupt the naga Sultanate via a legal settlement. See The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook Dwight and Lucienne Sparkling Unicorn Enchanter and his Mandagot Fink navigator, Team Sparkles (Book 8) Foul-mouthed, hostile racers who nearly run over Carl, Donut and Rend fleeing a cave in Heat 1, then ambush a rival car at the Heat 2 starting line with a hidden weapon before the race properly begins, winning outright. Lucienne is killed partway through the book — the text only references her death after the fact, never stages it on-page. Dwight spirals afterward: stabs a DJ to death mid-bar-brawl while drunk and grieving, cheats his way to a Heat 5 win by driving over a factory roof instead of through it, and is finally killed in Heat 7 — Donut removes his head "in a single swipe" of her upgraded Claw the instant the race begins Drick Dream elf; adjutant for Team Retribution (Book 7) The elf Carl first met when he was pulled out of the game — he is not really an elf at all but a Valtay worm in a host body, which Juice Box discovers when her blade passes straight through him. Permanently unkillable as far as she can tell. Carries a tablet in one hand and a drink in the other, cannot fully turn his head, and spends the floor trying to teach Ferdinand — who has taken up residence on top of his head — how to use the warlord menus. Shares the live-update duty with Baroness Victory, and is usually mildly drunk while doing it. Calls foul against his own team over the war mages' killing of King Stalwart, forcing a full quorum Edgar Tortoise NPC; tattooist, mapmaker and scout for the Princess Posse (Book 6–7) Slow, ancient, and the most quietly indispensable NPC in the book. His Part of the Background skill is level 15, so an entire army can march past without noticing him, and his Sense Movement skill — also level 15 — lets him detect movement inside sealed structures, including invisible and non-corporeal movement. That second skill is the foundation of Operation Snake Pit: it is Edgar who confirms Rosetta's theory about the naga escape trick by watching a Bijou worship-tendril rise through the floors, and Edgar who finds the Blood Sultanate's entire standing army already dead and rotting in its own barracks. Also the party's real tattooist — Katia has to ink Carl's transfer tattoos herself only because Edgar is out scouting — and he inks the cartoon dog on Donut's flank. Rides the back half of the book strapped to Rosetta like a backpack Eunice & Ricky Joe Fathom Dwarf mother and son (Book 2) Eunice beats a city elf senseless with a rolling pin defending her boy; Ricky Joe loses an arm to Mongo mid-brawl (later healed but not regrown) after punching him Everly Sward Mantis Explosives Engineer; cookbook author, 5th edition (Books 3, 5, 7) Struck out alone from the thousands of fellow mantises who entered the dungeon with her rather than work as a group. Her Book 7 interlude follows her final minutes on Floor 8: hired to help an ogre dig an escape tunnel, she whispers the book's own title, "The Inevitable Ruin," to herself moments before an advertisement disguised as a tower collapses on both of them. He is heavily implied to be the AI itself in costume and never confirms it: during the foot-washing — a sacrament that supposedly cuts Carl off the feed so "the other gods cannot eavesdrop" — he answers a question Carl only asked in chat, then remarks "Parts of this conversation will still make the feed." Carl asks outright: "Are… are you the AI? Why are you pretending, then?" His entire answer is "We all have our roles… And our limitations." Paulie / Goff A Residual — an Open Intellect Pacifist Network asset seeded on Earth (Book 6) A deep-voiced homeless man in a Christmas-morning shelter memory: "People call me Paulie, but my real name is Goff." He is one of several thousand agents planted before the collapse, reciting a rehearsed daily speech that only triggers when a crawler stands nearby, on the theory that the crawl would eventually run a memory floor. The Network's real plan was to get Carl in earshot so that either the liaisons would yank him away and enrage the AI, or the Syndicate would hear what he heard and pull the failsafe — killing the star and ending the crawl. His speech notes that his kind can't be attacked by dungeon monsters until they transfer their knowledge: "Still, we always die in the end." Penn Level 62 human Fortification Engineer, one of the fifty thousand former crawlers smuggled in on the Homecoming Queen (Book 7) Carl's introduction to what his new army actually is. Penn and the other engineers are the only troopers who have gained levels; everyone else is flat level 60. He greets his warlord by starting a "Hup, hup, hup" chant that the entire construction site picks up, then claps Carl on the back, shoulders a structural beam and goes back to work without another word Porthus (Dr. P. Hu) Secret benefactor, The Open Intellect Pacifist Action Network (Book 4–6) Revealed in Book 4's epilogue as the true identity behind Carl's mysterious, extravagantly funded second sponsor — almost certainly the same Porthus who authored the Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook's 2nd edition generations ago and swore to spend his freedom fighting the system from outside. Sends Carl a note in Book 5 (signed "~P. Hu") coordinating a covert, multi-sponsor effort to power up Donut's Laundry Day spell. In Book 6 he is the one who recruited Tipid and Rosetta Thagra to the Homecoming Queen, with a single promise: "I can only promise two things. Eventual death. And eventual justice." Book 7: he gets his own opening interlude, smuggles Volteeg into the crawl disguised as an Operatic Collective mercenary, and turns King Rust's fortune into an escape. Rosetta Thagra kills Rust and drains his accounts on the field; Baroness Victory supplies the PIN, in a deal struck with Porthus before she was ever chosen as adjutant. The money buys two ships. In Rosetta's interlude he is boarding one of them with the families of the crawlers, bound for the Plenty system to trade a ship and the remaining money to the goats for passage through the "forbidden" gate at the Impetus Point, the tunnel node reaching the furthest known part of the galaxy.
