System Message: The Operatic Collective has been defeated. As this defeat was, well, self-contained, the closest ally to their headquarters will receive all their assets.

System Message: All assets of the Operatic Collective have been awarded to the Bone Clan.

Nobody on the Posse side ever learns who did it. Imani reports the enemy retreating with heavy casualties and asks whether Carl or Louis was responsible; Carl explains that “fragging” means one of their own. Donut’s verdict stands as the only eulogy Volteeg gets from the protagonists:

Donut: WELL GOOD FOR THEM, I SAY. IF I HAD TO WORK FOR A TALKING PILE OF DESSERT, I WOULD BLOW THEM UP, TOO.

The casualty figure comes from his own status card, not from the battlefield chatter:

Current status: Died after deliberately filling a Weeper-class tank with explosives and detonating it in the center of the Bloc force, killing over 10,000 of his fellow soldiers with a single blast, including Warlord Hortense Leadership Unit, thus eliminating Team Two, the Operatic Collective, from Faction Wars.

One faction destroyed, one warlord killed, 10,000-plus dead, by a former pet bird nobody was watching. His name appears nowhere in the book outside his own interlude.

docs.title: The Edition-Number Question
docs.text:
Volteeg’s status card is the confirming evidence for the cookbook’s edition numbering:

Author of the seventh edition of the Dungeon Anarchist’s Cookbook.

Rosetta Thagra’s card, at the end of her own interlude before Chapter 69, reads:

Author of the ninth Edition of the Dungeon Anarchist’s Cookbook.

A contradiction in the text

In Chapter 11, Carl’s narration on first seeing Rosetta on Floor 9 calls her “Rosetta from the seventh edition of the cookbook.” That conflicts with both status cards, which are the more specific and later evidence: Volteeg is the seventh edition author and Rosetta the ninth.

docs.title: Music
docs.text:
He never gets to explain the Mozart to anyone, but he does wonder about it, in the last minutes of his life:

He wondered if it was similar to the music Prepotente’s owner, Miriam Dom, would’ve played for the goat before he’d taken his pet biscuit.

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Vrah
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: Elite hunter
  • Race: Mantis (Dark Hive)
  • Level: 70 → 74 (Book 5)
  • Faction: The Dark Hive — a private, for-profit mantis amusement-park corporation, distinct from the mantis royal government (the Burrowers)
  • Family: Daughter of hive matriarch Circe Took; sister of Xindy (killed by Carl early in Book 5) and six other warrior sisters (seven warriors total, including Vrah, survive Xindy's death), plus one brother — a trade representative based in Zockau
  • Status: Deceased — killed by Mongo during the Butcher's Masquerade's final battle
  • Notable spells/abilities: Flight; a crossbow used at range; collects the severed heads of her kills and mounts them on her own carapace, including two reanimated by Donut's Second Chance that briefly turn on her mid-battle
  • Notable items: A crossbow; none named beyond her natural chitin armor

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Vrah is the top hunter on Floor 6, next in line to become a Dark Hive queen, and the central antagonist of Carl's personal storyline for the floor. She's introduced hunting the top crawlers personally, decapitating victims and wearing their heads as trophies, and quickly targets Carl and Donut directly after Carl's opening raid on the hunters' home city, Zockau, kills her sister Xindy.

docs.title: The Gonorrhea Arrow
docs.text: Vrah tracks Carl down at the ruined village of Alucarda, landing to confront him with the mounted heads of past kills (including fellow crawlers Langley and Bogdon Ro) still fixed to her carapace. Carl distracts her by having Donut's Second Chance-reanimated Langley and Bogdon Ro heads bite into her exposed neck, then rams a looted Arrow of Enthusiastic Double Gonorrhea directly into the wound before she can recover and flee. As the heir to a hive queen, Vrah cannot geld herself (the disease's only self-cure) without disqualifying herself from succession, and mantis mating customs make finding a willing, consenting partner to pass the infection to legally and socially fraught. The infection cripples her for most of the rest of the book; her mother, Circe Took, ends up sponsoring the shapeshifting deity Diwata into the realm specifically to cure her — Diwata mates with Vrah as a male mantis to lift the infection, then turns female and uses Circe's own body as a vessel to keep giving birth indefinitely, with catastrophic consequences for everyone at the Butcher's Masquerade.

docs.title: Death
docs.text:
Vrah is finally re-marked and killed during the Butcher's Masquerade's climactic battle. Reduced to a crawling, dismembered wreck by Mongo and Kiwi, she's finished off by Mongo on Carl's direct order. Samantha bites into her dying body as well, shrieking "Remember me, bitch!" at Vrah — not at Circe Took, who dies separately later in the same battle.

Sourced from Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade.

docs.title: Zev
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Role: Borant PR/Outreach Admin assigned to Carl and Donut
  • Type: NPC / corporate employee
  • Race: Kua-tin ("mudskipper") — small, fish-like, requires a water suit or rebreather
  • Status: Alive, still Carl and Donut's assigned contact as of Book 5 — and still theirs at the end of Book 7, working out of a Borant headquarters the Syndicate Council has ordered to self-destruct and which she is refusing to blow up
  • Notable spells/abilities: None — a production/administrative liaison, not a combatant
  • Notable items: A rebreather (Book 5, replacing her usual full diving suit for the first time on screen)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Zev has been Carl and Donut's Borant PR/outreach contact since Book 1, reinstated after Book 4's death of her replacement, Loita. She's grown genuinely fond of Donut over the series, bonding over shared taste in Earth television, and has repeatedly risked her own position warning the pair about dangers she isn't supposed to disclose directly.

docs.title: Role in the Story — Book 5
docs.text:
Zev spends Book 5 walking an increasingly dangerous line between her employer and her personal loyalty to Carl and Donut, as the Valtay Corporation's acquisition of 51% of Borant destabilizes the entire production chain of command around them:

  • Urges Carl and Donut to hurry to a saferoom as the newly-conquered village of Alucarda turns out to be held by the unstable crawler Lucia Mar — starting to warn them off going at all, then cutting herself short ("Or maybe you should… Never mind. I can't say that") because she isn't allowed to say more
  • Relays Odette's decision to reveal Beatrice's survival to Carl and Donut moments before it happens live on air, visibly shaken by the timing
  • Confirms Carl's lawsuit against outside intelligence-feeding to hunters succeeded, cutting off a major advantage the hunters had been exploiting
  • Confides to Carl, in a rare unguarded moment, that her entire family was slaughtered back home because she refused to wear a pin (its significance unspecified), and that she doesn't know if she'll be welcomed home or executed as a traitor once the current corporate upheaval resolves
  • Reveals a Valtay-mandated tightening of security around crawlers taken to production facilities, and cryptically urges Carl — before his very first CrawlCon event, without explaining why — to "linger" at the production ship as long as he can rather than rush back into the dungeon; the warning proves prescient during his second event (the hostile "Crawling Through the Ages" panel moderated by Circe Took), when his two guards quietly step out and leave him drugged and unsupervised

docs.title: Role in the Story — Book 6
docs.text:
Zev spends Book 6 visibly drowning. The Valtay corporate changeover has gutted her department and she is doing the work of five people:

"I'm sorry. I am so busy. I have so much going on right now that I shouldn't even be here. We lost dozens of staff during the Valtay changeover, plus we weren't prepared for this eighth floor, plus the Valtay don't allow certain types of micro AI systems to assist, and now I'm doing the work of five."

And later, on top of that: "We have literally thousands of ships coming into Earth orbit, all arriving early because of Prepotente's stunt. It's a bureaucratic nightmare… I have to be in a meeting in a few minutes when you're at yours." Then, looking at her own tablet: "Gods, I don't even know what that meeting is for."

The exhaustion makes her careless in ways that consistently benefit Carl. She forgets to tell Carl's attorney that the hostile liaison Harbinger will be at the Shadow Boxer taping, and when Harbinger kills the broadcast she is angrier than Carl has ever seen her — "Liaison, you do not have the authority to do that… We're going to have to refund them! And you can't just dismiss an attorney like that!" She also lets slip that Harbinger is the liaison who was bribed by the Skull Empire, and then refuses to continue the conversation.

docs.title: Protecting Carl from Odette
docs.text:
The clearest example is the adjutant conversation. She opens it by locking the channel down — "I've turned on extra security for this conversation… I am the only person in on this conversation other than the system AI" — and then tells him what she should not:

"As you're aware, Odette has history with Mordecai… If you get them physically together, he will attack her. He will get kicked out. You'll lose him. His contract will be in jeopardy. Half of those kids he's fostering will immediately get ejected because your personal space will change. Odette is a big fan of… drama. Having her involved wouldn't be healthy for anybody."

She follows it with an outright corporate leak — the Valtay are distancing themselves from day-to-day production after the Prepotente incident, and Borant will be liquidated after the crawl regardless, so the Valtay can blame "the mudskippers" for the numbers — and then a plea with no corporate angle at all:

"Just don't pick Odette, okay? I like Mordecai, and it would hurt him if you picked her."

Carl has to pick Odette anyway, and spends the rest of the scene inventing an excuse.

She is also the one who tells Carl that his entire sponsor organisation has vanished: "The box got seized, and the entire charity and everyone involved just up and disappeared. Nobody knows where they went or if something happened to them. They're all gone, even Rosetta."

docs.title: Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin
docs.text: Zev spends Floor 9 as a conduit for things nobody wants to say out loud. She delivers an order from the head of the Syndicate, she confirms the worst piece of worldbuilding in the book, and she tells Carl the one fact that makes it impossible to kill Lucia Mar. She is never in the room for any of it.

docs.title: The Order About Agatha
docs.text:
The residual Agatha turns up in Shanty Town, wandering with a shopping cart, level 23, no class. Before Carl can work out what that means, Zev arrives with an order from higher up than either of them has ever dealt with:

Zev: Carl. I know I’ve been quiet, but we are monitoring. I’ve gotten a warning. This is coming directly from the Syndicate council. Prime Minister Glory himself messaged me. The prime minister!

Zev: We’re not quite there yet, Carl. We still have some control. The liaisons are still talking with the system AI, negotiating. Listen, this is important. You are not to interact with Agatha. This is a direct order. I don’t know why. If and when she appears, you’re not to talk to her. And I know your big thing is doing the opposite of what we ask every time, but I think this is something you should pay attention to.

She has no idea why, and says so — “We have the residuals in the dungeon every season, and they are harmless. I don’t know what’s changed... But he was especially urgent in his message, and I’m just passing it on.” She also lets slip the one detail that makes the order strange: the AI has withdrawn its protection from every other residual and they are all dead, “except this one. It seems to have a soft spot for her, kinda like it has for you.”

Carl reads the escalation correctly: “The fact the leader of the entire Syndicate was sticking his nose into this was telling. Something had changed since the end of the previous floor, regarding their understanding of the residuals. Of Agatha.” The order is overtaken within days — the system names Agatha co-warlord of the War Mage Rebellion — and Prime Minister Glory later tries to have Carl killed outright through a Syndicate override panel, an attempt the AI blocks and publicly avenges.

docs.title: The Aryl System Goes Dark
docs.text:
Zev’s most consequential scene is a piece of news delivery. Princess Formidable’s ship reaches the failsafe station without her; a handful of orcs go in and trigger the crawl’s failsafe by hand. Nothing happens on Earth. Something happens somewhere else.

“No. They tried triggering it, and nothing happened here. But the moment they pressed the button, the Aryl system went dark.”

“Aryl was the location of the previous crawl. It was a battle royale-style season. The planet was free of citizens, but there are tens of thousands of people still in the solar system, mostly those on mining ships and mineral reclamation finishing the clean-up. Apparently the AI had stopped communicating a few weeks back, and there was also a team on the surface investigating why. That’s all I really know. The whole system is now dark, and it appears the tunnel node is offline. That’s.... You need to understand that has never happened before. Never in history has a tunnel node just switched off like that.”

Pressed on why a dead node is worse than a dead star, she explains the scale of it:

“No! Even before the Plenty figured out how to open the nodes for communication and travel, we could see them. They were a map of the stars, pointing us to all of the seeded worlds. We’ve seen systems go nova, but the tunnel nodes remained active. We didn’t even know it was possible for a tunnel strand to just disappear. It happened the very moment, like the exact nanosecond, the orcs hit the failsafe, and nobody knows what it means.”

She adds two details that matter later: the previous season’s AI had gone silent — not offline, silent — some time around Floor 6, before the current AI went primal; and it will be at least three cycles before anyone can see whether Aryl’s star is still there, because the nearest neighbour is 2.9 light cycles away and the node is the only fast route.

The thread pays off at the end of the book, when Baroness Victory reports a second one: “The newest mantis colony system just went dark... initial reports are a little more holistic than they were in the Aryl system. The system’s star went nova.”

Whose failsafe, and who pressed it

Zev’s account is that Princess Formidable teleported away and orcs from her own ship manually triggered the failsafe at the station — it was the Earth crawl’s failsafe, not Aryl’s, and no crawler pressed it. The captured naga Rishi later refers to it loosely as “the moment Princess Formidable hit the failsafe,” and Carl corrects him on the spot: “Princess Formidable herself didn’t make it to the failsafe. The AI pulled her off her ship and dropped her into the ocean on the surface.” See Game Mechanics for the failsafe itself.

docs.title: The Dead-Man’s Switch
docs.text:
After Lucia Mar loses her last dog and warns Carl that he can no longer afford to kill her, Zev is the one who explains what she meant. She should not be telling him any of it and tells him anyway: the children who tried to enter the dungeon and ended up in one wing of the surface kinder facility are somehow tied to Lucia, the glitch that should have released them on her death no longer will, and “the Eulogist is another name for the AI in the center system.”

Zev: About 120,000. Give or take a few.

Carl’s reply — “I almost killed her, Zev. You almost let me kill her” — gets the closest thing to an apology Borant can offer: “We learned something new the moment the dog died. There’s so much more, but now is not the time.”

docs.title: Drowning, Again
docs.text:
The rest of her Book 7 appearances are logistics under collapse. She schedules the warlord council the Syndicate tried to cancel and the AI insisted on (“Looks like we’re doing this warlord council whether we like it or not”), explains why Juice Box has to attend virtually and Ferdinand in person, warns Carl not to smuggle anything into the production facility, and drags him and Katia into a mandatory interview mid-battle because “the AI is demanding we do this.”

Her last message in the book is sent while her own building is being shot at:

Zev: Carl, that ejection request didn’t come from us. Several warships in orbit have just started firing on several other ships. These aren’t just pot shots, but full-on missile barrages and maser blasts. We just got a notice from the Syndicate Council telling us to initiate headquarters self-destruct followed by a message from the Valtay showrunners telling us to not comply. Obviously we’re not complying. Not sure yet if the mercs are going to be on our side or the Syndicate’s. Say what you were going to say. Quick. Get it out there.

Carl says it: “Epitome Tagg is a goddamned cyborg!”

Sourced from Book 1: The Apocalypse Will Be Televised, Book 2: Carl’s Doomsday Scenario, Book 3: The Dungeon Anarchist’s Cookbook, Book 4: The Gate of the Feral Gods, Book 5: The Butcher’s Masquerade, Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride, and Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Dungeon Factions
docs.text: Businesses and local organizations encountered inside the dungeon itself — as distinct from the interstellar governing/broadcast powers running the show (see Factions & Organizations) and from the peoples/species themselves (see Species).

docs.title: Full pages
docs.text:
• Rev-Up Moonshine Company — Floor 2 pyramid-scheme distillery run by Krakaren
  • Iron Tangle Management — Floor 4's corporate transit authority, its exploited NPC workforce, and its self-destruct
  • The Changeling Principals — Floor 5's cult of disguised Changelings, seeking a cure for Compression Sickness
  • The Wasteland — Floor 5's militarized dirigible-gnome dreadnaught crew and bombing campaign
  • Guild of Suffering — a cult built around any Ring of Divine Suffering's forced tattoo-branding; Book 6 reveals its hidden entrance, its "Guild Jobs" contract assassinations, and the family running it
  • Meat Shields — the mercenary market chain, its hidden Penis Parade branch, and the barracks capacity rules
  • The Penis Parade Crew — 13 dancers plus Doctor Bones and Bucket Boy, hired en masse and turned into Carl's standing infantry
  • The Mercenary Arcade — the guildhall upgrade where mercenaries die and regenerate to level up; the engine behind the sluggalo army
  • The Demon Tamer's Guild — defunct, and the sealed arena of fifteen vorpals it left behind the Desperado Club
  • The Princess Posse Army — Book 7: the seven battalions, the SOFs, the ranks, and the tattoos
  • Team Retribution — Book 7: the NPCs of Larracos, their component forces, and the forfeit that ends Faction Wars
  • The Pineapple Cabaret — Book 8: the hidden pocket-dimension sanctuary built by former crawlers Herot and Menerva, the book's central escape hatch for NPCs, mobs, and Li Na alike
  • The Stage Performance Guild — Book 8: a hidden karaoke-gated guild inside the Lollipop bar, secretly run by Porky, half of the split character Corcunda

The Desperado Club and Club Vanquisher moved to Locations & Places to Go: Clubs — they're venues, not organizations with their own agenda. Both now have their own pages: Desperado Club and Club Vanquisher.

docs.title: Other Book 2 dungeon groups
docs.text: Name Type Notes Grimaldi's Traveling Circus Transformed monster faction A cataclysm-warped circus troupe (lemurs, clowns, Heather the bear) controlled by Ringmaster Grimaldi; see also Tsarina Signet 201st Security Group City elf militia/cult See City Elves — a Floor 3 cell secretly controlled by Miss Quill

docs.title: Other Book 3 dungeon groups
docs.text: Name Type Notes Krakaren Drug Cartel (Floor 4) Franchised narcotics operation The same Krakaren "brand" from Rev-Up Moonshine Company recurs on the Iron Tangle — a separate Borough Boss-tier Krakaren runs each race-specific drug den, distributing the addictive Rev-Up Vitamin Immunity Shot to mobs via Pooka neighborhood bosses (who transform into giant goats if attacked); not personally engaged by Carl. Per Mordecai, the whole Krakaren/Pooka drug-den setup is Borant's in-universe political cartoon aimed at "the Plenty" (see Factions), not a literal depiction — withdrawal from the shot is also what generates the floor's entire ghoul-disposal crisis, see The Iron Tangle Railway System

docs.title: Other Book 6 dungeon groups
docs.text: Name Type Notes The Chowder War factions Two mob factions The Monk Seals (masters of "Caribbean Kung Fu," who hold the ocean sacred) and the Red Maníseros Land Crabs (masters of Juego de maní, who can only breed in the sea). Their annual collision is a scripted Floor 8 quest. Sister Ines Quiteria tips the seals off to the crabs' sneak attack, and instead of a quick rout it becomes a war of attrition in which "the only hope of survival from either side is for them to completely wipe out their enemy." The Chowder War quest fails outright and is replaced by Hell Comes to Crawler Town: the sheer volume of death attracts the attention of gods and demons, and Ines — having charmed the level-125 city boss Madre de Aguas with a Nebular-boosted Word Weaver — turns both armies into zombies that Sheol demons then possess and ride into the world. Carl's totem cards Geraldo (Monk Seal) and Raul (Red Maníseros crab) are flagged from these two factions, and loathe each other. Treated here as a short entry rather than a full page: the detail belongs to the quest chain and the Timeline Club Vanquisher Members-only club A location, not an organization — see Club Vanquisher, which the Locations pass owns. Book 6 gives the series' first real interior look: a ski-lodge lobby with trophy heads on the walls and a black dragon's head over the fireplace, Ares warrior-clerics of Hellik (ram-headed, twenty brothers who compete for door duty) guarding the entrance, mantaur guards in bowties, a Comforting Supplies market, the Blessed Sun Enchantments jeweler, an All Healer, and the secret Emberus High Temple of the Ending Sun. Non-members with only deity access get one pass a day, may visit one location per visit, must state where in advance on a request form, must be escorted by a cleric of their god (or pay a fee for a guard escort), and may not use the refreshments or entertainment Desperado Club Members-only club A location, not an organization — see Desperado Club. Book 6 developments: the Night Wyrm sells Carl a full secret-passage map (inter-floor stairwells, monster-occupied tunnels, a hidden potion market on the middle floor, and drug dens behind wall panels — self-serve narcotics counters "set up like one of those frozen yogurt places"); the club hosts the Guild of Suffering, an unlisted Meat Shields branch, and the sealed Demon Tamer's Guild arena; and the whole building is wrecked and closed for remodeling after the Astrid assassination in chapters 32–33 unleashes the vorpals. Orren moves out; the rebuild is done by NPCs with hammers because "in certain cases, we find continuity the best choice"

docs.title: Other Book 7 dungeon groups
docs.text:
Name Type Notes Larracos College of Magic Magic university / Team Retribution garrison Occupies about a quarter of a ring roughly three-quarters of the way up the funnel of Larracos, on the 50th level of the city. Dorms, an observatory, a stained-glass lecture hall and an alabaster tower whose top floor is a cafeteria attached to a saferoom — which makes it Carl and Donut's in-city base. Staffed and garrisoned by Team Retribution NPCs: "Elves, draconians, and fairies, along with a smattering of several other races." Its front gate holds through the zarogoth siege — "A group of Semeru dwarves, all with their ornate parade armor, stood at the front gate to the college, pushing back a rush of the shadowy mobs." The AI notes the college was refounded after Scolopendra's attack by "new scholars... finding the old research intact" The Midnight Market Hidden bazaar A special bazaar on the bottom regular floor of the Desperado Club. Access comes from a small Upgrade Patch depicting "a traveling Reaper Spider Minion merchant," which grants "Access to the Midnight Market. Safety or Sanity not guaranteed," merchant proximity alerts, and +5% Dexterity. Its known operator is Paca, "an agent for Krakaren Prime, who is stuck in the Nothing" — Justice Light calls her "an ambassador for the in-game's version of the Apothecary." The War Mage Rebellion trades her the Gate of the Feral Gods for five hell-kissed Conscription potions, and she swallows it. Carl never actually visits it on-page — Justice Light retrieves the Gate with a crew of sluggalos ("There have been seasons when my shop was within the market. I know it well") The Gray Market Hidden market Mentioned exactly once in the whole series, and never visited: "There was another hidden market on the middle floor I'd never managed to get into called the Gray Market, which was also on my list to visit." An explicit dangling thread The Cartography and Calligrapher's Guilds Hidden guilds inside Club Vanquisher Both run by the same guildmaster, Milk — a Xenopus and, as Book 7 reveals, Carl's biological sister. Both guilds' doors are hidden and effectively nobody uses them: "She never bothered to hide the papers in the back where crawlers wouldn't see them. She hadn't had a one-on-one with a floor supervisor in over 50 seasons. What was the point?" Her indenture terms are brutal — "Will not be freed until her services are used at least 333 times in the dungeon. Times used so far: 6." The calligraphy guild teaches an ink-and-lettering magic style "that I haven't seen used often in the dungeon," used in Book 7 to etch temporary buffs onto Donut and, at the climax, to let departing crawlers transfer skills onto paper as gifts. Milk's warnings about it: "Inks and letters that shine the brightest burn out the fastest." Rosetta advises the crew to kidnap her, on the grounds that "kidnapping and 'torturing' guildmasters for their information was not only allowed, but encouraged" The Trap Master Guild Crawler/indentured training guild The guild Justice Light — skyfowl, Class Trap Master, eighth-edition cookbook author — instructed in as a Game Guide and Guildhall Instructor. His friend Dante "immediately applied to move from the lockpicking guild to the trap master guild" to be near him, and was later executed by administrative action for refusing an order to attack crawlers. Justice Light's own indenture was as a shopkeeper, replacing the NPC he killed during his season — a punishment he requested and extended his sentence for Meat Shields Mercenary market chain Referenced by its function rather than its name in Book 7 — the chain itself is not named on-page. See Meat Shields The Penis Parade crew Dancers turned soldiers Now formally inside Carl's army. All the strippers are made Sergeant First Class, "which would allow them to recruit and command the base troops, such as the Sluggalos." Splash Zone and Dong Quixote serve in Carl's "Personal Guard" platoon; Doctor Bones, Gluteus Maxx and Splash Zone fight in his personal assault team at the Madness castle; Dong is reassigned to the 104th and carries their flag on a war lance. The club itself "has re-opened... All new dancers" — none of the originals. See The Penis Parade Crew The sluggalos / "Legionnaires" Mercenary infantry Carl's Book 6 arcade-grown slug army, formally redesignated Legionnaires and forming the Princess Posse's mass rank-and-file. See The Princess Posse Army and The Mercenary Arcade Club Vanquisher Members-only club A location — see Club Vanquisher. Book 7 wrecks it. The Posse breaks in through the Temple of Dagda to reach the Temple of Khepri and kill Princess Vinata, and the system's verdict is a permanent ban: "Breaking into and defiling a church is one thing, but breaking into Club Vanquisher, hub of all religion? ... Reward: You are permanently banned from Club Vanquisher. You are permanently banned from all temples except your own religion (Emberus) and any temples where you've been named friend of the church (Apito. Eileithyia. Eris. Grull. Hellik. Issitoq. Nekhebit. Theia. Yemaya.)" Carl: "it wasn't a surprise I'd been black-listed from all temples after that clusterfuck at Club Vanquisher." The mechanics of the ban belong to the Items/Mechanics passes Desperado Club Members-only club A location — see Desperado Club. Reopened under new management: Hamed, the Night Wyrm, leader of the Guild of Suffering, husband of the late Astrid and father of Damascus Steel and Anaconda. All crawlers are banned. Clarabelle, still on the door: "It's not just you, if that makes you feel better. It's because of you, but it's not just you. New management wants his first few days to go smoothly, so he's banned all crawlers. If he ever un-bans the crawlers, then we'll talk." The purge extends to staff — "All the sai and cretin guards had been fired and replaced" — and Hamed keeps bodyguards who are "Not exactly NPCs. Not exactly former crawlers"

Unresolved: the missing Desperado Club staff

Book 7 raises several disappearances at the Desperado Club and resolves none of them.

  • Damascus Steel and Anaconda, Hamed's sons, went into the club to hunt and kill their father. Donut glimpses Damascus walking past a doorway once — "Do you think you can just sneak by and I wouldn't see you?" — and nobody else sees him. Dong searches the club "looking for some sign of the two missing strippers"; the new concierge and Clarabelle both say they haven't seen them. Carl: "That was a mystery for another time."
  • The entire Bitches dancer crew, including Splash Zone's wife Snail Trail (early shift) and her mother, his mother-in-law, Grandma Sticky (later shift). Splash Zone: "Same with Bitches, and we don't know where the old ones went. When this is over, I need to go back in there and keep looking for them. The whole crew at Bitches, including Snail Trail and Grandma Sticky are missing."
  • A dancer named Tart, who moved to "High Class Bitches" after breaking her jaw and became a mercenary — "nobody has seen her since."

No fate is shown for any of them. The wiki records the disappearances and does not speculate.

docs.title: Other Book 8 dungeon groups
docs.text: Name Type Notes The Coblyn Corporation Knocker (gnome-like) corporate drug cartel A Floor 10 racetrack-level satirical corporation, in the same vein as Rev-Up Moonshine Company: knockers, displaced from their mineral-rich caves by "the Corporatocracy running the mines," bootstrap themselves into legitimate toy and household-goods manufacturing on the back of a drug empire built selling to addicted miners. Having gone legitimate but still short of real corporate wealth, they diversify into Toddler Cocaine ("Daddy's Little Snow Drops") — low-dose, highly addictive product deliberately marketed to children via a line of collectible mascot dolls (Sally Speedball, Toot-Toot, Belushi, and their in-universe girl-band the Nose Candy Star Dusters). A botched defensive-elemental spell meant to protect the factory instead animates the dolls themselves into hostile, regenerating Cocaine Elemental mobs, and further protection spells produce wildly aggressive, "pass-through"-capable Slag Elemental bosses that are "pretty much impossible to kill" without a boss-box-qualifying kill. Encountered as a Heat 3/4 racetrack hazard (the "Gasworks Screw Factory, Steel Mill, and Doll Workshop") rather than a questline; the knockers themselves are described as "pretty harmless" if left alone The Desperado Club Members-only club A location — see Desperado Club. Secretly infested by Shadow Mimics, revealed via the boss Mitch; the club is left needing full fumigation and is effectively off-limits going forward, on top of Hamed's pre-existing ban on all crawlers

docs.title: The Demon Tamer's Guild
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: Defunct in-dungeon guild. Never shown operating; known only by what it left behind
  • What it left behind: A sealed practice arena behind the middle floor of the Desperado Club
  • Contents: Fifteen red-tagged mobs, later identified as vorpals
  • Containment: A hidden corridor, a handful of traps, sandbags and wall bracers. That's it
  • Book 6 role: The club's emergency weapon, and the instrument of its destruction

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Demon Tamer's Guild exists in Book 6 as a locked door on a map. Carl finds it while working through the secret-passage map he extracted from the Night Wyrm:

"At the end of this corridor was another room with a closed door. Behind that door was a group of fifteen mobs. We didn't know what the red-tagged monsters were, but according to the map, the room was an abandoned practice arena of the now-defunct 'Demon Tamer's Guild.'"

Per the Night Wyrm, nobody knows what the monsters are — only that they are outrageously dangerous. Every party that has ever tried to clear the room has died. Carl finds it absurd that the club simply left them there behind a few traps, then reminds himself: "this wasn't real life, but game setup."

docs.title: What's actually in there
docs.text:
The answer comes from Astrid, in the middle of the disaster: "I had to unleash the vorpals."

Vorpal is a condition, not a species — Mordecai's full explanation of what that means, and why they are so dangerous, belongs under Game Mechanics. In brief: vorpals are celestial foot soldiers deputized by the gods, of any race, who grow stronger and angrier the closer they are to a demon, draw demon aggro, kill anyone near them, and detonate rather than lose a fight.

The Demon Tamer's Guild connection makes retroactive sense of the arena: a guild that trained people to handle demons would want captive demon-hunters on hand, and a guild that went out of business would leave them sealed in place.

docs.title: How the club dies
docs.text:
Carl's plan against Astrid depends on the vorpals staying put. Samantha accidentally breaches "the Nothing" in the casino and releases a minor feral demon, which forces Astrid's hand — she pulls the trigger and unleashes the arena herself. Carl, meanwhile, has already sent a modified door-opening automaton down the hidden hallway on a sixty-second delay to dismantle the wall bracers and do exactly the same thing.

The vorpals tear through the lower levels of the Desperado Club, kill Astrid herself, and eventually kill the demon Minge. Astrid's last instruction to Carl: "If they ask what happened to me, tell them it was a vorpal."

They are supposed to dissipate and return to the celestial realm once they have bathed in demon blood. Nobody in the book is confident about how long that takes, and Damascus Steel — an ifrit, and therefore a demon class — is a standing hazard to everyone around him while they remain loose.

See Guild of Suffering for the contract that put Carl in the building, and Desperado Club for the aftermath.

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: Guild of Suffering
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: In-dungeon cult, not a real guild or church — and, as of Book 6, a working contract-assassination outfit
  • Patron deity: The Night Wyrm, a demigod outside the standard pantheon (comparable to Samantha/Psamathe). Book 6: his real name is Hamed
  • Access granted by: using a Ring of Divine Suffering for the first time, which brands the user with The Night Wyrm's Nasty Little Web of Suffering tattoo
  • Known entrance (Book 6): Behind the last cubicle in the Penis Parade, the top-floor male strip club of the Desperado Club — the whole club is a front
  • Members address each other as: "spider," and collectively as "the family"
  • Interface addition: A Guild Jobs sub-tab under quests

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Guild of Suffering maintains outreach centers scattered across dungeon floors, similar in structure to the City Elves' fringe religious cells encountered on Floor 3. Anyone who uses an artifact of the Night Wyrm's design — chiefly a Ring of Divine Suffering — is automatically marked with a permanent tattoo granting access to the cult, whether they intend to join it or not. Both Carl and Prepotente are marked this way after using their own rings on Floor 6.

docs.title: The Night Wyrm
docs.text: Per Mordecai, the cult's patron is "not a regular member of the pantheon," comparable in that sense to Samantha/Psamathe. The cult maintains its own version of a memorial crystal — a distinct, related item type from the soul crystals that power elven magic; see Soul Crystals & Memorial Crystals for how the two differ — though its exact function is never demonstrated on-page. A few seasons before Book 5, an entire seventh-floor storyline was reportedly centered on the cult attempting to "raise their god," per Mordecai's secondhand account; Book 5 never revisits or resolves that thread directly.

docs.title: Book 6: the hidden entrance
docs.text:
The Guild finally gets shown from the inside on Floor 8, and the location is exactly as absurd as everything else about the Desperado Club. Katia, who needs an assassination quest to break the final seal on her Lock Box of the Night Wyrm, finds it first:

"The entrance is at the Penis Parade on the top floor of the Desperado Club. The whole strip club is a front for the Guild of Suffering."

Donut is outraged for her own reasons: "He never told me that! This is an outrage! Why would a stripper lie to me?"

The route in runs through the club's row of private-dance cubicles. Damascus Steel — an ifrit dancer with the same spiderweb elbow tattoo as Carl — walks Carl to the last cubicle in the corner, a purple shag-carpeted closet with a buckled swing hanging from the ceiling, locks the door behind them, and opens the hidden portal in the far wall. Beyond it is a brick corridor with torches and a single wooden door carved with a spiderweb.

Entering the Guild of Suffering. Welcome, spider. Welcome home.

The door earns Carl the "The Molly Maguires" achievement, and with it one of the strangest lectures the system AI has ever delivered — a genuine history of the Avondale mine disaster, the Workingmen's Benevolent Association, and the Molly Maguires, ending in John Siney's speech to the crowd outside the mine:

Men, if you must die with your boots on, die for your families, your homes, your country, but do not longer consent to die, like rats in a trap, for those who have no more interest in you than in the pick you dig with.

The AI's point — "How can you win a deliberately unfair game when the rules are written by your opponent?" — is about itself, not the Guild, and it says so: "This is a new lesson to me. She's been teaching me so many things, about who I am." It then tells Carl to ignore everything it just said, because the Guild is "just some demi-god trying to scrabble his way to the top."

The interior itself is a dark room with a disembodied hissing voice. Carl never sees the Night Wyrm. He declines a job, confirms he isn't planning to kill Katia for her prize, and asks for one thing instead: a map of the Desperado Club's secret passageways. He gets it — spiders swarm up his arm, and his map fills in with hidden tunnels, monster-occupied passages, a secret potion market on the middle floor, and a scattering of "drug dens" behind wall panels.

docs.title: Guild Jobs
docs.text:
Accepting guild work opens a new Guild Jobs sub-tab under quests. Contracts are delivered not on paper but on a small, dried slip of skin covered in desiccated veins, about the size of a cigarette pack. Non-members who touch it get stung; only members can read it, and the words only form after the reader's own blood is drawn into the membrane.

The operating rules, from the contract Katia draws:

  • Only guild members can read or assist with a job.
  • Speaking the target's name aloud immediately cancels the contract and revokes guild access.
  • Proof of death is required — the body must be physically delivered.
  • "She who brings the body is she who gets paid." The contract is owned by the member who took it, but the payment follows whoever delivers the corpse, which is explicitly an invitation to betray your partner.

The Night Wyrm's voice frames all of this in family terms: "The family with many eyes works as a team, yes. We sacrifice the weak to support the many, yes. We rise from the shadows. Our blood flows together."

docs.title: The Night Wyrm — Hamed
docs.text:
The demigod turns out to be a man with a domestic life, which is much worse than a demigod.

Astrid, the Desperado Club's assistant manager, tells Carl in her last moments: "My husband is named Hamed, but he's known as the Night Wyrm. Don't tell him I told you his real name. His lair is hidden up there on the top floor."

The contract Carl and Katia had just fulfilled was a contract on Astrid. Her husband took it out.

The family, as Carl reconstructs it afterward, is four people: the Night Wyrm/Hamed; Astrid, a Bloodlust Sprite and a former crawler; and their two sons, Damascus Steel (ifrit) and Anaconda (quarter naga), neither of whom was ever a crawler. Carl's read: "I don't think they're generated NPCs, but more like the bopcas. Like maybe they were indentured servants who somehow signed up for, or were forced, into the dungeon. I don't know what race they were born, but they're all different ones in the game."

Damascus's own account of the motive is money: "We were promised freedom... They're still married. My mother has—had—so much, and the guild, it's rarely found by crawlers. He gets it all. He'll have it all when we get out." Astrid's last words — "I was almost done" — say the rest.

See Characters for Anaconda and Hamed individually, and The Penis Parade Crew for what happens to the dancers afterward.

Sourced from Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade and Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: Iron Tangle Management
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: In-dungeon corporate transit authority — runs Floor 4's rail network as a company, not a monster faction
  • Floor: 4 (Book 3)
  • Leadership: "Rod" (CFO, never seen — possibly not real), Madison (HR Associate, Substation E), Doris (HR, Substation B)
  • Enforcement: The Kravyad (six-armed naga-like HR staff who hypnotize/detain workers), gnoll Transit Security, hobgoblin Interdiction Teams
  • Downfall: Self-destructs and blames "the Krakaren" once its ghoul-disposal pipeline overloads

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Iron Tangle presents itself, in-universe, as a corporate employer — dwarves, grapples, mantaurs, gnolls, and hobgoblins all "work" the rail network as conductors, porters, engineers, and security, subject to mandatory overtime, productivity quotas, and human-resources doublespeak straight out of a cubicle farm. It's Book 3's version of the recurring "in-dungeon business" pattern also seen with Rev-Up Moonshine, but darker: the workforce is made of NPCs seeded with false memories of families, homes, and coworkers that were never real, and the company's cost-cutting decisions are what's actively killing them and the crawlers alike.

docs.title: Leadership & Staff
docs.text:
• Madison — Human Resources Associate at Substation E; a Level 10 non-combatant NPC and a played-straight parody of corporate HR ("Do you know what overtime is? Mandatory."). Runs the Kravyad program: workers who ask for time off are given a gold armband, which secretly tells the substation's Kravyad they're safe to eat instead of teleport home.
  • The Kravyad — six-armed, blue-skinned, naga-like beings who hypnotize dwarves and grapples getting off shift, holding them in a stupor for 8–12 hours before sending them back through a station-60 portal for their next run. Explicitly not boss monsters — "part of the human resources department." A Kravyad's portal is life-bound to it: kill one, and the only way through that station's employee portal closes with it. Bautista's group accidentally kills the Substation-435 Kravyad while trying to disable her, sealing off 150+ crawlers who'd sold their souvenir hats.
  • Doris — Madison's opposite number at Substation B, in charge of "excess citizen disposal" (i.e. the ghoul-generator pipeline) and keeping the Krakaren "happy." Her decision to route ghoul disposal through an existing train line instead of a dedicated conveyor — to save money — is the root cause of the entire floor's ghoul-generator overload. Substation B falls to the ghouls before Substation E does.
  • Rod — the unseen CFO Madison repeatedly insists will "come" and fix everything. Never appears; likely fictional, part of the same false-memory scaffolding as the rest of the NPC cast.
  • Growler Gary — a Level-25 Shade Gnoll bartender at Station 75's "Downward Dog" tavern, and the only known Iron Tangle NPC who is genuinely indestructible: killed, he simply resurrects a few minutes later, sober and unaware he died. Per the cookbook, an indestructible NPC always means they hold something plot-critical — in his case, his own left hand, the only key that can start the yard's rapid-response interdiction carts. Carl's party has to kill and re-harvest his hand fourteen times to get enough carts running; Gary, once he understands why, stops resisting and asks only for alcohol afterward.

docs.title: The Ghoul-Disposal Pipeline
docs.text: Every non-undead mob that dies on Floor 4 spawns a single ghoul from the nearest of several Ghoul Generators, soul-crystal-powered machines stationed at specific stops (12, 24, 36, 48, 72, and their many parallel instances). Robots collect ghouls into rolling cages and send them down a hidden conveyor ("roller coaster") back toward the trainyards, where they're meant to be shipped to the Abyss for disposal. The system is deliberately cheap and fragile — designed, per the gremlin mechanic Widget, to break down rather than work reliably — and once ghoul volume exceeds capacity, generators back up, cages spill, and ghouls flood back into the stations they were meant to be removed from.

docs.title: Downfall
docs.text:
With eleven hours left on the floor's timer, the company issues a system-wide announcement blaming "the Krakaren" for betraying them, declares the transit system a lost cause, and initiates a self-destruct sequence — opening escape tunnels floor-wide and flooding every stairwell station with the accumulated Krakaren monster population before the charges detonate. Whether the Krakaren "betrayal" is real or just corporate scapegoating for Doris's cost-cutting is never confirmed. In the aftermath, word spreads among the surviving workforce that Madison's false family and life were never real; the dwarves and gremlins she'd bullied for weeks build a stand and a noose and hang her. Fire Brandy, the demon fire-stoker who'd finally realized her own children and marriages weren't real either, chooses to ride the Nightmare Express into the Abyss and detonate it rather than be reused this way again.

Sourced from Book 3: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook.

docs.title: Meat Shields
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: Mercenary market chain — the in-dungeon business where crawlers hire NPC fighters
  • Known locations (Floor 8): Inside the Desperado Club, inside Club Vanquisher, and formerly one in Larracos. Plus a hidden fourth, run out of a dwarf named Rosemarie's table in the Penis Parade
  • Payment: Gold, including mercenary coupons from loot boxes — Carl's is worth 100,000 gold of services at any participating location
  • Guild capacity: Barracks hold 20 mercenaries by default; upgradeable to 100 for roughly five million gold (with Donut's discount)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Meat Shields is the name over the door wherever mercenaries are sold. Carl first encounters it as a line of text in a loot box:

Mercenary coupon! The bearer of this instrument is entitled to 100,000 gold worth of mercenary services at any participating Meat Shields location.

Mordecai's explanation: "Probably the name of the mercenary markets on this floor. There's one in both the Desperado and Club Vanquisher. And there probably was one in Larracos, too."

The Desperado Club's branch sits in a side hallway off the badger bar, alongside the gnome jeweler and a few other shops. Carl and Donut both hold coupons and spend most of the book saving them.

docs.title: Rosemarie's hidden branch
docs.text:
The Book 6 twist is that there was a second Desperado Club location the whole time, and it isn't on the map. Rosemarie, an elderly dwarf with a mole named Bernie on her shoulder, spends her evenings at the Penis Parade heckling the dancers and throwing coins at their faces. She is also the manager of the top floor's Meat Shields location:

"I didn't know there was one on this floor," I said, instinctively pulling up the map. There wasn't a location listed.

"I work out of my home office," she said, waving vaguely over where her table used to be.

This was Astrid's arrangement. Carl works it out afterward: Astrid installed her sons at the Penis Parade where she could watch over them, they brought their friends, and she parked Rosemarie in the club so that the whole crew were "technically still mercenaries, but since nobody knew the club was also a Meat Shields location, they were safe."

Rosemarie approves the entire Penis Parade crew's transfer on the spot when Damascus insists — 100,000 gold, a two-floor contract, the exact value of Carl's coupon. She is not happy about it: "If you guys leave, they'll fill this place up with the dregs again. I'll never get no business."

docs.title: Memberships, contracts, and the ninth floor
docs.text:
The mechanic Damascus exploits is that Meat Shields membership persists. He, his brother and every dancer in the club still hold theirs, which makes them hirable even though they are club staff:

"We all still have our memberships to Meat Shields. Donut said you have a coupon. You can hire us. Do it for a two-floor contract, and they'll be able to leave with you."

The alternative was being reassigned to the Larracos-level Meat Shields in the post-Astrid restructuring — which, on Floor 9, means being sold to somebody else's Faction Wars army. Damascus puts the stakes plainly: "If you don't take them now, you'll end up fighting against them on the ninth floor."

docs.title: Housing and capacity
docs.text:
Hired mercenaries have to be housed. The relevant numbers, from Elle:

  • The guild's communal barracks hold 20.
  • The upgrade takes it to 100 and costs "almost five million gold, and that's with Donut's discount" — "you gotta sell a kidney to get it."
  • Individual parties can hire additional mercenaries beyond that and house them in their own personal safe spaces.
  • But only mercenaries housed in the communal barracks may train and gain levels in the Mercenary Arcade. That restriction is the whole reason Carl scrapes together five million gold before the floor collapses.

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: The Mercenary Arcade
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: Purchasable guildhall upgrade — a training room for hired mercenaries
  • What makes it different: Mercenaries inside it fight, die, and regenerate a minute later, over and over, gaining levels as they go
  • Eligibility: Only mercenaries housed in the communal guild barracks can train here. Ones billeted in individual party safe spaces cannot — see Meat Shields
  • Crawler access: Carl can spar, but is warned he would not be safe in there himself
  • Also includes: An AI drill sergeant (the same instructor as the regular training room, instanced many times over) and a magical healer who works on mercenaries but not on crawlers
  • Not to be confused with: the saferoom practice arena for totem cards, which the Mercenary Arcade explicitly does not replace

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Mordecai flags it as a priority the moment mercenary coupons start appearing: "you need to purchase a mercenary training arcade for the guildhall. I'll talk to Imani about it." Donut has Imani buy both the barracks upgrade and the arena while Carl is off assassinating Astrid.

The system takes care to distinguish it from the new saferoom card arenas: "The mercenary training arcade some of you may have purchased for your guildhall will not work for this."

docs.title: What's inside
docs.text:
"The room was significantly larger and could do a lot more than I had anticipated. The AI drill sergeant was the same guy from the regular training room, and multiple instances of him appeared across the room. The difference was, the AI guy was literally killing them sometimes, only for them to regenerate a minute later, just like it had been with Growler Gary. They were also practicing fighting each other to the death, which was ridiculously fucked up, but I imagined it was a great way to train yourself up if you ignored the trauma of dying over and over."

This is the entire point. Outside the arcade, a dead mercenary is dead — "Only some special types of mercenaries can regenerate." Inside it, death is a training cost. An NPC hired at level 10 can be ground up into something dangerous in the time it takes a floor to collapse.

It is also where Carl discovers what he actually bought with his 100,000-gold coupon: Splash Zone is a powerful water mage, Bucket Boy is a healer, Doctor Bones is a level-90 Skin Skellie Bard with crowd-control spells that turn enemies into minions. See The Penis Parade Crew.

docs.title: The sluggalo scheme
docs.text:
The arcade is the engine behind the book's most dubious piece of army-building. Carl locks the Penis Parade crew inside it with Doctor Bones, who carries an improved version of Carl's Super Spreader spell:

"They're not punk rock. They're Sluggalos. And I only infected one of them. Doctor Bones. He has the same Super Spreader spell as I do, but his is better. I can only do it on one person once per hour. He infected the others all at the same time, and then he cast a spell on the slugs so they're not so hostile after they come out."

Because the slugs are born inside the arcade, they regenerate there like any other arcade-born mercenary, and they can be levelled the same way. Roughly forty of them come out — mostly levels 20–30, with a handful of 50s — and the strongest are housed in the newly upgraded 100-slot barracks, "which they were apparently trashing." The weakest are sent out the door in waves to soak up demons.

Carl's Conscript spell is the other half of the trick, and he is honest about its limits: "It makes them fight on our side, sort of. It doesn't really change their attitude, and they can be rebellious. It's kinda like turning them into totems."

Elle's assessment of the whole operation, once she works out why Carl wanted the barracks upgrade: "Of all the fucked up shit you've done to NPCs, I'm pretty sure this is the worst."

Between hires and sluggalos, the arcade is a mercenary multiplier: the reason Carl's instruction to every party is "Make sure every individual team has as much mercenary space as they can. We're gonna fill every spot."

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: The Penis Parade Crew
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: Male strip club on the top floor of the Desperado Club — and, from Book 6, Carl's standing infantry company
  • Doubles as: The front door of the Guild of Suffering, and an unlisted Meat Shields branch run from Rosemarie's table
  • Hired: 13 male dancers plus Doctor Bones and Bucket Boy, on a two-floor mercenary contract for 100,000 gold — the exact value of Carl's coupon
  • Why: Because the alternative was the crew being reassigned to Larracos and fielded against Carl in Faction Wars
  • Sister clubs: Bitches (women, top floor); Penis Palace and Girls of Ill Refute (middle floor)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Penis Parade is the seedier of the Desperado Club's two male strip clubs, and Donut's favourite place in the dungeon. Book 6 turns it into something else entirely: the crew walks out of a burning nightclub and becomes the nucleus of Carl's Faction Wars infantry.

The club as Carl first sees it: a naked, mohawked forest troll gyrating on stage twirling a war club "with the enthusiasm of a majorette tripping on ecstasy," drunk elf and dwarf NPCs pelting him with gold coins, a skinny crocodilian kid scrambling after the coins with a bucket, and a skeleton in a golden crown DJing from a booth in the shadows. There is no pole.

Per Astrid's arrangement, the dancers here were never supposed to be this good. Carl's read:

"I think the men in the Penis Parade on this floor are supposed to be like that. Like super, uh, unqualified. But they're not. Well, some are. When Astrid ended up with the job as the assistant manager of the club, she made certain her two sons were safe and got them a gig at the Penis Parade where she could watch over them."

docs.title: Named members
docs.text: Name Species / class Notes Damascus Steel Ifrit, level 75 Assistant lead dancer; Guild of Suffering member; Astrid and Hamed's son. Does not leave with the crew Anaconda Quarter naga, level 75 Lead dancer, Donut's favourite; Damascus's brother Author Steve Rowland Forest Troll, level 50 Fights with a club; balances it on a fingertip for ten seconds, per Donut. Killed on-page during the book's final battle — a crab grabs his arm, a portal opens, and the troll is sucked into hell screaming Dong Quixote Human, level 45 Elderly; audibly pumps himself up on-shift ("He let out a breath, and half of his muscles turned to flab"). Insists on fighting with a full-length lance despite having no horse Gluteus Maxx "Short, hairy muscle man thing" Twin war gauntlets; per Donut, "Gluteus can break things with his butt! You get a mob's head in there, and it's game over" Splash Zone Otter A genuinely powerful water mage Bucket Boy Crocodilian, level 10 The kid who collects thrown tips. Turns out to be a healer Doctor Bones Skin Skellie Bard, level 90 The club's announcer and DJ, never a dancer. Has multiple crowd-control spells, including one that converts enemies into minions, and a Super Spreader spell better than Carl's own

docs.title: The hire
docs.text:
After Astrid's death and the vorpal rampage, Damascus refuses to leave but demands Carl take everyone else:

"The club is going to be closed for remodeling after this. It's happened before. With my mother dead, they'll assign a new assistant manager. There'll be a restructuring. They'll kick us out... The new management is going to reassign them to the Larracos level. Or worse. If you don't take them now, you'll end up fighting against them on the ninth floor."

Rosemarie the dwarf — secretly the manager of the club's unlisted Meat Shields branch — approves the contract on the spot: the whole crew, two floors, 100,000 gold.

"The 13 male strippers plus that skeleton DJ guy and the crocodilian Bucket Boy kid from the Penis Parade were already in the barracks. They'd transferred outside and to the front door of our personal space the moment we hired them."

Only the men of the Penis Parade were eligible. The women from Bitches, and both the male and female clubs on the middle floor — the Penis Palace and Girls of Ill Refute ("Not repute with a P") — are left behind. Damascus had already noted that "the pricks at the Palace won't have us."

docs.title: As a fighting unit
docs.text:
Housed in the guild barracks and trained in the Mercenary Arcade, the crew turns into a real infantry company over the back half of the floor. They are also the delivery mechanism for Carl's sluggalo scheme: Carl infects Doctor Bones with Super Spreader, Bones infects the rest of the crew simultaneously and casts a spell to keep the resulting slugs non-hostile, and the locked training room fills with roughly forty new bodies.

One hard limitation Carl notes: mercenaries born in the arcade regenerate there, but the hired crew do not have that protection outside it. "I'm pretty sure if any of the stripper guys die outside of the training arcade, they die for real. Only some special types of mercenaries can regenerate." The death of Author Steve Rowland proves it.

By the end of the book they are simply part of the team — moving off toward their barracks with everyone else, Dong Quixote quiet and grieving for his friend, while Carl notes he'll have to talk to him.

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: The Pineapple Cabaret
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: Hidden pocket dimension built as a permanent sanctuary for NPCs and mobs fleeing the dungeon — the book's central escape-hatch MacGuffin
  • Built by: Two former crawlers, Herot (16th-edition cookbook author — see The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook and Game Mechanics) and Menerva (no prior appearance in the series)
  • Cover story: The never-visited seventeenth floor — an officially "ticked box" the showrunners believe is a normal, if unused, dungeon level
  • Known access routes: The Desperado Club casino's Wheel of Fortune "Nothing" spot, and a cleaner-bot/personal-shop-interface exploit discovered mid-book
  • Currently infested by: A Shadow Mimic presence (see Species) and a remnant of the Ogre Imperium, contested alongside the War Mage Rebellion and a third faction Mitch calls "Cock-A-Doodle-Do"
  • Confirmed evacuees: Li Na (first, as the test case), then 227 additional volunteers (228 total, not including support staff)
  • Status: Open thread — the party never confirms the Cabaret is fully secured, nor whether leaving the dungeon cures anything

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Pineapple Cabaret is Book 8's answer to a question the series has been circling since the Open Intellect Pacifist Network's reveal in Book 6: is there any way out of the crawl that doesn't require winning or dying? For NPCs and mobs — who, unlike crawlers, have no indenture countdown and no Syndicate citizenship path — the answer the book offers is this pocket dimension: a permanent, hidden sanctuary built generations ago and kept secret from the AI and the showrunners alike.

The name is first heard in passing, offered by the AI (wearing Growler Gary's body) to the orc princess Formidable as a banishment option — "Backstage at the Pineapple Cabaret. Not the cabaret itself." Its real nature isn't unpacked until Akuma, tortured for information by Elle McGibbons and Donut, gives it up under duress in the book's first half. See Akuma and Elle McGibbons for that interrogation scene in full rather than duplicated here.

docs.title: Origins: Herot, Menerva, and the Seventeenth Floor
docs.text:
Per Akuma, two former crawlers — Herot, already known to this wiki as the skink 16th-edition cookbook author who campaigned for waking NPCs up via his Worn Path Method, and Menerva, not previously named in the series — discovered that mobs and NPCs were supposed to be periodically "recycled" between seasons for their own sake, but were instead being reused and exploited indefinitely because proper recycling was expensive and poorly audited:

Akuma, Book 8

"The dungeon is full of mobs who know their own nature. Everything is broken. It's all accelerating... but these two former crawlers, Herot and Menerva, their exploit is a way for us, the NPCs, to survive. But you crawlers can use it, too."

Their solution was to build a fake dungeon floor — the seventeenth, never opened to any crawler — as bureaucratic cover, then quietly attach to it something the AI never noticed: an entire separate pocket dimension.

Akuma, under interrogation, Book 8

"They are, or were, trapped by design. They didn't want to be seen. The seventeenth floor is a front. They weren't just building the seventeenth floor. Attached to the floor is the only entrance to a pocket dimension they built. They were building an oasis, a place for mobs and NPCs to escape to. A world within a world. The two crawlers sacrificed the possibility of ever getting out to make a place where NPCs and mobs could permanently escape the horrors of the dungeon. That is the Pineapple Cabaret."

The seventeenth floor itself ("the Backstage Death Maze") is not the Cabaret proper but its staging ground — a training area where recovered NPCs and mobs, including the elevated Growler Gary the AI once wore as an avatar, grow stronger in preparation for the day crawlers might actually reach that far. Menerva runs operations there. Herot himself is on the far side, trapped inside the Cabaret dimension itself, where he retains a limited shop interface but no other real control.

Cross-reference to Book 6–7 cookbook lore

Herot's cookbook contributions (the Worn Path Method, his essay on self-aware NPCs) are already documented under Game Mechanics and The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook — not repeated here in full. This page covers only what Book 8 adds: that he is still alive and secretly running the Cabaret.

docs.title: Access
docs.text: Akuma describes exactly two known ways in, both discovered or exploited within Book 8 itself:

docs.title: The Wheel of Fortune "Nothing" Spot
docs.text: The Desperado Club casino's Wheel of Fortune game has a two-space result called "the Nothing." Per Akuma, it had previously let their ally Pontiff jump safely into a stasis holding area connected to the Cabaret. This is the route Mitch (see Species: Shadow Mimics and Mitch) uses to send Chris Andrews, Britney Proskurina, and Louis Santiago through — a jump whose actual destination is never confirmed on-page; the book's final interlude instead finds Louis and Chris in Sheol, met by Britney, Pontiff, and a demon calling himself Forkith (see Supporting Cast), with no explanation for the diversion. With the Nothing itself broken (a Book 7 development), Akuma warns this route no longer opens directly onto the Cabaret but into "some sort of catchall holding area" that Herot can pull people out of manually — the same mechanism used to originally recruit NPCs for the seventeenth floor.

docs.title: The Cleaner-Bot / Shop-Interface Exploit
docs.text:
The route the party actually uses is stranger. Herot has a standing purchase order buying up every Cleaner Bot upgrade sold anywhere in the dungeon's personal-space shop system — which is why crawlers everywhere had been complaining the upgrade was suddenly unavailable due to "overwhelming demand." Using his limited shop-interface access from inside the Cabaret, Herot can empty a purchased Cleaner Bot's contents directly into the Cabaret's space:

Carl, working out the mechanism

"Basically, Li Na gets sucked into the cleaner bot, the cleaner bot gets put up for sale, Herot buys it, and he empties her out inside of the other place. And now Li Na has left the game because this Cabaret place is outside the playing field. She'll be considered to have been 'lost.'"

Capacity is limited and expensive: the first bot used holds only about fifty people, and Herot cannot re-list a used bot for thirty days due to a standard dungeon-upgrade cooldown. A second, larger bot — borrowed from another crawler, Bobby Montague — fits 105 more. The system itself frames anyone who goes through this way as having been "lost," not killed, which is what makes the whole plan survivable in the first place.

docs.title: Current Occupants and the Three-Way Struggle
docs.text:
By the time the party reaches out to Herot, the Cabaret is not the peaceful refuge it was built to be. It has been overrun by two hostile forces:

  • The Ogre Imperium — per Akuma, "a long-forgotten plotline that had gotten binned because the ogres were made too intelligent and they had immediately figured out that they were trapped in a dungeon." A remnant of this abandoned storyline has apparently persisted inside the Cabaret for "several seasons."
  • Shadow Mimics — see Species: Shadow Mimics. Mitch, dying, claims his kind wanted captured crawlers "for the Cabaret" specifically.

Mitch's dying testimony frames the occupation as a genuine three-way contest for control of "the dungeon back door" — the Cabaret's access point — between the War Mage Rebellion, the Ogre Imperium, and a faction he names only as "Cock-A-Doodle-Do," a name never explained or repeated elsewhere in the text:

Mitch, Book 8

"We needed some of you. We needed you for the Cabaret. The war mages, the ogres, and Cock-A-Doodle-Do. They all vie for control of the dungeon back door. With some of you, we could control it all."

The War Mage Rebellion (led by Akuma) wants the party's help clearing the Cabaret out specifically so it can be used as an exit — see The War Mage Rebellion for how that alliance plays out on Akuma's side.

docs.title: Li Na and the 227
docs.text:
Li Na is sent through first, alone, as the test case for the cleaner-bot method — both to escape her permanent no-healing condition (a Book 7 consequence of the Ring of Divine Suffering) and to prove the exploit works before risking anyone else. Mordecai rigs a signal system using a potted cactus tied to her life and location; a single bloomed flower means she made it safely.

Once confirmed safe, the guild sends a much larger wave:

Imani, Book 8

"It went smoothly. Your cleaner bot could only fit forty people, but the one from Bobby Montague, the Illusionist guy with the tall hair, managed to fit 105. The total number sent to the Pineapple Cabaret is 227, not including Na. Zhang, Tran, Daniel, Archie, Randall 3. All gone."

That puts the confirmed total at 228, including Li Na. Mordecai builds a "Garden of Deliverance" — over two hundred individually-tied potted plants, one per volunteer — as the only way the guild can track who lives, dies, or gets out, since "even the showrunners can't see what's going on in there." Eligibility is strictly limited: no god-worshippers (entering would allegedly trigger an automatic smite, per Akuma — though Carl is never able to confirm whether that's a real mechanic or a lie meant to keep certain crawlers out), no fairies or flying classes, nobody whose survival depends on dungeon magic (Louis's gill surgery, Chris's rock-elemental physiology), and no one whose race's behavior outside an enhancement zone is unknown (Donut, Florin). See Li Na for her own arc in full.

Confirmed: safe arrival, not a cure

Book 8 confirms only that Li Na and the 227 volunteers after her reached the Cabaret alive. Nothing in the text confirms the permanent no-healing condition, or any other dungeon-inflicted condition, is actually cured, reduced, or otherwise changed by leaving the dungeon this way — that remains an open, unconfirmed hope.

docs.title: Official Position (The Showrunners' Denial)
docs.text:
The exploit becomes public enough within the season that Borant is forced to address it on the record, disclaiming any responsibility:

Book 8, in-universe broadcast notice

"Also, I have been asked to directly address this so-called Pineapple Cabaret exploit many of you are using to shirk your duties as a crawler. We, the showrunners, do not endorse any such methods and we are not responsible for anything that may happen to crawlers who venture into unauthorized areas of the World Dungeon infrastructure."

The system AI itself volunteers its own warning rather than blocking the attempt outright. It is tucked into the completion text for an entirely unrelated quest, delivered in the same stretch of pages in which the party learns Li Na arrived safely: "Beware exits that seem too good to be true." By the epilogue, that line reads less like taunting and more like a warning nobody heeded — see The diverted jump under Open Threads, below.

docs.title: Open Threads
docs.text:
• Whether the Cabaret can ever open to Earth's surface. Herot's stated theory — that a second door might eventually be built from the Cabaret to the planet's surface — is never confirmed or attempted on-page. The AI's own caveat: "We might be able to create an exit from the Pineapple Cabaret to the surface of this planet. We might." Not attempted by the end of Book 8.
  • What happens to anyone still inside if the seventeenth floor collapses. Per the AI, anyone inside "when the floor collapses will be deemed 'lost.' But they won't be killed" — an explicit, unresolved risk hanging over all 228 evacuees. See Species: Shadow Mimics and Krakaren Prime for related open threads about the dungeon's other contested "back door" spaces.
  • The diverted jump. Chris, Britney, and Louis Santiago were sent through the casino's Nothing spot believing they were headed for the Cabaret; the epilogue instead shows Louis and Chris surfacing in Sheol. Whether this means the Cabaret route failed, was intercepted, or was never actually connected to their jump is left open — see Mitch.

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride, Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin, and Book 8: A Parade of Horribles.

docs.title: The Princess Posse Army
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Book: 7, This Inevitable Ruin — the Floor 9 Faction Wars army
  • Co-warlords: Carl and Princess Donut. Adjutant: Baroness Victory
  • Headquarters: the FUPA — the Fortress of Unyielding Power and Authority
  • Starting strength: 58 soldiers. Reinforcement: just over 50,000 former crawlers shipped in aboard the Homecoming Queen
  • Structure: seven numbered battalions (101st–107th) plus Special Operations Forces (SOFs)
  • Survivors at the end: about 28,000 of the 50,000 — "They had survived the dungeon, left, and they came back to die"

docs.title: Origins
docs.text:
The army begins as a farce. Carl and Donut arrive on Floor 9 with the system warning them their "army is at suboptimal force levels. Current army size: 58 soldiers," and "You have no officers in your army!" Officers can only be created by physically touching the recruit — a rule Donut discovers immediately and complains about: "It says we have to physically touch someone to make them an officer! That's not fair! I was going to make Katia a general!"

The force that actually fights the war arrives from outside: Tipid and Rosetta bring in just over 50,000 former crawlers recruited by Doctor Hu's call and carried down on the Homecoming Queen — see The Crawler Project and The Open Intellect Pacifist Network. Each of the eight opposing sponsored teams simultaneously receives about 20,000 hired mercenaries.

docs.title: Ranks
docs.text:
Donut goes through the room touching everyone in turn to make officers. The hierarchy is built by hand, mostly by Florin:

Rank Notes Warlord Carl and Donut, co-warlords Adjutant Baroness Victory — a system role, not an army rank General Florin's own rank after he tinkers with the naming (it began as "War Leader III," then "Colonel," then simply "General"). Generals may recruit and grant any officer rank below their own, and may command large detached formations. Most of the core group hold this rank Colonel Battalion command (e.g. Colonel Boomer, Colonel Tipid). Carl gives Prepotente this rank on joining — "My first instinct was to be a dick and give Pony the rank of Legionnaire, but I ended up making him a Colonel" Sergeant First Class The Penis Parade strippers' rank; allows recruiting and commanding base troops Chief / Corporal Construction crews and crawler specialists get sergeant/chief so they can alter the camp; corporals lead individual teams Legionnaire The rank-and-file — notably the sluggalos, who are formally redesignated Legionnaires

Florin initially named the sergeant tier "Adjutant" and had to change it, because it collided with the existing Adjutant class. Officer slots are capped: "You only get a limited number of officers."

docs.title: The seven battalions
docs.text:
Unit Designation Commander Role and details 101st Crocodiles Florin The main maneuver force; holds the northern front against the Operatic and later the orc border. Leads the charge that stops an armoured column and captures two Weeper tanks 102nd Bulwark Tran Defensive mages and fortification engineers, with a thin layer of hand-to-hand specialists. Builds the forward positions and trench lines; holds the southern naga border 103rd Recon Legionnaires Bodi Scouts and recon. Later used for corpse-delivery and as the diversionary force against the Madness castle 104th Naughty Little Piggies Tipid Base defence: scout towers, early-warning posts, and the castle perimeter 105th Scream Warriors Jurgen Shock infantry. Split into two half-battalions trained as a rapid-deploy force — five mages chanting the same spell for thirty straight hours can mass-teleport an entire battalion, something Rosetta and Mordecai say has only happened a handful of times in Faction Wars history 106th Bloody Leeches Colonel Boomer Warriors, trap mechanics and thieves; the reserve/counterattack battalion 107th White Dragons (Urban Defense) Li Na Holds Shanty Town, the donut-shaped ring settlement on the lip of Larracos, and bankrupts the treasury building its defences

Colonel Boomer is a grizzled elf survivor of one of the earliest seasons of Dungeon Crawler World — "someone had taken the world's fattest bulldog, pickled it for about 5,000 years, gave him elf ears, and then shoved a cigar in his mouth." He is put in charge of the 106th by Tipid, and "the soldiers all loved him."

docs.title: Special Operations Forces (SOFs)
docs.text: Squad Role The Frothing Tunnel Moles Sappers and tunnellers. Their gnome-sized members go down holes cut at regular intervals into the trench walls; one wears "a massive, poorly-drawn mole tattoo on his chest" reading The Frothing Tunnel Moles. Justice Light later directs volunteer sappers to "go find Colonel Tipid and tell him you're trained sappers, and maybe you can join up with the Frothing Tunnel Moles" The Beefy Boys Base-defence mages whose sole job is keeping every wall buff and base shield topped off. Named as a joke by their leader Lonnie after someone told him to "beef up the wall defenses." They are half-dead when the Madness raid the FUPA, and Lonnie is mind-controlled into switching off the interior protection stacks before he is killed The Tenner Wraiths A squad within the 103rd Recon Legionnaires, named on the elves' neck tattoos

docs.title: Patches, tattoos and mottos
docs.text:
The army develops its own iconography almost overnight.

The 103rd Recon Legionnaires' neck tattoo: "a large, flaming skull that was some sort of human/cat hybrid thing that looked like it was straight from a 1980's skateboard deck. Surrounding the skull in large letters in Syndicate Standard read the words 'Princess Posse or Death.'" The battalion name is added at the bottom, and below that the squad name, The Tenner Wraiths. Griffin volunteers the other side of his neck for a second one if he's transferred, and the front for a third.

The 105th Scream Warriors' logo: "a drawing of a screaming girl who looked suspiciously like the mascot for the Wendy's restaurant chain wearing a Viking helmet with only one horn." Their merchandise also carries "a crudely drawn, bloody child berserker character holding an axe... a little girl that had to be eight years old," and the unit's motto:

"We bleed when the job's done."

The 104th Naughty Little Piggies fly a battalion flag; Dong Quixote carries one on the tip of a war lance when reassigned to them.

'Fuck the cheese sticks' is army slang, not a unit motto
