"Cheese stick" is what the whole Princess Posse army calls enemy soldiers. Carl: "I had no idea where the term 'Cheese Stick' had originated, but it had spread through the army like wildfire. It's what everyone called the enemy soldiers. I'd seen a few 'Fuck the Cheese Sticks' tattoos already." It is shouted as a battle cry going over the top ("'Fuck the cheese sticks' someone else yelled as they, too, propelled themselves onto No Man's Land"), used casually by Boomer and Florin in dispatches, and is the subject of a running argument with Samantha, who insists it should be "cheese dicks." The only quoted unit motto in the book is the 105th's.

docs.title: Attached and irregular forces
docs.text:
• The sluggalos ("Legionnaires") — Carl's Book 6 mercenary infantry, carried straight into Faction Wars as the army's mass rank-and-file. Their tactical doctrine is unchanged: "they'd swarm the castle face-first, inexpertly killing and getting themselves splattered like a bunch of idiots." They are fiercely protective of Imani, and chase Prepotente across naga territory on foot after he insults her, nearly wrecking Operation: Snake Pit. Sneaky Tyler C is the lead sluggalo; Kandy "Bigs" Newton gets credit for killing the Sepsis Whore. The system counts them as a distinct class of NPC, which makes them immune to several area effects that hit everyone else. See The Mercenary Arcade
  • The Penis Parade crew — now officers. The strippers are all made Sergeant First Class, and Dong Quixote is reassigned into the 104th for the Madness assault. Splash Zone, Doctor Bones and Gluteus Maxx fight on Carl's personal assault team. See The Penis Parade Crew
  • Prepotente — joins late as a Colonel after an extended, furious refusal
  • Team Retribution — the allied NPCs, coordinated through Britney, who "has become quite close with Juice Box" and works "multiple lines of communication with the skill of a seasoned police dispatcher." See Team Retribution
  • Justice Light — works semi-independently beneath the FUPA on a trans-dimensional trap and a buried "antenna," using sluggalo labour because they "didn't seem to mind the idea of accidentally tripping traps and getting themselves skewered"

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Rev-Up Moonshine Company
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: In-dungeon pyramid-scheme moonshine business
  • Floor: 2
  • Leadership: Krakaren (see the Krakaren Clone boss page) and her "downline consultants"
  • Workforce: Clurichauns (rank-and-file) and Laminak fairies (Elite Consultants)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Rev-Up presents itself as a multi-level-marketing opportunity ("Rev-Up. Make Money. Be Your Own Boss. Move to the next floor down") staffed almost entirely by exploited fae workers. A recovered recruitment pamphlet is transparently a pyramid scheme — literally illustrated with a pyramid captioned "It's not a pyramid!" — and advertises a discontinued product line, "Rev-Up Smoothies," crossed out and marked "Discontinued."

docs.title: Product & Distillery
docs.text: The company's flagship product is Rev-Up Toilet-Grade Moonshine, 180-proof liquor distilled using Brindle Grub slime trails and an undisclosed "proprietary source." It's sought after by drinking establishments on Floors 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, and 18. Drinking a 1.5oz swig inflicts the Shit-Faced debuff, has a 50% chance of 30-hour blindness, a 5% chance of instant death, and a 45% chance of permanently raising a random stat by two points.

docs.title: Labor Structure
docs.text:
• Clurichauns — rank-and-file distillery workers
  • Laminak Rev-Up Consultant Elites — the management tier; per their monster card, underlings who fall behind quota are punished by being forced to drink the product, with survivors "repurposed as workers for the filling room, or worse, as still engineers, working directly under Krakaren herself"

docs.title: Role in the Story
docs.text:
Carl improvises a "Rev-Up Immunity Smoothie" (moonshine blended with a dead laminak fairy) using a recipe found in the distillery, reviving the discontinued smoothie line's namesake to cure/ prevent the Taint, a mucus-borne infection inflicted by the Krakaren Clone boss.

Sourced from Book 1: The Apocalypse Will Be Televised.

docs.title: The Stage Performance Guild
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: Hidden, task-based guild — teaches performance/showmanship skills
  • Location: Behind a secret door inside the Lollipop, a karaoke bar in Floor 10's Over City hub (Book 8)
  • Entrance requirement: Complete one of a handful of secretly-marked karaoke songs from start to finish with the performance gauge ("the needle") staying in the green the entire time
  • Guildmaster: Porky, the left half of the split mantaur Corcunda
  • Discovered/entered by: Carl and Princess Donut, singing a-ha's "Take On Me" mid-bar-brawl
  • Structurally parallel to: The Cartography and Calligraphy Guilds inside Club Vanquisher (Book 7), both secretly run by Milk

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Stage Performance Guild is Book 8's version of a pattern the wiki has already seen once: a guild hidden in plain sight inside a members' club, gatekept by an obscure trigger nobody thinks to try, and secretly staffed by an NPC whose real identity ties into the book's emotional core. Where Book 7's Cartography and Calligraphy Guilds turned out to be run by Carl's own sister, Book 8's Stage Performance Guild turns out to be run by Porky — the other half of Corcunda, the half-mantaur reunion-and-tragedy storyline running in parallel across the same floor.

docs.title: The Entrance Exam
docs.text:
The trigger is a secret mark on select songs in the karaoke bar's binder-bound song list, explained to Carl by the bartender Tipid:

Tipid, Book 8

"There's a secret mark on a handful of songs. If you pick the right song, it'll engage the entrance sequence for the guild... Only those who get the green needle the whole time will be able to enter. So if you want in, you gotta sing."

Carl and Donut's attempt happens under the worst possible conditions: mid-song, the bar's DJ is stabbed by a drunk unicorn NPC named Dwight, and the karaoke performance becomes the backdrop to a full brawl breaking out across the room — glass, fireballs, and a dinosaur (Mongo) all crossing the stage while Carl, wearing a Gelded Choirboy scroll effect that spikes his voice an octave, sings a-ha's "Take On Me" opposite Donut. Both performance gauges stay pinned in the green through the entire song despite the chaos, and Carl's chimes with an extra flourish ("little flames coming out of the top") that Donut's does not — a discrepancy she refuses to let go of.

Book 8

"Congratulations, Carl. You have been granted permanent access to the Stage Performance Guild! New Achievement! Sing for your supper!"

The reward text is characteristically snide about the whole endeavor ("The next thing you know, you'll be earning a third of a cent per stream on Spotify..."), but the mechanical payoff is real: discovering the guild this way permanently reveals other hidden, entrance-gated guilds on Carl's map whenever he's near one. Donut, singing her own verses correctly, still FAILS the exam outright — an outcome she immediately declares off-limits for future discussion ("We are never going to mention this again... I do love that song, though").

docs.title: Porky, the Guildmaster
docs.text:
Behind the secret door is a full theater — "a whole damn theater with red velvet chairs that looked as if it could fit five hundred people" — dusty and unused, with a single spotlight trained on the guild's sole occupant: Porky, lying on the stage floor with a stuck zipper on his containment suit.

Porky is the left half of Corcunda, split from his other half (Corky) years earlier by the spell Split Personality and never reunited until this floor's central quest resolves it. He has been running the guild alone and unnoticed for an unstated length of time, offering services and skill-ups to anyone who manages to pass the entrance test:

Porky, Book 8

"Welcome to the stage performance guild. I can see you have some rudimentary levels in performance skills, but the fact you were able to gain entrance suggests you have a lot of raw talent. And for helping me today, I will throw a few free skill levels onto your Razzmatazz skill."

Porky is fluent in showmanship theory even in total isolation — his answer to Donut's questions about "bringing the house down" ("Any performance is 10% talent, 90% presence... You want them to limp out of the theater after you're done with them, gasping for breath as if you've just made love to their very soul") reads as a man who has had nothing to do for a very long time but think about his craft.

Carl uses his discovery of Porky to drive the book's other major Floor 10 storyline: reuniting him with Corky before the race that would otherwise kill his other half. See Corcunda for the reunion, Grull's smiting of the newly-whole Corcunda for religious apostasy accrued during the years apart, and her and Dong Quixote's joint death — covered there in full rather than duplicated on this page.

docs.title: Structurally Parallel to the Cartography and Calligraphy Guilds
docs.text:
The Stage Performance Guild is a direct structural echo of Book 7's Cartography and Calligraphy Guilds, hidden inside Club Vanquisher and secretly run by the same guildmaster, Milk — Carl's own biological sister. Both pairs of guilds share the same shape: an obscure, easy-to-miss entrance condition, a near-total absence of patrons ("She never bothered to hide the papers in the back where crawlers wouldn't see them... What was the point?"), and a lonely NPC guildmaster whose personal story turns out to matter more than the guild's nominal function. Carl draws the comparison himself, internally, while talking to Porky in his spartan backstage quarters: "I wondered how long Milk had spent alone in that lonely guild. This was an NPC, but still..."

No dedicated page exists yet for the Cartography and Calligraphy Guilds; see Dungeon Factions: Other Book 7 dungeon groups for their existing entry.

docs.title: Aftermath: An Open Question
docs.text:
Once reunited into a single Corcunda, Porky ceases to exist as a separate identity — and Corcunda dies minutes later, smitten by Grull for religious apostasy accrued during the split. Book 8 never states what becomes of the Stage Performance Guild, its "Razzmatazz" skill line, or its hidden-guild-detection reward after its sole guildmaster is gone. Whether the guild remains accessible, closes, or transfers to new management is left unresolved.

Sourced from Book 8: A Parade of Horribles.

docs.title: Team Retribution
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Who they are: the NPCs of Larracos — the tenth Faction Wars team, created by Carl's Book 6 action item and named by the NPCs themselves
  • Book 6 name: the Home Team. "Team Retribution" is their own choice
  • Co-warlords: Juice Box (a changeling) and Sir Ferdinand (a cat)
  • Adjutant: Drick, an "elf outworlder" who is not really an elf
  • Role in the game: the defending team. They hold Larracos; every other team must take it
  • Alliance: The Good Guys, with the Princess Posse — the only alliance on the board that never breaks
  • Fate: voluntarily forfeit at the very end, handing the Princess Posse the win

docs.title: Origin and standing
docs.text:
Cascadia's opening broadcast introduces them dismissively — "those ungrateful NPC upstarts" — and then sets out their unique position:

"Anyway, there are ten teams total. Nine attacking teams and one defending team, the NPCs, who have decided to call themselves Team Retribution. They are headquartered in Larracos. Everyone else is spread out like a pie with Larracos in the center."

Their soldiers are marked on the map as white dots with a green outline. Crucially, Team Retribution's allies also get to stay inside the city when the ceasefire expires — which is why Donut's snap acceptance of their truce offer, minutes into the floor, matters so much.

Ferdinand's warlord access exists only as a workaround: "Ferdinand was added because the system didn't allow Juice Box access to the warlord menu."

docs.title: The Larracos Defence Force
docs.text:
The city's standing military, commanded by War Leader Arief, a level 80 Semeru dwarf:

War Leader Arief. Level 80 Semeru Dwarf. Commander of the Larracos Defense Force Infantry. This is an ally. As you are both officers, attacking him will automatically negate your peace treaty if there are witnesses.

Arief greets Carl and Donut at the Larracos College of Magic with a deep bow — "Honored Warlords Carl and Princess Donut. It is an honor to have you within our borders" — apparently unaware, or unbothered, that they are the two who flooded his city. Every Semeru in the force carries the permanent Despondent debuff from Ysalte's death: a 15% hit to all stats and 10% extra damage taken from worshippers of other deities.

docs.title: The Jatismara
docs.text:
Semeru who remember previous crawl seasons. Arief, on his uncle:

"I don't remember this, but there are some with the memory quickened. I believe I am new, as are most of us. But some have persisted. My uncle remembers dozens of seasons now. Not as many as Juice Box, but he's one of the Jatismara, and he sits upon her war council."

That single sentence is the entirety of what the series says about them — see Semeru Dwarves.

docs.title: The changeling network
docs.text:
Juice Box is a changeling herself, and changelings form the team's intelligence apparatus and a chunk of its officer corps. When reinforcements crash the courtyard late in the book:

"It was a horror show of monstrosities of all shapes and sizes, and for a terrifying moment, I thought we were about to get overrun. But then I saw the indicators over them. Team Retribution. And not just that, but officers. Changelings."

Book 7 also introduces a formal classification — "class A and B NPC changelings" — which matters because Justice Light miscalculates by assuming procedurally generated NPCs (his sluggalos) can't be copied by them.

docs.title: Dwarven diggers
docs.text: The Semeru's giant excavation machines: "basically a boxy, god-sized robot covered in all directions with spiral digging arms and goblin-murder-dozer-like spinning wheels," crewed by a pair of Semeru in a shoulder control panel. Tunnels criss-cross the whole floor to move them.

docs.title: The general citizenry
docs.text: The college campus is staffed by "Elves, draconians, and fairies, along with a smattering of several other races," all flagged as Team Retribution soldiers. When Juice Box finally commits ground troops to Shanty Town, they are "mostly Semeru dwarves and the regular citizens of Larracos."

docs.title: The alliance in practice
docs.text:
Relations with the Princess Posse start cordial and stay guarded. Juice Box marries the crawler Louis Santiago in a small ceremony that formalises the crawler/NPC alliance. Britney becomes the standing liaison — "Britney will coordinate all of our communication with Team Retribution. It seems she's become quite close with Juice Box. She's gotten very good at being a go-between, working multiple lines of communication with the skill of a seasoned police dispatcher."

But the NPCs never entirely trust the crawlers, and Justice Light says so to Juice Box's face:

"You are distrustful of us former crawlers. I understand that. You fear we crawlers will sacrifice you to save ourselves, and you have positioned yourselves to protect against that."

docs.title: Their action items
docs.text:
Ferdinand's two emergency action items are among the most consequential in the book, and both are delivered in his own register. The first shuts down the live feeds:

"Because them alien cunts on other floors are being little bitches and cheating, we propose that nobody in the dungeon, including those pricks partying it up in that centipede's asshole, be allowed to watch any outside feeds for the remainder of this little game."

It is approved immediately. The loophole that survives it — every off-world team buys the galactic news media centre upgrade and communicates by repeatedly renaming its own channels — is Odette's scoop at the warlord council.

The second, late in the book, keeps the summoned gods on the board:

"Gods that appear during Faction Wars don't gotta go home right away. Uh, Juice Box told me to say a bunch of other stuff too but now I can't remember it all."

docs.title: Their military record
docs.text: Team Retribution take both the Bone Clan's and the Dream's throne rooms during the endgame — neither of which Carl planned — and inherit all of the Skull Empire's assets when the War Mage Rebellion kills Stalwart, because the war mages were not an active team. Juice Box also possesses Louis to drop the bomb that kills Warlord Fang of the Reavers.

docs.title: The forfeit
docs.text:
Agatha's third action item makes the endgame zero-sum: every soldier and warlord of a defeated team now drops dead where they stand. With both teams unable to coexist, Juice Box and Ferdinand simply walk off the board:

System Message: Both Warlords Ferdinand and Juice Box have left the realm. Under the current ruleset, they have abandoned their posts and have forfeited their position.

System Message: Team Retribution has been defeated.

System Message: The Princess Posse has won Faction Wars.

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: The Changeling Principals
docs.text: A secretive cult sect of Changelings, disguised as the guard ranks of Hump Town's Dromedarian population on Floor 5. Their public role — negotiating and maintaining the town's "collateral" arrangement with the Dirigible Gnomes to prevent bombing — masks their real, generations-long agenda: obtaining a plant-based cure for Compression Sickness, the increasingly common birth defect afflicting their species.

docs.title: Leadership and Method
docs.text:
Henrik, posing as Hump Town's elder statesman, leads the sect. Believing the ghost Quetzalcoatlus is the only living knowledge-holder of the needed spell, the Principals maintain the gnome hostage Wynne — a Flesh Mechanic capable of temporarily giving a ghost physical form — specifically to force him to give Quetzalcoatlus flesh so a Principal could touch her and learn the cure. Wynne cooperated under drug coercion (via a psychoactive mushroom) for years before resisting, at which point the Principals began forcibly overdosing him.

The hostage arrangement itself runs through a pair of magically-linked pocket watches — one of the three pieces of the Gate of the Feral Gods — exchanged daily with Commandant Kane of the Wasteland as proof Wynne remains alive.

docs.title: Collapse
docs.text: The plan unravels when a rival crawler group (led by the hostile "D-Bag Geek" Low Thi) kills Wynne before the Principals can force the resurrection spell out of him, triggering an in-universe "Cockblock" achievement for the killers and starting a countdown to the gnomes' retaliatory bombing of the town. Henrik and the surviving Principals — including a Level 49 lieutenant named Svern, killed by Carl in a single hit via Talon Strike — abandon the hostage plot afterward and retreat into the Necropolis of Anser itself, attempting a "Plan B or C" to reach Quetzalcoatlus directly by way of the drowned Akula submarine wreck. Henrik is ultimately killed there by Quetzalcoatlus herself, and every remaining Principal dies in the necropolis alongside the crawlers sent to clear it.

docs.title: Aftermath
docs.text:
• Carl and Katia impersonate Henrik and a resurrected, decoy version of Wynne to trick the gnomes into a face-to-face negotiation, using the ruse to ambush and destroy the airship Vahana and its crew mid-flight — see The Wasteland
  • Juice Box, Henrik's sister and the only Principal who openly sides with Carl's party, survives the floor and agrees to carry a hidden piece of the Gate through to Floor 6 in exchange for Carl's promise to try to bring surviving changelings down with him on future floors

Sourced from Book 4: The Gate of the Feral Gods.

docs.title: The Wasteland
docs.text: The military crew of the dirigible-gnome dreadnaught the Wasteland, the airborne antagonist faction of Floor 5's Air Quadrant. Once peaceful "sky garden" builders who tried to stay neutral above the world's conflicts, the Dirigible Gnomes militarized generations ago after hostile crawler-like "winged predators" arrived through a portal and refused to share the skies — repurposing their old ceremonial peace balloons (Legate Balloons, still recognizable by their black-and-gold stripes) into the war fleet Carl encounters.

docs.title: Leadership
docs.text:
• Commandant Kane — commands the Wasteland and personally orders the bombing of the Bactrian settlement after their hostage collateral (a pet pig) is killed; found dead in his own house at the hands of his own pet, Denise the Feral Goose Mother, shortly before Carl's party arrives.
  • Leon the Commissar — Kane's chief political officer and negotiator; a "master politician" who inspects hostage collateral in person and personally casts changeling-detection spells. Killed mid-air during Carl's decoy-negotiation ambush.
  • Crixus — Kane's sniper captain, armed with a wide-bore rifle firing Live Ammo Balls (clamshell munitions each containing a stasis-trapped Frenzied Gerbil). Killed by Katia mid-fight.
  • Bonnie — Kane's young daughter and the Wasteland's true final resident; recovered alive by Carl's party after the dreadnaught is destroyed.

docs.title: The Collateral System
docs.text: To keep towns from being bombed outright, the Wasteland maintains a hostage arrangement with each Dromedarian/Bactrian settlement, confirmed daily via a pair of magically-linked pocket watches — one of the three pieces of the Gate of the Feral Gods. Hostages are periodically inspected in person by Leon, who casts a spell to confirm they haven't been replaced by a Changeling.

docs.title: Downfall
docs.text: After the Changeling Principals' gnome hostage, Wynne, is killed by a rival crawler group, Carl exploits the collateral-verification ritual itself: Donut resurrects Wynne's corpse into a temporary zombie state, Katia disguises herself as both Wynne's undead body and the (already-dead) Henrik's corpse, and the trick convinces Leon to fly the group aboard the Vahana legate balloon under a false truce. Mid-flight, Carl's allied archers destroy the escort fleet with missiles while Donut's Hole spell drops Leon, Crixus, and the pilot out of the basket to their deaths; Carl then pilots the balloon directly at the Wasteland itself and fires the last of his missiles into its exposed underside before the party parachutes clear. The dreadnaught is destroyed in the resulting explosion, killing the bulk of its remaining crew — Carl gains two character levels from the kill count alone.

docs.title: Aftermath
docs.text:
• Bonnie survives the crash in the wreckage of the family "castle" (an ordinary suburban house kept aloft by a soul-crystal-powered balloon), guarded by the boss Denise; Carl and Donut adopt her into Hump Town's care afterward
  • Surviving gnomes who bail out or crash-land are hunted down individually over the following day, including a second, unexpected wave of gerbil-swarm retaliation — see Frenzied Gerbil
  • The house/castle's soul crystal and the second piece of the Gate of the Feral Gods (looted from Kane's corpse) both pass into Carl's possession afterward

Sourced from Book 4: The Gate of the Feral Gods.

docs.title: Factions & Organizations
docs.text: Interstellar governing and broadcast powers — the entities running the show, as distinct from groups encountered inside the dungeon itself (see Dungeon Factions) and from the peoples/species themselves (see Species). Full pages exist for factions with real plot weight in Book 1; everything else is listed below.

docs.title: Full pages
docs.text:
• Borant Corporation — current season operator; runs the dungeon as a broadcast
  • The Dark Hive — Circe Took's private mantis hunting corporation, distinct from the mantis government
  • Nebular Sin Patrol — nomadic religious cult that fields hunter-priests every season
  • The Nebulars / Nebular Balance — the parent religion behind the Sin Patrol: AI-worshipping, outwardly pacifist, and committed to eradicating every planet that could host a crawl
  • The Open Intellect Pacifist Network — Carl's sponsor, revealed in Book 6 to be former crawlers trying to destroy the crawl; by Book 8, renamed the Open Intellect Action Network, it seizes every major ship in Earth orbit in a single day
  • Long Haul Biological Waste Management Solutions — Crest corpse-disposal company, Donut's new sponsor, and owner of the Homecoming Queen
  • The Prism Kingdom — Empress D'Nadia's trade kingdom and its Book 6 heel turn
  • The Valtay Corporation — Book 6: steps back from production, then engineers an extinction event
  • The Syndicate Council — the real council, first shown in session in Book 6's epilogue
  • The Faction Wars Teams — all ten Floor 9 teams, their warlords, and the mass abdication the quarantine refused
  • The Faction Wars Campaign — Book 7: the Bloc, the Good Guys, the mid-book fracture, the full elimination order and the betrayals
  • The War Mage Rebellion — the "non-team entity" that a procedural ruling accidentally promoted to a warlord
  • The Crawler Project — Dr. Porthus Hu's advocacy non-profit, and the citizenship and healthcare rights it won for released crawlers
  • The Great Consensus — the anti-Syndicate isolationist philosophy spreading across the kua-tin, mantid and naga systems

docs.title: The Big Six
docs.text:
The system AI's own explicit taxonomy of every power group vying for control of or escape from the dungeon, delivered mid-fight during the Floor 10 Shadow Mimic ambush (see Mitch) after Akuma had already been circling the same framework earlier in the book. This is a worldbuilding/mechanics concept (the AI's own analytical framework for the endgame) rather than a faction in its own right, so the full quoted breakdown of all six groups — including the still-unidentified "Group Six" — lives on the Game Mechanics page rather than here, to avoid duplicating the same quotes in two places.

See Carl: Book 8 and Mitch for the scene itself, and Species: Shadow Mimics for how one member of Group Four is treated on its own dedicated page.

docs.title: Other Book 1 organizations
docs.text: Name Type Notes The Syndicate Interstellar government Sets the overarching legal framework (resource-reclamation law, the World Dungeon format itself); dispatches the "neutral observer AI" narrator Squim Conglomerate Rival season operator Runs a "battle royale-style" season instead of a structured dungeon; mentioned by Mordecai as less profitable than Borant's format Valtay Corporation Corporate system government Referenced via found tech in Book 1; in Book 2, destroys a Skull Empire royal yacht in retaliation for the death of their sponsored singer Manasa, escalating a bankruptcy-collection dispute with the kua-tin into open hostility. Becomes Carl's own sponsor in Book 3, after his Floor 4 fight with Gore-Gore the Mantaur; their slogan, "Keeping the Best of You Alive," ties to Book 1's revelation they're brain-parasite Intellect Hunters. Gifts Carl a permanent Neural Enhancer implant that lets him see through subspace portals — see The Iron Tangle Railway System. Book 5: wins a Syndicate ruling acquiring 51% ownership of the Borant Corporation mid-Floor-6, formally severing Borant from the kua-tin home-system government; the crawl itself keeps running under the same kua-tin production staff, but the sixth floor's own AI begins quietly disregarding Syndicate court rulings it disagrees with in the fallout — see Game Mechanics. Book 6: steps back from day-to-day production after the Floor 7 disaster, and then proposes an engineered extinction event as its "solution" to the quarantine — see The Valtay Corporation The Plenty Interstellar communications-technology company A real caprid (goat-like) species who invented the modern real-time subspace tunnel network, replacing Borant's older, slower communications relays — Borant's in-dungeon "Pooka," goat-like drug-den distributors, are a deliberately unflattering caricature of them. Book 5: sponsors Carl, Prepotente, and Miriam Dom directly; their children are shown at a CrawlCon art contest answering in creepy unison ("Judgment received"), and their own mythology includes a boogeyman figure, the Midnight Epicure ("the Caprid Who Devours the Sky"), whose ward-symbol doubles as a real anti-vampire/anti-lycanthrope charm The Krakaren (real species) Telepathic collective-mind species, sometimes called "the Apothecary" A real, galaxy-spanning hive-mind species capable of synthesizing substances from whatever they consume; per Mordecai, Borant's in-dungeon "Krakaren" bosses (drug dealers, moonshiners) are a hostile caricature of them, part of the same anti-Plenty propaganda campaign — see Dungeon Factions for the in-dungeon caricature itself. Book 5: sponsors Carl, Donut, and most of the rest of the top 10 as "the Apothecary"; a masked human-presenting spokeswoman appears in person at both a Floor 6 battlefield and Carl's CrawlCon panel, publicly egging him on against Circe Took — heavily implied to be coordinating with the Plenty toward Carl and Donut's survival. Book 6: the epilogue reveals the Apothecary runs many thousands of Residual agents seeded across Earth, all ordered to kill themselves if they fail to make it inside the dungeon — and that they are one side of a shadow war against the rival Residual faction that Agatha belongs to. Agatha obtained the Apothecary's informational feed and equipment by hunting down and killing one of those agents and taking over its body. Her own side numbers a handful against the Apothecary's thousands, and she concedes her competitors "were the only ones who ever had any sort of success so far"

docs.title: Other Book 2 organizations
docs.text: Name Type Notes Sensation Entertainment, Incorporated Independent production studio Produces the serialized drama Vengeance of the Daughter (Tsarina Signet's storyline); not Kua-Tin owned — the Kua-Tin are noted as generally bad at scripted drama Skull Empire Orc royal dynasty Ruled by King Rust; Prince Maestro is stripped of his title after the "Pork Boy" incident. Presumed killed alongside Queen Consort Ugloo in the Valtay yacht strike, but Book 3 reveals he survived — secretly smuggled into the dungeon by his brother beforehand — and resurfaces as Grull's sponsor during the Floor 4 Mimic Rex Death Challenge, humiliated by Carl a third time. Book 5: fields Floor 6 hunters (including the ill-fated "The Talent" and "Future Huntress"); Prince Maestro's ongoing Faction Wars franchise ownership is revealed to run through a Skull-Empire-linked subsidiary — see Game Mechanics — and the Empire is the only other faction besides Carl's own Princess Posse willing to vote in favor of removing Faction Wars' sponsor safety protocols The Prism Kingdom Small but influential trade-focused kingdom Ruled by Princess D'nadia (a Saccathian); formally condemns the Skull Empire's attack after it kills her friend Manasa. Book 5: D'Nadia — now Empress after her father's retirement — sponsors Donut, judges the Butcher's Masquerade's pet/talent contests in person, and claims one of two Faction Wars spots vacated when the Dreadnought Clan and the Burrowers both withdraw. Book 6: a full heel turn — sells Donut's sponsorship and burns all three Emergency Action Items trying to delete the Larracos NPCs, bar crawlers from Faction Wars, and delete Carl and Donut; all three rejected by the system. Now has its own page: The Prism Kingdom

docs.title: Other Book 5 organizations
docs.text: Name Type Notes The Dream Galaxy-spanning elf hunting organization Fields Floor 6 hunters (Akland, Chin'Dua) under family patriarch Epitome Tagg (son of Epitome Noflex); claims Louis Santiago as a personal target after a grudge involving Juice Box impersonating Noflex; runs a recreational "fantasy hunter camp" that feeds its real hunting roster The Burrowers Mantis system government The actual ruling/military mantis power, distinct from the private Dark Hive; historically performs poorly in Faction Wars; withdraws its Faction Wars spot entirely after Book 5's events, one of two openings claimed by the Prism Kingdom and Carl's new Princess Posse. Book 6: the AI reveals the timing — the mantis-led Burrower team "took their ball and went home the very same day" the fact that the mantises jettison unwanted infant AIs into a star became public, via a lawsuit brief. At the epilogue's emergency council session, Princess Formidable accuses them of having "sold the Kua-Tin a damaged and deranged AI and allowed it to be installed into the planet"; the mantid rep, silent until that moment, shouts "That is a lie!" and Formidable answers "Then why did you flee the system?" It is the Burrower rep who then proposes the decorum sanction that gets her muted — see The Syndicate Council The Crafters Hunter group Claims Elle McGibbons and Eva Sigrid as Floor 6 targets The Filigree Hunter group Operates near Skull-Empire-claimed territory on Floor 6; overlaps with Katia/Louis/Elle's group late in the book Society for the Eradication of Cocker Spaniels (Princess Posse Enterprises) Fan-founded advocacy nonprofit / Faction Wars sponsor Donut's in-universe fan club, founded around her running "genocide of cocker spaniels" bit; crowdfunds a real anti-cocker-spaniel lawsuit and, after the Dreadnought Clan and Burrowers both drop out, buys the vacated Faction Wars slot outright — fielding The Princess Posse, co-led by Carl and Donut, as one of the nine Floor 9 factions

docs.title: Other Book 6 organizations
docs.text: Name Type Notes Icon Industries Habitat-structures megacorporation Run by Huanxin Jinx, a Grixist heiress "the type of rich where governments come to her when they need a loan." She plays the Celestial Ascendency through sponsored deities — driving Dodola in the Floor 11 flashback and Eileithyia on Carl's floor — and has never won, having once taken a multi-season suspension and a ban on her old goddess for illegal bribery The Fortent Syndicate Council member state Argues against pulling the failsafe in the epilogue session, mainly by accusing every advocate of it of having a personal motive. Nothing else is established about them — see The Syndicate Council Hereford War Machines, Inc. Arms manufacturer Taurine-owned, "known to outfit some of the most elite mercenary squads in the galaxy." Makes The Bull Rush, Donut's Book 6 bespoke personal shield Naughty Boys Employment Agency In-dungeon staffing business Owned by Astrid, the Desperado Club's assistant manager; the Night Wyrm's contract on her cites her dual role — running the agency and the club — as the reason she has to die. See Guild of Suffering

docs.title: Other Book 7 organizations
docs.text:
Book 7's corporate subplots share a theme: every one of them turns out to be lethal.

Name Type Notes Dictum Waystation Controls, Limited Waystation infrastructure corporation; crawler sponsor Murdered its own sponsored crawler to run an ad. The mantis crawler Everly received a benefactor box from Dictum containing Gordon's Compass of Vertical Labyrinth Management, 49 uses, which guided her and ten mercenaries up a fifty-storey tower. At the top, instead of a fan box, was a folded paper note the system read aloud: "Never trust your life to Gordon Waystation Outfitters. There's no safe or cheap path to safety. This dead end was sponsored by Dictum Waystation Controls, Limited. 'Don't get caught with nowhere to go.'" The entire tower was an advertisement attacking a competitor, built by her own sponsor, and the ceiling begins crushing downward the moment she reads it. Her chapter supplies the book's title: "The Inevitable Ruin." The AI notes sponsored traps were "a pilot program this season" Gordon Waystation Outfitters Rival waystation corporation Exists in Book 7 only as the target of Dictum's attack ad; the compass is named after it. Also rendered in the same passage as "Gordon Waystation Controls" Colloid Bank The orc faction's bank "The only bank the orcs use." The instrument of Rosetta's heist: after killing King Rust she uses his signet ring, his eyeball and a password to move the Skull Empire's liquid reserves out — "'Transfer approved! Thank you for using Colloid Bank.'" She drops the datapad and sobs. A Valtay representative, fielding the furious call afterward: "They're trying to claw it back, but she's already transferred it to a credit chit, and it looks like she then sent it off... Monetary transactions aren't covered in the communications blackout... the only one with the authority to possibly have stopped it, maybe, just got splattered all over the playing field by one of his own." The money funds Porthus's ship purchases Sensation Entertainment, Incorporated Production studio Bought by a subsidiary of the Dream between books, and immediately weaponized. Quasar: with Tsarina Signet dead, "that guarantee of a third season we negotiated is about to haunt the fuck out of us. Sensation Entertainment just got purchased by a subsidiary of the Dream, and things are moving. They're demanding their third season... the new showrunners won't be caring about that anymore. They're going to try to use your contractual obligation to ass fuck you." An elite subsequently tries to kill Donut under that cover; Baroness Victory calls it "an unlawful assassination attempt by Sensation Entertainment" and files a grievance against the Dream for "exerting undue influence on one of their elites to affect Faction Wars" Blood Hunter Holdings Naga-owned entertainment studio Odette reveals on live television that the Blood Sultanate "fielded several dramas this season through their Blood Hunter Holdings studio" — including Blood Hunter. She winks at Carl as she says it; the revelation lands "like a meteor" Icon Industries Habitat-structures megacorporation Huanxin Jinx continues to play the Celestial Ascendency through a sponsored deity (Eileithyia). She is killed on-page late in the book: "Huaxin Jinx, CEO of Icon industries rocketed backwards, slid across the floor, and came to a rest at Victory's feet, dead" Hereford War Machines, Inc. Arms manufacturer Not mentioned in Book 7 The Operatic Banker's Federation Interstellar banking body The Operatic Collective's financial arm; War Chief Stalwart invokes it when demanding his father's stolen credits back — "The banker's federation will not stand for this!" Dictum (leaseholder) Waystation landlord In the epilogue, a ruined waystation operator named Zander owes "a 25,000 credit a month lease to Dictum I can't pay" after the embargo kills his traffic — the same corporation, seen from the bottom

docs.title: Borant Corporation
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: Media/mining corporation, current season operator of Dungeon Crawler World
  • Owned by: The kua-tin (an aquatic species)
  • Role in Book 1: Runs the dungeon Carl and Donut are trapped in; assigns Carl's PR agent (Zev)
  • Rival: The Squim Conglomerate (runs a battle-royale-format season instead)

docs.title: What They Are
docs.text: Per the opening Syndicate announcement, Earth was seized under "the Mined Material Reclamation act along with subsection 35 of the Indigenous Planetary Species Protection Act," and Borant — "having been assigned regency over this solar system" — chose "option 3, also known as the 18-Level World Dungeon" as the method of resource reclamation. Borant retains "all rights to broadcast, exploit, and otherwise control all aspects of the World Dungeon" as long as it follows Syndicate regulations.

docs.title: Business Model
docs.text:
Per Mordecai, Borant's revenue comes from three sources: the mining operation itself, advertising revenue from the broadcast, and "a commission on every credit spent by patrons" who sponsor crawlers with loot boxes. The real money, per Mordecai, is in the show, not the mining: "It's a big universe out there, and there are plenty of places to mine. That's not why they're really here."

Not every season is run by Borant — different corporations rotate control of a given world's season, and formats vary wildly by operator. The rival Squim Conglomerate, for example, runs a "battle royale-style" season instead of a structured dungeon crawl. Borant is specifically known, per Mordecai, for running "the most elaborate, most entertaining dungeons."

docs.title: Political Pressure
docs.text: Later in Book 1, Zev reveals Borant is under real strain: the kua-tin system government (led by the ultra-nationalist party the Bloom) forced an early release of this season for a cash grab, even though Borant doesn't see any of the patron/advertising money until the season concludes. Borant has already received a formal warning over "bugs" (design failures like the bathroom punishment mechanic and overpowered mobs) — one more violation risks losing the season entirely. Mordecai is careful to distinguish the corporation from its owners: "Some of those folks are okay. All they want is to put on a good show," in contrast to "nobody likes the kua-tin, at least not their system of government."

docs.title: Rules & Enforcement
docs.text: The in-dungeon "system AI" monitors crawler speech about Borant and the Syndicate; disparaging either on-camera risks having a crawler's "experience... 'accelerated'" — an ominous, undefined threat.

docs.title: Book 2: Financial Crisis
docs.text:
Borant's finances become an explicit plot point once Carl and Donut reach Floor 3. Loot boxes are taxed by the Syndicate per unit given out — Celestial-tier boxes especially, since a single one can make an underperforming crawler "almost immortal" through Floor 9. Each season is allotted only a handful of free Celestial boxes before the tax becomes ruinous; historically, only 18 have ever been awarded in a single season (a Naga-run season, which lost money and effectively ended that faction's ability to run its own crawls afterward).

A quest exploit engineered by Carl, Donut, and Katia — using stacked "Hadji" and "Bandit" achievement upgrades — nearly forces Borant to pay out 83 Celestial Quest Boxes in one event. Borant appeals to a Syndicate court and wins the right to void all quest rewards from the incident using its single free veto for the season (normally saved for high-stakes rulings on Floor 10+) — a decision made before the tenth floor for the first time in the season's history, underscoring how close to the financial edge the company is running. One crawler who'd already opened his box before the ruling keeps his; Borant is stuck paying for that single Celestial box regardless.

Separately, an assassination attempt against Carl and Donut (ordered by the Skull Empire, see Skull Empire) accidentally kills a popular Valtay-sponsored singer instead, escalating tensions between two of Borant's most powerful rivals/creditors right as the company can least afford instability.

Sourced from Book 1: The Apocalypse Will Be Televised and Book 2: Carl's Doomsday Scenario.

docs.title: The Crawler Project
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: Non-profit advocacy organization for released former crawlers
  • Founder: Doctor Porthus Hu — author of the second edition of the Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook and "the first crawler to receive the item"
  • Relationship to the OIPN: The Crawler Project came first and is the larger, more legitimate body; Hu founded the Open Intellect Pacifist Network later as a smaller, more radical offshoot
  • Signal achievement: automatic Syndicate citizenship, free healthcare and guaranteed housing for released crawlers
  • Status at the start of Book 7: scattered, after the authorities declared it a terrorist organization

docs.title: The reveal
docs.text:
Book 7 finally connects two names the series had been carrying separately. Tipid, telling the story of his life after release, mentions "Doctor Hu of the Crawler Project, an NFC organization dedicated to helping former crawlers navigate the universe after release" — and Carl's narration lands the point in four words:

Dr Hu. Dr Porthus Hu. Author of the second edition of the cookbook. The first crawler to receive the item.

Porthus, Carl's own sponsor's frontman, is the founder of both organizations.

docs.title: What it won
docs.text:
The Crawler Project is the respectable arm, and it worked:

"Dr. Hu's work had been instrumental in helping to create multiple laws that would protect crawlers upon release. Because of the Crawler Project's campaigning, all released crawlers were now automatically citizens of the Syndicate and given access to the inner system primary zone, which came with free healthcare and guaranteed housing. When Tipid was released, he wasn't afforded any of that."

Tipid is the counter-example that motivated the whole thing: released with no citizenship, no healthcare, and crushing debt from the surgery that kept him alive.

Mistress Tiatha, drunk as usual, provides the sceptical footnote:

"That citizenship perk is only for new crawlers... And they'll still bleed you dry on taxes. Us old guard are gonna get extra fucked when we're released. They tell us we'll be 'full citizens,' but I don't believe it. The rich folk sure like getting their faces up on the screen when they're donating to some charity, but the moment a scruffy, former crawler shows up in their home system looking to settle down, they'll fight like hell to prevent it. Mark my words."

docs.title: The split, and the crackdown
docs.text:
"In addition to the Crawler Project, Dr. Hu formed the Open Intellect Pacifist Network, which was a smaller, more focused group whose purpose was to end the crawl all together. This organization did not have nearly as much support."

The OIPN's methods eventually poison both. Carl's own Floor 8 meeting with Paulie the residual in the Florida shelter "had been just one of several actions that had caused authorities to finally start to crack down on the non-profit," and by Book 7 the members have scattered under a terrorism accusation. Tipid, asked where Hu is: "We all had to scatter when they accused us of being a terrorist organization. I don't know where he is."

Rosetta is unbothered: "Oh, I hope they try, warlord. But now that we're in the game, there is nothing they can do. They'll wait until we get out to try to arrest us."

docs.title: The Homecoming Queen
docs.text:
The link from advocacy to armed intervention runs through one practical suggestion. After Tipid settled in a Crest colony working for a waste-management company, "it was Doctor Hu who had suggested the idea of refurbishing one of the garbage freighters into a passenger liner. He put out a call to former crawlers who wanted to get back into the game to help us with Faction Wars, and he'd been overwhelmed by the response."

That freighter is the Homecoming Queen, and the response is the 50,000 former crawlers who enlist in the Princess Posse army. Carl:

"They'd come to help fight their former captors. Even when I managed to get the protections turned off, they still came."

'NFC'

The text reads "an NFC organization." Elsewhere in the same passage it is called "the non-profit," so this is almost certainly a typo for NFP. Quoted here as printed.

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: The Dark Hive
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: Private, for-profit mantis-run hunting/entertainment corporation
  • Distinct from: The Burrowers, the actual mantis system government
  • Owner: Circe Took, a minor hive queen who also owns an amusement park
  • Notable hunters: Vrah (heir), Xindy (her sister, killed on Floor 6's first day), a male merchant/accountant named Edict

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Dark Hive is not the mantis species' government — that's the separate, much more conservative Burrowers — but a private corporation, run by Circe Took's family, that fields professional hunter teams for the Dungeon Crawler World hunt and also operates an interstellar amusement park. Circe's daughters (all warriors) and at least one son (a non-combatant merchant who handles trading and logistics) make up its Floor 6 hunting roster: seven warrior-daughters plus Vrah as heir-apparent, alongside a male representative, Edict, who stays behind in Zockau to buy and resell looted gear.

Dark Hive hunters answer only to their own chain of command and are widely feared by the floor's other hunter groups — a few seasons before Book 5, Vrah legally killed a rival hunter in a dispute, and "since then, people just do what the Dark Hive says." They also poach kills from other hunting groups by swooping in from above, a habit resented across the hunter population but tolerated out of fear.

docs.title: Mantis Mating and Honor Culture
docs.text:
Mantis coupling customs carry real legal and social weight: all pairings must be registered ahead of time with a trial and psychological counseling for the male, and unauthorized coupling between rival hives (such as the government-employed Burrowers and the for-profit Dark Hive) is treated as a serious act of dishonor. During mating, the female decapitates the male, who survives briefly on a secondary abdominal brain. This custom becomes a direct plot weapon in Book 5: Carl deliberately infects Vrah with a venereal disease (the Arrow of Enthusiastic Double Gonorrhea — see Items) specifically because the only cure is either self-sterilization (disqualifying her from becoming hive queen) or passing it on through mating — and no eligible, honor-compliant partner exists for her on the floor.

Edict, the Dark Hive's own merchant, is caught between this rule and Vrah's demand that he cure her: coupling with her would dishonor his own hive (contracted to the Burrowers), refusing would bring the Dark Hive's wrath down on his family, and simply waiting her out risks his own death by association. He resolves it the only way his culture allows — provoking his own honor-death by attacking Carl three times inside a saferoom, triggering an automatic ejection-and-death penalty — dumping all his collected loot on the ground as he goes.

docs.title: Book 5's Climax
docs.text:
Vrah's mother, Circe Took, ultimately breaks mantis reproductive taboo herself, using her sponsorship of the goddess Diwata to temporarily assume male mantis form, mate with (and cure) her own daughter, then return to female form and begin giving birth to a swarm of mantis nymphs — simultaneously Vrah's children and siblings. This floods the High Elf Castle with hostile nymphs during the Butcher's Masquerade, in a last-ditch attempt to force the peace seal to break.

By the book's climax, every one of Circe's warrior-daughters is dead, including Vrah (killed by Mongo and Kiwi after Carl marks her with the Ring of Divine Suffering) and Circe herself (torn apart by her own newborn nymphs once Donut strips Diwata's divine protection with Laundry Day).

Sourced from Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade.

docs.title: The Faction Wars Campaign (Floor 9)
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Book: 7, This Inevitable Ruin
  • Setting: The plains and city of Larracos, the ninth floor
  • Format: Ten teams — nine attacking, one defending — arranged "like a pie with Larracos in the center"
  • Opening alignment: eight sponsored teams form The Bloc and declare war on both the Princess Posse and the NPCs' Team Retribution; those two form The Good Guys
  • Winner: The Princess Posse

This page covers how Faction Wars actually played out. For the roster as it stood at the end of Book 6 — the warlords, the preproduction meeting, the mass abdication — see The Faction Wars Teams.

docs.title: The rules Cascadia announces
docs.text:
Cascadia's opening broadcast (audibly drunk or stoned, per Carl) sets the terms:

  • Ten teams total: nine attacking, one defending. The defenders are the NPCs, Team Retribution, headquartered in Larracos. Everyone else holds a numbered wedge of the surrounding Plains of Larracos.
  • A 60-hour ceasefire opens the floor. When it ends, only Team Retribution, unaffiliated NPCs, and Team Retribution's allies may remain inside the city.
  • Crawlers may freely enlist with any team during the ceasefire. Crawlers who don't enlist can be conscripted by force once the fighting starts.
  • The city stays sealed until four teams remain, at which point the final phase — "The Peeling of Larracos" — begins. The defenders win by holding a full week; an attacker wins by holding the throne room for six hours.
  • Only individual teams, not alliances, may take the throne room.
  • An attacking team is eliminated when its warlord(s) die or its own primary throne room is held by an enemy for six hours.
  • 293 stairwell chambers are seeded across the floor, but none open until Faction Wars is won or 30 hours remain to floor collapse.

Two other rules changes matter enormously. The AI altered the 15K rule to let outside mercenaries in: each of the eight sponsored teams receives roughly 20,000 hired mercenaries (≈150,000 total), while the Princess Posse receives just over 50,000 former crawlers shipped in aboard the Homecoming Queen. Baroness Victory's read on the opposition is that most of them are security contractors, not soldiers: "These 'warlords' are called that in name only... They'll be looking for a single punch knock-out."

docs.title: Opening alignment: the Bloc versus the Good Guys
docs.text:
Within minutes of Carl and Donut's arrival, the eight other sponsored teams line up against them:

Warning: The Bone Clan has announced a formal truce with The Operatic Collective.

The Blood Sultanate has joined the truce. The Prism Kingdom has joined the truce. The Dream has joined the truce. The Lemig Sortion has joined the truce. The Madness has joined the truce. The Reavers have joined the truce.

The eight teams within this truce have been named "The Bloc."

The Bloc has declared war against Team Retribution.

The Bloc has declared war against the Princess Posse. That's you!

Donut, still sitting in the mud reading the warlord help files, accepts Team Retribution's counter-offer unilaterally before Carl can finish his sentence — "But before we accept the truce..." — and the counter-alliance is formed on the spot. She names it, and Ferdinand immediately renames it:

Warlord Donut of the Princess Posse has named the truce "The Good Guys."

Warlord Ferdinand of Team Retribution has renamed the truce "Ferdinand and his Bird."

Donut: "Hey! Carl, it won't let me change it back!" The name reverts to The Good Guys later in the book.

The practical effect of Donut's snap decision is enormous: as Team Retribution's ally, the Princess Posse is not ejected from Larracos when the ceasefire expires.

docs.title: The Skull Empire's name change
docs.text:
The orc team competes in Book 7 as the Bone Clan — the Skull Empire's Faction Wars banner — and its warlord is War Chief / King Stalwart. Their wedge, spot 1, holds The King's Point, the only one of the nine wedges that comes with a pre-built castle. Likewise, the Lemig team is listed throughout Book 7 as the Democratic Sortion, and the Prism Kingdom's team is called simply the Prism.

The Princess Posse's own stronghold is the Fortress of Unyielding Power and Authority — which the AI refuses to let Donut rename once Carl works out the acronym. Everyone, including the system, calls it the FUPA.

docs.title: Mid-book: the Bloc fractures
docs.text:
Three shocks land almost at once.

King Rust dies. The orc king marches his horde to the Posse's line in person to deliver a warning — his daughter Princess Formidable has seized a Skull Empire cruiser and is hours from reaching the monitor station where she intends to manually trigger the system failsafe, which would kill everyone in the system. Rosetta kills him on the spot. (Formidable never reaches it; the AI pulls her off her own ship and drops her in the ocean.)

The orcs' backdoors are exposed. Rust confirms it himself before he dies:

"The Skull Empire manufactures the satellites. We build backdoors into everything we manufacture so they can't be used against us. This was a secret until my daughter announced it to the whole galaxy."

Volteeg's POV chapter gives the Bloc's-eye view of what Formidable's broadcast actually did to the alliance: "Not only are you all going to die, but guess what? My family has been spying on you this whole time. Also, you know all that military hardware you've been buying from us for thousands of years? We have a button that can turn it all off with a flick of a switch. We can even make it turn against you." Every remaining team begins deactivating all Skull-Empire-manufactured hardware — Epitome Tagg says so on camera at the warlord council, and one of the Dream's own news channels is caught renaming itself Yes. We have Deactivated the Infected Hardware as a covert signal.

The naga plot leaks. Rishi later explains that "just before the meeting of the warlords, news broke that laid out our plans regarding our intention to renege on our shipyard contracts, which caused immediate chaos in our system" — see The Great Consensus.

The result:

Warlord Message. The Bone Clan is no longer a member of the Bloc.

Warlord Message. The Dream is no longer a member of the Bloc.

Alliance Update:

The Bloc Alliance: The Blood Sultanate / The Madness / The Reavers

The Good Guys Alliance: Team Retribution / The Princess Posse

Unaffiliated: The Bone Clan. The Dream.

Donut's reaction: "Wow. What happened? I was expecting the orc guys to break up because of that whole 'We've been spying on you' thing. But what happened with the bald Dream guys?" Carl's read: "The fact everyone is making these moves now suggests they already know the failsafe isn't going off."

docs.title: Full elimination order
docs.text:
# Team How they fell 1 The Democratic Sortion (Lemig) Warlord Commander Stockade kills himself mid-hearing — "Credit for the kill has been ruled as a psychosis-induced suicide." Ruled a voluntary defeat; all Lemig assets are awarded to the Madness 2 The Prism "Warlord D'Nadia of the Prism has fallen. Credit for the kill has been given to pet Mongo of the Princess Posse" 3 The Operatic Collective Warlord Hortense Leadership Unit killed when Volteeg fills a Weeper-class tank with explosives and detonates it inside the Bloc's own formation, killing over 10,000 of his own side. The system: "Credit for the kill has been ruled as either accidental or a fragging incident, which would be funny as shit." Assets to the Bone Clan 4 The Blood Sultanate "The Sepsis Whore of the Blood Sultanate has fallen. Credit for the kill has been given to Kandy 'Bigs' Newton" — the sluggalo who burst out of Carl's back with a hatchet 5 The Bone Clan (Skull Empire) "War Chief Stalwart of the Bone Clan has fallen. Credit for the kill has been given to three members of the War Mage Rebellion." Because the War Mages are not an active team, Stalwart's assets go to Team Retribution, who were holding his throne room 6 The Madness "Architect Houston of the Madness has fallen. Credit for the kill has been given to Warlord Carl" 7 The War Mage Rebellion "Warlord Akuma has left the realm. As per the current season's ruleset, the War Mage rebellion has been defeated. They have no assets to award" 8 The Reavers Warlord Fang of the Reavers, hiding inside a dragon, dies when Carl detonates a bomb dropped by a wraith-possessed Louis Santiago 2 under Juice Box's control. Assets to the Princess Posse 9 The Dream "Warlord Epitome Tagg of the Dream has fallen" — credit given, after visible AI deliberation, to pet Mongo 10 Team Retribution Voluntary forfeit. "Both Warlords Ferdinand and Juice Box have left the realm. Under the current ruleset, they have abandoned their posts and have forfeited their position"

System Message: The Princess Posse has won Faction Wars.

Congratulations, Champions.

Order differs from the intuitive one

The War Mage Rebellion falls before the Reavers and the Dream, not after. Akuma withdraws the moment he has what he came for, while Fang and Tagg are still alive and holding territory.

docs.title: Notable betrayals and self-inflicted wounds
docs.text:
Commander Stockade cheats and destroys his own team. Stockade and Architect Houston of the Madness conspire to use the secured messaging system to reach Nurse Yugoslav of the Madness on the 18th floor, who relayed live feed intelligence through a third party in the Celestial Ascendency. Their plan was to extract Shi Maria from Carl and turn him into a vegetable while the spider killed everyone in the Posse's base. It goes catastrophically wrong: the spider manifests in the Lemig throne room instead and slaughters fifty-odd Lemig, including Stockade's beloved Luke. Adjutant Panford's verdict:

"What happened is exactly what always happens when you attempt to improperly extract an entity that powerful. This is your fault... Unless you can prove you have a mole in the Princess Posse camp, I am going to assume you have an external influence assisting you, which is clearly cheating."

Houston sacrifices Stockade. Houston refuses to confess, and the quorum clears him — Victory: "Houston is obviously guilty, but unless he admits it, he was smart enough to let Stockade do all of his dirty work." When Stockade, hit with a delayed dose of the spider's Insanity spell, begins beating his own face to pulp on the floor, Victory offers Houston the chance to intervene: "Feel free to help him. Or call his guards." Houston does not move; he stares at Carl the whole time. The payoff is procedural — Stockade's death is a voluntary withdrawal, which triggers acceleration scenario two, shortening the ceasefire by 23.33 hours and ending it instantly, and hands every Lemig asset to the Madness. Houston's private message to Carl beforehand: "You are in mortal danger at this very moment, and you don't even realize it."

The Dream and the Madness squabble over the vacated Prism castle — exactly as Carl predicted. After killing D'Nadia, Carl can't hold non-contiguous land, so he parks a captured Madness mercenary named Lockjaw in the Prism throne room with a chair and snacks:

"By making the Madness mercenary sit in there, it would at least force the other leaders to make a decision. If Epitome Tagg was as much of an ass as I suspected, he was going to make a move and usurp poor Lockjaw out of that room. That would, hopefully, piss off Architect Houston of the Madness. I had the impression none of these leaders liked each other very much. So hopefully this would sow a little discord."

It works. The castle "changed hands for the third time, which reset the six-hour clock... as if the Madness and the Dream were fighting over who had the rights to the sliver of land. But as long as they kept going back and forth, the castle remained Posse territory." Volteeg's chapter confirms the knock-on: "The Dream and the Madness were now bickering." The castle is only finally ceded to the Dream after the Bloc has already fractured.

The War Mage Rebellion breaks its own team's Conscription enchantment to kill its own king. Victory's post-mortem:

"It appears the War Mages broke their own allegiance against the Skull Empire, which they shouldn't be able to do. They were under strict Conscription rules, but they used a clever combination of Pull spells to kill Stalwart anyway. I think Stalwart might've ejected them from his army on purpose in an attempt to get them to stop hurting him. It didn't work."

Stalwart's last words, as three war mages tear his flesh apart: "My sister was right."

Agatha hijacks the War Mage Rebellion, and its actual leader asks Carl to kill her. See The War Mage Rebellion.

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: The Faction Wars Teams
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Count: Nine at the start of Book 6, ten by the last page
  • Structure: Eight sponsored (non-crawler) teams, plus the crawlers' Princess Posse, plus the NPC Home Team added in the closing chapter
  • Setting: The ninth floor, based on the city and castle of Larracos — see Semeru Dwarves
  • Key Book 6 event: Six of the eight sponsored teams try to quit. All six are refused

docs.title: The teams
docs.text:
# Team Faction Warlord / representative shown in Book 6 1 — Skull Empire Crown Prince Stalwart, the Maestro's older brother. Refuses to introduce himself ("I don't announce myself"), threatens to skin Donut and line his codpiece with her pelt, and is renamed "Captain Enormous" by Donut in a rejected action item 2 — Operatic Collective "Voting Admin Cell Mass Number Three" — a three-tier green Jell-o-mold blob containing three individuals, one named Hortense. Donut renames him "Green Jiggly" 3 Princess Posse Society for the Eradication of Cocker Spaniels / Princess Posse Enterprises Carl and Princess Donut, co-warlords. Adjutant: Odette 4 — Blood Sultanate Rishi — a four-armed green-and-purple naga in dented plate, explicitly "not a member of the royal family," married into it. Carl's instinct: "I had an uneasy feeling about this guy" 5 Prism Kingdom Clan The Prism Kingdom Empress D'Nadia 6 — The Dream Epitome Tagg — bald, regal, "one of the richest men in the entire galaxy." The Dream control food-growing operations across numerous systems and hold patents on multiple types of food 7 — Lemig Sortion Luke, a green goblin/nullian-looking Lemig who talks like a surfer. Their earlier commander, Commander Stockade, was trapped in the Desperado Club and eaten in the flooded Larracos 8 The Madness The viceroys An unnamed masked viceroy, decapitated at the table during introductions — he "regenerates at sunset, isn't that right? At least until the games begin," per Epitome Noflex, who killed him 9 — The Reavers Warlord Fangs, a brain-only machine person appearing as a 1960s tin robot for Carl's benefit 10 Home Team The NPCs of Larracos Co-warlords Juice Box and Sir Ferdinand — both NPCs. Added by audience vote in the book's final chapter

For the species behind these factions — viceroys, Reavers, the Operatic Collective, the Lemig — see Other Book 6 species.

docs.title: The preproduction meeting
docs.text:
The fifth preproduction meeting, chaired by Cascadia with the mexx robot U56KL ("Urkel") running the action-item queue, is where Carl and Donut meet the other warlords for the first time. Two things happen there that shape everything after:

Epitome Noflex crashes it. The viceroy's head falls off mid-meeting because Juice Box, wearing the face of Epitome Tagg's mother, has just killed him. She takes his chair and puts her feet on the table. Tagg — who had told the others he'd "taken care of this" — demands Cascadia intervene and is told she can't: "The rules haven't changed. She's an NPC. The AI won't let us touch this."

Tagg's parting complaint is the thesis of the entire back half of the book:

"They're becoming self-aware. All of them... It's going to be impossible for anybody to win."

Carl proposes the tenth team. In the same meeting: "I propose a new action item. A tenth team populated with NPCs, afforded the same protections as the rest."

docs.title: The mass abdication
docs.text:
Late in Book 6, six of the eight sponsored teams give up at once:

The Operatic Collective has abdicated their spot and indicated their intention to abandon Faction Wars. The Blood Sultanate has abdicated their spot... The Dream has abdicated their spot... The Lemig Sortion has abdicated their spot... The Madness has abdicated their spot... The Reavers have abdicated their spot...

Please Wait...

Offboarding request has been denied. The teams will remain as designated. All off-boarding requests are currently suspended while the Earth system remains in quarantine per Syndicate rule 470.B through 495 in the System AI Stability Addendum. And as you all know, the rules must be followed.

Donut, arriving covered in tinsel: "Carl, Carl, did you see that? They tried to run away!"

The two that don't try to quit are the Princess Posse and the Prism Kingdom — the crawlers who want the fight, and the Empress who spent everything she had to buy her way in.

The Burrowers and the Dreadnought Clan are absent from the roster entirely; both had already withdrawn at the end of Book 5, and it is those two vacated slots the Prism Kingdom and the Princess Posse bought.

docs.title: The final action items
docs.text:
With both warlords forced into the stairwell early, Carl spends the Princess Posse's first Emergency Action Item on a procedural request: that all remaining pending action-item votes be handed to the viewers, or failing that decided by the AI. It is granted immediately.

"Zev said the AI is a lot friendlier if you ask nicely and if you give it options. Have you read all the previous emergency action items? Everyone was being complete dicks about it. Of course the AI is going to reject it. They still treat it like a computer, and it's not. They call it an AI, but there's nothing artificial about it."

The audience then decides the queue in thirty-second increments:

Proposed by Item Result The Madness Limit Celestial Summoning events to five per team Rejected, 37% — existing limit of fifteen stands The Dream Relax physics limits on long-range artillery; raise the playing-field ceiling Passed, 72% The Reavers Accelerate pet leveling during Faction Wars Passed, 83% Princess Posse Remove safety protections for faction sponsors Passed, 98% Princess Posse A tenth team populated with NPCs, afforded the same protections as the rest Passed, 52%

The tenth-team result carries the detail that matters:

This team will be designated as Home Team with the city of Larracos as their base. Effective immediately, peace rules apply until the game starts. This team's assigned co-warlords are the NPCs Juice Box and Sir Ferdinand.

An adjutant will be assigned before the battles commence.

Sir Ferdinand already has a full page from Book 5 — see Ferdinand.

The 98% vote to strip sponsor safety protections is the one Carl reacts to out loud, jabbing a finger at the ceiling: "Your people voted for this. Your own citizens said, yes, we're okay with the crawlers killing you one by one."

docs.title: The other side of the board
docs.text:
What none of the teams know at the end of Book 6 is that the AI has also agreed to let the Valtay distribute over 150,000 mercenaries and private soldiers evenly across the eight sponsored teams, with orders to kill every crawler — and that the Open Intellect Pacifist Network has simultaneously boarded 50,000 former crawlers onto the Princess Posse's roster aboard the Homecoming Queen. Rosetta asks the obvious follow-up in the book's last exchange:

"I am worried about that tenth team... If the AI is going to allow the eight sponsors plus the crawler team to bolster their numbers so much, what's it doing for the NPCs?"

Common misattribution

Commander Stockade belongs to the Lemig Sortion, not the Operatic Collective. Odette names him as "Commander Stockade of the Lemig Sortion... the last of the 35 to be devoured," and Quasar had earlier noted that the Lemigs' commander was stuck in the Desperado Club. Separately, Odette and Carl watch "a submerged viceroy from team Madness get devoured by a shark" — two different deaths, two different teams.

docs.title: What happens next
docs.text:
Book 7 renames several of these teams and then destroys all of them. The Home Team becomes Team Retribution; the Skull Empire competes as the Bone Clan, the Lemig Sortion as the Democratic Sortion, and the Prism Kingdom Clan as the Prism. Eight of the nine sponsored teams immediately ally as The Bloc against the crawlers and the NPCs, and the Princess Posse wins. For the alliances, the elimination order and the betrayals, see The Faction Wars Campaign.

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: Long Haul Biological Waste Management Solutions
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: Galactic corpse-disposal company, owned and crewed by the Crest
  • Business model: They show up after a crawl is over. "It wasn't until the last crawler drew their final breath before they started their grim task"
  • Book 6 role: Becomes Princess Donut's new sponsor after Empress D'Nadia sells her sponsorship
  • Their freighter: the Homecoming Queen, the largest ship in Earth orbit — twice the size of a Valtay warship
  • Epilogue reveal: The Homecoming Queen is a converted troop transport carrying 50,000 former crawlers, cleared to board Faction Wars as troopers for the Princess Posse

docs.title: Donut's new sponsor
docs.text:
Mid-battle on Floor 8, Donut gets a notification that Empress D'Nadia has sold her sponsorship to someone else. Carl isn't surprised — D'Nadia had overextended herself buying a Faction Wars spot, and she's about to be fighting Donut. Donut is devastated, and then finds out who bought her:

Donut: "MY NEW SPONSOR IS NAMED LONG HAUL BIOLOGICAL WASTE MANAGEMENT SOLUTIONS, AND I JUST CAN'T WITH THAT. I KNOW I'M SUPPOSED TO APPEAR GRATEFUL, BUT THAT SOUNDS ABSOLUTELY DISGUSTING. CARL, ARE THEY GOING TO SHOW COMMERCIALS FOR GARBAGE TRUCKS ON MY FEED? THIS IS NOT ACCEPTABLE."

Carl's reaction is quieter and more accurate: "Biological waste? I didn't like the sound of that."

The joke lands twice. The first time, it's a status humiliation — a princess sponsored by a garbage company. The second time is the epilogue.

docs.title: The Homecoming Queen
docs.text:
Princess Formidable, stewing in her cruiser after being muted by the Syndicate Council, notices a ship she can't place:

"Her eyes focused on a single, out-of-place garbage freighter floating not too far away. It was easily the largest ship in orbit. The thing was twice the size of one of those Valtay warships. It was one of the freighters from Long Haul Biological Waste Management Solutions.

This particular ship's name was Homecoming Queen. She grunted. Those Crest always named their vessels the strangest things."

She writes it off as a corpse hauler that turned up early and got caught by the quarantine like everyone else — "They usually didn't bother showing up until after the crawl was done." Then she reconsiders:

But then again, she thought, they're probably right on time.

docs.title: What's really aboard
docs.text:
The last scene of the book is inside that freighter's cockpit. Tipid and Rosetta — both Crest, both former crawlers, both of the Open Intellect Pacifist Network — are watching Carl and Donut's escape from Floor 8 on replay. Tipid converted the ship at enormous expense. The name is newly given.

"You have been cleared for on-boarding."

"Okay, folks. We have been cleared for onboarding. The AI has approved our request. We are officially all troopers now for the Princess Posse."

Cheers rose up through the hull. Fifty-thousand former crawlers, all hidden inside the newly-renamed Homecoming Queen. Once they made it onboard into the system, there was nothing anybody could do to stop it.

Their stated motive is not rescue. Rosetta, asked if she wants to back out: "And miss the opportunity to really kill some of those bastards?" Tipid is under no illusion about the odds — "I always knew I would die in the dungeon. Even after I got out, I always knew."

The corpse-disposal cover story is the point. A company whose entire business is arriving to collect crawler bodies is the one organization in the galaxy that can park the largest ship in orbit without anyone asking what's inside it.

Sponsorship and the troop ship

Book 6 does not spell out whether Long Haul's purchase of Donut's sponsorship was itself part of the Open Intellect plan or an unrelated transaction the network later exploited. Tipid does mention paying for "that Celestial box we just sent Princess Donut," which strongly implies the two are the same operation, but the book never states it outright.

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: Nebular Sin Patrol
docs.text:
Parent organization

The Sin Patrol is the hunter wing of a much larger religious civilization. Book 6 finally explains what that civilization wants — see The Nebulars / Nebular Balance.

Quick facts

  • Type: Nomadic, mechanically/bio-augmented religious cult (not a single species)
  • Floor 6 role: One of several hunting groups; claimed Prepotente and Miriam Dom as targets
  • Doctrine: "The Ballad of Survival" — nonviolence and anti-scarcity preaching, contradicted by its own hunting practices

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Nebular Sin Patrol are not a distinct alien species but a religious order drawn from many species at once — soothers, humans, elves, and others — identifiable mainly by their full-body robes, tubes, and tall, distinctive hats. They worship a "space oddity" deity said to sit at the center of the inner system, and live nomadically, settling only empty or barely-habitable worlds just long enough to raise a generation of bioengineered children before half the community moves on to a new world.

Their central religious tenets, quoted from their own hymn, the Ballad of Survival, sound pacifistic: "Violence breeds chaos. From chaos we were born and into chaos we will succumb." In practice, their young men — priests-in-training — are sent to hunt crawlers as a literal crusade, believing anyone born on a "seeded" world (i.e., every crawler) is an abomination. The Sin Patrol is one of the few hunter organizations that reliably fields a team on every crawl, spending enormous sums (including deity sponsorships) to do so, and is actively campaigning for the right to run an entire season of Dungeon Crawler World itself one day.

docs.title: The Burrower Feud
docs.text: The Nebular Sin Patrol has a long-standing grudge against the mantis system, stemming from an incident where nebular settlers squatted uninvited in territory belonging to the Burrowers (the mantis government, distinct from the private Dark Hive) — a dispute that several hunters conflate with the unrelated Dark Hive when discussing it. This old feud resurfaces on Floor 6: once Vrah is publicly humiliated and the Dark Hive's grip on "who's allowed to hunt whom" starts slipping, the Sin Patrol's priests openly move against targets the Dark Hive had claimed for itself, including attacking Lucia Mar despite her being a Dark Hive-claimed target.

docs.title: Wiped Out Before the Masquerade
docs.text: The Sin Patrol's feud with the Dark Hive comes to a head earlier than the Butcher's Masquerade itself: when Carl teleports back into the ambushed village of Alucarda (mid-book, well before the party), roughly ten robed Sin Patrol priests and a handful of Dark Hive mantis warriors are already there together, having moved in on Lucia Mar at the same time. Carl's trap-triggered "Ballroom Blitz" song inflicts an Unsettled debuff on the mantises, and in the resulting chaos — compounded by Carl's own hob-lobber and marked kills — the two hunter factions turn on each other outright. By the time the dust settles, every one of the Sin Patrol priests present is dead, along with all but one of the mantis warriors (who then hunts Carl and Donut down personally). No Sin Patrol priests are shown at the Butcher's Masquerade itself; the hunter side of that final battle is instead overrun by Vrah's Dark Hive kin and a flood of Circe Took/Diwata's newborn mantis nymphs.

docs.title: Book 6: the parent body resurfaces
docs.text:
The Sin Patrol itself doesn't field a Floor 8 team, but the Nebulars do not go away. They sponsor and patron Sister Ines Quiteria through her descent, and separately sponsor the goddess Ysalte via a cleric called Pontifex Shine of the Nebular Balance.
