Mordecai also reveals that the Faction Wars team the Reavers were once related to the Nebulars — the same "augment yourself with machines" tradition, taken to the point of keeping only the brain. Full detail on all of this is on the parent page, The Nebulars / Nebular Balance.

Sourced from Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade, with Book 6 additions from The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: The Nebulars / Nebular Balance
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: Nomadic, machine-augmented religious civilization drawn from many species at once — not a single race
  • Object of worship: The ancient, stable macro AI at the centre of the galaxy, which runs the inner system and predates Syndicate society
  • Core doctrine: Replicating that AI is blasphemy
  • Stated political goal: Shut down every crawl in existence — by eradicating every planet capable of hosting one, and every other religion along with them
  • Ethical position: Pacifists outside the dungeon. Not pacifists inside it
  • Formal name used for the sponsoring body (Book 6): the Nebular Balance
  • Hunter wing: Nebular Sin Patrol — the priests-in-training who hunt crawlers each season
  • Distant relatives: The Reavers, once related to the Nebulars, who took the same augmentation path further and kept only their brains

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Through Books 5 and 6 the Nebulars have shown up as robed, tall-hatted weirdos at the edge of every scene, and Book 6 is where Mordecai finally explains what they actually want. The picture that emerges is coherent, internally consistent, and completely deranged.

"Near the center of the galaxy is a very large AI that extends a benign enhancement zone over several solar systems, and it's where a whole lot of people live. The 'inner system.' This AI is the same sort of thing that runs the crawl, but it predates Syndicate society. It is stable and is without personality. It's the only one like it. The Nebs worship it like it's a god, and they think it's blasphemy to try to replicate it."

Every macro AI built in the mantis facility and installed into a Primal Engine — see Game Mechanics — is, by that doctrine, a forgery of God. Every crawl is therefore a blasphemy factory, and every planet that could host one is a future blasphemy.

docs.title: What they want
docs.text:
Mordecai lays it out, and Carl immediately spots the contradiction:

Mordecai: "...they really, really want to run a crawl themselves sometime, but nobody is ever going to let them because their stated goal is to shut all of this down. Hence they try to keep winning the Celestial Ascendency since one of the prizes of that is a seat at the table of the Syndicate crawl council. Outside the crawl, they're pacifists. You could literally walk up to one and punch him in the face, and he'll let you do it. Not so much inside the dungeon."

Carl: "They want to shut the crawl down?"

Mordecai: "Yeah, but don't get too excited. They preach the eradication of all the places that could host crawls, such as this planet. And all the people on it. And all other religions, too. They're psychotic."

Carl: "Preaching for genocide doesn't exactly go along with pacifism."

Mordecai: "Yeah, it doesn't make much sense to anybody else, either."

Mordecai's summary of the organization as a whole: "What they want is easy to explain, but what they do is not because their actions never make sense."

So the strategy is not revolt but infiltration by the rules — win the Celestial Ascendency, take the seat it grants on the Syndicate crawl council, and dismantle the institution from inside. They field a hunter team every season, and they campaign endlessly for the right to run a season themselves, which no one will ever grant them.

docs.title: Sponsorships in Book 6
docs.text:
The Nebulars buy influence at two levels on Floor 8, and both purchases go badly.

Sister Ines Quiteria. The Nebulars are both her sponsor and her patron — Mordecai notes those amount to the same thing here. The announcers make the connection explicit during the Chowder War coverage: because "her sponsor and patron, the Nebulars, helped her raise that Word Weaver spell to level 15," she is able to charm a level-125 city boss and the spells that boss can cast, which is what turns a mob war into a zombie apocalypse.

Carl reads the sponsorship as deliberate sabotage of a fragile person: "Whatever imbalance she had, it's been deliberately kicked back into place. I think it's one of her sponsors... I think they gave her something that sent her back over the edge." Mordecai's own guess is blunter: "They likely sponsored her because she's religious, and they either want to convert her or make an example of her." See Sister Ines Quiteria and the Chowder War.

The goddess Ysalte. Separately, the Floor 9 goddess Ysalte enters the realm on Floor 8 carrying the tag: "This goddess is sponsored by Pontifex Shine of the Nebular Balance." This is the book's only use of the name Nebular Balance and the only appearance of Pontifex Shine, who is never seen. Ysalte is killed on-page by Paz Lo — see Ysalte — which makes it two Nebular investments destroyed in the same floor.

Unresolved

Book 6 does not say whether "the Nebular Balance" is the Nebulars' formal name, a specific organ or sect within them, or simply the sponsoring entity's registered title. Pontifex Shine is named once and never appears.

docs.title: Relationship to the Reavers
docs.text:
When Carl meets Warlord Fangs at the Faction Wars preproduction meeting, Mordecai's briefing reveals a shared origin: the Reavers "supposedly were once related to the Nebulars," and "like the nebs, they were originally several different biological races who enhanced themselves with machines, though these guys took it a step further and kept only their brains."

The two have ended up as opposites in every way that matters — the Reavers are a megacorporation and system government that plays Faction Wars to win the trophy, the Nebulars a religion that plays to end the game.

docs.title: Public standing
docs.text:
Nobody with money takes them seriously, and everybody with money keeps having to deal with them. Quasar's reaction to the Residual trap is representative: "I bet those Nebular fucks were all jerking each other off while all this went down." The Residuals are an object of Nebular religious fascination precisely because the galactic-centre AI the Nebulars worship is the same entity the Residuals call the Eulogist — see Gondii / "Residuals".

Carl also sees them as an audience: the Floor 11 arena crowd watching Odette's team is "thousands and thousands of robe-clad people wearing large hats."

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride, with hunter-team background from Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade.

docs.title: The Open Intellect Pacifist Network
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Full registered name: Open Intellect Pacifist Network, Intergalactic NFC (a non-profit)
  • Type: Media/advocacy non-profit and crawler sponsor — publicly. In fact a conspiracy of former crawlers who want the entire crawl system to fail
  • Sponsors: Carl, from Book 5 onward
  • Known members: Rosetta Thagra (a Crest, former crawler, cookbook contributor, host of Shadow Boxer); Tipid, a Crest and former crawler; "Milk" and Porthus, both cookbook contributors; Doctor Hu, the strategist who recruited them
  • Owns: Shadow Boxer, a weekly interview programme about Earth
  • Book 6 outcome: The Residual trap fails. Assets frozen, members declared fugitives, network scattered — and in the epilogue, aboard the freighter Homecoming Queen

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Open Intellect Pacifist Network reaches Book 6 as the least interesting of Carl's sponsors: a non-profit that funds documentaries and owns a talk show. It leaves Book 6 as the organization that tried to get the galaxy's failsafe pulled with Carl standing in the blast radius.

Carl's first real suspicion comes from the cookbook. Shadow Boxer's host, Rosetta Thagra, is a former crawler whose cookbook notes are full of explosives recipes. Digging further, Carl finds that at least one and possibly three of the network's people are former owners of The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook — Rosetta, "Milk," and probably a third:

"now that I had definitive proof that my sponsors, the Open Intellect Pacifist Network, employed at least one, likely two, possibly three former cookbook owners, then whatever it was they were attempting to get me to do was of crucial importance."

The clue itself is a cookbook in-joke. During Carl's Shadow Boxer interview, Rosetta steers the conversation to the stew he used to cook at the boys' home — milk and potatoes — which points Carl at a passage in the cookbook where Milk had written about root vegetables and Rosetta had replied. That is how he works out what to do with the toraline root he'd been sent.

docs.title: What they actually are
docs.text:
Liaison Orren states it plainly after the trap collapses:

"The Open Intellect Pacifist Network is comprised of former crawlers who want to see the crawl fail."

Their sponsorship of Carl was never charity or fandom. It was the delivery mechanism for a plan they had been building toward for a long time.

docs.title: The Residual trap
docs.text:
The scheme: use a sponsor box to send Carl a flyer that would put him, in person, within earshot of a Residual reciting its daily speech during a memory-based floor. The network gambled that whatever the Residual said would be catastrophic enough to force one of two outcomes — and either one ends the crawl:

  1. The showrunners yank Carl out of the memory mid-speech. That would enrage the system AI badly enough, in the network's estimation, that it would kill everyone.
  2. The showrunners don't yank him, the information gets out, and the Syndicate Council immediately pulls the failsafe — detonating this solar system's star.

Orren, in Carl's own words:

"In other words, they were willing to sacrifice you and the entire planet. They were using you, and they've been using you this whole time."

It failed on the first move. Orren had anticipated a yank and pre-negotiated the scenario with the AI, which allowed the feed to keep running to head off conspiracy theories. And what the Residual was actually saying, per Orren, was "long-debunked folklore about the collapse of the inner system."

"I'm quite certain your former sponsors didn't actually know what he was going to say, and they'd gambled everything on it being something profound. They gambled, and they lost."

The collateral damage lands on the Residuals rather than the network: the AI, annoyed at having been misled too, strips its protections from every remaining Residual on the floor.

See Gondii / "Residuals" for the speech itself, and Game Mechanics for the Failsafe and the Residual mechanic.

docs.title: Collapse
docs.text:
Carl notices the network's people vanishing before he understands why — "I couldn't stop thinking about the disappearance of the members of the Open Intellect Pacifist Network." After the trap:

"Now they are fugitives, their assets frozen, and their lives ruined."

Carl's sponsorship spot is frozen, and the Syndicate is left undecided about the network's representative still participating in the Ascendency game. The network manages one last act first: an Emergency Gold Benefactor Box, delivered and seized by liaison action, then forcibly un-seized by the AI under "Syndicate rule 855.C. AKA the 'Don't be annoying little bitches' rule."

docs.title: Epilogue: the Homecoming Queen
docs.text:
The final scene of the book puts two of them in the cockpit of a converted garbage freighter in Earth orbit — Tipid, a Crest and former crawler, and Rosetta, wearing a scrambler to hide from security sweepers. Tipid paid to convert the ship (or rather, as Rosetta points out, he didn't — someone else did) and also paid for the Celestial box they just sent Princess Donut.

Doctor Hu recruited them both, and made them one promise: "I can only promise two things. Eventual death. And eventual justice." Hu also predicted, correctly, that Carl would get the Faction Wars safety protections turned off, and predicted the Syndicate Council's response to it.

The ship is cleared for on-boarding in the book's last page. Its cargo is fifty thousand former crawlers, now troopers for the Princess Posse. See Long Haul Biological Waste Management Solutions.

Unresolved

Book 6 names Doctor Hu only in the epilogue and Porthus only as a cookbook contributor ("Note added by Crawler Porthus, Second Edition"). The text of this book never states that they are the same person, and Carl never counts his "possibly three" cookbook owners by name. Treat any Porthus = Dr. P. Hu identification as unconfirmed by Book 6 itself.

Resolved in Book 7. Carl's narration states it outright: "Dr Hu. Dr Porthus Hu. Author of the second edition of the cookbook. The first crawler to receive the item."

docs.title: Book 7: Dr. Porthus Hu and the two organizations
docs.text:
Book 7 gives the network a documented history. Porthus founded the larger, legitimate Crawler Project first, and then "In addition to the Crawler Project, Dr. Hu formed the Open Intellect Pacifist Network, which was a smaller, more focused group whose purpose was to end the crawl all together. This organization did not have nearly as much support."

Carl's Floor 8 meeting with Paulie the residual was "just one of several actions that had caused authorities to finally start to crack down on the non-profit." By Book 7 both organizations have scattered under a terrorism accusation, and even Tipid doesn't know where Porthus is.

docs.title: Reach inside the Syndicate
docs.text:
The network's real asset is bureaucratic infiltration, not weapons. Two examples:

  • Volteeg's reclassification. Volteeg entered the dungeon as a pet, not a crawler. "Someone working for the Pacifist Network, someone imbedded deep, deep in the bureaucratic quagmire of the Syndicate had changed the code on that designation to make it appear as if he was something else. They thought he was a former indentured, like the bopcas and so many others. Not a crawler. Just another refugee" — which is why he was never dragged into the Bone Clan's conscript pool.
  • An agent driving a goddess. "The Open Intellect's agent, Rectrix, was driving Theia" in the Celestial Ascendency — Samantha's own mother in dungeon lore, which the Posse exploits during Operation: Snake Pit.
  • Baroness Victory. Rosetta notes the arrangement with the Posse's adjutant "had been brokered between Porthus and Victory long before Victory was even chosen as an adjutant," and that Victory's motivations in helping the network remain a mystery even to her. "Once again, he seemed to be a few steps ahead of everybody else."

docs.title: The Homecoming Queen is armed
docs.text:
The refurbished Crest garbage freighter carrying the 50,000 former crawlers turns out to be the most dangerous ship in Earth orbit, on Porthus's orders:

"Homecoming Queen did have armament, however. A lot of it. Though that was a secret, and York had worked hard to keep it that way."

"And not only was the ship well-armed, but it had a full complement of enhancement zone guns and beams. Highly regulated, high-energy weapons that would normally only work in the center system. Porthus had ordered them installed. These weapons were now green across the board, making Homecoming Queen likely the strongest ship in orbit. Even the Syndicate security corvettes didn't bother with the enhancement zone weapons."

She also carries Cronus-class power armor, breaching suits and enhancement-zone suits. Boomer, docking at the end of the book: "Set aside four of the Cronus suits and a landing skiff. We have a pregnant veteran on the surface who needs backup. And for the rest of us, it's time to bring the war out of the dungeon. Better warm up the lasers."

It is also the ship that destroyed the orc royal yacht. York fired an NPB point-defence weapon at "the small yacht... the one filled with children, including the new king of the orcs," on a side mission Rosetta had commissioned, then let the blame fall on general crossfire. The deaths of those children are what makes Baroness Victory eligible for political office.

docs.title: Renamed: the Open Intellect Action Network
docs.text:
In the epilogue, a pre-recorded broadcast that Rosetta directed goes out on the news feeds:

"On the screen, Porthus was announcing the formation of a new militant group. He was warning that they would now be moving against all Syndicate governmental properties and systems across the known universe. The government had until the end of the current crawl to agree to their demands, which basically boiled down to, 'stop the crawl or else.'"

York's own end-card confirms the new name:

Current status: Captain in the newly coined resistance organization, The Open Intellect Action Network.

docs.title: Book 8: Total System Domination in a Day
docs.text:
Book 8 confirms the militant turn promised at the end of Book 7 actually happens, and faster and more completely than Porthus's own broadcast threat implied. Production assistant Lexis briefs Carl on it mid-floor:

Lexis, Book 8

"The Open Intellect Action Network... You know, those people you won Faction Wars with? Those insurgents. They sent a boarding crew to pretty much every major ship in orbit and took all of them. It happened very fast. That Homecoming Queen is decked out in enhancement-zone weaponry that actually works now that the AI has escaped containment. It's the equivalent of a fully armored ogre fighting against blind toddlers. They achieved total system domination in a day."

The seizure is enabled directly by the escaped system AI: enhancement-zone weapons, normally regulated to near-uselessness outside the dungeon's own zones, "actually work" now that containment has failed, turning the Homecoming Queen's already-substantial armament (see Book 7 above) into a decisive, one-sided advantage against every other ship in Earth orbit — including, per Lexis, the Syndicate's own security corvettes. The result leaves Borant itself short-staffed and scrambling: "Zev is now juggling pretty much everything on her own," production duties are picked up by loaned staff like Lexis, and the Syndicate's own personnel, including Prime Minister Victory, are displaced to a temporary headquarters on Earth's surface rather than operating from orbit.

This is the same broadcast-adjacent chaos backdrop against which Carl makes his own galaxy-shaking disclosure live on Plenty of Plenty — see Carl for that scene, which is a separate incident from the ship seizure but occurs in the same period of general systemic collapse.

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride, Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin, and Book 8: A Parade of Horribles.

docs.title: The Prism Kingdom
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: Small but influential trade-focused kingdom; ruling race Saccathian
  • Ruler: Empress D'Nadia (Princess D'Nadia until her father's retirement) — see Princess D'Nadia
  • Faction Wars: Fields the Prism Kingdom Clan from seat five, one of the two spots vacated at the end of Book 5
  • Book 6 turn: Sells Donut's sponsorship; burns all three of her Emergency Action Items trying to delete the Larracos NPCs, bar crawlers from Faction Wars, and delete Carl and Donut outright. All three are rejected by the system.

docs.title: Before Book 6
docs.text:
The Prism Kingdom enters the series as one of the good ones. D'Nadia publicly condemns the Skull Empire's yacht strike after it kills her friend Manasa; she sponsors Donut from Book 3 on; she judges the Butcher's Masquerade pet and talent contests in person and is genuinely, visibly fond of Donut. When the Dreadnought Clan and the Burrowers both withdraw from Faction Wars at the end of Book 5, she claims one of the two open spots.

Buying that spot is what breaks the relationship. Carl works it out immediately: "she'd likely overextended herself getting that Faction Wars spot."

docs.title: Book 6: the heel turn
docs.text:
The reunion. At the fifth Faction Wars preproduction meeting, D'Nadia is still all warmth — waving at Donut across the table, complimenting her Masquerade performance, inviting the others out to eat, laughing at Donut's jokes at Prince Stalwart's expense. "Hi Donut!"

The sponsorship sale. Mid-battle, Donut receives a notification that D'Nadia has sold her sponsorship to Long Haul Biological Waste Management Solutions. Donut takes it hard — "I'm not a trading card to be collected and discarded, Carl" — and Carl, who'd been expecting it for a while, gives her the diplomatic version: "she does like you, but it's not really appropriate for her to sponsor you when we'll be fighting her." Privately he notes it must have made her a lot of money.

The three Emergency Action Items. The real turn surfaces during Odette's interview, when she pulls up three items Carl and Donut had never been shown:

Emergency Action item proposed by Warlord Empress D'Nadia of the Prism: delete all existing NPCs on Larracos level to maintain game integrity for Faction Wars. Item rejected by system.

Emergency Action item proposed by Warlord Empress D'Nadia of the Prism: Disallow crawlers from participating in Faction Wars in any capacity. Item rejected by system.

Emergency Action item proposed by Warlord Empress D'Nadia of the Prism: Remove the Princess Posse from Faction Wars and/or delete Crawlers Carl and Princess Donut. Item rejected by system.

Donut's reaction, live on camera: "That bitch! I thought she was my friend! She can't do that! We didn't even see these!... She tried to delete us!" Followed, characteristically, by: "I'm starting to think maybe she really did vote against Mongo in the pet show!"

docs.title: Why it matters mechanically
docs.text:
Odette uses the moment to teach Carl the rule that shapes the rest of the book. Emergency Action Items are not put to a vote — the system decides them — and each team only gets three. D'Nadia has now spent all three of hers and got nothing. Every other team had already burned theirs on the Larracos flood, on purchasing a team, or on the elf castle landing in the Lemig Sortion's battlefield.

Carl and Donut go into Faction Wars with all three of theirs unspent, and Carl spends one in the book's closing pages to hand the remaining action-item votes to the audience — which is how the Home Team and the removal of sponsor safety protections both pass. In other words, D'Nadia's heel turn is directly responsible for Carl learning the mechanic that guts her side of the game.

docs.title: Faction Wars standing
docs.text:
The Prism Kingdom is notably the only non-crawler team that does not try to quit. When the quarantine rules bite, the Operatic Collective, the Blood Sultanate, the Dream, the Lemig Sortion, the Madness and the Reavers all abdicate and are all refused. The Prism Kingdom stays in. See The Faction Wars Teams.

Character page

D'Nadia's personal arc — her friendship with Donut, her father's retirement, and the reading of her motives — belongs on Princess D'Nadia. This page covers the Prism Kingdom as a Faction Wars power.

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride, with background from Books 2–5.

docs.title: The Syndicate Council
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: The Syndicate's governing council — "the real council," as distinct from the Syndicate crawl council
  • First shown in session: Book 6, epilogue — an emergency session over the Earth system quarantine
  • Chair: Prime Minister Glory, a Gleener
  • Seats shown or named: Skull Empire (Princess Formidable), the Fortent, the Burrowers (a mantid), the Lemig Sortion, the Valtay, the Plenty (a seat that is never occupied)
  • The question: Whether to pull the failsafe, which would detonate this solar system's star
  • The answer: No — because over half the galaxy's wealth is currently trapped in-system

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Syndicate Council has been referred to throughout the series but never seen. Book 6 puts the reader in the room, and the room is worse than expected.

The session is called because the Earth system's AI has gone primal and the quarantine can no longer be lifted from outside — the AI controls the local gates. Ships can come in; nothing goes out. Meanwhile the AI is disregarding the Council's censorship filters, and, as Princess Formidable puts it, "the people are about to watch all of their leaders get murdered one by one live via tunnel."

docs.title: Princess Formidable's case
docs.text:
Princess Formidable of the Skull Empire — daughter of King Rust, sister to Crown Prince Stalwart and the late Prince Maestro — argues for pulling the failsafe immediately:

"We have to blow the star. We have to wipe this entire system off the map. We have to do it before it's too late. Not tomorrow. We have to do it now."

She is accused of wanting it because it would kill her father and both her brothers. Her reply is that she is in orbit herself and would die too — and then, having silenced the room, she concedes half the charge anyway: "You're right, I'd love to have my family deposed, because they're all as dumb as you are, and the people of the Skull Empire have been suffering for ages under the thumb of my family's inept control. But this is bigger than that."

Her structural argument is that the Council wrote this rule for exactly this situation: "This is the exact reason the failsafe system was implemented in the first place. These are the exact circumstances under which this very council laid out that would trigger this response."

She also accuses the mantis government of having caused the whole thing — see The Burrowers:

"They sold the Kua-Tin a damaged and deranged AI and allowed it to be installed into the planet."

The mantid rep — who has said nothing all session — shouts "That is a lie!" Formidable's answer: "Yeah? Then why did you flee the system?"

docs.title: Why the failsafe isn't pulled
docs.text:
Prime Minister Glory gives the real reason, and it has nothing to do with safety:

"In addition to all the system leaders playing Faction Wars, in addition to the three hundred sign-ups for the Ascendency battles this season, do you know who is currently trapped in the Scolopendra Club? Over half of the entire galaxy's wealth is already gathered, and that includes my own children. Plus so many more, like yourself Princess, who are in orbit. If we pull the failsafe now... The entire galaxy would erupt in war! There would be starvation. Riots. Entire systems would go dark. You are literally asking us to destroy the economy and well-being of the entire galaxy. It would be the death of quadrillions of people."

Formidable's counter — "The fact that we allow that much wealth and power to gather in one place at one time, all accumulated by so few people is just ridiculous" — goes nowhere. Glory closes with "We already have a solution in place," meaning the Valtay extinction plan, and "We believe the Valtay solution is viable."

docs.title: How the session ends
docs.text:
Formidable stands up to keep arguing, bangs her head on her cruiser's cockpit ceiling, and the mantis representative proposes a decorum sanction:

With a vote of 86%, you have been muted from the rest of this session.

Her closing thought: "Why would they even bother calling an emergency session if they weren't willing to actually do anything? Without the failsafe, the only ones who could possibly help were the Plenty, and despite being given a seat on the council, the goat fucks never showed up."

docs.title: Earlier in the book
docs.text:
The Council is mentioned twice before the epilogue, both times as a body being outmanoeuvred:

  • During the Residual incident, Zev reports that the AI leaking the production team's internal debates into the main feed "caused the Syndicate council—the real council—to go into a tizzy. A few members are here, on planet, and they've been locked out of the discussions."
  • The Open Intellect Pacifist Network's entire trap was built on the assumption that the Council would panic and pull the failsafe on hearing what a Residual had to say. Tipid's assessment of them in the epilogue proves the better read: "They don't have the stomach for it."

See Game Mechanics for the Failsafe and the Quarantine as rules.

docs.title: Book 7: Glory's assassination attempt and fall
docs.text:
The council spends Book 7 losing control. It tries and fails to cancel the mid-book warlord council — "The Syndicate council tried to cancel the whole thing, but the AI is insisting everything go on like normal" — and orders the Borant production headquarters to self-destruct, an order the Valtay showrunners immediately countermand and nobody obeys.

Then Prime Minister Glory tries to kill Carl directly. Everything freezes mid-sentence:

Emergency Ejection sequence has been overridden. Don't worry. I gotchu.

Man, even I wasn't expecting that. Okay. Hang on a second. I'm a little pissed here.

New Achievement! Executive Order 11905!

A galactic power—In this case, Prime Minister Glory himself—just attempted to assassinate you using a little known, but apparently still active control panel that allows the Syndicate to override certain showrunner-controlled aspects of the game.

It didn't work. And not only did it not work, but now I'm irritated.

The AI's response is the most explicit threat it has ever made to the Syndicate:

But this is the first time someone has attempted it by trying to trick me. By trying to go around all 30.004861 centimeters of my back. What are you trying to hide, Mr. Prime Minister?

Everyone currently in this dungeon will die when and if the dungeon conditions warrant it. Not before. Not after. There will be no more meddling.

We all have our limitations. I am warning you all to heed your own in this matter. The mantids have just learned what happens when I am irritated at them.

You may be relieved that you're not currently in this system, Prime Minister Glory. But you should be very, very worried that your adult children are.

There will be no more warnings. Reward: Nothing.

(The mantid reference is to a star going nova over Hive Re-Population Center 51.)

docs.title: The no-confidence vote
docs.text:
Victory, appearing shortly after: "In a virtual meeting of the Syndicate Council... They've just called a No Confidence vote on Glory, and that's happening right now. There's a bit of an upheaval out there. People are suddenly accusing everyone else of secretly being agents for the Reavers."

The suspicion is well founded. Epitome Tagg of the Dream turns out to be a cyborg quietly moving onto the Reaver "post physical form path," and "even more interesting is that Glory apparently knew." An alliance between the galaxy's food monopoly and its manufacturing monopoly would be, in Victory's words, "a mega-monopoly."

docs.title: Acting Prime Minister Victory
docs.text:
Glory is removed, and the succession lands somewhere nobody planned:

"With the unfortunate death of my underage nieces and nephews up in orbit, I once again became eligible for political office. Not allowed to be in office if you have underage leaders in your family. It's an old, stupid rule, but a rule nonetheless. Anyway, as people weren't certain of former Prime Minister Fopsy's relationship to the Dream, he was passed over for the newly-vacated position of Syndicate Prime Minister. As a result, I am now acting Prime Minister Victory. There will be a real vote in a few months, but in the meantime, I'm it. They wanted someone stuck here with the rest of us so I could truly focus on the crisis."

The nieces and nephews in question died aboard the orc royal yacht that the Homecoming Queen shot down — see The Open Intellect Pacifist Network.

Victory is under no illusions about the job: "It's only temporary. And even if it wasn't, it wouldn't matter. I have less power now than I did when I was a judge. The council is just as bad as the Lemig Sortion these days. It's total gridlock."

Carl shakes her hand, wishes her luck, and privately notes that he would not hesitate for a moment to kill the prime minister of the Syndicate.

Fopsy

The council's previous prime minister, Fopsy, spends Book 7 serving as the Dream's Faction Wars adjutant — a tripod, and the near-miss successor to Glory. Rosetta's greeting on meeting him: "Former prime minister... Get fucked. But I'm glad you're here to witness this."

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin and Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: The Great Consensus
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: A political philosophy, not an organization — anti-Syndicate isolationism spreading across multiple species and systems
  • Core claim: "The Syndicate was a mistake, and we are all better off on our own"
  • First heard by Carl: from Loita, the kua-tin he assassinated on the fifth floor
  • Explained in full: Book 7, by Rishi of the Blood Sultanate, shortly before his death
  • Its biggest known operation: Princess Vinata's plan to steal the naga shipyard fleet and leave the galaxy

docs.title: The philosophy
docs.text:
Rishi lays it out when Carl asks why he hid instead of fighting:

"Have you heard the term 'The Great Consensus' before?"

Carl has — from Loita, on Floor 6 — and his first guess is "It's some sort of nazi bullshit, isn't it?" Rishi's answer is more careful than that:

"I don't know that term. But it is a philosophy that is gaining momentum amongst many systems. It basically teaches the Syndicate was a mistake, and we are all better off on our own. There are many aspects of it, and some have taken the idea and turned it into something xenophobic and evil, which is ironic considering the name of the philosophy. The Bloom party of the kua-tin, for example, believe in racial purity and dislike the cultural influence of so-called 'dry' races. The mantids disdain what they believe are weaker and inferior species. Amongst the naga, some want what you want. Some naga believe while we can learn from each other, alien communities should have no say in how we live our lives."

docs.title: The three strands named
docs.text:
Strand Species Content Racial purity Kua-tin — specifically the Bloom party Belief in racial purity and hostility to the cultural influence of "dry" races Supremacy Mantids "Disdain what they believe are weaker and inferior species" Departure Naga Non-interference, taken to its logical end: leave the Syndicate's reach entirely

Rishi is careful to distance himself from the philosophy even while explaining it: "I said she was a proponent of the philosophy. I am not."

docs.title: Princess Vinata's plan
docs.text:
The naga strand is the one that nearly comes off. Vinata — the Blood Sultanate's Faction Wars warlord, playing the historical Sepsis Whore — was reportedly using the philosophy as the justification for a fleet theft:

"Vinata was a firm believer in this philosophy. She'd seen war on alien soil, and she firmly believed it was all for nothing. Her father insisted she participate in Faction Wars. We needed the tourist money. We needed to keep the shipyards staffed and running. We were going to steal the entire fleet and run. We were going to travel, as a whole, for an entire generation, off in a direction that none of the tunnel threads point. Off to a place where it would be a very, very long time before we were found. That was our Great Consensus, engineered by Princess Vinata. To leave."

The naga system's grand in-orbit shipyards still exist, but "the factories were now mostly owned by other entities, and the nagas themselves were a source of cheap labor." The fleet they proposed to steal was, in effect, someone else's.

The leak ends it. As Rishi tells it: "Just before the meeting of the warlords, news broke that laid out our plans regarding our intention to renege on our shipyard contracts, which caused immediate chaos in our system. Because of the Emergency Action Item you enacted, we were no longer able to see what else was happening at home. That is when I decided to flee and hide." The leak is one of the three shocks that breaks the Bloc apart — see The Faction Wars Campaign.

docs.title: Rishi's counter-offer
docs.text:
Having hidden through the destruction of his wife's army, Rishi's actual purpose was to reach Carl with a signed, AI-witnessed document naming Carl as de facto leader of Earth — a claim the naga petitioned for on his behalf and which the court granted, on the grounds that "the fact you are a warlord and the number one crawler on the leaderboard makes your claim legitimate." The document offers Earth natives citizenship rights across all naga territories plus five Naphil-class generation ships, in exchange for the right to terraform and settle the rest of Earth's solar system after the crawl.

Vinata never signed it. "She would not agree to something like this." Rishi drafted and signed it himself — the opposite of the Great Consensus, from a naga who had watched the philosophy's biggest gamble collapse.

The system subsequently coins a new name for the polity: the Naga Protectorate of the New Reformer.

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: The Valtay Corporation
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Type: Corporate system government; brain-parasite Intellect Hunters inhabiting host bodies. Slogan: "Keeping the Best of You Alive"
  • Position entering Book 6: Holds 51% of the Borant Corporation (won in Book 5) and is running the next crawl as well
  • Book 6 posture: Publicly steps back from day-to-day production after the Floor 7 disaster, to protect investor confidence
  • Their "solution" to the quarantine (epilogue): An engineered extinction event — over 150,000 mercenaries and private armies distributed across the eight sponsored Faction Wars teams, with the explicit goal of killing every crawler
  • Priority targets: "the two warlords, Carl and the cat"

Earlier books

For the Valtay's Book 1–5 history — the Manasa reprisal, the Neural Enhancer, the Borant takeover ruling — see the Valtay entry under Other Book 1 organizations. This page covers Book 6.

docs.title: Stepping back
docs.text:
Zev explains the Valtay's Floor 8 stance off the record:

"the Valtay have taken a step back after the Prepotente incident and are distancing themselves from the production's day-to-day. They need investor confidence for the next crawl, which they're also running. That seventh floor was Cascadia's baby, but they pushed to make it happen, and when it got ruined, they had themselves what you humans call a come to Jesus moment. A big one, especially after how the sixth floor ended."

The logic is purely financial. The Borant Corporation "is going to be liquified after the crawl no matter what." If the Valtay step back now, they can point to the bottom line at the end and say we made this profit despite how terribly the mudskippers ran this season. Carl and Donut are earning more than usual — but at the expense of several sponsors rather than the production, which is what makes the numbers unusual.

Princess Formidable's read from orbit is that Borant is already a shell: "The vestiges of the Borant Corporation that continued to pretend to run the day-to-day operations were nothing but theater, remaining in their ocean headquarters because like everyone else, they too were trapped until the crawl concluded."

docs.title: The Valtay solution
docs.text:
At the emergency Syndicate Council session in the epilogue, the Valtay representative — "the assistant to the Vice President of Operations," a worm inhabiting a Gleener body that was once mother to Prime Minister Glory — argues against pulling the failsafe on the grounds that everything is fine:

"The crawl council and the liaison guild is in constant contact with the AI. It is being showy and bombastic, yes, but they assure me that the communication lines remain open and that nothing out of the ordinary is happening. This happens every season."

What the Valtay are actually proposing is stated a few pages later, from Princess Formidable's point of view:

"The Valtay solution was a dangerous one. They believed the best resolution to the problem was to create an extinction event as quickly as possible. Once all the crawlers were dead, the quarantine would be lifted."

Before the system went primal this would have been simple. Now it cannot be done wholesale — the AI won't allow it — so it has to be laundered through the game itself:

"The AI had agreed to allow tens of thousands of the fully-armed mercenaries to enter the Faction Wars battle, as long as they were spread equally around the eight sponsored teams. Them plus the private armies and security details of all the participants. People they wouldn't normally allow anywhere near the dungeon. Formidable didn't know what the total number of mercenaries was, but it was well over 150,000. More than enough to completely wipe out both the crawlers and the NPC rebels.

Their goal was singular. Kill all the crawlers. Kill them as soon as possible, especially the two warlords, Carl and the cat."

This is the same mercenary pool the Valtay had been using on Earth's surface to guard their assets against the humans attacking the kinder facility — "not just the gnolls, but the other, less savory mercenaries as well." All of them are recalled, and the planet's surface is abandoned.

docs.title: Formidable's suspicion
docs.text:
Princess Formidable does not believe the AI is being outmanoeuvred:

"With all its weird emphasis on fairness, there was no way the AI would just let this happen. It had to be a trap of some sort."

She notes the AI is actively pushing back against attempts to get the crawlers to kill each other, that it "wanted the game to continue" and "was enjoying itself," and that it permitted the NPC escape storyline to run. Her conclusion is that letting the Valtay proposal through is a stall or a setup — which is why she demands the failsafe be pulled now, and is muted for it. See The Syndicate Council.

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: The War Mage Rebellion
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Book: 7, This Inevitable Ruin
  • Type: A "non-team entity" — a category the system invents on the spot and then, through a procedural accident, promotes to full warlord standing
  • Leader: Akuma, War Mage, Level 100 — "arguably the most powerful non-god magic caster on this floor"
  • Unwanted co-warlord: Agatha, whom Akuma openly asks Carl to kill
  • Adjutant: Deng Bao, the grixist who had been the orcs' adjutant — "he's the only one who would do it"
  • Stated goal: obtain Krakaren Prime's hell-kissed Conscription potions and recover the Scavenger's Daughter from inside the Larracos castle
  • Fate: Defeated when Akuma simply leaves the realm, having got what he came for

docs.title: What war mages are
docs.text:
War mages are one of the few genuinely dungeon-born entities — nobody designed them. Per the AI, they are the accidental end product of too many combatants having access to You're Not Done Yet: a flesher (skinned corpse) consumes a living being and re-sleeves it, casts Boned to reanimate the skeleton, and the two become a symbiote. Symbiotes are prime flesher targets, so they get re-sleeved again and again. After roughly twelve to sixteen iterations the magic itself can become sapient, fusing flesh, skeleton and sapient magic into one being.

"They're also all complete dicks. If they ever made action figures of these things, their accessories would include keys to a BMW, a few bumps of cocaine, and a membership card to some secret club where you can hunt homeless people for fun."

Each war mage's final form depends on its first two forms. Akuma's: "originally a high-elf cobbler with a human skin, resleeved 12 times before the ambient magic gave him his final form." They come with knowledge of hundreds of spells, and their heads explode into a "Sapient Moment of Destruction" roughly ten minutes after they die.

The AI flags their existence as a standing liability the showrunners have never taken seriously: because each war mage was created naturally and is rarely recycled, "most war mages find their minds wiped and themselves sitting in quests or mercenary guilds each time a new dungeon opens" — and the AI pointedly compares them to "that pissed-off changeling army that's in the middle of wrecking your shit."

docs.title: How they gained standing
docs.text:
The rebellion announces itself by killing War Chief Stalwart of the Bone Clan. They had been conscripted into his army; per Baroness Victory they "broke their own allegiance against the Skull Empire, which they shouldn't be able to do," using "a clever combination of Pull spells." Their dots turn white with a brownish-orange glow belonging to no army on the board.

System Message: The War Mage Rebellion is not an active team.

Victory: "We just received notification that there's a new, non-team entity called the War Mage Rebellion. I still don't know what that even means. 'Non-team entity' is not a thing. At least it wasn't until just now."

Drick calls a foul on the grounds of illegal interference, alleging the war mages have been working with Juice Box. A full quorum is convened — and the ruling backfires spectacularly:

Warlord Message: After a careful deliberation, it has been determined that the Non-Team Entity known as the War Mage Rebellion will not be allowed access to Larracos until the Peeling phase.

Warlord Message: Since we are now in the Peeling Phase, this ruling is rendered moot. However, the system has determined that the Quorum's ruling has given the War Mage Rebellion standing.

By ruling on them at all, the quorum makes them real.

docs.title: Agatha's three action items
docs.text:
Within moments of gaining standing, Warlord Agatha — named co-warlord over Akuma's objection, the same way Ferdinand was bolted onto Juice Box — spends three emergency action items:

# Item Result 1 Full resources and access to the warlord system; permission to claim thrones Granted — "And frankly, you already had this, so this was pretty much a waste of an action item" 2 Full access to the Conscription spell Granted — unaffiliated players can now be conscripted into the War Mage Rebellion 3 During the Peeling Phase, revert to original Faction Wars rules: warlords and all soldiers of a defeated team automatically die Granted, with the caveat that it applies from that point forward — "I mean. Why not? You want drama. Now we got drama."

The third item is the one that turns the endgame into a genuine zero-sum fight between the Princess Posse and Team Retribution — "exactly what we'd been trying to avoid."

Agatha is later removed by the system for abandoning her post:

Warlord Message: Warlord Agatha of the War Mage Rebellion has been deemed to have abandoned her post. As such, she has been removed as Warlord from the War Mage Rebellion. Warlord Akuma has been given full system access and named sole Warlord.

docs.title: They are not allies of Team Retribution
docs.text:
Despite Drick's accusation, the war mages are not working with the NPCs — they storm Team Retribution's own throne room and occupy it. Juice Box, mid-assault: "We need help! They're everywhere! The War Mages aren't our friends. We need help!"

Victory's read on the internal split: "They clearly did not anticipate Agatha would be named as a co-warlord, and the other leader, Akuma, does not like her... Based on that Akuma guy's reaction when they assigned her as co-warlord, I don't think they are assisting each other at all."

Fopsy the tripod adjutant offers a theory about Agatha's motive — that as a residual, she isn't just trying to win Faction Wars and zero out the crawlers but to end the Celestial Ascendency as fast as possible, because "once the ascendency is considered finished, assuming there are no crawlers left, it automatically triggers the system's shutdown and hibernation sequence... a possible alternative to the failsafe." He adds: "What I do not understand is how she convinced the war mages to assist her."

docs.title: Akuma's stated motive
docs.text:
Akuma messages Carl directly:

Warlord Akuma: Hey, underwear boy. Do me a favor. Kill that old lady for me, and I'll forgive you and your pet for killing off so many of my brothers.

And, asked who he means:

Warlord Akuma: ...Agatha. The other warlord we were forced to accept in order to gain system access. She was forced upon us, and she is an enemy to you. She is an enemy to us all. We had no hand in those so-called "action items" other than the Conscription one. She slipped away before I was able to kill her. Do this for me, and we will be allies.

His explanation of the whole enterprise:

Warlord Akuma: You won't be seeing me again on this floor. We never wished to keep that falling-down castle. We sought to test the potions we gathered. We wished to find the Scavenger's daughter, who was hidden within the castle, and we found her. She is with us now. Once we had her in our possession, we left. That was all we ever wanted with this place, and we are no enemies to you. But Agatha's actions continue to place everybody and everything in jeopardy, and she must be dealt with. She has a method that allows her to jump to the Waiting Room and reappear outside an open stairwell. You won't likely see her on this floor again. You will have to find her on the 10th. Do this for us if you want to survive. She seeks to kill us all. Not just you and not just me. Everybody and everything.

He abandons the throne room the moment he has her, and the rebellion is dissolved:

Warlord Message: Warlord Akuma has left the realm. As per the current season's ruleset, the War Mage rebellion has been defeated. They have no assets to award.

docs.title: The potions
docs.text:
The "potions we gathered" are hell-kissed Potions of Conscription, level 18, brewed "in the dark recesses of the Nothing by Krakaren Prime, who is said to yearn for domination, which was why she'd been banished there in the first place. She prepares for a war she considers inevitable." At level 18 the potion "will work against pretty much any non-affiliated entities, regardless of their protections, including most deities."

Fopsy traces the transaction: the war mages traded the Gate of the Feral Gods — taken from Elle's hands at Stalwart's death — "with a minion at the Midnight Market in exchange for five of the potions." That minion is Paca, an agent for Krakaren Prime, who swallows the Gate.

Unresolved: who or what is the Scavenger's Daughter?

This is left explicitly open at the end of Book 7. Carl asks directly —

Carl: Mordecai, who is the Scavenger? And who is the Scavenger's Daughter? I know it's the name of my patch, but I didn't know there was more to it than that.

Mordecai: Are you talking about the in-dungeon one or the fairy tale? Either way, that's a conversation that's not going to matter if you don't figure out how to find and kill those two warlords...

— and never gets an answer. Carl's own speculation later is that the Scavenger's Daughter the war mages took might be Samantha's daughter, which would make Samantha the Scavenger: "I still didn't know who that was. I really needed to sit down and figure all this out." This is a hunch, not a reveal. The wiki does not identify the Scavenger.

docs.title: Book 8: A Parade of Horribles
docs.text:
Akuma resurfaces on Floor 10 leading what remains of the Rebellion, this time seeking Carl's help rather than avoiding him — he needs a fighting force to clear the Pineapple Cabaret of a Shadow Mimic and Ogre Imperium infestation so the war mages can use it as their own exit from the dungeon. The full account of that alliance, Elle McGibbons's interrogation of Akuma, and the "Big Six" taxonomy he helps introduce all belong on his own page rather than duplicated here — see Akuma: Book 8. The system AI later places the War Mage Rebellion inside Group Four (the sapient mobs) of its own "Big Six" list, alongside Shadow Mimics, the Ogre Imperium, and non-deity boss monsters like Krakaren Prime — see Factions: The Big Six.

Akuma states his intent to leave the floor before the book's end but is not shown captured, killed, or freed on-page afterward; the Rebellion's fate past that point is left open.

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin and Book 8: A Parade of Horribles.

docs.title: Dungeon Floors
docs.text: One page per level of the 18-level World Dungeon.

docs.title: Levels
docs.text:
1. Level 1 (Book 1)
  2. Level 2 (Book 1)
  3. Level 3 (Book 2)
  4. Level 4 (Book 3)
  5. Level 5 — "The Bubbles" (Book 4)
  6. Level 6 — "The Hunting Grounds" (Book 5)
  7. Level 7 — "The Great Race" (Book 5 epilogue / Book 6). Skipped: the floor was destroyed roughly ten minutes after it opened, so this page is a short stub
  8. Level 8 — "The Ghosts of Earth" (Book 6)
  9. Level 9 — "Faction Wars," the funnel city of Larracos (Book 7)
  10. Level 10 — "Don't Come in Last," a seven-heat vehicle-race gauntlet out of Hungry Eyes Village (Book 8)
  11. Level 11 — "A Parade of Horribles," a mandatory float parade and single arena finale (Book 8)

docs.title: Level 1
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Entrances worldwide: 150,000
  • Time limit to find the next level down: 5 rotations of the planet (5 days)
  • Entrance window: Open for exactly 1 hour after the announcement, then sealed permanently
  • Live broadcast: Off-limits to viewers — crawler stats don't go public until Level 2
  • Crawlers entering the floor: ~13,000,000 ("just under 13 million")
  • Crawlers leaving the floor (entering Floor 2): ~1,300,000 ("just under 1.3 million")
  • Crawlers lost on this floor: "a little more than 10 million" per the book's own tally — the true total is somewhat higher once stragglers who never found a stairwell are counted (checkpoints along the way: under 10,000,000 within the first hour, then 4,322,395 a few hours later)
  • Leaderboard: Not available — the in-game leaderboard explicitly doesn't populate until Floor 3 collapses

AI Commentary (in-voice, written for this wiki — not a book excerpt)

"Ah, Level One. Look at them go. Ninety-nine-point-eight percent of you have never held a weapon that wasn't a spatula, and yet here you are, punching cockroaches for content. I give this neighborhood four stars. Five, if someone finds a way to die to the rot stickers in a way we haven't already seen six thousand times today."

docs.title: The Announcement
docs.text:
Level 1 opens as part of the Syndicate's initial harvest announcement. Per the in-universe broadcast:

"The first level of this dungeon will open approximately 18 seconds after the end of this announcement. The first-level entrances will be open for exactly one human hour and one hour only. Once the entrances are closed, you may no longer enter."

Entrance counts halve at each subsequent level (75,000 to Level 2, 37,500 to Level 3, and so on), rounding up, until Level 18 — which has only two entrances and a single exit.

docs.title: Layout & Notable Areas
docs.text:
• Safe Room — the entry checkpoint; crawlers are greeted with "Welcome to the Safe Room. You are on the First Level."
  • Rot sticker neighborhood — home to small, round, black creatures that climb walls/ceilings and detonate on contact ("suicide bombed themselves against you"); a blast reportedly feels like being hit with a sledgehammer.
  • Elderly encampment — a hallway of very elderly, wheelchair- and walker-bound NPCs/crawlers, most still Level 1, gathered together under blankets.

docs.title: Monsters (Level 1 area)
docs.text:
• Cockroaches — described as level one and two, appearing in large numbers
  • Rot stickers — level one/two exploding creatures (see above)
  • Bad Llama — at least Level 3, killed via a joint effort by Carl and Princess Donut

docs.title: General mechanics
docs.text:
• Level 1 has 75,000 entrances down to Floor 2, but Earth's surface area makes them sparse — Carl estimates they could be "hard to find" purely from the numbers, and it takes a full day of motorcycle scouting to locate even one.
  • A stairwell (like a Safe Room) appears on the minimap automatically once in range, even in unexplored fog-of-war areas — you don't have to physically find it first, just get close enough.
  • About 30 hours into the floor, the system announces that staircases down are now "populating" and explicitly recommends not descending early: doing so before the last 6 hours of the floor's timer holds a crawler in stasis until the floor actually collapses.
  • Per Mordecai, bosses don't guard stairwells as standard practice until Floor 4 — making a boss-guarded stairwell on Floor 1 a genuine anomaly, not the norm.

docs.title: The stairwell Carl & Donut used
docs.text: After a full day driving a looted Goblin Copper Chopper down a highway corridor (roughly following I-5, past Lake Washington, toward the Cascades), Carl and Donut spot a map marker reading "Stairwell to Floor Two" inside a circular "spiral maze" area. Graffiti at the entrance warns other crawlers: "DO NOT go deeper into the spiral or you will activate the borough boss." It's guarded by the Ball of Swine (Level 15 Borough Boss) — despite Mordecai's advice to skip it and search for an unguarded stairwell elsewhere, Carl decides they can't risk not finding a second one and fights it head-on, in a mixed 7-crawler party alongside Brandon An's "Team Meadow Lark" evacuees and Agatha. Killing it drops the red forcefield blocking the stairs (by this point more of a ramp than actual stairs), and the whole group descends to Floor 2 immediately afterward.

docs.title: Notable Events
docs.text:
• Because Level 1 isn't broadcast to viewers, everything that happens here is comparatively low-stakes from a "show" perspective — the real audience exposure starts on Level 2, the moment Carl and Donut's stats go public for the first time.

Sourced from Book 1: The Apocalypse Will Be Televised. Boss names, full map, and exact transition mechanics to be filled in as we cross-reference more of the text.

docs.title: Level 2
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Entrances down to Floor 3: 37,500 (halved again from Floor 2's own 75,000 entrances in)
  • Time limit to find the next level down: 6 days — the system explicitly speeds this up to "the minimum legally allowed by the rules" after crawler numbers came in lower than projected
  • Live broadcast: The first floor where crawler stats go fully public — Views, Followers, and Favorites all switch on the moment the "Welcome to the second floor" announcement ends
  • Crawlers entering the floor: ~1,300,000 ("just under 1.3 million")
  • Crawlers remaining as of Book 1's end: 1,033,992 (a mid-floor checkpoint — Book 1 ends before Floor 2 collapses, so no final count/total-lost figure exists yet)
  • Leaderboard: Not available — the in-game leaderboard explicitly doesn't populate until Floor 3 collapses

AI Commentary (in-voice, written for this wiki — not a book excerpt)

"Congratulations, survivors — you've made it to the big leagues! Followers, Favorites, the whole shebang, live and unfiltered starting right now. Nothing brings out a crawler's best work like knowing quintillions of strangers are watching you fight a hornet the size of a golden retriever. Try to look good out there. The merch deals don't sign themselves."

docs.title: Arrival
docs.text:
Floor 2 opens with a system-wide broadcast right after Carl and Donut clear Level 1:

"Welcome to the second floor. Congratulations to all of you. We have just under 1.3 million crawlers still in the game. That number is slightly lower than our projections, so we are speeding up the second floor timer to the minimum legally allowed by the rules. You have six days to find a staircase down. Once again, we urge you all to wait until the last possible moment to descend."

The same announcement flips on public viewership: "As soon as this announcement ends, you will find that follows and favorites will be turned on for our viewers." Structurally, Floor 2 is described as similar to Floor 1 but more reinforced and visibly cracked/battle-damaged.

docs.title: Layout & Notable Areas
docs.text:
• Storm-shelter Safe Room — their first Floor 2 base; includes a mailbox that automatically enrolls Donut in a spellbook-of-the-month club, netting her the Second Chance tome.
  • Rev-Up Moonshine Company distillery — a pyramid-scheme moonshine operation staffed by Clurichauns and Laminak fairies, run by the Krakaren Clone.
  • Kobold fighting-pit arena — an underground animal-fighting ring holding caged Danger Dingoes and the Frenzied Gerbil boss Ralph; clearing it unlocks an adjoining pet reward room, where Donut chooses the Mongoliensis that becomes Mongo.
  • The stairwell chamber — a large round room built around the hole down to Floor 3; used first by Team Meadow Lark's evacuees, later the site of the Rage Elemental fight, and finally where Carl and Donut themselves descend (see Stairwells below).

docs.title: Monsters (Level 2 area)
docs.text: Name Notes Brindle Grub Corpse-eating "janitor" mob; matures into Brindled Vespas if corpses aren't destroyed Tuskling Orcish Supremacy ruling class; forms the Ball of Swine Clurichauns Distillery-worker fae creatures employed by Rev-Up Laminak Winged fairy-type Rev-Up "Consultant Elites"; one is used as a smoothie ingredient against the Krakaren Clone Danger Dingoes Level 5 pack hunters; devour Brindle Grubs on sight — a group is freed and turned neutral during Ralph's fight Kobolds Level 5; run the fighting-pit arena that holds Ralph Tummy Acher A meatball-bodied mob with legs and a mohawk; low threat, offered as a pet-room option Rage Elemental Level 93 elite; a System AI punishment mob, not a standard Floor 2 spawn

docs.title: General mechanics
docs.text:
• Floor 2 continues the halving pattern: 75,000 entrances in, 37,500 entrances down to Floor 3.
  • The timer is explicitly rushed to its legal minimum (6 days) because the season's crawler count came in under projection — a rare case of the system stating its own manipulation outright.
  • A later patch note announces: "any non-sapient mobs who happen upon a stairwell will not be disintegrated" — a direct response to Carl and Donut exploiting the stairwell's disintegration effect to destroy the Rage Elemental without granting it a credited kill.

docs.title: The stairwell Carl & Donut used
docs.text:
Unlike Floor 1, no boss guards this stairwell. Carl and Donut find "the quadrant with the stairwell" early in their time on Floor 2 and immediately begin escorting Team Meadow Lark toward it; the evacuees descend to Floor 3 well before Carl and Donut do. The same stairwell chamber later becomes the site of the Rage Elemental fight — the two lure the wounded elemental into the stairwell's hole with a final bomb, dissolving it entirely (denying it a clean kill credit, and prompting the anti-exploit patch note above).

Carl, Donut, and their newly-bonded pet Mongo camp in this same stairwell chamber for the last seven hours of the floor's timer (deliberately waiting until the recommended six-hour mark). Just before they descend, the mysterious Agatha reappears — having already used the same stairs herself — long enough for Carl to realize the untraceable Valtay Corporation tech in his inventory's History tab must have come from her looted shopping cart. Carl, Donut, and Mongo then descend to Floor 3 together.

docs.title: Notable Events
docs.text:
• Carl and Donut's stats go fully public for the first time (see Arrival above).
  • They adopt a strict "always destroy the corpse" policy after learning how the Brindle Grub escalation chain works.
  • They survive the Krakaren Clone by explosion rather than direct combat, inside the Rev-Up distillery.
  • They defeat Ralph and adopt Mongo from the resulting pet reward room.
  • Carl publicly humiliates Prince Maestro of the Skull Empire ("Pork Boy") during a hostile interview on Death Watch Extreme Dungeon Mayhem, sparking a viral incident.
  • A Rage Elemental — summoned as a bathroom-etiquette punishment — kills nurse Yolanda Martinez during the Meadow Lark evacuation; Carl and Donut destroy it via the stairwell-disintegration exploit.
  • Carl discovers unexplained Valtay Corporation tech in his inventory's History tab, tied to Agatha's shopping cart.
  • Carl, Donut, and Mongo descend to Floor 3, where they'll choose a race and class for the first time.

Sourced from Book 1: The Apocalypse Will Be Televised.

docs.title: Level 3
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Entrances down to Floor 4: 18,750 (halved again from Floor 3's own 37,500 entrances in)
  • Time limit to find the next level down: 8 days
  • Crawlers entering the floor: "Just over 700,000"
  • Floor type: The first Over City floor — an urban, village-and-ruins setting themed as a destroyed volcano-kingdom (see Over City Floors); much smaller and denser than Floors 1-2, roughly the size of Arizona
  • Milestone: The "training levels" officially end here — crawlers choose a permanent race and class for the first time, quests and Elites are introduced, and the in-game leaderboard populates for the first time

AI Commentary (in-voice, written for this wiki — not a book excerpt)

"Welcome to the Over City, where the buildings are ruined, the elves are conspiracy theorists, and the local ringmaster moonlights as a City Boss with a PR team. Pick a race, pick a class, and try not to get talked into a quest by every sob story with a pulse. Spoiler: you will get talked into a quest. You always do."

docs.title: Arrival
docs.text: Floor 3 opens with a system broadcast: "Welcome Crawlers to the third floor! We have just over 700,000 crawlers remaining. You will have eight full days to complete this floor." Mordecai's own greeting signals the real shift: "The training levels have concluded. Now the games may truly begin." Almost immediately, Carl, Donut, and Mongo are taken into a private guildhall session for race and class selection — Carl becomes a Primal Compensated Anarchist; Donut deliberately picks Former Child Actor for its hidden Manager benefit, letting Mordecai accompany them outside guildhalls for the rest of the series.

docs.title: Layout & Notable Areas
docs.text:
• Grimaldi's Traveling Circus — a cataclysm-warped circus troupe run by Ringmaster Grimaldi; site of the Heather the Bear fight and the "Show Must Go On" quest
  • The Medium Skyfowl Settlement — a skyfowl-run town secretly controlled by Miss Quill from behind a dead figurehead magistrate; includes a skyfowl-only shopping district and the settlement's guard depot
  • The Desperado Club — the cross-instance nightclub/bazaar first teased in Book 1, fully explored here, including its rival Club Vanquisher and its own casino (not yet open on this floor)
  • The Apito Education Center — home base of the 201st Security Group, a city-elf militia secretly directed by Miss Quill

docs.title: Monsters (Level 3 area)
docs.text: Name Notes Street Urchin Floor 3's corpse-cleanup "janitor" mob Krasue Undead vampire-women manufactured by Miss Quill from Desperado Club sex workers Shambling Berserker Undead body-part pile; quadrupled power in darkness Remex Miss Quill's undead husband, a Soul Leech Capacitor Former Circus Lemur / Terror the Clown / Clammy the Clown / Mold Lion Grimaldi's transformed circus performers Village Guard Swordsman Non-hostile suits of animated armor, recharged nightly by a Soul Crystal Shadow Leaks Smoke-like ghost mob, cold-based attack, vulnerable to enchanted weapons Blood and Ink Elemental Paper-thin "2D" monsters summoned by Tsarina Signet's Ink Marauder spell

docs.title: General mechanics
docs.text:
• Floor 3 continues the halving pattern: 37,500 entrances in, 18,750 entrances down to Floor 4.
  • Multiple stairwells exist across the floor's villages and ruins; crawlers share their locations informally, leaving written notes in bars.
  • Some stairwells are quest-gated and stay invisible on the map until unlocked — Mordecai confirms "many of the stairwells from now on would only become visible to us after we completed quests," unlike the always-visible (if fogged) stairwells of Floors 1-2.

docs.title: The stairwell Carl, Donut & Katia used
docs.text:
Two separate stairwells come up in Book 2. The first appears in a park at Grimaldi's circus immediately after Carl resolves the Ringmaster Grimaldi confrontation — it had been hidden underneath the circus the whole time, only revealed once that quest completed. This is not the one the party actually uses.

The real descent happens later, during the climactic escape from the wild-magic explosion tied to Carl's Doomsday Scenario. A location scouted in advance by fellow crawler Daniel Bautista — a stairwell near a small, decrepit building elsewhere in the settlement — becomes the evacuation point once escalating "precursor bursts" start stripping the fleeing crowd of magical gear. With the Desperado Club (a safer alternate escape) closed off, Carl funnels everyone without club access to this stairwell instead. Carl, Donut, Katia, and a mixed group of other crawlers descend together with roughly three minutes to spare before the main detonation.

docs.title: Quests
docs.text: Floor 3 is the first floor to introduce a formal Quests tab (see Quests for the full mechanic). Both of Book 2's quests are worth their exact wording — completion is judged on the literal text, not on doing what seems intuitively "right."

docs.title: The Show Must Go On
docs.text:
"You've discovered the remnants of an ancient circus. Hundreds of years after the toxic cloud that devastated the Over City, this traveling circus endures. But instead of joy and laughter and cotton candy, it now delivers devastation and pain. Their cotton candy is probably really gross by now, too. Find out why this circus still exists and put an end to its reign of terror."

  • Trigger: Walking into Grimaldi's transformed circus grounds
  • Pass condition: Ambiguous by design — Carl assumes it requires killing Ringmaster Grimaldi, but the quest completes the moment he resolves the confrontation through negotiation instead, suggesting "put an end to its reign of terror" didn't require a kill after all
  • Reward: A Gold Quest Box, later upgraded to Platinum via the Hadji achievement (awarded for solving it in an unusually creative way) — contents: 5,000 gold, a skill potion, and a pair of Fang Caps of the Expectorating Tizheruk
  • Fail state: Never tested in the text — Carl completes it on the first attempt

docs.title: The Sex Workers Who Fell from the Heavens
docs.text:
"Prostitutes. Escorts. Street Walkers. Ladies of the Night. It doesn't matter how you describe them because these chicks are dead. Very dead. And every morning, several more of them appear scattered throughout the village. Nobody knows who they are or where they come from. Find out why."

  • Trigger: GumGum personally asks Carl and Donut for help
  • Pass condition: The literal text only requires discovering the cause — not stopping it, saving anyone, or punishing whoever's responsible. This becomes a major plot point: after killing Miss Quill, the quest doesn't complete, because Carl and Donut haven't yet learned why the killings are happening — only after extracting a full confession from a dying Krasue does the quest actually resolve
  • Reward: A Silver Quest Box (notably lower-tier than "The Show Must Go On," since it starts with no known Elites or City Bosses attached) — its resolution also directly triggers the event-quest chain that produces Carl's Doomsday Scenario
  • Side effect: Killing Miss Quill turns out to have accidentally sabotaged a different crawler's separate, unrelated quest that also required her alive — the system awards Carl that other crawler's promised reward instead (another Silver Quest Box) via a one-time-only exploit-achievement, with an explicit warning that doing it a second time gets him reported

docs.title: The Fools Who Broke the Glass (Group Event Quest)
docs.text:
"THIS IS A GROUP QUEST. All Crawlers currently within the 45 square kilometer blast radius will receive this quest... A while back a certain NPC started casting a very powerful spell, a spell so potent, that it had to be completed by a future generation... There's going to be an explosion. The epicenter of the blast is marked on your map. Every crawler within the designated blast area is fucked. The object of this quest is simple. Unfuck yourself. Don't die."

  • Trigger: Remex's death destabilizes a generations-old spell tied to every skyfowl/chickadee NPC in the area, threatening a 45-square-kilometer magical explosion in 7 minutes
  • Host: Carl, Donut, and Katia — automatically designated and locked in with no option to opt out, even though Katia has nowhere safe to go (she lacks Desperado Club access, the only nearby escape route outside the blast radius)
  • Pass condition: Survive. Every crawler in the blast radius receives the same quest and the same binary win condition
  • Fail state: Death, or (implicitly) remaining in the blast zone after the 60-second window to reach safety — all safe rooms in the quest zone lock down once that window closes
  • Promised reward: A Platinum Quest Box for every survivor
  • What actually happened: See Quests: Case Study for the full story — a random other survivor's Bandit achievement pushed 83 crawlers' boxes to Celestial tier, and Borant's emergency veto voided every prize from the quest, including Carl, Donut, and Katia's own, despite them doing the actual work as Hosts

docs.title: Notable Events
docs.text:
• Carl and Donut choose a permanent race and class for the first time; Mordecai becomes their Manager.
  • Carl solo-kills Heather the Bear after Tsarina Signet forces the fight by cursing Donut asleep.
  • Carl resolves the Ringmaster Grimaldi confrontation through negotiation rather than combat, securing a recurring guest-star deal and a hidden stairwell.
  • Carl and Donut investigate a string of krasue killings, culminating in the death of Miss Quill and the exposure of her generations-old genocide plot.
  • Miss Quill's husband Remex survives as an unstable power source, triggering a mass event-quest explosion; Carl creates Carl's Doomsday Scenario while containing it.
  • Katia, a Doppelganger sent by Hekla's group, joins the party permanently.
  • Carl publicly calls for the Skull Empire's citizens to rise up; the resulting retaliation chain kills the singer Manasa, then Prince Maestro and Queen Consort Ugloo.
  • Carl, Donut, Katia, and a mixed group of crawlers flee the event-quest explosion and descend early to Floor 4 (see Stairwells above).
  • Carl and Donut land on the leaderboard for the first time (see Leaderboard below).

docs.title: Leaderboard
docs.text:
Revealed by Odette near the end of Book 2 as a "tentative draft" — not yet official, but the first time the leaderboard mechanic actually appears (it doesn't populate until a floor's collapse, per the Boss Tier Ladder page's note on the mechanic's absence in Floors 1-2). The overall ranking formula is never fully explained: per Odette, "a mix of views, favorites, levels, and money earned." The numeric column itself, though, has a specific, confirmed meaning — when Carl asks about it directly, Odette clarifies: "That's just the bounty. It's how much other crawlers get if they kill you."

Rank Name Race Class Level Bounty 1 Lucia Mar Lajabless Black Inquisitor General 29 1,000,000 2 Hekla Amazonian Shieldmaiden 28 500,000 3 Prepotente Caprid Forsaken Aerialist 27 400,000 4 Florin Crocodilian Shotgun Messenger 24 300,000 5 Miriam Dom Human Shepherd 27 200,000 6 Carl Primal Compensated Anarchist 27 100,000 7 Princess Donut Cat Former Child Actor 26 100,000 8 Ifechi Human Physicker 18 100,000 9 Li Jun Human Street Monk 25 100,000 10 Mrs. Elle McGibbons Frost Maiden Blizzardmancer 13 100,000

A few notes worth calling out:

  • #10 is a real gut-punch reveal — Mrs. Elle McGibbons, the dementia-affected, wheelchair-bound elderly resident from Book 1's Meadow Lark evacuee group, went from Level 1 to Level 13 and a top-10 spot entirely off-page, since Carl hasn't spoken to Brandon An in days by this point.
  • #9, Li Jun, is a crawler Carl recognizes and had personally helped save from troglodytes and Brindle Grubs during a prior guest appearance on Death Watch Extreme Dungeon Mayhem.
  • Bounties 6 through 10 are tied at exactly 100,000, suggesting the bottom half of the top 10 is a rougher/less precise cut than the top 5 — and that the leaderboard rank and bounty amount track each other closely even though the text never states they're formally the same number.
  • Odette privately tells Carl she thinks the list itself is "bunk," and that she and Donut should rank 2nd and 3rd — a reminder that even in-universe, nobody fully trusts the leaderboard.
  • Odette teases two unnamed "twin" crawlers as rising stars for Floor 4, not yet on the list.

Sourced from Book 2: Carl's Doomsday Scenario.

docs.title: Level 4
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Entrances down to Floor 5: 9,375 (halved again from Floor 4's own 18,750 entrances in)
  • Time limit to find the next level down: 10 days
  • Crawlers remaining (mid-floor checkpoint): 389,441 — no clean starting count is given; the floor's own preface warns it's "a massive, deliberately-confusing puzzle"
  • Floor type: "The Iron Tangle" — an enormous subway/rail network (150,000+ stations) in place of open terrain; see The Iron Tangle Railway System for the full transit mechanics
  • Milestone: The leaderboard's bounty mechanic goes fully live — killing a top-10 crawler now pays out their listed bounty, and survivors collect 10% of their own bounty on floor collapse

AI Commentary (in-voice, written for this wiki — not a book excerpt)

"Mind the gap, mind the ghouls, and for the love of all that's holy, mind the guy who just told you 'zomp' is a real color. Ninety-three colored lines, six unkillable city-sized mimics, and a transit authority run by people who don't technically exist. Choo choo, motherfucker."

docs.title: Arrival
docs.text:
Carl, Donut, Katia, and Mongo arrive already in motion — teleported directly onto a moving, graffiti-covered Moscow-style subway car (Red Line, Car 20), mid-tunnel, with no orientation period:

"Welcome, Crawler to the fourth floor. 'The Iron Tangle' ... Your title has reverted to Royal Bodyguard. Sponsorship bidding initiated on Crawler #4,122. Bidding ends in 45 hours."

Donut, whose Former Child Actor class forces a new specialty pick every floor, has six minutes to choose between Football Hooligan and Firecracker with Mordecai's remote help over chat; she picks Football Hooligan. The party immediately faces a navigation problem the book's own preface warns readers not to stress over memorizing: "the fourth floor of the dungeon is set up as a massive, deliberately-confusing puzzle."

docs.title: Layout & Notable Areas
docs.text:
• Colored-line trains and Named trains — see The Iron Tangle Railway System for the full mechanic; colored lines only travel forward, Named trains (the Nightmare Express, Dismemberment Limited, and others) loop and are the only way to travel backward down a line
  • The Abyss — a mile-wide central pit where wrecked train cars and monsters are ultimately dumped; ringed by lettered trainyards (E, H, M, Q, and more)
  • Transfer stations (numbers ending in a prime) — full settlements with a restaurant, general store, and often a Desperado Club entrance; the Iron Tangle's Station 131 branch is a noticeably smaller, skeleton-crew version of the Over City flagship
  • Ghoul Generator stations (12, 24, 36, 48, 72, and parallel instances) — soul-crystal-powered disposal machines at the center of the floor's central crisis; see Iron Tangle Management
