  • Station 75's "Downward Dog" tavern — home of Growler Gary, the indestructible bartender whose severed hand keys the rapid-response interdiction carts
  • Station 433/Terminus — lair of Mimic Rex, one of six floor-wide Station Mimics, and (once she's gone) the site of a hidden level stairwell

docs.title: Monsters (Level 4 area)
docs.text:
Name Notes Drek Swarming, demonic-baby horde mob Jikininki First-tier ghoul "janitor" mob in the corpse-disposal pipeline Mantaur Centaur-bull warriors devoted to Grull; staff the trains as "engineers" — see Species and Gore-Gore the Mantaur Jabbering Jibber-Jabber Rhinoceros-sized minion of Mimic Rex; splits when killed Festering / Blister / Wrath Ghouls Escalating withdrawal-mutation tiers from the Rev-Up Vitamin Shot; Wrath Ghouls can fuse into a Province Boss Razor Fox (Stage 3 DTs) Terminal DT mutation; explodes into Krakaren Crotch Dumplings on death Dismember the War Mage Commands the Dismemberment Limited's Flesher army; killed by Carl's party via a Hole-spell decapitation Growler Gary Indestructible Shade Gnoll bartender — see Iron Tangle Management

See the Mobs overview for the full Floor 4 catalog — this floor introduces more mob variety than any prior one.

docs.title: Quests
docs.text: No individually-named discovery quest is called out for Floor 4 the way "The Show Must Go On" or "The Sex Workers Who Fell from the Heavens" were on Floor 3 — the floor's central crisis (the ghoul-generator overload) plays out as an open, floor-wide survival effort rather than a personal quest chain, coordinated informally between Carl's group and allies like Imani C, Elle McGibbons, Li Jun, and Daniel Bautista rather than triggered by a system quest card.

docs.title: General mechanics
docs.text:
• Floor 4 continues the halving pattern: 18,750 entrances in, 9,375 entrances down to Floor 5.
  • Stairwells are tied to specific stations (12, 24, 36, 48, 72, and the hidden Station 433) rather than scattered freely — a sharp contrast to the open, find-anywhere stairwells of Floors 1-2.
  • A boss occupying a stairwell station hides it from the map entirely until the boss is gone — confirmed twice now, first with Ringmaster Grimaldi on Floor 3 and again with Mimic Rex at Station 433.
  • During the floor's climax, Iron Tangle management's self-destruct announcement reveals the stairwells are centrally controlled: "these stairwell portals are powering up now and will open in exactly 18 hours. They will only be open for six hours before the self-destruction charges will blow."

docs.title: The stairwell Carl, Donut & Katia used
docs.text: After destroying the ghoul generator threatening Station 36 — the culmination of the rescue-and-demolition operation built around hijacked Named trains and stolen interdiction carts — Carl's group returns to Station 36 to find the stairwell already open, powered up as part of the self-destruct sequence, with the assembled survivor group waiting for them rather than descending without them. Agatha, still alive and pushing her shopping cart, descends first; Carl and the rest of the party follow shortly after.

docs.title: Notable Events
docs.text:
• Carl fights and kills Gore-Gore the Mantaur, narrowly avoiding an accidental full summon of Grull via his own War Gauntlet; gains a new sponsor, the Valtay Corporation.
  • Carl learns the full story behind Book 2's dynamite trap from Frank Q at the Desperado Club, shortly before Chris Andrews kills him.
  • Hekla is killed by Katia's off-target Rush attack while secretly orchestrating a plot against Katia and her own healer — ending the Book 1-2 rival/antagonist arc and disbanding Brynhild's Daughters.
  • Brandon An dies holding a defensive line during the floor's crisis.
  • Carl accidentally teleports Mimic Rex into a trainyard, triggering a broadcast Death Challenge against the involuntarily-summoned war god Grull — secretly piloted by a very-much-alive Prince Maestro.
  • With 11 hours left on the timer, Iron Tangle management announces a system-wide self-destruct, blaming "the Krakaren," and floods every stairwell station with its accumulated monster population.
  • Carl, Katia, and allies mount an improvised rescue operation using hijacked Named trains and interdiction carts to evacuate stranded crawlers and funnel monster hordes into the Abyss.
  • Fire Brandy and the dwarf Tizquick ride the Nightmare train into the Abyss and detonate it to help collapse the ghoul-generator network.
  • Carl ends the book at Level 41 (from 27), Donut at 33; the floor's ghoul crisis is contained, though not fully resolved, as the timer runs out.

docs.title: Leaderboard
docs.text:
Unlike Floor 3's single tentative reveal, Floor 4's leaderboard is live and changes multiple times over the course of the book — and per an early-floor system announcement, killing a top-10 crawler now pays out their listed bounty directly: "hunting season is open." A late-book reveal, right after Hekla's death airs, shows the list reshuffled:

Rank Name Race Class Level Bounty 1 Lucia Mar Lajabless Black Inquisitor General 35 1,000,000 2 Prepotente Caprid Forsaken Aerialist 34 500,000 3 Carl Primal Compensated Anarchist 34 400,000 4 Princess Donut Cat Former Child Actor 32 300,000 5 Quan Ch Half-Elf Imperial Security Trooper 38 200,000 6 Florin Crocodilian Shotgun Messenger 32 100,000 7 Miriam Dom Human Shepherd 30 100,000 8 Katia Doppelganger Monster Truck Driver 37 100,000 9 Dmitri and Maxim Popov Nodling Illusionist and Bogatyr 30 100,000 10 Ifechi Human Physicker 29 100,000

Notes worth calling out:

  • Carl himself starts the floor already ranked 6th (a holdover from Floor 3's list) before this reshuffle bumps him to 3rd.
  • Quan Ch — the accidental beneficiary of Book 2's "Fools Who Broke the Glass" disaster — is now the dungeon's single highest-leveled crawler (38), a fact Donut refuses to accept gracefully, repeatedly calling him "a cheater."
  • Dmitri and Maxim Popov are the "twin" up-and-comers Odette teased back on Floor 3.
  • Donut is indignant that she and Carl don't get separate individual ranks ("Carl and I should both be number three!") and that Prepotente — "that goat thing" — barely gets any screen time despite ranking 2nd.
  • Mrs. Elle McGibbons, 10th on the Floor 3 list, falls off the top 10 entirely by this point in Book 3.

Sourced from Book 3: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook.

docs.title: Level 5
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Crawlers entering the floor: 178,887 (confirmed exact figure; the welcome broadcast rounds it to "just over 178,000")
  • Structure: Not a single open floor — 1,172 sealed "bubbles" floating in a dark in-between space called the Lacuna, ~150 crawlers per bubble, no two alike. Carl's party lands in Bubble #543, Air Quadrant
  • Entrances/stairwells: Breaks the halving pattern entirely — over 4,000 castles floor-wide, one per quadrant per bubble, each containing its bubble's stairwell. A bubble's own stairwell won't open until all four of its quadrant castles (Land, Sea, Air, Subterranean) are taken
  • Time limit: No single stated day-count in the welcome broadcast; checkpoints in-text put it at roughly 10 days total (confirmed "five days left" at the five-day mark, and "four and a half days left" shortly after)
  • Milestone: The bounty-doubling leaderboard mechanic debuts here — surviving a floor while ranked in the top 10 permanently doubles all of a crawler's future bounties, via the achievement "The Quarry Sees Another Spring"

AI Commentary (in-voice, written for this wiki — not a book excerpt)

"Welcome to the Bubbles, population: everybody, divided into 1,172 pocket dimensions like a dystopian egg carton. Four castles, four quadrants, one stairwell, zero flying lessons included. Best of luck figuring out the airplane thing. We certainly didn't."

docs.title: Arrival
docs.text:
The party steps directly from a Floor 4 evacuation warehouse into Floor 5's desert wind, "just a few minutes after the fourth level collapsed." The system confirms the numbers immediately:

"Welcome, Crawler, to the fifth floor. 'The Bubbles.' ... Remaining Crawlers: 178,887. Entering Bubble #543 out of 1172. Air Quadrant."

The same notification wave delivers the bounty-doubling achievement. Donut, given only minutes to pick a new Former Child Actor specialty, chooses Glass Cannon — trading away all future Constitution training for a flat +15 base Constitution, faster spell training, lower mana costs, and a massively raised cap on resurrection-type spells like Second Chance (see Game Mechanics).

docs.title: Layout & Notable Areas
docs.text:
• Hump Town — the party's home base, a Dromedarian brothel settlement built around a roughly circular "bowl" about three miles across, secretly infiltrated by The Changeling Principals
  • The Air Quadrant castle — guarded by Ruckus, a Level 55 spring-loaded Chicken Hawk Sentinel
  • The Land Quadrant's Sandcastle — held by the mage Ghazi and Mrs. Ghazi; its collapse floods survivors down into the Water Quadrant rather than resolving cleanly
  • The wrecked submarine Akula (Water Quadrant) — swallowed whole, along with Carl's boarding party, by the City Boss Lusca in a live broadcast Special Event
  • The Necropolis of Anser (Subterranean Quadrant) — an ancient flooded tomb guarded by Quetzalcoatlus, possessed by the banished lesser deity Psamathe
  • The dirigible dreadnaught the Wasteland — The Wasteland faction's airship, destroyed mid-air after a fake-resurrection negotiation trick
  • Pandinus — the Land Quadrant's pazuzu-run town, home to a Club Vanquisher branch (temporarily closed for "cleansing" after an incident involving Prepotente's hellspawn familiar)

docs.title: Monsters (Level 5 area)
docs.text: See the Mobs overview for the full Floor 5 catalog — notable entries include Thorny Devils, Night Frights, Nude Glabers, Concierge Sharks, and the Changeling Principal cultists disguised as Hump Town's own guards.

docs.title: Get Orthrus (World Quest)
docs.text:
"New Quest! Get Orthrus. This is a world quest! All living crawlers on the fifth floor will receive this message! ... Orthrus, the two-headed puppy is bounding his way happily through the Lacuna, the world that houses the bubbles. This very adorable pup is running back to his former master's father. ... Let's kill it."

  • Trigger: Automatically sent to every living crawler on Floor 5 once Orthrus — a perfectly innocent puppy warped by prolonged exposure to the Nothing — starts rampaging through the Lacuna trying to reach his father, the deity Emberus
  • Pass condition: Kill Orthrus before he reunites with Emberus
  • Reward: 1,000,000 gold, five level-up potions, and a pet monkey named Jimbo, for whoever lands the kill
  • What actually happened: Carl's group actively works against the quest's own goal, flying an improvised aircraft to help Orthrus safely reunite with Emberus instead of killing him — Carl publicly threatens to kill anyone who harms the dog, and physically intervenes when the rival crawler Quan Ch tries to snipe it for the reward. Nobody collects the prize; Orthrus is saved.

docs.title: General mechanics
docs.text:
• Floor 5 abandons the halving-entrance pattern used on Floors 1-4 entirely. Instead: over 4,000 castles floor-wide, one per quadrant per bubble, each housing that quadrant's throne room and the bubble's single stairwell.
  • A bubble's stairwell stays closed until all four of its quadrant castles are conquered (throne room occupied or quadrant boss killed) — crawlers who finish their own quadrant early may cross into other quadrants within their bubble to help finish the rest.
  • Once all four castles fall, the bubble "pops" and its crawlers may leave it — but they still cannot enter any other bubble until that one has also been popped.
  • Each bubble typically hides one environmental "easy mode" shortcut per quadrant that bypasses its throne-room boss fight entirely.

docs.title: The stairwell Carl, Donut & Katia used
docs.text: With all four of Bubble #543's quadrant castles eventually cleared (Ruckus in the Air, the Sandcastle in the Land, Lusca's wreck in the Water, and Quetzalcoatlus in the Subterranean), the bubble's own stairwell — located back near Hump Town — opens normally. Carl's group spends their remaining time using the newly-assembled Gate of the Feral Gods to rescue crawlers trapped in other, still-sealed bubbles rather than leaving immediately, before finally descending together with about five minutes left on the clock — Chris Andrews enters first, with Carl, Donut, and Mongo right behind.

docs.title: Notable Events
docs.text:
• Carl kills Ruckus (Level 55 Borough Boss) while field-testing homemade missiles, then uncovers and thwarts a Skull-Empire-backed Changeling Principals infiltration of Hump Town's guard ranks.
  • After hostage gnome Wynne is killed by a rival crawler group, Carl, Donut, and Katia trick the dirigible dreadnaught The Wasteland into a face-to-face negotiation and destroy it mid-air, rescuing Commandant Kane's daughter Bonnie from Denise the Feral Goose Mother.
  • Carl accidentally assassinates dungeon admin Loita with a rigged toy-robot device during a sponsor infomercial taping, then talks his way out of a Syndicate liaison investigation.
  • Katia's separate team kills the mage Ghazi and Mrs. Ghazi at the Land Quadrant's Sandcastle, though its collapse washes survivors into the Water Quadrant instead.
  • Carl, Katia, and two survivors are swallowed by Lusca in a live-broadcast Special Event and kill her from inside using a berserking potion and a salvaged buzzsaw.
  • Maggie My — revealed to be an Infiltrator (Scree) who has fully puppeted Chris Andrews since Floor 4 — is extracted and killed; Chris rejoins the party.
  • Quetzalcoatlus, possessed by the banished deity Psamathe, is destroyed via an environmental lightning-tower trap at the cost of every crawler remaining in the Subterranean Quadrant.
  • With all four castles cleared, Carl assembles the Gate of the Feral Gods and uses it to evacuate other sealed bubbles, releasing a feral god or demon into each one — including the puppy-god Orthrus, safely reunited with his father Emberus, God of Sun and Ash, whom Carl accidentally acquires as his own patron deity via a Celestial Grenade.
  • In the finale, Carl sends a final feral god through a portal directly into the Ninth Floor's Larracos marketplace instead of releasing it onto the open floor, crippling every Faction War army's ability to resupply ahead of schedule.
  • Carl ends the book as the dungeon's #1-ranked crawler (Level 47); Katia splits off from the main party to protect Eva Sigrid's scattered followers; Chris Andrews joins the core party.

docs.title: Leaderboard
docs.text:
The bounty-doubling mechanic (marked "(x2)") is visible throughout Floor 5's leaderboard reveals. The final table, shown near the book's end after Lucia Mar finally loses the #1 spot:

Rank Name Race Class Level Bounty 1 Carl Primal Compensated Anarchist 47 1,000,000 (x2) 2 Lucia Mar Lajabless Black Inquisitor General 48 500,000 (x2) 3 Prepotente Caprid Forsaken Aerialist 55 400,000 (x2) 4 Princess Donut Cat Former Child Actor 39 300,000 (x2) 5 Dmitri and Maxim Popov Nodling Illusionist and Bogatyr 43 200,000 (x2) 6 Miriam Dom Vampire Shepherd 52 100,000 (x2) 7 Elle McGib Frost Maiden Blizzardmancer 47 100,000 8 Bogdon Ro Human Legatus 44 100,000 9 Eva Sigrid Half Nagini, Half-Orc Nimblefoot Enforcer 40 100,000 10 Quan Ch Half Elf Imperial Security Trooper 48 100,000 (x2)

Notes worth calling out:

  • Carl reaches #1 for the first time in the series here, unseating Lucia Mar.
  • Miriam Dom's race has changed to Vampire since her last appearance — an unexplained transformation worth investigating when a later book clarifies it.
  • Eva Sigrid appears on the leaderboard despite Katia splitting off to protect her followers — the two threads are connected but not fully reconciled by book's end.
  • Florin drops off the list entirely mid-book after Ifechi's death, last seen refusing to choose a bubble quadrant.

Sourced from Book 4: The Gate of the Feral Gods.

docs.title: Level 6
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Crawlers entering the floor: 85,223, per the welcome broadcast
  • Hunters: 360 registered bounty hunters held under a 30-hour Grace Period in the city of Zockau before release — the floor's central twist. Registration stayed open through the Grace Period, and the count had swelled past 1,000 by the time they were actually released (peaking near 1,013 shortly before release, dropping to roughly 290 and then far fewer as crawlers hunted them down). Carl enters as reigning #1 crawler, bounty 3,000,000 gold, making him the hunters' single biggest target
  • Time limit: 17 Days to level collapse, stated at the very start of the floor
  • Floor type: A "Scolopendra level" — see Zerzura, which is relevant to how Carl's group eventually gets a group of endangered NPCs off the floor
  • Theme: "The Hunting Grounds" — the floor's entire premise is crawler-vs-crawler: once the Grace Period ends, the 360 hunters are released to hunt marked crawlers for bounty, layered on top of the usual monsters and bosses

AI Commentary (in-voice, written for this wiki — not a book excerpt)

"Welcome to the Hunting Grounds, where the real monsters have been sitting in a nice hotel in Zockau for the last thirty hours, sharpening their bounty lists. Run."

docs.title: Arrival
docs.text:
The floor opens with Carl's stats broadcast front and center — 512 sextillion views, 142 quadrillion followers, and his standing as the #1-ranked crawler with a 3,000,000-gold bounty — before the system confirms the floor's premise directly:

"Welcome, Crawler, to the sixth floor. 'The Hunting Grounds' ... Remaining Crawlers: 85,223 ... Remaining Hunters: 360. Grace Period begins now. All hunters have been transferred to the city of Zockau. They will be released in 30 hours. Run."

The 360 hunters are professional bounty-killers rather than ordinary crawlers, released specifically to hunt the floor's highest-value targets — with Carl, as the top-bountied crawler on the leaderboard, marked as their most valuable kill from the opening bell.

docs.title: Layout & Notable Areas
docs.text:
• Zockau — the city where all the hunters are held during the Grace Period; also the site of Carl's early Desperado Club scenes and, via Orren's liaison office, his negotiations over the mercenary-bodyguard deal
  • Point Mongo — a large Ursine settlement Carl and Donut personally conquer (killing mayor Elmer) right as the Grace Period ends; Donut renames it, rules it as its "leadership charm" holder, and has Mordecai train its funeral-bell guards to fight off hunter raids before the party moves on
  • Fort Freedom — the former Naiad royal palace, occupied by the corrupt Naiad Confederacy; the target of Part One of Signet's "Vengeance of the Daughter" quest, taken in an amphibious night assault (and a fight with the boss Claude Sludgington) — not itself part of the hunter-versus-crawler conflict
  • The Butcher's Masquerade — the floor's signature Special Event, a mass costume ball weaponized against attending crawlers; see Game Mechanics
  • The High Elf Castle — Queen Imogen's stronghold, the last standing town in the party's area as the floor collapse approaches, and the eventual target of the Zerzura cast (see Stairwells below)
  • The Dark Hive — the Dark Hive faction's territory, home to Vrah and the mantis hive queen Circe Took

docs.title: Monsters (Level 6 area)
docs.text: See the Mobs overview for the full Floor 6 catalog. Notable mechanics layered onto the floor's usual monsters include the Odious Creepers (mutated, self-reassembling corpse-fragment monsters spawned by Big Tina and the "Creeping Apocalypse" world quest below), the Gehenna Bramble — an unstoppable wall of thorned, undulating vines that swallowed the entire map after that quest's deadline was missed — and a floor-wide vampirism curse originating from Miriam Dom — see Game Mechanics for all three.

docs.title: Quests
docs.text:
Floor 6's structural "quest" is the Settlement Conquest & Collar Charm system rather than a single world quest — see Game Mechanics for the trigger/reward mechanics governing town takeovers on this floor. On top of that baseline system, three major, book-specific quest threads run through the floor:

  • The Recital — a personal quest to stop (or redeem) Big Tina, a rampaging Allosaurus who was once Tina, an Ursine child whose father cut short her dance recital just before Scolopendra's attack transformed the village's women into dinosaurs. Resolved not by killing her but by reuniting her with her mother, Kiwi, and staging the recital she never got to finish during the Butcher's Masquerade talent show.
  • The Creeping Apocalypse — a floor-wide world quest triggered by the death of the vampire Miriam Dom: every crawler and hunter must hunt down and kill 50 boss-tier Odious Creepers before sundown. Failing it (as happened here) triggers the punishing Gehenna Bramble effect above.
  • The Vengeance of the Daughter — the elite Tsarina Signet's two-part quest chain: Part One is the assault on Fort Freedom against the Naiad Confederacy; Part Two is killing Signet's half-sister, Queen Imogen. Carl and Donut are contractually bound to help via Signet's licensed secondary show, and the questline's climax is deliberately folded into the Butcher's Masquerade itself (see Notable Events).

docs.title: General mechanics
docs.text: Floor 6 does not reveal a single, floor-wide stairwell rule the way earlier floors did (e.g. the halving-entrance pattern, or Floor 5's four-castle bubble gating). Individual settlements each gain a stairwell once their local boss is defeated or the settlement is otherwise conquered — consistent with the Settlement Conquest mechanic above.

docs.title: The exit Carl, Donut & the High Elf castle group used
docs.text:
Two separate exits happen at the close of Floor 6, and they should not be conflated:

  • The High Elf castle group: faced with losing a group of rescued changeling children to the collapsing floor, Carl's allies smuggle them into the castle during the Butcher's Masquerade and have The Sledge cast Zerzura on the High Elf castle itself once he fights his way inside. The cast completes moments after Queen Imogen's death, during the final boss fight, and confirmed passengers include Sledge, the changeling children (including Bonnie), Kiwi (transformed back into an Ursine), Big Tina, and the reanimated "tattoo" companions of the late Tsarina Signet. Per Zerzura's own mechanics, Floor 6 being a Scolopendra level means this cast skips floors entirely — the vanished castle is confirmed to land on Floor 9, not Floor 7 or 8. Whether the castle group is struck by the spell's revenant curse on landing is not confirmed by anything read for this page — see Zerzura for what is and isn't established.
  • Carl and Donut's own exit: entirely separate from the castle. In the final chapter, they (with Prepotente) are pulled into a Pole Position Chamber — an individual glass "fish tank" capsule tethered to one of a corkscrewing stack of round, doorless portal-stairwells. Prepotente, having pieced together the next floor's theme from clues in his mother's item description, deliberately shatters the chamber's wall early, collapsing the whole holding structure and sucking every waiting crawler into the stairwells at once. Carl and Donut land in the transition chamber between floors and cross into Floor 7, "The Great Race," with Carl re-ranked to #3 on the leaderboard and a bounty of 1,600,000 gold.

docs.title: Notable Events
docs.text:
• Carl negotiates a mercenary-bodyguard deal with a kua-tin Borant admin, brokered by his attorney Quasar, surrendering the Gate of the Feral Gods as collateral in exchange for protection — including "The Sledge," the mercenary who carries the Zerzura spell.
  • Carl infects Vrah, a Dark Hive heir hunter, with an incurable venereal disease during a confrontation; Vrah is later killed at the Butcher's Masquerade, finished off by Mongo, Kiwi, and Samantha after Carl reanimates two of her own trophy-heads to buy the opening.
  • The vampire Miriam Dom dies by Carl's own hand (at her request, to save Prepotente and cure the floor's spreading vampirism curse), triggering the world quest "The Creeping Apocalypse" and, after its deadline is missed, the Gehenna Bramble that consumes the map.
  • The floor-wide Butcher's Masquerade Special Event — nominally a sacred, no-violence peace ritual thrown by Queen Imogen — turns into a trap once Vrah's mother sabotages it from within, effectively becoming a weaponized ambush against the attending crawlers.
  • Circe Took, the mantis hive queen, sponsors the manifestation of the forest goddess Diwata, who takes on Circe's own form to cure Vrah's disease by giving birth to a swarm of mantis nymphs; during the masquerade's final battle, Donut's maxed-out Laundry Day spell strips away Diwata's divine "armor," and the newly-exposed, mortal Circe is killed moments later — swarmed by her own children.
  • Queen Imogen, the Floor 6 country boss and Tsarina Signet's half-sister, is killed (the finishing blow struck by Prepotente), unlocking the High Elf castle's stairwell.
  • Tsarina Signet sacrifices herself mid-party — cutting her own throat to power an Ink Marauder spell — deliberately breaking the masquerade's peace seal so Carl's group can fight back; her mother's memory-golem and her fallen companions' "tattoo" warriors briefly manifest at full size to join the battle.
  • Big Tina (Level 80 City Boss) is not killed outright; the Recital quest is resolved by reuniting her with her mother Kiwi (restored to Ursine form via a potion), and both are then swept away to Floor 9 along with the vanishing High Elf castle.
  • With the floor collapsing, Carl's allies cast Zerzura on the High Elf castle to save a group of rescued changeling children, including Bonnie, rather than let them be lost to the collapse.
  • In the epilogue, Prepotente shatters his and Carl's shared Pole Position holding chamber ahead of schedule, collapsing the structure and launching every waiting crawler into the Floor 7 stairwells simultaneously; Carl ends the floor ranked #3 with a bounty of 1,600,000 gold.

docs.title: Leaderboard
docs.text:
A top-10 list is shown during the floor's first recap episode, though it's explicitly a holdover ("hadn't changed from the end of the previous floor") rather than a fresh Floor 6 ranking:

Rank Crawler Race Class Level Bounty 1 Carl Primal Agent Provocateur 54 1,000,000 (x3) 2 Lucia Mar Lajabless Black Inquisitor General 48 500,000 (x3) 3 Prepotente Caprid Profane Vitiate 55 400,000 (x3) 4 Donut Cat Former Child Actor 41 300,000 (x3) 5 Dmitri and Maxim Popov Nodling Visionary / Bogatyr 44 200,000 (x3) 6 Miriam Dom Vampire Shepherd 52 100,000 (x3) 7 Elle McGib Frost Maiden Tundra Princess 47 100,000 (x2) 8 Bogdon Ro Human Legatus 44 100,000 (x2) 9 Eva Sigrid Half Nagini, Half-Orc Nimblefoot Enforcer 40 100,000 (x2) 10 Quan Ch Half Elf Sergeant at Arms 48 100,000 (x3)

No further full leaderboard table is shown later in the book — only a "top 1,000 can see their own rank" system update and scattered individual mentions (e.g. Bautista at #23, Britney breaking into the top 50, Tserendolgor hovering around #38–54). The only other confirmed individual data points are personal broadcast readouts at the floor's open and close: Carl opens the floor ranked #1 with a bounty of 3,000,000 gold, and closes it — crossing into Floor 7 — ranked #3 with a bounty of 1,600,000 gold.

Sourced from Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade.

docs.title: Level 7
docs.text:
This is a stub, and deliberately so

Floor 7 lasted roughly ten minutes of in-world time. Prepotente shattered the floor's starting chamber before the rules announcement even finished, dumping every crawler straight through to Floor 8. Almost none of the floor's actual content — the maze, its monsters, its bosses, its loot — was ever seen by anybody. Most of the Quick Facts fields below are therefore minimal or not applicable, not missing.

Quick facts

  • Crawlers entering the floor: not stated. The floor's welcome broadcast skipped the remaining-crawler line entirely. The next confirmed count is 38,532 at the opening of Level 8
  • Time limit: 20 Days to level collapse, per the welcome broadcast. The floor survived about ten minutes of it
  • Structure: A single, enormous sealed maze — "several hundred kilometers of twisting and turning tubes." Crawlers were held in individual glass Pole Position Chambers stacked in a corkscrew around a vertical shaft of doorless, round stairwell portals leading to Floor 8
  • Deaths: Zero. Confirmed in Book 6 — "Without anyone actually dying on the seventh, the dungeon had some catching up to do"
  • Floor spellbook: None delivered. Donut's saferoom mailbox never produced the usual book-of-the-floor prize, and Mordecai's verdict was "You snooze you lose"
  • Carl's standing: Enters ranked #3 with a bounty of 1,600,000 gold; receives a Platinum Venison Box on arrival
  • Theme: "The Great Race" — built to mirror a well-known in-universe fairytale of the same name, exactly and fatally

AI Commentary (in-voice, written for this wiki — not a book excerpt)

"Twenty days of maze. Hundreds of kilometers of tube. Years of engineering. One goat with a hammer. We are not going to be talking about this floor again."

docs.title: Arrival
docs.text:
Carl, Donut, and Prepotente descend from Level 6 — see that page's Stairwells section for the Floor 6 side of this transition — and land directly inside a Pole Position Chamber:

"Welcome, Crawler to the Seventh floor. 'The Great Race.' ... Time to Level Collapse: 20 Days. Leaderboard rank: 3. Bounty: 1,600,000 gold ... Entering Pole Position Chamber. The race will commence shortly. Stay tuned for the rules announcement in ten minutes."

The chamber is a featureless glass box roughly the size of an apartment living room — Donut's immediate reaction is "Carl! We're in a fish tank!" Three walls are solid; the fourth is thick vertical glass bars opening onto a tunnel that curves away downward like a waterslide. A gentle tug pulls everything inside toward the bars.

The system immediately tried to lock the occupants down — Peace-Bonded, Frozen, Paralyzed, Slowed, teleported, placed under an Administrative Hold, and finally four armed gnolls materialised in the chamber. Every single attempt was negated, one after another, by AI resolution; the gnolls popped out of existence within seconds. Borant knew what Prepotente intended and was structurally unable to stop him.

docs.title: Layout & Notable Areas
docs.text:
• The Pole Position Chambers — one glass capsule per crawler (or party), arranged in a corkscrewing spiral stack. Carl, Donut and Prepotente were at the very bottom step of the spiral. Occupants could see neighbouring capsules above and to the side; Donut believed she spotted Agatha and her shopping cart in one of them
  • The stairwell column — the glowing shaft at the centre of the spiral, which turned out to be a vertical string of Floor 8 stairwell portals. No stairs, no doors; round portals enterable from any direction. They sat directly behind the back wall of every capsule
  • The maze — never entered. Per the aborted rules announcement, each capsule was to slide to a starting chute and release its crawler into a system of branching tubes. Nodes offered multiple onward paths (sometimes hundreds), each labelled with a danger level and distance; pitstop saferooms sat in the nodes; backtracking was forbidden; some paths required solving maths problems or puzzles. A path closed once ten crawlers or one full party had used it. Each major node held one zero tube — a danger-free route, usable exactly once, ever

docs.title: Monsters (Level 7 area)
docs.text: None recorded. No crawler reached the maze, so no Floor 7 mob or boss was ever fought, described, or catalogued. Carl's achievement list from the floor includes "Pacifist!" — "You survived an entire floor without hurting a single, poor mob."

docs.title: Quests
docs.text: None issued. The floor collapsed before the rules announcement finished, and no floor quest, world quest, or regional quest was ever handed out.

docs.title: The fairytale, and the flaw
docs.text:
Prepotente worked the floor out in advance. The Floor 7 boon Seventh Floor Pole Position had been on sale at the Butcher's Masquerade prize counter for thirty hands, and he bought it. He then identified what the floor actually was:

"This level is called the Great Race which also happens to be the name of a well-known fairytale popular in the universe. Based on some additional clues, I determined the seventh floor is indeed based on this tale."

His sources were a muted interview appearance in which the host and Cascadia discussed the floor in front of him, and — decisively — the description text on his late mother Miriam Dom's Boots of Kiznet's Final Flight, an item description 503% longer than average and therefore, to Prepotente, an obvious signal. The boots told the whole tale.

The fairytale itself, in his summary: a boy trapped in a maze where every tunnel seals behind him once taken, presented with thousands of paths, forever choosing the wrong one, dying, being resurrected by a god and starting again. Prepotente describes it as a mash-up of the Achilles, Sisyphus and Wu Gang stories. In the tale the boy spent years trying to crack the walls of the impossible maze, finally succeeding at the resurrection chamber at the very entrance.

Borant's engineers built the floor to mirror that story exactly — including the part where the maze can be broken from the starting chamber. Structurally, the entire level behaved like a Prince Rupert's drop at enormous scale: enormously tough almost everywhere, and catastrophically self-destructing if nicked at the single correct point.

docs.title: The shattering
docs.text:
With about five minutes on the clock and the rules announcement still playing, Prepotente splashed a potion onto the back wall of the capsule, took a thermometer-like instrument to find the spot, pushed The Enchanted Stick of Cascadia's Screams halfway into the softened glass, and gave it one very small tap with a ball-peen hammer.

Cascadia broke into the announcement to beg him personally not to: "Godsdamnit, Prepotente. Don't do it. Please. I worked so hard to make this floor happen."

A lightning pattern of fissures spread. Then the wall shattered — and not just that wall. Every wall on the floor detonated into fine dust simultaneously, and every crawler still waiting in a capsule was sucked into the Floor 8 stairwells at once. The last thing Carl heard was Cascadia screaming over the dungeon PA.

Carl and Donut landed in the same style of inter-floor globe chamber they had used between Floors 4 and 5, where Donut — now squad leader — chose the Floor 8 starting region. She was aiming for the Bahamas, and picked Cuba instead.

docs.title: Notable Events
docs.text:
• Donut briefly becomes a Viper Queen. Given a class choice inside the capsule with no chat access and no time, she picked without reading it. She kept the class for only a few minutes, but carried its Venom Spitter skill (level 3) forward into Floor 8 as a permanent ability — see the Spells overview.
  • Mordecai spends the floor as a slime. His between-floors form reroll gave him no arms at all: "It's better than the form I'd taken for the ten minutes the seventh floor was open. I was a slime. I had no goddamned arms."
  • No floor prizes. Donut's book-of-the-floor spellbook never arrived, and she spent part of Floor 8 demanding Carl's attorney sue over it.
  • Prepotente leaves the party in the capsule, seconds before breaking the floor, handing party leadership to Donut.

  • The engineers take the blame. Relaying what Mistress Tiatha (Elle McGibbons' manager) had just told him, Mordecai explains on Floor 8 that Prepotente is unlikely to be punished:

    "This one is on the engineers. They fashioned that level so it was just like the fairytale. The kid in the story did the exact same thing the goat did, but it took him thousands of years to figure it out. They should never have built it that way."

    He notes this is not the first doomed-from-the-start floor — there was a bacterial-infection incident in a previous Borant season, and a floor where crawlers had to hand-build bridges out of materials that made it impossible — but it is the first he knows of that failed this fast. The Apothecary and the Plenty, who supplied Prepotente the means, land on the Valtay's blacklist; Mordecai reads the whole affair as a political manoeuvre to make money for those two sponsors at the Borant Corporation's and the Syndicate's expense. The Syndicate pays for tunnel bandwidth in advance and gets no refund for a skipped floor. - Cascadia's floor. Zev later confirms the seventh floor "was Cascadia's baby," pushed through by the Valtay; its destruction triggered a serious loss of nerve among the new showrunners, who stepped back from day-to-day production afterwards. - Skipped-floor compensation. Loot quality across the board spikes at the start of Floor 8, which Mordecai attributes partly to the AI compensating for the missing floor. Carl's own haul includes a "Fuck This Floor" achievement — "You went down the stairs less than an hour after you arrived upon the level" — and a "Collective Bargaining!" achievement for more than 1,000 crawlers receiving the identical box at the identical moment.

docs.title: Leaderboard
docs.text:
No Floor 7 leaderboard was ever published. The only ranking data attached to the floor are the personal readouts in the arrival broadcast — Carl at #3 with a 1,600,000 gold bounty — and Donut's delighted discovery, inside the capsule, that she had reached #1 for the first time. Both figures were already stale by the time the next recap aired on Floor 8.

Sourced from Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade (epilogue) and Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: Level 8
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Crawlers entering the floor: 38,532, per the arrival broadcast. 33,804 were still alive when Carl left — roughly 4,700 dead, a figure Carl treats as a stunning success given that the floor was engineered as a mass-culling event
  • Time limit: 21 Days to level collapse
  • Opening date: in-world December 10th. The Earth being simulated is a recording of the weeks before the collapse, so the floor runs on that calendar. The actual date is roughly March 20th, per the clock on Chris Andrews' iPod and confirmed by Li Na — the crawlers celebrate "Christmas" on the floor anyway
  • Carl's standing at arrival: rank #3, bounty 2,000,000 gold, 13 septillion views, 331 quadrillion followers, 41 quadrillion favorites. Donut drops from #1 to #2 on arrival
  • Structure: 293 regions drawn at roughly a 99 km radius (shortened where regions would overlap; island regions extend 6 km offshore). 205 regions were occupied. Two stairwells per region; crawlers spawn next to one of the two. Carl and Donut start in the rotunda of El Capitolio Nacional de Cuba
  • Theme: "The Ghosts of Earth" — a full-scale, physically solid replica of Earth's surface, recorded from the weeks before the collapse, populated by intangible memory ghosts and by mobs drawn from each region's own folklore
  • Signature system: the T'Ghee card squad/deck game — see T'Ghee Cards

AI Commentary (in-voice, written for this wiki — not a book excerpt)

"We rebuilt your entire planet from memory, filled it with your own half-researched monsters, handed you a collectible card game, and then made you fight each other for the door. You're welcome. Try not to cry on the merchandise."

docs.title: Arrival
docs.text:
Carl and Donut step directly out of the Floor 7 globe chamber — see Level 7 for how that transition was forced — into the marble rotunda of El Capitolio Nacional de Cuba, in the small hours of a warm December morning. They are the only two crawlers at their stairwell.

"Welcome, Crawler to the eighth floor. 'The Ghosts of Earth.' Time to Level Collapse: 21 Days ... Leaderboard rank: 3. Bounty: 2,000,000 gold ... Remaining Crawlers: 38,532. It is December 10th. Your squad has six open slots. Entering El Capitolio Nacional de Cuba."

Donut, as squad leader, had picked Cuba herself in the globe chamber — reasoning that the Bahamas (where Miss Beatrice had gone on holiday) was too obvious a trap. Carl's view is that she simply missed. The exit stairwell is right there in the building, and locked: it needs a key nobody has yet.

docs.title: The floor's central conceit
docs.text:
Cascadia's welcome broadcast lays out the rules of the replica:

  • The starting area is an exact replica of Earth's surface as captured on the indicated date — geography, buildings, vehicles, and people.
  • Mobile biological entities are intangible memory ghosts. They do not appear on maps, cannot see crawlers, and cannot be touched or hurt. Walking through one rips the clothing off it; the clothes become real objects on the ground and the exposed parts of the ghost render as a wavy translucent outline, while the ghost carries on with its day as though nothing happened.
  • Everything non-biological is solid and keeps its real mass and momentum until a crawler, a mob, or an environmental factor interferes. Crawlers can enter buildings, break windows, drive vehicles, take an item out of a ghost's hand — and be run over and killed by a bus.
  • Anything looted from the Earth memory turns to dust when the floor collapses. Carl's first instinct, arming the party out of a military base, is explicitly pre-empted.
  • Mobs are seeded from each region's own folklore — and the research is bad. Carl recognises the work from the Earth Beautiful production crew, who admitted to sourcing everything from an incomplete copy of the internet. The result is real legends flattened into Saturday-morning cartoons and freely blended with pop culture, an offence Sister Ines Quiteria takes personally and furiously.

Within hours the traffic system collapses worldwide, as crawlers and mobs cause pile-ups that cascade until the roads are wholly blocked and the streets fill with drifting, naked, oblivious ghosts.

docs.title: Phase One — 14 days (Dec 10 to Dec 24)
docs.text:
Every crawler is locked into a squad of no more than five. Parties of six or more are split into equal squads; leaving a party does not leave a squad. Each squad has six slots above its crawler count (a solo crawler's squad has seven slots total). Squads must be filled before Phase Two or they will be filled at random.

Slots are filled with monsters. Each squad leader receives twenty flags bearing an auto-generated squad logo — Donut's is a pair of heart-covered boxer shorts with a bomb patch over the crotch, reading "The Royal Court of Princess Donut." Driving any living entity below 5% health and physically planting a flag in it converts it into a T'Ghee totem card in the squad leader's inventory. Lost flags are not replaced. Totems can be traded and stolen; surplus totems dissipate at the start of Phase Two. Each surviving squad may keep one card past the floor's collapse.

The deck game layered on top — hands of four, ten-second draws, totems/utility/snare/mystic/special card types, and the rule that a squad leader loses access to spells and inventory during deck combat — is covered in full on the T'Ghee Cards mechanics page.

Carl and Donut's region is Cuba, and it contains exactly one other squad: Sister Ines Quiteria, Paz Lo, and Anton Lopez, three Cubans who came into the dungeon together from a women's prison where the two men were guards.

docs.title: Phase Two — the assault (Dec 24 to Dec 26)
docs.text:
At 12:01 AM on December 24 every crawler is teleported to a choosing chamber. Only the squad leader enters; the rest of the squad is held in stasis while the leader picks a new region from a shortlist and fights a first, deliberately easy opponent alone. The squad then joins them.

In the new region the squad must collect nine tokens from nine card-wielding deckmasters, each five levels stronger than the last, standing frozen at intervals along the route. The tokens go into a vending machine that unlocks the keymaster — the tenth deckmaster — who holds the region's exit key. The key location is 10–15 km away and the squad has 48 hours. Totems not in the active deck are lost; from this point a squad may hold exactly six totems, no more and no fewer, and any totem taken from a defeated opponent must replace one of your own.

Carl and Donut draw Monroe County, Florida — the Keys. Donut had chosen Miami; a placement glitch first reported them as being in Iowa, then resolved itself by physically tearing a chunk of Dallas County, Iowa out of the ground and dropping it on top of the Keys as a roughly 700-foot mountain of snowmelt mud, with the key location on its summit. The mountain visibly erodes into the ocean for the whole two days they are on it. Zev's department confirms this was done on purpose, as "the only way to do it without breaking anything further."

docs.title: Phase Three — the door (Dec 26 onward)
docs.text:
At midnight on December 26:

  • Keyholders and their squads teleport back to a random point inside their original region and must make their way to their own stairwell.
  • Keyless squads teleport to the doorway of a stairwell belonging to someone who does hold a key — that is, directly into the keyholder's path. Multiple keyless squads can be dropped at the same door. The design intent is stated outright: "the potential of crawler on crawler violence is quite high. Doesn't that sound just great?"
  • A keyholder who plays a Flee card now loses a key to their opponent, chosen at random if they hold more than one. Keys cannot be voluntarily dropped or handed over; the only way to give one away is to start a fight and flee it.
  • The doorway to a stairwell chamber can be destroyed — and destroying it destroys its key. The stairwell itself, and the sealed chamber around it, remain indestructible and unreachable. Several squads lost their only route out this way, including Carl and Donut's own Capitolio exit.

By Carl's estimate, roughly one key existed for every three or four squads.

docs.title: Layout & Notable Areas
docs.text:
• Havana, Cuba — Carl and Donut's Phase One region. El Capitolio Nacional de Cuba (start point and one of two stairwells), Old Havana, the coast road, the suburbs to the south, the southern marshlands, and the Iglesia de Jesús de Miramar (the second stairwell, and the one they eventually leave through)
  • The Colón Cemetery — walled off and fog-filled, revealed to be a Medium Ghommid Settlement corrupted by the orisha Asojano. It contains a saferoom pub ("The Yellow Zone") and, at its centre, a Club Vanquisher entrance temple
  • The Bay of Pigs marshlands — the land crab migration route and the web-choked swamp domain of Shi Maria, the Bedlam Bride
  • A roadside Desperado Club south of Havana — the site of the Astrid assassination and of the club's near-total destruction
  • Monroe County, Florida (the Keys) and the transplanted chunk of Dallas County, Iowa — Phase Two. The Iowa slab holds a commercial turkey barn, a trailer park, and Carl's father's trailer
  • The FOCSA building, Havana — a 32-storey Y-shaped tower, the site of the floor's final battle
  • Elsewhere: Iceland (Katia's squad), the Pacific Northwest and Belgium (Elle), Detroit (Imani), Beijing (Li Na and Li Jun), Ecuador and later Nigeria (Florin), the Bahamas and later northern Italy (Prepotente), Vietnam and Ukraine, Tokyo, Brazil, Turkey

docs.title: Monsters (Level 8 area)
docs.text:
The floor's regular mobs are drawn from local folklore, badly researched and freely mixed with pop culture — see the Mobs overview for the Book 6 regional catalog. Representative Cuban examples include the Experience (a Taíno guardian of the dead rendered as a dog with Che Guevara's head), duendes, Monk Seal Picket Sentries (masters of "Caribbean Kung Fu"), Red Maníseros Land Crabs (masters of Juego de maní), and the Unsettled Ghommids of the Colón Cemetery. Elsewhere crawlers report a Bermuda-shorts-wearing sasquatch, an undead Easter Bunny, sentient umbrellas in Tokyo, Icelandic Nykur, and a Chinese dragon.

Named bosses and deity-tier entities encountered on the floor:

Name Tier / level Where Notes Asojano Level 130 City Boss (Orisha, non-corporeal) Colón Cemetery Lord of Smallpox; source of the ghommid corruption; flagged by Carl rather than killed Ogun Level 250 deity, unsponsored Temple of Yemaya God of blacksmiths; kills Anton personally and strips Paz of his grace Yemaya Level 250 deity, locked Her own temple River mother, re-ascended by the Thorn Room choice; retainer to Eileithyia Eileithyia Level 250 deity, sponsored by Huanxin Jinx Temple of Yemaya Goddess of childbirth; the "Spiders" quest is her cover for talking to Carl Shi Maria / The Bedlam Bride Level 140 City Boss, demi-god Southern Cuban swamp Reaper Spider Minion; flagged by agreement rather than defeated Madre de Aguas Level 125 City Boss Cuban north coast Giant boa; charmed by Sister Ines, then infected with zombism Minge Level 225 Minor Feral Demon Desperado Club casino Slit's sister; escapes the Nothing and destroys the club's middle floor The Visitor Level 70, Deckmaster 7 of 10 Dallas County, Iowa A Nightgaunt; enraged past usefulness by Carl's nightgaunt cloak Tom Level 75, Deckmaster 8 of 10 Iowa turkey barn Bereft shaman of the Great Wild Turkey Sharp-Elbows Level 80, Deckmaster 9 of 10 Iowa turkey barn Ogre necromancer; fought simultaneously with Tom The Reminiscence Hydra of Malicious Compliance Level 125 City Boss Carl's father's trailer Nine heads built from Carl's and Donut's dead; created by the AI with no input parameters Ysalte Level 250 deity, sponsored by Pontifex Shine FOCSA building The Vinegar Bitch; Sister Ines's patron; killed by Paz Amayon Level 250 Demon Prince of Sheol FOCSA building Evicted from hell into the body of the Madre de Aguas; the floor's exit

docs.title: The Chowder War — Failed
docs.text: An automatic quest received on examining a Monk Seal. The seals hold the ocean sacred; the Red Maníseros Land Crabs must spawn in it; the AI frames the resulting conflict in the crudest possible terms and demands that crawlers pick a side. Sister Ines warned the Monk Seal Abbot of the crabs' sneak attack, which turned what would have been a quick rout into a war of attrition that gutted both species. The quest is then formally marked Quest Failed and replaced with Hell Comes to Crawler Town — it is not a win, and should not be recorded as one.

docs.title: Hell Comes to Crawler Town — Complete
docs.text: The Chowder War's replacement, and the floor's pivot into its endgame. The mass death from the crab–seal war, layered on top of a global zombie outbreak that Carl personally started by punting zombie turkeys off the Iowa cliff into the ocean, attracts the attention of hell. The Demon Eviction event begins (see Game Mechanics). Win condition: get down the stairs without being dragged into Sheol.

docs.title: Pueblo de los Olvidados — Complete
docs.text: A compulsory quest triggered by entering the Colón Cemetery, which seals behind the party. The ghommid village has been driven mad by the trapped orisha Asojano; the fix is to repair his shrine so he can leave, or to kill him. Resolving it instead opens the Celestial Thorn Room (below). Reward: a Silver Quest Box, the settlement restored, and a working Club Vanquisher entrance.

docs.title: Spiders — Complete
docs.text: A deity quest from Eileithyia: kill five spiders a day in her name. It is transparently a cover — its real function is to give the goddess (and through her, her sponsor Huanxin Jinx) a private messaging channel to Carl that the system is not permitted to monitor, plus a pretext for awarding his party a boon. Donut enjoys it enormously.

docs.title: The Astrid assassination — Complete
docs.text: Katia's third and final seal on the Engaged Lock Box of the Night Wyrm requires an assassination contract from the Guild of Suffering, whose entrance is hidden behind the Penis Parade in the Desperado Club. The target: Astrid, Level 125 Bloodlust Sprite, assistant manager of the Desperado Club — who turns out to be the Night Wyrm's own wife and the mother of the dancers Damascus Steel and Anaconda. The job is completed, and the plan to do it cleanly falls apart completely (see Notable Events).

docs.title: The Bedlam Bride — ongoing
docs.text: An escort quest: get Shi Maria to the city of Larracos on Floor 9. Donut rips the spider's card at the end of the floor; the quest does not go away, because Shi Maria has by then tattooed herself into Carl's chest.

docs.title: Where the Sidewalk Ends → The Missing Piece — Complete
docs.text: The regional quest hosted by Carl's squad once enough crawlers commit to his escape plan, and its successor world quest. Part One, "The Big O," requires refilling the world with the right kind of souls and then powering Amayon up enough that his portal covers the entire planet. Part Two, "Falling Up," is the escape itself.

docs.title: Carried over from earlier books
docs.text:
• Vengeance of the Daughter — Tsarina Signet's questline pays out at the start of the floor. Carl's Gold Quest Box contains Edgar the tortoise's stick-and-poke tattoo kit; the promised right to loot the High Elf castle is worthless, the castle having been teleported to Floor 9. The kit becomes the instrument of the floor's final horror.
  • Find Out Who Killed My Son — Emberus's quest regarding the murder of the god Geyrun advances substantially. Pater Coal, high cleric of Emberus in Club Vanquisher (and, Carl suspects, the AI wearing a face), names two threads: the origin of Katia's crossbow and the origin of Donut's oak bracelet, neither explorable without Osvaldo's memorial crystal. Later, Amayon states outright that he witnessed the deal being signed and will name the culprit only if Emberus helps him kill his three brothers. Hellik remains the nominal suspect; the existence of a memorial crystal for the still-living goddess Apito remains unexplained.

docs.title: Notable Events
docs.text:
• The Shadow Boxer broadcast. Carl and Donut appear on a documentary programme run by Rosetta Thagra — a former crawler, ninth-edition author of the Cookbook, and employee of Carl's sponsor the Open Intellect Pacifist Network. She forces Carl through his mother's suicide on his fifteenth birthday, his father's abandonment, the police interrogation, and the Anacortes Boys' Ranch, on air. Buried in it are two coded messages: "potatoes and milk" (pointing him back to Crawler Milk's cookbook entries and the toraline root vegetable) and a run of Miami-set TV screencaps telling Donut where to go in Phase Two. The liaison Harbinger kills the interview mid-sentence, bans Rosetta from crawler programming, and tells Carl to his face that he is working to have him "disposed."
  • The Celestial Thorn Room. Seven ruined Orisha shrines, one Sun of Reawakening, one repair. On a last-second warning from Katia — who has been wearing the Crown of the Sepsis Whore since Eva Sigrid threw it at her — Carl has Bomo rebuild Yemaya's shrine instead of Ogun's, resurrecting Yemaya and buying Katia a path out of the crown. The cost is immediate and permanent: Ogun appears in person, strips Paz of his grace and of any ability to heal his death-debuff, and crushes Anton's head underfoot. Bomo is teleported to Floor 9 as a reward for his work and is lost to the party. As Paz dies, Sister Ines flags him with her squad banner and turns him into a card rather than let him go.
  • Katia's addiction is revealed. Sent by Carl's own directions to a hidden drug den in the Desperado Club, Katia is found comatose for ten hours. She is addicted to four substances — Travis Priest, Creamsicle Charm, blitz sticks, and a single dose of Glory Bound — and the blitz habit turns out to predate the floor by a long way. Her stats are permanently scrambled and her Constitution gutted. Mordecai privately tells Carl the smart move is to let her self-destruct, because it is Katia or Donut; Carl refuses to discuss it.
  • The Astrid assassination disaster. Carl's carefully trapped ambush corridor is never used. Samantha, sent to cause a diversion, blunders into the casino and tears open a portal to the Nothing, releasing Minge, a Level 225 feral demon. Astrid unleashes the vorpals — celestial suicide-bomber guards — and dies knowing she was about to be freed. Carl rips her wings off; Katia's totems finish her. The Desperado Club is destroyed and closed for reconstruction, which incidentally ejects thirty-five trapped Faction Wars officials into the shark-infested flood of Larracos. Carl uses a mercenary coupon to hire the entire Penis Parade — thirteen dancers plus Doctor Bones and Bucket Boy — into the guild.
  • Odette's confession and sponsorship switch. Rather than become the Princess Posse's adjutant as Huanxin Jinx had arranged, Odette announces on air that she is entering the dungeon herself as the sponsor of the goddess Nekhebit. Off the record afterwards she tells Carl the whole story: Pieter, Armita, the rigged tenth-floor summoning that killed Mordecai's brother Uzzi, her confession, Armita's murder, and her conviction that the crawl must be shut down without collapsing the inner system's fuel supply. The Princess Posse's adjutant ends up being Baroness Victory, an orc judge and half-sister of the late Queen Consort Ugloo.
  • The AI seizes control of the crawl. After building the Reminiscence Hydra with no input parameters at all — "It was created by me with no contribution whatsoever" — the system AI takes the crawl away from Borant. The liaison Orren negotiates it back on air, the earliest a crawl has ever gone primal. Six of the nine Faction Wars teams immediately try to abdicate and are refused under the quarantine rules.
  • Carl discovers his half-brother. The Phase Two keymaster's lair is his father's trailer, spliced in from a different date, and Carl is locked in with it for 42 minutes. He watches his father die of a morphine overdose administered by a stepmother he never knew existed, and meets Asher, the six-year-old half-brother he never knew existed either. Donut later reveals Beatrice knew about Asher and hid it.
  • The Reminiscence Hydra. The keymaster fight: a nine-headed flesh boss whose heads are Asher, his mother Tami-Lynn, Beatrice's mother, Carl's friend Monobrow Sam, his boss Dick, his landlord Mr Roth, a coworker named Sally, Donut's cousin Sugar Cube, and cat-show judge Lucian. Every head is somebody who died in the collapse. Its totems include an "Alpha Male Carl" and a resurrected Frank Q, the first time the dungeon has fielded a dead crawler as a card.
  • The Residual and the failed trap. A benefactor box from the Open Intellect Pacifist Network sends Carl alone to a homeless shelter in Homestead, Florida on Christmas morning to hear a Residual named Paulie recite his daily speech. Orren yanks Carl out mid-sentence and explains it as a suicide gambit by his own sponsors, who are now fugitives with their assets frozen. Carl trades the Residual's stash away rather than be killed for it.
  • The Christmas party power struggle. Louis, furious, forces a Christmas celebration on a guild that has just been told most of them will not get a key. Carl's objection — "This isn't Christmas" — collapses when he produces a turkey for the bopca to roast.
  • Quan Ch, Tserendolgor, and the Capitolio. Quan Ch out-plays Donut's deck twice with Force Play and takes both Cuban keys. Carl teleports across the city via a trap anchor lodged inside Samantha, and Quan is killed. But the Capitolio doorway is already dying; when it crumbles, its key dies with it. Tserendolgor — Ren, the dog-soldier crawler and Donut's nemesis — will not fight them for the last one. She confesses on the record that she did cheat the pet show and that Mongo was the rightful champion, hands Carl her entire inventory and her pet Garret, and detonates a self-destruct bracer rather than give the showrunners the fight they wanted. Her squadmate Chuluuna was already dead; Khulan follows her.
  • Sister Ines's collapse and Ysalte's death. Sponsored and patronised by the Nebulars, Sister Ines is pushed back over the edge her medication had held her behind. Her level-15 Word Weaver charm takes the Madre de Aguas — and through it every creature within earshot — and eventually Amayon himself. Louis kills her. Her patron, the goddess Ysalte, the Vinegar Bitch, arrives for revenge and is decapitated by her own Paz totem, whom Katia armed with the Bolt of Ophiotaurus.
  • Shi Maria's tattoo. A Golden Combo card intended for Alpha Male Carl retargets onto Carl himself when the spider kills its intended partner. For 180 seconds Shi Maria wears Carl's body, rifles his inventory, burns a hole through the floor with Self-Immolation, gouges out and eats Li Jun's eye for the blood on the needle, and uses the Vengeance of the Daughter tattoo kit to ink the Eye of the Bedlam Bride into his chest — anchoring herself to him permanently so that ripping her card can no longer be rid of her.

docs.title: Stairwells
docs.text:
Floor 8's official exits are the two stairwells per region, each behind a locked door that only a key opens, and each usable only by the keyholder's own squad. Most of the survivors left that way.

Carl, Donut and Imani did not, and neither did thousands of others, because the design guaranteed there were nowhere near enough keys — and because destroyed doorways destroyed their keys outright. The chamber around a stairwell is sealed and indestructible; Hole, Phase Through Walls, and digging all fail against it.

Carl's solution, worked out with Prepotente over chat, exploits the Demon Eviction event itself:

  1. Kill Sister Ines, freeing Amayon from her charm.
  2. Teleport Amayon out of the Madre de Aguas's body so he takes his true, full-power form.
  3. Refill the world with the exact type of souls that broke Sheol in the first place — crab spawn — which required talking Raul the crab into it.
  4. Buff Amayon with Sheol fire, using Emberus's Martyr's Path boon to ignite every footstep Carl had taken outdoors, including the ones directly beneath the demon.

Powered that far, Amayon's homecoming portal expands to cover the entire planet. When it opens, everything solid on Earth is sucked upward into the sky. The indestructible stairwell chambers are torn out of the ground with everything else — and the moment a chamber strikes the hell portal, its walls teleport away and the stairwell inside is exposed. Crawlers who dug trenches underneath their chamber and stood directly beneath it were carried up alongside it and hit the stairwell in mid-air.

The floor therefore has no conventional final descent. Carl, Donut and Imani stand in a tunnel under the Iglesia de Jesús de Miramar with a neon X painted on the ceiling above them, the heavens open over Cuba, the world is stripped bare, and they are swept up into the sky and onto Floor 9. The floor's last words:

Welcome, Crawler.

Welcome to Faction Wars.

Immediately before leaving, Carl spends the first of the Princess Posse's three Emergency Action Items, arguing that the other Faction Wars teams' refusal to vote endangers the integrity of the game and asking the AI to put the pending procedural votes to the viewing audience. It is granted. Among the results:

  • Remove Safety Protections For Faction Sponsors — passed, 98% audience vote.
  • A tenth team populated with NPCs, afforded the same protections as the rest — passed, 52%. Designated the Home Team, based in Larracos, co-warlords Juice Box and Sir Ferdinand.
  • Long-range artillery limits raised, accelerated pet leveling, and an enlarged Faction Wars playing field.

docs.title: Leaderboard
docs.text:
No full leaderboard table with races, classes, levels and bounties is published anywhere on Floor 8. The only ranking data the book gives are narrative.

A top ten is read out after the floor's first recap episode:

Rank Crawler 1 Prepotente 2 Princess Donut 3 Carl 4 Lucia Mar 5 Elle McGibbons 6 Katia 7 Florin 8 Osvaldo — Level 60 Curupira Ranger, a first appearance on the list 9 Li Na 10 Burcu — Level 59 badger-headed Porsuk, class Swashbuckler, also a newcomer

Other confirmed data points: Carl opens the floor at #3 with a 2,000,000 gold bounty and Donut slips from #1 to #2 in the same instant; Quan Ch is confirmed to have climbed back into the top ten before Donut is credited with killing him ("A champion has fallen. A bounty has been claimed"). Carl reaches level 73 and Donut level 63 by the floor's end; Elle jumps six levels at once — to 72 — from a single Graupel cast.

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: Level 9
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Crawlers entering the floor: 32,429, per the arrival broadcast. Over 1,300 had died in the four days between the Floor 8 collapse and materialising here. 20,221 were still alive when the floor ended — described in-text as a record, with the second-highest total "not even close"
  • Time limit: 30 Days, or 90 hours after a winner is declared, whichever is sooner. Neither clock ran out: the floor was destroyed early by the god Emberus on a 66-minute doomsday countdown
  • Carl's standing at arrival: rank #1, bounty 6,000,000 gold, 231 septillion views, 887 quadrillion followers, 420 quadrillion favorites. He also receives a Platinum Venison Box on arrival
  • Setting: Larracos, City of Dreams — a funnel-shaped city sunk into an enormous pit, with 66 numbered rings counted from the bottom up, and the Semeru dwarves' castle at the very bottom, built on the roots of the All Tree. The surrounding Plains of Larracos are cut into nine pie-slice territories, one per attacking team; a tenth NPC team defends the city itself instead of holding a slice
  • Theme: "Faction Wars" — the dungeon's long-running inter-government war game, played for the first time with a crawler team on the board, an NPC team on the board, and every participant's safety protections switched off
  • Structure: four combat phases — the Ceasefire, the Ramp-Up, Open Hostilities, and the Peeling of Larracos. The book's four Parts map onto them exactly
  • Exits: 293 stairwell chambers seeded across the floor, sealed until Faction Wars is won or 30 hours remain to collapse, whichever comes first

AI Commentary (in-voice, written for this wiki — not a book excerpt)

"Nine of the richest creatures in the galaxy paid a fortune to come down here and play soldier with people who couldn't say no. Then I took their safety off. Then I took their showrunners' crawl. Now get out there and kill, kill, kill."

docs.title: Arrival
docs.text:
Floor 9 opens directly out of Floor 8's ending, with no gap and no globe chamber. Carl and Donut materialise in a wet, stinking alley between two crumbling stone buildings on a recently-drained lower ring, the mud still reeking of the Floor 5 ocean and the corpse of a Concierge Shark ("Killed by suffocation when the Semeru Warden finally decided to open the drain") lying deeper in the alley. Imani lands elsewhere in the city and reaches them by chat within seconds.

"Welcome, Crawler. Welcome to Faction Wars. You are on the ninth floor. Time to Level Collapse: 30 Days or 90 hours after a winner is declared, whichever is sooner ... Leaderboard rank: 1. Bounty: 6,000,000 gold ... Remaining Crawlers: 32,429 ... 10 teams remain. Entering Larracos, City of Dreams."

The arrival warnings do most of the work of setting the floor up: everything looted from the Floor 8 memory simulation is stripped out of inventories; the Ceasefire is announced at 60 hours; and, tucked in among the routine army/officer notifications, the system delivers the floor's actual thesis statement — the reason Faction Wars deaths are real deaths for the first time in the series:

Warning: Protection enhancements have now been removed. While some protections exist during a ceasefire, those of you who were getting regenerated can now die. So don't trip and break your neck. At least wait until the ceasefire ends.

It's delivered as a throwaway line-item warning, sandwiched between "you have no officers in your army" and a truce announcement — no fanfare, no dramatic buildup. That flatness is the point: after eight floors of narrative safety nets, "dead is dead" finally applies to Faction Wars combat exactly as bluntly as it applied to mobs back on Floor 1.

Within minutes of landing the board reshuffles itself. Eight of the nine off-world teams form a truce named The Bloc and declare war on both Team Retribution and the Princess Posse. Donut accepts Team Retribution's counter-offer of a truce before Carl can finish a sentence, which turns out to be the single most important decision of the floor: allied with the defenders, the Posse is never expelled from Larracos.

docs.title: The floor's central premise
docs.text:
Cascadia's welcome broadcast (delivered in a slurring, clearly drunk voice) lays out the shape of the thing:

  • Ten teams. Nine attacking teams spread around Larracos "like a pie," and one defending NPC team headquartered in the city.
  • The goal is the castle at the centre. Attacking teams are eliminated if their warlord is killed or if their own throne room is held for six hours. Soldiers of an eliminated team are "traditionally given the option to join the new team or be slaughtered."
  • Crawlers are, in theory, bystanders. They may enlist with any faction during the Ceasefire, or flee into the woods — but every team can hunt down strays and conscript them. This is why recruiting every surviving crawler into the Princess Posse becomes Carl and Donut's first job.
  • The city is closed until four teams remain. Only then does the final phase, the Peeling of Larracos, begin.
  • This season the NPCs fight back from the start, which the game has never seen before. The Semeru dwarves are drilling, mining explosives into the down-ramps, and sabotaging enemy camps before the shooting starts.

Two developments turn the floor from a spectator sport into a massacre. First, around 50,000 former crawlers — organised by Doctor Porthus Hu's Open Intellect Pacifist Network, shipped in aboard a refitted garbage freighter named Homecoming Queen — volunteer into the Princess Posse at level 60 with no gear. Second, each of the other eight teams is simultaneously handed roughly 20,000 armed mercenaries apiece, about 150,000 in total, who keep their off-world weapons and power armour.

docs.title: Phase One — The Ceasefire (nominally 60 hours)
docs.text:
Saferoom rules apply everywhere inside Larracos; crawlers can cast and build but cannot harm anyone living within the city. Teams recruit, fortify, and lock their thrones in place. The phase ends the moment the last warlord marks themselves ready, or by unanimous vote, or — the loophole that actually fires — if a warlord voluntarily withdraws, which shortens the clock by a preset amount.

It does not last 60 hours. Commander Stockade of the Lemig ("Democratic") Sortion, driven insane by a dose of Shi Maria's madness during a botched attempt to weaponise her against Carl, smashes his own skull open against the floor of Queen Imogen's kitchen. The system rules it a psychosis-induced suicide, counts it as a voluntary withdrawal, and cuts the ceasefire by 23.33 hours. Total elapsed Ceasefire: roughly 37 hours.

docs.title: Phase Two — The Ramp-Up (180 hours)
docs.text:
The rules that define the floor's first week of fighting:

  • No offensive magic. A suppression field covers the whole floor. Spells that heal, buff, shield, obfuscate, dig, or build still work; anything designed to directly harm does not.
  • No teleport-based magic or skills. Puddle Jumper, the Gate of the Feral Gods, and teleport traps are all dead. Carl's Gloom Wraith Phase survives on a technicality — it is a phase, not a teleport.
  • No celestial summonings.
  • Entry into enemy territory only through designated corridors roughly one kilometre wide, at fixed points. Only crawlers with the Scout endorsement (18 per team) may cross elsewhere.

The intent is stated outright by Baroness Victory: "It is designed to force bloody, hand-to-hand combat. And non-magical artillery." Against opponents with pulse rifles and trebuchets, it is designed to kill the Princess Posse in the first week.

docs.title: Phase Three — Open Hostilities
docs.text: Triggers when the Ramp-Up expires. No corridors, no magic ban, no restrictions on summoning — borders stop meaning anything and every team can move anywhere. This is the phase the Posse opens with Operation Ruin, a simultaneous four-front offensive.

docs.title: Phase Four — The Peeling of Larracos
docs.text: Triggers automatically once only four teams remain. The city opens to everyone. Any attacking team that holds the central throne room for six continuous hours wins Faction Wars; the defending team must hold it for a full week to win, and re-taking the room restarts that week. Only single teams, never alliances, may claim the throne. Whoever holds it controls Larracos's network of 100-plus automated defence towers, with a half-hour grace period after the room changes hands.

docs.title: The ten teams
docs.text:
Spot Team Warlord(s) Fate How eliminated 1 The Bone Clan / Skull Empire Crown Prince, later King Stalwart; King Rust joins as war chief 5th eliminated King Stalwart is torn apart by his own war mages after ejecting them from his army; with no eligible claimant on the kill, the system awards the Bone Clan's remaining assets to Team Retribution instead 2 The Operatic Collective Hortense Leadership Unit 3rd eliminated Volteeg detonates a suicide tank, killing the Hortense Leadership Unit along with roughly 10,000 Bloc soldiers 3 The Princess Posse Carl and Princess Donut Winner — 4 The Blood Sultanate Princess Vinata, "the Sepsis Whore" 4th eliminated Princess Vinata is killed at the Temple of Khepri by Kandy "Bigs" Newton, a level-29 sluggalo, with a head-mounted hatchet 5 The Prism Kingdom Empress D'Nadia 2nd eliminated Empress D'Nadia is killed by Mongo on Donut's order, ending her dynasty's line 6 The Dream Epitome Tagg 9th eliminated Warlord Epitome Tagg, secretly grafted into Louis Santiago's replacement heart and lungs, is killed when Mongo eats them 7 The Lemig / "Democratic" Sortion Commander Stockade 1st eliminated Commander Stockade, driven mad by Shi Maria's insanity effect, kills himself 8 The Madness Architect Houston 6th eliminated Architect Houston is killed by Carl's Gloom Wraith Phase mid-experiment 9 The Reavers Warlord Fang 8th eliminated Warlord Fang dies hiding inside his pet dragon Calliope when the Reaver castle chain-detonates — Team Retribution (NPCs, defending Larracos) Juice Box and Sir Ferdinand Voluntary forfeit (10th) Warlords Ferdinand and Juice Box voluntarily abandon Larracos rather than keep fighting, forfeiting to the Princess Posse

An eleventh entity nobody planned for, the War Mage Rebellion, emerges mid-floor when a procedural quorum ruling accidentally grants it standing as a "non-team entity." It is led by the war mage Akuma and then hijacked by Agatha, the Residual with the shopping cart, whom the system installs as co-warlord over Akuma's furious objections. See Faction Wars Teams for the fuller roster.

docs.title: Layout & Notable Areas
docs.text:
• Larracos, City of Dreams — the funnel city, 66 numbered rings counted from the bottom up (not all of them complete circles), each ring a wide terrace with a yawning hole at its centre. Gothic stone architecture, vine-covered arches, a single waterfall falling from the upper rings and cascading down the roofs like a staircase. Ring 50 holds the Larracos College of Magic and the upper cultural district; ring 49 is housing; ring 45 is clothing shops; ring 9 holds the Piccadilly Theatre, directly under the waterfall; ring 4 holds the Desperado Club. The lower rings are still flooded on arrival from Carl and Katia's Floor 5 water dump, drained down to ring 3 by the time the floor opens
  • The Semeru castle — at the very bottom, built along the roots of the All Tree as "a monument. An apology." Still submerged at the start of the floor. Below it, once the city is gone, nothing but a bed of dead roots as thick as elephant trunks over a hole
  • Shanty Town — a ring of hovels and markets that sprang up out of nowhere around the top lip of the funnel after the flooding, far larger than the shanty town that normally forms. It encircles the entire entrance, counts as a settlement in its own right, and is the only neutral ground bordering every territory. Carl buys the mayorship off Ferdinand for a bowler hat
  • The Plains of Larracos — nine slices of mostly flat grassland, the exception being the rocky, occasionally lava-wreathed mountain in the north where the orcs' pre-built castle, The King's Point, sits. The region's only major river runs off that mountain and into Larracos as the waterfall
  • The FUPA — the Princess Posse stronghold, the Fortress of Unyielding Power and Authority, so named after a tug-of-war between the changelings and the Sledge left the AI to break the tie. Built around a bait-shop saferoom on a hill in spot 3
  • The high elf castle (the "Sugar Cube") from Floor 6, transferred down and used as the Lemig Sortion's headquarters — see High Elf Castle
  • Area 52 — a forest saferoom and forward base used for missile batteries and for reloading Louis's bomber
  • The Nest — a purpose-built granite synergy tower on the lip of Shanty Town, the tallest structure on the floor, keyed to Atrocity-class spells. Donut fights the last third of the war from its parapet
  • Club Vanquisher — reached this season through two entrance temples, one in Larracos and one in Shanty Town (the Temple of the Dagda). Site of Operation Snake Pit and of the floor's worst single atrocity

docs.title: Monsters (Level 9 area)
docs.text:
Faction Wars is a war, not a dungeon crawl, and most of what the crawlers kill are soldiers rather than mobs. The floor's regular wildlife lives in the expanded outer forests that the AI bolted on at the last minute, and consists of recycled mobs from earlier floors levelled up to suit — chilly goats from Floor 1, danger-dingo-riding kobolds from Floor 2, and a Rolling Battle Formation Ball (Level 70) that is a straight riff on the Ball of Swine, stuffed with Skank Skunk Warriors (Level 45) under the command of a Fancy Boy Battle Wizard (Level 55). See the Mobs overview for the wider catalog.

The manufactured and imported creatures matter more:

Name Tier / level Where Notes Zarogoth Level 50 generated mob Larracos "Sludge ghouls." Corrupted souls in a humanoid sausage casing, mass-produced by a soul-crystal generator hidden in the Piccadilly Theatre. Pierce them low and they drain out Reaver Cyborg Drop Trooper Level ~53 mercenary Princess Posse base Warlord Fang's personal defence deployment, dropped by paratrooper transport into the FUPA Juiced Rot Sticker Behemoth Level 40 pet Southern front Reaver pets raised with affection, then dosed with the Gurgles, insanity and rabies and fired at the Posse trenches as living bombs Flesher / War Mage Level 1 to 100 Everywhere A skin torn from a corpse becomes a flesher; a flesher that re-sleeves a body enough times becomes a war mage.
