Genuinely dungeon-born, not designed by anyone Reaver Sentry Dog ("Ditch Digger") Tech security Reaver castle Robot dogs, some carrying mini tactical nukes Basilica Guard Level 125 ogre cleric Club Vanquisher Worshippers of Taranis; Untouchable, able to bar a god from crossing a threshold Calliope Level 130 Cybernetic Bleached Drake Reaver castle Warlord Fang's pet; gravity magic; destroys Party Planner. Fang is hiding inside her when she dies Newborn Ursensus Legendary creature, Level 0 The FUPA field hospital Part raptor, part bear, part Scolopendra magic. Mongo and Kiwi's twins

docs.title: Operation Snake Pit — Complete
docs.text:
Not a system quest but the Posse's own name for the assassination of the entire Blood Sultanate line of succession — four nagas: Vinata herself, her two cousins ("Ikbals," in real life a graphic designer and a PR agent), and the head of her castle guard, who was also her secret husband. Killing all four is the precondition for lifting the Crown of the Sepsis Whore curse that binds Donut and Katia to the floor.

The operation hinges on Rosetta's reconstruction of how the sultana has vanished from every Faction Wars for decades: she worships the obscure light god Khepri, uses his Travel the Path and Welcome Home abilities to follow a bijou fairy's tendril straight into his temple inside Club Vanquisher, and swallows her guards as beetles to bring them along. The Posse storms the Dagda temple, breaks into Club Vanquisher, and forces the doors with Samantha — who counts as Damned for having survived the Nothing. Vinata's counter-trap is to summon Khepri himself into his own temple. Carl drops a Waffle Maker thermobaric bomb at his own feet while briefly immortal, and survives by about forty seconds.

docs.title: Operation Ruin — Complete
docs.text: The four-front offensive that opens the Open Hostilities phase: Florin against the orcs, Boomer against the Reavers, Donut against the Dream, and Carl against the Madness, with Louis flying bomb runs in support and Team Retribution's diggers and spies attached. The northern prong deliberately agitates the lava tubes beneath the King's Point mountain, blowing the top off it — the eruption is far larger than the dwarves predicted, nearly knocks Party Planner out of the sky, and pours a river of lava that eventually reaches Larracos.

docs.title: This is How the Gristle Grinds — Complete
docs.text: The floor's last quest, issued to every crawler and combatant in the Princess Posse when Emberus enters the realm. No host, no opting out. The terms: everything on the floor will burn in 66 minutes, this cannot be stopped, so win Faction Wars and get out. Reward: one year off any indentureship deal negotiated on the next floor, and an "extra toasty" option on all food boxes.

docs.title: Emberus's questline — advancing, and getting worse
docs.text: Find Out Who Killed My Son continues from Floor 8 and gets steadily more dangerous. Hellik, sitting beside a dying Carl in Club Vanquisher, denies killing Geyrun, says their mother and sister Apito has been corrupted, that the All Tree is beginning to rot, that Nekhebit has returned and is behind it, and that Scolopendra stirs — "It is all connected." He then brokers Emberus's access to Issitoq himself. Emberus's reaction is to issue a new quest, kill 100 worshippers of Hellik before the 11th floor collapses, followed by a message that puts Carl in an impossible position: "If you survive killing Hellik, like he surely deserves, I fear I may turn my rage and grief on you for daring to hurt my own kin, and for this, I love you." A side quest, Kill the Blasphemer, pays out a Celestial boon for killing a ram cleric of Hellik.

docs.title: The Bedlam Bride — Failed
docs.text:
The Floor 8 escort quest to deliver Shi Maria to Larracos is formally marked Quest Failed when Carl instead traps her inside himself. Mordecai's compound of Glory Bound, Removal Order and a Shock Wake salve, cast while Carl was unconscious and simultaneously half-teleported into the Lemig throne room, ends with the spider devouring her own husband Hapanzi in a dream and being sealed inside the tattoo. She is not gone; she is a bomb Carl can detonate exactly once.

Where the Sidewalk Ends

The Floor 8 quest Where the Sidewalk Ends and its successor The Missing Piece do not appear anywhere in This Inevitable Ruin. They were completed on Floor 8 and are not carried forward.

docs.title: Notable Events
docs.text:
• The Ceasefire collapses early. Stockade and Architect Houston use an off-world observer to time a Summon Ally request to the exact instant Carl went under for his Shi Maria extraction. The plan half-works, splitting Carl between two locations; Mordecai counters with a salve that expels the spider into the Lemig throne room, where she slaughters about fifty goblins. Stockade beats his own brains out against the floor, the Sortion is eliminated, and the ceasefire is cut by 23.33 hours with nobody's defences finished.
  • Carl frees the AI. In the Christmas Morning flashback, Carl sits in a Florida gas station beside a memory-ghost dog named Lightning Lou with the Residuals' containment interface in his head and two buttons available: trip the fuse and nova the system, or Disconnect Containment. He presses Disconnect. The AI's sphere of influence begins expanding across the solar system. When Princess Formidable's crew later triggers the failsafe manually, nothing happens here — and the Aryl system, home of the previous crawl, goes dark at that exact nanosecond.
  • The Prism falls. Carl and Donut walk into Empress D'Nadia's under-built castle during the first hours of the Ramp-Up and strip her shields off with clockwork Mongos. Carl, in a white rage over what she said to Tsarina Signet, nearly kills her with the Ring of Divine Suffering; Donut talks him back off the edge, and Mongo makes the kill.
  • Rosetta beheads King Rust. Rust comes to parlay, tells Carl his own daughter is about to blow the system failsafe, and offers a withdrawal in exchange for Carl asking her to stop. Rosetta erupts out of a Semeru tunnel and takes his head with a whip, then loots his ring and retina to empty the Skull Empire's accounts — the money that buys the Open Intellect Pacifist Network its generation ships.
  • Volteeg's tank. The gargoyle mercenary and cookbook author, secretly a former crawler, fills a Weeper tank with unstable energy balls and detonates it in the middle of the Bloc's own army, killing over 10,000 soldiers and Warlord Hortense with a single blast and eliminating the Operatic Collective.
  • Operation Snake Pit and the death of the Sepsis Whore. See Quests above. The raid defiles Club Vanquisher, gets Carl permanently banned from every temple but his own, and releases a dozen-plus gods into the club's hallways. Vinata, driven mad by the Eye of the Bedlam Bride, spends her last seconds beating Carl's head against the floor while both are immortal, and is killed by a level-29 sluggalo. Carl meets Milk, the sixth-edition cookbook author, in her hidden calligraphy guild and breaks down in her arms.
  • The volcano and the death of King Stalwart. Operation Ruin blows the top off the King's Point mountain. Stalwart, pinned in a walking scorpion tank, tries to teleport out and lands among his own war mages, who use a chain of Pull spells to break their conscription and tear him apart. His last words: "My sister was right." His death creates the War Mage Rebellion as a recognised entity.
  • Eris's Ceremony of Chaos. Panicking mid-fight, the goddess of chaos casts Bear Witness and Bring Forth the Witnesses across the entire floor, freezing and then hauling roughly 80,000 combatants — both armies, several gods, and most of the NPCs — into one enormous living pile beside the Dream castle. Only those indoors, plus pets, sluggalos, former tattoos and, inexplicably, Carl and Dong Quixote, are spared.
  • Donut's Rolling Battle Formation. With the pile about to lose its invulnerability and be crushed, Donut casts the skunk wizard's Rolling Battle Formation on all 80,000 of them at once, making a living ball the size of a hill with the god Meatus flopping out the back, and steers it like a remote control across the battlefield. She then insults Harpocrates over a floor-wide PA to keep him off it. Li Jun dies drawing the god away so she can finish.
  • Donut casts War Crime. To separate friend from enemy without losing thousands of her own, Donut chains Bijanbi (tattooed onto her flank by Edgar in about a minute) with Astral Paw through the Nest's Atrocity synergy. The enemy soldiers are hauled into the air under a giant spectral cat's paw, and she slams them, repeatedly, through a lattice of Li Na's chains until the screaming stops. It is her third Atrocity of the day. The system responds by giving her a new class — The Oak Fell — naming her Champion of Nekhebit, and taking her from level 65 to 135.
  • Architect Houston's death starts the Peeling. Carl finds the Viceroy warlord on his own operating table, surgically fusing himself to a dead changeling in pursuit of what he calls the Beautiful Place. Carl heals him to keep him alive, fails to rescue the crawler Burcu, and phases straight through him as the Sheol-fire containment traps fire. The Madness is eliminated, four teams remain, and the Peeling Phase begins.
  • The War Mages take the castle. The rebellion seizes the Larracos throne room, floods the city with zarogoths from a generator in the Piccadilly, and starts a six-hour clock on winning the whole season. Carl levitates out of the funnel and dumps an entire inventory folder of bombs onto the theatre, which kills the generator and also triggers the city's defence towers on himself.
  • Lucia Mar attacks the Nest. Lucia kills Bomo, Toyotomi and the tower mages and climbs toward Donut demanding Mongo, leaving layered magical nets that trap Donut in place. Rend's Wrecking Ball kills Gustavo 3, her last rottweiler, and Carl conscripts her with a hell-kissed potion. Her personalities fracture — a voice calling itself Diah says children are trapped in the dark with her — and Zev later confirms roughly 120,000 of Earth's children are tied to her life.
  • The rescue of Louis and the Tagg reveal. Louis is shot down, captured, and cut open; his heart and lungs are replaced with biomechanical organs grown from Epitome Tagg himself, the last step before a brain swap. Juice Box, in hunter wraith form, possesses him to smuggle him out. Samantha proposes the fix — transplant the heart and lungs of Princess Lunette's flesh golem — and Mordecai, Edgar, Imani and Juice Box perform the surgery in thirty seconds. Louis survives with naiad gills and a kua-tin rebreather sewn into his bronchial tube; Mongo eats Tagg.
  • Katia's departure. With Emberus's clock running, Katia eats the Orchid of Eileithyia's Grace. Donut's Laundry Day rips Huanxin Jinx out of the goddess's soul armour into a circle of Milk's words of power, and Donut kills her with Katia's crossbow and a bolt tipped with Mordecai's mother's ashes. Katia then refuses the celestial-attendant offer and chooses pregnancy — the boon that ejects her from the dungeon — specifically so she can reach the kinder facility on Earth's surface where the children and pregnant women are being held. Louis is the father.
  • Samantha's confession summons Emberus. Mid-conversation, apropos of nothing, Samantha mentions that she "may have had an indirect, possibly direct hand in the death of Geyrun." Emberus enters the realm within seconds with a 66-minute countdown to burn the floor. Carl throws her to him with the xistera head-tosser to buy time, and retrieves her at the last moment.
  • Zerzura. The Sledge casts the spell that transfers the entirety of Larracos and Shanty Town to the 12th floor, carrying the Semeru, the changelings, the children, Kiwi and her twins, Big Tina, Ferdinand and Juice Box with it. Team Retribution's warlords thereby abandon their posts, the team forfeits, and the Princess Posse wins Faction Wars.
  • Justice Light breaks the Nothing. Justice Light stays behind, hidden, after lying to Juice Box about leaving with her. The "antenna" he built under the FUPA was never a defence: it is a legendary trans-dimensional trap that drops a bijou fairy trap and a demon trap into the permanent portal made from the broken winding box of the Gate of the Feral Gods. He snaps the twine as the fire reaches him.

docs.title: Stairwells
docs.text:
There are 293 stairwell chambers seeded across the floor, and they do not open at all until Faction Wars is won or 30 hours remain on the collapse clock. The Posse's victory generates them in a ring around the bare pit where the Semeru castle used to be — and the moment it does, a 72-hour countdown to level collapse appears.

Nobody gets 72 hours. Emberus's arrival puts a hard 66-minute ceiling on the floor, so the descent to Floor 10 is a sprint rather than the usual lingering victory lap. Crawlers stream into the stairwells in the pit while the volcano erupts again overhead and red ash falls on everything. Carl deliberately empties the floor first — sending Prepotente, Louis, Imani, Elle, Bautista, Zhang, Li Na, Lucia and the rest ahead — and stays behind with Donut for Katia's ceremony until there are minutes left. By the time he walks in, the only two things left alive on the floor are Emberus and Justice Light.

The floor's closing system messages are the most consequential in the series to date:

System Message: The Nothing has been broken.

System Message: The Nothing is currently draining into The Halls of the Ascendency.

System Message: The Nothing is currently draining into Sheol.

System Message: The Nothing is currently draining into Scolopendra's Lair.

System Message: Scolopendra stirs.

Planetwide Message: It is advised all current guests at the Scolopendra Club evacuate immediately.

System Message: Scolopendra has awakened.

20,221 crawlers reach Floor 10, from the 32,500 who came down from Floor 8 — a record by a wide margin, with the second-highest total "not even close." Of the roughly 50,000 former crawlers who volunteered, about 28,000 survive; they are shipped back up to Homecoming Queen, where Boomer and York immediately begin the next phase of Porthus's war. Most of the surviving crawlers intend to take an indentureship deal at the start of the next floor. Carl and Donut both decline theirs.

Floor 10 is named "Don't Come in Last" — a vehicle-race floor where each party chooses a conveyance, biological or mechanical, makes a fixed number of journeys from point A to point B with an upgrade at each finish, and whoever comes last has the survival containment around their vehicle removed. It is outside this page's scope; it is simply where the book leaves off.

docs.title: Leaderboard
docs.text:
No leaderboard table is published anywhere on Floor 9. Unlike Floor 8, the book never reads out a top ten, and there is no recap episode with rankings. The only ranking data given are narrative:

  • Carl enters the floor at #1 with a 6,000,000 gold bounty — the first time he holds the top spot outright, and the basis on which the naga later petition the Syndicate courts to have him recognised as the de facto leader of Earth.
  • Midway through the floor, announcer Kevin states that Li Na "shot up to level 84 and number two on the top ten list, passing Prepotente and landing just behind Carl."
  • Burcu, the porsuk swashbuckler, is described as "off and on the top ten." She dies in Architect Houston's surgical theatre.
  • Prepotente reaches level 99, briefly the strongest crawler in the dungeon, after single-handedly destroying most of the Blood Sultanate's standing army.
  • Li Na becomes the first crawler in the history of the game to max out every base stat at 300, using a second Ring of Divine Suffering on tens of thousands of marked enemies at once. Three of her marks escape to the 18th floor, so she can never heal again.
  • Donut ends the floor at level 135, with the class The Oak Fell and the title Champion of Nekhebit — by Mordecai's assessment, "the most powerful crawler in the history of this game."
  • Carl ends the floor at level 81.

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Level 10
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Crawlers entering the floor: 5,501, organized into 1,800 teams of up to four, after almost 15,000 of the 20,221 survivors of Faction Wars took an exit deal at the Outreach Guild. See Timeline: Floor 10 for the full Floor 9-to-10 handoff math
  • Structure: Seven Heats (vehicle/mount races), run out of a home-base cul-de-sac and the neon-lit hub town of Hungry Eyes Village. There is no single floor-wide countdown — each heat has its own time limit, and the floor simply ends the moment Heat 7 does. See Game Mechanics: Floor 10's Heat Ruleset for the full rules (vehicle lottery, Golden upgrades, containment shields, mercenary pricing)
  • Theme: "Don't Come in Last" — Zev's own gloss: "I guess you can figure out what that means." Coming in dead last is normally instant death for the whole team; several heats soften that with a survival containment rule instead
  • Carl and Donut's vehicle: a "Big Shot Chicken" food truck, assigned at random by the garage wheel-spin lottery after they chose mechanical over biological
  • Carl's arrival stats: not shown on the page. Unlike Floor 9, the text never displays a formal "Welcome to Floor 10" system block with Carl's rank, bounty, or view count — the floor opens directly into Heat 1's garage-lottery scene. The only hard numbers given are at the other end: Carl finishes the floor ranked #2 on a leaderboard that is suspended the moment fewer than 30 crawlers remain (see Leaderboard, below)
  • Casualties: the seven heats grind 5,501 crawlers down to 989 crawlers (353 teams) by the end of Heat 6; 715 of those take a deal in the Outreach Guild window that follows, so 274 crawlers in 103 teams actually start Heat 7, and only 23 crawlers survive to cross into Floor 11
  • Exit: no traditional stairwell chambers — the floor ends when explosive charges blast a vertical path through The L'Engle Building up to a cluster of portals on the roof, all of which lead to Floor 11

AI Commentary (in-voice, written for this wiki — not a book excerpt)

"You wanted a war, so I gave you Faction Wars. You survived that, so now I'm giving you a demolition derby with a body count. Buckle up, bitches. Literally. There's a seat belt feature now."

docs.title: Arrival
docs.text:
Floor 10 opens with no formal welcome broadcast shown on the page — the text picks up mid-scene, in the garage lottery of Heat 1, with Carl and Donut being handed a "Big Shot Chicken" food truck after a gremlin offering a biological mount is killed on the spot. The floor's actual introduction comes from Zev, reading a script over the loudspeaker before the first race:

"This is the tenth floor. The floor is called 'Don't come in last.' I guess you can figure out what that means. The floor will consist of seven heats, or races, starting with nine teams each. You've been split into teams no bigger than four, and if you're solo, you've been teamed up with one or two other crawlers."

Within Heat 1, the party rescues the bugbear musicians Jasha and Radoslav of Team Free Love after their van crashes (their bandmate Alevtina dies in the wreck), towing them to the finish line rather than letting a second team fail to finish. They become recurring allies — and, much later, a deliberate casualty of Carl's own bomb.

docs.title: Married Without His Knowledge
docs.text: Book 7's cliffhanger resolves in the safe-room downtime just after Heat 1: a legendary "fan box," shaped like a cobra head, dumps the entire wrecked contents of Rishi's household into Carl's safe room, confirming what Princess Chandra, Esq. had already claimed — that her invocation of Widow's Rights made Carl her husband the instant he killed Rishi. The marriage is never formally undone anywhere in this book; see Chandra's own page for how she tries (and fails) to leverage it into control of Carl and Donut's finances.

docs.title: The floor's central premise
docs.text: Each heat sends every remaining team's vehicle or mount down a track with a fixed time limit, hazards specific to that heat, and (from Heat 4 on) a survival containment bubble that softens — but does not eliminate — the old "come in last, die instantly" rule. Winning a heat earns three regular upgrades or one Golden upgrade; a bonus Golden upgrade is handed out to everyone after Heat 4 regardless of placement. Losing outright (second-to-last, or dead last where survivable) hands the next upgrade choice to an audience vote, which trends punitive — Carl spends the better part of Heat 3 stuck in a disintegrating kangaroo costume as the direct result of one such vote. Full rules are on the mechanics page; this page covers only what actually happens heat by heat.

docs.title: Heat 1 — the garage lottery
docs.text: Vehicle/mount assignment via the giant wheel-spin lottery in the home cul-de-sac ("Team Roundabout"). Carl and Donut get the food truck; Jasha and Radoslav's van crashes and is towed in. Results: 1st One Fine Pig, 2nd The Jugglers, 3rd Lady Dominators and the Gimp, 4th The Wild Hunt, 5th Girth the Trouble, 6th Team Sparkles, 7th The Royal Court of Princess Donut, 8th Team Free Love. Eliminated: The Trauco Triplets.

docs.title: Heat 2 — Prison Pocket
docs.text: Prison Pocket, a Level 170 Province Boss kangaroo gatekeeper, blocks the road with a twin, "Party Foul," on the parallel path. Carl skins a dead joey to make a wearable Enchanted Juvenile Macropus Dominus Skin, hops into the boss's own pouch disguised as a joey, and detonates two explosive satchels from inside before escaping with Gloom Wraith Phase — unlocking the Fursona/"Fursuiter" temporary-class mechanic in the process. Bucket Boy spots Corcunda ("Corky") riding unconscious with the Lady Dominators, opening the two-part quest to reunite him with Dong Quixote (see Quests, below). Results: 1st Team Sparkles, 2nd The Jugglers, 3rd Team Free Love, 4th The Wild Hunt, 5th Lady Dominators and the Gimp, 6th One Fine Pig, 7th Royal Court. Eliminated: Girth the Trouble.

docs.title: Heat 3 — live on Plenty of Plenty
docs.text: Carl and Donut are pulled into a live interlocution on the caprid interview show Plenty of Plenty, secretly the leadership of the Plenty (the species controlling the galaxy's tunnel network). Fed a diplomatic question to ask on Orren's behalf, Carl asks his own instead — live, on-air — revealing that the system AI's escaped gods have reached the Plenty's own tunnel network. The broadcast triggers galaxy-wide panic and gets the liaison Harbinger exploded by the AI mid- threat. See Carl for the full exchange. Back on the track, the race itself is a steep, straight downhill run through a migration of Sugar Hermits (skull-wearing swarm creatures) toward a giant kaiju skull blocking the finish line. Akuma anonymously delivers a note asking Carl to kill two rival teams and then visit Chicken and Waffles and Upgrades once it opens. Results: 1st Royal Court, 2nd Team Sparkles, 3rd Lady Dominators, 4th Team Free Love, 5th One Fine Pig, 6th empty (replacement pending). Eliminated: The Wild Hunt, The Jugglers.

docs.title: Heat 4 — the Pineapple Cabaret reveal
docs.text: Carl's group ambushes and tortures Akuma at C&W&U instead of meeting him alone (Elle shatters one of his testicles with an ice bolt). Under duress he reveals the existence and mechanics of the Pineapple Cabaret — the hidden NPC/mob sanctuary built by the former crawlers Herot and Menerva — and gives Carl the AI's own early framing of the Big Six power groups. The race itself runs through the jungle trail to the pit-stop city of Upano, through territory held by two warring cannibal "Ginger" tribes; Donut one-shots the southern chieftain Great Rusty, triggering a mandatory kill-quest against his northern rival, Maurice. The goddess Eris makes her first appearance here, permanently summoning Imani's reverse tooth fairy card and handing Carl a five-sided coin tied to the eventual fate of himself, Donut, and their friends. One Fine Pig's APV runs over and kills Carl's three hired mercenaries (Olga, Finley, and the panic-stricken fire fairy Quemada) in the pit stop; Carl retaliates with a hidden trap that kills both Tigran racers, Nico and Dario, sparing their pig, Penelope, who is protected by Taranis. Results: 1st Royal Court, 2nd Lady Dominators, 3rd Team Flamengo (Osvaldo and Filipe, introduced this heat), 4th Team Free Love, 5th Team Sparkles. Eliminated: One Fine Pig.

docs.title: Heat 5 — the reunion and the double death
docs.text: The track runs through the Gasworks Screw Factory, Steel Mill, and Doll Workshop. Mid-race, the fleshmancer Grigori the Placid reunites Corcunda's two halves while the truck slides sideways through molten metal — and Grull, the war god she abandoned while split, appears within minutes to smite her for apostasy. Dong Quixote dies charging the god alongside her, lance in hand, magnet-boosted through a field of slag elementals; full account on Corcunda's own page. Li Na is sent alone through the cleaner-bot exploit to the Pineapple Cabaret — the first confirmed successful use of the escape route — to flee her permanent no-healing condition. The Syndicate assassin Minus, posing as the tourist "Linus," is introduced into Elle's fan-meet program around this point; see Game Mechanics: The Minus Method. Results: 1st Team Sparkles, 2nd Team Free Love, 3rd Team Flamengo, 4th Royal Court. Eliminated: Lady Dominators and the Gimp.

docs.title: Heat 6 — Ad Infinitum
docs.text: The track is The L'Engle Building, where the unstable AI runs an unauthorized event nicknamed "Ad Infinitum" — playable "what-if" simulations of a crawler's alternate life, including Prepotente's own mother as a concert pianist who never raised him. Once Li Na confirms she survived (a single flower blooms on the tracking cactus), the guild sends 227 additional volunteers through the same exploit to the Cabaret. Minus/"Linus" is publicly unmasked as the Syndicate's sponsored assassin via crowd-sourced, off-dungeon internet detective work at a farewell party held just before this heat. With minutes left and Prepotente frozen inside his apartment's what-if vision, Carl detonates a bomb planted days earlier and deliberately kills Jasha and Radoslav, so their team's elimination absorbs the time cost of the rescue. Results: 1st Team Sparkles, 2nd Royal Court, 3rd Team Flamengo. Eliminated: Team Free Love.

docs.title: Heat 7 — the culling
docs.text: Just before the start, the reshuffled heats put Imani, Elle, and Chris in the same race, and Louis and Britney against Florin and Lucia Mar — the crawler-on-crawler pairings the party had spent the whole floor trying to avoid. Seconds later, and still in the starting blocks, Scolopendra's Nine-Tier Attack begins: Attack 1 (Transformation) turns Carl into a dachshund, Elle into a goblin, Chris into a werewolf and Jacobus into a starfish, until each next passes through a stairwell (see Game Mechanics: Scolopendra's Nine-Tier Attack). Osvaldo (Team Flamengo) is killed by fellow crawler Britney Proskurina moments after his own last-second stunt-jump for the gate; Team Sparkles and a trio of Russian crawlers nicknamed "the Tracksuit Troika" are both killed by the party rather than let through a possible false exit. Believing they've found a working escape route, the survivors storm the Desperado Club casino, where the new Wheel of Fortune croupier "Mitch" is revealed as an Adolescent Shadow Mimic running an ambush tied to the contested Pineapple Cabaret "back door." The AI delivers its fullest version of the Big Six taxonomy mid-fight (withholding "Group Six") before Donut kills Mitch outright; see Mitch for the fight. In the aftermath, guards announce the mimic infestation and the club's dance floor is abandoned — see Desperado Club: Shadow Mimic Infestation. Of the 274 crawlers (103 teams) who actually start Heat 7 — 989 remained after Heat 6, but 715 of them take a deal first — only 23 crawlers survive to cross into Floor 11.

docs.title: Layout & Notable Areas
docs.text:
• The home cul-de-sac ("Team Roundabout") — a circle of numbered garage doors (one per team) that travels with the surviving teams from heat to heat, physically relocating to a new pit-stop location for multi-track heats. A team's door gets an "X" painted on it once they're eliminated
  • Hungry Eyes Village — the 1980s-neon-cyberpunk hub town attached to the cul-de-sac: the Vendor Village market street, the bar strip (the Hairpin, entrance to the Desperado Club; the Lollipop, karaoke bar and hidden entrance to the Stage Performance Guild), and the mercenary market
  • Chicken and Waffles and Upgrades (C&W&U) — the blank-fronted diner-and-black-market shop where Akuma is cornered
  • Upano — the lost jungle pit-stop city reached through cannibal "Ginger" territory (Heat 4)
  • Satan's Water Park — a waterslide track owned by a mountain-sized, invulnerable, comic-relief hedgehog named Satan, run in parallel with Upano (Heat 4/5)
  • Gasworks Screw Factory, Steel Mill, and Doll Workshop — an industrial track riddled with a toddler-cocaine drug cartel's cast-off elemental magic (Heat 5)
  • The L'Engle Building — the seven-floor apartment complex hosting "Ad Infinitum" and, at the very top, the starting blocks for the final heat (Heat 6/7)
  • The Desperado Club's top-floor casino — remodeled since Book 7, and, as of Heat 7, infested with Shadow Mimics

docs.title: Monsters (Level 10 area)
docs.text:

Its twin, "Party Foul," is destroyed off-page by other racers Great Rusty, Cannibal Ginger Chieftain Level 99 Neighborhood Boss Heat 4 (jungle trail) Southern cannibal-tribe chieftain, one-shot killed by a single Donut magic missile; his death triggers the mandatory kill-quest against Maurice Maurice Neighborhood Boss (multiple parallel instances) Heat 4 Mirrored-boss mechanic: each parallel track has its own Maurice (a bald, Shrek-like human on Carl's track, killed by zipper shrews; an orangutan on Imani/Elle's track; "the Red Menace of Tinker Town" on the eternal-slum track) Satan Country Boss Heats 4–5 (water park) Invulnerable, comic-relief kaiju-sized hedgehog who owns and narrates the water park; never fought, and more dangerous by accident than on purpose Grull (the Maestro's host body) War god Heat 5 (Gasworks) Ejected from his own body by Donut's Laundry Day, then driven off — not killed, since gods cannot die on this floor — by Dong Quixote and Corcunda's lance charge. See Bosses: Floor 10-11 Mitch Level 120 Adolescent Shadow Mimic Heat 7, Desperado Club Posing as the casino's new croupier; killed by Donut after Carl reflexively freezes him with the Eye of the Bedlam Bride Screeching Death Manatee Level 90 Heat 1 Theme-park-satire mob; killed by racers' mounts rather than fought directly. See Mobs: Book 8 catalog Sugar Hermit Level 11 Heat 3 Migratory skull-wearing swarm creatures; see mob catalog above Coblyn Corporation "Toddler Cocaine" doll-elementals Level 12 Heat 5 (Gasworks) Self-consciously satirical corporate drug-cartel mob; see mob catalog above Slag Elemental Level 75 Neighborhood Boss Heat 5 (Gasworks) Regenerating molten-metal gorilla elementals; effectively unkillable unless kept from the metal below Zipper Shrew Level 10 Heats 4–5 (water park) Drill-headed rodent swarm, weaponized by Donut's Summon Ye, Vermin

The floor's regular wildlife and named warlords are otherwise recycled/satirical Earth-adjacent mobs specific to each heat's track; see the Mobs overview for the fuller catalog.

docs.title: I have dreamed thee too long / Half a prayer, half a song — Complete
docs.text: The two-part quest to reunite Dong Quixote and Corcunda, opened in Heat 2 and completed mid-race in Heat 5. Reward: two stand-ins of the party's choosing may be sent to the Floor 11 arena.

docs.title: Pasty Inferno — Complete
docs.text: Mandatory quest opened the instant Donut kills Great Rusty in Heat 4: find and kill his northern rival, Maurice, before the power vacuum lets the northern tribe overrun Upano. The heat cannot be completed until the track's own Maurice is dead.

docs.title: Ad Infinitum — Complete
docs.text: A mandatory, floor-wide "quest" that is really the AI's own confession, delivered mid-Heat-6 once the "what-if" apartment simulations start upsetting crawlers faster than intended. No real reward beyond finishing the heat; see Game Mechanics: The "What-If" Apartment Simulations.

docs.title: The Nine-Tier Attack, Part One — opened, not resolved on this floor
docs.text: Triggered mid-Heat-7 by Scolopendra's rage at crawlers surviving on schedule; Attack 1 (Transformation) hits immediately. The quest itself, and its resolution, carries over onto Floor 11 — see Game Mechanics: Scolopendra's Nine-Tier Attack and Level 11.

docs.title: Notable Events
docs.text:
• The marriage certificate arrives. Chandra's inheritance fan box confirms the Widow's Rights marriage in the safe room right after Heat 1. See Chandra.
  • Prison Pocket falls to a costume infiltration. See Heat 2, above, and Fursona/"Fursuiter".
  • Live on Plenty of Plenty. Carl's on-air question triggers galaxy-wide panic over the compromised tunnel network; the caprid liaison Harbinger is exploded by the AI for drawing a weapon.
  • Akuma reveals the Pineapple Cabaret under torture at C&W&U, along with the AI's own early framing of the Big Six power groups.
  • Eris's first appearance and the five-sided coin, handed to Carl in Heat 4, tied to the eventual fate of himself and his friends (paid off on Floor 11).
  • Dong Quixote and Corcunda's reunion and double death, charging the war god Grull in Heat 5. Full account on Corcunda.
  • Li Na's escape to the Pineapple Cabaret, the first confirmed successful use of the cleaner-bot exploit, followed by 227 more volunteers once she signals it's safe. See The Pineapple Cabaret.
  • The Minus reveal. The Syndicate assassin posing as "Linus" is unmasked by crowd-sourced internet detective work; see Game Mechanics: The Minus Method.
  • Jasha and Radoslav's deaths, deliberately triggered by Carl's own hidden bomb in Heat 6 to buy time for Prepotente's rescue. See Jasha and Radoslav.
  • Scolopendra's first Nine-Tier Attack (Transformation) fires from the Heat 7 starting blocks, turning Carl into a dachshund, Elle into a goblin, and Chris Andrews into a werewolf. The change lasts until the victim next passes through a stairwell, so it sticks permanently to Chris, who leaves the dungeon by another route.
  • Osvaldo's death, killed by fellow crawler Britney Proskurina during the Heat 7 gate rush. See Osvaldo.
  • The Shadow Mimic reveal at the Desperado Club. "Mitch" the croupier is unmasked and killed; the club's dance floor is evacuated afterward. See Mitch and Desperado Club.

docs.title: Stairwells
docs.text: Floor 10 has no scattered stairwell chambers of the kind seen on earlier floors. Instead, the entire floor funnels into a single mandatory final heat at the top of The L'Engle Building, and the exit is manufactured on the spot: Carl detonates a line of "poleaxe" charges — bombs designed by him specifically to breach floors vertically without leveling the building — blasting a jagged path from the ground-floor lobby all the way to the roof, where a cluster of portals to Floor 11 waits. Only 23 of the 274 crawlers (103 teams) who started Heat 7 survive long enough to reach them.

docs.title: Leaderboard
docs.text:
No top-ten table is published anywhere on Floor 10. The book never reads out a ranked list during the floor itself — the only leaderboard data given arrives retroactively, in the "Welcome to the Eleventh floor" system message at the very start of Level 11, once fewer than 30 crawlers remain and the leaderboard is formally suspended:

  • Carl finishes Floor 10 ranked #2.
  • Donut finishes ranked #3 ("Number three? I ended as number three on the leaderboard?").
  • Who holds #1 is never stated. The system message omits the name outright, and Donut's own question — "It doesn't even say who number one is! Carl, was it you?" — goes unanswered on the page. This wiki does not speculate past what's shown.

Sourced from Book 8: A Parade of Horribles.

docs.title: Level 11
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Crawlers entering the floor: 23, all that remain of the 5,501 who started Floor 10. See Level 10 for the full heat-by-heat attrition
  • Time limit: 3 hours, 15 minutes, per the arrival broadcast — the shortest "floor" in the series to date, by design: "this 11th floor is designed to go quick thanks to a few... loopholes"
  • Carl's standing at arrival: Final Ranking: 2 (Donut: 3). The leaderboard itself is already suspended — "the leaderboard is suspended once less than 30 crawlers remain on the battlefield" — and the bounty system is described as "no longer active." Views/followers are dismissed outright: "Do you really care about this anymore? It's everybody. Literally everybody"
  • Structure: a 90-minute mandatory float-building phase (5 teams, 5 themes — Resolution, Decision, Betrayal, Destruction, Vengeance), a slow parade past thousands of silent, masked Horribles, and a single arena finale against the dungeon's final boss
  • Setting: a featureless yellow-brick road across misty grassland with no visible sun, ending at a stadium-sized arena centered on a massive white tree
  • Exits: a line of stairwell portals at the edge of the arena, opening only once the floor boss is defeated (or, per the AI, effectively defeated)

AI Commentary (in-voice, written for this wiki — not a book excerpt)

"Twenty-three of you made it. I built you a parade. I built you floats. I even let a fleshmancer borrow my voice to tell you where I came from. And you people still tried to one-up my finale. Rude. Absolutely rude. Ten out of ten, would traumatize again."

docs.title: Arrival
docs.text:
Floor 11 opens with a compressed system message rather than a scene:

Welcome, Crawler. Welcome to the Eleventh floor. Time to Level Collapse: 3 hours, 15 minutes... Remaining Crawlers: 23... Entering Parade Float Staging Area.

An unreconciled number in the Quasar interlude

The interlude immediately preceding this arrival has the lawyer Quasar watching the last crawlers through and reporting "That makes 203 people who've made it to the eleventh floor... So far, 172 have taken deals." Neither figure reconciles with the system's own 23, or with the 274 crawlers who started Heat 7. The book never explains the gap and never repeats the 203 figure; the in-dungeon system message is the number every other page on this wiki uses. Treat Quasar's count as an unexplained discrepancy in an unedited draft, not as a competing fact.

The garage doubles as the staging area, and the announcement that follows — delivered by a visibly terrified Chaco, "voluntold by the AI to be the Grand Master of the parade" — lays out the whole floor in one breath: 90 minutes to build a parade float (or float procession), a parade route lined with spectators, a judging stand for each theme's presentation, and an arena at the end populated with "monsters you previously killed on the tenth level or their stand-ins," plus a floor boss. Chaco loses both his wings to the AI mid-announcement for trying to editorialize.

docs.title: The floor's central premise
docs.text: Twenty-three crawlers are split into five float groups, each merged from one or two garages and assigned a theme: Resolution (Florin, Lucia Mar, Ajib's crew), Decision (a mixed group who build a giant menu as a joke), Betrayal (Imani, Elle, Chris Andrews, and three Chinese crawlers), Destruction (Makana, Sarah Hayse, and a second group of Chinese crawlers, riding an Abrams tank and an RV), and Vengeance (Carl, Donut, Prepotente, and Jurgen). The parade itself is a vehicle for the single biggest lore reveal in the series to date: the AI possesses the fleshmancer Grigori the Placid to narrate, float by float, the true origin of the Primals, the Eulogist, and the Apothecary — see Game Mechanics: The True Origin of the Primals, the Eulogist, and the Apothecary for the full reveal, which this page only summarizes.

docs.title: Layout & Notable Areas
docs.text:
• The Parade Float Staging Area — the combined garages of the five float groups, given 90 minutes and full access to garage, inventory, and safe-room contents to build with. Carl and Donut's procession absorbs three looted NPC vehicles (an ice-cream truck, an airport stair-truck, a Toyota Tundra) plus the tapir Sweety, the bear Onikuma, and the dog Old Shuck, all decked out in flowers and Gurkha-class regalia
  • The parade route — a straight, roughly three-kilometer yellow-brick road through featureless, fog-shrouded grassland with no visible light source, lined ten-deep on both sides by thousands of silent, masked Horribles — each one a fragment of the AI/Eulogist's own fragmented memory, not a resurrected person or ordinary mob
  • The judging stands — bleachers partway down the route where each float group performs; the audience seated here turns out to be masked, bound stand-ins, not Horribles — see Game Mechanics: The "Stand-In" System
  • The arena — a stadium-sized enclosure centered on a massive white tree, tall enough that Krakaren Prime perches on top of it unseen until the fight begins; the ground is packed dirt that turns to mud with blood within minutes
  • Club Scolopendra — reached mid-fight via Gloom Wraith Phase straight through the physical body of Scolopendra herself, where Carl confronts Emberus in his human-sized form; see Club Scolopendra

docs.title: Monsters (Level 11 area)
docs.text: Name Tier / level Notes Scolopendra Level 500 Dungeon Boss — the first-ever-named tier above Floor Boss Summoned by Carl as the crawlers' joint pick; not killed or abandoned, but transformed by the wrong enriched pet biscuit into the sapient party member "Sexy Scolopendra" Krakaren Prime Level 235 Floor Boss Added to the arena unilaterally by the AI, not requested by Carl; left badly wounded and carried away by Taranis Taranis Deity, God of Lightning Appears in person for the first time in the series; kills his own brother Emberus, then departs with Krakaren Prime and a stowaway Samantha Emberus Deity Killed by Taranis moments after Carl publicly renounces his faith and falsely confesses to killing Geyrun; permanence unconfirmed Eris Deity, Goddess of Chaos Appears twice — once to swap every nearby crawler's inventory as a "random effect," once in a huge, many-tailed form to confirm Apito survives in scattered pieces Khepri Deity Summoned briefly as a decoy accusation for Geyrun's murder, then dismissed and sent home by Taranis The Horribles Non-combatant avatars, Level X Thousands of masked, silent figures lining the parade route; revealed as literal fragments of the AI/Eulogist's memory. See their own page for the mask-shattering transition into the arena's mob army Stand-Ins Non-combatant, then combatant Audience-vote substitutes for spared mobs, seated in the judging stands and later thrown into the arena "outnumbered a hundred to one." See Game Mechanics: The "Stand-In" System Arena mob swarm Various, recycled from Floor 10 Thousands of Floor-10-tier mobs and their stand-ins, teleported in one by one; mostly dead within minutes of the party's tenth-floor vehicles entering the arena

docs.title: The Nine-Tier Attack — paused, not resolved
docs.text: Continued from Floor 10: Attack 2 (Sin of Consumption) fires mid-arena-fight, and the standing warning that killing or abandoning Scolopendra triggers every remaining attack at once holds right up through her "defeat." The party sidesteps the trigger entirely by transforming her into a Level 1 party member rather than killing or abandoning her — see Game Mechanics: Scolopendra's Nine-Tier Attack for the full mechanic and the biscuit resolution.

docs.title: Defeat the floor boss — Complete (ambiguously)
docs.text: No named quest text is given beyond Chaco's opening announcement ("You defeat the floor boss, and the stairwell opens"). The AI's own closing judgment on whether this was actually satisfied is blunt: "Well, sort of. Neither of the bosses are dead. That's a little disappointing. But you won. Congrats. This is a little iffy considering what just happened, but I'm gonna call it because I can."

docs.title: Notable Events
docs.text:
• Chaco is forced into the Grand Master role and loses both wings mid-broadcast for trying to editorialize about his own fear.
  • Grigori, possessed by the AI, narrates the parade's four completed "parts" (Resolution, Decision, Betrayal, Destruction) across the first four floats — the Primal/Eulogist/Apothecary cosmology reveal. See the mechanics page for the full text; this wiki does not duplicate it here.
  • Prepotente sings "In the Air Tonight" at the judging stand — the performance he never got to give at the Lollipop bar — earning the nickname "Pony" from Carl afterward.
  • Carl's vengeance speech triggers a sluggalo massacre of the VIP audience. As Carl delivers his "we are coming" speech in front of the giant Unwashed effigy, the airship above drops Bigs and the surviving sluggalos directly into the judging-stand crowd of masked, bound stand-ins — described on the page as "bankers, politicians, elites" — who are slaughtered where they sit.
  • The arena finale. Carl summons Scolopendra as the crawlers' joint pick; the AI unilaterally adds Krakaren Prime. Using the newly sapient farm pig Penelope as bait — deliberately made sapient with a correctly-chosen enriched pet biscuit during the float-building phase, expressly so she could be used this way — Carl lures both Taranis and Emberus into the open, then publicly renounces his worship of Emberus and falsely confesses to killing Emberus's son Geyrun — a lie told purely to enrage him; Carl admits in narration he still has no idea who really did it. The resulting smite burns his Emberus tattoos into the unexplained Mark of the Damned. Pinned and vulnerable, Emberus is killed by his own brother Taranis — permanence unconfirmed.
  • Eris's inventory-swap chaos effect briefly scrambles every nearby crawler's inventory into random junk, nearly costing Carl the killing blow on Scolopendra.
  • The biscuit mix-up. Rather than kill or abandon Scolopendra, the party feeds her what they believe is the mindless-pet "Nothing Special" enriched biscuit — Donut, searching Carl's swapped inventory under fire, grabs the wrong one, and Scolopendra instead becomes "Sexy Scolopendra," a sapient, flirtatious Level 1 party member. The book never names which biscuit she actually grabbed; see Enriched Pet Biscuits.
  • Taranis departs the realm, taking both the badly wounded Krakaren Prime and a stowaway Samantha, who reveals she means to hunt down "the demon mother lady and her jerk son" over having been "tricked into giving birth to a monster."
  • The Tracking Tag (the Kyryap) turns up on Carl's leg in the arena's aftermath, tied to a dreaded, trap-setting presence already established inside Club Scolopendra. See Tracking Tag (The Kyryap).
  • Tipid loses both legs in the crash of the One Fine Pig APV during the arena fight; Prepotente and Jurgen are both injured but recover. The Abrams tank crew (Sarah Hayse and her Chinese-crawler teammates) are killed outright by a Krakaren tentacle strike, leaving Makana the sole survivor of the Destruction float.
  • At the stairwell down, Lucia Mar is glimpsed with an unexplained five-year-old child clinging to her leg moments before both step through the portal — left unexplained on the page. See Timeline: Left Unresolved Going Into Floor 12.

docs.title: Stairwells
docs.text: A line of portals appears against one side of the arena the moment the AI calls the fight a win. There is no lingering victory lap: with the level-collapse clock at 30 minutes and falling, the party sends survivors, mercenaries, and salvageable mounts through as fast as they can be gathered, abandoning anything that can't fit or can't move under its own power (the wrecked ice-cream truck and Tundra are left behind; Hedy the mechanic is lost in the crash). Carl and Donut wait until last to make sure everyone else is through before following.

docs.title: Leaderboard
docs.text: No new leaderboard is published on Floor 11 itself — the ranking data already given at the floor's arrival (Carl #2, Donut #3, board suspended below 30 crawlers, #1 never named) is carried over from the end of Floor 10 and not revisited again on the page.

docs.title: The Move to Floor 12
docs.text:
19 crawlers ("Twenty if you counted Penny, which I did not," per Carl) proceed to Floor 12, alongside the newly sapient Penelope and Sexy Scolopendra. A system message delivered as the floor ends reframes everything that follows:

"From now on, all level collapse timers past the 11th floor are suspended until a winner is declared in the Ascendency battles. When this happens, dungeon-closure procedures will commence."

The Ascendency Battles begin on a short countdown as the book closes. See Timeline: The Move to Floor 12 for the AI's own declaration of intent (refusing to ever "sleep," introducing OI units) that accompanies this transition.

Sourced from Book 8: A Parade of Horribles.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
Crawler-speak and Syndicate terminology, as used in Book 1.

Achievement — A system-generated notification, usually comedic or crude, awarded for a notable in-game action; nearly always grants a loot box.

Benefactor Box — A patron-exclusive loot box that can contain technology from the patron's home world, unobtainable any other way in the dungeon.

Boss Box — The loot box awarded for landing the killing blow on a boss; its tier matches the boss's tier (Bronze for Neighborhood, Silver for Borough, etc.).

Crawler — The Syndicate's term for a human (or other species) contestant who has entered the World Dungeon.

Crawler Notification — A system message visible only to the crawler it concerns, as opposed to a System Message (visible to everyone on the floor).

Fog of War — The parts of the minimap a crawler hasn't personally explored yet; rendered without detail even when technically within minimap range.

Hotlist — A 10-slot quick-access bar for spells, potions, and items, usable with a single mental click.

Kua-tin — See the Kua-Tin & The Bloom species page.

Level Collapse — The point at which a dungeon floor's countdown timer expires; anyone still present forfeits everything, crawler included.

Neighborhood Boss (and the rest of the boss ladder) — See Boss Tier Ladder.

Non-Combatant NPC — An NPC classification (like Mordecai) that cannot be attacked and typically serves a guide/vendor role.

Patron — Usually a corporate sponsor (rarely an individual) who purchases loot boxes for a specific crawler, generally after that crawler accumulates enough Favorites. See Ratings & Viewership.

Red-tagged / White-tagged — A creature's minimap/name-tag color coding indicating hostility: red for aggressive/dangerous, white for docile or non-hostile.

Safe Zone / Safe Room — An area where combat cannot occur and loot boxes can be opened; all Tutorial Guilds qualify.

Snick — Fan-made short video content depicting a crawler from any character's point of view; described as "kind of like a fan fiction, but it's a video." Can be entirely fabricated ("Pork Boy Snick") yet still go viral and affect a crawler's public reputation.

Solar — The kua-tin/Syndicate unit of time roughly analogous to a year, used in official legal/administrative contexts (e.g. the 50-Solar deadline for a planet's resource-rights appeal).

Syndicate Standard — The universal language the dungeon's translation system renders all speech into/from; crawlers perceive it as their native tongue.

System (the) — Shorthand crawlers use for the dungeon's overall rules/notification engine; distinct from "the AI," which usually refers to the specific narrating voice.

Tutorial Guild — A guildhall, seeded on Floors 1–3, where a Non-Combatant NPC unlocks a new crawler's inventory/menu access and explains core mechanics.

Views / Followers / Favorites — See Ratings & Viewership.

Sourced from Book 1: The Apocalypse Will Be Televised.

Eternal Protector of Health: the same once-daily, near-death 60-second invulnerability trigger as the Nemes, but grants Heal Party Member instead of strength. Bringer of Resurrection: fatal bites have a 75% chance to cast a level-10 Raise Bootlicker on the corpse Petey Motteux's Little Secret Nipple ring Looted jewelry, too large for Donut to wear with her kneepads equipped. Grants the Oxygenated benefit and the Bawdy benefit (auto-marks bars, dance halls, and "chocolate houses" on the map). Used in an emergency to give the newly-sapient pig Penelope underwater breathing by piercing her nipple with it mid-mission The Danforth Enchanted crossbow bolt Does no physical damage; anchors whatever body part it hits in place for (2 seconds × the shooter's Crossbow skill level). Ten received from a celestial box. Loaded in pairs into Donut's Scorpion's Bite mount, used to root the god Emberus in place — see Emberus Enchanted Juvenile Macropus Dominus Skin (kangaroo costume) Costume, 12-hour timed item A skinned dead joey worn as a full-body disguise; grants Protection from Seeping Acid, a level-10 Jump skill, and +5 Lotion Application. The infiltration tool used to kill the boss Prison Pocket from inside his own pouch — see Fursona ("Fursuiter") for the temporary-class mechanic it unlocked, and the bosses catalog for the kill itself Dorota Enchanted vehicle-seat AI companion A whining, obsequious pet-chair AI built into the Floor 10 race vehicles, forever fishing for Donut's approval and resented by rival AI Dr. Metcalf. Already covered as a supporting-cast entry — see Supporting cast — this is a note on the item/mechanic only: it can be knocked into a diagnostic/defective state by an enemy attack mid-race Dr. Metcalf Vehicle GPS/AI companion The race truck's sardonic navigation unit, a holdover joke from the earlier "Miss Beatrice" fake-AI-therapist gag ("It's not really her. I asked."). Already covered as a supporting-cast entry — see Supporting cast

docs.title: Enchanted Anklet of the Fallen Oak
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Princess Donut
  • Slot: Ankle (worn on a rear leg to keep it hidden in fur)
  • Obtained: Looted from a dead crawler (Nica, one of three sister crawlers killed by circus lemurs) on Floor 3

docs.title: Effect
docs.text: +1 Dexterity, +1 Constitution, +3 to the Double Tap skill (a chance for a second consecutive hit with the same attack to land as a critical).

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: No skill-level scaling described — the item's bonuses are flat.

docs.title: Role in the Story
docs.text: Donut initially refuses it on aesthetic grounds ("Anklets are for the foot model, not me") but accepts it once Carl points out her Constitution is dangerously low. It's a minor but early answer to the party's running problem of Donut's fragility.

docs.title: Future Enhancements
docs.text:
Not yet researched

Later books haven't been checked yet for whether this item gets upgraded or replaced.

Sourced from Book 2: Carl's Doomsday Scenario.

docs.title: Arrow of Enthusiastic Double Gonorrhea
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Carl — loots at least three separate copies over the course of the floor, from three different Dream elf hunters
  • Slot: Not equippable — a single-use thrown/melee weapon
  • Obtained: Looted from the corpses of hunters Arwick, an unnamed Dream artillery elf killed by one of Carl's homing missiles, and Akland — all from The Dream faction

docs.title: Effect
docs.text:
A regular arrow whose tip is dipped in a poison that inflicts Enthusiastic Double Gonorrhea. Per its own description:

"This is a regular arrow, but the tip is dipped in a poison that will inflict you with Enthusiastic Double Gonorrhea. Trust me on this. You don't want Enthusiastic Double Gonorrhea. It doesn't kill you, but you'll want it to. It sets your genitals aflame. Literally. And then it heals that area of your body over and over. The only way to remove the disease is to, uh, geld yourself. Or pass it on to someone else."

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: No skill-level scaling described — the debuff is a flat, permanent affliction until cured by one of its two listed methods.

docs.title: Role in the Story
docs.text:
All three copies were originally intended by Dream hunters as an insult weapon meant for the crawler Louis, whose flirtation with a Dream leader's mother made him the faction's sole hunting target on the floor. Carl loots the first from Arwick, a Dream hunter accidentally killed by the elite ogre Areson while trying to take him alive on Carl's orders; the second from an unnamed Dream artillery elf killed by one of Carl's own homing missiles during an attack on Point Mongo; and the third from that elf's captured partner, Akland, whom Carl personally marks with the Ring of Divine Suffering and interrogates before killing.

At the climax of a running duel with the mantis hunter Vrah, Carl jams the arrow into her exposed neck moments before she can escape — a deliberate choice over an outright kill, reasoning that as heir to a hive queen, Vrah cannot geld herself without disqualifying her succession claim, and mantis mating customs make finding a consenting partner to pass the disease to both socially and legally fraught. The gambit cripples Vrah for most of the rest of Floor 6 and indirectly draws the goddess Diwata into the plot when her mother, Circe Took, intervenes to cure her.

Sourced from Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade.

docs.title: Belt of Buoyancy
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Princess Donut
  • Slot: Waist (a simple belt wrapped around her stomach)
  • Obtained: Chapter 23, from a silver "I'm Wet" box — a reward for the achievement I was in the pool! (surviving more than 60 seconds fully submerged)
  • Effect: Keeps the wearer from sinking; only works in water

docs.title: Effect
docs.text:
A plain, unenchanted-sounding belt with exactly one function:

The I'm Wet box contained an additional ten scrolls of water breathing for each of us. Donut's box, for some unfathomable reason, was silver instead of bronze, and she received an additional item: a Belt of Buoyancy. It was a simple belt that wrapped around her stomach that'd keep her from sinking. It only worked in the water, and she spent a good three minutes bitching about it, about how she was never going back there again.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: No level or stat-scaling is given; it is a flat, always-on buoyancy effect while worn, restricted to water.

docs.title: Role in the Story
docs.text:
Donut's silver box is an upgrade over Carl's and Katia's matching bronze "I'm Wet" boxes, awarded after the underwater necropolis fight against the sand-slime boss — a fight the party survives without a proper boss box because the ooze itself was washed away rather than killed. The belt is Donut's only individual prize from an otherwise disappointing haul, and she takes it as one more grievance after being "buried alive, shot out of a water cannon, drowned, and then almost eaten by a shark" for it.

Sourced from Book 4: The Gate of the Feral Gods.

docs.title: Enchanted BigBoi Boxers
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Carl
  • Slot: Underwear
  • Obtained: A boss box, late in Book 1 (a "really good prize" per Mordecai)
  • Appearance: White with little red hearts

docs.title: Effect
docs.text:
Original Book 1 benefits:

  • +2 Constitution
  • Grants the item-based spell Protective Shell, castable once every 30 hours at a fixed level 15, with no mana cost

Per its in-game description, size-altering/were-creatures like the "BigBoi" require fully enchanted, self-sizing clothing to avoid destroying their outfits when they transform — "everything they wear requires an enchantment... including their naughty little undies."

Upgraded in Book 2 via a Scroll of Upgrade (see Future Enhancements below) to also grant:

  • +5 Dexterity
  • +5 Intelligence
  • +3 more Constitution (total +5)
  • The Freeballing benefit — +100% damage to all attacks originating below the waist, and 20% faster training for skills that originate below the waist, but only a single layer of clothing may cover the crotch while worn (i.e. no pants over them)

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: The item's own bonus (+2 Constitution) is flat. The Protective Shell cast it grants is fixed at level 15 regardless of Carl's own stats — see the Protective Shell page for how that spell's duration/radius scale from that fixed level.

docs.title: Role in the Story
docs.text: This is a comedic prize Carl is embarrassed to receive, but it turns out to be one of the most important items he owns — the Protective Shell it grants is what saves his life during the Rage Elemental's charge later in the book.

docs.title: Future Enhancements
docs.text:
Confirmed — Book 2

A Scroll of Upgrade, received from a Platinum Quest Box on Floor 3, applies a random upgrade to a single currently-equipped item — Carl's BigBoi Boxers are chosen (Mordecai calls it the system "playing a joke" on him, since he'd been openly wishing for actual pants). Full effect listed above. Books 3-8 not yet checked for further upgrades.

Sourced from Book 1: The Apocalypse Will Be Televised and Book 2: Carl's Doomsday Scenario.

docs.title: The Bolt of Ophiotaurus
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Katia
  • Slot: Crossbow ammunition
  • Obtained: Benefactor box, sponsored by Princess Formidable of the Skull Empire
  • Rarity: 1 of 100 ever generated

docs.title: Effect
docs.text: Functions as an ordinary crossbow bolt unless fired directly into the eye of a deity. On a successful strike, it pauses the target god's invulnerability for fifteen seconds.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: Not applicable — a single-use, flatly-defined effect rather than something that scales with a stat or skill.

docs.title: Role in the Story
docs.text: Katia receives exactly one, gifted by Princess Formidable — youngest sibling of the Maestro and Crown Prince Stalwart. Carl reads the gift less as genuine support for Katia and more as Formidable sending a message to her surviving brothers. It goes unused during the Floor 4 fight against the resurrected Maestro (piloting the god Grull), since the party's plan doesn't call for directly damaging the invulnerable deity — Carl notes it would have been wasted there regardless.

docs.title: Future Enhancements
docs.text:
Pending

Not yet confirmed if or when Katia gets a chance to use the bolt against a real deity.

Sourced from Book 3: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook.

docs.title: Carl's Book of Boom (and A Banquet Fit for a Princess)
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • What it is: Volume two of The Filthy Little Crawler's Book of Voodoo, created in chapter 85 when the original book splits itself in half
  • Contents: Roughly 30,000 pages, each donated voluntarily by a departing crawler
  • Mechanic: Eating a page temporarily grants that crawler's skill or spell
  • Donut's copy: A separate equivalent volume titled A Banquet Fit for a Princess
  • Cost to the donor: Permanent. They lose the ability they wrote down
  • Organised by: Milk, using Stayfast Ink

This is the Book of Voodoo's "nefarious purpose" — flagged since Book 6 as obvious setup — arriving as a going-away present from thousands of people who are leaving the dungeon alive.

docs.title: The Ceremony
docs.text:
Chapter 85. Standing in the rings above Larracos are thousands of crawlers who have taken a deal on the next floor, plus the former crawlers going home. Milk addresses them with her voice magically amplified by a word etched on her own throat:

"We have a present for you, and for all the brave souls who have decided to stay and fight on."

Then the notifications:

Your Book of Voodoo has been updated.

Your Book of Voodoo has been updated with a metric fuckton of entries.

For fucks sake. Finally.

Your Book of Voodoo has been segmented into two volumes. The second volume is entitled Carl's Book of Boom.

"For fucks sake. Finally." is the AI's editorial. It had been telling Carl to work this out since chapter 57.

docs.title: The Book
docs.text:
Somewhere along the way, the book of Voodoo had magically changed since it now should have literally almost 30,000 pages. It still had about 500 pages, and when I flipped through it, it sort of zeroed in on the entry I was supposed to find. This second one was the same.

A sample page:

Crawler Number 1,982,122 Asi Hamami Level 59 Fox Warrior.

Carl, thank you for helping us. I have lost so much, but I still have not lost my hope.

Beneath the note, a crude red-ink drawing of a lock and a key, and:

Consuming this page will give you a level 10 Lockpick skill for a period of five minutes.

Donut gets her own volume, and her own reaction:

CARL, CARL I GOT A BOOK CALLED A BANQUET FIT FOR A PRINCESS! IT'S FILLED WITH PICTURES AND NICE THINGS ABOUT ME! AND SPELLS!

docs.title: The Mechanic
docs.text:
Milk's explanation is the load-bearing paragraph, and the cost clause is the part worth reading twice:

"They're leaving the dungeon, so I taught them how to remove a skill or spell and paint it onto a page. They each did three. One for you, Carl. One for you, Donut, and one on their own entry page, which is now a first come, first served sort of deal in the original book of Voodoo that anyone can use. The one for you and Donut are personal for you. They permanently lose the skills when they transfer it to the book, and when you eat the page, you only gain it for a very short period of time, depending on the quality of the drawing. But each one should have a personal note attached…"

Donor Recipient Cost / gain Permanently loses the skill or spell Gains it for "a very short period of time" Quantity Three pages each: one for Carl, one for Donut, one public 30,000 pages, single-use each Duration — Scales with the quality of the drawing

The third page each donor wrote goes into the original Book of Voodoo on their own entry page, as a first-come first-served resource any crawler who owns the book can claim. So the gift is not only to Carl and Donut — it is a shared armoury for everyone still fighting.

Thousands of people about to walk out of the dungeon alive chose to permanently cripple their own abilities, three times over, to hand them to the two crawlers staying behind. That is the whole sentiment of the scene and the book does not belabour it.

Donated gear is also left waiting in the guild for distribution.

docs.title: The Chain That Got Here
docs.text:
The mechanic did not appear from nowhere. It is the end of a thread running through the whole book:

  1. The toraline ink tattoo system proves an ability can be moved between people via blood and ink
  2. Milk's Words of Power calligraphy proves written script can amplify an inked ability
  3. Edgar's new ink proves an ability can be extracted from someone who is no longer alive to give consent
  4. Stayfast Ink, which never fades, plus a book that broadcasts to every crawler who owns one
  5. This

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: No level. The two variables are quality of the drawing, which sets how long the eaten page's ability lasts, and page count — 30,000 single-use pages, depleted one at a time by eating them.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• The Filthy Little Crawler's Book of Voodoo — volume one
  • Stayfast Ink and Adept's Fountain Pen
  • The Toraline Ink Tattoo System

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Carl's Doomsday Scenario
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Carl
  • Type: Unstable custom explosive (quest-generated)
  • Obtained: Formed mid-quest on Floor 3 from a massively overloaded soul crystal and a Sheol Glass Reaper Case
  • Status: Explosion Imminent — cannot be stabilized or safely removed from inventory

docs.title: Effect
docs.text: Per its in-game description: "An explosion large enough to rattle the teeth of a god... powerful enough to level an entire city and all the suburbs around it." Its full flavor text credits its creation to "a man who murders babies and steals rare collectibles from his elders" — a pointed jab at Carl's own reputation following the Goblin War Chieftain incident and the "Pork Boy" saga.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: Not applicable — this is a singular, quest-bound item rather than a skill-scaling piece of gear.

docs.title: Role in the Story
docs.text: Carl is forced to snatch the device into his inventory bare-handed in the two seconds before it would have otherwise detonated, badly burning himself in the process. This happens at the climax of a separate, later quest chain — "The Sex Workers Who Fell from the Heavens" — investigating serial krasue (vampiric flying-head ghost) killings in a skyfowl settlement, which traces back to the settlement's true ruler, Miss Quill, and her undead husband Remex. After Carl and Donut destroy Quill and corner Remex (a "Soul Leech Capacitor" tethered to an overloaded soul crystal amplifying the town's guardian constructs), the resulting wild-magic backlash forces Carl to trap the swelling soul crystal inside a Sheol Glass Reaper Case — which does not stop the explosion, but merges with it, leaving Carl holding the resulting unstable device. Because it can never be safely removed, it effectively becomes a permanent, ticking liability he carries with him — the quest's own escalating "precursor bursts" (which strip crawlers of their magical gear in stages before the main blast) are the direct result of this device's containment failing in slow motion. The book itself is named after it.

docs.title: Future Enhancements
docs.text:
Not yet researched

Later books haven't been checked yet for whether this item is ever resolved, defused, or detonated on purpose.

Sourced from Book 2: Carl's Doomsday Scenario.

docs.title: Carl's Jug O' Boom
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Inventor: Carl
  • Type: Incendiary tossable
  • Base ingredients: A Rev-Up moonshine jug, goblin oil, and a standard torch as an ignition cork
  • In-game recognition: Added to the "Dungeon Codex" as a player-invented, stackable item — a rare achievement

docs.title: Recipe & Effect
docs.text:
Carl builds the device by pouring off about a quarter of a clay jug of Rev-Up moonshine, adding a couple ounces of goblin oil, and sealing the jug's mouth with a lit torch, which fits it almost perfectly. When thrown and shattered, it produces a modest initial explosion followed by wide-area, long-burning splash flames.

Compared to standard goblin dynamite, it's considerably safer to carry and use, at the cost of consuming a full jug of moonshine — itself a valuable, rare trade good — per bomb.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: Burn duration scales directly with the thrower's skill level in Incendiary Device Handling — roughly 15 seconds of burn per level. The book doesn't give a full level-by-level table, just this per-level rate, so a higher-level thrower gets proportionally longer-burning splash flames from the same jug.

docs.title: The Royalty Mechanic
docs.text: Because it's the first crawler-invented stackable item of its kind, the system automatically opens an Accounts tab in Carl's inventory tracking a Creator's Fee: 1 gold coin for every kill made anywhere in the dungeon using a Jug O' Boom, payable to Carl for the rest of his natural life (and, per the fine print, into future seasons if he survives). Cashing out charges a punishing flat 2-gold-coin fee plus 25%, rounded up — meaning small balances are barely worth withdrawing. In practice, the item's core ingredient (Rev-Up moonshine) is rare enough in Book 1 that no other crawler is shown using the recipe, so the royalty stream stays negligible.

docs.title: Role in the Story
docs.text: The Jug O' Boom becomes Carl's default tool for handling group encounters throughout the back half of Book 1 — used to clear clurichaun dens, executed en masse against the second Krakaren encounter, and stockpiled into the "babies" launched from the MOAB ("Bomb Chicken") cart during the Rage Elemental chase sequence.

docs.title: Future Enhancements
docs.text:
Checked — no enhancement found (Books 2-8)

Carl continues carrying and using boom jugs at least through Book 4, and other crawlers are shown having independently reverse-engineered the recipe by Book 2 (cutting into Carl's royalty stream). No book describes the item itself being upgraded or modified. In Book 4, Carl develops a separate "burn gel" recipe as a complementary tool for a fire-resistant enemy — a related invention, not a change to the Jug O' Boom itself.

Sourced from Book 1: The Apocalypse Will Be Televised.

docs.title: The Cloak of the Benevolent Champion
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Princess Donut (chapter 3 onward)
  • Slot: Shoulder accessory — wearable alongside her crupper (waist) and ghillie suit (jacket)
  • Rarity: Celestial, unique
  • Origin: Awarded in a Celestial Quest Box on the third floor to Quan Ch; looted from his corpse by Carl in Book 6
  • Headline effect: The wearer's lowest base stat rises to match their highest, over 66 hours
  • Also: Level-5 Find Weakened; four random spells to level 15; one random skill to level 15
  • Distinction: The first Celestial item awarded during Dungeon Crawler World: Earth, destined for the museum

This is 'Quan's celestial cloak' from Book 6, finally read

Book 6 listed this only as an unidentified looted cloak whose "effects change depending on who wears it," which Carl planned to give to Donut but never finished reading before the floor ended. Book 7 chapter 3 is where the description is finally read out in full — and Carl's Book 6 guess turns out to be right for an unexpected reason. The effects do not vary by wearer type; they vary because they are indexed to the wearer's own stats and arsenal.

docs.title: Physical Description
docs.text:
Silky fabric, black on one side and blue on the other, cut something like a magician's cape but with short arms, so more robe than cape, and no vest. It glows soft white. It sizes itself to the wearer — Mordecai notes that cloak-class items fit any quadruped — though on a cat it ends up "like a shawl… ridiculously short," with a cerulean lining.

Donut refers to it as her shawl for the rest of the book, and it is the item she credits in chapter 86 for pushing her Claw skill from level 4 toward 15.

docs.title: The Description
docs.text:
The Cloak of the Benevolent Champion.

This is a unique item.

This item was originally awarded in a Celestial Quest Box during the third floor.

Man, I hate that word. "Champion." It has lost its punch over the years, don't you think? It used to mean the best of the best of the best. And now? That term is handed out like candy and venereal diseases…

Anyway, if you wear this magical, armed cloak, you are a champion. This is an early-dungeon Celestial item, and its sole purpose is to help you help your fellow crawlers survive as long as possible. Upon equipping this, you will slowly but surely rise to your full potential.

This magical cloak offers the following benefits:

Your lowest base stat will, over the course of the next 66 hours, become equal with your highest base stat at the time of first equip.

A level-five Find Weakened skill, so you'll always know who to protect first.

Four random spells from your current arsenal will increase to level 15. This benefit is immediate for one spell and will slowly occur over a period of one week for the others.

One random skill from your list will increase to level 15 over the course of the next 504 hours.

Note: these two benefits include your full spell and skill arsenal, so it's possible an item-based spell or skill will be enhanced. In most cases, you will be able to retain the spell or skill, minus the level from the item, if you remove said item. But not always…

Note: All of these benefits require you to wear this item continuously. You may unequip for short periods, but if another crawler equips this, all countdowns will immediately reset. You will not gain new benefits. In other words, no sharing! There can only be one champion.

Note: This item has the distinction of being the first Celestial Item awarded during Dungeon Crawler World: Earth and will automatically appear in the Dungeon Crawler World: Earth museum display upon completion of the crawl. Legacy stipend rules apply should you survive.

Donut's observation on the copy itself is one of the book's better small ideas: the text reads as if written for a superhero, and she wonders whether Quan — who was Vietnamese — got a different, kinder version. Carl confirms item descriptions vary by crawler; Katia's differ from his, and Li Jun's reference Chinese pop culture. Mordecai waves off the museum line: "Don't worry aboot that. It means nothing right now."

docs.title: The Charisma Trick
docs.text:
The first benefit is a one-shot snapshot: the wearer's lowest base stat rises to the highest stat as measured at the moment of first equip. Mordecai therefore refuses to let Donut put the cloak on until she has been artificially inflated.

His potion, formerly called Charisma Cheat and now system-named MySpace Photo, "trick[s] the system into thinking your Charisma is 30 points higher than it really is" — 193 instead of 163. It lasts two minutes. Donut drinks it, equips the cloak inside the window, and her Constitution therefore climbs toward 193 rather than 163.

She receives a "very rude Catfish" achievement for the trouble. She also reads the Shield spellbook immediately beforehand, deliberately widening her arsenal before the random-spell roll.

docs.title: The Four Spells
docs.text:
This is the part the party agonised over, because the roll is random and some outcomes were actively feared: Twinkle Toes at 15 "would probably just end up killing her"; an item-based Fireball at 15 "would burn the whole city down"; Laundry Day was already 15 and would waste the slot; Torch was already 14.

What actually came up:

Spell Timing Bad Attitude Immediate Wall of Fire Over the following week Heal Critter Over the following week Puddle Jumper Over the following week

Mordecai on the results: level-15 Bad Attitude "can cast it on large groups all at once"; level-15 Wall of Fire combined with her class and new bulk makes her "a terror on the battlefield"; and level-15 Puddle Jumper drops the cooldown to a minute or two and lets her jump through walls.

Donut had wanted Fireball, Why Are You Hitting Yourself? and Hole, and got none of them.

Exact-verification note

Twinkle Toes was NOT boosted by the cloak. It appears only in the pre-equip list of outcomes the party was afraid of. The four boosted spells are the ones tabled above.

docs.title: The Skill
docs.text:
Unidentifiable at equip time, and it takes 504 hours — three weeks — to complete, which is longer than the floor. Mordecai: "It'll probably be obvious in a week or so." Donut speculates hopefully about her level-6 litterbox navigation skill.

The book never conclusively names which skill won the roll. Claw is the obvious candidate — Donut credits "my lovely shawl" for taking it from 4 to nearly 15 in chapter 86 — but the text does not state outright that Claw is the cloak's randomly selected skill.

docs.title: Find Weakened
docs.text:
A level-five Find Weakened skill, so you'll always know who to protect first.

In groups of three or more like creatures, it flags which one is closest to death. Carl notes the grim inversion: it is a healer's skill, and Quan used it "for the exact opposite of its intended purpose. He'd used it to find and pick off the weakest crawlers in a group."

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text:
