The cloak itself has no level. Everything about it is a timer, and every timer is non-transferable:

Benefit Duration Restarts if another crawler equips it Lowest base stat → highest 66 hours Yes One spell → level 15 Immediate — Three more spells → level 15 ~1 week Yes One skill → level 15 504 hours Yes

Brief unequipping is permitted. Letting anyone else put it on resets everything and grants them nothing. "There can only be one champion."

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Find Weakened
  • Claw — the skill Donut credits the shawl for
  • Bad Attitude, Wall of Fire, Heal Critter, Puddle Jumper

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride (as Quan's unidentified cloak) and Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Enchanted Crown of the Sepsis Whore
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Princess Donut
  • Slot: Head
  • Rarity: Legendary, Fleeting, and Unique
  • Obtained: Donut's very first Legendary Quadruped Box (awarded for being the first cat to enter the dungeon)

docs.title: Effect
docs.text: +5 Intelligence. +5 to the "Good First Impression" skill. All of the wearer's attacks, including magic, gain a 15% chance to inflict the Sepsis debuff.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: No skill-level scaling described in Book 1 — the crown's bonuses (Intelligence, Good First Impression, the 15% Sepsis proc) are all presented as flat, one-time enchantments rather than something that grows with a skill level. The Sepsis debuff itself is shown in action (a Scatterer hit with it wanders off and eventually collapses), but no stronger/weaker variant of the debuff is ever described.

docs.title: The Catch
docs.text:
The crown is tagged Fleeting — it crumbles to dust the instant it's removed, at which point a new one is generated somewhere else in the dungeon for another crawler to find. Its bigger consequence is structural to the whole series' faction politics: putting it on permanently enrolls the wearer in the royal line of succession for the Blood Sultanate, one of the factions active on Floor 9. Removing the crown afterward does not undo this status. Members of the Blood Sultanate's royal line are required to kill the reigning Sultan and every other member of the royal family before they're permitted to descend past Floor 9.

Donut puts it on within seconds of receiving it — before Mordecai can finish reading her the warning — because it's purple, her favorite color.

docs.title: Why It Matters
docs.text: This is one of the first hard plot commitments made in the series: Donut is now locked into a Floor 9 storyline regardless of anything else that happens between now and then. Prince Maestro later confirms, mockingly, that the Blood Sultanate is a perennial underdog faction ("almost always the first of the nine to get eliminated") in the recurring "Faction Wars" — implying Carl and Donut are headed into one of the more dangerous political situations in the dungeon, sight unseen.

docs.title: Book 5: The Crown Reforms and Finds Katia
docs.text:
Book 5 confirms the crown itself regenerated somewhere in the dungeon after Donut's copy disintegrated in Book 2 (per the Legendary Boxes' single-owner mechanic) and, at some unspecified point, ended up in the possession of Eva Sigrid — carried openly on the back shoulder of her breastplate the whole time, disguised as part of the armor's own decoration, never actually worn. Carl privately reflects mid-book that Donut's succession obligation to the Blood Sultanate persists "which she didn't even have anymore," confirming this page's original note that removing the physical crown never lifted the underlying curse.

At the very end of the book, a dying Eva — killed by Katia during the Butcher's Masquerade's aftermath — pulls the hidden crown from her armor with her lower hand as a final, deliberate act of spite. Eva dies before the crown even finishes equipping, but it still finds its way onto Katia's bare head moments after — Katia's sponsor had sent her a hat that would've blocked this, but Katia had given it to Carl, leaving her own head uncovered. The crown instantly enrolls Katia in the same Blood Sultanate line of succession Donut has carried since Book 1. The text is explicit about the resulting stakes, realized by Katia herself in this same private, Katia-only closing scene: with two members of the same royal line now present, only one of Katia or Donut will be permitted to take the stairs from Floor 9 down to Floor 10. Neither Carl nor Donut learns any of this — the crown's reappearance, Eva's death, and the succession conflict it creates — before the book ends.

docs.title: Book 6: The Transfer Confirmed, and an Escape Hatch Prepared
docs.text:
Book 5's open question, answered

This page previously asked where the curse went after Book 5. Book 6 confirms it: Katia carries the Crown for the entire book, physically on her head, and tells Carl so directly mid-floor — "I have the Crown of the Sepsis Whore on my head, but there's a way out." Carl's reaction is exactly the one the Book 5 page anticipated: "How? How did she have the Crown of the Sepsis Whore on her head? The implications were staggering."

The succession problem itself is unchanged at book's end. Only one of Katia or Donut may descend from Floor 9 to Floor 10. What Book 6 adds is not a resolution but an escape route — one the party deliberately chooses not to take.

docs.title: The Orchid of Eileithyia's Grace
docs.text:
Katia's celestial prize box, earned in Book 5 for opening the Gate of the Feral Gods and flooding Larracos, turns out to be the Engaged Lock Box of the Night Wyrm, attuned to her alone. Visible inside it, behind slats she cannot open, is a pink orchid bud: The Orchid of Eileithyia's Grace.

Three seals must be broken to open the box:

Task Status Kill someone you are currently or formerly partied with ✓ Eva Sigrid (Book 5) Kill a country or level boss ✓ Queen Imogen (Book 5) Find a Guild of Suffering and complete an assassination quest ✓ Astrid killed ch. 32; quest marked "Job Complete" and the Orchid received ch. 33, after the body is delivered to the guild

Eating the orchid renders the user unconscious for one hour at 1% health with no healing possible. Survive that, and the goddess Eileithyia grants one of three permanent boons, at her discretion:

  1. Triple base Constitution — all future Constitution points count triple, all Constitution bonuses tripled. Stops working if Eileithyia dies or the user passes Floor 12
  2. Celestial Attendant — immediate transfer to Floor 12 as a temporary, non-combatant NPC until the Ascendency games begin, at which point the user may exit the dungeon or continue. Progress, sponsorships and inventory all freeze; the user leaves all parties
  3. Revert to your birth race and be made pregnant (father of the user's choosing, same race). Under this season's ruleset this disqualifies the user, exporting them to the Kinder Facility in Mumbai

Boons 2 and 3 both solve the Crown problem the same way — by removing Katia from the game entirely. Katia intends to take Celestial Attendant. Boon 1 does nothing for the succession.

docs.title: The Deal Behind It
docs.text:
Katia worshipped Eileithyia on an emergency scroll from Princess Formidable, and only then discovered the goddess was sponsored by Huanxin Jinx. Huanxin's offer was transactional: Huanxin needed Yemaya resurrected (Yemaya being Eileithyia's retainer for the Ascendency games), so Katia was to talk Carl into repairing Yemaya's shrine, and Carl was to secure Odette as the Princess Posse's Faction Wars adjutant. In exchange, Huanxin would "clear this issue with the Crown of the Sepsis Whore" and guarantee Katia a boon that let both her and Donut survive.

Carl delivered the shrine. Odette, on air, announced she would not be anyone's adjutant this season — she is entering the Ascendency as an immortal goddess herself. Huanxin honoured the deal anyway, and the third seal broke; Katia has the orchid.

docs.title: Where It Stood at the End of Book 6
docs.text:
Katia still has the Crown, and the orchid is uneaten. Carl, Donut and Bautista have all turned against the plan, precisely because Odette's entry into the Ascendency has made Huanxin's motives unreadable:

Using the flower would require all of us to trust in the word of Huanxin Jinx. She promised she would take Katia to the 12th floor and protect her. We worked so hard to make it happen, and now none of us wanted to use that path. I understood Huanxin's original motivations — one, to win the Ascendency throne, and two, to get revenge against Odette — but now that we knew Odette was actually going to be playing an immortal goddess herself, it changed everything.

Mordecai's warning is the concrete version: Celestial Attendants are high-value former crawlers surrounded by the Maestro, hostile sponsors, and the families of every hunter Carl killed — "You'd be walking into a viper den." Katia's own position is that it's "a death sentence if I don't use it." Donut's, on the last page: "Carl, I don't want Katia to eat that flower. I don't want her to go away."

The decision is explicitly deferred. Book 6 establishes the escape hatch and then leaves it unopened.

docs.title: Book 7: The Curse's Two Clauses
docs.text:
The curse turns out to have two separate clauses, resolved in two separate operations forty chapters apart — and the second is the harder of the two. The clean statement of both comes from Tempest's Floor 8 recap, before chapter 1:

"Look, the important stuff you need to remember is that on this upcoming ninth floor, neither Donut nor Katia can leave until all the Naga are dead. And even once that happens, only one of them can leave. … It's because they both put on some tiara."

docs.title: Clause One: Operation Snake Pit and the death of Princess Vinata
docs.text:
The reigning Sepsis Whore is Princess Vinata, a six-armed white naga who is, outside the dungeon, the daughter of the naga sultan, a war veteran and her father's lead advisor. In-game she play-acts a historical queen from her own people's history — the original Sepsis Whore, who poisoned almost all of her sons — and, per Carl, "she took the gig very, very seriously." Her introduction in chapter 42 is disarming: "My name is Princess Vinata. But for these games, you're welcome to call me the Whore." Her reputation is that she is "a ghost. Untouchable." The naga lose Faction Wars every season, and she has never once been killed in the game.

The curse clause does not require killing all eleven naga on the Blood Sultanate team, only the blood relatives in the line of succession. Tipid and Rosetta supply the list, and Carl's chapter-46 briefing names exactly four targets:

  1. Princess Vinata, the sultana
  2. Two female assistants titled Ikbal, both Vinata's real-life cousins
  3. The head of her castle guard, also a cousin

The other seven naga players are friends, subjects, or executives from the kingdom's tourism marketing agency — not blood, therefore not in the succession, therefore not targets. The lone surviving naga, Rishi, is explicitly exempt for the same reason.

The assassination plan is Operation: Snake Pit, named in chapter 39 and launched at the close of chapter 40. Its real purpose is not a straight fight: "We just needed the hornet's nest kicked. We needed Vinata's escape plan to get triggered on our schedule."

Vinata dies in chapter 55, and not to any of it. She has Carl pinned, slamming his head into the ground while burning alive, when a sluggalo Carl did not know was riding inside him bursts out of his back:

I was about to drop the next bomb when I felt the sluggalo burst out of my back. He—actually, a she—slipped out from under my shirt, whooped loudly, and planted a hatchet right between Vinata's eyes, killing her.

"Yeah, bitch! Right in the nugget!" the sluggalo woman shouted.

She is Kandy "Bigs" Newton, level 29, the size of a bulldog, with a hatchet growing out of the top of her head. The Sepsis Whore of the Blood Sultanate — untouchable for as many seasons as anyone can remember — is killed by a level-29 slug with a head axe, as an afterthought, in the middle of somebody else's fight.

The system messages follow immediately, in order:

System Message: The Sepsis Whore of the Blood Sultanate has fallen. Credit for the kill has been given to Kandy "Bigs" Newton of the Princess Posse.

System Message: The Blood Sultanate has been defeated.

System Message: All assets of the Blood Sultanate, as per prior arrangement, have been split evenly with the surviving blood relatives of the Sepsis Whore, Warlord Princess Donut and General Katia Grim, both of the Princess Posse. As per prior arrangement, all assets have been forfeited to the Princess Posse.

docs.title: Clause Two still stands — and it is worse than remembered
docs.text:
Killing the Whore satisfies "all the Naga must die." It does nothing at all about the second clause, and chapter 56 restates it in a form the earlier books had not made explicit:

I didn't want to think about the third option, which would mean only one of them, Donut or Katia, would be able to go down the stairs. And in fact, it was more insidious than that. Neither of them would be able to go down the stairs as long as the other was still alive. I refused to even entertain the thought.

That is the trap in its final form. It is not "one of you may pass." It is "neither of you may pass until the other is dead." Chapter 84 puts it plainly: "Donut wouldn't be able to leave until after Katia was whisked away. That was the price of the Crown of the Sepsis Whore."

docs.title: Chapter 84: Katia eats the orchid
docs.text:
With 65 minutes left before the floor collapses and the orchid taking exactly 60 to work, Carl gives the order in the middle of an evacuation:

"Eat the orchid. You have to do it now. Now, now, now!"

Katia climbs onto a table, eats it, and drops unconscious at 1% health with Waiting for the Goddess floating over her head.

System Message: The Orchid of Eileithyia has been consumed. The goddess has been summoned.

docs.title: Chapter 86: the second ambush
docs.text:
Eileithyia arrives — level 250, invulnerable, and wearing her sponsor Huanxin Jinx inside her soul armor. Katia has three boon choices in front of her and Huanxin, who controls which one the goddess grants, opens with a threat: "Choose already. Choose or I will kill the cat and Carl."

The party has spent the entire floor preparing for this exact two-minute window. The exploit, explained afterward by Baroness Victory, requires a choice-option boon and a sponsored god: "She can't move until Katia makes her choice. It's a little quirk of the system. She's not even seeing this, I don't think." For as long as Katia does not press the button, the goddess is frozen and the CEO inside her is exposed.

The kill chain, in order:

  1. Donut casts Laundry Day — level 15, enhanced to 16 — and rips Huanxin Jinx bodily out of the goddess's soul armor. Eileithyia remains standing. Huanxin hits the floor and slides to a stop inside a pre-drawn circle of words of power. No teleport was needed to place her; the spell delivered her into it.
  2. Carl explains the circle: "That was a last-minute addition. You can't teleport away while you're standing on that. Your tech shields will work, yes, but no magic will." Huanxin clicks the ring on her finger and nothing happens.
  3. Donut shreds the tech shields with Claw, a natural cat-race skill she has quietly trained from level 4 to nearly 15 on her new knee pads. Stacked with the Eileithyia proximity buff (500% female melee) and Carl's party bonus (another 500%), she crosses the circle faster than Carl can see and "the shields around Huanxin were now just simply gone." Her own assessment: "that wasn't necessary. I'm just showing off a little."
  4. The Scorpion's Bite quadruped weapon mount appears on Donut's back — a gold Apothecary benefactor box item, "non-magical bandolier accessory" — and Katia's Enchanted Repeating Crossbow of the Scavenger Mother of Mothers forms on it, unloaded.

  5. Mordecai walks in with the bolt. He is a non-combatant NPC and cannot touch her — "No, I can't. Not directly" — so he does not have to:

    "You see this?" He flicked the tip. "My brother died because of you and because of Odette and because of Chaco. But mostly because of you. Some of my mother's ashes are built into the tip of this bolt. It's a funeral rite in my culture. To make a weapon with the ashes of those you lost. My mother died before the crawl came to my world, and I'm grateful for the opportunity to allow her to avenge her son."

    He loads the bolt into the crossbow on Donut's back, says "Goodbye, Katia. Be safe, kid," and walks out of the tent.

  6. Donut, circling, delivers the line the whole ambush was staged for, and the crossbow fires between the alien's multiple sets of eyes:

    "You're strong, yes. But we are getting stronger every day. And you know what? We don't need to kill the gods and goddesses to win. No, honey..."

    The crossbow on her back fired, and the bolt slammed right between the multiple sets of eyes of the alien.

    "...We just need to kill you."

Victory's verdict: "It was all within the rules, but they won't care. Congratulations on your victory."

docs.title: Katia refuses the escape hatch and takes the exit instead
docs.text:
With Huanxin dead and the goddess free to act on her own judgment, Katia does not take Celestial Attendant — the boon the entire Book 6 arc was built around. Eileithyia offers it again directly: "If you come to assist me and Yemaya in my court, I promise you will be kept safe."

Katia asks for the pregnancy instead, and her reasoning is the point:

"The rules of this world are strange," Katia said. "If I am pregnant, I get sent somewhere else. There are no children or pregnant women allowed here in this place. At least not of my kind. But there are several children, up there," Katia said, pointing upward. "And they are mostly alone. I think they're in trouble. They all need help, and this is the only way I can get to them."

The children are real and the number is known: Zev tells Carl in chapter 73 that roughly 120,000 children — those who tried to enter the dungeon and were routed into one specific wing — are being held physically on the Earth's surface in the kinder facility, along with pregnant women. Eileithyia can sense them once Katia points, and cannot reach them: "There are so many of my daughters there, all alone and afraid. Why couldn't I sense them until now? I... I can't reach them." Donut supplies the answer — "You can't get there. But Katia can, and she can protect them for you."

Katia is not escaping the dungeon. She is redeploying.

docs.title: What she had been hiding
docs.text:
Eileithyia reverts her to human first, and what that reveals is the book's quietest gut-punch:

Her entire right arm was gone, all the way to the shoulder. Her left leg was gone. Her right leg was gone up to the knee. She was missing an ear as well.

Katia smiled sadly from the bed. "Just a few things I've lost along the way."

"I had no idea," I said.

"How could you? We've all become experts at hiding what we've really lost."

Seven floors of accumulated injuries, invisible for as long as she could shape-shift over them. Katia had built the cybernetic replacements herself, in anticipation of this moment, and left them in the crafting room; Bautista finished them and carried them in ("I got them done"), and the whole party fastens them on while the goddess waits.

Eileithyia requires a human father. She looks at Carl and rules him out — "I see who you wish for it to be, but it cannot be so" — and Katia asks Louis Santiago, who agrees after checking that he still qualifies as human.

"It is done. It will be a boy."

"Spoilers," Louis muttered.

We all backed up, and the word Ineligible appeared over Katia's head.

She waves with her new cybernetic right arm and disappears.

docs.title: Where It Stands at Book's End
docs.text:
Both clauses are discharged. The naga blood line is dead, Katia is out of the dungeon and tagged Ineligible, and Donut is free to descend without anyone having to fight anyone. There is no system message announcing it — the resolution is simply that in chapter 87 Carl and Donut walk into the stairwell together, and nobody stops them.

"I'm going to miss her," she said. "But you know what, Carl?"

"What's that?"

"They are not going to break me. No matter how hard they try."

Exact-verification notes

  • The book never prints a "succession obligation lifted" notification. Donut's freedom is established by Katia's Ineligible tag and by the unimpeded descent in chapter 87, not by an explicit clearance message.
  • Mordecai's brother is referred to only as "my brother" in Book 7. The name Uzzi does not appear anywhere in this book.
  • The prosthetics were made by Katia; Bautista finished and delivered them.

Sourced from Book 1: The Apocalypse Will Be Televised, Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade, Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride, and Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Desperado Pass (Tattoo)
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owners: Carl (a dagger design, on his neck) and Princess Donut (near her right shoulder blade)
  • Obtained: "Asshole Boxes" — a paired reward from the same neighborhood clear that yielded a Gold Asshole's Box
  • Type: Faction tattoo — branded directly onto the body, not stored in inventory

docs.title: Effect
docs.text:
Per its in-game description: "This pass allows access to the Desperado Club." A warning attached to it states that holding a Desperado Pass negates the ability to obtain a "Vanquisher Pass" — a trade-off never explained further in Book 1.

Donut is furious about receiving hers involuntarily, calling it "a disqualifying mark" and comparing it to being "defiled." Both tattoos brand themselves on regardless of consent, the same way the Goblin Pass did.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: None described — a binary faction pass, not something with levels.

docs.title: Role in the Story
docs.text: Mordecai flatly refuses to explain the Desperado Club when Carl asks directly, saying only that it's "off limits" and that Carl will "learn about the third floors soon enough" — one of several plot threads Book 1 deliberately leaves dangling.

docs.title: Future Enhancements
docs.text:
Not yet researched

Later books haven't been checked yet for whether the Desperado Club itself, or this tattoo, is explained or modified.

Sourced from Book 1: The Apocalypse Will Be Televised.

docs.title: Doctor Ratchet's Automaton Build-It Kit
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Carl
  • Obtained: A Legendary Scourge Box — awarded for killing the most hunters on Floor 6 — which contained 20,000 gold, two crafting-table upgrade coupons, and this
  • Form: A large, ridiculously heavy steampunk chest that hisses with clockwork gears
  • Contents: Parts for over fifteen automatons

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
This kit contains enough items to create over fifteen automatons! Fun for the whole family! From personal servants to flame-throwing sentinel droids, this kit has a little of everything. The only limit is your imagination. And your insurance policy.

It then lists off dozens of individual parts, several of which Carl recognises as exactly the components he'd been missing for recipes in the level-5 Automaton crafting table and instruction manual he stole from Dr. Ratchet at the Borant production facility in Book 5. His reaction is one word: "Excellent."

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: The kit itself doesn't level. What it unlocks is bounded by two other things: Carl's automaton crafting table (level 5, stolen in Book 5, upgradeable with the coupons from the same box) and the trap skill of whoever is affixing something to the finished robot. Carl's trap master skill lets him put traps on non-static items; Donut's trap skill (level 3) does not, though her Automaton Pilot skill (level 5) lets her affix a smaller set of traps to the robots' backs. The parts are finite — fifteen-plus builds — and Carl spends down to his last automaton by the end of the floor.

docs.title: Why It Matters: the Teleport-Trap Delivery System
docs.text:
This kit becomes the backbone of Carl's Part 3 tactics. The core insight is a chat message of his:

I can teleport if we use the automatons. We're doing it now. I can set the anchor on the back of the automaton and give it to someone else, and I can go wherever I want.

Teleport traps are two-part devices. Bolting the anchor half to a small, mobile, disposable spider automaton turns a static trap into a delivery vehicle, and from there into a personal fast-travel and battlefield-insertion system. Confirmed uses in Book 6:

  • Door-opening bot — a programmable automaton is sent unaccompanied down a hidden hallway inside Club Vanquisher on a sixty-second delay to dismantle Carl's wall bracers and release the vorpals, starting the Astrid assassination while he's on another floor
  • Suicide bomber — a spider automaton with a snare on its back attaches itself to the demon Minge and detonates, splashing her with blood water from the Emberus shrine
  • Carried inside Samantha — one spider, anchor-side up, is shoved into Samantha's severed limb so she can carry it somewhere Carl can't go
  • Emergency Loop-De-Loop — a red-painted automaton carrying Donut's trap, which swaps her position with anyone who touches it. Donut's trap skill of 3 means she can only target crawlers, and only non-party ones; anyone else touching it makes it misfire
  • Breaking the demon out of the boss — the last automaton in Carl's inventory carries both halves of a teleport trap, so that bumping into the Madre de Aguas triggers a teleport that goes nowhere. The snake stays put but still technically teleports, which is exactly enough to break Amayon out of the shell and force him into his true form

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: Drakea's Enchanted Kerchief of Disorder
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Carl
  • Slot: Head/face/neck (versatile — worn as a bandana around Carl's head)
  • Obtained: Boss box, awarded for killing the borough boss Ruckus
  • Namesake: Drakea, author of the Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook's 22nd edition — a bune crawler who died on (per Mordecai's uncertain memory) the 11th or 12th floor, but not before helping bankrupt the naga-controlled Sultanate via a legal settlement after one of his elaborate traps "unnaturally" backfired on him

docs.title: Effect
docs.text:
A black, white-paisley bandana that can be worn on the head, face, or limbs. It grants:

  • +5 to the Detect Traps skill
  • Access to a level-15 Tripper spell, once every five hours
  • The Remote Detonator benefit

docs.title: Tripper
docs.text:
"This spell automatically triggers all passage, motion, heat, and weight-based traps in a certain radius."

  • Target: A 10-meter-radius sphere centered on the caster's right hand, plus 10 meters per point of Intelligence
  • Duration: Instantaneous
  • Cost: No mana — it's an item-based spell tied to the kerchief; unequipping the item removes access without resetting the cooldown

Tripper sets off every qualifying trap in range at once — including any that summon or release monsters — without disarming them, making it a double-edged tool best used from a safe distance or with backup ready.

docs.title: Remote Detonator
docs.text:
"This benefit allows you to magically remote-detonate any explosive that has been designated by you."

Works in combination with a sapper's table, letting Carl trigger pre-placed bombs on demand rather than relying purely on fuses or impact detonation.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: Not otherwise detailed; Tripper's radius scales with Intelligence as noted above.

docs.title: Role in the Story
docs.text: Carl receives the kerchief as a boss-box reward for killing Ruckus and immediately ties it around his head, over Donut's fashion objections ("a cross between someone wearing a racist Halloween costume and an old dude desperately trying to be a rock star"). The Remote Detonator benefit becomes immediately useful, letting him trigger a hidden bomb hours later without needing to be physically present.

docs.title: Future Enhancements
docs.text:
Pending

Not yet confirmed how the Tripper spell or Remote Detonator benefit get used on Floor 6 or beyond.

Sourced from Book 4: The Gate of the Feral Gods.

docs.title: Enchanted Anarchist's Battle Rattle
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Carl
  • Slot: Torso (sleeveless jacket, replaces his original leather jacket)
  • Obtained: Platinum Spicy Box, awarded after the Wasteland assault

docs.title: Effect
docs.text:
A sleeveless, canvas jacket that glows faintly purple. Its core value isn't its base stats but its upgrade patch slots — it can host an unlimited number of compatible patches, making it one of the most upgradeable protection items Carl has found.

Base (unpatched) effects:

  • +1 to all base stats
  • +50% range and accuracy for all thrown explosives
  • Retains previously-granted access to the Desperado Club and the Naughty Boys Employment Agency

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: The jacket's base stat bonus increases by +1 for every compatible patch attached, doubled if the patch is specifically a "Back Patch." It ships with one starter patch already in the box (see below), and Mordecai immediately flags it as an item the party needs to actively hunt more patches for.

docs.title: Starter Patch
docs.text:
The same box includes an Upgrade Patch (Small) depicting Earth, granting:

  • +5% Strength
  • Immunity from cloud-based attacks

Patches are explicitly described as fragile: removing one destroys it, so once attached, Carl can't easily swap patches around later without losing them.

docs.title: Role in the Story
docs.text: Carl replaces his badly worn Book 1 leather jacket — burned, missing an arm, zipper broken for two floors — with the Battle Rattle at the end of the Floor 5 air-quadrant fight. Mordecai calls it a sign that "the dungeon is starting to solidify your look for you," and the jacket becomes Carl's new default torso slot for the rest of Book 4.

docs.title: Book 5: Three New Patches
docs.text:
Carl attaches three new patches to the jacket over the course of Floor 6. Katia carefully sews on the first two herself, to Donut's approval; the third goes on while Katia is away with Eva Sigrid's group, forcing Carl to sew it on himself — badly enough that Donut complains his "wide stitches" have ruined Katia's neat work on the patch beside it:

  • Small — "Twelve Flaming Arrows." Depicts the arrows the Skyfowl hero Radiant Star shot into his grandfather to end a frozen time. Grants +5% Dexterity and +5% damage to all ranged projectiles. From a Gold Ranged Weapon Box.
  • Medium — "The Bomb." Made from Spider Reaper Minion thread silk. Grants +11% Constitution, +6% damage to all explosives, +2 to Dangerous Explosives Handling, and a 15% discount from traveling Spider Reaper Minion merchants. From a Gold Spicy Box.
  • Medium — "The Midnight Epicure." A folk-tale ward symbol depicting a satanic goat, matching the tattoo already worn by Prepotente. Grants Protection against Vampirism, Protection against Lycanthropy, and +25% magical damage against all sapient undead. From a Gold Benefactor Box (the Plenty) — delivered the same day Donut independently receives an identical set of bonuses via a matching bracelet (see Enchanted Silver Bracelet of the Ab-solar), which both Carl and Mordecai read as a deliberate warning.

Each patch grants Carl's usual +1-per-patch flat stat bonus in addition to its own listed effects.

docs.title: Book 6: The Back Patch and Two More
docs.text:
Floor 8 is where the jacket's back-patch slot finally gets filled, and it more than doubles the garment's value. Two new small/medium patches and one back patch are sewn on — by Carl himself, badly, over Donut's loud running commentary on his stitching technique:

  • Small — the peace symbol. +10% Dexterity, neutral mobs less likely to fall into aggro, and +10% skill in playing the bongos. From a Gold Pacifist's Box
  • Medium — the burning book. +15% Intelligence and the Book Burner benefit — once a day, make an opponent forget a spell for 30 hours
  • Back patch — The Scavenger's Daughter. A divine, unique, fleeting patch from a Celestial Predator Box. It doubles every other patch's stat-point benefit, adds +25 Dexterity and +25 Strength on top, alerts Carl whenever a deity enters the area, and grants Climb, Soul Reaper, and the Mysterious Bone Key

Carl deliberately sews the small peace patch on first so that the back patch's doubling effect is certain to catch every regular patch.

The jacket is now expendable in exactly one way

Using the Mysterious Bone Key destroys the Scavenger's Daughter and this jacket with every patch on it. Carl designates it a last-resort item and never spends it in Book 6, but the entire Battle Rattle now sits as collateral against a single one-time escape option.

docs.title: Book 7: Never Named, But Still Working
docs.text:
Flag closed

This page previously asked what the jacket's patch count and contents looked like going into Floor 9. Two answers, and one of them is a non-answer:

  1. The jacket is never named in Book 7. A case-insensitive search of This Inevitable Ruin returns zero hits for "battle rattle" (and zero for "bone key"). It is referred to only as "your jacket" or "my jacket," and the patches only as "the patch."
  2. No total patch count is ever given. The nearest thing is Kevin the announcer counting Carl's Celestial items (the Scavenger's Daughter, the Gloom Wraith Phase potion, and the Hairbrush of the Beefmaster make three), which is a different tally entirely.

What Book 7 does give is two new patches — one installed, one refused — and a serious new liability on the back patch. Those are below.

docs.title: The two oblique references
docs.text:
Chapter 20, mid-battle, with the Scavenger's Daughter's soul charge held deliberately full:

"Carl," Donut said. "Your jacket is glowing again! Goodness, that patch is disgusting."

"I know," I said. "I need to keep it turned on for just a little longer. We need the power."

"Mordecai said not to keep it turned on for long."

"I'm fine," I said, ignoring the pang of pain that jolted across my midsection.

Chapter 57, Li Jun — who has noticed that Carl has stopped posting his loot to the group chat:

"Donut says you received over thirty loot boxes, but you've only really told us about your new brush and the potions. Donut said you got a patch, but you haven't put it on your jacket yet. You usually post all the items in the group chat."

Carl's reaction is one line: "I shrugged, suddenly uncomfortable." He is hiding the clover patch (below), and Li Jun has caught him at it.

docs.title: New — Small: the Reaper Spider Minion merchant patch (chapter 4)
docs.text:
From a Platinum "Hell in a Handbasket Box." A black-and-silver die-cut patch shaped like Shi Maria — shorter neck, shorter hair, and multiple wicker baskets lashed over her bulbous body. Donut recognises her instantly: "Hey! It's Shi Maria!"

Upgrade Patch. Small.

This upgrade patch depicts a traveling Reaper Spider Minion merchant. These guys are known for their sense of humor, and I highly recommend the first thing you do the next time you meet one is to insult them. They'll love it.

Affixing this patch to an eligible garment will imbue the following benefits:

Access to the Midnight Market. Safety or Sanity not guaranteed.

You will receive a notification if any traveling merchants are nearby.

Plus 5% to Dexterity.

Warning: Upgrade patches are fleeting items. You may remove them, but they will be destroyed in the process.

Carl installs it right away — "Like all patches, installing them increased my stats all across the board thanks to my Scavenger's Daughter patch, and I'd need to install this right away." The Midnight Market access is the part that matters; the traveling-merchant notification and the Dexterity bump are incidental.

docs.title: Refused — Small: the clover / bare-foot "Lucky Shot" patch (chapter 57)
docs.text:
From a Legendary Lucky Bitch Box, awarded for the "Liquified" achievement (blowing himself up while immortal). The artwork is a bare human foot crushing a patch of four-leaf clovers, and the description is written from the foot's point of view.

Upgrade Patch. Small.

This upgrade patch depicts a perfectly-perfect, mouthwatering human foot treading upon a patch of four-leaf clovers, creasing them as it presses down with gentle but oh-so-firm force. Despite their non-sentient nature, the clovers have a brief moment of awareness as they suffer, and it is fucking delicious.

Delicious.

Affixing this patch to an eligible garment will imbue the following benefits:

Lucky Shot. A fatal blow will be deflected into the body of a party member instead. This benefit may only be used once per floor.

Carl will not wear it, and — the more interesting decision — he will not tell anyone why:

Even with Donut's Cockroach skill, there was no way I would risk wearing this. I didn't care how valuable it was. I wouldn't wear it, and I didn't want the others to know what it did, lest they attempt to talk me into installing it.

The patch stays in his inventory for the rest of the book. He is tempted exactly once, and not by the survival value: facing a threatened smite from Emberus for killing Hellik, he wonders whether to take the smite instead, and notes that "was the 'out' that the patch gave me. I still wasn't even tempted to use it."

Exact-verification note

The description says the blow is deflected into "a party member." It does not say random. Nothing in the text specifies how the recipient is chosen.

docs.title: The back patch turns dangerous
docs.text:
The Scavenger's Daughter develops a new failure mode on Floor 9: letting its soul charge sit undischarged now inflicts Soul Poisoning, an escalating condition that culminates in Carl being knocked unconscious for 25 seconds after every use of the Daughter's Kiss. The jacket also cannot safely be unequipped while the charge is full. See that patch's page for the full mechanic.

Sourced from Book 4: The Gate of the Feral Gods, Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade, Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride, and Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Enchanted Auto Buckler of the Peach Pit
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Katia, then Carl (Book 3)
  • Slot: Wrist bracer that forms a shield on command
  • Obtained: Not described; already in Katia's possession before Book 3, transferred to Carl once her new Riot Shield makes it redundant

docs.title: Effect
docs.text: Forms a metallic buckler on command — via hotlist or by shaking the wrist. Enchanted with Shatter: any attack landing on the shield has a 1.5% chance to disarm the opponent. If a disarm triggers, there's a 90% chance the dropped weapon falls to the ground, a 5% chance it breaks outright, and a 5% chance it teleports directly into the shield-wearer's own inventory.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: No stated scaling — the 1.5% proc chance and its sub-outcome odds are flat values.

docs.title: Role in the Story
docs.text: Katia mostly used the buckler passively, to add bulk to her mass rather than for its disarm ability. She hands it off to Carl once her Book 3 fan-box shield renders it redundant (both occupy the same arm slot); Carl equips it immediately and starts experimenting with the wrist-flick activation.

docs.title: Book 6: Replaced
docs.text:
Carl never gets the Shatter proc to fire — "it supposedly disarmed opponents 1.5% of the time, but I'd never gotten it to work." At the start of Floor 8 a Legendary Scourge Box delivers a strictly better bracer for the same left-arm slot, the Enchanted Right Back Atcha Personal Shield, which catches physical attacks by Dexterity and magic bolts by Intelligence, reflects 75% of what it catches, and doubles the power of a reflected attack 25% of the time.

Mordecai's verdict is immediate: "That's much better than your existing shield, and the bracer matches your other one better." Carl pulls the Peach Pit off on the spot and adds it to the growing pile of gear being stockpiled for the Faction Wars team. See the Book 6 item catalog for the replacement's full stat line.

Sourced from Book 3: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook and Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: Enchanted Collar Charm of the Effete Bourgeoisie
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Princess Donut
  • Slot: Collar charm (replaces the Talisman of the Slate Butterfly)
  • Obtained: Awarded automatically upon conquering the Ursine settlement of Point Mongo, Floor 6

docs.title: Effect
docs.text:
Functions as the settlement-tracking counterpart to Carl's Necklace of the Haute Bourgeoisie: each conquered settlement adds a gemstone to the charm, and each gem grants its own bonus plus a gold tax stipend paid out every ten days. The charm must be worn (not merely owned) for its wearer to give orders to a settlement's guards.

Per its own description:

"The middle size of the chains of leadership, this pendant signifies you as a member of the elite. Each jewel encrusted upon this charm represents a settlement owned and controlled by the bearer... In order to upgrade this necklace, one must first conquer an Extra-Large-sized Settlement. Upgraded necklaces will also upgrade all existing gems."

Point Mongo's plain turquoise gem grants +8 Dexterity, +4 Intelligence, and the skill Snitch already at level 10 (the skill summons town guards to the wearer's location — 1 guard at skill level 5, 5 at level 10, all of them at level 15), plus a tax stipend of exactly 3,592 gold every ten days.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: Upgrading the necklace's overall tier (by conquering a larger settlement) upgrades every existing gem simultaneously, though this hasn't yet been demonstrated in the text.

docs.title: Role in the Story
docs.text:
Donut takes control of the settlement (renaming it from "Large Ursine Settlement" to "Point Mongo") by casting a spell that shoves its elderly bear mayor off the edge of town, killing him in the fall. She then switches her collar-charm slot over from the Talisman of the Slate Butterfly to make use of the newly-awarded charm, complaining loudly about the turquoise gem's color the entire time.

Sourced from Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade.

docs.title: The Enchanted Hairbrush of the Beefmaster
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Carl
  • Rarity: Celestial — his third, after the Scavenger's Daughter and the Gloom Wraith Phase potion
  • Obtained: Chapter 56, from a Celestial Who-Let-The-Gods-Out Box awarded for the attack on Club Vanquisher
  • Requirement: Male, with an average hair length of 25 centimetres or longer
  • Use: Brush for five minutes straight, once per day, on one person
  • Duration: 30 hours
  • Grants: Shining Charisma, Speedster, +25% Constitution, and a level-10 Entourage
  • It screams

The hair requirement is the joke that stopped being funny. Katia's hair-tonic mishap in chapter 5 left Carl with waist-length hair he had every intention of cutting off. This item makes cutting it a 25%-Constitution decision.

docs.title: The Description
docs.text:
The Enchanted Hairbrush of the Beefmaster.

This item may only be used on a male with an average hair length of 25 centimeters or longer.

This item may only be used on a single person, once per day.

Samson. Fabio. Michael Bolton. Jim Morrison. The entire band Stryper. Yanni.

Your history is filled with luscious men whose power resided in their lovely locks. Now, it's your turn.

If you use this magical hairbrush upon your head for five minutes straight, you will receive the following benefits for the next thirty hours:

The Shining Charisma benefit.

The Speedster benefit.

Plus 25% to your constitution.

Level 10 Entourage.

Plus your hair will be shiny and healthy, and it will goddamn glisten.

Exact-verification note

The item is usable once per day and the benefits last thirty hours. Those are two different numbers in the same block, not a single "once per 30 hours" limit.

docs.title: The Screaming
docs.text:
Donut owns an ordinary-looking magical hairbrush. This one is shining gold with a jewelled handle, and it does not brush quietly:

every time I pulled it through my hair, it screamed. It screamed like a group of women squealing and cheering at a rock concert. And when I stopped brushing my hair, the brush would shout "Encore! Encore!" for two minutes straight until the voices finally faded away.

Five minutes of continuous brushing, followed by two minutes of a phantom stadium demanding an encore, once every single day, for the rest of the floor.

docs.title: What the Benefits Are Actually Worth
docs.text:
Carl's own assessment, benefit by benefit, is refreshingly unsentimental:

Shining Charisma — gives everyone in his party an additional 20% of his Charisma. Donut's Charisma is already godlike, so she gains six points. Marginal.

Entourage at level 10 — an illusion spell that mirrors party members. Donut already has it as a bard skill. Redundant.

+25% Constitution — "huge… That alone made the brush frustratingly invaluable. It was just like with my boxers. It was now too good to give up.**" This is the one that traps him. The hair stays.

Speedster — the real prize:

The benefit was similar to Donut's Twinkle Toes spell, though instead of casting it on Mongo, it worked on myself. I could already run super-fast thanks to my strength and dexterity, but Speedster basically allowed me to move short distances very, very quickly. I wouldn't be quite like the Flash superhero, but I was still impressively quick. And while I couldn't do it long distance, I could flash across the battlefield in seconds. And best of all, I could combine it with my Gloom Wraith Phase, allowing the distance I could travel while phased to be much further.

Mordecai had never seen Speedster awarded by an item. It is normally a rare natural unlock at Dexterity 100, and even then uncommon — the crawler Osvaldo, not a member of the Princess Posse, is the only other person known to have it.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text:
The hairbrush has no level. Its granted Entourage is fixed at level 10 and the Constitution bonus is a flat percentage. The variables are entirely logistical:

  • Five uninterrupted minutes of brushing to activate, in a war
  • Once per day, for thirty hours of benefit — so the effect can be kept permanently active with six hours of overlap, provided nothing interrupts the daily ritual
  • 25 cm of hair minimum, which is now a permanent equipment constraint rather than a cosmetic choice

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Speedster — the standout benefit
  • Gloom Wraith Phase — what Speedster multiplies
  • Entourage — the redundant one

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Enchanted Night Wyrm's Ring of Divine Suffering
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Carl — looted from Frank Q's corpse; Prepotente acquires an identical second copy in Book 5
  • Slot: Ring
  • Status: Worn in earnest as of Book 5, once Floor 6's bounty-hunter war begins

docs.title: Effect
docs.text: A flat +5% bonus to all stats while worn, plus access to a Marked for Death skill: charging the ring up through kills lets its owner gain massively increased power with each subsequent kill, scaling exponentially the more it's used.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: The ring's stat bonus is flat and doesn't scale, but its Marked for Death skill compounds with use — per Mordecai, a combatant who charges one of these rings up sufficiently gains power "exponentially" per kill, which is why every historically victorious army in the Floor 9 faction wars has included a Divine Suffering ring-bearer.

docs.title: Danger and Mordecai's Warning
docs.text: Every season, several of these rings are seeded into the dungeon specifically as bait: their owners become known, hunted targets, since the ring can't otherwise be brought in from outside the game and factions competing in the Floor 9 wars are desperate to acquire one. Crawlers who equip one are typically the first to be tracked down and killed by hunters once they reach the Floor 6 hunting grounds. Mordecai reacts to Carl wearing it with unprecedented alarm — slapping him on the side of the head, an out-of-character loss of temper he immediately apologizes for (Carl privately notes his own real father used to hit him "much harder") — and threatens to keep Donut away from Carl once they reach Floor 6 if he doesn't get rid of it.

docs.title: Role in the Story
docs.text: Carl loots the ring from Frank Q's corpse and wears it on and off for a while, mostly out of stubbornness, before Mordecai's confrontation convinces him to remove it for good. He agrees to "talk about selling it on the fifth floor, before we get to the sixth," but keeps it in his inventory for the remainder of Floor 4.

docs.title: Book 4: Kept as Bait
docs.text: Carl never sells the ring on Floor 5. Amid a growing conflict with the Skull Empire (whose agents send both an Infiltrator-possessed Chris Andrews and later a summoned demon after him) and having just become the dungeon's #1-ranked crawler, Carl instead decides to lean into the target the ring paints on him. At the very end of the book, standing at the stairwell down to Floor 6's hunting grounds, he pulls the ring from inventory, holds it up, and publicly dares any Floor 6 bounty hunter to come and take it — vowing that "every single hunter who dares to set foot on the same floor as us will be dead" by the time that floor collapses. The ring itself remains unequipped and unused mechanically; its role here is purely as bait for a war Carl is deliberately starting.

docs.title: Book 5: Worn in Earnest
docs.text:
Carl finally wears the ring throughout Floor 6, using its Marked for Death skill exactly as Mordecai warned: every kill made while a target is marked grants a stacking, escalating number of free stat points, split according to the victim's own highest stat. Confirmed thresholds from the book: 1 point per kill at the ring's base level, jumping to 2 points after enough kills, then 3, then 4, then 5 points per kill by the book's end — each jump announced by the system message "Congratulations, Murderer." A separate, related mechanic (the "Guild of Suffering," unlocked by a companion tattoo the ring's use grants — see Carl) is introduced but never explored before the floor ends. Marking an NPC or elite is explicitly impossible; only crawlers, hunters, and regular mobs can be targeted.

Two major complications emerge:

  • Left to Fester. Left to Fester is inflicted on the wearer of the ring, not the marked target — it won't lift until the wearer's mark is dead. When Prepotente's own, separately-acquired copy of the ring activates involuntarily during a magical feedback loop with the vampire-hunting elite Viscount Fog, it marks Miriam Dom as Prepotente's target, saddling Prepotente himself with the debuff. Because the same magical bounce-back has also left Prepotente frozen and Fragile (one hit from death) and unable to act, Miriam — who is doomed regardless, having been caught by her elite hunter and now facing sunrise as a vampire — asks Carl to end her life so Prepotente can be freed once she's gone. Carl secretly marks her a second time with his own ring just as dawn breaks, inflicting Left to Fester on himself too. This isn't what kills her — the sunrise does that on its own, as it would to any vampire caught outdoors at daybreak — Carl marks her only so he can also collect the ring's stat-point reward for a kill that was already guaranteed, and hides the act from Donut, Miriam, and Prepotente. A system notification afterward pointedly calls this out: "Someone should probably ask Carl why he suddenly has three new points to his intelligence stat. Suspicious!"
  • Super Spreader. A separate toe ring Carl already owns — the Enchanted Toe Ring of the Leprous Bandit, looted from a Grull's-blessing quest box during Book 4 (its first ability, Sticky Feet, lets him briefly walk on ceilings) — turns out to have a second, previously unused ability during Floor 6: it can copy the Ring of Divine Suffering's active mark/debuff onto a second target simultaneously.

Prepotente, after Miriam Dom's death, retrieves his own copy of the ring from the ground and swallows it whole rather than loot it normally — its fate as of the end of Book 5 is unresolved.

docs.title: Future Enhancements
docs.text:
Pending

Not yet confirmed what happens to Prepotente's swallowed ring, or whether the Guild of Suffering tattoo perk is ever explored further.

Sourced from Book 3: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook, Book 4: The Gate of the Feral Gods, and Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade.

docs.title: Enchanted Nipple Ring of the Defiler
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Carl
  • Slot: Nipple ring — must be manually affixed the first time it is equipped
  • Appearance: A silver ring with an eyeball hanging from it
  • Obtained: A Platinum Apostate Box, from the achievement "Marked for Life" — for surviving being marked for death by the goddess Diwata and living through her actually entering the realm (a Book 5 event)
  • Restriction: "This may only be equipped on a crawler who has been Marked for Death by a god. Hey, that's you!"

docs.title: Effects
docs.text:
Instantly know the religious affiliation of all nearby mobs and crawlers.

Allows the destruction of church shrines without further ill effects from deities.

+25% damage against all clerics.

The ability to cast Black Nimbus once an hour.

Carl receives it the same evening as a stack of other divinity-flavoured loot, prompting Mordecai's flat assessment: "Lots of divinity-themed items. That's never good." He also notes with some irritation that Li Na could already do all of these things.

Donut is delighted, on the grounds that Carl had made fun of her own nipple ring first.

docs.title: Why It Matters
docs.text:
The religion-detection line is the one that actually shapes the floor. Floor 8's central hazard is the orisha shrine storyline — seven broken shrines, competing gods, and a rule that repairing the wrong one earns a smite — and Carl spends much of the early floor able to read at a glance which crawlers and mobs are on which side. The first thing it tells him is that the three crawlers he's just met (Paz, Anton, Sister Ines) include two worshippers of Ogun, which is what sends him to Mordecai for a briefing on the god in the first place.

The shrine-destruction clause is the practical counterpart: it lets Carl break shrines without repeating the Book 5 accident that got him marked by Diwata to begin with.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: No level-based scaling. All four effects are flat. The one scaling component belongs to the granted spell rather than the ring — Black Nimbus's duration is a formula of caster and target stats, and its chance of forcing a smite rises with spell level.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Black Nimbus — the granted spell
  • Enchanted Nipple Ring of the Superior Fire Demon's Hand Maiden — Donut's counterpart, received the same night

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: Enchanted Nipple Ring of the Superior Fire Demon's Hand Maiden
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Princess Donut
  • Slot: Nipple ring — must be manually affixed the first time it is equipped; quadruped and female only
  • Obtained: A Legendary Beguiler's Box, awarded for charming Ferdinand on Floor 6
  • Headline effect: All spells with a fire attack now deal (Intelligence)% more damage
  • Also grants: Removal of cursed items, immunity to natural fire and lava, resistance to fire spells, no health loss inside Sheol, and one daily cast of Bitch, What?

docs.title: Lore
docs.text: The description is a long, self-aware rant that Donut calls "the most sexist description I've ever read." Superior fire demons, per the AI, are a matriarchal hierarchy on the fifteenth level who are so dangerously unstable that the demon lords require all of them to be chaperoned by hellspawn familiars — "Sheol's version of a Xanax." The ring is one of the protective items those familiars use to survive their charges. Mordecai's advice: "Just ignore it and look at the stats."

docs.title: Effects
docs.text:
Allows the removal of cursed items.

User is impervious to natural fire.

User is impervious to lava attacks.

User is resistant to fire-based spells.

User will not lose health while inside Sheol.

All spells with a fire attack now deal (Intelligence)% more damage.

User may cast Bitch, What? Once a day.

Carl's verdict is instant: "We're putting this on you right away."

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: The damage line is the scaling: the bonus is equal to Donut's Intelligence, expressed as a percentage. There is no cap given, and Intelligence is the stat Donut stacks hardest (her Tiara of the Inebriated Dragonfly alone adds +10, the burning-book patch another +15%), so the multiplier climbs steadily across the book. The effect is visible in play — the first Wall of Fire she casts on Floor 8 "crackled bigger than ever thanks to her new nipple ring."

docs.title: Bitch, What? (Fire Berserker)
docs.text:
The once-daily granted spell is the one thing Mordecai wants to talk about before she equips it:

Bitch, What?

Type: Berserking Spell + partial invulnerability.

Target: Self only. Cost: Item based.

Duration: twenty seconds. Cooldown: Once every 30 hours.

Effect: You ever seen an angry, on-fire weasel tossed into a room full of chickens?

Mordecai has seen the state before and so has Carl — it is what a Rage Elemental is permanently in, and the system's internal name for it is Fire Berserker. He notes the AI has been renaming things far more than usual this season. His one instruction is that Donut may only cast it when she is by herself.

docs.title: Empowering Donut's Existing Fire Spells
docs.text:
This ring is what Mordecai is referring to immediately after its description is read aloud (ch. 2):

"Donut, only cast it when you're by yourself. You have three fire spells now. Fireball, Magic Missile, and Wall of Fire. All three of them are going to be much more intense. So, be very careful."

"You have three fire spells now" is inventory, not acquisition. Donut already knew all three — Fireball since Book 5 (from the Obsidian Bracelet of the Raggle Rouser), Wall of Fire since before Book 4, and Magic Missile since Book 1. The ring empowers them via the (Intelligence)% fire-damage line; it teaches nothing. The genuinely new information in the line is that Magic Missile counts as a fire spell, which had not been established before.

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: Enchanted Pauper's Ring of the Steadfast Emberus
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Carl
  • Slot: Finger
  • Made from: Carl's original Strength ring — "the first ring I'd received in the dungeon"
  • Made at: Blessed Sun Enchantments, inside Club Vanquisher, by a satyr jeweler who also worships Emberus, with high priest Pater Coal brokering
  • Cost: 1,000,000 gold — 10,000 down plus a 990,000-gold interest-free loan from the Temple of Emberus
  • Achievement: "Columbia House!"

docs.title: What It Does
docs.text:
When working properly, this ring will remove most health-seeping and disease-based debuff effects. Has a variable numbing effect on various other debuff types. This will not remove the debuff itself. Too many active debuffs of any kind may temporarily mute or overheat this ring.

Three warnings follow, and they are the actual content of the item:

Warning: This ring may only be worn by a worshipper of Emberus. This will turn into a cursed item if worn by a non-worshipper.

Warning: This ring's true nature may only be seen by a worshipper of Emberus. It is disguised as an enchanted Strength ring.

Warning: This ring has a debt attached to it. You may not sell this ring while this debt is attached. If you lose this ring, the loan payment will be accelerated. If you are expelled from the church while you are wearing this ring, the curse effect will activate.

Warning: This ring carries a curse effect. Non-worshippers who attempt to wear this ring will find themselves infected with every debuff suffered by anyone within 50 meters of this ring. That's... that's a bad one.

The jeweler's own caveat when he hands it back: "This isn't the most powerful base ring, but it will work for your slug condition, and it will help against a few other debuffs as well, but if it gets too overwhelmed, it might not work as intended."

docs.title: The Debt
docs.text:
The system's own notification is unusually blunt:

You have taken an interest-free* loan of 990,000 gold from the Temple of Emberus. You will no longer be allowed to renounce your religion while you are under debt. You may make payments directly to the Emberus shrine.

Carl asks what the asterisk means. Nobody answers. Instead the "Columbia House!" achievement fires — a long riff on twelve-albums-for-a-penny negative-option billing that closes with: "you have taken on a financial debt. You got the albums. Now you gotta pay. Or don't. Maybe there won't be any consequences. Maybe there will." He immediately regrets the whole transaction.

The binding clause is the one that matters strategically: Carl may not renounce his religion while in debt, which locks him into the Emberus storyline for the foreseeable future.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: No level scaling. The ring has a capacity rather than a level: it removes most health-seeping and disease debuffs and numbs others, but stacking too many active debuffs will "mute or overheat" it. This is shown in play — after being perforated by a porcupine deckmaster, Carl carries Woozy, Sore as Shit and Bonked simultaneously and feels the ring burn on his finger while it struggles.

docs.title: Narrative Placement
docs.text: The purchase is told out of order. Donut's prologue recap mentions "that weird ring Carl got that I think is giving him headaches" before the reader has seen it, the ring is first shown working during a chapter-42 card battle, and the shop scene itself is not dramatised until chapter 56, which opens with the header "Several Days Earlier." Donut only clocks that it isn't a Strength ring when she sees it glowing while healing him.

docs.title: Book 7: The Ring Works Hard. The Debt Is Never Mentioned.
docs.text:
Checked — and the answer is that nothing happens

This page previously asked whoever processed Book 7 to check whether the loan is repaid, called, or weaponised. It is none of those things. It is simply not addressed.

Literal, case-insensitive search results across the whole of This Inevitable Ruin:

Search term Hits 990,000 / 990000 0 interest-free / interest free 0 church loan 0 tithe 0 loan 2 — neither is Carl's (Tipid's real-life pension loan; a Donut trash-talk joke) debt 5 — none is Carl's (see below) Pater Coal 3 — all narrative, zero financial content

Pater Coal does not appear in Book 7. He is referred to three times, entirely as memory or quest-pointer: Carl recalls him being taken over by the AI (ch. 6); a situation is "just like with Pater Coal from the Emberus temple" (ch. 37); and Emberus sends a message "telling me I needed to find Pater Coal and go talk to somebody" (ch. 54), which goes nowhere within this book.

The 990,000-gold debt remains outstanding. The asterisk on "interest-free" remains unexplained. The curse clause remains armed. The renounce-your-religion lock remains in force. The flag stays open for Book 8.

Do not infer a resolution from the silence. Carl never thinks about the money, no one demands payment, and the Temple of Emberus's only Book 7 interactions with him are about worship and smiting, not accounts.

docs.title: The one mechanical acknowledgment that debt-bearing items exist
docs.text:
There is exactly one line in Book 7 that touches the category. It is in the description of Donut's Tiara of a Thousand Lights charge pillow:

Warning: Items carrying a debt cannot be absorbed into the pillow.

That is the whole of it — a fine-print exclusion in a different character's item, which happens to confirm that the dungeon tracks debt-encumbered gear as a class. This ring carries the clause the warning describes ("This ring has a debt attached to it. You may not sell this ring while this debt is attached"), and would therefore be categorically ineligible for the pillow. Nobody in the book connects the two.

docs.title: What the ring actually does on Floor 9
docs.text:
Named in full exactly once — inside the chapter 1 Soul Poisoning readout — and thereafter only as "the Emberus ring" or "my ring." It is in constant, load-bearing use, and it is visibly struggling for most of the book.

Partially blocking the new Soul Poisoning condition (ch. 1):

The effects of this condition are being partially blocked by your Pauper's ring of the Steadfast Emberus.

See The Scavenger's Daughter for that condition. "Partially" is doing real work: the poisoning still escalates through Post Coital Blues to Post Nut Clarity regardless.

Absorbing stacked debuffs, and losing:

  • Ch. 1, first onset: "My Emberus ring flashed and started to get warm."
  • Ch. 24, mid-battle with buffs and debuffs flickering on and off: "My Emberus ring burned."
  • Ch. 40: "On my finger, the Emberus ring was a little hotter than usual."
  • Ch. 54, the overload. With gods appearing all over the battlefield and the Scavenger's Daughter handing him a fresh effect from each one, the stack finally breaks it: "My finger burned. It was the Emberus ring. It was overloaded." Immediately: "I still had slugpox. I never had Imani cure it, and now that the ring wasn't working, I had a boil on my back."
  • Ch. 55, recovery: "Thankfully, the Emberus ring seemed to catch up as some of the other debuffs were contained, including the slugpox."
  • Ch. 65, cooling after holding a line: "'No need,' I said as the Emberus ring on my finger cooled. In my interface, dozens of mind-based spells crashed against me, but they didn't find purchase."

Book 6's stated capacity rule — "too many active debuffs of any kind may temporarily mute or overheat this ring" — is therefore confirmed in play, and Floor 9 is the environment that finds its ceiling. It is the difference between a working item and an item whose failure mode you have to plan around.

docs.title: Book 8: Removed, Then Renounced, Then Confessed
docs.text: At the Floor 11 arena climax, Carl springs a trap on his own god — see Emberus and Carl's own page for the confrontation itself (using Khepri as a decoy accusal, then Katia's Bolt of Ophiotaurus to strip Emberus's invulnerability). This page covers only the ring's own part in it, which the text gives in a precise, unambiguous order.

docs.title: The exact sequence
docs.text:
I reached over and pulled the Emberus ring off my finger, and I put it into my inventory. I moved into my menus, clicked over, and made my selection.

Here we go.

Uh, Carl? Are you fucking sure? Holy shit.

I clicked Yes.

Y-y-you have left your faith, and you no longer worship Emberus. You have abandoned your god. Prepare for a smite. Something tells me this is gonna be a bad one.

Both of the tattoos on the back of my hands burst into burning, searing flames. A notification appeared regarding the ring I'd just shoved into my inventory, and I waved it away.

So the order is fixed: ring off and into inventory first, then the renounce-faith menu confirmation, then the confession ("The other guy to kill your worthless smear of a son was me..."). The smite lands on the confirmation, not the confession — it burns the sun-shaped tattoos on the backs of both hands into permanent scars the system calls the Mark of the Damned (see that page; also covered on Carl's own page).

docs.title: The debt, the curse, and the asterisk: still explicitly unresolved
docs.text:
Deliberately ambiguous — do not resolve this

The text goes out of its way to raise the debt/curse question and then decline to answer it.

  • A notification about the ring fires the instant he renounces, and Carl waves it away unread. The book never shows what it said.
  • Later, in the arena dirt immediately after looting Emberus's Memorial Crystal and finding the Kyryap's tracking dart, Carl checks his own debuffs for something unrelated and finds this instead:

There was something new, but it had to do with my Emberus ring, not this, and it was something I'd have to deal with later.

That is the last word Book 8 has on the subject. What the new ring-related effect actually is, is never stated. - Book 6's warning was explicit: "If you are expelled from the church while you are wearing this ring, the curse effect will activate." Carl removed the ring before renouncing, so the letter of that clause (wearing it at the moment of expulsion) was arguably not met — but the book never says this dodge worked, never confirms the curse fired or didn't, and never revisits the 990,000-gold debt, the accelerated-payment clause for losing the ring, or what the "interest-free*" asterisk means. - Whether the debt is still owed, whether the curse is now armed against Carl's own inventory (since the ring is sitting in it, unworn, not sold, not destroyed), and what the deferred "something new" debuff turns out to be are all left open on purpose. Do not guess at any of them. This is explicit Book 9 setup, not an oversight.

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride, Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin, and Book 8: A Parade of Horribles.

docs.title: Enchanted Prison Tattoo Kit
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Carl
  • Obtained: A Gold Quest Box from the ongoing Vengeance of the Daughter storyline — the quest whose advertised reward (looting the High Elf castle) had been rendered worthless when the castle was Zerzura'd down to Floor 9
  • Type: Stick-and-poke tattoo kit
  • Contents: A long sharp needle, ink, a few sticks, and something that looks like a piece of sandpaper

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
This kit allows an artist to create a tattoo of their choosing upon the skin of a willing or unwilling target. Tattoo artistry is a skill that can imbue all sorts of magical buffs and upgrades. Or it can just make certain that your next mugshot goes viral. It all comes down to the talent of the artist.

The preamble is a bleak little riff about prison resolutions ending with "letting SkullFuck from the next cell come over and etch a poorly-drawn dragon on the side of my face." Donut is offended on a different axis entirely — "Hey, the dungeon stole my joke! I said the viral thing when you got one of your other tattoos!"

Carl has no idea what to do with it — "What the hell am I supposed to do with this?" — and puts it away.

docs.title: What It Is, In Series Terms
docs.text: This is the same class of item Edgar the shell-mage tortoise used on Tsarina Signet in Books 3–4, performing the "blood and ink" ritual that bound her fallen companions into her skin as sentient blood-and-ink elementals. The kit is not inherently sinister; the two operative clauses are "willing or unwilling target" and "it all comes down to the talent of the artist."

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: The kit has no level of its own. Its output scales entirely with the tattoo artistry skill of whoever is holding it — a talented artist can imbue magical buffs and upgrades; an untalented one produces a bad drawing. Carl has no such skill. The one person who uses it in Book 6 has a great deal of it.

docs.title: Use — Chapter 71
docs.text:
The kit's only on-page use is its worst possible one. While Shi Maria is controlling Carl's body during the Amayon climax, she rifles his inventory, finds this kit, and uses it to apply The Eye of the Bedlam Bride to his sternum — an unwilling target on both counts, since Carl is both the artist and the canvas and consents to neither.

The ink is brewed in front of him: a sliver of toraline root vegetable in a looted beaker, superheated by a forced Self-Immolation, mixed with Li Jun's eye, which Carl is made to gouge out with the kit's own stick and eat. Shi Maria's parting note as she finishes — "You will likely be doing more of this soon with the remaining ink" — suggests the kit and the leftover ink both survive into Book 7.

docs.title: Book 7: The Payoff Is a Whole System
docs.text:
Flag resolved — and it is much bigger than a payoff

This page previously noted only that the kit and Shi Maria's leftover ink "suggest" they survive into Book 7, and asked whether that goes anywhere. They do, and it does. The leftover toraline ink becomes the foundation of a full skill-and-spell-transfer mechanic developed across Floor 9 by Rosetta, Edgar, Mordecai and the crawler Milk — a system large enough that it has its own page:

→ The Toraline Ink Tattoo System

Shi Maria's line was not a throwaway. She was telling Carl what the ink was for, and he spent four chapters of Book 7 not understanding it while Rosetta — who understood immediately — was already demanding it from him.

The kit's own role in Book 7 is what it always was: it is the tool, not the magic. The magic is in the ink. In one-line summary:

  • Chapter 11. Rosetta asks for the toraline and the ink within minutes of the party's arrival on Floor 9, before she explains anything: "Give it to me, and give me the ink the spider used to make that tattoo."
  • The rule. Blood freely given lends a spell or skill temporarily. Blood taken by violence steals it permanently — which is the retroactive explanation for Carl already owning Li Jun's Walk on Air, acquired the night Shi Maria made him eat Li Jun's eye with this kit's own stick.
  • Three tattoos are inked with it: Li Na's Profane Iron onto Carl's forearm (Katia, ch. 40), Carl's Tripper onto Imani's ankle (Katia, ch. 47), and Bijanbi onto Donut's flank (Edgar, ch. 74).
  • The ink runs out. Katia's chapter-40 estimate — "We'll have just enough to do Imani's small tat next" — proves exactly right.
  • It is superseded. Edgar and Milk develop a new ink that does not need toraline at all and can extract abilities from the dead, and Milk gives Carl 825 ml of Stayfast Ink and an Adept's Fountain Pen as the replacement path, explicitly tied to The Filthy Little Crawler's Book of Voodoo.

Note that Edgar — named on this page since Book 6 as the artist who performed the "blood and ink" ritual on Tsarina Signet — turns out to be exactly the right person, and says so himself. Asked to do Donut's tattoo, he distinguishes the two crafts: Signet's work was "stabilizing and preserving a memory," while this is "something new, and I honestly don't know what will happen once it's complete."

Katia, who has never tattooed anyone in her life, does the first two because Edgar is away scouting naga territory. The system rates her chain dragon expert quality.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• The Toraline Ink Tattoo System — the full mechanic
  • The Eye of the Bedlam Bride — the kit's first output
  • Stayfast Ink and Adept's Fountain Pen — the successor

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride and Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Enchanted Repeating Crossbow of the Scavenger Mother of Mothers
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Katia — looted from Hekla's remains
  • Slot: Two-handed ranged weapon, female-only
  • Obtained: Found intact on the far side of a wall from Hekla's body after her death

docs.title: Effect
docs.text:
Per the item's own card:

"This is a repeating, ranged weapon. It has the buffet enchantment, meaning it will not run out of basic ammunition. You may load and fire additional ammunition types to use with this weapon, though any special bonuses will only apply to the stock ammunition... This item may only be wielded by a female. For every female in your party, up to thirty, this item's damage and firing speed is increased by 25 percent. Your strength+level increases base damage 1.5X more than a standard crossbow."

  • +15 Dexterity and +10 Strength while wielded
  • Casts Birth Defect on monster types that generate or birth additional monsters (relevant against the Krakaren-spawned juveniles later on Floor 4)
  • In practice, fires bolts at roughly two per second, auto-loading and auto-cocking between shots

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: The 25%-per-female party-member bonus scales linearly up to 30 women in the party. Separately, effectiveness in Katia's hands is gated by her own Crossbow skill, still only level 4 by the time she's using it against the Krakaren juveniles — enough to be useful, but not enough to reliably punch through tougher, armor-like monster hide without many repeated hits.

docs.title: Role in the Story
docs.text: The crossbow was Hekla's signature weapon throughout Books 1 and 2. Notably, Hekla herself never personally kills crawlers — Carl observes no player-killer skulls over her at all; that grim work is delegated to a lieutenant in her group, a woman marked with 13 skulls of her own. After Katia accidentally kills Hekla with a mistimed Rush attack (see Hekla) and her body is torn apart in the fight, Carl and Katia recover the crossbow intact from the far side of a wall. It becomes Katia's primary ranged weapon for the rest of the floor — mounted on a spider-leg tripod formed from her own Doppelganger mass in her "sentinel gun" combat configuration — though Carl notes it won't perform as well for Katia as it did for Hekla, since Katia lacks Hekla's stats and the female-party-bonus depends on a party composition Hekla had deliberately built around herself.

docs.title: Future Enhancements
docs.text:
Not yet checked against later books.

Sourced from Book 3: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook.

docs.title: Enchanted Shade Gnoll Riot Forces Crowd Control Shield
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Katia
  • Slot: Arm-mounted shield (requires the Rush ability to equip)
  • Obtained: Fan box, awarded shortly after Hekla's death

docs.title: Effect
docs.text:
• +5% Constitution
  • +5 to the Rooted in Place skill — makes the wearer much harder to knock over or back, though the item's own flavor text warns this isn't unambiguously good ("physics being what they are")
  • Upgrades Rush to Crowd Blast — see that page for the full effect

A tall, curved riot shield about six feet high, light enough to wield one-handed despite its size, with a small viewing window and "GET BACK" stenciled across the front in Syndicate Standard.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: Its flat Constitution bonus scales with Katia's already-massive Constitution stat. Rooted in Place is granted at a flat +5 skill level with no stated further scaling curve yet.

docs.title: Role in the Story
docs.text: The shield's requirement that the wearer already have Rush is a deliberate (and, per Katia, likely trolling) callback to the ability she used — completely by accident — to kill Hekla. It renders Katia's older Enchanted Auto Buckler of the Peach Pit redundant, since she can't equip both; she gives that item to Carl.

docs.title: Future Enhancements
docs.text:
Pending

Not yet confirmed how the Rooted in Place downside plays out in a real fight.

Sourced from Book 3: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook.

docs.title: Enchanted Shade Gnoll Riot Forces Telescoping Crowd Control Baton
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Katia
  • Slot: One-handed melee weapon
  • Obtained: Fan box, awarded alongside the matching Riot Shield

docs.title: Effect
docs.text: A telescoping baton adjustable in length from 25 centimeters to 3 meters. Automatically casts a Level-5 Cone of Knockback if swung into a group of ten or more similar mobs, on a five-minute cooldown.

docs.title: Scaling
