docs.text: The Cone of Knockback is fixed at level 5 with no stated scaling; the baton's main flexibility is its adjustable reach rather than any growth curve.

docs.title: Role in the Story
docs.text:
Paired with the Riot Shield as a matching set from the same fan box, both clearly styled after Katia's cowcatcher-and-crowd-control role during the Hekla confrontation. Gives Katia a reliable, low-cooldown crowd-clear option distinct from her once-a-day (now five-minute) Crowd Blast.

Sourced from Book 3: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook.

docs.title: Enchanted Spiked Knee Pads of the Munificent Goddess Kina
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owners: Katia (chapter 56), then Princess Donut (by chapter 86)
  • Rarity: Celestial and Divine, unique
  • Obtained: Katia's Celestial Who-Let-The-Gods-Out Box from the Club Vanquisher assault
  • Made of: The eyelashes of the sea goddess Kina
  • Grants: 25% melee damage reflect, Breathe Underwater, level-15 Swim, level-10 Iron Stomach, level-10 Eater of the Dead
  • As a divine item: Gains varying extra benefits near deities

Everyone assumed these would end up on Carl. They end up on Donut, and they are what lets her shred a CEO's tech shields in the last chapter.

docs.title: The Description
docs.text:
Note that the system's own title drops the "of":

The Enchanted Spiked Knee pads the Munificent Goddess Kina.

This is a Unique item.

This is a Divine Item.

These are knee pads. They are literally made of the eyelashes of the sea goddess Kina, who is really just a weird, horny—and when I say horny, I am using both versions of that term—sea-urchin- like, bottom feeder of a goddess who is into some really weird stuff that makes even me blush.

This item imbues the following effects:

Plus 25% Damage Reflect for melee attacks.

The Breathe Underwater benefit.

Level 15 Swim skill.

Level 10 Iron Stomach skill.

Level 10 Eater of the Dead skill.

As a divine item, These knee pads will imbue additional, varying benefits when they are in the presence of divine entities.

The reveal happens on air, in a Kevin/Baroness Victory/Drick interview, and Katia does not even have them on: "I left them in the guild… I didn't know we were getting interviewed." An image is spun in midair instead.

Drick's on-air read is that the award is a hint:

"Katia's knee pads are a bit of a waste, considering that she's planning on leaving the dungeon—one way or another—pretty soon. This was clearly awarded to her in hopes that she'll give them to Carl to replace his existing knee pads. They even look similar."

He is half right. She gives them away. She gives them to Donut.

docs.title: Iron Stomach
docs.text:
The headline skill, and it is new to the setting. Mordecai had never heard of it; Prepotente already has it.

Iron Stomach lets you eat magical items. The item is destroyed, and enough consumption permanently raises Intelligence by one point. At level 10 the ratio is one to one — one item, one point — and it becomes safe to eat cursed items with no ill effects.

Katia, who can shapeshift her mouth to any size and therefore swallow anything whole, immediately exploits this:

before she'd unequipped and given away the knee pads, [she] had managed to gain 20 levels to her intelligence by eating random, throwaway items before it became too much

Twenty Intelligence, from junk loot, in the time she had the pads on.

docs.title: Eater of the Dead
docs.text: The same mechanic applied to corpses. Bodies must exceed a mass threshold, which decreases as the skill levels. It requires considerably more consumption per stat point than Iron Stomach does, and the stat raised is random between Constitution, Strength and Dexterity.

docs.title: Divine Item Stacking
docs.text:
Baroness Victory uses the pads to explain a rule the series had not previously stated. Divine-item benefits are generally identical between crawlers, but:

  • Katia's benefits would be significantly more powerful in Kina's own presence — and likewise amplified against Kina's enemies
  • If a crawler holds two divine items, they do not stack: "The more powerful of the two benefits will occur"
  • Matched divine armour sets exist

docs.title: Katia → Donut
docs.text:
The transfer is never dramatised, but it is confirmed in chapter 86, standing in front of the goddess Eileithyia, in what is functionally a villain monologue:

"And do you see my new knee pads? Aren't they lovely? They're a celestial item I got from Katia, but they fit me. I don't really need this with you, if we're being perfectly honest. But the Eileithyia boon is a 500% bonus against enemies. And because I'm partied with Carl, his bonus gives me another 500%. I don't have the same debuff he has because I'm a girl."

The divine-proximity clause is doing exactly what the description promised, and Donut has done the arithmetic in advance. With the Eileithyia buff stacked twice — once as a female combatant, once via Carl's party bonus — she crosses the circle faster than Carl can see and strips every tech shield off Huanxin Jinx with Claw. Her own verdict: "that wasn't necessary. I'm just showing off a little."

See Crown of the Sepsis Whore for the full sequence.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: Component Level Notes Damage reflect Flat 25% Melee only Breathe Underwater Benefit No level Swim 15 Fixed by the item Iron Stomach 10 1:1 item-to-Intelligence ratio; cursed items safe Eater of the Dead 10 Random stat; mass threshold falls per level Divine proximity Varies Amplified for Kina's worshippers and against her enemies

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Claw — what Donut pairs them with
  • Crown of the Sepsis Whore — the chapter-86 ambush
  • The Scavenger's Daughter — Carl's divine item, for the proximity rules

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Enchanted Tiara of the Inebriated Dragonfly
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Princess Donut
  • Slot: Head
  • Built from: A blank silver tiara + the Flawless Jeweler's Gem (a citrine), which came from a Legendary boss box for killing Queen Imogen
  • Made at: The gnome jeweler inside the Desperado Club, for 25,000 gold
  • Effects: 50% potion cooldown reduction, +10 Intelligence, poison protection, negates the inebriation Dexterity debuff, and a level-10 Hover skill

docs.title: Construction
docs.text:
The Flawless Jeweler's Gem sat unidentified in Donut's inventory from the very start of the floor — its effects can't be read until it's actually set into something. Buying the setting takes Donut twenty minutes of agonising over blank tiaras; she only picks a plain silver one when Carl threatens to leave. She dislikes the citrine's colour right up until she reads what it does.

Crucially, they keep the Enchanted Tiara of Mana Genita rather than trading it in — Carl notes it "might end up useful one day." The dragonfly tiara replaces it as her day-to-day wear, but the Mana Genita stays in inventory, and Donut swaps tiaras situationally throughout the book (she "switches into her dragonfly tiara" specifically in order to show off Hover).

docs.title: Effects
docs.text:
50% Reduction to potion cooldown.

Plus 10 to intelligence.

Protection from poisoning (already obtained.)

Negates the dexterity debuff when inebriated.

A level 10 Hover Skill.

The lore is a children's story about a dragonfly who gets too drunk to be let back into the nest and hovers outside all night waiting for his wife to fall asleep — which is where both the hover and the inebriation clause come from.

The potion cooldown halving is the effect Carl cares about (it is what makes chain-drinking situationally viable) and the Intelligence is what feeds Donut's fire-damage nipple ring. Donut cares about none of that. She cares about Hover.

docs.title: Hover
docs.text:
Property Value Skill level 10 Uses per day 5 Duration ~90 seconds Height 2–3 feet Cooldown 5 minutes

Unlike Levitate, it is not negated by taking damage, and if activated mid-fall it sets the user gently on the ground — meaning both Carl and Donut now have fall protection. Carl describes it as "a dollar store version of what Elle had."

Donut's response — "I can fly now. Carl, I can fly! I'm like Wonder Woman!" — sets up a running problem for the rest of the book: she burns hovers on practice, on showing off to other crawlers, and on simply not walking, and Carl spends the floor telling her to stop wasting them.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text:
The tiara's own bonuses are flat. The only levelled component is the granted Hover skill, fixed at level 10 by the item; there is no indication it can be trained higher. The +10 Intelligence does scale indirectly, since Donut's fire-spell damage bonus is equal to her Intelligence as a percentage.

There is one stated cost, raised when Donut considers a different hat: wearing anything else means losing both the Hover skill and the 10 Intelligence points.

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: Enchanted Toe Ring of the Well-Balanced
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Carl
  • Slot: Left pinky toe. The description is emphatic about this
  • Obtained: Chapter 4, from Carl's post-Floor-8 unboxing
  • Grants: Three linked sub-skills — Heart Balance, Mind Balance, Physical Balance, all at level 5
  • Why it matters: Mind Balance is what has been silently stopping Shi Maria from seizing Carl's body, and it becomes the first skill in the series trained past level 15 by battlefield conditions

The AI's framing in the description is unusually direct about the ring's purpose, and it is not a compliment.

docs.title: The Description
docs.text:
Enchanted Toe Ring of the Well-Balanced.

This special, dainty, perfectly delightful toe ring (which, by the way, must be equipped on your left pinky toe. Don't test me on this) represents balance. Balance in heart, mind, and your physical core. Yeah, I know that sounds like some yoga bullshit, but this has been given to you to save your ass because you're too dumb to realize how much danger you're in.

When properly equipped, (again, left pinky) this toe ring imbues the following effects:

Heart Balance, Level 5. Allows you to store one auto-trigger potion item if health reaches a certain criteria.

Mind Balance, Level 5. Allows protection from Enslavement and Conscription.

Physical Balance, Level 5. At level five, this skill imbues both the Extra Steady Balance skill and the Walk on Air Skill (already obtained.)

"Because you're too dumb to realize how much danger you're in" is not a joke. Carl is at that moment carrying a sealed demigod in his chest who has been trying to drive his body for weeks.

docs.title: Heart Balance
docs.text:
A stored auto-potion. On equipping, Carl is prompted to select a potion and a trigger condition; he picks a gold-standard healing potion, set to fire at 2% health.

That is the whole of it — one potion, one threshold, fired automatically. It is the least discussed of the three and the only one that never surprises anyone.

docs.title: Mind Balance
docs.text:
Mind Balance, Level 5. Allows protection from Enslavement and Conscription.

Followed, immediately after equipping, by:

Mind Balance is currently triggered.

No further information. Carl does not find out what that means for another ten chapters.

See Mind Balance for the full account — the hundreds of blocked Shi Maria casts, the silent arms race, and the level-16 break. The short version:

  • It had been triggered from the moment he put the ring on, because Shi Maria never stopped trying
  • It blocks Conscript, the defining threat of Floor 9
  • It levels through use, and use is involuntary — every attempt Shi Maria makes trains it
  • The skill outgrows the ring. By chapter 14 Carl notes "now it was trained up so much, I'd still have the skill, minus five levels, even if I took the ring off. I didn't dare."
  • At level 16 it negates Bear Witness, a level-20 divine ceremony

docs.title: Physical Balance
docs.text:
Two granted abilities, and the second one detonates a Book 6 plot thread in Carl's face:

Physical Balance, Level 5. At level five, this skill imbues both the Extra Steady Balance skill and the Walk on Air Skill (already obtained.)

Extra Steady Balance is never separately described. Walk on Air is the problem:

"Already obtained?" I asked out loud. That didn't make sense. I moved into my menu. I knew what Walk on Air did, but I didn't have that skill. It was what Li Jun…

I swallowed, suddenly feeling very, very dirty.

It was what Li Jun used when he fought.

What follows is the memory of the taste of Li Jun's eye, and Shi Maria's line from Book 6 — "you may gain some of your friend's powers, too, with the blood on the needle." Carl has had Walk on Air since that night, taken from a friend by violence, and had never once checked. He messages Li Jun to apologise and gets no answer.

This is also the first hard evidence of the mechanic that the toraline ink tattoo system is built on: blood taken by force transfers abilities permanently. The party works the rule out backward from this one line of item text.

See Walk on Air for the skill itself.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text:
Sub-skill Starting level Observed progression Heart Balance 5 No change shown Mind Balance 5 → 9 (ch. 14) → 16 (ch. 65) Physical Balance 5 No change shown

Only Mind Balance is shown to level, and it does so because it is under constant involuntary attack. Once trained above the ring's own level-5 grant, the skill is partially retained even without the ring, at minus five levels.

Exact-verification note

Only three Balance sub-skills exist in Book 7 — Heart, Mind and Physical. "Extra Steady Balance" is granted by Physical Balance and is not a fourth sub-skill. No others are named.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Mind Balance — the one that matters
  • Walk on Air — "already obtained," and why
  • The Eye of the Bedlam Bride — what Mind Balance is holding shut
  • Conscript — the threat it was issued against
  • The Toraline Ink Tattoo System

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Enchanted Tooth Cap of Hi-Yo Silver
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Wearer: Rend, Carl's Tummy Acher pet
  • Type: Tooth cap, designed for mounts — similar to Mongo's fang caps
  • Obtained: Chapter 65. "Someone had donated a tooth cap"
  • Effect: Summons the pet to its owner's position across up to 5 kilometres, at great speed, through walls
  • Cooldown: Three minutes
  • Not a teleport. The pet physically travels the distance
  • Donut refuses to put one on Mongo

Exact-verification note

No system description block exists. The single narrated paragraph below is the entire description the book gives. The ability is cast by name as "Hi-Yo Silver."

docs.title: The Description
docs.text:
Someone had donated a tooth cap, similar to the ones Mongo had for his sharp teeth, but this was designed for mounts. It was called The Enchanted Tooth Cap of Hi-Yo Silver. We installed it over his single, round tooth, making the tooth gleam silver. It allowed me to summon Rend to my position. It wasn't a teleport spell, but it had about a five kilometer range. The cooldown was only three minutes. When I summoned him, he'd get inexorably pulled toward me at great speed. If there was a wall in the way, he'd—possibly—smash through the wall. The skill was somewhat dangerous which was why Donut absolutely refused to put it on Mongo. But for Rend, it would work well, especially when combined with his new Wrecking Ball special ability.

The distinction between "summon" and "teleport" is the whole item. The pet does not vanish and reappear — it is dragged bodily across up to five kilometres of terrain, and anything between the pet and the owner is a problem for that thing rather than for the pet. "Possibly smash through the wall" is the part Donut objected to.

docs.title: Why It Works on Rend and Not Mongo
docs.text:
Rend is a Tummy Acher, also called a Belly Acher or Colon Worm. The species description from chapter 5:

Tummy Achers… are named such because they were originally parasites, living in the intestinal tracts of Jotan-class Titans. They are generally good-natured, though infants can be a little... difficult to control. They are voracious eaters, and when they reach full size can swallow just about anything. They have multiple tank-based special abilities and are generally resistant to most types of damage. They can survive in almost any environment. In addition, while not necessarily known for their offensive skills, their Wrecking Ball attack is considered a terror on any battlefield.

So the cap's one genuine hazard — that the pet may be flung through solid walls to reach you — is irrelevant to a creature that is a rolling armoured tank and delighted about it. On a velociraptor it would be a way to kill the velociraptor.

docs.title: The Combination
docs.text:
The tooth cap alone is a recall tool. Paired with Wrecking Ball it becomes a weapon, because Wrecking Ball scales with mass and speed — and the cap supplies the speed for free.

Carl uses it in chapter 72, at almost point-blank range, while being blown off his feet by a gale:

"Wrecking Ball!" I wheezed as I cast Hi-Yo Silver a second time. Another gale hit me, and I spun head over heels landing on my stomach.

I watched, as if in slow motion, as Rend started rolling toward me. And as he was magically pulled in my direction, he activated the only skill he had. Wrecking Ball. The special attack increased his mass and speed, and it did exactly what the name implied. The back half of Gustavo 3, the second of Lucia Mar's two rottweilers, terror of the dungeon, exploded in a red mist as Rend rushed right up to me, stopping inches from my face.

Carl aimed a pet at himself, from behind an enemy, and let the item do the aiming. The summon is targeted at the owner, so the way to fire Rend at something is to put yourself on the far side of it.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text:
No level. Fixed values throughout:

Property Value Range ~5 kilometres Cooldown 3 minutes Target Always the owner's position Obstacles Smashed through, "possibly"

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Wrecking Ball — the combination that makes it lethal
  • Fang Caps of the Expectorating Tizheruk — Mongo's equivalent slot, and why Donut said no

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Enchanted Wrestling Belt of the Great Gorgo
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Katia
  • Slot: Waist
  • Obtained: Platinum Slam Master fan box, awarded for killing a set number of mobs using momentum-based attacks

docs.title: Effect
docs.text:
• +5% Strength
  • +5% Constitution
  • The Avalanche benefit

Avalanche: if the wearer hits a living creature with their own body while moving, the force exerted is as if they'd been hit with twice their actual mass. Requires the wearer's entire body to be in motion; the bonus does not transfer to weapons.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: The stat bonuses are flat percentages of Katia's own (very high) Constitution and Strength, so their effective value scales directly with her stat growth. The Avalanche benefit doesn't have a stated numeric scaling, but synergizes directly with her momentum-based Rush/Crowd Blast ability — a fact Carl privately notes without saying out loud, given Katia's discomfort with the skill after using it to kill Hekla.

docs.title: Role in the Story
docs.text:
Awarded via fan vote alongside the Riot Shield and Riot Baton, all three clearly a comedic-but-effective nod to Katia's train-cowcatcher moment against Hekla. Its Avalanche effect doubles down on exactly the kind of body-as-weapon combat Katia has already improvised on her own.

Sourced from Book 3: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook.

docs.title: Enriched Pet Biscuits
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • What it is: A refined, guaranteed-result subtype of the long-running Enhanced Pet Biscuit item, introduced in Book 8
  • Source: Celestial boxes — Prepotente receives three at once, each different
  • Contrast with the base item: Standard enhanced pet biscuits roll from "over a hundred different possibilities," good and bad, entirely by chance. Enriched ones name their exact result up front
  • Named subtree paths shown on-page: The Paramour, Nothing Special, Nothing Special Party Companion
  • Central to: The deliberate transformation of the farm pig Penelope into a sapient party member, and — separately, and by mistake — the transformation of the dungeon boss Scolopendra

This page covers the item and its taxonomy. Scolopendra's own transformation is covered from the boss's side on her page; this page does not repeat that narrative and instead explains the mechanic that made it possible.

docs.title: Background: the Base Item
docs.text: The plain Enhanced Pet Biscuit has been in the series since Book 1 — the item Carl force-fed Donut to make her sapient. Per Mordecai, feeding one to a pet or animal-class mob rolls from "over a hundred different possibilities," and the result can be very good (Donut, Prepotente, the demon familiar Bianca) or very bad (Miriam Dom's herd of goats, one of whom turned on and killed several others after a bad roll). It is, by design, a gamble every time.

docs.title: The Enriched Variant
docs.text:
Book 8 introduces a refined tier of the same item family: the Enriched Pet Biscuit. Where the base biscuit gambles, the enriched version names its exact outcome on the label before it's ever fed to anything:

Enriched Pet Biscuit. "The Paramour."

This is a unique item.

Okay, so we all know by now what enhanced pet biscuits do.

While extremely valuable, enhanced pet biscuits are items that leave the result up to chance, and when you feed your pet one, there's a very real risk you'll be saying goodbye to your furry friend forever. Or they'll be saying goodbye to you.

...

This is an Enriched Pet Biscuit. This leaves nothing to chance. These are highly refined pet biscuits with a known result.

Prepotente receives three enriched biscuits at once from a celestial box, each a different named result: "Nothing Special Party Companion," "Nothing Special," and "The Paramour."

docs.title: The Taxonomy
docs.text: The base biscuit's "over a hundred possibilities" sort into at least two named subtrees, both referenced by the in-game description:

docs.title: The Party Companion subtree
docs.text:
Results under this subtree keep the pet's original form (or a variant of it) and grant sapience, party membership, and the ability to level, use skills, spells, and equipment upgrades like any other crawler.

Tree path Known result Effect Path one Enhanced Growth (Donut's own result, Book 1) Sapience granted; pet keeps its original anatomy — no speech ability, no "subtree two-B" physical transformation Path one "Nothing Special Party Companion" The same base outcome as Donut's, minus the Enhanced Growth stat boost. Sapient, stays in existing form, party-eligible — but does not gain the ability to speak out loud (communicates via party chat instead) Path two Smarty-Pants (Prepotente's own result, prior book) Sapience granted plus a subtree two-B physical transformation: reshapes the creature into an oxygen-breathing, upright, 1–2.5 meter humanoid form — "basically a cat girl. A mascot. A furry depending on what their original form was." Winged creatures keep wings but lose natural flight Path two "The Paramour" Everything path two normally grants, plus a permanent, incurable* charm: the transformed creature falls hopelessly in love with whoever fed it the biscuit

Regardless of path, any Party Companion result also does the following: raises a non-sapient pet's Intelligence and Wisdom* to at least 3 (scaled to their original form), resets their level to 1, assigns dungeon-born pets a crawler number and crawler status, and — if consumed after the third floor has begun — requires the newly-sapient creature to reach a safe room and choose a class before it can do anything else.

docs.title: The Pet subtree
docs.text:
Result Effect "Nothing Special" The most basic possible result. Transforms a creature into an ordinary dungeon pet — able to gain levels, skills, spells, and equipment upgrades like Mongo or Rend — but grants no sapience whatsoever and reverts the creature to juvenile form Hellspawn Familiar (Bianca's own result, prior book) A Pet-subtree outcome distinct from "Nothing Special," details not given here

The plain "Nothing Special" biscuit was the one the party actually wanted for Scolopendra: a harmless, mindless, juvenile pet, safely carriable in inventory as a fail-safe against the Dungeon Boss's own remaining nine-tier attacks (see Scolopendra for why a caged pet, rather than a kill or an abandonment, was the plan).

docs.title: The Mix-Up
docs.text:
Book 8 feeds enriched biscuits to two creatures. Only the second is an accident, and it is worth separating them cleanly, because the wiki previously ran them together:

  1. Penelope — deliberate, and it worked exactly as labelled. Carl needed a way to make a farm pig sapient on short notice, to use as bait against Taranis and Emberus. He feeds her himself ("Penny, come here. I got a snack for you") during Floor 11's ninety-minute float-building phase, well before the arena fight and well before Eris ever scrambles anyone's inventory. Carl's own retrospective confirms both the item and the intent: "We'd fed her the enriched pet biscuit. The Nothing Special Party Companion one. This was the one that turned her into a sapient party member, but it didn't give her the ability to talk out loud." Penny becomes Crawler #12,953,454, "Penelope 3," Level 10, and communicates by party chat. Because Carl fed her, she is automatically partied with him. See Penelope for her side of it.
  2. Scolopendra — the actual mix-up. Mid-fight, Eris's chaos effect swaps every nearby crawler's inventory at random; Donut ends up holding Carl's. Working from his hotlist under fire, Carl tells her to combine "the ball in slot ten with the biscuit in slot twelve" — a banger sphere and what should have been the plain "Nothing Special" taming biscuit. Donut's hotlist has ten slots, not twenty-five; she has to search Carl's inventory blind, and grabs the wrong biscuit. The Level 500 Dungeon Boss collapses as intended, but resurfaces as a fully sapient, flirtatious ally rather than a mindless caged pet. See Scolopendra for the full scene, including her chapter-98 introduction as "Sexy Scolopendra."

The book never says which biscuit Donut actually grabbed

Donut confesses to "a really, really bad" mistake, but neither she nor the narration ever names the item. The result rules out the plain "Nothing Special" (no sapience, juvenile form) and argues strongly against the "Nothing Special Party Companion" already spent on Penny, since that result is path one — existing form retained, "the anatomy won't change at all, meaning they won't gain the ability to talk" — and Scolopendra emerges human-sized, upright, with a humanlike face, and speaking aloud. Those are subtree two-B traits, i.e. path two, and the only enriched path-two result named in the book is "The Paramour," whose signature extra is a permanent charm toward whoever fed the creature — which is exactly how she behaves toward Carl, who threw the biscuit. The text never draws that conclusion, never shows Prepotente's unique Paramour biscuit changing hands, and never says the three biscuits Prepotente received are the only ones in existence. Record this as unresolved, not as a Paramour confirmation.

The system's own reaction to the Scolopendra half of it is the closest thing to editorial comment either page gets:

New Achievement. What the actual fuck, Carl? Okay, so there are power moves. And then there's this... Reward: ... Yeah, I got nothing for this.

docs.title: What's Still Open
docs.text:
• "The Paramour" is never used on-page — explicitly. Prepotente considers using it on his ex-girlfriend, a goat named Ragazzaccia, and Donut talks him out of it entirely — see Prepotente. Its permanent-charm effect is documented from its description only. The one place it may have been used is the Scolopendra mix-up above, where the outcome matches a Paramour result but the item is never named; that remains an inference, not something the book states.
  • The full "over a hundred possibilities" list of the base (non-enriched) biscuit's outcomes is never given. Only the specific named results above are shown on-page across Books 1–8.
  • Whether more enriched biscuits exist beyond the three Prepotente received is not stated.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Scolopendra — the Dungeon Boss transformed by the mix-up
  • Penelope — the pig transformed the same way, moments earlier
  • Prepotente — holds the unused Paramour biscuit
  • Princess Donut — the original recipient of a base enhanced pet biscuit, and the one who grabs the wrong one for Scolopendra

Sourced from Book 8: A Parade of Horribles, with background from Book 1: The Apocalypse Will Be Televised.

docs.title: Enchanted Fae Scale Quadruped Crupper of the Fleet
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Princess Donut
  • Slot: Body armor (worn like a skirt over her hindquarters, with a tail slot)
  • Obtained: An "Asshole Box," the same reward that gave Donut her Desperado Pass
  • Material: Fae Steel

docs.title: Effect
docs.text: +2 Dexterity. Per its description: "Light and flexible, this scale armor is made from Fae Steel. While not as strong as Elven mail or even good Orcish steel, it's the strongest alloy that fairy folk can wear. It's not the best protection, but it'll make your ass look oh so pretty."

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: None described — a flat +2 Dexterity bonus with no level curve.

docs.title: Role in the Story
docs.text: A minor defensive upgrade received in the same batch of loot as Donut's cursed Crown of the Sepsis Whore and her Desperado Pass tattoo — notable mostly for how little it covers ("doesn't cover the tattoo, not even close").

docs.title: Future Enhancements
docs.text:
Not yet researched

Later books haven't been checked yet for whether this item gets upgraded or replaced.

Sourced from Book 1: The Apocalypse Will Be Televised.

docs.title: Enchanted Fang Caps of the Expectorating Tizheruk
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Mongo (transferred from Donut, who couldn't use them)
  • Slot: A pair of teeth (Mongo can wear up to six pairs — unique to his creature type)
  • Obtained: Platinum Quest Box, from the "Johnny Quest" + double "Hadji" achievement upgrade
  • Type: Fleeting item (disappears permanently once removed)

docs.title: Effect
docs.text:
Per the item's description, the caps "turn two of your incisors into ripping, tearing, deadly chompers." Effects:

  • +50% melee bite damage
  • 25% chance per bite to inflict a level-5 Poisoned status
  • 10% chance per bite to inflict a level-5 Paralyzed status

Once installed, Mongo's bite crackles with small bursts of electricity — startling enough that he accidentally urinated on himself the first time it happened, before realizing the sparks don't hurt him.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: The percentages and damage bonus are flat, stated values with no described level curve — the book gives no indication they improve with Mongo's own level or a skill.

docs.title: Role in the Story
docs.text: Donut receives the caps as loot but can't use them (they don't suit her fighting style), so they're transferred to Mongo instead — one of the few gear types the book notes can be swapped directly between a crawler and their bonded pet. They become a small but real combat upgrade for him, used against everything from Street Urchins to the krasue haunting Miss Quill's settlement.

docs.title: Future Enhancements
docs.text:
Not yet researched

Later books haven't been checked yet for whether this item is upgraded or replaced.

Sourced from Book 2: Carl's Doomsday Scenario.

docs.title: Enchanted Fur Brush of the Ecclesiastic
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Princess Donut
  • Type: Grooming tool (used by Carl on Donut, not worn/equipped by her directly)
  • Obtained: A boss box, late in Book 1
  • Functional analog: Works like Carl's Enchanted Pedicure Kit of the Sylph (see items catalog)

docs.title: Effect
docs.text: +2 Constitution for 30 hours, granted as long as Donut is brushed for 10 minutes every night. Even with the buff active, her Constitution only reaches 4 — reflecting how low her base Constitution is under the Enhanced Growth buff (see Princess Donut).

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: None described — a flat, time-limited buff with a fixed duration and fixed bonus, not something that scales with a skill level.

docs.title: Role in the Story
docs.text: A small but meaningful item given how fragile Donut's Constitution otherwise is — it's one of the few ways the pair have found to meaningfully improve her survivability rather than just her damage output.

Not yet researched

docs.title: The Gate of the Feral Gods
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Carl (kept rather than destroyed)
  • Tier: Celestial-equivalent artifact — appearing three floors earlier than artifacts normally do (Mordecai says they usually don't show up until Floor 8 or 9)
  • Composition: Three separate pieces — two enchanted pocket watches and a wooden winding box — that must be reunited to function
  • Origin: Built by the ancient emperor Anser's court, on Floor 5's Necropolis of Anser

docs.title: Effect
docs.text:
The gate is a portal-opening device built around the mirrored pair of watches and the winding box:

  1. Dialing a time on one watch mirrors the same time onto the second, wherever it is
  2. Placing both watches in the winding box and activating it "winds" the second watch's hands until they sync with the dialed destination time — the process can take moments or a full turn of the watch depending on distance
  3. Removing the watches opens a one-way portal to the dialed destination, lasting roughly 20 minutes or until the box and both watches are carried through it
  4. The origin side of the portal remains open afterward as a two-way gate into "the Nothing" until a creature — usually a feral god — comes through from the other side; anyone still near the open gate when this happens risks "feral madness"

Per notes recovered from the Mad Dune Mage Ghazi, the winding box itself is also a standalone conduit to the Nothing: winding it and feeding it charged energy opens a portal to the Nothing directly, without needing a destination at all — this was how Ghazi accidentally summoned the minor deity Psamathe (later hired as Samantha) instead of the god he intended.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: The gate has no combat stats — its power scales entirely with what comes through the far-side portal. Per Ghazi's notes, nearly every use-combination results in something emerging on the opening side; only one specific configuration (one watch on each side of the portal, with the winding box itself passed through) avoids releasing anything at all, at the cost of destroying the artifact.

docs.title: Role in the Story
docs.text:
The gate's three pieces are scattered between three of Floor 5's four factions: the changeling principal Henrik carries one watch, gnomish Commandant Kane the other, and the Mad Dune Mage Ghazi the winding box. Seven of the nine Floor 9 factions sue (unsuccessfully) to keep Carl from assembling it, correctly guessing what he intends to do with it.

Once complete, Carl uses the gate twice:

  • Rescue operation: Opening repeated short-range portals from stranded, doomed bubbles to Hump Town's Desperado Club, evacuating roughly 2,300 crawlers who would otherwise have died when their floor timer expired — at the cost of releasing a feral god into each abandoned bubble as the portal closes
  • The Larracos strike: Rather than release a god onto the Floor 9 battlefield as everyone expects, Carl sends changeling ally Juice Box safely through to Larracos's underground faction market while leaving the second watch behind — flooding the market with seawater, timed bombs, and sharks instead of summoning anything, crippling seven factions' ability to resupply their armies ahead of the Floor 9 wars

Mordecai repeatedly urges Carl to destroy the gate (using the "safe" configuration) rather than keep it, warning that carrying a working portal to the Nothing is an active liability. Carl refuses and keeps all three pieces in inventory as Floor 5 ends.

docs.title: Future Enhancements
docs.text:
Pending

Not yet confirmed whether Carl uses the gate again on Floor 6 or beyond, or whether the Skull Empire and the other Floor 9 factions retaliate for the Larracos strike.

Sourced from Book 4: The Gate of the Feral Gods.

docs.title: Ghillie Suit and Boonie Hat
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Princess Donut
  • Slots: Ghillie suit — jacket (magically covers her whole body despite the slot); boonie hat — head
  • Obtained: Floor 9 opening (Book 7, chapter 1), bundled in as the accessory kit for her new Deathbed Hellcat class; collected from the saferoom mailbox in chapter 2
  • Effects: Suit — Blend into the Background, Cone of Silence; Hat — Targeting, increased spell range
  • Combined effect: Worn together, all of the above benefits are further amplified

docs.title: The Class Kit
docs.text:
Donut's new class, Deathbed Hellcat — a long-range sniper/assassin class — quadruples the range of all her existing spells, raises her Dexterity, improves her instakill odds, and grants at-will invisibility. It also ships with an accessory kit: a cat-sized ghillie suit and a matching boonie hat, neither of which Donut recognises by name:

Donut: IT COMES WITH A HAT! OMG! AND SOMETHING ELSE! WHAT'S A GHILLIE SUIT?

Carl has to explain both terms to her once they're laid out on the saferoom floor: "And it's ghillie suit. Not ghoulie." and "We call those boonie hats. It's not the same thing as a bucket hat. It's what snipers wear."

docs.title: The Ghillie Suit
docs.text:
I returned my attention to the small, cat-sized ghillie suit. It came with a few interesting benefits, though she would indeed look absolutely ridiculous in it. The thing looked to be made of long, shredded bits of color-changing fabric that blended into the background. It took up a "jacket" slot on in her inventory even though it magically covered her entire body once she wore it. The suit added a skill called Blend into the Background, which I hadn't yet had the time to examine, and a Cone of Silence benefit. Combined with invisibility, it would be great.

Donut's own verdict, before she's talked into wearing it, is considerably less enthusiastic: "I am absolutely not wearing this. It's like one of Signet's tattoo people fell through a paper shredder. If I put that on, I'll look like a tassel."

docs.title: The Boonie Hat
docs.text:
The floppy hat added a Targeting skill, which allowed her to zoom in and examine mobs from afar. It was similar to the gnomish farseerer, but a lot less awkward. It also increased the range of all her spells, even more than they were already buffed.

Donut is more forgiving of the hat, mainly on aesthetic grounds: "At least the hat is nice... I'm not a huge fan of beige-colored items as a rule, but it is extra floppy, and that's always a nice bonus."

docs.title: Worn Together
docs.text:
If she wore both the suit and hat at the same time, all the benefits were buffed even further. She'd be able to snipe line-of-sight enemies from well over a mile away.

Carl's own reaction is unease rather than triumph — he immediately notes that enemy factions have access to equivalent gear.

Mordecai later confirms both items can be worn simultaneously with Donut's other accessories: the crupper (waist), the Cloak of the Benevolent Champion (shoulder), and the ghillie suit (jacket) all occupy different slots.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: No numeric level or stat values are given for either item; the effects are described only qualitatively (increased range, added skills, mutual amplification when worn as a set).

docs.title: Role in the Story
docs.text: The kit becomes a visual signature for Donut through the rest of Floor 9 — by chapter 85 she is seen atop the Nest tower "dressed in her ghillie suit," a camouflage suit undercut by the fact that her Tiara of a Thousand Lights "glowed like a lighthouse beacon" on her head, marking her position for every enemy gunner on the field. Both items vanish from her person (along with the crupper) in the Book 7 epilogue when her old gear is retired.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Tiara of a Thousand Lights — the celestial hat she wears alongside the boonie hat, to comically counterproductive effect
  • Cloak of the Benevolent Champion — worn on a separate shoulder slot at the same time
  • Blend into the Background
  • Targeting

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Goblin Pass (Tattoo)
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owners: Carl (left inner forearm) and Princess Donut
  • Obtained: A starting loot box, opened during the Floor 1 tutorial
  • Type: Faction tattoo — branded directly onto the body, not stored in inventory

docs.title: Effect
docs.text:
Removes automatic goblin hostility. Allows free passage through goblin-controlled territory. Carries a stated drawback: holding a Goblin Pass causes fairy-class creatures to deal 20% more damage against the wearer. Per its own description, "it looks kinda badass" regardless.

The tattoo brands itself onto the skin the moment the box is opened — Carl describes it burning like an actual brand, with the mark appearing both on his skin and on the exterior of his jacket.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: None described — this is a binary, always-on faction pass rather than something with levels.

docs.title: Role in the Story
docs.text: This pass is what allows Carl and Donut to walk safely into goblin territory and strike the trade deals (vehicles, supplies) that drive much of the Floor 1 goblin storyline, including the events leading to the Goblin War Chieftain fight.

docs.title: Future Enhancements
docs.text:
Not yet researched

Later books haven't been checked yet for whether this tattoo is ever modified or removed.

Sourced from Book 1: The Apocalypse Will Be Televised.

docs.title: Hell-Kissed Potion of Conscription (Level 18)
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Level: 18 — three levels above what the series had treated as the ceiling
  • Brewed by: Krakaren Prime, inside the Nothing
  • Effect: Conscripts "pretty much any non-affiliated entities, regardless of their protections, including most deities**"
  • Risk: "Using the potion is likely suicide for the caster if the level disparity is too high"
  • Restricted to: Floors 9, 12, 15, 17 and 18
  • Confirmed kills of the concept: Three gods conscripted in Book 7 — Yarilo, Harpocrates, Lucia Mar

The bottle is shaped like a demonic head with no eyes and multiple tentacles, and when Carl takes it "the eyeless face started to scream."

docs.title: The Description
docs.text:
Hell-Kissed Potion of Conscription, level 18.

This works like a regular potion of Conscription, but it has been hell-kissed. At level 18, it will work against pretty much any non-affiliated entities, regardless of their protections, including most deities. Most. It was brewed in the dark recesses of the Nothing by Krakaren Prime, who is said to yearn for domination, which was why she'd been banished there in the first place. She prepares for a war she considers inevitable. There's an irony that the in-dungeon version of Krakaren has supplied these potions to the War Mages. Then again, now that this potion has found its way to your hands, maybe it's not so ironic after all.

Conscription potions only work on the 9th, 12th, 15th, 17th, and 18th floors.

Three things in that block are worth separating out:

  1. "Most." The description deliberately declines to say the potion works on all deities, and never elaborates on which ones it would fail against.
  2. Krakaren Prime is a real, named, extant entity — banished into the Nothing for ambition, arming a rebellion from exile, and "prepar[ing] for a war she considers inevitable." The in-dungeon Krakaren the party fought on Floor 1 is a copy of her.
  3. The floor list — 9, 12, 15, 17, 18 — is a near-match for the Scolopendra levels, and confirms conscription is a designed feature of specific floors rather than an ambient rule.

Krakaren Prime surfaces again in chapter 76: the War Mages trade the Gate of the Feral Gods to a Midnight Market merchant named Paca, "an agent for Krakaren Prime, who is stuck in the Nothing. Paca has the gate in her stomach."

docs.title: The Risk
docs.text:
Baroness Victory, chapter 69, on why this is not a free win:

"They're using potions, not the spell. They'll have to be hell-kissed versions. Those will be level 18. But, it also means using the potion is likely suicide for the caster if the level disparity is too high."

Confirmed within minutes. The first war mage to conscript a god is dead before the god finishes turning around:

Samantha: A WAR MAGE JUST CAME OUT OF NOWHERE AND TOSSED A CONSCRIPTION POTION ON YARILO, AND IT WORKED! BUT THE MOMENT HE CAST THE SPELL, THE WAR MAGE GUY JUST BLEW UP!

Carl's reaction: "Holy fucking shit. The war mages were conscripting gods into their army."

docs.title: How the Party Got One
docs.text: Li Na loots the potion from the war mage who attacked Harpocrates and duplicates it using Li Jun's scroll of potion duplication. She uses the original on Harpocrates herself and gives the copy to Carl.

docs.title: The Three Uses
docs.text:
Target Chapter Caster Outcome Yarilo 69 Unnamed war mage Succeeded. The caster exploded Lucia Mar 71 Carl — smashed it against her head Succeeded. Under Orders appears over her; she is physically stopped by an invisible wall when she tries to attack him Harpocrates, level 250 72 Li Na Succeeded, and she survived. "Warlord Message: Harpocrates has been successfully conscripted. Harpocrates, level 250 is now a member of the Princess Posse."

Carl's read on the durability of the effect, immediately after taking Lucia:

There were ways to break conscription, as the war mages figured out, but it was all but impossible during the first few days. Especially with this version of the Conscription spell.

And the hard limit: "The conscription only lasts until the end of this floor."

Holding a god is not the same as controlling one. Chapter 74 shows Li Na "literally riding Harpocrates like he was a mount… the god was clearly enraged by this, but so far the conscription held," with the practical constraint that "he's harder to control when I'm not near him."

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: The potion's level is fixed at 18. What varies is the gap between the potion's level and the target's, which governs whether the caster survives the casting. No formula is given — only Victory's warning and the immediate demonstration of what happens when the gap is too wide.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Conscript — the base spell and the Faction Wars context
  • Mind Balance — the only personal protection against it
  • Enchanted Toe Ring of the Well-Balanced

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Mark of the Damned
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Bearer: Carl
  • Type: Permanent scar-tattoo, backs of both hands
  • Received: Floor 11 arena climax, the instant Carl renounces his worship of Emberus
  • In-game description: "Mark of the Damned" — and nothing else
  • Mechanical effect: None stated anywhere in Book 8

docs.title: What Happened
docs.text:
Carl already carried sun-shaped tattoos on the backs of both hands from his time as a Devotee of Emberus (Book 6). At the Floor 11 climax, he pulls off the Enchanted Pauper's Ring of the Steadfast Emberus and formally renounces his faith as part of a trap to draw Emberus into a confrontation over the death of the god's son, Geyrun (see Carl's own page for the full confrontation and confession). The smite that follows the renunciation doesn't strike him down — it burns the existing tattoos into something new:

The tattoos on the back of my hands no longer glowed. The sun shapes remained, but they now were raised, angry scars. When I examined them, they both had the same description with no further explanation. Mark of the Damned.

docs.title: What It Does
docs.text:
Nothing stated. No level, no benefit, no debuff, no further examination text. The name is the whole of it.

Open thread for Book 9

Book 8 never revisits the Mark of the Damned after this scene. There is no indication of what, if anything, it does mechanically, whether it marks Carl to other gods or NPCs, or whether it connects to the unresolved ring debt/curse question. Do not invent an effect for it. Treat it as deliberate, unresolved setup.

docs.text:

  • Emberus — the god whose smite caused this
  • Carl — the renunciation and confession in full

docs.title: Memorial Crystal: Emberus
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Owner: Carl
  • Type: Memorial crystal — see Soul Crystals & Memorial Crystals for the general mechanic
  • Formed from: The death of the god Emberus, Floor 11 arena climax
  • Looted: Moments after the kill, half-buried in the arena dirt
  • Description: "Memorial Crystal. Emberus." — nothing further given

docs.title: What It Is
docs.text: Memorial crystals form from the deaths of gods and demigods (as distinct from ordinary soul crystals, mined rather than dropped). Per the mechanic established in Book 5, a memorial crystal stores its source's god-tier spells and knowledge, extractable by charging it through continued use in combat, or worn as jewelry, or installed on a weapon or armor.

docs.title: How Carl Gets It
docs.text:
Immediately after Taranis kills his own brother Emberus at the Floor 11 arena climax — see Emberus for the kill itself, which this page does not repeat — Carl steps on something half-buried in the dirt:

As I shifted, I stepped on something in the dirt. Just sitting there half-buried was an amber-hued glowing crystal. I reached down to pick it up.

Memorial Crystal. Emberus.

I took it into my inventory.

Nothing else is examined or extracted from it on the page. Carl pockets it and moves on almost immediately — in the same breath, he discovers the Tracking Tag ("The Kyryap has claimed you") planted on his own leg, and the scene shifts before either item gets a second look.

docs.title: The Apito-Family Memorial Crystal Subplot
docs.text:
This is not the only memorial crystal connected to Carl's own family of gods. Emberus is Apito's son, which makes this the second Apito-family memorial crystal in play by the end of Book 8 — already covered in detail on the Characters pass and cross-linked here rather than repeated:

  • Prepotente holds Queen Imogen's memorial crystal — Apito's own — passed to him by Osvaldo out of exhaustion and spite rather than generosity, and central to Carl's own long-running Emberus-quest thread.
  • Osvaldo is the crossed thread underneath that handoff: two separate, non-functional memorial crystals, a stolen one and a chased one, and a standing quest asking why memorial crystals in general "aren't working right."
  • Taranis loses his own memorial crystal to an unnamed thief mid-book — a third crystal in the same family orbit, stolen rather than looted.
  • Britney Proskurina ends up holding Ysalte's memorial crystal, the one Osvaldo had been chasing all book — a fourth data point in the same subplot.

Book 8 never draws these four crystals together into a single explanation of what's wrong with the Apito pantheon's memorial crystals specifically, or why so many are changing hands at once. Treat that as ongoing Characters-pass territory rather than something to resolve here.

docs.title: Status at Book's End
docs.text: Sitting unopened and unexamined in Carl's inventory. No spells or knowledge have been extracted from it on the page. Whether Emberus's death (see Emberus's own page for the "is he actually dead" question) is even permanent enough for the crystal's contents to matter is itself an open question.

docs.text:
