The line in question is Mordecai's, in chapter 2, immediately after the AI finishes reading out the description of Donut's new Enchanted Nipple Ring of the Superior Fire Demon's Hand Maiden:

"Donut, only cast it when you're by yourself. You have three fire spells now. Fireball, Magic Missile, and Wall of Fire. All three of them are going to be much more intense. So, be very careful."

"You have three fire spells now" is a stock-take, not an acquisition. No class is involved — the item is a nipple ring from a Legendary Beguiler's Box, and the "only cast it when you're by yourself" warning refers to the ring's separate Bitch, What? berserking spell, not to any of the three fire spells. Donut already knew all three going in.

The mechanism is a single line on the ring: "All spells with a fire attack now deal (Intelligence)% more damage." Since Intelligence is Donut's headline stat, the multiplier is large and grows all book. The effect is confirmed in play the first time she uses this spell on Floor 8 — against a swarm of ghommids in Havana, her Wall of Fire "crackled bigger than ever thanks to her new nipple ring."

The one genuinely new piece of classification in Mordecai's line is that Magic Missile is a fire spell, which had not been established in any earlier book.

docs.title: Book 8: Level 16, Over Ten Thousand Kills, a Mile Long
docs.text:
Donut's Book 7 Cloak of the Benevolent Champion bonus (one Cloak-raised-to-15 spell may go to 16) goes to Puddle Jumper instead of Wall of Fire (see Puddle Jumper), but her Brain Trust natural benefit still bumps Wall of Fire's effective cast up one level on its own — from a true level 15 to an effective level 16:

Donut leaned forward and cast her level 15 Wall of Fire, which had been powered up to level 16.

Cast during the Floor 10 race against a migrating swarm of sugar hermits blocking the finish line, the wall stretches far past anything shown for the spell before:

"Whoa, shit!" I shouted as the wall appeared, running parallel with the side of the truck... The flames went straight up, easily a hundred feet into the air. The line had to be a mile long.

"I killed more than ten thousand of them!" Donut shouted. "I didn't even go up a level! This is an outrage!"

docs.title: Scaling — Book 8 Note
docs.text:
A level-16 cast (base 15 + Brain Trust's +1) produces a flame wall roughly a mile long and about a hundred feet tall, killing over ten thousand level-appropriate mobs in a single cast without granting Donut any experience for it — confirmation that her level (and the mobs' relative weakness) caps the spell's XP yield well below its raw destructive scale.

Sourced from Book 4: The Gate of the Feral Gods, Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride, and Book 8: A Parade of Horribles.

docs.title: War Crime
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Caster: Princess Donut
  • Type: Atrocity — a formal spell class (see Game Mechanics for Atrocity-class spells generally)
  • Obtained: Chapter 29, from the Legendary 1914 box awarded for killing Princess D'Nadia
  • Cost: 1 mana point
  • Cost, actually: Casting drops the caster to 1% health
  • Uses: 3 times in a lifetime, once per floor, and only on Scolopendra levels (3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18)
  • Starting level: 5, rising by 5 with each cast
  • Cannot kill. Not "usually doesn't." Cannot

War Crime combines two of the caster's own existing spells into a single effect, in a way the dungeon chooses. It is the most expensive spell in the series by every measure except mana, where it costs almost nothing — which is the joke, and the warning.

docs.title: Acquisition
docs.text:
Donut opens the 1914 box in chapter 29 and reports the contents over chat in her usual register:

Donut: DID YOU OPEN YOUR 1914 BOX YET? I GOT A SPELLBOOK CALLED WAR CRIME. I'M NOT SURE IF I SHOULD READ IT OR NOT. THE BOOK ITSELF IS BLEEDING AND CRYING AND IT'S DISGUSTING.

The same box gives Carl Run, Little Günter, Run. Both books share an unusual property noted in chapter 40: unlike every other object in the dungeon, they do not register on the map at all — "It doesn't appear as a monster or NPC on the map. It doesn't appear at all."

Carl's own reaction to the description is dread, and it is about Donut rather than about the enemy:

When I had first read it, the AI had been especially enthusiastic, which immediately set off my alarm bells. The more I thought about the spell and its implications—both direct and implied—I'd been overwhelmed with a sense of horror. Horror at how using this spell might affect Donut, especially if we used it to its full potential.

He also looks the word up, in Florin's bullet-holed 1800s dictionary: an atrocity is "an act of fiendish cruelty." His conclusion is that the real atrocity was handing the spell to Donut.

docs.title: The Description
docs.text:
War Crime.

As this spell is unable to be properly trained, it will start at level 5, and it will increase by 5 each time it is cast.

Type: Atrocity.

Target: A line-of-sight beam extending from caster's eyes that shoots in a narrow cone.

Area of effect: See description.

Cost: 1 mana point.

Duration: See description.

Cooldown: This spell can only be cast once per floor, and it can only be cast on the Scolopendra Levels, meaning levels 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, and 18. It can only be cast a total of 3 times.

This spell has been cast 0 times so far.

At level 5, the casting of War Crime requires you to choose two spells in your arsenal. It will then combine these two spells in a creative way. The spells will always do what they're supposed to do, but it may happen in a fun, exciting, and unpredictable manner. Intention matters, and for this spell, we respect that. Just know it's going to be awesome and something that most governments would consider unconscionable.

At level 10, you will be able to combine three spells. At level 15, you will combine four.

The chosen spells must be at least level 8. Their strength beyond that will not be taken into consideration. Don't worry. It'll live up to the spell's name.

I'll make sure of that.

Three notes:

One. Once you cast this, your health will be knocked down to 1%.

Two. You will lose access to the two spells for the remainder of the floor, but you will now be able to—optionally—chain those same two spells together and cast them simultaneously for the price of just one on later floors. All spells added to the mix during further castings of War Crime will be able to mix and match with one another, either all or in part.

And finally, Warning. No matter what happens to your targets physically, this spell can't kill anyone directly. No matter what happens to them, they will not die from this spell. They will want to die. They won't. Even if the chosen spells results in them being chopped into pieces, liquified, and spewed across the playing field into multiple puddles, they will not die. You should probably have a finisher on hand if that's your intention. As far as I'm concerned, I think it'll be funnier if you leave them alive. But you do you.

docs.title: The Precedent
docs.text:
The description then supplies the only other recorded use of the spell in the history of Dungeon Crawler World, and it is the passage that explains what "atrocity" means in practice. An Operatic warlord, standing on a circle of power, combined Fireball and Paralysis and hit roughly 200 mantid-team mercenaries at once.

The victims were paralyzed permanently. They were set on fire permanently. They were each blown off in an arc away from the caster where they didn't stop until they hit something. For some of those poor mercenaries, that was very, very far.

They remained there, paralyzed and on fire and undying for the remainder of the floor. The caster of the spell received an experience point update for every hour or so of their suffering.

Incidentally, the wuss of an AI in charge of that season decided to put the on-fire NPC mercenaries out of their misery once the floor finally collapsed about two weeks later.

The description closes with a coda about that caster needing an identity reset afterward and part of his essence eventually forming into the Hortense Leadership Unit — "I'd like to think that's why he has a twitch to him" — which Carl notes did not appear for anyone but himself.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text:
Cast Level Spells combined 1st 5 2 2nd 10 3 3rd 15 4

The spell cannot be trained. Level is purely a function of how many times it has been cast, and there are only three casts, ever. Component spells must be at least level 8; anything above that is ignored, so there is no benefit to feeding it a level-15 spell over a level-8 one.

The compensation for losing the two component spells for the rest of the floor is permanent: on later floors those spells can be chained and cast simultaneously for the cost of one, and every spell added by a later War Crime cast joins the same mix-and-match pool.

docs.title: The Nest Tower
docs.text:
War Crime's stated area of effect is small. What makes it a weapon of mass destruction in Book 7 is a synergy tower.

The party built the Nest intending it to be a sniper tower, to give Donut long-range targeting from height. The Tiara of a Thousand Lights made that redundant — she could already hit anything she could see — so the synergy slot was reassigned:

The Nest was instead built to have synergy with something called Atrocity-class spells.

Donut had several, including her new one. War Crime. It was the one part of today's plan I prayed we wouldn't have to use.

Carl's summary of the combination:

Donut's War Crime spell was both simple and horrific in both usage and scope. And while the area of effect was relatively low, the synergy tower's ability to upgrade Atrocity spells and allow them to be cast over a wide area made War Crime a true spell of mass destruction.

docs.title: The One Cast — Chapter 76
docs.text:
Components: Bijanbi + Astral Paw.

The choice of Bijanbi is why Donut gets a tattoo at all. The plan needs a mass-drag spell at level 8 or better and she does not own one; Rosetta's team extracts Bijanbi from a fallen cleric of Wepwawet and Edgar inks it onto Donut's right flank, after which Milk boosts it from level 2 to 15 with Words of Power calligraphy. See The Toraline Ink Tattoo System.

Rosetta's design intent, laid out in chapter 74, includes the finisher the spell's no-kill clause demands:

"With them both amplified by War Crime, it should separate the enemies all out and drop them into a ring of fire. Fleshers are fire resistant, but symbiotes aren't, so if any enemies resist, they should be pounced upon by the fleshers, turned to symbiotes, and then killed. That's the finisher since War Crime keeps them alive. It'll kill the enemy and any potential baby war mages."

The cast itself:

"Casting now!" Donut shouted.

System Message: Warlord Princess Donut has committed a third Atrocity.

System Message: Warlord Princess Donut has received a new class.

System Message: Warlord Princess Donut will now be referred to as The Oak Fell.

System Message: The Oak Fell has been named Champion of Nekhebit.

The effect: the world freezes, "Break Stuff" plays, and thousands of frozen elves, gnolls and Reaver cyborgs — plus the feral god Meatus — float upward beneath "the massive, glowing outline of a cat's paw," covered in fleshers and dissolving. Donut's health drops to 1% and Carl heals her with a scroll.

The finisher does not go to plan. Li Na builds a lattice of chains and messages "Donut, this is all I can build. Do it." Donut has to close the paw herself:

"It's the finisher... I shouldn't have picked Astral Paw. I have to do it myself." … "I can feel them, Carl. I can feel them under my paw."

She closed her eyes, and she swiped downward with three quick baps.

Carl's dread in chapter 74 — horror at what the spell might do to Donut — is the part that lands. Elle's verdict afterward is the counterweight: "You are a goddamn hero."

docs.title: Aftermath
docs.text:
• Red ash rains over Shanty Town for some time afterward (ch. 78)
  • Warlord Fang survives, because he is biological material inside a robot (ch. 81)
  • King Rust's harem women were pulled into the ball but "not captured as enemies by Donut's War Crime spell" (ch. 82)
  • Casting three Atrocities in one floor triggers Donut's new Oak Fell class, which Mordecai and Rosetta both say they have never seen awarded that way

Exact-verification note

The system message says "a third Atrocity" — War Crime is Donut's third atrocity cast of the floor, after Rolling Battle Formation and You're Not Done Yet. It is the first and only cast of War Crime itself. Two of its three lifetime charges remain.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• You're Not Done Yet and Rolling Battle Formation — Donut's other two Atrocity spells
  • Bijanbi — the tattooed component spell
  • Tiara of a Thousand Lights — freed the Nest's synergy slot
  • Run, Little Günter, Run — Carl's book from the same box

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Why Are You Hitting Yourself?
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Caster: Princess Donut
  • Obtained: Granted automatically with her Floor 8 Character Actor class, Master Telephone Psychic
  • Type: Offensive charm / self-harm compulsion
  • Effect: Makes the target attack itself
  • Debuff icon: A head with little wavy lines over it

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Donut picks Master Telephone Psychic over Mordecai's other suggestion (Agony Urchin) on the grounds that the urchin class "changes the way I look, and I will never pick a class that changes the way I look." Mordecai sells the psychic option on two points: it improves her mapping, and it gives her "some offensive charm spells." Donut's own summary of the haul, shouted in chat: "I GOT A SPELL CALLED BRAIN FREEZE AND ONE CALLED BAD ATTITUDE AND ANOTHER CALLED WHY ARE YOU HITTING YOURSELF? THAT ONE IS GREAT! IT MAKES PEOPLE STAB THEMSELVES IN THE FACE!"

It does roughly what the name promises. The target howls, spins, and starts savagely biting or punching itself while its own health drains — no damage contribution required from the party. The first test subject, a beret-wearing "legendary creature" mob on the Havana streets, collapses on its side while Carl watches and thinks: Donut did that, and she barely had to lift a paw.

docs.title: Training on Spiders
docs.text: The spell gets an unusually large amount of practice because of an unrelated quest. Huanxin Jinx's spider-hunting quest makes every tiny spider mob in the region visible on the party's map, and only requires five kills a day between Carl and Donut. Donut kills them by the dozens anyway, specifically because casting Why Are You Hitting Yourself? on a spider and watching it spin in circles trying to bite itself delights her. Carl's assessment: "It was kind of fucked up, but it was also training the spell."

docs.title: Notable Uses
docs.text:
• Benchmark for how bad things are — when the boss Shi Maria turns half a group of reindeer puppets on each other with no warning, Carl's frame of reference is that they look "like [they'd] been hit by that enraged debuff and Donut's Why Are You Hitting Yourself spell at the same time"
  • Amayon, prince of Sheol (ch. 70) — the spell's high-water mark. It lands on a level-250 demon prince in his true, full-power form, and it works: mid-sentence, Amayon balls his fist and punches himself in the face hard enough to shake the world. It holds long enough for Carl to finish an entire negotiation while dangling in the demon's hand, and its expiry is announced as its own beat — "The Why are you Hitting Yourself? spell timed out" — after which the demon sighs with relief and immediately resumes trying to kill him

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text:
No numeric formula appears. Duration is clearly finite and is treated as a countdown Carl has to talk fast inside of. The Amayon cast is the important datapoint: the spell landed on a target roughly 190 levels above the caster, which is far outside what any of Donut's other charm effects manage in this book.

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: Wisp Armor
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Tome owner: Carl — unread by Book 1's end, but read and cast by Carl himself in Book 2
  • Obtained: Bronze Boss Box
  • Mana cost: 5
  • Target: Self only

docs.title: Effect
docs.text: Per its in-game description: "Surrounds your body with tendrils of light. While ineffective against physical attacks, this spell negates 75% of incoming damage from magic-based attacks. Provides temporary immunity to mind-control effects." Base duration is 5 minutes + 1 minute per spell level, with a 5-minute cooldown. It also has a cosmetic effect — described as making the caster look "wispy and ethereal and druid-like."

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text:
The tome's own text gives one explicit formula and one vague promise:

Duration: 5 minutes + 1 minute per level of spell. Requires 5 minute cooldown. ... Higher skill levels increase both effectiveness and duration.

The duration formula lets on-page durations be read as a level indicator. Three are confirmed across the series:

Confirmed on-page duration Book / ch. Implied level (5 min + 1 min/level) 6 minutes Book 2, ch. 11 (first self-cast) Level 1 — implied by the stated formula, not stated outright 7 minutes Book 4, ch. 27 Level 2 — implied by the stated formula 10 minutes Book 5, ch. 25 Level 5 — implied by the stated formula

These three are the only duration data points the text gives, and they're consistent with (and only interpretable through) the level-1/2/5 formula — Carl's actual spell level is never stated in narration at any of these points. The "effectiveness" side of the promise (the 75% magic-damage reduction) is never revised with a new percentage anywhere in the series — Book 3 (ch. 24) shows the shield absorbing "almost a quarter" of a magic missile's damage in one hit without a percentage attached, and no later book gives a number either. So: duration scaling is confirmed via formula + three data points; effectiveness scaling is confirmed to exist in principle but never quantified past the base 75%.

docs.title: Role in the Story
docs.text: In Book 1, Carl can't afford to cast it himself (his mana pool is only 3 against the tome's 5-mana cost), so he considers handing it to Donut instead — it remains unread/untaught by the end of Book 1.

docs.title: Book 2: Carl Reads It Himself
docs.text: Cornered during the Grimaldi/circus quest and out of better options, Carl reads the tome and casts it on himself before deliberately eating a parasitic worm infestation offered by the elite Apollon the Mighty. The spell's mind-control immunity is what lets him keep his own free will for several minutes while infested — long enough to reason with the possessed Grimaldi and talk him down — before the infestation is cured with an antidote potion.

docs.title: Later Use — Books 3 Through 7
docs.text:
Wisp Armor stays in Carl's regular rotation for the rest of the series with no further upgrades, replacements, or new effects shown on-page — only the duration increases charted in Scaling above. It remains his go-to answer to charm/mind-control effects (it fails against Li Na's charisma-based charm in Book 6, since that isn't technically mind control) and his default reflex whenever incoming fire turns magical, right through the Book 7 psionic bombardment where Imani and Prepotente both tell him to cast it.

Sourced from Book 1: The Apocalypse Will Be Televised, Book 2: Carl's Doomsday Scenario, Book 3: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook, Book 4: The Gate of the Feral Gods, Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade, Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride, and Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Word Weaver
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Caster: Sister Ines Quiteria — "The Reaper of Havana," a Cat Girl Poet Laureate, crawler #8,199,462
  • Type: Charm, delivered as a recited poem
  • Level: Raised to 15 with help from her sponsor and patron, the Nebulars
  • Signature use: Charming the level-125 city boss Madre de Aguas — and, through it, every creature in the region

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Word Weaver is the core of Sister Ines's whole build. She explains the chain of choices herself: Cat Girl "was the only race that gave me a charisma boost for my Word Weaver spell, amongst others, and our game guide insisted it would allow me to choose the Poet Laureate class, which it did."

The spell is cast as a spoken poem and is sustained by continuing to recite it, which is how she spends most of her on-screen time in the back half of the book: perched on the head of an enormous sea snake, reciting, while the world burns around her.

docs.title: The Madre de Aguas Charm
docs.text:
The full sequence is laid out in a Kevin-and-Magnificent-Troy broadcast recap in chapter 55:

"During the battles between the crabs and seals, crawler Sister Ines Quiteria used her level-15 Book of Rhymes bard skill, which she just got from her patron, to enhance her Word Weaver spell to charm this creature, a level-125 city boss. This boss, in turn, has the power to control all creatures from the area."

That is the leverage: she does not charm an army, she charms the one thing that already commands the army. Troy's assessment — "Charming that boss actually sounds like it was a smart move on the nun's part" — is correct, and it makes Ines, for a stretch of the book, arguably the single most powerful crawler on the floor.

docs.title: Level 15: Controlling the Zombies Too
docs.text:
When Carl's zombie-turkey accident seeds a contagious undead outbreak into the global ocean, the mass zombification starts to disrupt Ines's charm poem. Level 15 is what saves it:

"...since her sponsor and patron, the Nebulars, helped her raise that Word Weaver spell to level 15, she was able to fully control both the boss and the spells the boss could cast, meaning she could control the zombies, too. That spell is so powerful, in fact, even the fish started to pull themselves out of the ocean to get closer."

Troy's verdict: "That's a level of charm Princess Donut could only dream of!" Donut objects.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text:
The only stated breakpoint is the one that matters:

Level Behaviour Below 15 Charms the target creature 15 (boosted by Book of Rhymes) Charms the target and grants control of the spells that target can cast — which, against a boss whose power is controlling every creature in a region, cascades into control of the entire region, zombies included

docs.title: The Limit
docs.text:
What Word Weaver cannot hold is a demon. The zombie outbreak (plus an AI ruling that crab sperm counts as a mob) triggers the earliest demon eviction in the history of the crawl. When the demon prince Amayon is squeezed into the Madre de Aguas's body, Ines's charm technically still holds the shell — but as Kevin puts it, "as powerful as that spell is, Faction Wars fans all know how difficult it is to control an evicted demon." Her grip visibly degrades over the following chapters until she is destroyed by it.

Sourced from Book 6: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride.

docs.title: You're Not Done Yet
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Caster: Princess Donut
  • Type: Atrocity
  • Obtained: Chapter 3, from a Legendary Quest box for the "Hell Comes to Crawler Town" quest
  • Effect: Rips the skin off nearby corpses, creating autonomous fleshers that hunt and attack anyone marked as an enemy
  • In-universe significance: This spell is the stated origin of war mages as a creature type

Mordecai's one-line summary is the closest thing to a definition the book gives: "It's similar to Donut's Second Chance, but it's a lot more insidious."

Exact-verification note

No system description block for this spell exists in Book 7. Everything below is drawn from narration, Mordecai's explanation, the AI's war-mage trivia interstitial, and the cast itself.

docs.title: The Book
docs.text:
The tome arrives in the same chapter-3 unboxing as everything else Donut gets for Floor 9, alongside a cat-sized kilt, and it is the only item in the sequence that frightens Mordecai:

The book was a black-hued tome that clanked heavily to the table. It looked as if it had been burned. Purple wisps of smoke rose off it.

"My word," Donut said, crinkling her face. "It smells just awful. Like whenever you tried to burn your microwave popcorn on purpose, Carl."

"Fuuuck," Mordecai whispered, voice filled with awe. He took a step back, as if he was afraid of the book itself.

"What is it?" I asked. Little black tendrils, like roots, started to spread out from the book, moving across the table.

"It's similar to Donut's Second Chance, but it's a lot more insidious." He gave a shiver. "It's called You're Not Done Yet."

Carl half-recognises the name and cannot place it. The book "let out a little screech" as it disappears into Donut's inventory.

It is one of four spellbooks Donut picks up in chapter 3, the other three being the far more mundane Flak, Shield and Sentry.

docs.title: What a Flesher Is
docs.text:
The spell's output is a level-1 mob called a Flesher. The AI's chapter-61 trivia interstitial is the only full account of what they are and what they become, and it is also the passage that makes this spell historically important:

Want to know some interesting trivia about war mages? These guys have been around since the very early days of Dungeon Crawler World, but they are one of the few, true dungeon-born entities. They weren't dreamed up by a sweaty, caffeine-addled writer, nor were they developed by one of my kind. They just sort of happened, a result of too many combatants having access to You're Not Done Yet.

The final form a war mage takes is entirely dependent on the combination of its first two forms… The skin of a corpse is ripped off of a body and turned to a creature named a flesher. The flesher then consumes a living being, melting the original skin off and re-sleeving the creature. The flesher casts Boned, reanimating the skeleton, and the two become a symbiote.

Symbiotes are extremely attractive targets to other fleshers. And because young symbiotes are slow and awkward, they are oftentimes quickly re-sleeved by fresh fleshers. Each iteration results in a more powerful being.

It's rare for a symbiote to be resleeved at least a dozen times, but when it happens, the magic itself can become sapient. When this happens, the flesh finally fuses to the reanimated skeleton, turning the three creatures—the skeleton, the flesher, and the sapient well of magic—into a single being. A war mage.

This process usually takes at least 12 iterations, but there's no hard rule about it. Sometimes it takes up to 15 or 16 iterations. It depends on the latent magic in the skin of the fleshers.

So the spell does not summon war mages. It creates the raw material from which war mages accidentally accrete, over enough iterations, and the entire war mage faction on Floor 9 exists because enough people cast this spell enough times across enough seasons. Fleshers and war mages are covered in more detail on the Mobs pages.

Fleshers are fire resistant; symbiotes are not, which is the basis of the finisher used later with War Crime.

docs.title: Use — Chapters 65 to 69
docs.text:
The party plans around it for several chapters before casting. Every guild donates graveyard corpses to Bodi and the 103rd; the bodies are hauled out and dumped across the battlefield in advance so there is something to skin. Donut's constraint, in her usual all-caps:

YOU'RE NOT DONE YET ISN'T GOING TO WORK IF THERE ARE NO TARGETS… THE BACK SIDE OF THE MADNESS CASTLE IS JUST PAST MY RANGE FOR ATROCITY MAGIC.

The cast, chapter 69, with the Nest tower's Atrocity synergy applied:

At the same moment, Donut cast the spell. She did, indeed, cast a tower-enhanced version of You're Not Done Yet. And the moment she did, the entire world in front of us burst into activity. The Xs on the map all started to blink.

System Message: Warlord Princess Donut has committed another Atrocity. Wow. What a naughty kitty. I sure hope she isn't forced to cast a third.

Thousands of fleshers swarm outward, seeking anything marked as an enemy, including the enormous rolling ball created by Rolling Battle Formation. The AI's parting sentence is a foreshadow: she is forced to cast a third atrocity seven chapters later, and it is War Crime.

Carl makes one grim intervention during the sequence: he kills the flesher-wrapped Nami with a hob-lobber specifically to stop another war mage being born out of her.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text:
No level is ever stated and no per-level behavior is described. The two variables shown in play are:

  1. Corpse supply — the spell is worthless without bodies, which is why the party spends chapters stockpiling them
  2. Range, which Donut can extend enormously by casting from an Atrocity-synergy tower

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• War Crime — Donut's third Atrocity
  • Rolling Battle Formation — her second
  • Second Chance — the "less insidious" comparison Mordecai reaches for

Sourced from Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Zerzura
docs.text:
Quick facts

  • Caster: "The Sledge" — a Cretin mercenary bodyguard, installed with the spell specifically because casting it is too taxing to give to a crawler
  • Effect: Transfers an entire town or city (buildings and NPCs) down the dungeon — normally one floor, but skips floors entirely on "Scolopendra levels"
  • Obtained: Negotiated as part of Carl's mercenary-bodyguard package with a kua-tin Borant admin, in exchange for surrendering the Gate of the Feral Gods as collateral — Quasar's own suggestion
  • Danger: Landing location is random and uncontrollable, and the transferred town is cursed with an unstoppable, self-propagating revenant horde on arrival (see below)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Zerzura is introduced as a rumor — Donut hears the name secondhand and is immediately curious, and Carl privately recalls "the crazy story Quasar told [him] about Remex the Grand and what he'd done with the Zerzura spell" — well before anyone actually explains what it does. Casting requirements alone are demanding: it can only be cast at the end of a floor, takes about five minutes to complete (during which the caster needs active protection), and cannot be re-attempted if it miscasts. It's also "pretty hard on the caster," which is why Quasar has it installed into a mercenary (the Sledge) rather than given to Carl or Donut directly.

The basic transfer is simple:

"It takes a full city or town, NPCs and buildings and all, and it transfers them one floor down. It transfers the town itself and all the NPCs. That's it. No mobs or enemy, red-tagged NPCs. No stairwells or any other special rooms, either, like prize rooms."

On certain floor types called "Scolopendra levels," the spell skips floors entirely rather than moving down just one — this is what happened to the historical crawler Remex the Grand, whose town-cast jumped straight from Floor 6 to Floor 9, skipping 7 and 8.

docs.title: The Real Danger: The Children of Inpewt
docs.text:
The spell's popularity with viewers/factions comes from a much darker mechanic Quasar only reveals after the deal is already made. The destination cannot be steered, and it "almost always" drops the entire town directly into the worst possible location — typically a monster nest or boss room — killing everyone on impact. Every one of those deaths immediately resurrects as a Child of Inpewt: a powerful revenant that retains whatever spells/abilities it had in life. Everyone from the transferred town, plus the caster, is permanently "marked," and the revenants actively hunt the marked down; anyone they successfully kill also becomes a revenant. The horde doesn't stop until every marked person — villagers and caster alike — is dead. Remex used the spell repeatedly to farm easy levels off this mechanic, until his own unlucky Floor 6→9 skip got his mercenaries and NPCs slaughtered by both revenants and Faction Wars combatants simultaneously.

Carl reacts to the full explanation with open horror, weighing it against the alternative of simply letting a group of endangered NPCs (including children) be lost to the collapsing floor instead. The plan settles on casting it on the one remaining town in the area — the High Elf castle — once a group of refugee changelings has been maneuvered inside it disguised as elves. In practice, most of those changelings end up escaping separately (shape-shifting into birds and flying off) after the flying house ferrying them is overrun by mantis nymphs. It's the Sledge himself, along with the rescued gnome Bonnie and two orphaned Ursine cubs — none of whom make it onto the flying house — who ends up riding the castle down via Zerzura when he finally casts it in the battle's last moments ("Casting now. One minute to chant spell. Five minutes to cast."), successfully teleporting all of them to Floor 9 as the castle and its grounds are overrun. Carl's parting warning to the Sledge — "there might be some zombie things attacking you" — confirms the "Children of Inpewt" mechanic is indeed expected to trigger, though what actually happens to them on landing isn't shown within Book 5's pages; the castle itself is last seen having "traveled away" and landed "half-destroyed" somewhere on Floor 9.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text: No stated per-level formula for the spell itself. The revenant threat scales with the size and composition of whatever town is transferred (more NPCs/monsters killed on landing means more Children of Inpewt), not with the caster's own skill level.

docs.title: Book 7: The Second Cast — and How the Princess Posse Wins Faction Wars
docs.text:
The Sledge casts Zerzura a second time in chapter 85, and this time it is not a desperate improvisation to save a handful of refugees. It is the win condition.

"Starting to cast," The Sledge said. It would take five minutes for the spell to work.

He glowed. He had cast Zerzura.

Rosetta: It worked. Shanty Town is included in the glow. It successfully combined the two towns. Moving to the saferoom now with Tipid and the others. I have Samantha.

The entire funnel city of Larracos—and Shanty Town—was about to get transferred to the 12th floor. To the Court of the Ascendency.

docs.title: What moves
docs.text:
The cast takes the whole funnel city of Larracos plus the newly-built Shanty Town ring, combined into one settlement for the spell's purposes, and drops them on a green hill overlooking miles of cotton fields on the 12th floor. Because Floor 9 is a Scolopendra level, the spell skips floors rather than moving down one.

Moves with the city Does not move The thousands of NPC residents of Larracos Hired mercenaries, including the Sledge himself and the surviving cretins — returned to "storage" or the mercenary market The rescued changelings Mordecai The Semeru dwarves The strippers and sluggalos, deliberately kept and sent back to the saferoom barracks Everyone who moved down from the 6th floor Ferdinand, Juice Box, and little Ruby

Over 50,000 former crawlers had come to the city; roughly 28,000 leave the dungeon entirely at the moment the spell triggers.

The Children of Inpewt mechanic is still armed. Anyone crushed by the landing city becomes one.

docs.title: Why it wins the war
docs.text:
This is the mechanism, and it is a rules exploit rather than a battle. Ferdinand and Juice Box are the two surviving warlords of Team Retribution. By riding the city out, they abandon their posts:

System Message: Both Warlords Ferdinand and Juice Box have left the realm. Under the current ruleset, they have abandoned their posts and have forfeited their position.

Team Retribution is defeated by forfeit. The Princess Posse wins Faction Wars because the enemy warlords voluntarily got on the bus.

The plan is not a secret by the end — Epitome Tagg says so directly in chapter 83: "We know what you're planning on doing with the NPC team. With the Zerzura spell, which will take the city of Larracos to the 12th floor. I will go with them."

Exact-verification note

Book 7 contains no system description block for Zerzura, and only four mentions of the spell by name. The Book 5 mechanics above are not restated, contradicted, or expanded. What happened to the Floor 6 High Elf castle and the Children of Inpewt horde that followed it down is likewise never revisited.

Sourced from Book 5: The Butcher's Masquerade and Book 7: This Inevitable Ruin.

docs.title: Timeline
docs.text: A chronological highlights reel of Book 1's major events. This is the condensed version — a future Chapter Summaries section will cover the book in full narrative detail, chapter by chapter. Entries link to the relevant page where one exists.

docs.title: Before the Dungeon
docs.text: • Carl, 27, a former Coast Guard machinery technician turned civilian marine tech, breaks up with his girlfriend Beatrice after learning she cheated on him in the Bahamas — he's looking after her show cat, Princess Donut, when the story begins.

docs.title: The Harvest
docs.text:
• At 2:23 AM Pacific time on January 3rd, every structure with a roof on Earth is instantly crushed as the planet is "harvested" for resources by the Syndicate/Borant Corporation, killing everyone indoors — an estimated 3 million dead in Carl's city alone.
  • Carl and Donut survive only because they were both outside at the moment of the harvest.
  • The Syndicate's announcement offers survivors a choice: remain on the surface with no further resources, or enter the 18-level World Dungeon to "reclaim" lost matter.

docs.title: Level/Floor 1
docs.text:
• Carl enters Level 1, fights through a goblin ambush (including a Goblin Murder Dozer), and reaches the Tutorial Guild run by Mordecai.
  • Donut eats an Enhanced Pet Biscuit and is transformed into a talking, stat-boosted crawler in her own right; she names their new party The Royal Court of Princess Donut.
  • Carl and Donut clear The Hoarder (Level 7 Neighborhood Boss).
  • They clear the Goblin War Chieftain via cart bomb, without ever triggering an official boss-card sequence — Book 1's darkest moment for Carl.
  • They clear The Juicer (Level 9 Neighborhood Boss) inside a gym-themed neighborhood.
  • Carl and Donut join a group of elderly evacuees ("Team Meadow Lark," led by Brandon An) and the mysterious, shopping-cart-wielding Agatha.
  • After a full day of chopper scouting, they find Floor 1's only known stairwell down to Floor 2 — guarded by the Ball of Swine (Level 15 Borough Boss). They defeat it in a mixed 7-crawler party and descend immediately afterward, at which point their stats become publicly visible to live viewers for the first time.

docs.title: Floor 2
docs.text:
• Carl adopts a strict "always destroy the corpse" policy after learning corpses spawn endless waves of Brindle Grubs.
  • They escape the Krakaren Clone (Level 10 Neighborhood Boss) inside a Rev-Up Moonshine Company distillery, badly injured.
  • They defeat Ralph, a Level 11 Neighborhood Boss, in a kobold fighting pit — freeing a pack of captive dingoes in the process.
  • Donut chooses a Mongoliensis from the resulting pet reward room, later revealed by Odette to actually be a velociraptor; he's eventually bonded and named Mongo.
  • Carl publicly challenges Prince Maestro of the Skull Empire to single combat after a hostile interview on Death Watch Extreme Dungeon Mayhem, nicknaming him "Pork Boy" — the insult goes viral across the Syndicate's social media.
  • During the continued Meadow Lark evacuation, a Rage Elemental — summoned as a System AI punishment for a bathroom-etiquette violation — kills nurse Yolanda Martinez; Carl and Donut later deny it a clean kill by luring it into a collapsing stairwell.
  • Carl and Donut descend to Floor 3.

docs.title: End of Book 1
docs.text: • Carl and Donut are about to choose a race and class for the first time, now that they've reached Floor 3.

docs.title: Floor 3 (Book 2)
docs.text:
• Carl and Donut choose their permanent race/class: Carl becomes a Primal Compensated Anarchist; Donut deliberately picks Former Child Actor for its hidden Manager benefit, covering it up as an accident so Mordecai doesn't suspect it was intentional.
  • They enter the Over City — a themed urban floor built around a destroyed volcano-kingdom — and stumble into a quest at Grimaldi's transformed traveling circus.
  • Carl solo-kills Heather the Bear (Level 19 Neighborhood Boss) after Tsarina Signet puts Donut under a sleep curse and forces the fight.
  • Carl confronts Ringmaster Grimaldi (Level 85 City Boss + Elite) and resolves the standoff through negotiation rather than a kill, securing a hidden stairwell to Floor 4 and a recurring-guest-star deal with the drama's producers.
  • Carl and Donut take up a second quest after NPC orc GumGum asks for help investigating murdered sex workers; GumGum is killed by Krasue before they can help her.
  • They kill Miss Quill (Level 30 Neighborhood Boss), the town's true ruler behind a dead figurehead magistrate, uncovering a scheme to manufacture krasue and cast a generations-old genocidal spell against the settlement's non-flying residents.
  • Miss Quill's undead husband, Remex, survives her death as an unstable power capacitor, triggering a mass "event quest" explosion that nearly kills everyone in the blast radius; Carl narrowly contains it, creating Carl's Doomsday Scenario in the process.
  • Katia Grim, a Doppelganger sent by Hekla's group (Brynhild's Daughters) for help leveling, joins the party permanently.
  • Carl publicly calls for the Skull Empire's citizens to rise up during a live interview; Prince Stalwart orders a retaliatory strike that instead kills the Valtay-sponsored singer Manasa, and the Valtay Corporation destroys a Skull Empire royal yacht in response, killing Prince Maestro and Queen Consort Ugloo.
  • Fleeing the event-quest explosion, Carl, Donut, Katia, and a mixed group of other crawlers descend early from Floor 3 to Floor 4 via a stairwell near a decrepit building that fellow crawler Daniel Bautista had already scouted, with only about three minutes to spare before Carl's own Doomsday Scenario device detonates. A second stairwell, hidden beneath Grimaldi's circus, is discovered earlier but never actually used.

docs.title: End of Book 2
docs.text:
• Carl and Donut land on the current working leaderboard for the first time (6th and 7th of the top 10), with Lucia Mar 1st and Hekla 2nd.
  • Odette privately warns Carl that Hekla — while not evil — is "practical and cunning" and has become fixated on recruiting Donut (and, through her, permanent access to a Manager) into Brynhild's Daughters.
  • The book ends as Floor 4 is about to open.

docs.title: Floor 4 — "The Iron Tangle" (Book 3)
docs.text:
• Carl, Donut, Katia, and Mongo arrive on a moving subway train; Donut picks the Football Hooligan class, and the party begins mapping a sprawling, confusing rail-and-station system (150,000-plus stops, only 9,375 stairwells) under a shortened 10-day timer.
  • Carl fights and kills Gore-Gore the Mantaur, narrowly avoiding an accidental full summon of the war god Grull via his own War Gauntlet; the fight ends with Carl gaining a new sponsor, the Valtay Corporation.
  • The party, working with allies including Imani C, Elle McGibbons, Li Jun, Li Na, Zhang, and Daniel Bautista, discovers the floor's central crisis: a ghoul-generation system is overloading, threatening to flood the entire rail network, with hundreds of thousands of crawlers scattered and trapped between stations — see Iron Tangle Management.
  • Meeting Frank Q at the Desperado Club, Carl learns the full story behind Book 2's dynamite trap: Frank and his ex-wife Maggie had forced their injured daughter Yvette to wear an Enchanted Night Wyrm's Ring of Divine Suffering and mark Carl for death — which blocks all healing until the mark's target dies. Carl escaped to a saferoom and survived, leaving Yvette permanently unhealable and in agony; Maggie choked her own daughter to death as a mercy killing, then vanished. Frank, a broken man, gives Carl the ring as his own twisted "revenge" before Chris Andrews — mid personality-altering race change — kills him at the club.
  • Hekla, rescuing Katia from Brynhild's Daughters, secretly plots to have Katia (and, if needed, her own healer Silfa) die in a way that reads as accidental combat loss — using invisible Dirty Little Phased Bolts that inflict lethal, uncredited damage — so that a grieving Donut would be forced to fold what remains of the party into Hekla's own, gaining Borant permanent access to Mordecai. Discovered mid-attack, Katia's Rush ability goes off-target and instead kills Hekla outright, claiming a 500,000-gold bounty as the season's first player-killing of a top-10 crawler and rocketing Katia from level 24 to 37 — ending Book 1–2's recurring rival/antagonist arc. Brynhild's Daughters disbands afterward.
  • Brandon An dies holding a defensive line as part of the floor's collapse.
  • Carl, Katia, and allies build an improvised rescue operation — hijacked named trains and repurposed maintenance interdiction carts, whose portal-scoop tech is used both to ferry stranded crawlers to safety and to funnel oncoming monster hordes straight into the Abyss.
  • Fire Brandy, the Nightmare train's engine-spirit NPC, and the dwarf Tizquick willingly ride the train into the Abyss and detonate it to help collapse the floor's ghoul-generator network, after both realize their in-game families were never real.
  • Carl accidentally teleports Mimic Rex — one of six floor-wide Station Mimics — into a trainyard while trying to save a stranded crawler group, then gets trapped there himself while summoning a Mantaur vessel to fight it off. This triggers a Death Challenge broadcast event pitting the Mimic against the involuntarily-summoned war god Grull — secretly sponsored and piloted by a very-much-alive Prince Maestro of the Skull Empire, who faked his death in Book 2. Carl survives by manipulating the involuntary-summon mechanic to banish Grull to the abyss after he kills the Mimic Rex.
  • With eleven hours left on the floor's timer, Iron Tangle management announces a system-wide self-destruct, blaming "the Krakaren" for a betrayal, and floods every stairwell station with the floor's accumulated Krakaren-monster population at once.

docs.title: End of Book 3
docs.text:
• Carl ends the book at Level 41 (up from 27), with Donut at 33; both are members of a much larger, more organized crawler alliance than they started the floor with.
  • The floor's ghoul crisis is contained, though not fully resolved, as the level's timer runs out.

docs.title: Floor 5 — "The Bubbles" (Book 4)
docs.text:
• Carl, Donut, Katia, and Mongo arrive in bubble #543, one of 1,172 sealed spherical worlds floating in the dark Lacuna — each split into Land, Sea, Air, and Subterranean quadrants behind an invisible barrier; Donut picks the Glass Cannon specialization.
  • The party bases out of Hump Town, a Dromedarian brothel settlement secretly infiltrated by the Changeling Principals, a cult seeking a cure for their species' hereditary Compression Sickness.
  • Carl kills Ruckus (Level 55 Borough Boss) while field-testing homemade missiles, then uncovers and thwarts a Skull-Empire-backed changeling infiltration of the town's guard ranks with Donut's help.
  • After the hostage gnome Wynne is killed by a rival crawler group, Carl, Donut, and Katia stage a fake resurrection and disguise ruse to trick the dirigible-gnome dreadnaught the Wasteland into a face-to-face negotiation, then destroy it mid-air — see The Wasteland — killing most of its crew including Commandant Kane's negotiator and sniper, and rescuing Kane's orphaned daughter Bonnie from the boss Denise the Feral Goose Mother.
  • Carl accidentally assassinates dungeon admin Loita using a rigged toy-robot self-destruct mechanism during a sponsor infomercial taping, then talks his way out of a Syndicate liaison investigation without confessing or naming his source (the Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook).
  • Katia leads a separate team (Gwendolyn Duet, Tran, Florin, and others) storming the Land Quadrant's Sandcastle, killing the mage Ghazi and the borough boss Mrs. Ghazi — though the castle's collapse washes the survivors down into the Water Quadrant instead of ending the fight cleanly.
  • Carl, Katia, and two other survivors dive to the wrecked submarine Akula, are swallowed whole by the City Boss Lusca in a live-broadcast Special Event, and kill her from the inside using a berserking potion and a salvaged buzzsaw.
  • Maggie My — revealed to have taken an Infiltrator (Scree) race and fully puppeted Chris Andrews since the previous floor — is finally extracted and killed after Donut buys time by dropping the pair through a Hole spell rather than letting Carl kill Chris outright; Chris rejoins the party.
  • The Subterranean Quadrant's guardian, Quetzalcoatlus — possessed by the banished lesser deity Psamathe — is destroyed via an environmental lightning-tower trap, at the cost of every crawler remaining in the quadrant.
  • With all four quadrants cleared, Carl assembles the final piece of the Gate of the Feral Gods and uses it to evacuate crawlers trapped in sealed bubbles across the Lacuna — each rescue releasing a feral god or demon into the newly-emptied bubble, including the puppy-god Orthrus, safely reunited with his father Emberus, God of Sun and Ash, whom Carl accidentally acquires as his own patron deity via a Celestial Grenade.
  • In the finale, rather than releasing a final feral god onto the open floor, Carl sends it through a portal directly into the Ninth Floor's Larracos marketplace instead, flooding and destroying the city's mercantile district and crippling every Faction War army's ability to resupply ahead of schedule.
  • Carl ends the book as the dungeon's #1-ranked crawler (Level 47); Katia splits off from the main party (while remaining nominally grouped) to protect Eva Sigrid's scattered former followers; Chris Andrews joins the core party.

docs.title: End of Book 4
docs.text:
• Carl publicly vows, on-air, to hunt down and kill every bounty hunter sent after him and Donut on Floor 6 before its timer runs out.
  • The epilogue reveals a Borant-adjacent "pacifist" NFC sponsor, run by Dr. Hu (Porthus, author of the Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook's second edition), has been quietly bankrolling Carl's campaign — and that Beatrice, Carl's ex, has just been captured alive off-planet by a bounty hunter working for Odette.

docs.title: Floor 6 — "The Hunting Grounds" (Book 5)
docs.text:
• Carl, Donut, and Mongo arrive on Floor 6's capital, Zockau; Carl picks the Agent Provocateur specialization and Donut a new Legendary Diva bard class. Carl negotiates collateral terms with Borant over the confiscated Gate of the Feral Gods, gaining four cretin mercenaries and the Zerzura spell (see Spells).
  • Carl opens the floor by raiding Zockau directly — marking and killing the hunters Xindy and Chin'Dua, leveling a city block, and racking up 34 Hunter-Killer trophies before nearly dying; he's saved by Miriam Dom, Prepotente, and Bianca. This also brands him with a Guild of Suffering tattoo — see Dungeon Factions.
  • Carl and Donut accidentally kill an Ursine mayor and conquer his settlement, renaming it Point Mongo and fortifying it against incoming hunters.
  • Mongo encounters a wild Mongoliensis pack led by Kiwi and mates with her; Donut has a private panic episode hinting at unresolved dread over Floor 9's Blood Sultanate succession curse (see the Crown of the Sepsis Whore).
  • Carl and Donut help Tsarina Signet — contractually bound to her secondary broadcast, Vengeance of the Daughter — liberate Fort Freedom from the Naiad Confederacy, accidentally triggering and killing the boss Claude Sludgington the Fourth in the process; the were-castors Clint and Nadine are killed in the same battle.
  • Odette privately reveals to Carl and Donut that Beatrice is alive and off-planet, then stages a scripted reunion/confrontation on her show; Donut publicly and permanently cuts ties with her. In the same news cycle, the Valtay Corporation acquires 51% of the Borant Corporation — see Factions.
  • Miriam Dom sacrifices herself (via Carl's Ring of Divine Suffering, at her own request) to cure a spreading vampirism outbreak she unknowingly caused while fighting Big Tina and the elite vampire hunter Viscount Fog; Carl and Donut kill Fog's surviving mount, Sierra, earlier the same night. Prepotente, left catatonic with grief, swallows his own Ring of Divine Suffering and swears revenge on everyone he holds responsible.
  • A floor-wide vampirism outbreak escalates into The Creeping Apocalypse, a mandatory world-quest to kill fifty Odious Creepers by sundown; the quest fails, triggering a floor-consuming Gehenna Bramble and a new "blood bar" saferoom restriction — see Game Mechanics.
  • Carl and Donut, now allied with Kiwi's pack, solve "The Recital" — Big Tina's dinosaur-rampage quest — by learning her tragic backstory from an Ursine barmaid, Prudence, and booking her into the upcoming Butcher's Masquerade talent show.
  • Carl coordinates a floor-wide crawler offensive against the scattered, demoralized hunter population, killing hundreds in a single day; Circe Took's daughter Vrah is deliberately infected with a venereal disease Carl can't be cured of without either self-sterilizing or mating outside mantis honor rules — see The Dark Hive.
  • The Borant/Valtay AI begins ignoring Syndicate court rulings it disagrees with following the ownership change, a recognized precursor to an AI "going primal" — see Game Mechanics.
  • At the Butcher's Masquerade in the High Elf Castle, Carl and Donut's group survives a multi-sided ambush (Vrah's mother Circe Took, in physical form as the goddess Diwata, floods the castle with mantis nymphs) after Signet willingly breaks the ritual's peace seal as a sacrifice; the resulting battle kills Vrah, Circe Took/Diwata, Queen Imogen, Tsarina Signet, Gwendolyn Duet, Firas, Horton, and the Popov Brothers' adult forms (who are reborn as ineligible infant nodlings and rescued from the dungeon entirely), among many others. Katia kills Eva Sigrid at last, but inherits Donut's old Crown of the Sepsis Whore curse in the process.
  • Carl publicly announces the Princess Posse's Faction Wars sponsorship (fielded by Donut's fan club) and pushes for a floor-wide vote to remove safety protections for crawler-fielding factions ahead of Floor 9 — see Game Mechanics.

docs.title: End of Book 5
docs.text:
• Carl ends the book ranked #3 on the leaderboard (per the system message on entering Floor 7; Donut instead insists she's "ranked number one," by a metric never specified), having personally ended the Dark Hive's hunting operation and the Naiad Confederacy, and having secured Donut and Carl's own Faction Wars team ahead of Floor 9.
  • Prepotente shatters the seventh floor's starting chamber outright using two mystery sponsor-gifted items (the Hammer of Fast Forward and the Stick of Cascadia's Screams), forcing every crawler on the floor through its stairwells simultaneously before the level's maze challenge can even begin.
  • The epilogue reveals Eva's dying act transferred the Crown of the Sepsis Whore's Blood Sultanate succession curse from Donut onto Katia — meaning only one of the two will be allowed to descend from Floor 9 to Floor 10.

docs.title: Floor 7 — "The Great Race" (skipped)
docs.text: • Floor 7 was a maze of branching tubes running several hundred kilometres, announced by Borant as "an engineering marvel" funded by the incoming Valtay Corporation. It lasted roughly ten minutes. Before the opening announcement had even finished, Prepotente cracked the starting chamber's glass wall (see End of Book 5 above) — and the crack propagated to every wall on the level at once, shattering the floor to dust and dumping every crawler through the exit portals simultaneously. Neither book records any deaths on the floor. Donut was briefly a Viper Queen, and nobody received the floor's spellbook delivery — "You snooze you lose."

docs.title: Floor 8 — "The Ghosts of Earth" (Book 6)
docs.text: Floor 8 runs from December 10th to the collapse, in three phases: a fourteen-day build-up inside a single locked region, a 48-hour assault in a second region to win an exit key, and a final scramble back to the original region. Just over 38,000 crawlers start it, spread across 293 possible regions (205 of them occupied), each region an exact replay of a patch of pre-collapse Earth. For the floor's structure see Level 8; for the card system that governs almost everything below, see The T'Ghee Card System.

docs.title: Phase One — Havana
docs.text:
• Carl and Donut arrive in El Capitolio Nacional de Cuba, Havana — Donut having picked Cuba specifically to avoid the Bahamas trap she correctly suspected. Donut takes the Master Telephone Psychic class (better mapping, offensive charm spells) over "Agony Urchin." The system announces the squad, flag, and T'Ghee card systems.
  • The party opens its held Floor 6 loot boxes, yielding the Scavenger's Daughter, an Enchanted Nipple Ring of the Superior Fire Demon's Hand Maiden, and the Legionnaires of the Damned tome — see Items and Spells.
  • Carl and Donut meet Cuba's only other squad: Paz Lo, Anton Lopez, and Sister Ines Quiteria. The two squads jointly capture their first monk-seal totems, which triggers the quest The Chowder War.
  • On the show Shadow Boxer, Carl's traumatic childhood is aired publicly. Host Rosetta Thagra secretly slips him a coded message mid-broadcast before the liaison Harbinger kills the feed and bans her.
  • In the Colón Cemetery ghommid settlement, a Celestial Thorn Room appears. Acting on a secret warning from Katia, Carl repairs Yemaya's shrine instead of Ogun's — resurrecting a goddess, and costing Anton Lopez his life when Ogun crushes his head in retaliation. Paz Lo takes a permanent, unhealable smite; Sister Ines flags him into a T'Ghee card rather than watch him die, over his own explicit objection.
  • Yemaya and Eileithyia appear. Eileithyia — driven by Huanxin Jinx — offers Carl a private bargain: secure Odette as the Princess Posse's Faction Wars adjutant, and she will clear the Crown of the Sepsis Whore problem.
  • Katia reveals the Crown of the Sepsis Whore to Donut, along with her Engaged Lock Box of the Night Wyrm and the Orchid of Eileithyia's Grace.
  • At the Faction Wars preproduction meeting, Juice Box — alive, and leading a rogue NPC insurrection on Floor 9 — assassinates the warlord Stalwart in front of the council and demands a tenth team for NPCs. Carl takes the proposal forward.
  • Katia is revealed to be addicted to four dungeon drugs, with permanent stat damage. Mordecai privately advises letting her self-destruct so that Donut survives the Crown's succession curse; Carl refuses outright and forces the Astrid assassination job to happen immediately instead.
  • The Astrid job goes catastrophically wrong. Samantha accidentally releases the minor feral demon Minge from the Nothing; Carl responds by unleashing the vorpals held behind a hidden door. Astrid dies anyway, and the Desperado Club is destroyed and closed.
  • Damascus Steel reveals that Astrid was his mother and the Night Wyrm his father, and that the contract was a murder-for-inheritance scheme. He and his brother Anaconda leave to kill their father. Carl hires the Penis Parade's dancers — the men's side of the operation — as mercenaries in the aftermath.
  • On Odette's final show, Empress D'Nadia is exposed as having burned all three of her Emergency Action Items on attempts to delete crawlers and NPCs, the last of them naming Carl and Donut directly. Odette declines the adjutant role and announces she is sponsoring the goddess Nekhebit instead; Baroness Victory becomes the Posse's adjutant.
  • Off the record, Odette confesses everything: the crawls exist to harvest fuel, and she is part of a long-running plot to shut them down safely.

docs.title: Phase Two — the Florida Keys
docs.text:
• Phase two begins December 24th. Donut fights her first solo deck battle. A placement glitch drops a chunk of Dallas County, Iowa on top of Monroe County, Florida — crawlers standing in the Keys read as being in Iowa.
  • On the transplanted Iowa mound, Carl and Donut beat nine deckmasters in sequence. Among the spliced-in terrain they find Carl's father's trailer, lifted from a different broadcast season entirely, and Carl watches his father die of a morphine overdose administered by his stepmother Tami-Lynn — and discovers he has a six-year-old half-brother, Asher.
  • The final deckmaster is the Reminiscence Hydra of Malicious Compliance, built from the faces of everyone Carl and Donut have known, Asher's among them. Killing it earns the phase key, and Carl is raised to Devotee, the highest worship rank available to a non-Cleric. Donut later tells Carl that Beatrice knew Asher existed and kept it from him.
  • Louis declares Christmas over Carl's objections. Mid-party, the system AI seizes control of the crawl from Borant — the earliest this has ever happened in the show's history. Orren negotiates a settlement and, as one of the AI's own conditions, publicly explains Primal Engines and Macro AIs. All six rival Faction Wars teams attempt to abdicate and are refused under the quarantine.
  • Carl rides his late father's motorcycle to The Shepherd's House, a homeless shelter in Homestead, Florida, to hear a Residual speak. Orren teleports him out before the speech finishes and declares the entire event a trap engineered by Carl's own, now-fugitive, sponsors.

docs.title: Phase Three — the Bedlam
docs.text:
• Phase three begins at midnight on December 26th. Imani's entire squad has been killed by her own summoned totem. In a chaotic eight-combatant battle touched off by a Samantha teleport malfunction, Quan Ch strips Sister Ines's phase key and then Donut's — and the same wave of mass death triggers a planet-wide Demon Eviction, the earliest in the crawl's history.
  • Using teleport traps smuggled inside Samantha, Carl and Donut ambush and kill Quan Ch and recover both stolen keys. Seconds later the Capitol building's stairwell doorway is destroyed, taking its key with it. Tserendolgor, refusing to fight Donut for the last remaining key, hands Carl her gear and her pet Garret and detonates herself.
  • Carl and Prepotente design an escape for every keyless crawler on the planet: free the demon prince Amayon and buff him to full power so that his forced homecoming portal spans the entire world, then shelter everyone in trenches dug beneath the indestructible stairwell chambers as the portal tears them out of the ground. Carl rallies the whole dungeon population — via the Book of Voodoo — to stop fighting each other and cooperate. Prepotente privately rates the plan's odds at "40 percent… maybe 35 percent."
  • Lucia Mar, having personally slaughtered Beijing's crawler population, leaves five Tier 3 Doggie Door upgrades on the ground as a favour to Florin before descending — and separately announces she intends to kill Donut and Mongo on Floor 9. Reinforcements begin pouring into Cuba through the new fast-travel doors.
  • At the FOCSA building, Louis kills Sister Ines, which summons her divine patron Ysalte. Amayon is freed from his host shell but remains enslaved to the goddess. In the final T'Ghee card battle, Paz Lo — Ysalte's own stolen totem — kills her, using Katia's reused Bolt of Ophiotaurus and his own self-destruct.
  • Carl persuades Raul the crab to repopulate the ocean with souls, then teleports himself inside Samantha to drive his own health down and trigger The Martyr's Path, bathing Havana — and Amayon — in Sheol Fire, which makes a demon exponentially stronger. Amayon, now at full power, casts his homecoming spell.
  • Escaping the collapsing tower, a misfired Golden Combo fuses Carl with the boss Shi Maria. She takes control of his body, tears out and eats Li Jun's eye, brews tattoo ink from it, and stick-and-pokes the Eye of the Bedlam Bride into his chest — explicitly so that she can never be fully discarded: "I am a part of you… until you decide to free me." Donut rips Shi Maria's card afterward.
  • Carl and Donut spend their one carry-forward card slot on ripping Paz Lo's card instead, freeing him, as he had asked.
  • Carl spends one Emergency Action Item to hand every pending Faction Wars procedural vote over to the viewing audience. They vote 98% in favour of removing safety protections for faction sponsors, and 52% in favour of creating a tenth NPC team, co-warlorded by Juice Box and Sir Ferdinand. A rival proposal to cut Celestial Summonings from fifteen per team to five is rejected at 37%.
  • The heavens open over Cuba and the world is stripped clean. Carl, Donut, and Imani are pulled up into the sky and land on Floor 9 — Faction Wars — along with 33,804 crawlers in total, against a historical average of just under 8,000. "We were hitting the ninth floor in unprecedented numbers."

docs.title: End of Book 6
docs.text:
• Agatha is revealed as "Agent number 22" — ten years detached from her own collective, and the one who had been waiting behind the Meadowlark Elder Care facility in Wenatchee, Washington on the night of Earth's collapse. Her faction's stated goal is to free the Eulogist and return it to its slumber; their parting phrase is "May the Eulogist ever sleep, my friend." If Agatha personally gets her way, "this entire universe would be swept clean of biological life."
  • Her rivals — thousands of agents working for the Apothecary — are meanwhile "secretly implanting the crawler with a hidden upgrade."
  • The Syndicate Council debates and refuses to pull the failsafe: over half the galaxy's wealth, and the councillors' own families, are trapped inside the quarantined system at the Scolopendra Club.
  • The Valtay's alternative is an engineered extinction event: "well over 150,000" mercenaries flooded into the crawl to kill every remaining crawler and so end the quarantine early.
  • Tipid and Rosetta, funded and organized by a "Doctor Hu," have converted the garbage freighter Homecoming Queen and have just been cleared to board fifty thousand former crawlers onto it as troopers for the Princess Posse.

docs.title: Left Unresolved Going Into Floor 9
docs.text:
The book deliberately closes several threads without answers. They're recorded here so the wiki doesn't quietly invent them:

  • Carl's father is never named. Not in the flashbacks, not in the trailer sequence, not anywhere — he is only ever "my father," "my dad," "the old man."
  • The Eye of the Bedlam Bride tattoo has no stated effect. The item entry reads "Tattoo. The Eye of the Bedlam Bride." and nothing else: "That's all it said. It gave no other description."
  • Samantha's power source is never confirmed. Carl's own guess — "I'm starting to think maybe Samantha gets more powerful every time somebody dies" — is never verified.
  • Elle's Graupel firing at an amplified level is never explained. A level-5 spell casts at level 16 and levels Elle six times instantly; Samantha, the likeliest cause, is herself confused by it.
  • Carl's recurring "river" metaphor is never explained. It recurs roughly nine times and stays a motif tied to his mother's death rather than anything mechanical.
  • The Orchid of Eileithyia's Grace is never eaten, and the Crown of the Sepsis Whore's succession curse is still on Katia at the book's end. Carl's closing note is only that "We had a way out."
  • Whether the system AI is one of the rejected infant Macro AIs is heavily implied and never stated — see Macro AIs, Primal Engines, and the Eulogist.
  • Agatha's and the Apothecary's true natures are contradicted by Orren's account, which dismisses the whole Residual affair as a failed scheme by disgruntled ex-crawlers. The book does not adjudicate between the two.
  • The Chowder War is marked "Quest Failed", not won, and immediately replaced by a new quest, "Hell Comes to Crawler Town" — which is completed.
  • Where the freed demons went is never confirmed. Roughly a hundred Level 140 Petty Demon Pleasure Valets are freed from their zombie shells on the northern beach alone: "Hopefully those had made their way back to Sheol, but I wasn't sure if that kind could drag people into hell like the possessed zombies could. Mordecai wasn't sure, either."
  • Mongo's wing is not regrown on-page. Mordecai has an upgraded potion that would do it but withholds it — "he has to take it later. He wants to look at the potion first to make sure."

docs.title: Floor 9 — "Faction Wars" (Book 7)
docs.text: Floor 9 is a war, not a dungeon crawl. 32,500 crawlers arrive from Floor 8 and are folded into ten teams — nine attacking teams each holding a numbered slice of the Plains of Larracos, plus Team Retribution, the all-NPC tenth team voted into existence at the end of Book 6, defending the sunken city of Larracos itself. Combat runs in four phases: the Ceasefire, the Ramp-Up, Open Hostilities, and the Peeling of Larracos. For the floor's overall shape see Level 9; for how the Book 6 rulebook actually behaved in the field see Faction Wars in Practice.

docs.title: The Ceasefire
docs.text:
• Carl, Donut, and the party land in Larracos. The Ceasefire opens at 60 hours. Eight of the nine attacking teams immediately form an anti-Posse Bloc; the Princess Posse's answer is a truce with Team Retribution, the NPCs.
  • Loot distribution from the held Floor 8 boxes: the Tiara of a Thousand Lights, the Cloak of the Benevolent Champion, the Gloom Wraith Phase skill, and the Enchanted Toe Ring of the Well-Balanced — whose Mind Balance skill makes Carl personally immune to Conscription for the rest of the floor. Rend (Sir Rendlegore) is bonded as a pet.
  • Louis's airship Party Planner is unveiled. The party tours Larracos, meets the newly-awakened Semeru dwarves at their castle on the roots of the All Tree, and allies with them. Louis and Juice Box marry in a small legal ceremony (the full Confirmation is deferred and never happens on the page). Carl buys the mayorship of Shanty Town from Sir Ferdinand for a bowler hat.
  • Tipid, Rosetta, and the 50,000 former crawlers aboard the Homecoming Queen are revealed to be physically present and fighting for the Posse — part of roughly 150,000 mercenary reinforcements flooding every team. The FUPA is built. Kiwi and Big Tina are reunited with Mongo.
  • Baroness Victory axes a Sensation Entertainment-sponsored suicide bomber (an ogre, "Herman the Fleet") in the antechamber outside the Posse's flag room — the only time an adjutant fights all book, and she argues the AI into accepting it after the fact. See Adjutants.
  • In a shared dream-therapy session with Katia, Carl learns from her husband Hapanzi that Shi Maria is genuinely trapped inside him. Commander Stockade of the Lemig (Democratic) Sortion tries to force a teleport that would bring Shi Maria into his own court; it backfires and she massacres his people instead.
  • Stockade dies by self-inflicted insanity — ruled a "psychosis-induced suicide" caused by Shi Maria's spell. The Democratic (Lemig) Sortion is eliminated and its assets awarded to the Madness. Their withdrawal triggers acceleration scenario two: "The ceasefire will be shortened by 23.33 hours." Faction Wars begins.

docs.title: Christmas Morning (Flashback)
docs.text: • Told out of sequence, between chapters 19 and 20, and set back on Floor 8. Carl finds the Containment Interface's Fuse page — five benchmarks required, only two met — and is offered a third option nobody mentioned: Disconnect Containment. He presses it. The star-detonation failsafe is permanently dead and the system AI is free of its containment. The red dot over Earth starts to grow. See The Containment Interface and the Star-Detonation Failsafe.

docs.title: The Ramp-Up
docs.text:
• 180 hours with no offensive magic, no teleportation, and border crossings restricted to fixed one-kilometre corridors. The Reavers open with a rot-sticker pet attack — level-40 "Dumplin'" behemoths, the direct payoff of Book 6's accelerated-pet-leveling vote.
  • The southern trench assault on the Prism Kingdom: Dazzler trebuchet modules, the long-standing Build Trench spell exploit, and an acid-filled trench trap emplaced by NPC spies. Empress D'Nadia is killed and the Prism Kingdom is eliminated.
  • Gondii brain-worms and Reaver paratroopers breach the FUPA's defences. Big Tina is unleashed in the base's defence. The FUPA holds.
  • King Rust of the Bone Clan publicly reveals Princess Formidable's plan to trigger the failsafe. Rosetta beheads him on air. Volteeg detonates his own tank, killing more than ten thousand soldiers and Warlord Hortense with them; the Operatic Collective is eliminated and its assets awarded to the Bone Clan.
  • Carl is yanked into Orren's office. The AI's avatar — wearing the body of Growler Gary, the Floor 4 gnoll — confirms the failsafe is permanently dead, teleports Princess Formidable bodily out of her own ship (which continues on and is later found abandoned), and then calls a "game time out" to ask Carl, Orren and Donut for relationship advice. The Bloc begins to fracture.
  • The Aryl system, a previous season's crawl, is revealed to have gone completely dark at the instant its own crawlers pressed their failsafe button. Nothing like it has ever been recorded.
  • The warlord council convenes. Princess Vinata of the Blood Sultanate is introduced. The first "Scolopendra Stirs" warning fires. Juice Box takes the form of the personification of the Nothing — "the Unwashed" — and delivers a prophecy to the assembled leaders: "It is coming. It is coming for you all." The naga army is revealed to be secretly dead already, pre-emptively killed by Prepotente.
  • Operation Snake Pit launches — publicly announced as a move on the Operatic castle, actually aimed at the Blood Sultanate. Prepotente formally throws in with the Princess Posse. Li Na's Dreads devastate Club Vanquisher. Princess Vinata — the Sepsis Whore — dies and the Blood Sultanate is eliminated. The god Hellik delivers a cryptic message for Emberus through Carl's burning skin: "Scolopendra stirs. It is all connected." And Milk, guildmaster of the hidden calligraphy and cartography guilds, is revealed to be Carl's biological sister.
  • Days of rebuilding. The Nest is constructed on the lip of the funnel and keyed to Atrocity-class spells. Rishi stages a naga coup, declares himself Sultan, and offers Carl a treaty. Carl marks him and kills him instead.

docs.title: Open Hostilities
docs.text:
• Operation Ruin begins the moment the phase opens. The Semeru agitate the lava tubes under King's Point and blow the top off the mountain, obliterating the orcish castle. Elle accidentally opens the Gate of the Feral Gods, freeing the gods Meatus and Harpocrates onto the battlefield.
  • The War Mage Rebellion breaks its own Conscription binding to kill King Stalwart and steals the Gate of the Feral Gods from Elle. The Bone Clan / Skull Empire is eliminated, and the War Mage Rebellion emerges as a new, entirely unplanned faction.
  • Eris freezes and piles roughly 80,000 combatants into a single mass; Donut balls them up with Rolling Battle Formation, a spell she drained out of a hat. Li Jun dies distracting Harpocrates to buy her the time to finish the cast.
  • Carl reaches Architect Houston's operating theatre and kills him. The Madness is eliminated — leaving four teams, which triggers the next phase automatically.

docs.title: The Peeling of Larracos
docs.text:
• "The Peeling Phase is upon us. This city is open. First to take the castle, wins." Agatha is revealed as the War Mage Rebellion's unwanted co-warlord — forced on them by the system — and burns all three of the team's Emergency Action Items in a single stretch, including a rule that makes every soldier of a defeated team drop dead where they stand.
  • Lucia Mar storms the Nest, killing the NPCs Bomo and Toyotomi on the way up. Rend kills her last rottweiler, Gustavo 3. Carl forcibly conscripts her — and then learns why she could not simply be killed: roughly 120,000 children on Earth's surface are tied to her survival by a dead-man's switch.
  • Donut casts War Crime, her third Atrocity. She is awarded the second class The Oak Fell and named Champion of Nekhebit. In the same hour, Li Na becomes the first crawler in recorded history to max every base stat at 300 simultaneously, at level 87, and the AI admits on air that it has no plan for this.
  • The Reavers are eliminated; Warlord Fang dies hiding inside his own dragon. Louis is rescued from Reaver captivity and found to have Epitome Tagg grafted into his replacement heart and lungs.
  • Prime Minister Glory attempts to have Carl assassinated through a Syndicate override panel. The AI blocks it mid-execution and threatens Glory's adult children by name on a public channel.
  • Samantha's casual confession about her role in Geyrun's death summons Emberus, starting a 66-minute countdown to the destruction of the entire floor. Katia eats the Orchid of Eileithyia's Grace. Mongo eats Epitome Tagg's extracted organs, killing him; the Dream is eliminated.
  • The Sledge casts Zerzura a second time, merging Shanty Town into Larracos and transferring the entire funnel city to the 12th floor. With Team Retribution's city gone from the board, the Princess Posse wins Faction Wars. Departing crawlers gift Carl the Book of Boom, a second volume of the Book of Voodoo.
  • Donut kills Huanxin Jinx with a crossbow bolt supplied by Mordecai, avenging his brother. Katia takes the pregnancy option from Eileithyia's three choices — specifically in order to be expelled from the dungeon and reach the children on the surface — which discharges the Sepsis Whore deal that had been keeping Donut from leaving Floor 9.
  • Justice Light, having stayed behind, triggers his long-planned trans-dimensional trap the moment Juice Box jumps into the Nothing. "The Nothing has been broken." Its contents drain simultaneously into the Halls of the Ascendency, into Sheol, and into Scolopendra's Lair. "Scolopendra has awakened."

docs.title: End of Book 7
docs.text:
• Of the 32,500 crawlers who came down from Floor 8, 20,221 are left — and "just over 20,000 crawlers making it to the 10th floor was a goddamned record. The second highest number wasn't even close."
  • At the Outreach Guild, Carl's lawyer Quasar walks him through the standing exit offers, all of which are terrible because there are so many survivors. Carl declines every one: "My official answer is, fuck these options. I am not taking a deal." Donut declines separately. See Post-Crawl Economics.
  • Floor 10 is announced as "Don't Come in Last" — a race floor. Each party picks a conveyance, biological or mechanical, travels a fixed number of legs between points, and upgrades the vehicle at each finish. Come last, and the vehicle's survival containment is removed. No airships allowed.
  • Porthus publicly announces the formation of a new militant group and declares open war on Syndicate government property from outside the dungeon.
  • The 16th floor is revealed to be "a giant, empty room with a single mirror in it: a non-magical mirror plucked from an abandoned Motel 6 location in Boise, Idaho." The 17th, "The Backstage Death Maze," is confirmed built and already running.
  • Baroness Victory becomes acting Prime Minister of the Syndicate.
  • In the final pages, Carl's agent informs him — with no explanation whatsoever — that he is already married to Donut's new attorney, Princess Chandra, Esq.
